Two Forgotten Stars

KnockTok

Summary:

Anastasia Hoshin had it all: money, powerful and loyal allies, a thriving business, and a path towards royalty. All of it now lay in shambles as her name was scrubbed from history because of the Archbishop of Gluttony. However, she will not break. She will not bend to the will of the world. She will rise again, all the way from the bottom.

Now, if only she could survive being at the sharp end of a random mugging.

A Re:Forgotten tale (how unique) fully exploring the romance between Anastasia and Subaru, whose names were forgotten at the end of Arc 5. Watch as the pair of stars find comfort and love again despite losing everything.
Inspired by Lost Then Found by Ferum and many other Re:Forgotten stories

Notes:

  • Translation into Español available: Two Forgotten Stars (Traducción al español) by Lufercy

This fic will be updated at least one day a week, usually Monday.

If you are interested in daily updates, consider following one of my socials, Twitter (X)/Reddit/Youtube: KnockTok's Socials

(See the end of the work for more notes and other works inspired by this one.)

Chapter 1: Prologue: Sharp Negotiation

Chapter Text

Anastasia Hoshin was down on her luck. To be fair, her starting hand was always rotten. Born and abandoned within the slums of Kararagi, her chances of surviving were abysmal. And yet she survived, no, flourished despite the odds.

By the time she was 23, she was the chairman of her own company, surrounded by loyal allies she can call family, and was in the running for becoming the king of her very own country. However, it all came crashing down without warning in Priestella.

The battle of Priestella was all but finished. The Archbishop of Greed was defeated and the Archbishop of Wrath was captured. Yet, in a cruel twist of fate, Gluttony struck her at her most vulnerable. With none of her campmates nearby, her name was taken and she ended up abandoned and forgotten.

 

In the aftermath of the conflict, she wandered aimlessly, trying to scrounge up as much money as she could. While most of her assets were now under the Juukulius family, she had stored money and some contraband in discrete locations all around Lugunica in case of emergencies. Unfortunately, such emergencies were planned with the forethought that her allies would help secure the funds with efficiency. With only herself, it took her a whole month to gather enough money to start again.

Now at the capital with her newly bought carriage, she took one last look at the city. A sense of nostalgia and melancholy rushed through her mind: memories of eating at a restaurant with a trio of cat demi-humans, memories of her negotiating with a certain honorable knight, and memories of her being given her star pin by a boisterous wolf-man. Out of habit, she reached for her neck to grasp her absent scarf and was left with only a bitter feeling of longing.

 

Anastasia Hoshin was truly alone.

 

However, she was determined to start again. Sure, she had to start again from zero, but if she could do it once before, she can do once more. Such optimism would usually fill her with renewed hope… if she wasn’t currently being threatened at knifepoint.

 

“…Ya know, there are better ways to ask for a ride?” Anastasia joked.

Her current assailant had snuck up behind her while she was looking back at the city one last time. She silently chastised herself for letting her emotions keep her from escaping from the capital, especially since the guards were in a state of emergency trying to find an escaped Archbishop. Most of them were at the Royal Capital and noble district, trying to protect high value targets like the Sage Council from any harm.

“…” her assailant was silent.

Anxiety crept up Anastasia’s throat, as the silence stretched from seconds to minutes. What was her assailant thinking?

 

Before she could say something else, the figure behind her lowered the knife from her neck and pushed her forward. Quickly turning around, she noticed that the person accosting her was just a boy a few years younger than her. In fact, he was barely of average height and was visibly scrawny. However, what caught her attention was his scary narrow eyes, gaunt sunken cheeks, and white hair. The boy looked like he had seen hell but was peculiarly absent of any visible wounds, despite some blood and open crevices splotching his weird attire. To be frank, the boy looked like he had just risen from the grave as a ghost.

 

“…Why are you here, Anastasia?” the boy muttered.

 

What?

 

How did he know her name? She hadn’t given out her real name once since she lost it. Perhaps she said it accidentally without thinking? Has the boy been stalking her? She needed more information.

“Well, that is quite a rude way to start a conversation. Can’t a merchant leave when danger is afoot?”

He quickly pointed the knife at her.

 

“ANSWER THE DAMN QUESTION!” Anastasia was startled by the sudden yelling. “Why is a royal candidate leaving the capital in the middle of the night with not a knight or mercenary in sight?”

 

So, he does recognize her, this wasn’t just a sudden mugging. He knew her from before Priestella.

Is he immune to the effects of Gluttony?

The boy looked frantic and almost paranoid, darting eyes every which way while keeping her in sight. As if he was prepared someone was waiting in the shadows, about to strike. She needed to be careful, lest the knife end her life.

 

She brought both her hands up, “…I ain’t a royal candidate anymore. Everyone forgot about me since the witch cult attacked Priestella. The Archbishop of Gluttony struck right at the end of the assault,” Anastasia answered honestly.

The answer startled the boy, he genuinely looked distraught. Almost, sympathetic of her plight.

 

“Sorry,” Anastasia rose an eyebrow, “It must have been rough having everyone you love forget about you.” The boy said bitterly while shaking his head.

 

“…You ain’t gotta apologize for that, not like you were responsible for it. Though an apology for almost slittin’ my throat would help.” Anastasia joked.

 

The boy winced and lowered his knife, “Sorry. I wasn’t going to hurt you. Honest. I was just confused why someone important like you was all alone.”

The boy was a conundrum to Anastasia. On the one hand, he looked and acted like a maniac. On the other hand, the boy spouted empathy and kindness like it was second nature. She needs to figure out which was true and which was a ploy.

 

“I’ll just let you be on your way-“

“Now hold on,” Anastasia quickly interrupted, “Ya can’t just interrogate a young gal in the middle of the night without introducing yourself. It’s only fair.” She said with a smirk.

He’s the only one who remembers me. I can’t just let him slip away without understanding what makes him different.

 

“… Natsuki Subaru. Emilia’s former knight.”

Whatever she expected to hear, it wasn’t that. She never heard of his family name, much less recognized his peculiar appearance. The eyes and hair should be unique enough that someone who was a knight of the most hated royal candidate would be easily recognizable. That and the specific qualifier “former”-

“You lost your name as well, didn’t you?” Anastasia gambled.

 

The boy startled, visibly shocked. “How did you-?” His reaction confirmed it, her bet paid off.

 

“It doesn’t take a genius to figure it out. Your unique appearance coupled with the fact that no one would pretend to be the knight of a half-elf. It’s obvious that ya got your name snatched and you’re in the same situation as me.”

To be honest, there was an equal chance that he was absolutely insane, simply being a self-proclaimed knight obsessing over a beautiful witch lookalike. But all signs say otherwise, now she just needed to figure out why he was so cautious of her in the first place.

 

“So, my only question now is: why are you here? Emilia’s camp is situated in the Miload domain. Her camp is also fairly nice and understandin’. I’m sure they would accept ya back all things considered.”

The boy’s shocked face quickly scowled. “Never. I’m not going back. Even if I wanted to, they’ll just throw me back into that hellish nightmare without a second thought. The only thing they care about was what I did for them, not who I was!”

 

Natsuki raised his knife back at Anastasia. “And you still didn’t answer my original question: why are you here alone?! Where’s Julius, Ricardo, the triplets? Shouldn’t you have no difficulty returning to them?”

 

Aaaaand we are back to square one.

Sigh.

One wrong misstep and the tension that was about to dissipate is back to full. On the bright side, she now had a better understanding of the boy. He was scared. Time to gamble one last time.

She took a deep breath.

 

“Apologies, I didn’t mean to assume anything. To answer your question: I’m… afraid of what will happen if I reunite with them.”

 

She took a step towards him.

 

“That they’ll hate you and reject you?!” The boy spoke with shock and a tinge of bitterness, stepping back at the same time. This only confirmed her theory, the boy tried to reach out to his old friends and was soundly rejected. Of course, the boy was afraid, he was not only forgotten but all of his former allies turned against him.

 

“No, I’m afraid that the relationships I had will never be the same again.”

 

She took another step.

She needed to be honest and precise, the boy may be manic, but he spoke honestly and sincerely. She needed to respond in kind to get him to trust her.

 

“That even if I try to reconnect, all of the memories I had of them.”

 

Another.

“All of the little quirks, all of the trials we faced, and all of the good we experienced: it would only be remembered by me.“

 

One foot over the other.

 

“That the family I cultivated would never come back.”

 

One final step.

 

Her heart wrenched with each word, but it was worth the effort. The boy was less frantic, as if her words were grounding him, as understanding and sympathy crept into his mind. She needed to seal the deal. She was almost face to face with him, the knife barely reaching her chest.

 

“So, I chose to leave and start again, instead of facing that cruel reality.”

 

 She softly added with a faint laugh,

 

“I’m truly slothful ain’t I?”

 

Seconds passed as Anastasia braced for the expected reaction. Suspicion, pity, indifference, all possible outcomes from her gambit.

 

 

Sniff. Sob.

…

But Anastasia Hoshin could not believe her eyes. The boy who was just recently holding her at knifepoint, the boy who was frantically paranoid of everything around him, the boy who looked like he had just left an active warzone: was on the verge of tears out of pure empathy for her woes.

“Wait-“

“Don’t say that,” the boy interrupted while wiping his eyes, “Anybody in your situation would have the same reaction. Sure, strong people may say the right way is to push on in spite of fear. But it’s easier to say than do. The feeling of despair, the isolation, grasping at what you lost. Those feelings are valid.”

With tears dotting his eyes, the knife he held clattering onto the cobblestone road, and while gently grasping Anastasia’s hands,

 

“It was hard, wasn’t it?”

…

 

The dam within her heart broke. Days of sleepless nights, frantic searching for money and anyone who could remember her, and paranoia over her broken gate. A human can only hold back so much. And this boy. This stupidly kind boy, who looked like he had been through worse, is weeping for her sake. Anastasia could only cry in response.

“…I was afraid. I was alone with everyone I knew possibly dead. And when I finally found them, they thought I was just a hapless civilian. I thought it was a joke, just one big nightmare. But that wasn’t just it. All of my work, the company I built, everything I accomplished: gone. Over 20 years of hard work, gone in an instant. The worst part wasn’t that. It was walking up to Julius and the Iron Fang, and all I could see in their eyes, was pity. No happiness, no recognition, not even a hint of familiar concern. Just pity towards a random girl found in a war torn city. I was a nobody again.”

The tears wouldn’t stop falling. If someone were witnessing this from afar, they would see a boy and a girl clutching each other, crying and wailing with no restraint.

 

“I know. I know,” the boy softly cooed back between sobs, “You’re not alone. I know how you feel. You are not a nobody.”

 

Anastasia was clutching Natsuki’s chest while the boy patted her head to comfort her. For a moment, the two were in their own little world.

Stomp. Stomp. Clop. Clop.

Until both started to hear thundering footsteps and clattering armor getting closer to them. Anastasia could hear the boy’s heart start quickening in response.

 

“No. nonononono-“The boy looked like he was having a panic attack. For a second, Anastasia was confused by the boy’s reaction, until she connected the puzzle pieces together.

Oh, what have they done to this poor boy? She thought to herself.

 

Thinking fast, she quickly held the boy’s hand and brought him to her carriage. Flinging the door open, she moved the supplies around and brought out a tarp.

The thunder was getting louder.

“Quickly! Hide in here.” She whispered.

The boy only looked at her incredulously, “I-.”

“Trust me. Please.”

With a second of hesitation, the boy climbed in and hid himself under the tarp, surrounded by various goods and knickknacks.

“No matter what, stay here until I say it’s safe to come out.” Anastasia quietly closed the door and prepared herself. She was already disheveled, with bloodshot eyes and tear stains to boot, but quickly acted as if she was pushed onto the floor.

 

Right as the thundering was about to reach the corner of the street, she quickly screamed at the top of her lungs,

“HELP PLEASE!!”

Just as she did, a battalion of guards came rushing around the corner towards her. Their leader, a middle-aged man with blue hair strode up towards her and helped lift her up.

“Ma’am are you alright? What happened?” He said urgently.

Anastasia put on her best damsel-in-distress face,

“It was terrible, a man in a cloak came out of nowhere and threatened me with a knife!” She quickly pointed at said knife resting on the floor.

“H-he kept askin’ me about where the Karsten manor was, sayin somethin’ about takin’ revenge. I-I didn’t know anythin’ but he wouldn’t take no for an answer. I thought I was dead but I think he got scared from hearin’ y’alls footsteps because he suddenly sprinted off that way.” She pointed a finger opposite from where the knights had come from, deeper into the city.

 

Shaking his head, the guard captain looked to his men, “He must be trying to make his way towards the royal candidates. We’ll need to split up. Cornelius: take your squadron to the Karsten villa in the Noble district and secure the parameter. Meanwhile, I will lead the rest down the street towards his last known direction.”

Before the guards could start organizing toward their intended directions, Anastasia meekly grasped at the captain’s sleeve and looked up with her best puppy dog eyes,

 

“Sir please, if you don’t mind me askin’, could you let one of your men escort me out of the city?”

 

For a moment, the captain frowned, but before he could even ponder the request, Anastasia started bawling, “P-please sir, I’m so scared. I just want to take my wares and leave in peace. I-I’m afraid that bad man will come back to silence me.”

 

Visibly taken aback by the sudden tears, “O-of course miss, rest assured! I’ll send one of my best men to get you out of the city safe and sound.” With a swift cough and clearing of his throat:

 

“BECKLAM!”

“Y-yes captain!”

The captain sighed, “Take Miss, uh-“

“Anastasia.”

“Yes, Miss Anastasia towards the city gates and help her leave the capital safely. Afterwards, reconvene with the rest at the Karsten villa. Is that clear?”

“Yes captain!”

“Good. You take care miss, the knights will sort this all out.”

Anastasia only responded with her cutest smile.

While the rest of the battalion left towards their intended destination, the young knight helped escort Anastasia to the outskirts of the capital.

 

…

 

“Sorry for the trouble Miss Anastasia.”

“Oh? What for?”

“No lady should be accosted at night, especially by some dirty witch cultist…”

“Oh, it’s quite alright, I’m just thankful ya brave and handsome knights came to save little ole me.”

The young knight blushed at her response.

And thank you for the wonderful information you are about to give me. Anastasia thought.

 

“So, if you don’t mind me asking: how did the cultist escape?”

For a second the knight hesitated, “I don’t quite know myself miss, it’s a conundrum. From what the others were saying, it looked like the cultist just walked out. All of the guards were covered in wounds and knocked out.”

Yet, Natsuki was without any marks or scratches when I met him. Strange given that all signs point to a fight.

“That’s so scary! Thank goodness you’re here to protect me,” she said with a wink.

The knight blushed a deeper red, “O-of course ma’am! Though, I don’t think the guy will put that much of a fight.”

“Oh? Why is that?”

“I was one of the rotating guards for the prison. Last time I saw him, well that cultist was not looking too hot.”

“…What do you mean?”

The knight grimaced, “Oh apologies, I don’t think a lady should hear such uncouth things.”

…

 

They tortured him. They tortured a boy who would cry for a woman who suffered far less. Disgusting.

 

“I feel bad for him.” Anastasia blurted out.

Visibly shocked, the guard replied “Oh no miss, such sympathies are worthless towards such scoundrels-“

Anastasia began tuning out the knight’s honest, yet misplaced, soliloquy. A part of her doesn’t understand why she said such a thing. It was illogical. It could have put her on the spot as a Witch Cult sympathizer. She should be grabbing as much information as she could. Yet, how could she not? When the supposed Archbishop of Pride as they were claiming him to be, was just a scared boy hiding right behind her.

 

“When he ran away, he looked so young. He didn’t look like he could hurt anybody.”

The young knight looked at Anastasia with pity, “Your heart is in the right place Miss. But remember: those witch cultists are a bunch of insane psychopaths. They may look like normal people, but they are anything but normal.”

“…I-“ A loud thud and crashing of objects from inside the carriage interrupted the conversation.

“What was that?!” the guard exclaimed.

Oh no, not now.

Thinking fast, “Ah! Uhh, it must have been one of the metias I’m selling.”

“Metias? Those must be expensive. Would you like to take a second to check if everything is secure?”

“Oh no, that is not necessary!” She said a little too fast, “I wouldn’t want to bother you.”

“Nonsense, if you would like, I could take a quick peek and see if everything is okay-”

“WAIT!” The guard’s eyes started to narrow with suspicion, “T-the thing is these metias are very special.”

“Well that should not-“

“Special for women.”

 

“…Elaborate.”

Faking a blush, “Well sometimes, young ladies like myself need a bit of… help now and then.”

“Oh.”

“Ooohhhhh,” the knight started connecting the dots, “A-apologies ma’am, I shouldn’t have been so invasive.”

“It’s quite alright…”

She could barely tell but Anastasia swears she could hear a faint snickering from within the carriage.

…

I take it all back. The boy is a little shit.

The rest of the trip to the gates of the capital was done in an awkward silence.

At the gate, a lone soldier was waiting.

“Becklam!” He cried out, “I thought you left to join the others?”

“Well, I did initially, but the archbishop had a run-in with the young lady here.” Becklam pointed a thumb at Anastasia.

“I was given the job to escort her out of the city so she can continue with her business.”

“Well, I guess that makes sense. We’ll need to check her carriage before she leaves though.” The gate guard replied.

Anastasia’s heart started to beat faster.

Before she could reply, “Uh Arth,” Becklam coughed, “you got a minute?”

Arth confused, nodded. Becklam put an arm around Arth’s shoulder and started walking a bit away from Anastasia. “So, about Miss Anastasia’s business-“

As the conversation slowly dissipated from her ears, Anastasia sighed in relief. Taking a moment to collect her thoughts, she started realizing the exact situation she was in.

Oh my Od, I’m smuggling a wanted criminal out of the royal capital. I could be executed for this.

She thought back to all that happened in the last few hours: from being held at knifepoint to crying her heart out to putting on her best award-winning acting performance. It all felt surreal.

Did she regret it?

… Not really, no. Sure, the situation was tense. Sure, she might have put all her trust into what could be a psychopath that was tricking her into escaping. Sure, her overall state of affairs was still royally screwed.

But something in her gut was telling her she made the right call. That her bad hand was turning out in her favor.

Pfft, maybe the world is finally turning in my favor, eh baroness?

 

Somewhere out in the deep south, in the country of Vollachia, a certain Sun Princess let out a cute sneeze. Followed by the metallic thud of her companion’s head getting smashed into the dirt.

 

Anastasia’s musing was interrupted by the pair of guards returning, with one having slightly pink cheeks.

Arth coughed, “Yeah you are free to go ma’am. Sorry for the wait.”

“I thank ya both kindly for your service,” Anastasia smiled in response.

“Oh, before you go, you think you could help my friend out. You see, his lover has a bit more energy than he does, so he’s having a bit of trouble-“

Becklam smacks him upside the head.

“OW- WHY?!”

“I don’t know,” Becklam responded, “Maybe it’s because I’m a man dying of thirst watching another man drowning in water?!”

“It ain’t my fault your dumb ass can’t keep a girl for more than two days.”

“Well, I would be able to if SOMEONE DIDN’T KEEP TELLING ALL THE GIRLS I FLIRT WITH ABOUT MY PREFERENCES.”

“I’M SAVING YOU THE TROUBLE, NO SANE GIRL IS GOING TO USE WATER MAGIC ON YOUR-“

 

This is hell. All of my choices led to this very moment. I deserve this.

Nursing back a migraine, and with a deep breath, “BOYS!”

The two quit their argument and turn their heads up toward the violet-haired maiden.

“It’s getting’ late, I think I’ll start movin’. Thank y’all so much again for all the help.” She said with her greatest professional smile.

“Yeah, uh no problem,” “Sorry miss. You take care.”

…

After a bit of driving, when the capital was slowly becoming smaller and smaller, Anastasia started to finally relax.

…

“… Pfft…hehehe…”

She straightened her back again.

“Heheheheheh-”

She slowly turned her head back towards the carriage.

“BWAHAHAHHAHA!!!”

She slammed open the rectangular slit to look inside the boxed up carriage,

“LISTEN HERE YOU LITTLE SHIT-“

Anastasia briefly said in a rage, before noticing an interesting sight. The white haired boy, who was still laughing his head off, was giving the brightest genuine smile she has seen in months. Before, the paranoid boy was tense and on edge. Now he looked like he was having the time of his life. It was truly contagious.

“Pftt… bahahahHAHAHA!” Before long, Anastasia was laughing as well. They laughed, and laughed, until they were basically wheezing.

 

“Hahaha… ha.”

 “Why did you do that?” Natsuki finally asked.

“… Well, I couldn’t just leave you to the wolves. Plus, with the city on high alert, I needed a way to easily get out without trouble. Having a guard escorting me would expedite it plus-“

“No, I mean: why did you trust me? You could have turned me in, most likely gotten a reward, and life would have been much easier for you. Now, you are harboring a wanted criminal, who very well could have been a Witch Cult Archbishop?”

“…Are you an Archbishop?” Anastasia asked.

“No! Absolutely not.” Natsuki denied.

“Well then, I believe you.”

Looking back, she could see the boy’s jaw drop, as if he could not fathom her reasoning.

…

“There was no reason to trust me…” the boy looked down.

“You gave me ample reason.”

The boy looked up again, confused.

“All of the archbishops I met were not only complete psychopaths but were also incredibly strong and gave little to no regard to anyone around them. Sure, you did threaten me in the beginning. But not only did you apologize for that, you subsequently sympathized with me about my lost name and then proceeded to sincerely cry with me about it. You had many opportunities to kill me and leave. But you didn’t. So, yes, you gave me ample reason to trust you.”

 

Sniff. Sob.

She heard a familiar sound again. This time, she decided to give the boy some privacy, closing the slit behind her. She drove in silence for the next few hours.

 

…

“… Anastasia-san.”

The monotony was broken, “Yes?”

“Stop and let me out here.” She quickly looked around. They were getting close to a town but were still miles away from anything remotely civilized.

After a few seconds, “No.”

“What?! What do you mean-“

“You owe me.”

“I- uh. Er-“

“I smuggled you out of that city at my own risk. You’re an investment for me now. One I wish to capitalize on by having you repay your debt.”

Natsuki pondered for a bit, “… I don’t have any money. And well, I don’t think you’ll like my body that much-”

“Not that kind of repayment you idiot,” she sighed. Still, a part of her was happy that the boy seemed to have retained some humor despite all he went through.

“You were Emilia’s knight, correct? Well, as you can see, I am both knightless and resourceless. The latter will be resolved in due time, the former will be solved by you.”

“So, I protect you and you, do what you do best: make money and talk to people?”

“Essentially, yes. An equal partnership. Dissolved when both parties agree that they are no longer in need of each other’s service. I’ll provide you with opportunities and resources while you protect me from hoodlums and scourges of the Witch Cult.” Anastasia explained.

“…Sure.”

Anastasia was surprised, “That fast, huh? No bargaining or anything?”

“No, I’m sure. I’m broke beyond compare and got nothing besides my name. This is probably the best deal I can get.”

Anastasia sighed, “Remind me to teach you a bit about proper negotiation later. You shouldn’t so easily show your whole hand, otherwise you’ll get taken advantage of.”

Natsuki only smirked in response, “Funny you say that. Someone told me something similar in the past.”

“Wow, that person must have been the smartest person you laid eyes on. You must be so grateful,” she said sarcastically.

“Haha, you have no idea. I owe her more than you could ever realize…”

 

They finally made it to a town to rest the earth dragons and find a proper inn for a night’s rest. While getting far away from Lugunica was important, being sleep deprived would bring its own set of problems.

“You need a disguise. Here take this.” Anastasia handed him a cloak and a mask with a purple scar on the right eye with black feathers on the back.

“… This looks ridiculous.”

“Well, I’m sorry, I wasn’t expecting to hide a criminal in plain sight, so this is all I have,” Anastasia huffed.

“Sorry, sorry. It just reminds me of what some people I knew used to wear when they were younger,” Natsuki shuddered with memories of people clutching their eye or arm in fake pain.

“You’ll also need an alias, can’t have people tracing your name, at least until we get to Kararagi.”

“…How about Atlas?”

“Hmmm, not bad, does it mean anything?”

“It’s related to a story in my world as well as to my name. It was either that or Alcor but honestly that name sounded kind of dumb.”

“You’ll have to tell me more later, for now, try to follow my lead.”

After donning his disguise, the pair entered the inn.

“Two rooms ple-urgk!” Natsuki tried to start with until Anastasia elbowed his sides before quickly hugging his arm and edging close to him.

“What my darlin husband Atlas meant to say, was that we wanted one room with a single bed please?”

“Yeah, uh, whatever my honey bunny wants,” Natsuki grimaced while Anastasia stifled a laugh.

The old proprietor simply softly smiled at this and gave the two a key to their room in exchange for a few copper coins.

…

Once they were out of earshot, “What was that about?”

Anastasia rolled her eyes, “What? I got us a great deal on a room and now we have got a great alibi if anyone tries to come find us. See? This is why you need me.”

Natsuki only pinched his nose bridge and closed his eyes as a response. “Wait, I’m curious why do you talk like that only sometimes?”

“Like what sometimes?”

“Like that Kans- I mean, Kararagi accent. You used it with the guards or the innkeeper, but usually it goes away with me. So, what’s that about?”

Anastasia was silent for a moment before responding, “It helps me convince people.”

“Huh?”

“Kararagi is known for its economic power and its witty merchants. I figured an accent will help me sell the image that I’m a competent businesswoman. So, I do it out of habit, I guess.”

“…But you don’t do it with me becauseee?”

“I guess I trust you, Natsuki-san. You know who I am, despite Gluttony, and we are in a kind of partnership right now.”

Natsuki was silent for a bit as they entered their room.

“… Call me Subaru.”

“Your family name, I mean if you prefer that-“

Subaru shook his head, “No. In my home country, we use a different naming format. My family name is Natsuki, while my personal name is Subaru. So, call me Subaru.”

“Huh. Alright Subaru-kun, where is your home country anyway?”

“It’s a small island country in the East.”

“…But Lugunica is the eastern most country. The only thing east is the Great Waterfall.”

Anastasia’s eyes widened.

“Yeah…I’m from a place beyond the Great Waterfall.”

Anastasia expected Subaru to laugh and say it was a joke but the boy looked at her sincerely.

“Well, that is hard for me to fully comprehend but I’ll trust your word.”

Anastasia promptly laid on the bed and patted an open area.

“Come on, let’s get some sleep.”

Subaru blushed, “Y-yeah! I’ll uh, let you sleep first. I can keep watch for a bit OHHH-”

Before he could finish, Anastasia grabbed his arm and dragged him into bed.  Subaru was now nestled between her arms, blushing mad, trying to make sense of what was happening.

“Nope! We are both exhausted, and we both need to get some rest before heading out at dawn.”

“But what if someone tries to break in?! Or what if the guards catch up to us?!”

“Then we will deal with it then… Besides, I’m used to hugging something fluffy while sleeping,” memories of a certain fox flashed in her mind, “And you’re the closest substitute I got.”

And at that, Subaru promptly surrendered.

“That bit of information is in exchange for what you told me about your home.”

Subaru looked up at her.

“This was an equal partnership remember? So, whatever you give, I’ll give in equal compensation. Same vice versa. Although, you still owe me something.”

Subaru was now confused, “You mean for saving me? Again, my body isn’t for sale- ARGH!”

Anastasia started pinching his cheek, “No you little shit! I meant when I told you all about how I felt after Gluttony. You still haven’t told me what happened to you.”

Subaru was silent now, his scary eyes in deep contemplation.

Her eyes softened, “…You don’t have to tell me if you are uncomfortable. It must have been hard. Harder than I can ever imagine. But that’s why I want to know, I want to know so that burden doesn’t have to be only on your shoulders.”

And so that I can pay you back for the kindness you gave me. You don’t have to be alone either, Subaru-kun.

After a bit more silence, “I’ll tell… I don’t think I can tell you everything. Not yet at least. But I’ll tell you what I can.”

And so, the pair talked as the night passed, about all the horrors the boy faced for the last two months, before silently falling asleep in each other’s arms.

 

Hidden out of sight, two pairs of eyes silently watch over the pair of stars, waiting and planning in the shadows.

 

 

 

 

 

 

Chapter 2: Echoes

Summary:

A fragment of that night is shown while our two stars begin their journey.

Notes:

Over 200 kudos, over 30 bookmarks, and tons of comments showing interest. I am shocked and thankful for all of the support for this fic. I promise I’ll make this fic a memorable one. Not the bad kind hopefully

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

 

Drip. Drip. Drip.

Within the royal capital of Lugunica lies the sturdy prison tower, where all manner of hoodlums and insane cultists reside as punishment for their wickedness. Within the muck and desolate atmosphere, lies the brightest black star of another world, falsely imprisoned and tortured for any information regarding the cult and its future activities.

Drip. Drip. Drip.

The star languishes in the dark, teetering between madness and somber resignation of his state. He only hears the faint dripping of water in the background. Echoes of a past he endeavors to recover and a future that no longer exists, again and again, haunt his very bones.

Drip. Drip. Drip.

He regrets. He cries. He languishes. He screams. He loves. He hates. He rages. He defies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He dies. He-

“Hello again, Archbishop-nyan!” A cheery voice broke the insanity.

With a creak of his neck, he looks up, and blinks slowly in response. The origin of the voice appears to be a young demi human with catlike features, wearing a knights uniform. The knight would usually be the picturesque symbol of feminine charm; if the disheveled hair, filthy clothing, and sunken eyes weren’t currently marring his physique.

“…”

“Come on, Archbishop-nyan! It’s quite rude to nyot say a greeting to a guest.”

“…”

The knight simply shrugged in response to the silence and continued conversing, “Well then, I guess I’ll do the talking for the both of us. Aren’t you so grateful~!”

Taking a chair, he sat down in front of the dying star.

“How was my day? Fine~, so fine. Thank you for asking! I got up bright and early today and helped Crusch-sama get ready for the day. Then, after breakfast and some paperwork, Crusch-sama and I went out on a walk along the garden.”

The knight sighed in false contentment, “It was really beautiful. The flowers just started blooming and everything looked so serene. We met Wilhelm there also. He’s been spending a lot of time there recently since we got back from Priestella. He’s doing a lot better now, especially after all that happened. I’ll let him know you’re thinking of him by the way~.”

The knight winked and posed in faux gratitude before continuing, “He and Reinhard are a bit tense right now. Well, Reinhard and I are also a bit tense at the moment. After our… disagreement, he hasn’t really been talking to me too much. And when we do, it usually devolves into shouting.”

The knight leans in smiling, and under the brief glint of candle light, the star could see there was no humane light to be found in the demi-human’s eyes.

“I blame you for that, you know?”

The air shifted, and for a moment, it felt like the shadows were coalescing around them.

“He kept asking about you. Asking how you have been doing since Wilhelm and I barred him from coming here. Even had to get the Sages to rally his attention somewhere else. Reinhard is a sweet guy. Too kind. Too nice. Too forgiving to a piece of shit like you.”

The shadows continued to gather, purple light ebbing and flowing, converging behind the knight.

“That’s why I must do this. Because Reinhard can’t. Julius wouldn’t. And Crusch-sama should not. But I will. Because that’s what being a knight is about. Shouldering the burdens of others for the good of all. Even if the very actions you take, disgust you. Even if the ones you do it for, will never forgive you!”

He slowly stood up and grabbed the remaining fragments of clothing that surrounded the star and hoisted him up to eye level.

“So, come on. Tell me! TELL ME WHERE THE CULT IS! TELL ME HOW TO CURE CRUSCH-SAMA’S ILLNESS!!”

The knight’s lifeless manic eyes gazed into the abyss of the star’s.

“…”

“…Useless.” The knight muttered before dropping the star like a sack of tatoes.

“I know you’re still there, you can still hear me. We can do this like yesterday. And the day before!” He brandished a knife. “My offer still stands: give me what I NEED and I’ll make the pain stop.”

Shadows pulsed and shuddered behind the knight, the very air around them shimmering.

“…”

“…Have it your way-“

The star twitched on the floor, briefly startling the knight. The shadows paused.

 

“…Felix,” the star whispered.

Desperately, Felix pounced on the opportunity, diving to the floor in a vain attempt to hear anything of use from the supposed witch cultist. The knife scattering onto the floor.

“…” Seconds passed by.

“I’m sorry…”

 

Felix froze.

 

Drip. Drip. Drip.

 

An eternity passes.

 

Drip. Drip. Drip.


And then the ocean breaks with hideous laughter.

The knight threw his head up and cackled in disbelief.

“YOUR SORRY?!” He cried before laughing again at the sheer insanity of the situation.

The laughter echoes throughout the tower.

“This isn’t real. This isn’t real! Not real, not real, not real, not real. No no no no no-”

He was becoming manic, bashing his head into the ground until his blood splashed onto the floor. He collapses onto the ground crying.

“Nearly two months of work. Agonizing work to pry anything out of you. And the only thing you say is sorry?!”

Felix laughed and laughed and laughed again. As tears were shed, he vomited onto the floor.

“I can’t. I can’t. I can’t keep doing this Crusch. Fourier forgive me. Please forgive me. Disgusting. Your Ferris has become disgusting.”

The demi-human kept muttering the same words over and over, cradling himself right next to the star.

 

After what seemed like another eternity, Felix slowly stood up and started walking out of the prison. Using his water magic, he healed and cleaned up his self-made wounds.

 

Before exiting the star’s cell, he straightened his back, spun on his heel to briefly look at the star and shouted,

“That’s all for today, Archbishop-nyan! Ferris is feeling really tired today but don’t you worry~.”

With a faux smile, “I’ll be back soon,” before skipping out of the dungeon, humming a cheerful tune.

 

Drip. Drip. Drip.

As the star laid on the floor, closing his eyes, echoes of the past began resurfacing once again.

Who are you? How do you have a contract with Betty?! This is not possible, in fact. Betty would have remembered... Betty would not have forgotten!

I’m reaaally sorry. I don’t recognize you. I wish I could offer you anything. Please, just tell us about the cult and this will all be over quickly. I promise you.

I don’t recall you at all sir. The Iron Fang saved me from your brethren, but I do not remember you being among them. If I could offer any advice, I’d recommend complying with the knights’ demands.

My amazin’ self is the knight of the princess Emilia, not you, get that through your thick skull!

How do you know about my sister?  Were you there?! Answer me! How do I get her to wake up?!

This is barbarism Felix-dono, end his life before you sully your honor anymore.

Felix this is immoral. You’ve strayed past interrogation and went straight towards torture! As a knight, I won’t stand for this! Felix what are you doing? Stop!

I’m sorry, I should have done something sooner. If what your saying is true, then I have failed you, as a friend. I’ll talk to the Sage council tomorrow.

You shouldn’t have done that Archbishop-nyan~. I don’t know how you brainwashed them but you won’t have any more chances.

Drip. Drip. Drip.

For a moment, he felt as if his hands were being held, again by the pair of oni sisters.

Drip. Drip. Drip. Sob. Drip. Drip.

“Please...” he whispered into the abyss.

Opening his weeping eyes, he realized it was all an echo, same as the others. He began counting to pass the time again.

 

Hours passed by as the star counted the minutes to midnight. When the guards would change shifts and his cell will be checked and cleaned. A pair of guards approached the star’s cell and started surveying the aftermath of Felix’s visit.

“Dear Volcanica… this place is filthy!”

“Blame that disgusting beast knight, he always leaves this place worse than when he arrived.”

“Ugh, well, go ahead.”

“The fuck you mean go ahead, isn’t it your turn?”

“I didn’t sign up to clean vomit, you know how I am with that shit! If I go over there, I’ll practically add to the pile.”

“That’s disgusting, you absolute pansy.”

“Yeah, well it’s the truth so either you go over there and clean it or we’ll both get in trouble when the archbishop gets sick and dies before we get anything from him.”

“Really?” The shorter scrawnier guard glared up at the taller brawnier guard.

The tall guard just shrugged in response.

“Ugh, fine, then go check in on the other prisoners and the rest of the boys. Do fucking something at least.”

“You sure? Like the guy’s tied up but he’s still an Archbishop. What if he does some of his weird culty thing and blows your head up with his mind.”

“One: the guy is practically a walking corpse. Two: if he really could blow up my head, he would have done so already. And three: you’re giving me a fucking mind blowing migraine, so get going before I throttle you!”

“Jeez alright, no need to get all aggressive. Hey, by the way, have you heard anything from Darcy? She’s been gone for months now and I’m starting to get worried. It’s not like her to not mail-”

“Of course not, I’m not your fucking dad. If you’re worried, go to Priestella and check on her yourself. Now are you leaving or not!?”

“Alright, alright! Jeez, you think you know a guy for years…”

“Fucking dipshit.” The short guard muttered as the other strolled away.

The short guard approached the star and started cleaning up the muck and grime surrounding him. After finishing his work, he looked down on the star and noticed several freshly made knife wounds all over his body.

He started kicking him.

“Fucking disgusting cultist. You’re lucky your even remotely important.”

He started kicking harder and harder, until he heard bones getting broken.

“… pant…pant… That’ll show you!” He gave one last kick before spitting on the star.

Briefly looking around, he realized his fellow guard was taking a bit more time than he should be. He turned towards the exit.

“Did the fucker get lost or something? Should have known he couldn’t do something so simple! Maybe I’ll visit his sister again… relieve some stress and-“

Pain, pain pain pain pain pain pain.

All the guard could feel was pain. He felt small wounds perforate his body as his bones ruptured and broke in an instant. He was on the floor, barely cognizant, vomiting on the freshly cleaned floor from the shock of the sudden attack. With his last bits of consciousness, he glanced up to see the star standing over him, without a single open wound or broken arm. He looked practically brand new, as new as a pale ghost could look.

“please… help… me.”

He was bleeding out, the wounds were numerous and deep within the guard.

“…I’m sorry,” Subaru replied before slitting the guard’s throat with the knife he pocketed from Felix.

Subaru crept to the entrance of his cell, shouldering the wall, and took a brief look out. The next guard rotation will be in 2 hours, more than enough time, but there should be other guard pairs nearby to watch out for.

But the place was eerily empty. Speaking of, where was the other guard that just left?

Taking a deep breath of courage, he started stealthily inching his way through the tower. The air tasted strangely sweet, mixed with the bitterness of the dilapidated building. However, he came upon a peculiar sight, guards littered on the floor, breathing but unconscious. Some with weirdly shaped perforations riddling their bodies. Yet, not a corpse in sight, all had clear pulses.

This doesn’t make sense… I should be extra cautious while checking the other floors.

He did find the other tall guard from before, however, slumped over on the floor with his ass sticking out like an ostrich. He briefly rummaged through some of the guards’ pockets for keys. Before leaving for the next floor, Subaru briefly hesitated before finding a piece of paper and writing a quick note for the tall guard.

Check your friend’s basement. You’ll find your sister there.

I’m sorry.

Satisfied, he crept his way to the next floor and noticed that a similar situation was occurring there also. As well as the next floor. And the floor after that.

Becoming more alarmed, he quickly concentrated and looked down towards the floor. He saw multiple red and grey lights pulsating, though he focused on one particularly bright red star.

“… Sirius is still there, so it wasn’t her.”

He contemplated for a second before moving on.

“This is new. Did someone else break out as well… or maybe it’s a trap? What changed?” Subaru muttered to himself before deciding it was best not to question his good fortune before making it to safety.

He made his way down to the ground floor, making sure the other archbishop’s door was still locked, and found that even the guards at the entrance to the prison tower were knocked out. And not a single other cell was open.

…Questions for later. For now, I have to move fast and leave the capital, I only have an hour left.

As he exited the dungeon, he felt, for the first time in possibly years, the cold night air briskly waft over his body. Taking a deep breath, he quickly absconded into the night.

Deep in his mind though, he could still hear the faint dripping, despite being so far away from the lonely tower.

Drip. Drip. Drip.

Anastasia woke up to the sun beaming down on her. Blinking her eyes, she almost leapt up in shock before remembering everything that happened the night before.

So, it really wasn’t a dream.

She started gazing over the boy’s features, checking him for any damage. Again, surprisingly for her, he lacked any sort of wounds at all despite his story of leaving the tower.

She frowned.

Did Felix heal his wounds and he forgot to mention that?

Despite the severe lack of bodily harm, she noticed how frail and pale the boy looked. His hair was bleached white but she noticed strands of black mixed within. The boy was obviously malnourished.

We need to fix that promptly. Can’t have a knight who’ll fall to pieces any second. Speaking of, I should get some food for both of us before I break apart as well.

Lifting her arms out of the embrace, she sat at the edge of the bed before looking at the mirror adorning the wall of the room. Her hair was a mess, her eyes still slightly red from crying twice in one night. Once in the royal capital and another silently before she fell asleep. Despite her natural beauty, she positively looked horrendous.

“…One step at a time girl. You can look good when your home.”

Brief flashes of her camp flew by her mind, causing her to grimace before standing up to freshen up and change.

As she finished and was about to head off to grab breakfast, she heard muttering from her newly appointed knight.

“…sorry…” was the only word she can hear, the rest sounding like faint gibberish.

She looked towards the door before sighing and made her way back to the edge of the bed close to Subaru. Now closer, she can clearly hear what he was whispering:

“Emilia… sorry… please… don’t leave me alone again.”

Again? Did this happen before?

She shook her head.

No. He must be having a nightmare of Priestella.

Her assumption proved correct, as it looked like he was starting to curl into a fetal position while shivering. Thinking of what to do next, she decided to wait a little longer before getting food.

She lifted the boy’s head onto her lap and started brushing his hair with her fingers softly.

“Shhh, it’s okay. I’m here. I promised I won’t leave,” before jokingly adding, “I still have to teach you how to bargain before your robbed blind.”

At first the boy seemed to grimace, before relaxing by the end of her words. He seemed almost peaceful. He laid there, serenely, as Anastasia continued running her fingers through his hair while contemplating their situation.

“Hmmm.”

We have a good stockpile of goods and money. Thankfully, I got lucky, and most of what I stored in the carriage should sell out pretty quickly once we are in Kararagi. The problem is what to invest in once we have enough liquidity.

Her hands keep fussing over Subaru’s hair as she starts spiraling into deep thought.

We need proper inventory, a place to live and maybe even set up shop, and start training employees. Should I try apprenticing under a trading company to build connections? No, what I need is reputation, something to get an edge on the competition. But what to sell?

“…Anastasia?”

No, wait, the businesses can wait. We need to find a spirit to drain my excess mana. No point in worrying about starting a business if I’ll be dead before the end of the month.

“Oi, Anastasia?”

But where?! Oh, it would be so easy if I could just find Echidna but she disappeared when I got knocked out in Priestella. Maybe I should have contacted Julius before leaving, I could have persuaded him to help me contract a spirit.

“Ow, hey, be gentle with my hair. GENTLE!”

No, it would have taken a lot of time to convince him. That path’s dead in the water unless I want to throw Subaru to the wolves. Speaking of, I wonder how far they’ll try to look for him?

“Are you even listening to me?!”

He’ll have to wear his disguise everywhere but that might draw attention, at least until Kararagi maybe? Acting eccentric now is fine but it could cause issues later. What if they catch up? We’ll have to incapacitate them non-lethally. But how long can we keep that up? Some day we will have to use more force. The only problem is burying the evid-

FLICK

With a snap, Subaru flicked Anastasia’s nose to bring her out of her stupor.

“OW! You ass, what was that for?!”

“Given that you were about to turn my luscious locks into a barren field, I feel that was justified!”

She quickly looked down and saw that Subaru’s hair now looked like it was pulled and clumped into neat little pockets, looking like a chaotic mess.

Her cheeks darkened and she looked sideways, “Sorry… sometimes I get a little lost in my head.”

“Hey, its okay. I have the same habit,” he grinned cheekily, “besides, not everyday I get to wake up in a lap pillow.”

Anastasia’s blush deepened. She then pushed Subaru gently, so he would roll and hit the floor. Hard.

“Ow! Damn it! What was that for?!”

“Given you were being a little shit, you deserved it. Come on get ready, we got to get some food before we head out.”

“Yes ma’am.”

Subaru quickly donned his disguise and they made their way to the ground floor, in time to order one of the breakfast sets: Subaru getting a scrambled eggs and tatoes platter while Anastasia got a cup of coff and a pastry.

“That’s all you’re going to eat?” Subaru asked.

“I’m not that hungry. Besides, I don’t need much food to work.”

“Well, you won’t grow big and strong with that attitu-OW!”

Anastasia pinched Subaru’s hand, “I’m 23, you child.”

“Hey, I’m 18! At least I look like an adult.”

“Barely, and you certainly don’t act like one.”

“Hey, I’ll have you know my boyish charm is one of my best attractive traits.”

Anastasia scoffs, “And who are you attracting? Sex deviants.”

Subaru quickly replies, “Hey I’m not the one who looks like a legal loli.”

“What does that even mean?!”

Cough. COUGH.

They both looked to the side to see the waitress standing with their food, while wearing an expression that screamed customer-approved politeness.

“Would the young couple like to eat their breakfast outside?” Her eyebrow twitched.

They both glanced at each other and gulped.

“Sorry, ma’am.” “We’ll be more quiet.”

“Fantastic! Now would you guys like anything else? Oh! We have the new sauce everyone’s been raving about: mayonnaise.”

“Yes! Absolutely!” Anastasia was startled by Subaru’s sudden excitement. The man looked like he was dying of thirst and was just offered water from a Great Spirit.

“What’s got you so excited, its just a new sauce that’s trending?”

“Hey, I’ll have you know this is liquid gold. It goes with everything and makes all dishes 200% better.” He said as he squirted an inhumane amount of stuff onto his eggs and tatoes.

Anastasia visibly grimaced in disgust, “Urgh, you sure?”

Quickly taking a bite, “Mmmm! Delicious!”

The boy looked positively ecstatic.

Anastasia, despite her initial disgust, felt a rising warmth seeing the boy in front of her so happy with something so simple.

She took a sip of her coff. Alright maybe he had a point about his boyish charm.

She quickly frowned.

Calm down brain. It’s not like that. This is just a temporary partnership until we get back on our feet. No use trying to get too attached.

Yeah right, ‘too attached?’ Says the girl who basically helped him escape from the authorities, smuggled him out of the capital, and slept very CLOSELY with him at night. All in the same day. If you got more attached, you’d basically be joined at the hip to him.

Shut up brain.

“You good?”

“Hm?” Anastasia looked up.

“You looked like you were about to contemplate the meaning of life again.”

“Ha. Ha.”

“Well, you won’t find the number 42 with that attitude.”

“What does that mean-“ Her question was cut off by a spoonful of eggs, tatoes, and a generous helping of mayo being shoved in her face.

“Here, you need brain food with all that thinking you’re doing.”

She frowned, “I’ll pass.”

“Come on, unless widdle ole Ana can’t stand a widdle mayo~?”

Her frown deepened but just as she opened her mouth to retort, he shoved the spooned into her mouth.

“Hey!” she said as her mouth was stuffed with food, before realizing, “That’s actually not that bad.”

“Right? It’s my favorite. Thank god Rem helped me make this stuff back then.”

“Wait, what did you just say?

“Hm? It’s my favorite?” He replied as Subaru was dividing his dish in half.

“No after that.”

He lifted another spoonful of grub to her face.

She looked at him.

He looked at her.

Seconds passed.

He motions with his hand as if saying, “Well you going to eat it or not?”

She motions back as if saying, “Are you serious right now?”

Subaru simply shrugs in response. Anastasia pinches her nose.

She then goes in for another bite.

“Yeah so, Rem helped me make mayo because we couldn’t find it anywhere here.”

“Wait so you’re telling me YOU invented a new condiment?!”

He lifted another spoonful. She stared at it. She then begrudgingly took another bite.

“Well technically I didn’t invent it. It came from my home and I just sort of copied it. Plus, even then, Rem did most of the work to figure out what ingredients were needed.”

“Why didn’t you tell me this before?!”

“It wasn’t something important to bring up!”

“I STRONGLY FEEL BEING AN INNOVATOR IS A WORTHWHILE THING TO BRING UP!”

“IT’S BEEN ONE DAY!”

SLAM! The waitress from before slammed a couple of plates on the counter while glaring at them with a smile that was slowly becoming more brittle.

Both of them sheepishly gave her a smile before getting back to the conversation.

“Okay this actually solves one of my issues,” Anastasia whispers.

Subaru raises the spoon once more before asking, “Was it what you were thinking about in the room?”

She mindlessly took a bite before continuing, “Yes. We need a product to sell consistently once we get to Kararagi. Something new to corner the market. That way we can get the attention of any investors and accelerate building a trading company.”

“Wow. You really have been planning stuff thoroughly. Have I ever mentioned how impressed I am by your diligence?

Another breakfast shipment on the Subaru express down Anastasia’s gullet.

“Nope, you really should sing my praises more often though.”

“Fantastic! Smartest gal of our generation! Breaking news: greediest merchant alive makes billions! Stay tuned for more!”

“Thank you, thank you, hold your applause,” she replied dryly.

They both stared at each other before breaking into snickering.

“Oh, going back to that mayo business, how much were you able to make from selling the recipe?”

Subaru froze.

“Because given how popular it became, I’m sure people were scrambling for a chance to distribute it. Depending on where you stored the coins, maybe we can find a way to sneak some out for a bit more extra savings or investment money.”

Subaru started sweating.

“Though given that your name was forgotten, it might be more trouble than its worth. Where did you keep your savings Subaru?”

“…”

“Subaru?”

“So, here’s the thing…”

 

…

 

“YOU DID WHAT?!!!”

Miles away in a certain mansion in the Miload territory, a certain pink-haired maid’s ears perked up.

“…Ram senses a disturbance.”

A confused and frankly disturbed grey-haired merchant sitting nearby replied, “What do you mean by that?”

“As if someone has completely validated Ram’s beliefs of certain people.”

Her eyes narrowed, “Which couldn’t be true because Ram’s beliefs are never wrong and Bottoto has no friends to validate his existence with.”

“Okay you didn’t need to tag that last part on! Also, Bottoto? You can’t just put a B in front of my name and call it a day!”

“Ram can, could, and would do as she pleases. Ram has done it before and will do it again.”

“Oh, like who?” Otto replied with an incredulous look.

Ram brought a finger up to retort, paused, and hesitated. “…Ram doesn’t know.”

The pink-haired maid feels like she has done such a naming scheme before but can’t recall. For some reason, it gives her a distasteful and frustrating feeling to not remember, but she doesn’t dwell on it.

“Anyway, know that your existence is suboptimal, and you should work on that,” she finished before walking away.

Otto simply sighed before adjusting his hat. “I really need better friends.”

He frowned, “Still, it was kind of weird of her to just straight up admit she doesn’t know something. I expected her to make up an example or something similar.”

He started contemplating if there was anyone she gave a similar nickname to before a migraine started to form.

“Ugh, maybe I should just get a drink. Ah, but I still need to order another earth dragon to replace Patrasche. I know she never liked living here but to run off and leave us at Priestella is too mean! Too much work and no play makes Otto a dull boy.”

Briefly wondering where he got that last phrase from, Otto suddenly froze.

“And I really need to stop talking to myself!”

Back to our intrepid two stars.

“So, you’re telling me. You were somehow able to recreate an invention from your home. Seemingly with incomplete background knowledge. And instead of using it to make a business or selling the idea to a company for profit. You gave out the recipe for free to anyone who asked! AND YOU THOUGHT THIS WAS A GOOD IDEA?!”

Anastasia was currently looming over Subaru, hands bone white from firmly grasping both his shoulders as she was giving him a death glare.

“…Yesssss?” Subaru replied with a sheepish grin while shrugging his shoulders.

“…”

“…”

“When we get to Kararagi. I am going to bash your brain with so much financial knowledge that you’ll be able to bargain with the Witch of Envy herself. And win. Understand me?”

He nodded rapidly in response.

Seconds passed in silence.

Anastasia then left her mouth open slightly ajar. Subaru then delicately shoved the last bits of Anastasia’s portion into her mouth.

“Good.”

“Excuse me,” both Subaru and Anastasia heard, laced with venom.

They both slowly swiveled their heads to see an absolutely volcanic waitress glaring down at both of them with little politeness remaining.

“Get the fuck out,” the waitress bluntly stated.

“…”

“You didn’t, uh, switch what you were thinking with what you intended to say?” Sheepishly asked by Subaru.

If looks could kill, then the glare she then levied solely at Subaru would have killed him twice as much as he had died in the last one and a half years.

“No. No I did not.”

Subaru finished up his portion of the meal quickly, which Anastasia noted he used the spoon he was feeding her with, and they got back onto the road towards Kararagi. Subaru and Anastasia both sat at the front, while Anastasia handled guiding the Earth dragons to their destination.

“…”

“So, as I was saying in the inn, we need to secure a product that we can reasonably use to enter the market. Not only that, but we also need to find a spirit.”

Subaru raised an eyebrow, “Why do we need a spirit?”

Anastasia hesitated before realizing that it would be better to come clean now before the worst case scenario happens, “…My gate is defective and if I’m not careful, I might start dying from mana poisoning.”

“Oh, same here!”

Anastasia’s jaw dropped, “And you didn’t think it was a good idea to bring this up earlier!”

“There wasn’t a good time! Again, ONE DAY! And don’t be hypocritical, you didn’t either.”

Anastasia rubbed her temples with one hand, “Fair point.”

I swear I’m going to ruin my throat just because of the little shit.

“So how did you break your gate?”

“I didn’t, I was born this way,” Anastasia stated.

“Wait, so how have you been able to delay mana poisoning all this time? Did you have a contract with a spirit before Priestella?”

“Mana poisoning wasn’t really an issue because my gate couldn’t really absorb mana in the first place. There was no mana to expel, besides what I innately had. And technically I did not have a contract with a spirit but a spirit did help me cast magic if I needed it. Unfortunately, because I was trying to survive near the end of the battle, I ended up needing mana in desperation. Thus, I accidentally ended up absorbing a ton of mana into my body near the end.”

“… And you lost your name before being able to expel it.”

“Yes. I also got knocked out and my spirit disappeared, leaving me desperate for the last two months to find a spirit to get this mana out before I end up exploding or slowly be poisoned.”

Subaru grimaced, “That must have been terrifying. I’m sorry you went through that.”

Him and his dumb empathy. He was dealing with the same situation ON TOP of getting tortured. Dumb boy and his dumb selflessness. He should be more worried about himself.

“Not like you aren’t going through the same thing. I’m guessing you damaged your gate until it became defective, which means you can still absorb but can’t expel.”

“Got it in one smart gal!” he said with a stupid finger gun pose and a wink.

In response, Anastasia puffed up and posed with her hands on her hips.

After settling her posture again, “So, if you don’t mind me asking, what led to your gate breaking?”

Subaru thought for a moment before, “Well apparently my gate was already underdeveloped when I came here. Then it got worse because I kept getting into situations, my fault included, where I had to use it. It then broke when I got in a fight with one of my sworn brothers.”

Anastasia just stared at him in disbelief before shaking her head, “Boys.”

At least Subaru looked sheepish, “To be fair, I was under a lot of pressure at the time.”

“Well either way, that means its even more important that we both get a spirit to drain our mana before we implode.”

“Agreed.”

They kept driving in silence for some time before Subaru broke it.

…

“So, what’s your favorite food?”

“Hm? What, you trying to butter up your employer with her favorites before starting your first day? Oh my! How daring~,” she teased.

“Gotta put in the leg work if I want to make a good first impression,” he joked back.

“Oh, I’ve hired a flatterer, how troublesome. But if you must know, my favorite food nowadays is daisukiyaki.”

“Daisukiyaki? OH! You mean okonomiyaki?”

“Oko what?”

“It’s a dish that was also popular from my home. I was actually surprised seeing it in Priestella with all the other camps.”

I almost forgot. Since he was a knight of Emilia, that means he must have been there when I introduced everyone to Kararagi cuisine in Priestella.

Anastasia began to frown before her eyes started to widen in realization.

Oh, how I hate gluttony. I can’t even remember if he enjoyed the dish. Wait, he said it was found in his hometown! Does that mean… either some people from where he originated, settled in Kararagi. Or maybe Hoshin himself came from the same place as Subaru! He did say he recognized the accent, so many possibilities!!

“Well, if you like okonomiyaki so much, you’ll love it with mayonnaise. Once we get to Kararagi you definitely have to try it together, people love it in Japan.”

“Hmm, maybe I will. Anyway, Subaru I have a question-“

“HURGHK!” Suddenly, Subaru convulsed in pain.

“Subaru?! What’s wrong?” She leaned toward him to see if he was okay.

Before she could get an answer, he suddenly pulled her towards him in an embrace. Her face began to blush.

Thunk! Thunk! Thunk!

She was about to berate him about boundaries until she realized what was now pinned to her carriage.

An arrow. And it was aimed directly at where her head was supposed to be.

“Anastasia, I think we’re under attack.”

Notes:

Subaru: I think we’re under attack.
Anastasia: Oh wow I didn’t notice thanks for pointing that out~!
Subaru: Is this really the time for sarcasm?!
Anastasia: IT COMES OUT WHEN IM SCARED OKAY!!
Subaru:…
Anastasia:…
Subaru: pffffftttt
Anastasia: I hate you so much

Chapter 3: Ambush

Summary:

Subaru and Anastasia are under attack, but what else is lurking in the shadows…

Notes:

Here’s an early chapter present, don’t worry, weekly chapters are still happening, so there will be another chapter next week.

Enjoy ~ :D

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Anastasia Hoshin is really starting to hate her luck right now. It’s only been approximately one day since she left the royal capital and she is now currently under assault by armed bandits.

Thankfully Subaru has supernatural reflexes and timing, otherwise my head would have become a pincushion.

Unfortunately, the same couldn’t be said about their earth dragons. Two nicely placed shots were put into each dragon’s skull, effectively stranding them in the forest. They were currently surrounded at all sides by around seven bandits, with possibly more hiding within the forest nearby.

Tsk. The odds are against us. We couldn’t secure weapons before leaving the capital. The only thing I have is an emergency knife in my bag. Regardless of our armaments, Subaru still looks too weak to fight, he’s barely had any time to recover. We need to get out of here no matter what.

A skinny, ugly bandit armed with a whip began moving closer to the carriage.

“Hello, hello! Good morning to you! Now I’m sure you’re in quite a hurry to get to wherever you’re trying to go. Time is money and all that.”

He grinned a toothy smile, despite missing several teeth.

“So, let’s get this over with and without any fighting. We’re proper folk, despite what you might be thinking, and we don’t want any unintentional blood on our hands. So let me lay out what’s going to happen: you’re going to give me half of whatever is in that carriage of yours and all the coins you have on you. Then we’ll let you go free of charge.”

Free of charge my ass, they’re basically going to take everything we have. Hmm, no use trying to be aggressive. Maybe we can bargain with them? Worst case scenario, hide some coins and see if they don’t notice-

“Free of charge my ass! No way we’re giving you anything!” Subaru exclaimed.

Anastasia’s jaw dropped in shock.

What is he thinking! Is he trying to get us killed?!

“Oh ho ho! We got a mouthy one with us this time boys. Now what do we do with a mouthy type?”

Fwoosh. Thunk.

“ARGH!” An arrow flew into Subaru’s shoulder.

“And it is super effective! Now be careful. That’s just a warning shot,” the bandit proclaimed.

“No!” Anastasia exclaimed before huddling around Subaru.

With her back towards the bandits, Anastasia whispered, “What do you think you’re doing?! Stay quiet and let me handle this.”

“No,” Anastasia flinched at the pure venom laced in his voice, “No matter what we try, it won’t end at just them taking our shit.”

“How do you even know that will happen?! We should try to negotiate a bit at first. At least buy some time.”

Subaru shook his head, “It’s a waste of time. Besides, I already have a plan.”

Anastasia stared at him in disbelief, “But-“

“Anastasia, please trust me,” he gave her a cocky grin while looking her straight in the eyes, “I promise, I’ll keep you safe.”

Anastasia gulped, despite how worried she was, she felt reassured by his determined gaze.

“… Alright. Alright, I’ll trust you!”

“Has the young couple finished? Or do you guys need another reminder?” the bandit said in a bored tone.

Subaru rose to his feet and jumped onto the ground facing the bandits. There were three bandits on his left and two on his right. Two bandits in front, one held a bow and arrow that shot at Subaru and the other seemed to be the spokesperson of the group.

I don’t like this. I don’t like this at all! Wait, what is he doing?

Subaru grabbed at the shaft of the arrow, twisted, and yanked it and the head out of his shoulder.

Oh my Od!

“What the fuck!? Are you stupid?! Have you never had an arrow in you? You just made everything so much worse,” the bandit exclaimed in shock.

“Ugh…” Subaru weakly cried.

“Jeez, the guy is either brainless or broken in the head,” the bandit shook his head, “Either way, are you going to surrender or are we going to do this the hard way?”

“…Neither.” Subaru lifted the arrow in the air and all of the bandits tensed up, ready to fight.

However, the tension turned to confusion as he then started to use the arrow to stab himself in the legs, arms, and body. Like a madman, he vigorously butchered not only his body but especially one of his hands.

What is he doing?! Is he trying to kill himself? Is he trying to make them think he is a psycho? Oh, I’m going to be sick.

“Okay I guess he is actually broken in the head. Damn, this is just plain sad. Alright, what do you guys think we should do with him?” The bandit looked at his fellow brothers but was met with an alarming sight.

Nearly all of them were writhing in pain on the ground, with holes suddenly appearing on their bodies. The bandit holding the bow dropped it and he could clearly see the guy’s right hand completely covered in wounds.

“What the fuck-“The bandit barely finished as he got the wind knocked out of him by being tackled by Subaru.

“Oi get the fuck off-OW!”

Subaru sat on top of the bandit, landing blow after blow on the guy’s face, as he broke his nose. Before he could do any more damage, the bandit managed to throw Subaru off of him before quickly getting back on his feet.

“You bwoke my nose, you asshole! I’m going to fucking kill you!” The bandit quickly reached for his whip but grasped at nothing.

“Huh?”

CRACK!

He was then met with a sudden crack, before feeling a laceration on his shoulder, knocking him on to his back again. Lifting his head up, he managed to see Subaru using his whip to knock out a bandit on his right before the man was able to recover.

How in the hell was Subaru able to do all that?

Anastasia was in absolute shock throughout the whole, barely more than a minute, battle. Her eyes narrowed on Subaru.

The wound on his shoulder. It’s gone. So are all the other wounds he made, even his hand is completely normal.

She looked at the bandit that shot Subaru originally.

His right hand is all bloody and mangled. It almost looks like what Subaru did to his own. Could it be?

She quickly shook her head.

Shit. This isn’t the time for speculation.

She brought her gaze back to the battlefield and noticed the mangled bandit getting up to grab his bow.

“Subaru! On your left, bandit with a bow!”

Subaru quickly spun to face the aforementioned bandit but was too late to react as he was able to shoot off a volley of arrows before Subaru’s whip knocked him unconscious.

Two of the arrows missed but the third hit its target: right in Subaru’s throat. Subaru, winded, was brought to his knees while grasping at the arrow shaft lodged in his neck.

No! Please don’t die, please don’t die! Oh-

“Subaru, BEHIND YOU!”

A bigger, brawnier bandit managed to sneak up behind Subaru as he was dealing with the bow bandit. As the bandit raised his sword to cut Subaru in half, Subaru yanked the arrow out of his throat, blood gushing out of his neck.

Not even a second later, the brawny bandit dropped his sword behind him, instead using both hands to try to stop the suddenly new gush of blood coming from the hole in his neck.

“You fucking bastard! El Hu-“

The spokesperson bandit managed to pick himself back up, trying to focus mana to form a spell, before Subaru tripped him on his back again, using his whip to pull the guy’s right foot forward.

“Damnit, stop knocking me over!”

The brawny bandit dropped to his knees, still ineffectually trying to stop the bleeding.

Subaru quickly lodged the arrow in his hand into the bandit’s eye, before picking up the dropped short sword.

With whip and sword in hand, he faced the three still conscious and now recovered bandits.

All three rushed but before they could reach him, he stabbed himself quickly in both legs and then slit his throat. All three wounds transferred separately, one for each bandit.

The one with the slit throat, collapsed from sudden bleeding and pain. The two with leg injuries were brought to their knees.

CRACK.

With one swift motion, Subaru used his whip to swipe at one of the bandits’ heads, knocking him out. He then rushed and used the short sword to pierce the remaining bandit’s chest before knocking him forward, dead.

“That’s enough! El huma!” The loudmouthed bandit was able to finally get back up and launch a spell at Subaru, shooting a spear of ice directly at Subaru’s chest.

Thunk!

Direct hit, it pierced his heart.

“Haha! Take that you bastard… Oh wait, shit!”

Subaru quickly tore the spear out and immediately, the loudmouth’s chest and heart burst.

“You… fucking… monster,” the bandit weakly cried before tumbling face first onto the ground.

Gasping, Subaru took a moment to catch this breath.

“…Dumbass.” Subaru slowly turned to see if Anastasia was okay before he was accosted by a speeding purple haired missile.

“AH!” Was all he screamed before being knocked onto the ground.

“…” Anastasia was silent, desperately grabbing Subaru and checking his whole body.

“Uh Anastasia?” As Anastasia was manhandling him, he started getting more and more flustered.

After confirming that there were no important wounds to worry over, she let out a deep breath she was holding in the entire time. She then looked into Subaru’s eyes and gave him a death glare.

“What is wrong with you!? Are you insane?!”

“Uh-“

“No, of course you’re insane, no sane man fights like that. Stabbing and giving himself fatal wounds just to transfer it to someone else. Some kind of suicidal, self-harming martial art! Why didn’t you at least let me try to negotiate with them? You could have at least had a better advantage without having to almost kill yourself four FUCKING times. Oh my Od, what is wrong with you?!”

“Well-“

“Why didn’t you tell me you had some insane power like that,” before he could retort, she pointed at him, “Don’t you dare say it’s only been ONE DAY! Here’s what we’re going to do: we’re going to tie the rest up, loot whatever we can, and maybe interrogate them a bit before leaving. Then, until we get to Kararagi, you’re going to tell me everything about you! Every. Single. Thing. NO MORE SURPRISES THAT WILL GIVE ME A HEART ATTACK!”

“…”

“…”

He slowly nodded and said, “Okay.”

Anastasia quickly wrapped her arms around him into an embrace, shocking him.

Sniff. Sob.

“You are such a stupid, stupid boy. Thank you.”

Subaru’s jaw dropped.

Tears dotting her eyes, she said, “You saved me. Despite everything I said, you can’t even begin to imagine how grateful I am that you did all that to protect me. I just hate that you basically put yourself at death’s door every time you did so.”

She looked Subaru fiercely in the eyes while grabbing his face, “We’re also going to talk extensively about alternative ways of fighting. I don’t care if your way is effective or not! I’m not going to stand here and watch you butcher yourself just to protect us. No buts! This is non-negotiable, at the very least, you will prioritize alternative strategies other than harming yourself. Am I clear?”

“…Yes, ma’am.”

“Good, now let’s tie the rest of these bastards up. Let’s see if there is any more of them we have to deal with.”

After rummaging through some of the corpses, Anastasia took some rope from her carriage and tied the three unconscious bandits together.

Winding up a kick, she aimed low, intending to wake the bow bandit out of Subaru-induced slumber.

“WAKE UP!” she yelled as she kicked him right in the groin.

“AUGH!!”

“Ooo, yeesh! You really don’t play around Ana.”

“It’s the least they deserve. And you don’t get to talk Mr. ‘stabs his own throat to fight.’”

“Oh Od!” The bandit was writhing in pain, “Why the fuck did you do that?”

“Consider it repayment for trying to rob and kill us. Now answer my question: are there more of you?”

“Go fuck yourself.”

“Wrong answer.”

And she kicked him the groin. Again.

“AUGH! Why? Why in the dick?!”

“Answer my questions and we don’t have to figure out how many kicks it takes to crack a bandit.”

“…We got a whole camp of us ready to tear you guys a new asshole.”

“Where is this camp?”

“Wouldn’t you like to know?”

She winded up her foot again for another pain train to bandit dick-ville.

“Wait wait wait wait stop! Jeez, girl learn to take a joke.”

“Where. Is. It?”

“Close by, in fact, so close that hypothetically, if we had a scout watching us in case we got into a whole heap a trouble, it would take barely any time for them to run over and get some backup.”

STOMP, STOMP, STOMP!

Suddenly, large footsteps alongside loud rustling of leaves were heard coming from the forest.

“And guess how much time I’ve been wasting?! YOU BOTH ARE SO FUCKED NOW!”

Subaru readied his whip while Anastasia readied the knife she grabbed from her bag.

However, whatever they were expecting, it wasn’t one manic bandit screaming at the top of his lungs.

“SHIT! SHIT! SHIT! GUYS WE NEED TO GET THE FUCK OUT OF HERE EVERYONE-“

That’s all the new bandit said before he was suddenly tackled by a large black earth dragon that was barreling towards him from behind.

The bandit went soaring into the distance, bouncing twice, before landing on his face.

Collectively, everyone’s jaw dropped at the sheer insanity of the situation just as the black dragon roared in the air in triumph.

“Patrasche!?” Subaru exclaimed as he was able to recognize the black dragon.

He knows the dragon’s name?!

Patrasche lowered her gaze to the new humans and subsequently found herself entranced. Cautiously, she slowly made her way to the scary-eyed human and started to look over him extensively. Trying to see why this particular human has such a magnificent aura.

Circling the interesting human, Patrasche searched through her memory banks but couldn’t quite remember him, though he seemed to recognize her.

Suddenly, she stopped in front of him, pausing in contemplation.
