Regardless of her lack of recognition, she could sense a sort of affinity to him that she can’t quite articulate. As a result, she decreed that the human shall be bestowed the right to prove his worth. In celebration, he shall be given a gift.

Patrasche began licking his face.

“Haha, oh jeez, girl, it’s good to see you too! I didn’t think you would recognize me but maybe gluttony doesn’t work on animals. Or maybe you and I were always meant to be. Either way, I am not complaining.”

Anastasia stood there baffled, staring awkwardly at Subaru somehow being able to tame a random dragon who he just so happened to recognize.

“So, you going to introduce her to me or not?”

“Hm? Oh, sorry Anastasia. This is Patrasche! She and I go way back. Got her from Crusch when we fought the white whale together and we have been thick as thieves ever since.”

Wait, he was involved in the White Whale hunt! How involved was he in the royal selection? Ugh, every second with Subaru feels like a brand-new mystery, danger at every turn, or complete bafflement of his personality. Sometimes all three at once.

Anastasia began to walk closer to Subaru and Patrasche. Just now noticing the human girl, Patrasche glares at the frilly purple thing and hisses.

Anastasia, at first confused by the reaction, instinctively glares back. For a second, it’s as if lightning sparked between them.

A silent conversation played between them.

Patrasche’s glare deepens at Anastasia. Back off, I have decreed this human as mine. Get your own.

Anastasia’s eyes dart to Subaru and back. Oh please. This ain’t a competition. And even if it was, you can have him.

Patrasche rolls her eyes. You say that but I can see you throwing glances at him as if you want him as a mate.

Anastasia blushes. It’s nothing like that!

Patrasche snorts. Well, if it is or isn’t, he can certainly do better.

Anastasia’s eyes narrowed. Oh, you bitch.

Subaru, who was on the sideline watching this all go down, was thoroughly confused.

“Sooo, are we going to see where Patrasche came from?”

Anastasia blinked and turned her head to Subaru, while simultaneously realizing what she was just doing.

Oh my Od, I’m going insane. It’s only been one day and the boy has already driven me to start nonsensical, in my head, conversations with an earth dragon. In two months, I’ll probably be talking to the dead.

“Yes, but first we should tie up that bandit Patrasche sent flying, see what he was trying to warn everyone about.”

After bringing the new guy into the clump of tied up bandits, they were able to surmise that there was a sudden attack on the bandit camp just a few minutes ago. Apparently, the scout was watching the fight between Subaru and the bandits stationed on the road, and thought to go report to the main camp. However, just as he arrived, explosions and magic rained down on everyone. Seems Patrasche, who was wandering around aimlessly, was captured just a few days previously and was subsequently released during the onslaught.

To Anastasia, it all felt too coincidental and too much good luck at once for it to feel like a random event.

Could someone be following us? For that matter, how could it be that a dragon that has a connection to Subaru just so happened to be here and just so happened to be reunited with us just as we lost our other earth dragons? I don’t like this. Either way, our next plan of action is clear.

“We need to leave. Now.”

Subaru was confused, “Wait, shouldn’t we see what happened to the rest of the bandits?”

Anastasia shook her head, “There are too many variables. We have an unknown entity who was able to wipe out an entire bandit camp singlehandedly. Either they are a monster who just so happened to stumble upon the camp or a powerful individual who may or may not have bad intentions to us. It’s too risky. We should cut our losses and just keep moving.”

Anastasia looked towards the four bandits, “Now what to do about them.”

Subaru looked pensive.

Unfortunately, we might have to kill them. We can’t leave a trail where they could be found by knights which will lead them right to us. We can’t take them with us either, it’s still too far from Kararagi. The only problem is, I wonder if Subaru would be okay with that. Killing in self-defense is one thing. Execution is another.

“…We should kill them,” Subaru stated firmly.

Anastasia blinked, surprised and a little curious, “I was thinking the same, but could you tell me your reasons?”

Subaru looked at her and smiled grimly, ”Sure but only if you told me yours as well.”

Anastasia huffed as if that was a foregone conclusion.

“My reasons were that we can’t leave a trail for the knights to follow us. Plus, we can’t take them with us as Kararagi is still too far and we will have to feed them,” Anastasia summarized.

Subaru nodded at her explanation, “I had similar thoughts, but I had two more reasons. One: they are still bandits and letting them go means putting others at risk of getting robbed in the future.”

Subaru contemplated for a second, before he looked back towards the bandits with a steel gaze, “And two: if we were captured by them, they would have done far worse to us than just kill. This is frankly a mercy.”

For a second, Anastasia could feel as if Subaru had an even deeper reason for it, but she refrained from asking. There are just some things you shouldn’t prod, at least not until they were closer.

“Alright then, so we agree, I’ll take two and you take two.”

Subaru blinked, “Woah, what do you mean? You’re not going to do any killing.”

She rolled her eyes in response, “Don’t be absurd. Remember what I said: this is an equal partnership. That means we share all burdens, including situations like this.”

He shook his head and pointed at her, “You’re the one who talks to people while I protect you. It’s my job to take care of stuff like this.”

Anastasia gazed into his eyes and stepped closely to him. “You say that, but I can tell you really don’t want to kill them.”

Subaru winced before looking down. “…”

She placed her hand on his heart, “The way it took you a second before you were able to follow through, mentioning they need to die. How you hesitated before confirming your last reason. Deep down, your heart doesn’t want to take a life so easily.”

“…I’m sorry, you must think I’m weak-willed,” he whispered as he gazed back into her eyes.

Anastasia’s eyes softened and she gave a faint smile, “It’s not a bad thing. Frankly, I think it’s wonderful how despite all you went through, you still have compassion in you. Even if these guys don’t deserve it.”

She continued, “I don’t want that compassion to die within you Subaru. Having an honest and just heart is needed in this world, more than ever. But given where we’re going, we’ll have to make more decisions like this, and I will not let you face such situations alone,” she put both of Subaru’s hands in her own, “We’re in this together, thick as thieves as you say.”

Subaru snickered, “… Thank you.”

I should be thanking you. Saved my life twice and was willing to make a hard choice on my behalf. My debt keeps rising. This is the least I could do to repay it.

They turned towards the four bandits and both started marching towards them, hand in hand.

“Oh! Has the lovely couple finally finished flirting? Please, get a room, there is only so much mushy gushy lovey nonsense I can take,” the bow bandit joked with a grimace.

“…” They kept marching in silence as Anastasia brandished a knife while Subaru a short sword.

“Oi! What’s with the silent treatment?” The bandit began to get nervous.

Four.

“H-hey, what the fu-“ his words were cut off in the same instance as his head.

Three.

“OH SHIT! They killed him!” The scout hypocritically screamed.

Anastasia dug her knife into another bandit’s throat before quickly taking it out.

Two.

“W-we told you what you wanted! Come on man, let us go. We won’t rob anymore. Honest!” The scout kept trying to bargain.

“…I’m sorry,” said Subaru as he cut the head off one more bandit.

One.

“Monsters! BOTH OF YOU ARE MONSTERS!” Screamed the scout.

“Yeah, we are. Wonder what that makes you?” Anastasia coldly replied before finally ending the scout’s life.

For a second, they both just stood there, before Anastasia gently took Subaru’s hand and guided them back to the carriage. Patrasche followed silently behind and allowed them to tie her to the reins of the carriage.

Anastasia took the reins in one hand still holding onto Subaru’s in the other. She squeezed his hand as they both looked at each other with somber smiles. With a quick flick of the wrist, they set off down the road.

Meanwhile, as the two stars began their journey once more, two pairs of eyes were watching them silently from the forest.

“…Are you sure this was a wise decision?”

“…”

“You are only delaying the inevitable. The more you wait, the less chances you will get. In time, you will come to regret your hesitation.”

“…”

One of the eyes sighed before both disappeared once more, following the two bright stars on the horizon.

Notes:

EN: Anastasia: we ride together, we die together, we bury bodies together.

Patrasche: I’ve only had Subaru for 2 seconds, but if anything were to happen to him, I’ll kill everyone in this country and then myself.

Bandit: *explodes Subaru’s head*
Subaru: no u
Bandit: wait wat *fucking explodes*

Chapter 4: Questions, Answers, and More Questions

Summary:

Subaru and Anastasia have a Q&A session. Things get a bit heated…

Notes:

Over 500 kudos and over 90 bookmarks. Over 7000 hits and nearly 150 unique comments (not counting mine). In just three chapters. In just 9 days. Once again, thank you all for the love and support. I enjoy reading all comments, whether they are simply just saying peak, discussing discrepancies in my writing, or gushing at certain moments. You all are truly wonderful and motivate me to make my stories better and better. Hope you enjoy this chapter.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

 

As the two stars traveled to the land of wealth and opportunity, Subaru made due on his promise to Anastasia and both made it a priority to discuss everything they could think of, within reason, during the journey.

 

Day 1

 

They were currently traveling to the nearest inn, hopefully to wash the blood and dirt off their clothes from the recent bandit assault.

 

“Okay, so what do you want to know?” Subaru asked.

 

“Too much for just one day. But what I want to focus on the most is that special power of yours,” she noticed Subaru slightly flinched and quickly added, “what you accomplished as a knight, and details about your home.”

 

Subaru looked visibly tense.

 

Baby steps, I’d rather he not close himself off by pushing him before he is comfortable. I’ll work my way up to how in the world he can just heal himself without mana.

 

“However, since it’s the first day, let’s start off small and leave the important stuff for later.”

 

Subaru now looked relieved, “Alright that sounds good to me. Then what do you want to know first?”

 

“Hmmm. How about what brought you to Lugunica?”

 

“Oh that’s easy. One day I was buying some snacks from a convenience store and I was making my way back home.”

 

Note to self: what is a convenience store and what kind of snacks can we copy?

 

“…Then I blinked and I ended up in the middle of the royal capital.”

 

 

 

 

What?

 

What? “What?”

 

And thus began a series of conversations that consistently baffled, intrigued, and frustrated Anastasia for twelve straight days. Of course not all of the conversations evoked the same feeling.

 

 

 

“You almost died to the Bowel Hunter?!”

 

Day 2

 

Some conversations were enlightening:

 

Now, much cleaner and in a better headspace, Anastasia had some questions at breakfast.

 

“So you were at the subjugation of the White Whale, fought Sloth, killed the White Rabbit horde, and you were at Priestella? Am I missing anything else?”

 

Subaru was eating an omelette, with ham and peppirs, while Anastasia ate toast with butter and fruit jam.

 

“No that’s about it.”

 

“And you arrived a month before the White Whale subjugation?”

 

Subaru lathered mayo onto his pound of eggs. Anastasia did the same. For her toast, butter, and fruit jam. Subaru did not question it.

 

“Yep.”

 

“…and your occupation before coming here was?”

 

“A shut in.”

 

“…”

 

“…”

 

“No.”

 

“What do you mean no?”

 

“I mean how is it possible, that a person who spent all his time indoors-“

 

“It was only really a few months.”

 

“And had no understanding of our written language despite being able to understand every person verbally-“

 

“Yeah I still don’t understand how that works.”

 

“Could come in and literally spearhead some of the greatest achievements Lugunica has witnessed in nearly decades and act like that’s no big deal?!”

 

“Woah woah woah! Spearhead? I didn’t say that! Technically, I didn’t do much compared to the others. Everyone else did the grunt work.”

 

During the whole tirade, Subaru was sneaking eggs and mayo onto Anastasia’s plate.

 

She looked down at her plate and back up at him.

 

Anastasia simply pinched her nose and glared before continuing.

 

“Subaru, despite your failed attempts to downplay it, I can read between the lines. Emilia was not involved in the subjugation of the whale. At all. From my memory: Crusch and I negotiated a deal to hunt the white whale together. Then, we figured out Sloth was targeting Emilia after rescuing Suwen from some cultists.”

 

Anastasia then pointed at Subaru.

 

“But from what your recollection shows: you were part of both. And given that neither Crusch nor I had any reason to involve Emilia, that I know of, the only reason you would have been involved was if you played a major part. See where I’m going with this?”

 

He grimaced but motioned for her to continue.

 

“You are not that physically strong. I doubt your power would be useful against the white whale. Crusch and I barely knew you before this. However, given what I saw when you were fighting, you move and act with tactics rather than instinct. Stealing a familiar weapon, disarming the only long range enemy first, and leveraging one on one fights at all times. That’s what someone who thinks on a macroscale does. So, the only reason I could think for you to be involved is that you were integral to planning the subjugation. It’s highly likely that you somehow were involved in coordinating us and could have spearheaded the whole Sloth operation, considering it was your candidate who was in trouble. Perhaps you even united us in the first place.”

 

“That’s a lot of theoretical conjecture.

 

“But am I wrong at all!?”

 

“…Technically, Crusch still led the battle of the White Whale. And Crusch was still going to hunt the whale, I just took advantage of the fact that she wanted to hunt it in the first place.”

 

“And thus my point still stands. And if you were important for that mission, there’s a strong chance you were for the others.”

 

In fact, I’m starting to recontextualize Priestella. I know Reinhard saved Emilia, and together they defeated Greed. But would her knight so easily defer to another camp for help to save their candidate? Without Subaru himself? Unlikely.

 

“Hey! You don’t know, maybe someone else from my camp stepped up.”

 

“Highly unlikely.” Before he could retort, she raised a hand and continued.

 

“Don’t get me wrong. Nothing against the Emilia camp, but not a single one of them was known for their strategic brilliance.”

 

“I mean we had Otto.”

 

“Suwen has the tactical foresight of a bundle of sticks. A skilled diplomat and orator he may be, a strategist he is not. He bought oil when the cost peaked, putting him in debt.”

 

“Okay-“

 

“Right before their selling price dramatically dropped.”

 

“Well that’s just bad luck-“

 

“Right after Gusteko closed their borders from Lugunica. Which was easily predicted by anyone who looked into the political situation of Gusteko even a little bit.”

 

“…”

 

“…”

 

“Yeah I got nothing.”

 

Anastasia waved her hand, “He could have rectified his mistake, by ripping off someone else, but that would mean throwing them under the wagon instead of him. Suwen just isn’t ruthless enough.”

 

As she finished, she noticed something. What was that?

 

However, Subaru was stubborn.

 

“Okay then what about Ros-chi? He’s the head court mage which means he’s pretty smart.”

 

Anastasia just rolled her eyes, “Smart at magic, not tactics. Remember Sloth? Why would a noble housing a Dragon Candidate, who had been a known active target of the witch cult, not hire a militia, more bodyguards, or more staff to defend their manor? And why leave her unattended right when she is announced to the public? Is he trying to get her killed?!”

 

She saw it clearly this time. His eyebrow twitched.

 

A weakness in the Emilia camp? Coincidence or not, better to capitalize on potential info. Let’s try something.

“I-“

“Actually you know what? Let’s go down the whole list that I know: Garfiel Tinsel. From what I can summarize from Mimi, without the rose colored glasses, ‘he is super strong and super good at fighting.’ But when it comes to general strategy, he doesn’t think beyond the current fight. More likely to rush in without thinking, consequences be damned.”

 

That’s how the bastard got Mimi injured. Wait! There it is again.

 

“Garfiel isn’t that bad-“

 

“Ram, Frederica, and Petra are all maids. From what I can tell, they all got a good head on their shoulders. However, in order: Ram is lazy, Frederica defers to her master too often, and Petra is a child.”

 

It only twitched when I talked about Ram. Four times is no coincidence, especially when he didn’t react to the other two maids. Is it related to his camp rejecting him?

 

“How do you even know this?” Subaru asked in disbelief of how much information she knows about their camp.

 

“Spy network, social gossip of maids and nobles, and I have eyes and common sense,” Anastasia said as she counted down on her fingers.

 

By this point Subaru had all but conceded, however, Anastasia had one last point to hammer in.

 

Alright, one last test. If I’m right, convincing him to abandon his camp may be easier than I thought.

 

“And finally: Emilia is Emilia.”

 

He waited for her to elaborate.

 

 

 

She did not.

 

“That’s unfair!”

 

“Is it? Is it really? You were her knight and even you have to admit that she is more of a powerhouse physically and magically than mentally.”

 

Subaru huffed but didn’t disagree.

 

No twitch that time. What is causing that reaction? I need more info. It’s weird how he is still so defensive of his camp, considering how obstinate he was against rejoining them before.

 

“So was there a point to this or was this just you venting about how stupid my camp is?”

 

Anastasia laughed, “Well besides proving what was already well known. Yes, I have a serious point.”

 

She then pointed at Subaru and said, “Stop acting like you're not important.”

 

Subaru was now visibly confused, “What?”

 

“It’s one thing to downplay your own worth to put your opponents off guard: that’s called strategy. It’s another thing to put yourself down because you don’t think you're important enough to be cared about: that’s called low self-esteem.”

 

Now it was Subaru’s turn to be baffled speechless.

 

At this point, Anastasia’s tone became softer, “Listen, I don’t know what made you so insistent about your own worth, but I’m not going to let you keep putting yourself down for no reason.”

 

Even the most humble people would have some confidence in their accomplishments, but he has none. It paints an ugly picture if possibly one of the most skilled people in your camp feels like they are useless.

 

“…Why do you even care?”

 

“Why wouldn’t I? We’re fr-,” Anastasia choked, ”Uh, I mean, business partners. I won’t profit from someone who isn’t motivated to prove their worth.”

 

What actually are we anyway? Temporary partners in crime? Temporary candidate and knight? Temporary friends/allies? I mean we kind of are friends. Though given how little we knew each other before, maybe not. Why was that so hard to say though?

 

Subaru frowned,“…”

 

Well that didn’t work. Hm, logical arguments don’t convince Subaru consistently, though previous history shows that appeals to emotion do. I’ll have to coax him in other ways.

 

Anastasia sighed.

 

Either way, it doesn’t matter. I don’t want him throwing his life away at the drop of a hat just because he thinks he isn’t important. It won’t help me, him, or anyone.

 

“Just, give it some thought. Please.”

 

“…Alright.”

 

Day 4

 

Some conversations were captivating:

 

“So these kaars, they did not need earth dragons?”

 

They were currently resting outside an inn talking about some amazing inventions of Subaru’s home. Anastasia was sitting on a rock, hands on her chin, watching Subaru tend to Patrasche.

 

“Nope! Cars used these engines which converted a liquid called gasoline into energy to push the machine forward.”

 

Subaru was currently brushing Patrasche’s scales, which the scaly queen appreciated immensely.

 

“Kyaaahh!” Patrasche screeched in indignation.

 

“Oh but no car could replace you Patrasche!” Subaru comforted the earth dragon and patted her on the head.

 

“Hmmm. You think we can make these?” Anastasia questioned. Subaru paused in contemplation.

 

Patrasche glared at Anastasia for interrupting the queen and her chosen human’s bonding time.

 

“Ehhh, probably not unless we have some factories and certain machines. Plus, despite my knowledge of them, making them is a whole other boat.”

 

Anastasia simply stuck her tongue out at Patrasche, before continuing with more queries.

 

“‘Whole other boat’, is that some kind of turn of phrase?” What about those machines, can we at least make those?”

 

Patrasche purred and nudged Subaru to continue brushing. Subaru obliged.

 

“Yes. And no, I can’t create those machines either easily.”

 

Anastasia rolled her eyes, “So what can you make?”

 

“Off the top of my head, with some trial and error, I could make tartar sauce and a lighter.”

 

Anastasia nodded.

 

“Let me guess: one is similar to mayonnaise while the other is… similar to kaars?

 

“Bingo! Well kind of, tartar sauce uses mayo as a base and is mixed with diced pickles and lemon juice. While a lighter is a small mechanical device that creates a small flame.”

 

Reminder to myself. Is bee-ngo a turn of phrase too or another Subaruism like that dumb pose he does? Anyway.

 

“Oh ho ho! Now, that we can work with! How soon do you think we can make a working model of those?”

 

Anastasia was vibrating with excitement.

 

“Hmm? I’d say tartar sauce would be easily within a week, if we can find pickles or lemons here. The lighter will take some work. Maybe one month or two.”

 

“Let’s focus on food then and work on other products in the background. Could you describe what pickles and lemons are?”

 

“Well lemons are these sour yellow fruits while pickles are green cylindrical vegetables that are fermented.”

 

“Oh so basically lemoms and icker umbers.”

 

Subaru paused before facepalming.

 

“…”

 

“…”

 

“I hate this world so much sometimes.”

 

“Well-“

 

He threw his hands in the air, “HALF OF THESE NAMES SOUND LIKE SOMEONE WAS HAVING A STROKE!”

 

 

Day 7

 

Some conversations were unnerving:

 

“A whole tub.”

 

“Yes.” Subaru said, his face in his hands.

 

“…How though?”

 

They were currently at a restaurant in a small town halfway to Priestella. Subaru was having a sandwich made with fowl meat and tometos. Anastasia was eating a salad with bovine meat and greens. Both dishes had ludicrous amounts of mayo, to the displeasure of the restaurant staff.

 

“Rem does as she pleases. She did 99% of the cleaning and cooking for an entire mansion. She fought and killed tens of mabeasts without breaking a sweat. Sometimes I woke up to her staring at me. I don’t even think she slept a full 6 hours. Ever.”

 

She portioned some salad and placed it on Subaru’s plate before she replied.

 

“Alright, we are going to uncover that cave of mabeasts later. So, did you do anything with the tub?

 

Subaru mindlessly ate the new addition of salad while handing half of his sandwich to her.

 

“I don’t know, didn’t check, and didn’t want to ask. For all I know, it’s still there.”

 

“…”

 

“…”

 

“Your camp is insane.”

 

“Eh we have Otto.”

 

“That is still a terrible standard to compare to!”

 

Day 9

 

Some conversations were hard to understand:

 

“So purple hair isn’t normal where you come from?”

 

“Not really, well naturally at least. It’s usually black, blonde, or brown. I’ve really only seen multicolored hair like here in anime.”

 

“What’s ann-ee-may?”

 

“Oh boy.”

 

After a couple of hours of explanation and Q&A at a tavern.

 

“Let’s talk about how teevees work later. How do they make money off anime? Not like showing them to people prints money. Wait, does it?”

 

The bartender handed a handle of lager to Anastasia and some fruit juice for Subaru.

 

“Physically no, metaphorically yes. And regarding how: well there’s advertisements, investments, and merch,” Subaru listed off.

 

“The first two make sense but what’s merch? Do you mean merchandise? If so, what kind?”

 

Subaru winced, “Yes, it’s short for that. And for what it is, well you know, like art of your favorite character or special edition boxes...”

 

The bartender returned, with various dried meats, snacks, and fried fowl meat before running back.

 

Anastasia says they are essential for drinking liquor. Subaru did not question it.

 

The bartender came back with two large bowls of mayo, before running into the kitchen again.

 

Anastasia narrowed her eyes, “You're hiding something.”

 

Subaru flinched, “No I’m not!”

 

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “Dangerous, personal, or uncomfortable?”

 

They settled on using three different qualifiers if they did not want to discuss a certain topic.

 

“Okay it’s more embarrassing than anything.”

 

“Then say it or give me a reason we shouldn’t talk about it.”

 

Subaru was visibly sweating.

 

“It’s not really that important…”

 

“Can we do something similar here?”

 

“…Yes.”

 

“Subaru!”

 

“No! Let’s talk about something else.”

 

The bartender returned, again. With another bowl of mayo. He saw one of the mayo bowls was already empty. He shuddered before shuffling away.

 

Anastasia glared before closing her eyes and acquiescing, “Fine.”

 

Subaru sighed in relief.

 

“Then explain to me what a loli is. I’ve heard lolicon before in Kararagi but never just the first part.”

 

Given Hoshin coined the term, this gives me more evidence that Hoshin is somehow related to Subaru in some way.

 

“…”

 

“Subaru?”

 

Anastasia opened her eyes and looked over at Subaru.

 

He was visibly sweating again.

 

 

Day 10

 

Some conversations needed some tact:

 

It was morning. Anastasia was currently pouting on the edge of the bed.

 

“…”

 

“…”

 

“Are you still angry?”

 

“No,” Anastasia lied.

 

“…”

 

“…Is it because I called you a loli before?”

 

Anastasia has a surprisingly good memory. So, she connected the dots when Subaru explained what a “loli” actually means.

 

Anastasia just puffed her cheeks in resentment.

 

“…”

 

Subaru sighed.

 

He relented, “…Alright. I’ll explain how we can make money off of anime.”

 

Anastasia immediately grabbed both of Subaru’s hands and started shaking them in exaggerated excitement.

 

“Pleasure doing business with you Subaru-kun~!”

 

Sucker.

 

“I’m going to regret this aren’t I…”

 

Later, during the same day:

 

They were outside a town, resting at a nearby field with Patrasche.

 

“That’s so stupid.” Anastasia stated.

 

“It’s a respectable hobby, don’t judge!”

 

“WHY WOULD YOU PAY SO MUCH FOR HALF-NAKED WOMEN!”

 

“THAT IS AN OVERSIMPLIFICATION OF WHAT I JUST TOLD YOU. IT'S MORE LIKE STATUES OF ART!”

 

“DON’T MAKE IT SOUND BETTER THAN IT ACTUALLY IS YOU PERVERT!!”

 

“SAYS THE ONE WHO HAS A MONEY FETISH!!”

 

Anastasia gasps, “How dare you?!”

 

“You literally told me one of your dreams is to swim in a big pile of money. Naked.”

 

“IT WAS A JOKE AND I DID NOT SAY THAT LAST PART!”

 

“YOU IMPLIED IT! I COULD SEE IT IN YOUR EYES!!”

 

“KYAAA!!” Patrasche screeched.

 

“DON’T JUST TAKE HER SIDE!” Subaru yelled indignantly.

 

This particular conversation went on for several hours. Until they were nursing sore throats and throbbing migraines.

 

“…”

 

“What color hair were your statues?

 

Subaru, visibly confused, replied, “Why is that important?”

 

“Just answer the question.”

 

“…Mostly white and blue. Maybe green, OW!” She pinched his leg, “What was that for?!”

 

“Because you're an idiot. And a little shit. And a pervert.” She then looked away and huffed.

 

Subaru was confused why she was irritated for several more hours.

 

Day 12

 

Finally, there were some conversations that revealed more than they should.

 

Time to talk about it, I’ve delayed enough.

 

“So that power, what exactly is it? Like is it magic? Or a divine protection?” Anastasia asked.

 

They were nearing Priestella at this point, the sun was setting and the evening colors began to flourish.

 

“…”

 

“Not a comfortable topic?”

 

“…No, it’s not that. It’s just hard to explain,” Subaru stated cautiously.

 

Alright, let’s take a different approach.

 

“Then, let’s make it simpler, what exactly does it do?”

 

“It’s… I can see people differently. If I concentrate, the world becomes darker while people become brighter. Their bodies glow with a specific color.”

 

That’s… interesting. Given his gate, it probably isn’t magic which leaves a divine protection. But then why would he say it’s too complicated to explain?

 

“If they are an ally, they glow bright white. If they are an enemy, they glow red. And if they are neither, they glow a dull grey.”

 

Very useful! Once our names return, I can recruit him to the Iron Fang. He could be an excellent commander or at least could help scout out potential threats.

 

“If they are an enemy, I can transfer any damage I took, any wounds and pain I have, to them. Can’t spread from an enemy to another though. I have to react and concentrate on which enemies get which wounds. I know I’m… successful, if a string of light connects between us. From what I can tell, the pain is even amplified as it seems to happen all at once. In return, all that pain and damage is gone from my body.”

 

He rubbed his arm, “… Still hurts a lot though and if I’m not careful, I’m basically two steps from death.”

 

And there’s the best part of that ability. He basically gets a ‘get out of jail’ key for most injuries, as long as he stays conscious and alive. Explains his lack of wounds when escaping.

 

“Can you do anything for allies and neutrals?”

 

“…No, I cannot.”

 

So it’s a technique that keeps track of people who have good and bad intentions toward you. And can even heal you while hurting your enemies. All useful. Still, there’s gotta be a catch…

 

“Any more weaknesses?”

 

“…”

 

“Subaru, please, I need to know what we have at our disposal. If you can’t tell me, at least tell me the reason.”

 

“…I can’t use it on allies or neutrals.”

 

Anastasia was confused, “Isn’t that a good thing?”

 

Subaru just gave a sad smile, “Not if your allies are trying to kill you.”

 

Anastasia froze.

 

Was it related to the eyebrow twitches?! No, please no, don’t tell me.

 

…

 

“Did your camp try to kill you?” Anastasia whispered before her eyes widened, “Did Emilia try to kill you?!”

 

“What?! No, she didn’t!”

 

He didn’t deny the first part. That supports my theory. Let’s check.

 

“Then how-“

 

“It was Felix!”

 

Wait, what? Not Otto, Garfiel, Roswaal, or Ram?

 

“…”

 

“I didn’t get it at first. One day, a guard who had a particularly red aura, came into my cell. He kept complaining about something. I can’t remember…but all I know was I was exhausted. Felix visited me earlier and didn’t heal me completely. And I,” he swallowed, “I-I just couldn’t take it anymore. I wanted the pain to just go away for once! And the guard just kept complaining, how his life was so hard, and I just wanted him to shut up! That if he experienced just a bit of what I had. He would crack. Then he tried to hurt me. Next thing I know, he has cuts on his arms appearing out of nowhere and he’s crying in pain. Then, one day Felix was in a bad mood.”

 

Subaru was breathing heavily, his hands clammy and bone white from gripping the edge of the carriage as he spoke.

 

“H-he tried to kill me. I don’t know what it was, but I think Crusch’s heart almost stopped the night before. He tried to kill me. And I was tired. So tired. I tried using it on him. And it didn’t work. I was so confused. It worked before on a guard but not him. And I didn’t understand. I couldn’t understand. After all he did, why… why couldn’t I fight back?”

 

“Subaru…”

 

He started to get more frantic, his eyes dilating.

 

“And that’s when I realized what the colors meant. He was still white, a softer white, but still white. I was scared of him, I hated what he did to me, but I couldn’t think of him as an enemy. Like, in my head, despite everything he did, I pitied him over everything else. Because like me, he was a victim. A victim of gluttony, of lust, of the whole fucking witch cult. Just like my camp. Just like Beako!”

 

Scratch. Scratch. Scratch!

 

“Subaru.”

 

“He did so much. He boiled my blood. Picked at my flesh with blades and saws. Nearly drowned me several times. And kept healing me back up. But in spite of all that, I still couldn’t see him as an enemy! Isn’t that so fucked up? What is wrong with me?! I hate myself. Why couldn’t I just hate him?! Am I that weak?! Why couldn’t it just end? Why can’t I just die-“

 

Scratch! SCRATCH! SCRATCH!!

 

“Subaru!”

 

The scratching stopped, Anastasia grabbed his one hand while the other arm was caked in marks and fresh blood.

 

He was gasping for air, his face pale.

 

“…”

 

So, it’s not how others feel about him. It’s how he feels about others. If he considers them friend or foe.

 

“…”

 

Despite all of that, he still had empathy for Felix. But, he didn’t for the bandits. No, wait, that interpretation is wrong. I saw him hesitate. I saw him actively not wanting to kill them. If it’s not empathy, is it a past connection? Wait, that’s not important right now. His face, he looks just like he did when I met him. I need to say something. I-I don’t know. What should I say?!

 

Anastasia truly didn’t know what to say. Every possible option, every idea she had thought of to continue the conversation, died at her lips. For once, the merchant couldn’t think of a way out through words alone.

 

So she just sat there, holding his hand. As they drifted towards Priestella.

 

They arrived outside an inn in Priestella. It was almost night now and there was barely anyone walking outside. The awkward tension in the air had barely dissipated. The memories of what occurred months ago did not help.

 

Flashes of memories. Of Anastasia desperately trying to run away from Gluttony. Begging Echidna for help. Absorbing as much mana into her body as possible and brute forcing her body into acquiring the Flow Method.

 

“Thank you for the meal ~tsu! We will enjoy it, thoroughly.”

 

She nearly puked. It was all for nothing. He still caught up. Knocked her out and ate her name. Julius, Ricardo, Mimi, Hetaro, Tivey-

 

“I’m sorry.” Subaru croaked out.

 

Anastasia blinked, turning towards Subaru, she noticed how exhausted he looked. He looked less malnourished but his hair was still a dull white. With the mask and disguise on, he practically looked spiritual. An undying phantom of his past.

 

“For what?”

 

“For being such a shit knight.”

 

“Subaru-“

 

“Don’t. I am not a good knight. I’m not strong. I’m not particularly smart. And the only way I can protect people is by ki-,” he swallowed and his voice wavered, “nearly killing myself. Hell, you even just saw it. I’m barely keeping myself together. Half the time I dream of going back to my camp happily. The other half I’m happy because I will never see them again. Yet, I still think of someone who has been literally torturing me. As a friend. It’s not the first time. I’m a mess. You would have been better off with Julius if he lost his name. Or anybody. I’m worthless.”

 

That’s not true, that’s not true at all!

 

“…”

 

They both got off the carriage, standing before the inn, still holding each other hand-in-hand.

 

Anastasia was looking at the ground in contemplation.

 

I have to say something.

 

“Once we’re in Kararagi, you should hire a bodyguard. I’ll write my recipes and ideas before I leave. You deserve better.”

 

Anything!

 

“…I’ll find another inn. Good night Anastasia.”

 

 

He tried to leave but was stopped as Anastasia was still holding his hand.

 

Come on you stupid, stupid girl. Think! Before he leaves and disappears forever. Just like the others.

 

He pulled but her grip was still strong.

 

Anastasia reached deep into her mind, behind the curtain where madness lies. Where her deepest, darkest regrets and fears lay dormant. The ones that she suppressed with all her might. And there, she found a possible answer.

 

Being rational doesn’t work for Subaru. He just closes himself off more. I need to be emotional, raw and honest, just like before. Another gamble, here goes nothing.

 

She took a deep breath.

 

“When I was a child, I was in a terrible situation,” she blurted out.

 

Too general, too general!

 

Subaru was confused and a little shocked, “You mean when you met Ricardo, you told me that story-“

 

Anastasia raised her hand and shook her head, “A story from before that time. A story I never told to anyone, not even Ricardo. Years ago, when I was out on the streets, I was taken in by a courtesan. She was a high ranking prostitute. She treated me well, so well that I basically considered her my mother. It was the first time I met someone who treated me with kindness. Who I thought treated me with kindness.”

 

Sob stories are easy to tell. Great for negotiation, especially with happy endings. I gave Subaru one sob story from my past, and he gave me treasure troves of info.

 

But not this one, no one got a happy ending. If he can stab himself to protect me, I can go back down the nightmare road. Just this once.

 

Anastasia swallowed but continued, “But she was not a good person. She bought slaves. Slaves that were more pretty than her were… were mutilated. Slaves that were less pretty… she would give them her love. Whether they wanted it or not. I-I regret not helping them. I promised myself I wouldn’t do that again, leaving them to rot.”

 

Memories of meeting Ricardo, of trying to help those two fox demi-humans, flashed by her mind.

 

I couldn’t let that happen to anyone else, not again.

 

“…” Subaru was slowly getting more and more disturbed.

 

“Maybe I was lucky, but all she did was hit me every once in a while or call me names. But I was so happy because she would still treat me nicely and she would sometimes cry to me about her problems. She relied on me and cared for me. I was happy.”

 

I couldn’t trust anyone after that. Everyone has a hidden agenda, even with good intentions.

 

Anastasia took a second to catch her breath, her mouth was dry, and she was seconds away from dry heaving.

 

“…And then she died.”

 

“…” Subaru rubbed Anastasia’s hand with his thumb. Anastasia looked like she was at the brink of tears, her gut felt like a black hole.

 

Ricardo was kind to me because he believed in my potential. I was kind to Subaru because I believed he was a hidden jackpot. Good intentions but something to gain out of it. But Subaru?

 

She continued, “A high profile client killed her in a fit of rage, and I cried so much that day. I missed her despite how terrible she was to me. To everyone. Just because she would treat me well sometimes. After that I was sent back on the streets.”

 

Subaru was kind. Just kind. Nothing hidden, just is. Why? I don’t understand. What makes you care so much for such little personal benefit?

 

She felt like she was about to choke. But she had to keep going.

 

…I don’t know why I’m doing this. But I know I have to try.

 

I just have to.

 

“What I’m trying to say is. We can’t help how we feel sometimes. Sometimes, despite what we should feel, we can’t help but cling to the small bits of happiness. Maybe I should have hated her. For being terrible. And a part of me did. And a part of me didn’t. And both still remain.”

 

Please, I don’t know what else to say.

 

I can’t deal with this alone. And I don’t think he can either.

 

“…That still doesn’t mean you don’t deserve better than some messed up knight. If Julius was here-“

 

“Julius isn’t here!” Subaru was startled by her shouting.

 

Anastasia, on the brink of tears, whispered, “But you are. You chose to stop that night and comfort me despite being chased. You chose to fight those bandits in such a suicidal way to protect me. And you chose to tell me so much about your past when you never had to.”

 

She then gripped his hand tight, “And despite how highly you think of Julius, he wasn’t perfect. Julius always strived for the ideal, the knight of knights. Which meant, despite how close our relationship was, he never could truly loosen up and open up to me. I had to coax him into relaxing all of the time.”

 

She gave a soft smile and continued, “You are completely different compared to him, and that’s what I like about you Subaru-kun. You act like a free-spirited child half the time. You're completely honest about your feelings and intentions all the time. And you never care about social tradition or etiquette any time. I could never have a six hour shouting match about naked women with Julius.”

 

Despite the situation, Subaru couldn’t help but snort, “You mean half-naked women.”

 

Much of the tension, that had been slowly dissipating, was all but gone now.

 

“Yeah, yeah you jackass.” Anastasia snickered.

 

Subaru laughed as well.

 

“…”

 

For a second, Anastasia looked thoughtful, “And hell, I’m no Emilia. I could barely think of what to do when you were freaking out besides holding your hand. My first intention when meeting you wasn’t exactly selfless. I’m not as kind or considerate as she is. And based on how you told it, she was basically a saint when you met her the first time. If she was here, you’d probably be in a much better head space.”

 

Maybe she could have dragged you out of this with more tact and success. No use speculating.

 

Subaru looked away, deep in thought, before returning to focus on Anastasia,

 

“… You’re right. You're not Emilia. Just like I’m not Julius. But Emilia wouldn’t spend multiple days asking me every single question under the sun about my home. Sure she would listen and believe me when I told stories, but she wouldn’t be super interested in the stories themselves, just that I’m telling them. And while we would argue, our fights would be either completely benign or earth shattering. When you and I argue, I never feel like our relationship may end just because I said the wrong thing. You’d clarify, try to understand my position, or at least reason with me. They’re actually fun. Sometimes it felt all or nothing with Emilia.”

 

Subaru smiled and grabbed Anastasia’s hand with both hands.

 

“You’re not my dragon candidate. You’re someone who believed in me when no one else would. Someone who gives me advice and comforts me in her own way, despite disagreeing with what I say or do. You’re someone that, despite how little time we’ve spent together, I can fully trust with my life.”

 

…Why trust me so much? I’ve done nothing in this life to earn that. Though I can’t really talk. The boy somehow has been worming his way into my heart.

 

Anastasia’s heart started to warm again. She knew what she had to say.

 

“… I was wrong to call you my knight. You’re my pillar of support. You’re someone I enjoy bantering with. You’re my-,” Anastasia started to choke, “my friend.”

 

Something within her cracked slightly, seeping bitterness and indignant at what she forced out of her mouth.

 

Subaru smiled even brighter, which made the lump in her throat feel even larger.

 

Yeah. Friend. Just like the others. And I didn’t even try. Would it have been this easy to begin again?

 

Subaru said, “You were wrong about one other thing,” Anastasia looked puzzled, “I do not have a high opinion of Julius.”

 

Anastasia rolled her eyes, “Oh please. What was that word you said, soon-there-ay? That’s you.”

 

“Pot meet kettle.”

 

“What does that even mean!? Tell me.” She glared at him in faux anger.

 

“Nah,” she pinched his cheek with her open hand, “Ow!”

 

“Little. Shit.”

 

“Okay, okay! I’ll tell you later!”

 

“You are also telling me what ‘okay’ means.”

 

Subaru rolled his eyes, “Wow what a demanding, greedy little princess I have for a friend.”

 

Anastasia simply puffed her cheeks and posed, “Hmph! You know it. And I’m proud of it.”

 

Both of them gazed into each other's eyes and simply chuckled.

 

“Now come on my now ex-knight. You’re still on body pillow duty.”

 

Subaru grimaced, “I really shouldn’t have explained to you what those are.”

 

“Suffer.”

 

Despite the warmth in her heart, Anastasia still couldn’t ignore the small tinge of bitterness in her soul. Not quite understanding her own heart, she delayed the problem to think about for tomorrow.

 

Meanwhile, at the manor of a certain Finest Knight.

 

Julius was not okay.

 

He was currently scouring several stacks of reports, all of which relating to the imprisonment of the Sin Archbishop of Pride, and was getting increasingly frustrated.

 

His eyes narrowed. Another discrepancy. Felix, what have you been doing for the last few months?

 

Ever since the Archbishop escaped, he has only had question after question raised. Arriving at the prison tower in the morning, he noticed the sweet smell in the air. After convening with Wilhelm, the answer was simple: Muskrim. Otherwise known as sleeping flower, its powder induces sleep on humans.

Which explained how most of the guards were knocked out. Those that were injured were known to be veterans and most likely were able to resist the powder. Interviewing them revealed little: the assailant attacked from the dark and with magic that they couldn’t recognize.

 

When the method was found, Julius tried to look into records, see if maybe the flower was snuck into the prison somehow, and someone got a hand on it.

 

Yet, all he found were mismatched reports, several guard reassignments, and copious amounts of materials that were not suitable for humane interrogation.

 

The guards were strangely tight lipped. Not offering anything of note and all had the same response,

 

“Blue was in charge of everything.”

 

He immediately went to Felix, looking for answers. Felix, however, was practically catatonic. Only focusing solely on preventing Crusch’s condition from worsening. No amount of prodding helped.

 

Wilhelm was no better. The man had been swamped with work since Priestella, managing all of the camp by himself. He only went to the prison during the first week of the cultist’s tenure there, and Felix barely met with him ever since.

 

Julius started rubbing his brow.

 

“Don’t worry Julius-kyun! Reinhard and I will handle this. You take care of the Priestella clean up.”

 

Julius’s eyes widened.

Reinhard.

He needed to find Reinhard. He was there, at least for the first day, before disappearing for months on several missions. He needed to catch Reinhard once he returned.

 

Knock. Knock.

 

With Julius’s focus broken, he put aside the reports, alongside his thoughts, for later.

 

“Come in.”

 

“Excuse me for the late arrival, Sir Julius. Frufoo has been a bit overworked considering she’s the only earth dragon we have at the moment.”

 

The merchant bowed in exaggerated gratitude before continuing.

 

“Thank you again for letting me stay in your home while I conduct business at the capital. Especially after organizing such a grand meeting in Priestella just a few months prior.”

 

Julius replied with his own fantastical bow.

 

“It is my pleasure Mr. Suwen. Think nothing of it. It’s the least I could do since the beginning of our legendary camaraderie during the war against the cult.”

 

After a few seconds, they both cocked their heads up, and laughed heartily in jest.

 

Julius smiled and waved him toward the chair in front of his desk, “It is good to see you again my friend.”

 

Otto grinned at that before taking a seat, “Likewise. Speaking of the alliance, how are Crusch and Felix doing?

 

Julius had a somber expression.

 

“Badly. Ever since the Archbishop escaped, Felix is basically out of commission besides helping Crusch. Crusch’s condition hasn’t improved either.”

 

Otto grimaced, “Any idea where he might have gone?”

 

Julius shook his head, “Not at all, the knights have been searching all over Lugunica. For all we know, he might be in another country.”

 

“You think? We could check in at Kararagi. Do you know anyone who may want to help?”

 

Julius contemplated for a bit, rubbing his chin,”I do have a company that my family owns based in Kararagi. Joshua is currently managing it. It fell into my lap back during the start of the election but it might be good to check on my contacts there.”

 

“The Hoshin Trading Company? It still surprises me ever since you told us in Priestella. Can’t believe the owner gifted it to you.”

 

Julius furrowed his brow, “Yeah, I couldn’t believe it either…”

 

Why did Chuden Agri gift it to us? He barely explained a thing and wouldn’t respond to my letters. And why change the name to the founder of Kararagi?

 

ACHOO!

 

Julius’s musings were interrupted by Otto’s sudden sneeze. “Are you okay my friend, sick?”

 

“Argh, no, but I have been sneezing a lot these past couple of days. Feels like someone has been talking about me,” Otto’s eyes narrowed, “in frankly insulting ways.”

 

“While your oddly specific instincts are noted, I’m curious, I’ve never heard of that type of saying before.”

 

Otto waved his hand, “I heard it way back when. Though I can’t exactly recall where.” Otto shrugged.

 

Julius nodded, “Going back to the Archbishop, I need a bit of help understanding something, you were there during the first week he was captured, correct?”

 

Otto’s face looked grim, “Yeah, my camp and I were. It was… strange.”

 

Julius raised an eyebrow, “Strange how?”

 

“Well… Felix told us that the cultist kept claiming he was a part of our camp, despite us not remembering him.”

 

Otto rubbed his chin before continuing,

 

“Yet, when we all visited him, he wouldn’t say a thing. Like… he was completely mute. No matter what we did, he wouldn’t react.”

 

“That is very strange… thank you my friend, you’ve done me a great service.”

 

I have a fledgling theory now, but if I’m correct, the consequences will be dire.

 

Felix… Did you mess with his mind?

 

Were you so desperate for answers, you brute forced the smallest possibilities?

 

Otto was slightly confused but stated, “Always happy to help a friend, even though I don’t know how exactly I did so.”

 

Julius simply gave a 10,000 gigawatt smile in response. He was positively shining.

 

Otto, now not only confused but blinded and annoyed, continued, “Anyway, regarding my business here. I was wondering if you’d be interested in a little expedition?”

 

Julius held his hand up, “If it’s anything related to the election, I’ll have to refuse. Might I kindly remind you of my family’s stance: we will support all dragon candidate’s equally. We will act as a liaison between candidates and unite the camps whenever it’s necessary. While the same can’t be said for the Iron Fang, they are currently still recovering and on vacation since Priestella.”

 

Otto merely rolled his eyes, “Do you have to do that every time?”

 

“Plausible deniability is a… knight’s best asset?”

 

Julius hesitated for a second. He felt like that wasn’t the correct saying but he had used it before.

 

There’s that odd feeling again. Maybe this whole debacle is corroding my wit.

 

The merchant ignored the hiccup and simply grinned in response, “Then, what about the mercenary Juli, would he be interested?”

 

The purple haired knight gave a subtle smirk, “While I am unaware of his whereabouts, I’m sure he would be ‘happy to help a friend’, just like with the Archbishop of Sloth.”

 

The two friends discussed plans for the expedition to the east, to the great sand dunes of Augria. Unknowing of what difficulties they will soon face.

Notes:

EN: Adding to canon is always a risk. Icker umbers? Stupid but low risk. An additional backstory to a fleshed out character? Could derail a whole fic. Anyway let me know what you think, this won’t happen that often and only if I think it would make sense and help add to scenes.
EN2: Otto has seasonal allergies. Started in season 2. Mostly Subaru related. Poor Bototo…
EN3: also has it ever been mentioned how frustratingly complex gluttony is? It can make three separate timelines to remember: the original, the one where you disappeared, and the one your friend disappeared. What a nightmare…

Chapter 5: Interruptions and Intrusions

Summary:

Anastasia and Subaru finally arrive at Banan in Kararagi, and are given a warm welcome…

Notes:

Thank you again to everyone for supporting this fic! Almost 700 kudos and almost 120 bookmarks. Let’s keep the ball rolling!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

“I think we should still hire a bodyguard,” Subaru began.

They were currently sitting outside the city of Banan awaiting entrance as dozens of caravans slowly received approval to enter. Subaru and Anastasia took the opportunity to plan out their objectives once they arrived inside.

“…” Anastasia was pensively sitting on the ground. Subaru was pacing around her.

Subaru was currently maskless, no disguise. It was decided he only needed his pseudo name in Kararagi. A change in hairstyle and clothing matching the regions style would be needed, the previous getup is too striking and would draw attention.

“I know I said it… when I was having a moment. But we should still be realistic. If you won’t allow me to use, that, in a fight then we will need someone else to fight for us.”

Subaru himself was looking healthier, more fat and muscle than just skin and bones. His black hair was returning at the roots, the white tips long and some reaching his neck from the back, reminiscent of salt and pepper. He wore mostly black traveling robes and an orange scarf given to him by Anastasia.

It’s the right move. But there’s so many variables to consider. We can’t trust just anyone and money is tight.

Anastasia was wearing one of her old merchant robes. Not exactly as elegant as what she wore during her time in Lugunica but still cute: white with purple accents and frills. Her star pin was ever present, paired on her head with a white ribbon shaped in a bow with Mimi’s face stitched on top. Guess who made the ribbon?

One wrong move and we either get ransomed off to Lugunica or get assassinated to prevent any further problems. We’re only lucky that the Reinhard Rule is still in effect.

“I know we are limited on options and money but it’s better safe than sorry, you know? Worst case scenario, we die before your business starts ramping up. Sure it could be hard to filter out all the nasty people, but you got a good eye and I can be of use by acting as a kind of bait or something. Act all naive and easy to manipulate, make people underestimate me. Ha, reminds me of Otto, man I miss him. Anyway, maybe if I put my disguise on, I can act all threatening and scare away the bad guys. Bad guys? Maybe not-“ Subaru continued to word vomit while pacing a hole in the ground.

He really does tend to ramble every now and then for some reason. I wonder why. Doesn’t matter, I should stop him before he has another episode.

Subaru’s episodes have been on and off since Priestella. Anastasia noticed it happens often in relation to his weird aura power, when he remembers his time in prison, or when he thinks of his camp too much.

Anastasia sighed before standing up and dusting herself off.

She walked over to Subaru and grabbed his arm, he tensed slightly, before realizing who she was and relaxing.

“You’re doing it again.”

Subaru blushed before looking away, “Sorry, hard to curb bad habits so soon…”

“It’s alright, reminds me when I think too much,” Anastasia then gave a wry grin, “Besides, I think it’s cute how you get all antsy~.”

Subaru’s blush deepened before he glared and pinched Anastasia’s nose. Hard.

“Hey- ouch! You ass, what was that for?”

“For playing with a poor boy’s heart.”

“Awww, but it’s so fun seeing you get all embawassed~,” Anastasia replied as she laughed.

Subaru huffed in faux anger before snickering, “Alright, but seriously, we need a body guard.”

Anastasia sighed, “No I agree. We just need to be careful. Let’s add it to the list,” she quickly looked over at the gate and saw their turn was next, “Speaking of, let’s go over it one last time.”

Subaru nodded and motioned her to go forward.

“Priority one: find and contract a spirit. Or at the very least get someone to drain our, specifically your, mana consistently. Priority two: secure a base of operations and begin product development. Priority three: begin networking and secure investors. Now, priority four: screen potential combatants as bodyguards. Anything else we should add?”

Subaru thought for a moment before adding, “No that’s all good. We should also consider looking into your old company, maybe gluttony left some stuff of yours abandoned like back in Lugunica.”

Anastasia grimaced at the thought of possibly seeing her old colleagues, employees, and friends but agreed with Subaru. They need to use everything they can. Can’t be too picky.

The guard yelled at them to enter, Anastasia grabbed Subaru’s hand.

Subaru led Patrasche and the carriage with his other hand.

They entered the beautiful city of Banan. Bustling crowds of people wearing vibrant kimonos, yukatas, and haoris marched around them. Towering architecture made of tiled roofs and wood palaces echoed the landscape.

To Subaru, it must have been a sight of wonder, given his gaping mouth.

To Anastasia, it was equal parts nostalgic and melancholic.

She hated how her previously happy memories just bring her pain now. Of Ricardo introducing her to the bar, meeting the triplets, and her fateful encounter with Echidna. She was going to bring Julius here more often, show him the sights. Bring everyone. It could have still happened. If she only wasn’t such a cow-

Subaru squeezed her hand, knocking her out of her spiral. She gazed at him and noticed how soft his eyes were. And how her other hand was death gripping the carriage. He must have noticed.

Subaru looked back towards the city, “… it’s so beautiful. It reminds me of home.”

Anastasia’s eyes widened slightly before softly giggling.

Of course. That almost confirms it. Kararagi was founded by Subaru’s people. Now I only need to show him Hoshin’s texts.

Anastasia sighed.

Ha, no use lingering on the past.

She laid back, yet her eyes still radiated determination and firm greed.

Have to build back up if I’m going to reclaim it. All of it. Just you wait guys. I’ll be back soon.

Anastasia took them to the broker she used to work with. Her goods from Lugunica were varied, done specifically to avoid a situation where one particular good depreciated too heavily in value.

Cough, cough, Otto.

She got lucky, nearly half their goods were highly in demand. Combined with her coin savings, she could rent a modest piece of housing for a few months and invest in maybe two inventions of Subaru’s. They parked Patrasche and the carriage in a secure location before leaving to accomplish priority number one.

“So where can we find a spirit to drain our mana?” Subaru asked.

They were currently wading through a crowd of people, it was midday and the weather was fairly sunny, albeit cloudy.

“Hm, the easiest way would probably be at a temple. There, we can find a miko who could help us contract a minor spirit.”

The crowd was getting more and more bustling.

“Wait, you have Shinto shamans here?!”

Anastasia looked at Subaru curiously before nearly tripping from someone bumping into her. Subaru caught her by the arm and brought her close.

Slightly blushing, Anastasia smiled and nodded in thanks.

“While I don’t know what sheentoe shamans are, mikos have been present in Kararagi for a while now. We aren’t quite as religious as Gusteko, but a good portion of spirit arts users are trained at temples to nurture their skills.”

Subaru hummed in thought before saying, “I can’t believe how much Kararagi reminds me of Japan. Most of the stuff here, from the accents to the houses to now even mikos, remind me of the Kansai area…”

Anastasia’s interest caught replied, “I’ve been meaning to ask that, do you think other people from your home settled here?”

“Maybe… it’s hard to tell. I always thought I wasn’t the first to arrive here though I’ve barely met anyone else from Japan. The only one I have is maybe Al, and I never had the chance to talk to him about it-“

Anastasia interrupted him by grabbing his cheek and turning him toward her, “What?”

Her face was smiling but her eyes looked anything but.

“Y-yeah Al, big guy, one arm. He and I are the only ones I know who got transported here from my world.”

…mmmmMMMMMM AAHHHHHHH!!!!

 

Meanwhile in Vollachia, a certain helmeted companion of a fiery princess was currently in the midst of a life or death battle.

ACHOO!

“Gah! My stars must be bad. I can’t believe someone’s talking about me right fucking now…”

That sneeze cost him nearly 20 lives.

 

Back to our intrepid stars:

Of course, the dumb half-elf with no ambition and the ambitious narcissist bimbo got two of the greatest gold mines of the world. And didn’t do shit with either! The little hellion even got Reinhard. Some people get all the luck.

Anastasia was currently still smiling at Subaru, her eyes positively dead, in the middle of the crowd of on-goers. Subaru, on the other hand, was visibly getting more flustered as Anastasia was still grabbing his cheek and looking into his eyes.

To onlookers, it was a scene out of a romance novel.

Internally? Both participants were screaming mentally for different reasons.

The deadlock breaks as Anastasia sighs and simply pats Subaru’s cheek before hooking her arm around his and beginning to drag him forward once more.

“…Remind me to punch Priscilla the next time I see her.”

Bewildered, Subaru asked, “Do you have a death wish?!”

“At this point, my spite outweighs my fear of dying.”

Subaru looked incredulously at her before shaking his head.

“So yeah, going back to your question: probably? The signs say yes, given how recognizable everything here is but it was probably pretty rare.”

Then that means highly skilled and influential people from his home settled here. My theory is Hoshin, and several other innovators of history, all had the same origin. Speaking of origins,

“Hey, I don’t mean to think you're lying, but it’s just so hard to believe that a place exists beyond the waterfall…”

Subaru didn’t look offended, in fact he looked incredibly understanding, “No I get it. Even I would be skeptical if people told me about a world where dragons flew, magic existed, and Demi-humans lived. All of that was fiction to people like me.”

Anastasia nodded at that, “Even with everything you told me, it’s hard for me to imagine. What I’d give to see it in person…”

She noticed him flinching.

Ah, I made a mistake.

Still looping arms, she nudged his side.

“Sorry, I didn’t mean to salt the wound. You must miss your home.”

Subaru swallowed but simply nodded, “… It doesn’t hurt as much as before, but yeah I do. I tried to move on but recently… it’s been hard not to get sentimental.”

Ah, all my questions.

She felt like she would regret this but, “We don’t have to talk about your home anymore. I know I asked a lot already-“

He interrupted, “No! No, that’s not what I meant. It really doesn’t bother me.”

Anastasia didn’t exactly believe him, “But-“

He interrupted again with his free hand held up, “Please let me explain.”

Subaru took a deep breath, “When I arrived here, I was actually so happy. For a time, I didn’t even think about home at all. There was too much going on. But then, when the dust settled, when I realized I would never,” Subaru choked but pressed on, “never see my parents again. It all hit at once.”

His voice wavered but he continued, “Due to certain events, I was able to move on and push it all to the back of my mind. And I never really talked about it with anyone besides Beako or Emilia-tan. It just felt like I was lingering in the past when I didn’t need to.”

His features softened, his gaze never averting from her.

“But when we talked, it felt like I was… opening up a photo book of my childhood. Nostalgic. Like I was walking down memory lane. Sure some memories felt bitter sweet. And sure, I still miss my parents. But it was fun. And oddly, freeing? Like having someone listen to me and being interested, makes those memories more real than before, if that makes sense? And if I can be of help to you, bringing stuff from my home here: well two birds with one stone you know?”

He gave a melancholic smile.

Anastasia simply gave her own small smile in response, but her mind was solemn and pensive.

‘Be of help to me.’ That wasn’t the first time he said something similar. Is.. is he trying to make himself useful? While I’m sure he isn’t lying about how he feels, why do I get the underlying feeling of something else? As if… he’s desperate.

Not wanting to open that can of worms just yet, as Subaru puts it, she decided to change the subject.

“So, ‘two birds with one stone,’ don’t mind explaining that, Professor Subaru?”

Subaru brightened before fauxly scoffing, “Elementary my dear Anastasia Watson,” he said in his most pretentious voice.

She simply giggled and waved for him to continue.

“The phrase comes from…!”

Subaru paused as if out of breath, his eyes blinking and unfocused.

“Subaru?” Anastasia was now concerned.

Is he okay? Oh no, is he having another episode-

Her thoughts were interrupted. His eyes refocused, hard, and lingered on her for a second before Subaru grabbed her hand and began leading her out of the crowd quickly.

“Subaru?!” She asked again. “What’s wrong?”

Subaru simply stated, “We need to leave. Now.”

He started sprinting with her down the street, ducking into alleys and crossing roads.

Are we being chased?! Did he see a knight? There’s no way they are already here?!

Anastasia started breathing heavily, her body not used to the exertion. But before she knew it, Subaru picked her up and started sprinting with her, bridal carry style.

Wait wait wait-

Before she could even feel the blood rush to her cheeks, Subaru croaked, “Sorry I know you don’t like this but bear with me here!”

Wait what-

He quickly rearranged her positioning. Where she was now being held like a sack of tatoes on his shoulder. He started sprinting faster.

…What is going on?

They dashed into an alley that opened into the downtown area of Banan. Before she could even process anything, Subaru threw open a nearby container. It was filled with garbage.

Wait no don’t tell me, SUBARU-

He unceremoniously chucked her inside before dumpster diving himself.

Closing the container from the inside, Subaru grabbed Anastasia and held her close, before whispering, “Please, just stay quiet for now.”

Bewildered, disgusted, and despite every part of her screaming, she decided to comply.

Moments later, she heard footsteps outside.

Step. Step. Stomp!

They were right outside. She could hear a faint muttering, as well as someone making a racket outside. For the next few seconds, she could only feel the tension in the air as well as the fast heartbeat of Subaru. Before she knew it, she heard whoever was outside, sprint away.

Stepstepstepstep… step… step…

 

They both sighed in relief. Now, with danger away, Anastasia’s mind realized the situation they were in. Barely an inch apart, knee deep in garbage. She wanted out.

“Subaru-“ however, she was interrupted again by Subaru pulling her closer.

I’m really getting sick of being interrupted all the time.

Before she could angrily pinch him for choosing a bad time for a hug, she felt him shudder.

“Subaru?”

“Please… just, I need a minute… I just need to know you’re still here.”

“…Okay.”

Maybe he remembers getting chased by the guards after escaping…

They sat there, in the dark, for a good ten minutes. As nice as it was cuddling in a trash heap, Anastasia had limits.

She lightly tapped his cheek, or what she thinks was his cheek.

“Okay… I’m okay now,” Subaru said, letting out a deep breath.

With quick adept motion, mirroring the dexterity of two raccoons, they scampered out of the dumpster.

Brushing herself off, and quickly throwing off a banina peel on her head, Anastasia had questions.

“Okay, you need to explain what just happened. Who was that? What happened back there? You just froze and then suddenly we are in a mad dash.”

Subaru quickly looked around, eyes concentrating, before locking onto Anastasia, “…I recognized someone in the crowd.”

Her eyes widened, “Knight, candidate, or something else?”

He shook his head and raised three fingers, “Something I dealt with before, I need to double check though. We should head to the temple.”

“What?! No, we should leave.”

No use staying here and risking our lives, Banan is the most profitable but it isn’t the only city to begin a business.

Again, Subaru shook his head, “It won’t change a thing. It’s better if we deal with this now rather than later.”

He’s being intentionally vague right now.

“Subaru-“

“I know what you're going to say. I know I’m not being exactly clear but I just don’t want to worry you until I confirm what we are dealing with.”

He gave a smile before continuing, “I promise, I’m not going to hide anything. We’re in this together, no matter what.”

While still skeptical in the mind, her heart felt warm, and her gut told her to trust the boy at least once more.

“Fine. But if I find out you hid anything for some dumb reason, there will be hell to pay,” she said as she pointed at his chest, “Now come on, despite how far we got, we can still make it to the temple before dinner.”

Subaru chuckled and did a dumb pose, “Yes ma’am! Lead the way!”

Anastasia exaggerated a sigh before she began trudging toward their destination as Subaru briefly lingered behind.

 

 

Gazing at her back, he muttered under his breath, “I won’t make the same mistakes again…”

He then briskly paced to walk by her side, continuing their conversation where they left off once more.

 

 

It was still mid-afternoon when they arrived at the temple. The temple resided on a small hill, with a staircase marked by overhead archways. The temple itself was of a modest size, not exactly towering as the rest of the city, but radiating an aura that one could only define as divine.

The more interesting sights were the various shrine priestesses, wearing traditional white kosodes and red hakamas. It was a fair mix of humans and demi-humans.

Despite focusing on the mikos, Subaru seemed surprisingly nonchalant about it all.

I know he’s seen it before in his home, but I expected his reaction to be at least a little more emotional.

She couldn’t help herself, however.

“What, I know the mikos are beautiful but you shouldn’t just gawk at them~,” she teased.

No visible reaction, he simply retorted, “They are quite beautiful. Should we buy one of their dresses for you?”

Her teasing deflected, she wasn’t exactly deterred, “Ohhh, is my favorite employee already trying to shmooze his way up the ladder~. Should I report you to Human Resources?”

Gotta use all that information I got from Subaru for something. Still deciding if I should implement an HR in Hoshin Company… Eh, questions for later.

Subaru deadpanned, “I’m your only employee. Patrasche doesn’t count.”

He then smirked and continued, “Besides, I’m serious, I’d think you look cute in that.”

She nearly choked.

W-where did this come from?!

She coughed before trying to retain her composure, “While I would certainly agree, I doubt they would let me take one.”

“Well it never hurts to ask, let’s go!”

This time she actually choked. He started walking forward.

Wait, wait, wait-

She scrambled after him.

“Wait, SUBARU!”

She caught up to his side, “Hold on a second! It might be sacrilegious for a non-miko to wear their robes. Don’t you think it would be rude of us to assume not?”

“Well we won’t know if we don’t ask! Besides, what is it you said about me? It’s not like I ever cared about social etiquette in the first place,” he said with a shit-eating grin and a quickened pace.

Damnit, what is with him today?!

Anastasia gripped him by the back of his clothes, trying to slow him down. It did not work.

Subaru dragged her to a fox demi-human miko whose smile started to grow as they edged closer.

“My, my~. To what do I owe the pleasure?”

“Ahoy! The name is Atlas and this is my darling companion Anastasia. I was absolutely blown away by the beautiful dresses you girls wear and I was wondering if my beautiful, gorgeous, adorable-“

As he kept listing off more adjectives he dragged Anastasia close to his side, preventing her from escaping. Anastasia was currently going through every shade of red possible.

So this is what it feels like to be on the other side. Well, not like his gambit will work, mikos have a reputation to uphold. She’ll likely rebuff him for being an idiot.

“-stunning, elegant, and absolutely incredible wife would be able to wear one such as yours!” He winked at the miko.

“Oh ho ho! Well, we’d have to first measure her.”

Wait no-

The miko started orbiting Anastasia, raising the white star’s arms and checking every inch of her body.

“While she isn’t exactly fitting the ideal body type of our shrine, it isn’t something we can’t work with.”

Oh you little-

The miko stopped orbiting, motioned for Subaru, and whispered in his ear.

Subaru simply nodded sagely and said, “Correct.”

Did she just-?!

The miko clapped her hands, “Wonderful! We could have one ready and made by the end of the we-“

Anastasia lost her self-control, “Can I get a say in this?!”

The miko didn’t stop, “-ek but unfortunately our dresses are only for mikos and miko-in-trainings. So, sorry,” she finished with a smirk and a bow.

Subaru also bowed, “Ah I figured but thank you for confirming.”

…

 

Anastasia slowly walked up to Subaru, and started lightly punching him in the stomach.

“Hmm? Something, pfttt, wrong Ana?” He said with barely, concealed laughter.

The punches started coming faster. Harder.

“Hehe, ow, wait Ana stop! Haha, stop, that's actually starting to hurt, hahaha!!”

Left, right, left, right. Future champion of boxing right here.

“Hahahaha, oh shit! OW! So worth it!”

 

Eventually, once Anastasia calmed down, they were able to ask for help contracting a spirit. The miko asked them to wait a second as she checked who was available.

Anastasia, pouting, poked his side, “So, tell me, was this all planned? Did you somehow find a way to signal that girl to tag team me?”

He just laughed again, “Nah, I could just tell she would roll with the punches.”

She swiped at him for the pun, he dodged.

She huffed, “Little shit.”

“Oh come on, don’t tell me you wouldn’t have done the same to me.”

She opened her mouth to deny it, paused, and then just puffed her cheeks and huffed again.

Subaru just poked her cheeks. She swiped at him again.

Before another boxing match could begin, the miko returned.

“Apologies for the wait. Unfortunately, most of our priestesses are busy healing the victims of the latest attack. We can still accommodate you, but it will have to be one at a time.”

Anastasia latched onto that one piece of info, “Victims? Was there a fight?”

The miko shook her head, “Serial killer. They’ve been killing people left and right at random. The most recent attack nearly butchered a whole group of mercenaries.”

She continued, “Now, let’s set aside such morbid topics, who would like to go first?”

Before she was able to respond, Subaru interjected, “Anastasia should go first.”

Surprised, Anastasia asked, “Why me? Your condition takes priority. It’s been too long since you’ve been drained and it will only get worse.”

He shook his head, “I understand but I’m used to having a ton of mana in me. You aren’t. Also, I’ll need to contract a spirit which will take time. You don’t have to, so I’d rather you go first to avoid waiting.”

She wanted to argue but he looked firm in his position.

The miko finally interjected, “If it helps, I did ask my sisters to come assist once they finished. More than likely, another will be able to come soon enough to help whoever is left.”

Anastasia sighed, “Fine. I’ll go first then.”

Subaru smirked in victory while Anastasia was led away.


“…”

“…”

“So,” the miko broke the silence, “How long have you and your husband been married?”

Anastasia sputtered before coughing, “T-that was a joke. We aren’t like that. We’re just friends and business partners.”

It was funny and useful in Lugunica. Can’t do that anymore here. Besides the fact that single ladies get more business opportunities, we can’t pretend to be lovey dovey all the time.

The miko didn’t look convinced, “Friends eh? Didn’t seem that way to me. Friends don’t adore each other in that way, like you both do.”

…That’s just because of how we met. We’re all we got until Gluttony bites it. Nothing more and nothing less.

Anastasia’s face showed no visible reaction, “We’ve been through a lot together. It’s trust your seein’, no love.”

“I see. Well then ya wouldn’t mind if I took him for myself.”

“…”

“He’s got the mature look, salt and peppir hair, that contrasts with that bit of puckish rogue mischief which would make any girl go wild-“

Anastasia interrupted the miko with a gentle but firm grasp on her shoulder, while smiling, “Let’s keep things professional shall we,” she shook a bag of coins and placed it in the priestess’s hand.

No reaction from the priestess but a smile, “Sorry, we don’t take payment for our services-“

Anastasia slammed another bag of coins in her hand.

“-but we do take generous gifts. What would you like to know?”

“More information on the attacks, events of the last few months, plans of the League of Cities, current trends and movements of these companies…”

The actual reason these temples exist: a top-tier information network. High ranking spirits are hard to track and can gather tons of information secretly. Coupled with temples having high concentrations of water spirits, ideal for healing, and you have a hotspot for info gathering.

“…especially Hoshin Company.”

“Alright, the Banan special it is. Let’s begin with events: there was a failed expedition to the caverns, Zarestia’s Bed, west of Banan a couple of months back, no survivors. The only other major event has been the serial killer assaults, which have been increasing in severity over the last month. While I did say the attacks were random, there was a particular trend. The mercenaries that were recently attacked were transporting a special prisoner: a witch cultist.”
