“And maybe Subaru should start saying the ‘but’ section to his point before I start reconsidering accepting.”

“Buuuuut! I want to be greedy. I want us to stay close no matter what. I want what I have now and I want what I had before. Even if it fails, I want to chase after that kind of happy ending.”

Anastasia sighed, “Alright. I already agreed, no need to justify it anymore. Let’s go get Halibel’s alcohol before he raises a fit.”

“Oh, I already have it,” Subaru brought out a huge bottle of what looked to be rice wine from under his shirt.

Anastasia raised her eyebrow before mentally slapping herself.

I must have been really out of my mind back then. Of course, it was an excuse.

“Let’s go home then.”

“Wow Ana. You’re really losing your touch. I even used one of your merchant tools against you back there.”

“Wait what are you-“Anastasia mentally slapped herself again, “Offer something big so they’d accept a smaller offer! You cheeky little shit!” She swiped at him.

I don’t even remember teaching him that!

He dodged, “Learned from the best!”

Our relationship changes once again, from friends to now, something special? I don't know. Maybe it will be romantic. Maybe it won't be. But at the very least, I'll see where my greed takes me.

They skipped and play-fought all the way back to the house. Only to find a huge hole in the front wall with food scattered everywhere. Also, Halibel and Zarestia were having a stand-off while blaming each other.

“…”

“…Let’s go eat at a restaurant.”

 

Notes:

EN: Spirits always seemed interesting to me. They are simultaneously some of the most childish characters in re:zero but also have depth and wisdom that makes sense considering how long they live. I think that's why I've written Tia like this.

EN2: This chapter had a lot of monologues. Maybe a bit too much. But I felt it was necessary, at the very least it was fun to write. Anyway, congratulations, the anabaru relationship has reached: 'undefined' relationship.

EN3: Also I mentioned this briefly in my other fic, I have not responded to many comments since last time, and that's because I was focused on writing competition submissions. This shall be rectified soon! Also, more blog posts coming.

Chapter 8: Interlude: A Glimpse into Rapture

Summary:

A glimpse into an unfathomable possibility...

Notes:

This interlude was made in celebration of hitting over 1000 kudos. This was originally part of my notes and plans. It was never meant to be released as I thought there was too many details I didn't want to show just yet. But I think you guys earned this. Have fun analyzing.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Probability. Possibility. An unthinkable present. In the web of entropy, there lies quantum events where any type of scenario can reasonably occur. If it could occur, then it is possible. Then, in that case, what is the probability that one’s ability to return does not occur? Low. Extremely low. Yet, if it did, what would be the unthinkable present left for those that remain. What would rise from those who remain?

 

Here lies that unthinkable present.

 

 

 

“…I… don’t want… to die.”

 

Anastasia rose from the abyss with a start, sweating heavily. She felt a pain in her head and the room felt too dark.

Where… am I?

“Ah, you have finally woken up.”

Anastasia startled, looked to her side to see an old woman in peasant robes whittling a piece of wood. It looked like an unfinished caricature of a child. She stopped carving and placed the knife onto the dresser.

“…Who are you?” Anastasia asked with suspicion. She tried to sit up but the pain made her flinch.

“Calm down girl, you’re in a safe place. You shouldn’t move too much either, your eye is still recovering. Well, what’s left of it.”

My eye? Wait…

She slowly reached for the right side of her face. Trying to grab at the source of her vision. And found nothing.

The room wasn’t dark because the light was spread unevenly, it was because she had become a cyclops overnight.

What… what happened? I remember being in the carriage with- shit! Where’s-

“Subaru!” Anastasia started moving frantically, ignoring the pain, “Where is he?!”

She tried climbing out of the bed but only managed to barely creep out before falling to the floor. The pain was excruciating but she needed answers.

The old woman silently watched and simply stood up and gently helped her to her feet.

“…You should worry about yourself more.”

Lacking patience, “…Where is the boy who was with me?”

The old lady stood pensive, seconds passed as Anastasia’s worry grew, until finally, “Follow me.”

As they began to walk, Anastasia nearly tripped again next to the dresser, slamming into it to prevent a fall. The old lady watched her for a second before offering her shoulder. Limping, Anastasia used the old lady’s shoulder as support and walked with her through the dilapidated house, until they came upon a door at the end of the hallway. As they walked, tattered memories flowed through Anastasia.

It was just a day after leaving the capital. They were riding next to a forest area. Subaru suddenly had a seizure or something. And then, something sharp hit her skull. And everything went black. Next thing she remembers is Subaru carrying her, bleeding profusely. Darkness came and went. She remembers talking. About something. But only fragments remained.

“Just wait a moment,” the old lady struggling to grab her keys woke Anastasia out of memory lane. The woman grabbed an ornate key and opened the door at the end of the hallway.

As they entered, Anastasia noticed how nice the room was, despite some dust and cobwebs here and there. Children’s clothes scattered about: a green shirt, a blue blouse, a pink dress. There were children’s toys, dolls and wooden puppets, placed neatly on the dresser as well as a small bookshelf with three books. She recognized one of them, she read it to Hetaro when he was younger.

A story of a doll brought to life.

She also noticed a body occupying the bed.

A body.

Body.

No.

The old woman helped Anastasia get closer to the bed.

As they edged closer, the body became more and more visible. Under the thin sheets, what looked like tablecloth, was a thin emaciated body. There were blotches of blood scattered here and there, especially near the bottom half of the body. No movement, no breathing, just a stale silence. Nothing.

“I’m sorry dear. We tried everything we could. He was most likely dead when he collapsed outside the village. He must’ve ran so far to get you here. His legs were practically gone when we found both of you.”

The old woman looked at Anastasia, under the soft glow of moonlight from the window, her face was expressionless. The worry that was clearly seen from the merchant beforehand, was gone. Replaced with an eerie calm. A nostalgic façade she was familiar with. The old woman looked to the nightstand that had a picture of a younger woman with two children. She sighed.

“…”

“…I’ll let you say your goodbyes.”

Seconds passed.

Anastasia stood there looking at the body, frozen as a statue.

She barely heard the creak and soft slam of the door closing.

Why?

Why?

Why?

Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why?

CREAK.

Anastasia flinched, her head slowly rotated to her right. Sitting there, with an expression that was almost melancholic, was a beautiful white fox. A fox she was familiar with.

“…Echidna.”

The fox flinched in surprise as well, not expecting recognition, “So, it seems we have met before.”

“…”

“…Apologies, that was not what I meant to say as a greeting. I wanted to express my condolences.”

“…Why?”

Echidna looked pensive, “It is never easy losing people. I didn’t want to leave-“

“No,” the merchant’s words became venomous, “I meant, why are you here? After all this time.”

“…”

“…”

“I…also, wanted to grieve. But not alone.”

Alone. I’ve been alone. You left me alone.

“…”

“Too much loss tonight. I wanted to make sure there was no more.”

Why were you not there when I woke up? Where have you been? Now? Of all times now? Disgusting.

“…”

“I was accompanying a… friend. They had something they wished to accomplish. Unfortunately, that wish has now become impossible,” Echidna said as she looked at the body in the bed.

Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting. Disgusting.

“…Apologies. It was not my place to interrupt your own grieving. I will-“

“Disgusting.”

The fox tilted her head in surprise, “Pardon?”

The merchant grit her teeth, her eyes widened and frantic. Anastasia shuffled in pain towards her old friend.

“You. Disgust me. You come back. After all this time. And act like you can just make it all back to normal. That things could remain the same as they once were! Is that how low you think of me?! To be cast aside and returned when it’s convenient! Disgusting. Immoral. Putrid.”

Anastasia’s façade broke. Every part of her felt like it was breaking. She got closer to the fox.

The fox took a step back, “Child. Please calm down.”

That only enraged the merchant even more, her eyes manic, “You will not tell me what I can feel. You have no right. No semblance of control over me! Never. NEVER! Never. Never. Never. Never. Never. Never. Never. Never. Never. Never. Never. You won’t ever control me again. Disgusting. I feel so disgusted I ever let you do so. You ruined me. Ruined everything. And you left without a care. Without a thought. Without remorse. Leaving me alone to suffer.”

She winced in pain, her body felt horrid and demented.

“I’m sorry. I do not remember-“

Swing! Thunk!

The fox was cut off by the knife that barely missed, sailing past her head, before being lodged in the floor behind her.

“OF COURSE YOU DON’T REMEMBER! I was forgotten!” Anastasia grabbed her head, gazing downward, gripping her hair, scratching with every word, “You forgot. Ricardo forgot. Mimi forgot. Hetaro forgot. Tivey forgot. Julius forgot. Everyone forgot me! And I was alone! Alone to deal with it all! Nobody left to care!! Left with my Od depleted, in a feeble attempt to escape!!! All for nothing. Nothing remained! I had to scrounge through the disgusting trash left by everyone. Again! Left by those who once cared! Now, nobody cared! Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody. Nobody!”

She fell to the floor, on her knees, and screamed. And screamed. And screamed. Until her throat died.

Until a single thought pierced the insanity.

No.

Somebody did care.

One boy.

A body.

Body.

Anastasia suddenly stopped, her hands slowly left her head with trails of lilac, she looked up to find the fox gone. Left alone once again.

No, not alone.

She looked back at the body that lay on the bed before her. She slowly crawled back by its side and laid her hand on its chest.

“…You didn’t. You remembered. You didn’t have to. But you cared. You cared for me when no one else did. And what did I do? I cursed you. Cursed you to throw your life away. Because I didn’t want to die. Because I told you I didn’t want to die. Why? WHY?! Why did I curse you. To give you a reason to care. To make you attached to me. And I left you to rot. And I will now have to leave you as a rotting corpse…”

The merchant began to cry from her remaining eye.

No. Her hand gripped the sheet. No. No. The grip tightened until her hand became bone white. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.

She flung the sheet off the body. It looked like him. It had his features. His face, his body, his eyes. All remained. But his legs? His feet? Mangled. As if they were torn apart in desperation. Dirt and grass clung to his clothes, streaking vertically. Dried blood drenched his corpse.

Silently, she crawled into the bed and wrapped her arms around it. It was cold. Lacking the warmth she so desperately craved. That she remembered being there only a day ago. An eternity ago.

I want him. I want him back. To pay him back for his kindness. Why did you care? Because I made you care for me? I tried to control you, used your empathy. I cursed you. I want to take him back. To not curse him with such a disgusting wish. A wish to save my disgusting life. To give back what he gave me. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back. Give him back.

She felt a warm sensation cascade down her face. It smelled of salt and iron. All originating from the brand-new gaping abyss in her head.

I don’t want to be alone. Don’t leave me. Please. I can’t be alone. I just can’t.

The merchant cried silently, begging.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

And something responded.

Suddenly, Anastasia felt warmth. An unusual warmth. As if the coldness was seeping away. And then she felt a sensation. As if her very being was connecting to it. To the body. And as she felt such a connection, she felt an impossible presence. It was as if it wrapped its arm around her. No. It was possible. Arms wrapped around her. His arms. But not his. A refreshing imitation. That nostalgic feeling she only felt just a day ago. It was back. A dream come true, from the nightmare of reality.

Rapture.

She smiled. She wept sanguine tears. She sang. She couldn’t stop smiling and crying. An unyielding joy born from a disgusting origin.

No longer alone. Never alone. I will never let you be alone again. Never left in this disgusting rot.

Anastasia embraced the body, embraced the dream. And never came back.

 

 

As the dawn rose, a knight was left horrified by what he found. A corpse of an old woman was discovered in her home. What was particularly peculiar was the state of her remains. Desiccated. As if her very essence was drained from her.

A legend was born that day. Stories in Lugunica spoke of a vampire that stalked the night. That it would be invited into homes, only to drain the blood and life of those who inhabited them.

Stories in Gusteko spoke of villages disappearing overnight, half of the inhabitants gone while the other half left as dried husks. Stories in Vollachia spoke of the dead rising back up, endlessly marching after a spirit in white. Stories in Kararagi spoke of a demon walking the streets, whole businesses and companies vanishing once the sun died.

Yet, all of the stories had one similar detail. Of a pale one-eyed witch accompanied by a dark phantom.

Forever hand in hand.

Never one without the other.

Never alone again.

Notes:

EN: I've always wondered what happens after a loop. Does the world reset or does it continue? The novel never concretely specified, only provided glimpses through the trials. So here is a glimpse, a peak into hell. A possibility that could happen, despite how low the chances are. Where the worst combination of variables occur. Those are how I interpret IF routes. Not just paths where Subaru made the wrong decision. But paths where they are combined with the worst possible outcomes of constants and variables. The dregs of entropy.

EN2: I may do more of these. Maybe every milestone, perhaps at 2000 kudos or possibly 250 bookmarks. Glimpses into possibilities.

Chapter 9: Three Necessary Conversations

Summary:

In this chapter, we check-in on a certain Sword Saint. Meanwhile, the Banan Gang have a chat.

Notes:

Hello again! This chapter is a bit longer than usual, as there is a lot to cover.

Hope you enjoy!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Hero. Monster. The strongest. Those are the titles many spoke of when describing the one called The Sword Saint. But there was one title only few dared to call him, the one he cherished the most: friend.

Yet, despite his attachment toward the latter, he could only really accept the former as fitting for someone such as him. For how he can call himself a friend, when he betrayed that very friend’s trust.

I should have been more assertive with Felix. I should have focused on pleading for his release rather than my missions. I should have checked on him more often.

These were the thoughts running through Reinhard’s head as he ran through the events he had missed in the last few months. The events he surmised from the bits and pieces he learned from the citizens of the Capital.

Of how an Archbishop of the Witch Cult by the name of Subaru Natsuki, escaped from the prison tower, and absconded to who knows where.

Of how the Archbishop made a fool of the knights of Lugunica.

Of how the Archbishop was a monster who was torn apart and tortured yet was able to completely demolish the guards of the prison with ease.

It was the last rumor that greatly concerned him. Torn apart. Tortured. He was not aware of this. He should have been aware. He is the Sword Saint. Why did he not check on the alleged Archbishop, the one who desperately called him a friend, not once after their first meeting?

No, he knows.

 

 

“Felix-dono, I do not know what you are expecting to gain from this, but it is a lost cause. He is not a Witch Cultist. You can see it in his eyes. We’ve seen how they act.”

“What if he’s lying but hiding it? You don’t know what I’ve seen. What if he has a power that could blend in? Remove his memories for a certain period of time? Maybe he doesn’t even look like that normally…”

“…Be that as it may, you shouldn’t be rash-“ Wilhelm noticed his presence finally, “You. What are you doing here?”

Reinhard bowed, “…Honorable Grandfather.“

“Reinhard van Astrea,” Wilhelm stood stilted.

Both sword masters gazed uncomfortably at each other. All three men were currently standing outside the cell holding the supposed Archbishop.

“…Answer my question. Shouldn’t you have greater duties to attend to?”

Reinhard shook his head, “This is a matter of grave importance. I must speak to the prisoner.”

Wilhelm raised his eyebrow, “Why? Haven’t you already done so?”

Felix intervened, “Ah, Reinhard claims he is a friend of his.”

Wilhelm began to bristle and focus intensely on Reinhard, “What do you mean, friend? Do you care for him?”

The Sword Saint was confused, “Yes but-“

“You care for him. Why? What makes him so special?”

The old man looked intensely at Reinhard, as if his answer would decide everything.

I cannot make a mistake here. I should focus on calming Grandfather’s worries.

“…It is my duty as a Sword Saint to protect the public and its people. I need to make sure he is not a threat and placate any worries of his association to the Witch Cult.”

That was the wrong answer, as Wilhelm’s expression twisted into a complex mix of anger, disgust, and sadness.

I do not know what I did wrong.

“…Leave Sword Saint. You have bigger worries than a measly interrogation,” Wilhelm said as he turned his back on his former grandson.

“Grandfather-“

Wilhelm’s voice was cold, “Enough. We have our duties. Yours and mine are unrelated to this. Leave now or I will escort you out.”

…Perhaps, I should come back tomorrow.

 

 

Tomorrow never came. Once he left the tower, he was thrust with a multitude of missions by the Sage Council. Sent on a wild goose chase around the country trying to find the Witch Cult or a solution to those afflicted with the Cursed Dragon’s Blood and Sleeping Beauty Syndrome from the Priestella incident.

Only to find nothing but dead ends.

The one time he returned, he was still unable to see the Archbishop. Felix barred him, stating that the Witch Cultist interrogation was progressing well and the Sword Saint was not needed.

That was a lie. The wind surrounding Felix whistled falsehoods. Just like he did before in front of the Sage Council. Why didn’t he confront Felix then? Why did he confront him now?

The answer was the same for both questions but originated from different sources: they called him friend.

Felix did. And so, he gave him the benefit of the doubt.

Subaru did. And so, he couldn’t leave him be.

But he did. The Sword Saint left his friend without care. Abandoned in a prison.

And for the first time, Reinhard got angry.

Reinhard didn’t remember what happened next. He does. He chooses not to.

By the end of the conversation, Felix looked frightened. Looked at him like he was a monster. And then his grandfather came. Reinhard knew he must have looked like a monster. And so, he quickly left. Deciding not to burden his grandfather anymore.

A monster. That’s all he was. A monster disguised-

“Would you stop moping!” A loud voice struck him out of his mental spiral, paired with a physical strike to his temple ala kick.

Reinhard blinked his eyes rapidly. He did not realize he went straight towards his office after returning.

Quickly stopping the foot with a gentle block, “Lady Felt? Apologies, I must have not heard you come in.”

Felt huffed, “You idiot. You’ve been gone for weeks. And then I find you fucking spacing out like a moron in your office,” she then glared up, “And will you let go of my foot?!”

Reinhard obliged, “I apologize once again Lady Felt, it was uncouth of me to ignore you once I had returned from my mission. As your knight, I should have reported to you immediately.”

Felt just got angrier, “That’s not the problem here! You’ve been acting all out of it, even when you came back. What’s with you?”

Ah, I made a mistake again.

“Apologies-“

“Apologies, apologies, apologies!” Felt said back in an annoying imitation of Reinhard, “Stop saying sorry. If you say sorry one more time, I’m going to kick you straight in the balls. Now, tell me: what’s wrong?”

“…Apolo-“he caught himself as Felt raised a finger at him, daring him to finish, “I mean, I believe… I have made a terrible mistake.”

Felt raised an eyebrow, “You?”

Reinhard nodded grimly, “Yes. I have. I believe my negligence, my sloth, led to an innocent man be wrongly accused of being a witch cultist. And as a result, he was tortured under my watch.”

Felt narrowed her eyes, “Explain.”

And thus, Reinhard went over every detail: how he discerned that the one called Subaru Natsuki was innocent, how he found Felix lying to the Sage Council but neglected confronting him out of friendship, how he left Subaru to an unjust fate because he trusted Felix, and how he ran away from his responsibility because he was a monster.

Felt now looked pensive, while Reinhard thought back to the last thing his… friend said to him.

“Thanks Reinhard. I know it’s a lot to swallow, but I am telling you the truth. I’m not a witch cultist. Once I get out of here, I’ll show you. We’ll be the best of friends, just like before!”

No, he wasn’t his friend. A friend would have tried their hardest to help. A friend wouldn’t have abandoned him like that. Reinhard did not deserve such a title.

Felt broke the silence, “So, when are we going to go find him?”

Reinhard blinked, “Go find him?”

Felt just snorted, “Well yeah. It’s not like we can just leave this be. Though I guess we gotta kill those fuckers who tortured him first,” Felt then placed her hand on her chin, “Felix will be hard to kill since he’s Blue and all. But I’m sure we can find a way to justify it.”

“Lady Felt-“

The former thief ignored him and simply snapped her fingers, “Actually, let’s find him first. Then we can prove his innocence and then kill the bastards. Maybe get a few of them to confess if we promise them leniency. I know the cat boy is the best healer or whatever. But I doubt he can escape if everyone throws him under the carriage. We can then assassinate the fuckers in secret later.”

“Lady-“

She kept ignoring him and nodded to herself, “Yeah, that works. Find your friend, prove he’s innocent, execute the dick heads. We should probably bring some more people with us just in case. Maybe bring the three idiots with us, it’ll be good practice for them. Or at the very least they can help bury any bodies.”

“Lady Felt,” before he could be ignored once more, he stepped forward in front of her, “I do not think it would be wise for us to do so.”

She raised an eyebrow, “Why?”

“Barring the amount of evidence we would need, the Archbishop may be outside the country by now. And unfortunately, due to the law pertaining to my presence as a deterrent, I am unable to travel beyond our borders, at least without strict regulations. The Sage Council would not allow this.”

Felt scoffed, “Who cares what they think? We’ll just do it in secret. Besides, are you really just going to let this all blow over? What do you really want to do?”

Reinhard held stern, “It is my duty as a Royal Knight of Lugunica to care. I cannot create an international crisis just because of my failure. It would lead to more problems and the citizens would suffer for my actions.”

Just like Subaru.

Felt glared at him, “You didn’t answer my last question.”

“…It is my duty as the Sword Saint-“

She interrupted him with a fist to the face, which he soundly blocked, “Oh my Od! Enough with the Sword Saint knight bullshit!”

Felt got in his face and pointed her finger at him, “What. Do. You. Want? None of this ‘honor’ or ‘duty’ crap you shove down my throat half the time. What does Reinhard, the person, want?”

The Sword Saint didn’t know what to say. He didn’t know what he wanted. He did. He just didn’t know if he deserved it.

“…”

Felt sighed, “Listen. I only barely know what’s going on, but even someone like me can tell this situation is a fucking mess. Now I understand why everyone has been freaking out: the knights and the council are probably knee deep in shit, shit of their own making. I bet they’re planning on sweeping this under the rug as much as possible.”

Reinhard grimaced, “I do not know what the intentions of the council and knights will be. Most likely, they will do what is required of them.”

He knew. But he couldn’t confirm or deny. He had to hold faith in their honor. As expected of him.

And Felt could see right through him, “You know that’s a bunch of dragon shit. They believe in that whole ‘status quo above all’ type of thing. They care more about their clean image over actually doing a damn thing…” Felt continued to grumble as she looked away.

Knock. Knock.

A soft voice pierced through the door, “Reinhard-sama, Felt-sama. A visitor has come looking for the Sword Saint. He said it was urgent.”

Reinhard looked toward his candidate, whose face screamed “This isn’t over.”

He cleared his throat, despite having no reason to, “Thank you Grassis, please tell him I will be there promptly.”

He then refocused on his Lady, “Felt-sama, please don’t mind me and return to your lessons.”

Felt flinched, “…You never fucking forget a thing don’t you.”

Reinhard chuckled softly, “It is my duty to remember your schedule.”

As Reinhard made his way to the exit, Felt gave him one last piece of advice, “Rein.”

He stopped at the door, looking back slightly, “Yes, my Lady?”

“…Your sense of duty is fucking annoying. And you’re an idiot.”

Reinhard smiled and was about to leave, but Felt finished, “But don’t lie to yourself. Sometimes, just. Do what you want, alright?”

He paused, and saw Felt was looking away from him. Not knowing what to say, he went to welcome their visitor.

 

 

Boss Lady. Dragon Candidate. Conniving bitch. All titles familiar to the one who was rumored to be soon renowned by the epithet: Great Businesswoman. But there was one title few dared to call her, the one she dreaded the most: weirdo. Why?

“Ana, you have to admit, your kind of weird.”

Because those who were calling her by that title had no right to do so.

Anastasia turned her head slowly towards the number one source of her irritation, “Pot.”

Almost like a reflex, Subaru replied, “Kettle.”

“Su makes a point, you are one strange bitch,” Tia said as she dipped a whole appa in teriyaki sauce before eating it. And here was source number two.

Anastasia stared at her in disdain.

It had been a few days since they officially moved into the shared tenement house. Tia took over the guest room while Subaru and Anastasia shared the main bedroom. As per their deal, Subaru made Hal-san a generous helping of tartar sauce for the month. Which spiked Tia’s interest, as she too wanted a special sauce made by Subaru. Anastasia punched him in the gut before he could say anything stupid.

And so, with some trial and error, Subaru recreated teriyaki sauce.

Anastasia huffed, “I am not strange. Subaru is strange!”

She pointed at him, “He puts mayo on everything. We are not the same. For example: toast with jam and butter, great with mayo. Toast with meat and jam, not great with mayo,” Anastasia pleaded her case.

Her third source of irritation, who was slamming down tartar sauce like a beverage, did not rule in her favor, “That is highly specific and weird Ana-bo.”

“Yeah, Ana-bo~,” Subaru said in a sing-along voice.

Anastasia glared at Subaru, “He eats mayo straight out of a bowl, like soup.”

Subaru nodded, as if that was a sane thing to do, and started slurping from his bowl.

“That is also, extremely weird and specific Su-san.”

“Yeah, Su-san~,” revenge is petty, and Anastasia has no shame.

Subaru looked betrayed, “Yeah! Well!” he pointed at Halibel, “You chase tartar sauce with liquor!”

Halibel just shrugged, “Yep yep, that’s a totally normal thing to do.”

“No it isn’t!” “No it ain’t!” Both stars screamed indignantly.

Meanwhile, the murderously docile woman just gnawed on her glazed apple, “All three of you are weirdos, I’m the only sane one.”

The trio of weirdos stared at the spirit. In succession,

“Silent but deadly.”

“Family jewels appraiser.”

“Ugly.”

She slammed her hands on the dining table, “Hey, I can fucking kill you all, ya know?!”

Anastasia just snorted as she dipped her toast in Subaru’s bowl, “You say that every time. But you never do. Guess you don’t have the family jewels for it.”

Anastasia dodged an appa core sent straight for her face. Subaru wasn’t so lucky.

“Oi! No throwing food at the dining table,” Subaru reprimanded her. Tia just stuck her tongue out at him.

Subaru used the age-old carrot and stick, “No more teriyaki sauce for a week.”

Tia’s eyes widened, before sulking, “…Sorry, I won’t do it again Su.”

Anastasia giggled before being pinched by Subaru, “Ow! Hey!”

He gave an annoyed look, “Don’t laugh, you provoked her.”

She pouted at him, “Says you, you called her a fart.”

Subaru shrugged, “Yeah well she didn’t get offended.”

Tia, who quickly turned back to infuriated, “That’s what that means?!”

Halibel just laughed while Subaru deflected with his thumb, “He called you ugly.”

Tia recalculated her glare’s direction toward the old wolf.

The playboy choked, “Su-san, how could you, my favorite drinkin’ buddy, betray me?!” He arched his back dramatically.

“Hal-san, I don’t even drink with you. Also, how is it that when we go to any bar, you always only find married women to flirt with?” he said as he swiped some toast from Anastasia’s plate.

“Su-san. One does not need to drink to be a drinkin’ buddy. It’s the presence that matters. And secondly, I am cursed with attractin’ forbidden romance,” wiping a fake tear from his eye.

The stars rolled their eyes while Tia raised a hand menacingly, “Maybe I should ‘appraise Hal’s family jewels.’ Permanently. All the women of Banan would thank me.”

Anastasia took Subaru’s cup and poured some of his milk into her coff, “It’s not worth it Tia. Besides, you don’t know where they’ve been, you might catch something,” she took a sip.

“Oof! Accosted from all sides! Su-san, you’re on my side, right?” Halibel used his best puppy dog eyes.

Subaru just smiled, “Sorry Hal-san, for the sake of my sanity, we may have to neuter you.”

“Gah! Su-san, don’t take Ms. Egghead’s side! What happened to that bro-code you told me all about?”

“Egghead?” Tia looked confused, until suddenly one of Halibel’s clones came up from behind and pulled her bangs up. It was truly a fivehead teetering over to six. And definitely in the form of an egg, at least vaguely.

Tia cut the clones head off with a flick of the wrist and shook with rage.

The Shinigami stepped onto the table with one foot, oozing a slight aura of malice, “For the safety of all Kararagi females, hand over your balls mutt.”

Halibel not deterred in the slightest, also stepped onto the table, his eyes glinting dangerously, “Try it if you dare, Shini-ugly, these jewels are the strongest of Kararagi!”

The most dangerous individuals in hundreds of miles glared at each other.

The stars side-eyed each other and then sighed. Subaru took to Tia’s side while Anastasia took to Halibel’s.

“Tartar sauce. One month.”  “Teriyaki sauce. One week.”

Both walking calamities froze before sheepishly returning to their seat.

“Sorry Ana-bo.” “My bad, Su.”

The stars settled back down with their newfound companions.

“Wait, what were we talking about again?” Anastasia looked toward Subaru.

Subaru contemplated, “How you’re the weirdest out of all of us?”

She swiped at him, “Not that you little shit. Before.”

“Ohhhh, about establishing the company?”

She snapped her fingers at him, “There we go. We need to prioritize distributing our first batch of product. We should also consider our brand name and how we will go about expansion.”

Their product was simple: a variety of sauces for individuals to enjoy with their food. Subaru already successfully recreated mayonnaise, tartar sauce, and teriyaki sauce. Subaru was planning and testing more condiments such as hot sauce, ketchup, mustard, sweet relish, ranch, and many others.

“Hmmm, perhaps you and Su-san can buy a stall at the festival?”

“The festival? Oh, the rain festival! Of course,” Anastasia smashed her fist onto her palm, “I almost forgot. The festival of storms should be happening soon. That should be the best place for us to start, we can get the best outreach.”

Subaru nodded while Tia looked pensive, Anastasia caught wind of the mood change, “Something wrong Tia?”

Tia blinked and then scowled, “…It’s nothing. Just. Bad memories. You’re going to be giving out stuff at the festival, right? Good. The mutt and I will be guarding you both. Tia-Two might strike then.”

Bad memories, huh? I’ll put that away for later, right next to Subaru’s messed up love life. Seriously: tortured by your crush, abandoned by your other crush, and having your crush not return your feelings for nearly a year and a half? He needs better taste in women.

“Huh, I thought we settled on callin’ her Dark Tia,” Halibel said lazily.

Subaru nudged Anastasia, his face nonverbally asking, “Everything alright? You made a weird face right then.”

Anastasia blinked and then returned a soft smile that meant, “It’s okay. Just had a weird thought. Nothing bad.”

Subaru smiled as well and squeezed her arm lightly, “Okay, I just wanted to check,” he then returned his attention back to the overall conversation.

Her heart felt very warm. Ever since their little talk, it feels like her and Subaru are becoming more in sync every day. It wasn’t a bad feeling. At least, she thinks it isn’t.

Tia shook her head, “That’s so lame. Dark Tia? At that point, why not call her Black Tia? Evil Tia. Psycho Tia.”

Halibel waved his hand, “I think ya mistakin’ her for yourself. Psycho Tia sounds more like you than her.”

Tia was about to step over and choke the life out of him until Anastasia intervened once more.

She cleared her throat, “Okay! We’ve settled on how to start distributing our product, by making a big wave at the festival. Now what about the actual stall as well as brand? We can’t just sell sauces themselves, and we need a name to call ourselves.”

It has to be something new, something that really stands out. Hoshin was a great name because it was bold, as if stating, “We are as great as the original founder.” This new company needs to have the same impact.

“Oh,” this time it was Subaru’s turn to slam a fist on his palm, “Back home we used to have markets that would sell spice mixtures by handing out free samples. They would mix it on top of rice and customers could try different combinations.”

Anastasia nodded excitedly, “I like that idea! We should use food that pairs well with all of the sauces. Oh, I know! Those furentch freyes you made for us; do you think you can make large batches of them?”

Subaru also nodded with enthusiasm, getting into it, “Oh that’s perfect! Used to have arguments with people online about what condiment was the best with french fries. I might need some new equipment, tatoes, and a lot of cooking oil, but I can probably set it up like McDonalds.”

She raised an eyebrow, “MacDawnald?”

“Oh yeah, I never explained fast food, did I? Okay so first off, imagine Ros-chi but like yellow, red, and somehow looking less like a sexual predator.”

Anastasia grimaced, “Ohhkayy? Not the worst nightmare I’ve imagined.”

While Subaru kept explaining the intricacies of clown-related dining, Tia and Halibel just watched with varying degrees of amusement.

The wolf chuckled, “There they go. Off in their own little world again. Once they start bouncin’ off ideas and tellin’ stories, it never ends.”

Tia just nodded, “They should really just become mates already.”

Halibel choked, “T-tia, you know what that means right?”

Tia looked at him annoyed, “Of course. They’ll basically become inseparable. Well, more inseparable than they already are somehow. And soon enough, we’ll be seeing little black and purple babies vomiting everywhere.”

Halibel sighed in relief, “Oh-kay good. I was afraid I would have to start explainin’ somethin’ I really didn’t want to.  Wait. Then why did you take the guest room next to them?”

Now she looked at him confused, “Why does where I sleep matter?”

Dumbfounded, the wolf started connecting the dots, and started laughing, “Ohohohoh. Hahahahaah! That’s too good!”

Angry Tia returns, “Hal! What’s so funny?! Explain why you started laughing! What did I say that was so funny? I’ll kill you if you don’t start explaining right now!” She said as she started shaking Halibel vigorously.

The playboy just laughed harder in response. He was looking forward to the next month. Or maybe even months, as he doubted his contract would end so soon. His dual star employers were too greedy. And he was having way too much fun already.

 

 

“… And that was all the guard told me.”

Reinhard’s visitor was one of the few people who would call him by the title he did not deserve. The Finest Knight, Julius Juukuulius had to come to him to exchange information about what occurred in the prison tower. It did not look good.

Julius had been investigating everything that happened that night and beforehand. All signs pointed toward manipulation and inner corruption. But nothing concrete. At least until a certain guard confessed.

The guard laid everything out: Felix mentally spiraled. At first, interrogations were normal. Until a week later, Felix resorted to torture methods to coax anything out of him. To hide his actions, he purposely switched in guards who were heavily affected by Witch Cult activity. He also paid and swore them to secrecy as an extra measure. Felix only brought Wilhelm when Reinhard came to visit, and even then, he always made sure Wilhelm was busy with camp operations and never knew anything related to the inner machinations of the prison tower.

“I asked the guard why he suddenly confessed. He should have known this could lead to his execution.”

Julius’s face screamed sympathy, “All he replied was, ‘I found out that night that my best friend of 15 years betrayed me. That, because I was so stupid, I could have lost my sister. And you know who helped me? The supposed Witch Cultist. Sure, I might die. But I’ll do everything I can to pay him back. It’s the bare minimum I should do.’”

Reinhard didn’t know what to feel. Guilt. Regret. Anger. Disappointment. All of it directed towards himself.

Still, he had a job to fulfill, “…What shall be done with Felix?”

Julius looked conflicted, “He will be punished, with extreme prejudice. This isn’t just a case of misguided intentions. He intentionally misused his privilege as a Royal Knight and Blue to torture information out of what was most likely an innocent man. If he somehow survives execution, he’ll never be allowed in Lugunica again.”

“Then, shall we get going? We can arrest him before nightfall.”

I have to do this.

Julius looked at him strangely.

“…Not just yet,” before Reinhard could retort, Julius raised his hand, “Trust me. While Felix is, no, was my friend, we have to think pragmatically. Without Felix, Crusch will die. He is spending every second staving off the curse, and I doubt anyone else could help with that.”

“That…I can agree with that. So, what shall we do now?” Reinhard looked toward his fellow knight for their next orders.

“...” Julius stared at Reinhard intensely.

“Julius?”

The Finest Knight’s eyes softened, he reached out and placed a hand on his friend’s shoulder, “Reinhard. Are you doing alright?”

What?

“What do you mean?”

“Oh please,” the knight chuckled, “While I may not be the most perceptive man, we’ve known each other for a while now that I can tell something is wrong. Your Divine Protections may hide it, but my instincts have gotten better at catching these kinds of things.”

Julius pointed toward his eyes, “I heard from somewhere that merchants often focus on their opponents’ eyes. Even the most stoic people can’t help but show their true feelings through habits and mannerisms. Eye twitches, changes in shape, pupil dilation: all tell-tale signs of something going wrong.”

“…What do my eyes tell you now?”

Julius gave a bittersweet smile, “They look similar to Felix’s. As if you can’t see the future anymore, guilt clouds your vision, so that you focus only on what you need to do.”

No. That is not true.

It was true. He was guilty. He felt guilty ever since the first day he left that prison. Because he didn’t just fail by leaving his friend to his fate, he failed beforehand.

“It was gluttony! That rat bastard, Archbishop of Gluttony. I think he ate my name or something, it’s how he stole Crusch’s memories and put Rem into a coma. Reinhard, you need to get me out of here. I was a knight of the Emilia camp, maybe someone could recognize me.”

He forgot his friend. He was at Priestella. He should have been there to help his friend. He failed him once and he failed him again. He didn’t have the courage to speak out against Felix or the Sages or his fellow knights. He didn’t deserve his title, friend or position as the Sword Saint.

“Julius… I,” his Divine Protections were helping calm his emotions, through sheer force of will he pushed them aside, “I-I, do not know what to do.”

He needed to feel this. No, he wanted to feel this.

Reinhard sat down, putting his hands in his face, “I have failed. I have failed my Lady. You. Felix. My family. And worst of all, I have failed my friend, who put all his trust into me. I do not deserve my accolades, my role as the Sword Saint. How can a Sword Saint be proud of himself? When he can’t save anyone correctly.”

He didn’t cry. He couldn’t. He hasn’t cried since he was a child.

“…”

“…”

“Reinhard,” he felt Julius sit down next to them, “Remember when I told you about how my brother and I snuck outside when we were younger?”

Reinhard took his hands off his face, and turned to face his friend, “Of course. You told me how it was foolish of you for going against your parents’ orders.”

Julius chuckled, “Yes. I did. But that wasn’t the whole story. My brother was sick. He still gets sick, but his illness was fierce when he was younger. Even worse, he didn’t exactly like me. In order to get closer, I decided we would go have some fun outside together as brothers. That. Was a mistake. He was fine in the beginning, but his illness caught up, and he wouldn’t stop coughing. He survived but only barely, I was ashamed of myself. For being so irresponsible and taking him out just so he would like me.”

Julius looked at the ground pensively before smiling, “However, that was when my relationship with Joshua changed. Joshua warmed up to me greatly. I am still ashamed of myself, yet I can’t help but look back on that moment fondly. It was not only the beginning of my brotherhood, but also when I started taking my knight’s training seriously. Joshua looked up to me. I wanted to be someone he could feel safe around. Someone that he would be proud of. I wanted to be a knight who can stand tall despite his failures. I wanted to be a hero, like the characters I used to read about.”

He then looked towards Reinhard, with warm intent, “I might not know the extent to which you feel, but I know that staying guilty will solve nothing. I could have wallowed in my shame back then and never became a knight. That would have only hurt the ones I loved. Just like now, blaming yourself will lead nowhere. You may think you deserve punishment but that’s not how I see it. From what you said and what I know from the guards and Wilhelm, Felix intentionally made it as difficult as possible for you to check in on the prison. He was always prepared for your visits. And if you still think you deserve a just punishment, then I must share it.”

Reinhard raised an eyebrow, “Julius. You have done nothing.”

“I have. And that’s the problem. We are knights. Royal Knights. We should not be so negligent to not check on our fellows, especially ones we call friends. I should have checked-in on Felix instead of believing he could handle everything. I wasn’t a good friend. Neither was he. He should have talked to us instead of spiraling into insanity. We share equal blame for not communicating properly. I have failed him, just as he failed us. And if what you say is correct, I have failed another fellow knight by forgetting him as well. But I want to change that. I feel this is a sign to begin changing. The knights have been too complacent; we’ve let our positions sour us on properly improving as people. We shouldn’t let our prejudices cloud our judgement, otherwise events like this will only be repeated.”

Julius rose with purpose, he extended his hand down towards Reinhard, “Sir Reinhard van Astrea! I ask you: will you sit here as the innocent suffer?! Will you let corruption fester?! Will you stay your hand any longer?! Or will you come and help right the wrongs we have committed. Though you may have fallen, it is your duty to rise again, to bring about true justice. I ask you, my friend: What. Do. You! Want?!”

Seconds passed, as Reinhard absorbed every word. If Reinhard could cry, he would be sobbing right now.

What do I want? I don’t, no, I do know what I want. I’ve always known.

“…I want to be worthy of being a knight. I want to hold my head up high as the Sword Saint! To be worthy of wielding Reid. And most of all, I want to be a better friend, a true friend even if I might not deserve it,” he said as the Sword Saint took the hand of the Finest Knight and stood tall once more.

Julius patted his friend on the shoulder proudly, “As you have wished it, so it shall be!”

Reinhard laughed, genuinely, “Alright. So, what is our next course of action?”

“We must assault the Sage’s Watchtower.”

 

 

“…Pardon me Julius, did you say assault the Watchtower?”

“Haha! I know how it must sound but there is a reason for my insanity: Gluttony and Lust. Weeks ago, our mutual friend Otto Suwen, approached me with an offer to send an expedition towards the Pleiades Watchtower in search of a cure for those afflicted in Priestella. Naturally, I declined outright,”

Reinhard interrupted, “Plausible deniability is a knight’s best skill, as you always say.”

Julius grimaced, “That still doesn’t sound right. Anyways, yes. Julius the knight could not play favorites. However, Juli the mercenary can. And given that your Lady has always had friendly relations with the Emilia camp, I doubt there would be any problems with you joining. I've read your reports as well as previous expeditions: we will need as much firepower and strategic minds as possible to figure out a way into the tower. This is why we will wait until the Iron Fang returns before adventuring. As for why I believe this is our best course of action, it pertains to what you said earlier about our falsely imprisoned friend: his name was taken by Gluttony.”

Reinhard connected the dots finally, “If the Watchtower can help us reclaim the names of those who were lost, we may be able to help Subaru be remembered as a knight and thus prove his innocence fully.”

“It may not fully make up for our transgressions against him, but it is a start towards a better future.”

“But how we can find him? He would be most likely hiding in another country, being vigilant of any possible action that could reveal his whereabouts to us.”

Julius tapped his head, “I’ve already found a solution to that. Through my investigations, I’ve discovered that there was only one carriage that left the capital that night. As well as only one reported sighting of the escaped convict, when he mugged an innocent merchant of that very same carriage. I already checked the records, the woman came into the city under a false name and left under another: Natasha and Anastasia. She was also reported to have a thick Kararagi accent. There is a chance our mutual friend became a stowaway and hitched a ride back to Kararagi.”

“And you were given Hoshin Trading Company, based in Banan. You can use them to help search for Subaru!”

Julius nodded, “The company already has a very extensive information network. If we can find our friend, or maybe even the woman, we could possibly send him a message. Tell him that he has allies on his side. We would need to find a way to placate him, however. I doubt his time in custody would make him particularly trusting, especially towards knights such as us.”

Reinhard began to think, “Perhaps we send him help. We’ll send necessary subsidies: food, water, money, a safe place to live. We’ll rebuild a relationship slowly and give honest explanations for our actions.”

“It’s a start. Then, once our expedition to the Watchtower has concluded, we can send him a request for a meeting by proxy and return his name to him. Or if it is not possible, we can at least offer him sanctuary or a promise that he will be given assistance until his death.”

“…”

Julius noticed his hesitation, “What is it Reinhard? Trust me, I will not judge whatever it is you wish to say.”

“…I wish to meet him directly. Even though our laws prevent me from doing so, I want to meet the friend I have forgotten. To express my sins. To tell him how sorry I am for abandoning him. To assist him with everything I have. And to selfishly ask if we can rebuild a friendship once more.”

“…Then we are of a similar mindset. I wish to also express my emotions directly, to hopefully learn more about the friend I never knew I lost. Though Reinhard and Julius may not be able to cross the border, perhaps Juli and Reiny will.”

Both knights, bound by honor and brotherhood, smiled warmly at their resolve to fix their mistakes.

At least until the mood was interrupted by a sharp voice,

“For the love of Od, please do not call yourselves that! Those names fucking suck,” Felt said as she dropped down from her hiding place.

Julius was alarmed, “Lady Felt! Were you eavesdropping this entire time?”

She snorted, “Of course! You didn’t ask for privacy, so I assumed I could.”

He pinched his nose, “The assumption should have been that you cannot. Did you know she was here?”

Julius gazed at the Sword Saint, who never once got surprised by anything since he’s known him.
Reinhard raised his hands in defense, “Unfortunately, I am just as startled as you. I was unable to detect her.”

Julius was stunned, narrowed his eyes in suspicion, before looking back towards the Dragon Candidate, “Please do not do that again.”

Felt had a surprised expression which quickly changed to mischievous as she noticed Reinhard wink at her from behind Julius, “Nah.”

As Julius looked like he was about to have a stroke, Reinhard chuckled to himself.

He did notice Felt. He didn’t wish to expose her as he didn’t want her to get in trouble.

And maybe, just maybe, he wanted to try subverting the rules out of selfishness rather than a sense of duty for once. It would be a nice bit of practice before he breaks international law in the future.

Hopefully his friend is surviving somewhere, safe and sound.

 

 

“Hoshin Company 2.0,” our brightest black star offered.

Our pale star was not enthused, “Rejected. We would immediately get a cease-and-desist order.”

“You guys have that here too?! Great. Alright what about: ‘Ana’s Special Sauce.’”

“That’s disgusting. While I’m sure I can market that to a certain group of people, I am not basing our whole future on something so perverted.”

Tia raised her hand, “How about ‘Black & Purple Things & Stuff?’”

Anastasia pinched her nose, “Besides how informal that sounds, I don’t want to own a company that sounds like what I would call a bruise.”

Halibel was fanning himself on the floor, “I still think ‘Playboy’ would be a wonderful name.”

Trying her best not to scream, “And I told you, Subaru already explained what Playboy was from his home. Barring that, same reason as the second, no perverted shit!”

Subaru began rubbing Anastasia’s shoulders, trying to calm her down, “Okay, what about ‘Sunset Wilderness?’”

It was working, “…That’s better. Though it does hold connotations with Hoshin still, something I want to avoid.”

He raised an eyebrow, “Really? I thought you would still want it to, considering you said it helped market your original company.”

She shook her head, “I want this company to be a new start. And not only that, but it also needs to be something that involves us both. This isn’t just my company, it’s ours. And I want a name that reflects that.”

Subaru looked away, slightly blushing while Anastasia was ignorantly enjoying the massage.

Tia then bluntly broke the nice mood, “What about, ‘Two Humans Should Start Mating Already.’ Reflects you both perfectly.”

Anastasia felt her blood pressure spike.

Calm down. You can’t fight her. Even though you really want to. Don’t lower yourself to her level.

Halibel started laughing, “Oh! What about ‘What Happens In Banan, Stays In Banan?’”

Calm. Calm.

Tia did not stop, “Female Wants Male So Badly She Bends Over Every Possible Opportunity?”

Subaru choked. Anastasia snapped.

…Fuck it.

“How about, ‘Dumbass Woman Wants To Fondle Balls Constantly?’”

Instead of getting pissed, Tia just smiled like a hunter whose prey took the bait, “Female Gets Horny Every Night With Male.”

Anastasia’s vein was popping, “Stupid Woman Can’t Understand Sarcasm.”

“Female Likes Cuddling Male.”

“Looks Like Prostitute.”

“Flat Board.”

“OH, YOU BITCH-“

Subaru started backing away from the hurricane of insults being flung at each other and sat next to Halibel, who was laughing like a maniac.

Halibel flung an invisible tear towards Subaru, “I don’t know whatcha told Ana-bo back then, but she’s become so much funnier ever since ya did. Great job.”

Subaru grimaced and threw the tear back, “I don’t think I actually did anything. Tia is just skilled at pissing her off.”

“Don’t be jealous, you are already talented at it. And you’ll get to that point eventually with her. Happens to every married couple.”

Subaru blushed again and glared at the playboy, “We’re not married!”

Halibel laughed again and then muttered under his breath, “Give it a few months.”

“What was that?”

“Nothiiiinnnnnn’~.”

By the end of the night, they still hadn’t decided on a name. At the very least, they still had some time until the festival.

Notes:

EN: Originally, I envisioned the relationship between the four to be like Sloth IF. But then I realized, hang on, Subaru is much more developed here. He confronted his insecurities rather than run away previously. Plus, his initial meeting with Tia is far less antagonistic. Anastasia also does not have the same starting relationship with the others as Rem did. So, this is how I envisioned their dynamics to play out. Hope you enjoyed it as much as I did.

EN2: Also, I just noticed I have too many line breaks. It's how the chapter turned out but there will not be as many in the future.

You can also interact with me on posts. Youtube will be where I stream and hopefully interact with y'all in real time. I'm planning on doing a short stream on 5/12 1:30PM CST, so subscribe or join in on the stream if you have questions or want to chat. Otherwise, I'll be chilling and writing while music plays in the background. I'll probably have regular streams and will announce their days and times on twitter.
