Chapter 12: A Spirit's Resolve

Summary:

We take a step back and see what Beatrice's life has been like, ever since Priestella.

Notes:

Enjoy the chapter!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

There are a lot of people Betty hates. She hates the clown that took away her mother. She hates the other clown that spawned from her friend’s delusional obsession. She even hates the half-elf princess for taking up her brother’s attention.

But there is one person Betty hates the most.

Herself.

And such a feeling became more and more pronounced ever since those last days in Priestella.

 

“Where is he?!” The spirit was panicking as she ran through the ruins of what was once a thriving metropolitan area. She was currently searching for her beloved contractor, following the connection brought about by their contract.

“Subaru!” She was desperate, they had gotten separated ever since he went after the Archbishop of Greed. Gluttony escaped, and she had a sneaking suspicion where. He kept obsessively talking about her contractor and left before Felt brought the Star Staff.

She needed to get to her contractor before it was too late.

She needed to.

She.

 

What was she doing, again?

Beatrice slowed down as she observed her surroundings.

It had been a hard-fought battle. Unfortunately, she was unable to eliminate the Archbishop of Gluttony and was left trying to follow his trail. She had split off from the rest, as she felt responsible for this failure. She needed to take responsibility.

 

Speaking of responsibility, she wonders if the half-elf had finally freed herself from the clutches of the Archbishop of Greed. While she trusts that the Sword Saint would be able to save her, she felt some disappointment in the candidate for putting herself in the situation in the first place. They were supposed to be here to bring back her beloved Bubby, not tactlessly involving themselves in these kinds of situations.

 

They should have left immediately once the meeting with that weird child lover had gone sour. But no. They had to stay. They had to try again. They had to go to that stupid tower and get involved in Wrath’s schemes. It made no sense to her. Bringing Bubby back was the main priority, not whatever nonsense the grey one kept spewing.

Ah, how annoying, I suppose. Betty does not envy Bubby. If Betty had a contractor, they would be much more-

“Beako?!”

Beatrice stopped and looked towards the source of the voice. She raised her eyebrow before freezing in shock.

At first, the source looked to be an average boy with odd hair and scary eyes. His frame was also average. However, he had this natural affinity that drew her eyes to him. She couldn’t help it. Though, this was all insignificant compared to the incredibly dense amount of miasma the boy was exuding.

A witch cultist?! No, wait, he doesn’t look like one. His eyes, they don’t hold the insanity of the others. But… what if it’s a trick? His miasma is comparable to the Archbishops, Betty has to be careful.

While Beatrice was caught off guard, the boy looked relieved when he saw her, and approached her, “Beako, it’s good to see you! Sorry I’m late. I barely escaped from that Lye guy. He tried to do something to me but I- “

“Stay right there, in fact!” Beatrice lifted her hand and started channeling her mana.

The boy looked confused, “Beako? It’s me, Subaru,” his eyes then widened, “wait, I’m not Lust! I can prove it: your favorite type of food is sweets, your mother’s name is Echidna, and last year you were really lonely and tried to follow me into the bathroom,” he said as he lifted three fingers individually.

Beatrice was even more confused, and also extremely embarrassed, “Huh?! B-betty would never follow a boy into the bathroom. Also, how do you know about mother? Who are you?!”

The boy’s face morphed into an unreadable expression, he reached his hand out, “Beako it’s me, your Subaru. Don’t you remember me. I’m your contractor.”

He looked desperate.

Contractor? Impossible. Betty has no contractor. She has not found That Person yet. Obviously, this is just a lie, Betty does not even have a contract-

The spirit paused.

It was there.

Faint.

But it was there. A contract.

But there was no name paired with it other than hers.

What?

How?

Why?

She doesn’t understand. When did this happen? She checked, she did not have a contract before Priestella. Who? Who did she contract with? It isn’t possible for a spirit to have a contract with no name? Is it? No, it doesn’t make sense. How did she not notice? Was it after the fire? No, she checked. She kept checking. She checked an immeasurable amount of times after she left the library. Wait, why did she check so much back then? No, she remembers. It was because she. Wanted. To. No, wait. That doesn’t make sense. None of this makes sense. Is it him? Why doesn’t she remember?

No. Wait.

The connection pulled her towards him. Only a slight amount. But it connected her to him.

 

Beatrice’s eyes started to dilate, her breathing sped up.

No. No. NO. NO. NO.

“Beako?” The boy edged closer, only to be stopped.

“NO! Stop! Don’t get any closer. Who are you? How do you have a contract with Betty?! This is not possible, in fact. Betty would have remembered... Betty would not have forgotten!”

No, wait. Is it even him? There is no name! But the connection? Why isn’t there a name on there? Did Betty make a mistake? Did Betty forget?!

Her breathing quickened; she felt her head spinning. None of this made sense to her. How in the world could a spirit suddenly have a contract, out of nowhere?

Unless.

Did she fail?

Did she fail before she ever tried?

The boy looked like he was on the cusp of tears, but he tried stepping closer, “C-calm down Beako. Please. I think I know what’s going on.”

Beatrice kept hyperventilating, screaming louder and louder, “Answer my questions! How do you have so much miasma?! Are you a cultist?! An Archbishop?! Is this some cruel joke of an authority?!”

He looked to be in pain but he kept moving forward, “No… I’m not a witch cultist. I’m Emilia’s knight. I was here to help her get a glintstone for Puck. I’m not joking. I think Gluttony did something to me. He must have stolen my name, just like he did with Rem.”

Beatrice wasn’t listening at this point, her head was pounding, she felt like she was about to vomit. The boy took her silence as some sort of response, he tried to reach for her to calm her down.

And Beatrice reacted very badly, “Do not touch me, in fact!”

THUD!

 

She frantically touched his hand and drained his mana incredibly fast, knocking him out.

Beatrice stood there, shaking.

After a second of shock, she realized what she just did.

She threw herself next to the boy checking if he got hurt from falling, “No! B-betty is sorry, Betty did not mean to do that…”

She double checked every part of him. He had an odd outfit on, some scrapes here and there as well as bandages, his arm and leg looked strange, however. Dark and almost completely black with purple veins.

Nothing hidden.

Why did Betty do that? This… is he, my contractor? But the name is not on the contract. He mentioned Gluttony. Could it be that an authority did something? Betty is not sure.

She could wait for him to wake up. But what if he became extremely angry for what Beatrice did and lashed out? She could bring him back to the others, but what if he was a cultist? What if the half-elf got hurt? Bubby would never forgive her. She could never do that to Bubby.

And then, Betty got a wonderful idea.

The Sword Saint! Or that green duchess? They have Divine Protections that can make sure he isn’t lying. Or maybe, see if he isn’t a cultist in disguise? The red one has so many Divine Protections, he must have something that could help with this.

She turned her head quickly before hesitating and looking back at the boy.

He looked vulnerable.

She looked around and noticed some sort of fabric nearby. She ran over and dragged it over to cover the boy.

She whispered to him before patting him for assurance, “…Betty is sorry. Betty will be back soon.”

She ran as fast as possible in order to find anyone who could help her resolve this situation.

 

 

Unbeknownst to her, a figure that was passing by had heard Beatrice screaming and arrived just as she left.

It was the last of the White Dragon’s Scales, Dynas Trussardi. He had originally separated from the others in search of the Archbishop of Gluttony but had no luck. Unfortunately, he heard a familiar child’s voice yelling in the distance.

“Beatrice-sama! I heard you yelling about a Witch Cultist, are you hurt?!”

He ran onto the scene but found no spirit in sight.

He did notice a familiar cloak on the ground, it was a cloak worn by members of the Witch Cult.

 And it had a body under it.

He edged closer to it with one of his katanas drawn, cautious in case this was a trap. He became calmer as he heard a faint snoring.

Lifting the cloak, he uncovered an unfamiliar person. He looked vaguely Gustekan or Vollachian, with his black hair and odd fashion sense.

“…Beatrice-sama mentioned a cultist or an Archbishop. Could it be? I’ll have to bring him to the others, just in case. If we are lucky, maybe we will have another of the bastards under lock and key.”

He looked around, “But where did she go?”

 

 

“Where is that stupid Sword Saint?!”

Beatrice had been running around, using Murak to cover great distances, in order to find the hero of Lugunica, to no avail. She was currently dashing between the buildings, when she saw something in the corner of her eye, a white blur flew in from somewhere and crash landed in the nearby alley.

White? The red weirdo wears white all the time, maybe it’s him?!

Not quite thinking straight, she desperately ran towards the first sign of help. Only to find an even more peculiar sight. It was a white fox, that was heavily damaged and looked like she was barely staying cognizant.

Tsk. It’s not the sword man, where could he be-

“Please… help… Anastasia. She’s not…” the fox fell to the ground unconscious.

Mother?! T-that was her voice. Wait, who is she?

Anastasia? Oh, the purple merchant thing. Wait, the fox looks familiar. Wasn’t the merchant wearing something similar.

Something similar.

Similar.

 

Beatrice stared at the white fox.

 

Has Betty seen her before? No. She hasn’t. She isn’t bleeding, is she a spirit? Maybe something made by Mother? Just like Betty and Bubby?

Beatrice hesitated. She was already running low on time; she had wasted so much trying to find the Sword Saint. Any longer and the boy could wake up and leave before Beatrice could confirm any of his statements.

 

But she was so lonely. Ever since Bubby had left, she felt a hole within her soul.

Maybe. Maybe if the fox turned out to be one of her siblings…

She looked around, and sighed, before moving to grab the unconscious fox.

 

“Where did he go?!”

Beatrice was getting really tired not finding anyone she wants to find. The white fox was currently resting around her neck, she immediately converted into some kind of scarf when Beatrice touched her.

After healing her and making sure the fox was still breathing, Beatrice immediately went back to find the boy she so callously left behind. Only to find no sign of him at all.

And so, she panicked once again and searched relentlessly for any sign of the boy.

After hours of searching, she eventually found one person.

The one person she did not care to find.

Ever.

“Beatrice-sama?! Where have you been? Are you hurt? Wait, what’s that thing around your neck?”

Ugh. The merchant. Or ex-merchant, I suppose.

Beatrice never really forgave Otto for burning down her entire library.

Beatrice pushed past him, “Places. No. And none of your business, in fact.”

She then suddenly stopped and turned her head, “Where is the Sword Saint?”

Otto raised an eyebrow, “Reinhard-san? He’s over there- “

She didn’t wait and immediately bolted towards him, only slowing down as she started to hear his conversation with the weird girl cat boy thing. She hid next to a wall and listened in.

“-a Witch Cultist? Are you sure?”

The cat thing looked manically excited, “Pretty sure Rein, one of the White Dragon’s Scales found them. Said they found him with one of their cloaks. He’s still out cold, maybe we can interrogate him when we get back.”

Beatrice grimaced, No! Betty did not mean to do that, it was an accident. Betty needs to correct this.

Before she could step out, the red one spoke, “Maybe. But we can’t be sure until we talk to him. For all we know, he could be a hapless citizen caught within an unfortunate situation. We shouldn’t be rash.”

Beatrice hesitated, ...Or maybe the Sword Saint can handle this. If he talks to him, maybe he can double check if the boy is a witch cultist or not. And if he isn’t, he’ll be released. What did he say? He was the half-elf’s knight, right? Then that must mean he’ll come to the mansion.

Betty started to smile, Then Betty can apologize. It was all a misunderstanding. Betty can then get to know him and see if he is That Person or not.

Betty nodded to herself as the two knights spoke to each other.

“Felix, are you alright, you seem agitated?”

The cat one’s eyes widened and he just looked away, “I’m fine Rein, just a little stressed, nya know?”

The cat tried to smile but it looked fake, and the red one obviously knew but decided to leave him alone, “…Alright. Though be aware, I am here if you would like some aid.”

Beatrice at this point had walked away, thinking of how to prepare for her possible contractor’s visit.

 

It has been one week since they had returned to home.

It has also been two weeks since she had seen the boy and she was getting worried.

Pacing back and forth within her bedroom, Where is he? Is he still in the capital? What happened? Maybe he’s a cultist? No, he would have been executed, the contract is still there. What if he wasn’t the person Betty contracted with? No, Betty felt the pull, it was towards him. Maybe he doesn’t want to come back? Maybe. Maybe Betty made a bad first impression. Maybe he felt betrayed by Betty’s actions.

She tried focusing on the connection of the contract, but she couldn’t feel anything. She felt a slight pull towards him in Priestella but it seems far distances decrease her connection. She would need to head to the capital to see if he was still there. But what if he wasn’t? He could be anywhere.

“Are you trying to make a hole in the ground? If so, I believe using a shovel would be much more efficient compared to simply walking back and forth for hours at a time.”

The spirit paused her thinking mode and simply glared at her ‘sister.’

After bringing back the fox to their home, Beatrice had learned three things: the fox had been pretending to be an accessory to a Hoshin Trading Company employee during the siege, the fox may have Mother’s voice and mannerisms but she did not have her memories or skills, and she was also very annoying.

“Betty does not appreciate such rude behavior. Respect your big sister.”

Echidna raised an eyebrow, “Are we sure you are the older sibling here? Logically, if you were the older sibling, you would have been aware of my creation. Rather, since you do not have any memory of me, it would imply that I am in fact the one who was created earlier, and thus I am the ‘big sister.’”

Beatrice simply stared at her big sister and then promptly threw a book at her, “Wrong, in fact.”

The fox dodged and lamented dramatically, “If one speaks the truth, they shall be shunned, a fact known throughout history.”

Beatrice ignored her and went promptly back to pacing.

“…Why don’t you simply go to the capital and check on the boy if you are so worried.”

Beatrice stopped and turned her head slightly, “…It’s not that simple.”

“But it is. If you go to the capital, you will know if the boy is still there or not. If he is, you can go ask why he hasn’t come back to his candidate’s camp. If he isn’t, then that means he has left for better pastures.”

Beatrice’s hand trembled, “…”

The fox sighed, “…In that case, would it not be more productive to be working on those new spells rather than worrying for nothing.”

“…That is a good idea, I suppose.”

Beatrice had been working on some ideas in order to impress her possible contractor. She had made a spell that could silence the sound around her, though it took a lot of concentration and mana to keep up. She was also thinking of a spell that could allow her to become invisible for a period of time. She did not want to share the spells she had made for Bubby as the names were quite embarrassing. Beatrice did not really understand her past’s self’s logic for naming the spells after Bubby’s contractor. While EMM (Emilia is Maybe not Mediocre) and EMT (Emilia Makes decent Tea) are incredibly genius ways to apply Yin magic, she would rather die than ever share them with anyone. Perhaps she will rename them later, Bubby would understand.

The fox rolled her head slowly from side to side, “Have you considered my suggestion from last time?”

“The idea that you and I could resonate mana? Hm, theoretically it could work, Betty has heard that the purple knight can connect gates with his spirits Yin and Yang spirits. Though, I don’t know if that can apply to us given the lack of a contractor who can help facilitate the connection.”

“In normal circumstances, yes. However, we are not normal spirits. Our creator gave us certain parameters: I am able to possess a person’s Od without a contract. I am unable to use magic efficiently but I have an affinity for Yang. You, however, are able to use magic and drain mana from any person. Perhaps, if I were to possess your Od, we may be able to tune our mana naturally. Allowing you to use my Yang affinity.”

Beatrice began tapping her chin, “It is possible, in fact. Perhaps we can connect our gates together through the possession. Hypothetically, when mana passes through the gate from the Od, it is attuned to a specific magic attribute, which allows the user to use a spell, in fact. Betty does not know what would happen when two gates attune the same mana particles with different elements.”

Echidna acted as an idea board, “Wouldn’t it work the same as that knight fellow? Or a mage with different affinities?”

Beatrice shook her head, “Not necessarily, in fact. Though Spirit Arts users act as conduits, they often do not actually use their gates to cast. As a result, the mana only usually passes through a spirit’s gate. Even the purple knight combines magic by externally combining the different mana particles as they pass through each spirit’s gate. And a mage has to individually charge different mana through their gate to combine them into a unique combination magic. It’s why mages like the clown, as Betty hates to admit, are incredible for being able to concentrate and combine so many different types of mana at once.”

“So, you believe that two gates would work differently if they were arranged parallel internally?”

Beatrice was on a roll, excitedly she started to word vomit, “It’s hard to say. One theory is that the mana may just simply transform into the last gate’s intended attribute. However, there is another possibility that the mana may attune to two different magic types at the same time, I suppose. Perhaps if one gate could transfer the mana to the other instantly or if the gates attune at the same time, the mana may take on attributes of both elements and create a whole new version of magic, I suppose!”

Echidna got swept up in the excitement, “Incredible. Then, what are we waiting for, let’s begin!”

Beatrice nodded vigorously and gestured to the fox to hop on.

The fox jumped onto Beatrice’s shoulders and morphed into her scarf form. She then began to meld her mind into Beatrice’s, connecting their Ods together.

 

The experience felt odd to Beatrice. At first, she expected Echidna would take over her body, as she explained. However, that is not what happened. Instead, it felt like two minds were controlling the same body. Perhaps the difference was because they were both spirits, maybe it was a result of their specific affinities, or maybe it was because of some innate characteristic given to them by their shared mother.

Either way, it felt incredibly nauseating.

“Ugh, this feels disgusting, I suppose…”

“This is an odd experience for me as well. I have never possessed someone only to have control be shared.”

Beatrice held felt like her insides were about cave in, “This…might take some getting used to. Let’s try casting a spell before Betty experiences vomiting, in fact.”

“Spirits cannot vomit.”

“Shut up, in fact.”

Beatrice, and Echidna, held up her hand and started channeling her mana through her gate.

Or in this case, gates.

As she did so, she noticed that one of her hypotheses was correct: the gates naturally connected to each other as if they were for one individual. The invisible organs were able to instantly transfer the mana to the other.

However, she was disappointed to find that the mana simply transformed from Yin to Yang and vice-versa.

“Jiwald.”

Her first experiment proved fruitful as a blast of light shot from her finger and burned a hole through the wall.

“…Perhaps we should have done this outside.”

“Too late, in fact. The experiment shall continue. Minya!”

Her second experiment proved fruitful as well, a violet crystal of frozen mana materialized within the air and shot forth, lodging itself right next to the burning hole.

“Hmm, let Betty try one last experiment.”

“You have an idea?”

“Possibly. If the mana can be transferred from one to the other, what if Betty tries channeling the mana constantly between them?”

“Either you will have two different mana sources, ready to cast two spells at the same time, or you will be simply swapping mana elements without it coalescing into a formable spell. I’m assuming you wish to see if your ‘new combined magic type’ theory proves true?”

Beatrice wobbled but was able to conjure enough energy to scoff, “Betty is a scholar, if there is a possibility to expand magic even more, Betty shall take it.”

“Hm, very well, just be aware that this possession is straining me as well. Our opposite affinities are proving more strenuous than I anticipated. We should finish quickly, I do not want to see what would happen if our connection was severed as we were channeling mana.”

Beatrice grimaced and silently agreed. Even her thirst for knowledge had limits, unlike her mother who would probably be delighted to see what would happen.

She began to channel the mana through the gates, switching constantly.

Something strange began to happen. As more mana began to build, the Yin mana and the Yang mana started to collide. While it seemed like instantaneous teleportation to Beatrice, the mana was actually moving at incredible speeds from one gate to the other. Usually, mana tends to clump towards similar mana types, akin to water. When different mana types combine externally, they often have to be pushed together forcefully in order to create an incredible burst of power.

So, what happens when multiple small bursts consistently happen within an internal connection? And what happens when the gates were incredibly close to each to other, allowing consistent collisions? And the two mana types in question were exact opposites of each other?

Beatrice started feeling her body burning up. As if out of nowhere, she felt energy exponentially building within her.

“Beatrice, you need to stop. Now.”

“Wait a moment, Betty has an idea, in fact.”

The energy from the small collisions was collecting into each other. The small opposing mana particles would usually collide and dissipate into a bright light. If one were to observe the phenomenon, it would be as if small stars were blinking into and out of existence rapidly.

“Your body can’t take this much energy! You need to release it!”

“Just a little more,” Beatrice began formulating a spell in front of her.

She imagined both the idea of a Jiwald and Minya simultaneously going off.

Her body began to shudder, heat emanating from her very core. It felt like she was on fire.

The stars were creating a miniature galaxy.

“RELEASE IT OR YOU WILL EXPLODE!”

As if by instinct, Beatrice created a new spell and finally let go,

“JINYA!”

 

Two orbs formed into existence in front of Beatrice. An orb of pure white, outlined in blue, and an orb of pure black, outlined in purple. These orbs began to pulse and rotate around each other, beginning slowly before rapidly spinning at a high velocity. The forward momentum of the orbs was quite slow.

It looked as if a binary star had come to life and began moving in slow motion.

But when that miniature astral phenomenon met the wall.

Everything blinked white.

 

And then it exploded.

 

BOOM!

 

As Beatrice blinked away the aftereffects of the bright light, she gawked in sheer wonder at what she had done.

The wall was completely blown apart. Not only that, the area outside had become completely decimated. The force of the explosion purged a great chunk of the earth and obliterated any vegetation nearby.

“Amazing, in fact…”

She tried rubbing the fox around her neck, “Do you see this sister, we’ve discovered a new way to cast magic, I suppose!”

“…”

“Sis?”

Echidna was currently unconscious. She cut the connection right after Beatrice fired the spell. The sheer strain from trying to maintain the build up of energy knocked her out.

Beatrice herself could barely stand up, black spots edged into her vision as she started to also pass out.

“Ha…Betty can’t wait to show this to her… contractor…”

THUD!

And with that, Beatrice joined her sister in dreamland.

Thump. Thump! THUMP! SLAM!

“What the hell just happened, is everyone alright?!” Otto Suwen said as he barged through the door to see what had caused such a loud noise.

He subsequently felt his jaw drop when he saw the utter mayhem caused by the little spirit.

He also felt his stomach drop when he realized how much money this would take to fix.

 

It was a headache for Beatrice to explain everything. Honestly, it wasn’t that much of a problem. She barely explained anything in the first place. Only when Petra prodded her did she simply mention that she was experimenting with new ways to cast magic. This raised excitement, more specifically dread in Otto’s case, for the whole camp as they had been in a sort of slump ever since Priestella.

Not that Beatrice cared, she was simply counting down the days until her supposed contractor would visit. She barely talked to anyone. She didn’t care that the clown was extremely morose and depressed nowadays. She didn’t care that the pink oni with a weird clown fetish was symbiotically depressed because of the clown. She didn’t care that the manly cat boy was bored and not listening to anyone. She didn’t care that the half-elf was lonely. She especially didn’t care that the former merchant was stressed from managing such a dysfunctional group of people.

The only two people who were remotely okay were the womanly cat maid and Petra. Though Petra seemed oddly unmotivated nowadays. She would often talk about wanting to restart her dream of becoming a tailor. It seems that the maid profession wasn’t as fulfilling for her as before.

 

Anyways, that wasn’t important. Beatrice was only focused on two objectives for the next two weeks: being ready for her contractor to finally visit and figuring out Yin-Yang magic. The latter was difficult to say the least. Yin-Yang magic was not viable for combat or practical use yet. One, it required an incredible amount of concentration between the two spirits. Two, the current spellcasting was inefficient, as Beatrice was almost drained of all her mana just from one cast. Following the first experiment, she ended up siphoning off mana from every person in the mansion, especially the grey advisor. Three, she was unable to combine other mana types. It seems that her highest affinity, that being Yin, allowed her to facilitate the constant mana stream with her sister’s Yang gate. Anything else would cause an instant disruption of the connection.

As for the former, Beatrice spent every waking moment practicing how she would welcome Subaru.

She made sure she would pronounce his name correctly, based on how she remembered him saying it.

By this point, she processed that Subaru was most likely not a cultist given her first impressions of him: he did not have a gospel on his body when she checked him for damage, he did not have the insane mannerisms of a typical cultist, and his words were very sincere when he spoke to her.

It also left her with a crushing feeling of guilt for reacting so badly at the start.

“Betty is… very sorry she knocked you out, in fact. Betty was very stressed from the events on that day. Betty also could not believe that she had a contract. The combination of meeting her contractor and seeing said contractor exuding a ton of miasma, especially after fighting Archbishops, had made Betty panic. However, Betty knows these are just excuses, in fact. That does not excuse Betty for acting in such a way and putting you in harm’s way. Betty would like to start again, from zero. Betty may not remember you but that does not matter, I suppose. Betty would like to try and create new memories. Even if you may not be That Person, Betty believes you may become someone akin to them.”

And then Beatrice imagined showing him all the new spells she had invented. She smiled at the potential future.

He would be so impressed, he would forgive her for being such a stupid idiot when they first met.

He would also hopefully forgive her for failing him in the first place, if the fact that she had forgotten him was true.

And then they would spend all of their time together, getting to know each other again.

And Beatrice would no longer be alone.

“Wonderful speech. Now if only you would finally build up the courage to say it in front of the actual person rather than a mirror.”

Well, Beatrice wasn’t exactly alone anymore. Though she hoped her potential contractor would be better and be less annoying company.

Without looking, Beatrice simply held out her hand, touched the fox next to her, and said, “Murak.”

Before she then hurled the fox toward the ceiling.

“…Well, that was completely uncalled for,” Echidna said as she floated aimlessly above her sister.

“Wrong, it was well deserved, in fact,” Beatrice said as she continued daydreaming of welcoming her contractor perfectly.

The fox sighed as she tried to reorient herself while spinning, “Well, if you must waste time, could you at least go get some more mana so that we can continue yesterday’s experiment. I would like to see if we can change Jinya’s intensity and mana cost. I’d rather prefer not having an early bedtime again.”

Beatrice huffed, “Betty will go because she wants to, and not because you said so, in fact.”

She then started walking towards the door, just as the fox realized something, “Wait a moment, turn off the spell before you leave. Betty? Beatrice?!”

Beatrice ignored her as she walked out of the room and down the halls. She had barely left her room ever since returning. Even moving into a new room did not change her introversion. The new room was rather strange, it held a lot of miscellaneous objects: a guiltylowe whip, a butler outfit, and even a sewing kit with dolls. Perhaps it was storage for the clown’s previous lives. Hopefully it wasn’t a sex thing, the whip and the butler outfit really didn’t help dissuade Beatrice from such a conclusion.

She was about to barge into the grey one’s room to demand mana when she noticed the door was slightly ajar.

As she moved closer, she heard a conversation between the grey one and the tiger maid, “Otto-sama, you mustn’t drink so much.”

“Ah, Frederica, is that you~?” The grey one slurred, “Did you know, besides Gar, you are my favorite person in this whole mansion~?”

He hiccupped.

“Fufufu, Otto-sama, save such comments for when you are sober. Otherwise, I might think you are trying to court me. It’s not good to play with a maiden’s heart.”

“But Frederica-san, getting the chance, hic, to court you would be a, hic, dream come true~.”

“…”

Beatrice could not see but she could tell that the yellow one was blushing.

Ugh, just mate already, you fools.

“Frederica-san? Can I be honest with ya?”

“Y-yes?! Of course, you can. I’m always here to listen to you.”

“…I think we’re screwed.”

“Otto…”

“We have to face the facts. We’re struggling compared to the other camps. Priscilla is currently leading due to her single-handedly capturing an Archbishop in Priestella. Crusch may be struggling due to the curse but even she has lingering support due to her subjugation of the White Whale and assistance in Sloth. Even though Felt shares the defeat of Greed with us, she is gaining a lot of traction from helping people in the slums. Despite a year passing, we have nothing to show for it compared to the others. We can’t even cash in on defeating the White Rabbit because there was nothing left to show. Some people are even saying it was Emilia-sama’s fault for getting captured by Greed, it’s not fair! Even after all this time, they still think she’s the reincarnation of Satella…”

“I know it must feel like our camp is barely holding on, but you are doing a wonderful job. Who else has been organizing us and preparing strategies for us since the beginning? Who has been supporting every single one of our members whenever they struggled? And who was able to beat Master Mathers in his own game? It was thanks to you that we are here, Otto-sama.”

“…”

“…”

“Frederica?”

“Yes, Otto-sama.”

“I can’t accept that.”

“Otto-“

“I’m serious. Ever since I’ve come here, I feel like I have gotten lucky. Getting saved from the Cult, Garfiel changing his mind at the last second, Beatrice deciding to help us at the last second, and even narrowly winning against Roswaal. I have not planned a single part of that. I feel I have been constantly riding the waves of this river of hell, and I do not know how long I can keep this up. I can barely organize anyone here! Maybe I should go back to being a merchant…”

“Do you truly want to leave?”

“…No. I don’t. Despite all my complaints, some part of me feels responsible. Like I have to stick it out for some reason. Even though I want to punch that reason so badly.”

“…Well at the very least, I hope you stay as long as possible. I am of the same opinion that, besides Garfiel and Petra, you are my favorite person here.”

“…Thank you, Frederica.”

Beatrice wanted to slam her head into the wall at how much ludicrous sexual tension there was between the maid and the advisor.

“It is my pleasure. By the way, are you still considering returning to the capital?”

Beatrice’s eyes widened.

“Yes. Though this time I will travel alone. It’s not urgent, however, I will probably leave in a month or so.”

“Will you be visiting the prisoner?”

Wait, what prisoner?

“No. Not this time, I’ll be checking in with Julius and the other camps. See how they are doing, especially Crusch-sama given how bad her condition was last time we spoke.”

“Oh, how terrible. Did the cultist say anything about Crusch-sama’s condition?”

“No. When we all visited, he was completely silent. Which was strange, Felix said he was very talkative on the first day. But when he arrived, he wouldn’t even acknowledge us. It felt… weird.”

“Weird, how?”

“…Do you ever get the feeling like you’ve seen someone before?”

“I think I can imagine.”

“Maybe it was his scary eyes or something, but something just felt off, like I’ve seen him in the past. But I don’t think so? It was strange. Heck, I feel like there was a moment when he did react to me, as if he recognized me. And yet, no matter what I said, he would never respond.”

“Strange. Did he mention his name at least?”

“Well, Felix did. Apparently, the guy’s name was Natsuki Subaru-“

SLAM!

The spirit heard enough. She slammed open the door and startled the two. Otto was sitting at his desk with a glass in his hand, a whiskey on his desk, and Frederica’s hands on his shoulders.

 She stared straight at the merchant, her face paling, “When was this, in fact?”

“Beatrice-sama- “

Beatrice jumped onto the desk, “ANSWER ME!”

Otto was afraid, “T-the prisoner talk? It was a few days after we got back. We asked you if you wanted to come but you said you were busy-“

Otto couldn’t finish as Beatrice drained all of his mana and knocked him out.

Frederica was shocked, “Beatrice-sama, what have you done?!”

“He’ll be fine, I suppose!”

Beatrice did not waste any time, she jumped off the desk and ran out of the room.

Her mind was racing.

She made a mistake. A very big mistake.

She assumed the Sword Saint would have absolved the boy of any connection to the Witch Cult.

Why did she assume that? How could she have trusted the Sword Saint to help her contractor?

No. She knows why. Because she’s a failure. Because she’s slothful. Because she hasn’t changed. At all.

She kept running through the hallways. Tears streaming down her eyes.

A pit of despair started growing within her stomach. Her mind started connecting the dots. And assuming the worst-case scenarios.

If they think he’s a Witch Cultist, and they think he has information. Oh no.

Why did she not visit him? Why did she not try to go to him first? Why couldn’t she just choose him?!

She knows why. She was afraid. She was afraid of being rejected. That she messed up her chance at happiness. And now she may have ruined any semblance of it.

SLAM!

“Oh, you’re finally back, I was able to get myself… down. Betty, what’s wrong?”

Beatrice was bawling at this point, “You were right. Betty has made a mistake. We have to go to the capital. Now.”

“Beatrice, wait a moment- “

Beatrice was not having it, “Betty has waited long enough!”

She grabbed the fox and threw her around her neck before jumping out the window and sprinting towards the direction of the capital.

Everything was a blur at this point.

She ignored everything.

She ignored her sister’s questions.

She just kept running.

 

Now she was at the capital. It’s been days.

Every second. She keeps focusing on her connection.

Praying. Hoping. That he wasn’t where she thought he was.

She was wrong. He was still there. The connection rang true at the prison tower.

 

She didn’t know how she got in. Or how no one saw her. Or why the pit in her stomach had become so large.

All she cared about was now right in front of her: the boy.

The same boy who was currently barely breathing, emaciated, wounds and scars covering his body, face gaunt, and hair white as snow.

She couldn’t breathe. She was trembling.

She wanted to scream. She wanted to die.

All she could think and feel.

Was immense hatred for herself.

Notes:

EN1: It's interesting to me that Re:Forgotten stories often have Beatrice's contract be switched to Emilia, considering Julius's canon contracts with his spirits. When he was forgotten, it was mentioned that his contract was still technically 'there.' It's just that spirits couldn't recognize him and it seems like a lot of the benefits of the contract were not allowed, despite the connection. Hell, we later see him break and reforge the contracts in the same arc. So wouldn't that mean if Subaru's name was forgotten, he would still have his contract. This was one of the reasons I wanted to write this story, I wanted to figure out a way that the scenario could still happen despite this still being there. So here's my interpretation of it. It mainly came from the idea: wouldn't it be an absolute mindfuck for spirits, especially sentient ones, to find a contract to someone they never really knew?

EN2: Honestly, a lot of this may seem circumstantial, but it came to me that a lot of tragedies or important events happened due to bad luck and a series of coincidences. Case in point? Just look up Archduke Ferdinand.

EN3:This was originally going to be a much longer chapter, was going to finish the Betty story in one, but it got too long. So sorry y'all, you'll have to wait until next week to see the conclusion to this arc.

EN4: Wow I have a lot of endnotes. Also, thank you all so much for the Kudos, bookmarks, and comments. We've reached 250 bookmarks! And as promised, I will give you an interlude sometime this week. However, the planned interlude I was going to write can't be given yet, we are not in that part of the timeline yet. So, instead I have an offer: you get to choose! I'll have a twitter poll up that will basically offer three possible interludes: a continuation of the last one, a react chapter where my version of Anastasia enters the Theater and reacts to the first few chapters along with the cast, or a fun chapter where Subaru and Anastasia go on a date.

The poll will go live right as I post this, so go check out my twitter and vote what you want! I'll keep it up for two days, and announce what will be written on Wednesday.

Chapter 13: A Spirit's Soliloquy

Summary:

Beatrice fails & we return to the present...

Notes:

The interlude is still planned! If you haven't seen my twitter post, it is looking to be around 15,000 words minimum at the moment. The react fic will be posted this week but it will just take some time due to the unexpected length. For now, enjoy the next chapter~!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

“Don’t do it. Not yet.”

“…”

“If you kill him now, you will put the rest of the kingdom on high alert. We can’t kill the Sword Saint. Not only that, but his Water magic affinity could also make him immensely durable. Yin-Yang magic is powerful, but can we kill him immediately? I do not know, and we can’t risk everything on a maybe.

“…”

Beatrice was currently in Felix’s room, at Karsten Manor, ready to annihilate the cat demi-human from existence.

“Think rationally.”

It would be so easy.

“Think about what’s at stake.”

Just a few Jinyas and this whole place would become a crater. It was the least he deserved.

 “Think about the boy.”

That made Beatrice pause. She had already made way too many mistakes. And it damned her contractor to nearly a month of suffering. Could she really afford to make another?

She put her hand down and stopped channeling mana, “…Then what you suppose we do, in fact?”

“…Drain his mana. We’ll have to be careful. Maybe not all of it. Just enough for him to feel exhausted and not notice something is wrong. He won’t be able to do much. Hopefully he’ll be too tired to hurt the boy.”

Beatrice gritted her teeth, “Might? Betty does not want to leave Subaru to this cat thing. And let them torture him anymore on a ‘maybe,’ in fact.”

“We’ll keep watch then. If there is any sign that they’ll continue, we can choose to act or perhaps even disorient them. Those other spells we made will help us. In the meantime, we’ll plan and improve. Find a way to get the boy out in the cleanest and most efficient way possible. Perhaps we can even talk to the boy beforehand-”

Beatrice flinched. She did not know if she could face him right now.

“…Or we’ll just stay in the shadows. At the very least we need to plan accordingly. We cannot risk his life on a dangerous escape route.”

“... Alright, I suppose,” Beatrice sighed, “Betty might have an idea. A flower that Mother was fond of: muskrim. If we get enough, we could use it to knock out the guards. Unfortunately, Betty only knows that it grows in Gusteko. Perhaps we can find it at the border.”

“Only one way to find out. Let’s split up our time efficiently: find the flower, drain mana from the prison guards and the cat thing daily, and see if we can tend to the boy’s wounds and his excess mana. It’s a miracle he has survived this long, given his broken gate.”

Beatrice’s fists tightened into a death grip. Felix’s snores could be heard in the background.

Beatrice turned to leave but took one last look at Blue.

…Spend your last days well, cat. Betty will kill you when this is all over, in fact. It is not a matter of if, only when.

 

 

“I blame you for that, you know?”

Beatrice felt her body tense. She tried her best for the last month. They found enough muskrim to cover the whole prison. They also honed their new spells: a Yin spell called Silen which helped silence their movements and conversations, Maujer which used Yin-Yang magic to replicate cognitive disruption, a less burdensome version of Jinya, and many others. The first two helped them stay near Subaru without anyone noticing, hiding in the rafters of the prison for the most part. They were ready to leave now. The only problem was when? When would be the best time to help him escape?

“He kept asking about you. Asking how you have been doing since Wilhelm and I barred him from coming here.”

Now? Beatrice channeled mana as she waited for the catboy to act. She was mostly successful during the last month, draining the cat just enough to get him back off from any further torture, the mana loss causing deliriousness and faulty decision making. However, it seems today he was very persistent. She needed to see if he would push his luck. Give her a reason to kill him as she promised.

“Do not make a rash decision! We are so close. The boy could die if they swarm this place. It needs to be quick and methodical. Do not ruin our plans before we can enact them, sister.”

Tsk. Betty knows.

But if the catboy made a move on her contractor, all bets were off.

“…Have it your way-“

“…Felix.”

Beatrice paused along with the disgraceful Blue. She had not heard one word out of her contractor the entire time he was here. And apparently that was not unusual given Blue was currently losing his mind and ranting about it.

…Maybe the boy has given up. Betty knows she would have given up if she were him. So, what would happen if Betty tried freeing him? Would he accept Betty? Or try to kill her?

A lingering feeling was left at the pit of her stomach. A feeling she hated. A feeling that put her current actions into doubt.

Noticing that Felix had finally left she dropped down silently from the rafters and quickly ran over to the boy to check his condition. Subaru had no new marks, but he still looked positively awful.

Beatrice still felt that terrible feeling. It told her that this might not be worth it. That she still had Bubby. That she was throwing away her brother just to save someone who may very well hate her. She deserved it. But what about Bubby? Doesn’t he deserve happiness? If she helps Subaru escape, that might mean she would never see Bubby again. Because Bubby would never trust her for releasing someone that could potentially harm his contractor, especially a supposed witch cultist.

Sob. Sob. Sob.

She was flung out of her doubts by the cries of the boy near her. He would get like this sometimes. Adrift asleep but still almost cognizant and constantly weeping. It pained her to see him like this. She went over and held his hands softly as she usually did each night.

The feeling still remained. Bubby or Subaru. Her brother or her supposed contractor. Someone she knows who loves her versus someone who may or may not anymore. She hated that she was feeling this. Such a rotten disgusting feel-

“Please…”

Beatrice swallowed and looked at her contractor. His face. Gaunt and like a ghost. It was so desperate, so devoid of hope.

She did that to him. This was her fault.

He didn’t deserve any of this. She did.

He loved her and she threw it away.

 

She knew what she needed to do.

She made a decision. Whatever happens: Subaru will come first. No matter the cost. Whatever she wants, doesn’t matter. It was the least she should do.

 

She felt him move slightly, his usual habit, before awakening. She moved back into the shadows. Hiding once more.

 

No matter what the cost: even if the cost is her.

It was time to act.

 

 

The muskrim was working almost perfectly. A few hours after Felix’s visit, they waited until the final guard shift change and conducted their plan. They grinded the plant into a powder and started spreading it from above. One by one every single one of the prison guards started to fall to the ground, asleep. The spirits mana drained them just in case. Any of them that managed to stay awake, mainly veterans were hit with a Jiwald or a Minya to weaken them, followed by a mana drain.

The abundance of mana has helped with channeling Silen and Maujer, otherwise their stealth would be ruined.

 

The only problem was that they were unlucky. A wandering patrol of guards checked on the prison tower and found all of the prison guards asleep. Half of the guards ran off to go warn the others while the other half remained to try investigating what was going on. Beatrice knocked out the remaining guards but cursed herself as she needed to chase the men who had left.

Using Murak and strengthening her legs with a Yang spell, Stolt, she raced after the man.

“What about the boy?! Sister, we should just grab the boy and go. The guard is a lost cause.”

They had been arguing about this for weeks. Beatrice did not want to show her face to Subaru. At least not yet. She wanted it to be perfect. It needed to be perfect. She needed a situation where Subaru would see Beatrice as useful. Capable. Someone that he can rely on and not the waste of mana that left him to die. She needed this to be perfect. She can’t make any mistakes.

So, she needed this runaway guard to be unconscious. Right. Now!

 

She failed. The guard managed to get to another patrol, and they sent a Goa into the air to signal the other knights.

She needed to get back to the prison. She needed to get Subaru out of here right now.

 

 

“Where is he, in fact?!”

Beatrice was panicking. Subaru was gone. The bodies were all there. But Subaru was nowhere to be found.

“Calm down, he might have left once the bodies started dropping. He’s smart, he might be making an escape attempt on his own.”

Beatrice continued to panic. Her contractor had left. And it was all her fault. Stupid. She was so stup-

“Betty! This is no time for you to blame yourself. Move now before the boy ends up captured. We at least have your contract with him. Its range may be low but it’s better than nothing.”

Beatrice flinched, “…Sorry, you’re right. It’s time for Betty to focus.”

 

Beatrice ran over the whole capital searching for her contractor while also sending the guards on wild goose chases. She used Yang magic to create false light images of Subaru’s form in order trick the guards towards as many false directions as possible.

 

She finally found him. But he was inside a merchant’s cart?

He must have snuck in while she was busy. She weightlessly leaped on on top of the cart as it left the capital, she was ready to take out the merchant, knock her our and save Betty’s contrac-

“BWAHAHAHA!!!”

“LISTEN HERE YOU LITTLE SHIT-“

Beatrice stumbled as she realized what was going on. She listened to their conversation. The merchant saved the boy.

She saved him.

 

And not Beatrice.

 

Beatrice lost her chance.

 

Wait why are they cuddling in bed now?

“Huh. Well, you didn’t tell me your contractor was a master at seduction~?”

Beatrice face palmed, “…Betty did not know either.”

 

And then morning came, both spirits continued watching the two stars as they ate and talked.

“I’m starting to like the two of them, they are quite fun when together.”

Beatrice pouted, “Betty could talk and have fun with her contractor, in fact. The girl is not special.”

They watched as Subaru doused his eggs in a heap of white liquid.

Both of them grimaced, “Could you eat that?”

They watched as the girl somehow was able to eat and enjoy the weird food combination, “…Maybe not.”

 

Some parts of the conversation were interesting to the spirits. They were currently back on top of the carriage, listening to the stars talk.

“So, the girl lost her spirit in Priestella? Curious…”

“Hm? Did you see her spirit before? Because Betty has not.”

“No. Which is interesting. We should be able to detect another spirit. And given its capabilities, it should be at east quasi or full spirit. So why didn’t we find it? Did it have the same cognitive disruption as me? Unless…”

“Do you have a theory, in fact?”

“…I’ll need more information.”

Beatrice sighed and idly looked around before noticing something in the distance behind them. It was still far away, but she could vaguely tell what it was: a group of knights.

And they were heading right towards the two stars.

“We’ll need to disorient them again.”

Beatrice looked down towards the two fake lovers chatting amicably, “Hopefully this won’t take long, I suppose.”

 

“What happened while we were gone, I suppose?!”

Beatrice returned to her contractor and found him tying up bandits while surrounded by tons of blood and several corpses.

It took a very long time. It wasn’t just one group. There were several heading towards them from different directions. Beatrice had to use multiple tricks: Yang copies of Subaru, Infinite Corridor variations to make it seem like they were going in the wrong direction, Jinya explosions to draw attention away. When one knight group was dealt with, more would come.

By the time they had finished, it took quite a while to rush back towards the carriage. To which they found the two stars in the aftermath of a bandit fight.

“Look over there! In the trees, someone just ran away. It must be a scout. We need to warn- “

Beatrice immediately sprinted after the bandit scout.

“What are you doing?!”

“This is Betty’s chance. They do not have earth dragons, you saw that, right? Betty will follow the bandit scout. The scout will lead her to their camp. They have earth dragons. She can then wipe the bandits out and grab their earth dragons. Once Betty brings them back, her contractor will think Betty is amazing and will need her!”

“…Betty, wouldn’t it be better to simply talk to the boy now? You don’t need to do all of this just to prove your worth.”

“…Betty needs to. Otherwise, the only memory Subaru will have, would be Betty rejecting him and throwing him into that prison. He’ll never accept Betty. Betty needs to do this, or she’ll never be able to face her contractor.”

The fox spirit was quiet for a few seconds before sighing.

“Alright. Then what do you supposed we do?”

 

 

Patrasche was extremely annoyed. First, she ended up having to follow the annoying human that can talk to her to help the other annoying half-elf and annoying tiger boy with whatever. Then, they ended up ignoring her for the next few days. The audacity of these humans! To leave her without any sort of gratitude. Fed up with their treatment, she quickly left without a care in the world. She had no reason to stay.

 

And then she got captured by some disgusting, and somehow more annoying, humans. They would force her to pull carriages and work without any breaks. She especially hates the fast human that would keep poking her with a stick.

She will break that human’s legs one day. So, help her.

She was currently resting at their camp in the forest but was expecting her rest to be interrupted very soon. It was always interrupted.

What she did not expect was the interruption to be explosive this time.

BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!

Explosive balls of mana, white and black, pelted the camp from the forest. She saw several of the very annoying humans get eliminated from existence. Bah! Good riddance.

Unfortunately, another annoyance came along: the spirit. The spirit was very, very annoying. So haughty and prideful. Why was she here? And why was she yelling at her about some nonsense? She isn’t going to follow her. Ever.

Her eyes quickly found their target; she growled with malicious intent.

No. She sees what she needs to do.

She aimed at the annoying fast human, who was currently trying to run away into the forest.

She had some vengeance to enact.

 

 

“…Are you sure this was a wise decision?”

The plan was a half success. The spirits were able to completely decimate the bandit threat. Unfortunately, the earth dragon would not heed the words of Beatrice, no matter how much she yelled. Instead, the damn thing ran after a bandit and ended up attaching itself to her contractor without Beatrice’s involvement ever being known.

“…”

And so, Beatrice failed once again. She was stuck watching as the carriage left with her contractor and the weird purple thing with him.

“You are only delaying the inevitable. The more you wait, the less chances you will get. In time, you will come to regret your hesitation.”

“…”

The fox spirit sighed as she jumped back onto Beatrice’s shoulders.

“Let’s follow them. But heed my words. This inaction of yours will be your undoing.”

…No, it won’t. Betty knows. There will be other chances. Other ways to impress her contractor. Opportunities where she can swoop in, save the day, and have her contractor love her once again.

But they never came.

Weeks passed. They passed by Priestella, traveled through Kararagi, and finally ended up in Banan.

They were able to divert the weird spirit hybrid away from her contractor using Yang light copies. But no more opportunities came.

Even when the hybrid came back, the wolf demi-human would drive it away singlehandedly. She was prepared to join at any moment. But she wasn’t needed.

Her contractor didn’t need her.

More time passed. She watched as Subaru got closer to Anastasia, the purple thing.

He would get closer to the Admirer, as well as the Great Spirit of Wind.

She hated that Great Spirit. She hated that the spirit could so easily barge into her contractor’s life without a care. No self-doubt restraining her. No self-hatred making her hesitate. Beatrice could not say the same.

She hated Tia.

But she hated herself more.

And then, the day before the festival came.

“So, are you two shits going to do anything? Because I don’t want anyone interrupting me when I confront my copy.”

Beatrice and Echidna were perched on the roof of the tenement house. Halibel and Tia were easily able to bypass and detect the two through their stealth magic. After some probing, they deemed the two spirits as non-threats. So, they let them be as long as the spirits did not do anything to their wards. The Banan duo even kept the spirit duo a secret from the two stars, after the little spirit pleaded for them to do so.

“…”

“You going to say anything? No? Pathetic. Lame. What a loser.”

Beatrice grinded her teeth, “…”

“Well, if you’re going to act like Ana, then so be it. I don’t care why you’re watching him like a stalker. So long as you stay out of our way tomorrow.”

Tia walked away, returning to her favorite two humans to try some of their new sauces.

“…Are you doing alright, sister?”

“…”

“…I know I’ve been harsh. But there is still time to rectify this- “

“You were right.”

“…”

“You were always right. Betty should have talked to him from the beginning. She should have gone to find him right when everyone returned to Lugunica, in fact.”

“…Sister,” the fox spoke aloud, concern radiating off of her.

“It’s alright. Betty accepts that her time is over. She’ll watch over her contractor one last time. And then break her contract.”

The fox was shocked. Beatrice looked defeated. She had given up.

“What will you do afterwards?”

“…Betty doesn’t know. She will travel. Or do something else.”

The ‘something else’ did not sound good to the fox spirit.

“Then I will accompany you.”

“You do not have to- “

“I want to.”

“What about the merchant? Didn’t you want to talk to her?”

“I do. But I won’t abandon you for that.”

Beatrice gripped her sister tightly, “…Thank you, sister.”

The fox chuckled, “We are in this together. Until the end, sister.”

 

 

Why was he staring at her?

Zarestia had just offered him a contract.

So why was he staring at Beatrice instead and not accepting yet?!

Did he know she was here all along? He has been acting weird this whole time, ever since they arrived in Banan. He would sometimes look around and linger his gaze at them. But she never even met him, so how could he know she was here?!

“Betty. He is about to accept. You need to do something.”

What can she even do?! She failed. Every single time she failed. She has nothing to show her contractor. Nothing to convince him to choose her.

“…If you won’t act, I will. You will thank me later.”

“Wait, what- “She felt the pull of her Od as Echidna took control of her body. She felt mana surge through her as her sister launched them both towards her contractor.

She waved her hands out, panic overflowing, causing tears to sprout. She was not ready. Not at all.

“STOP, IN FACT!” She screamed at her sister. But the fox would not. The fox knew the little girl needed to act now before it was too late. This was her last chance.

They landed right between Zarestia and Subaru.

“Please… please stop,” Beatrice now realized where she was, blurting out the first thing that came to mind, “Betty…Betty is sorry, I suppose.”

 

 

And now, we are back to the present.

Beatrice was staring straight at the ground.

“…What are you doing here Beatrice?”

Beatrice flinched. Her normal name, not the one given to her. Given to her before she forgot him. The one he would use whenever he spoke about her during his stories to the merchant. She loved to hear that name.

“Betty… Betty is here to-“

She felt herself choke. She kept looking down. Afraid of what she would see if she looked into his eyes.

Beatrice’s mind flashed through all of the events of the last few months. She ran through all she wanted to say. Everything she practiced. Her perfect speech. All the reasons her contractor should choose her again. And she came up with nothing. None of it would work. She waited too long. She didn’t deserve happiness. Every time. She waited too long.

 

Beatrice dared to look. Gazing straight at his face. A face that was a mixture of concern and resolve.

He looked ready to listen. Perhaps before he finally rejects her once and for all. Maybe that was what she truly deserved.

It was time.

She took a deep breath.

 

“Betty is sorry. But Betty does know what to do in fact!”

 

Subaru stepped back slightly but Beatrice continued.

She felt tears gather in her eyes as words vomited out of her, no cohesion or semblance of a plan, “Betty does not know what to do at all, in fact. Betty has spent 400 years waiting, 400 years of nothing! Then, while that idiot merchant burnt down Betty’s library, Betty had a choice to make. Leave and find Betty’s special person or burn with the library. Betty chose the former. She chose to spend her life with Bubby until that person came. Betty thought she had resolve, to no longer wallow in sloth, to find Betty’s special person instead of waiting for someone to choose Betty. Betty thought she had changed, but Betty was wrong! Betty is still the lonely spirit sitting in a library, too scared to take a step forward out of fear. So, when Betty saw you, miasma overflowing and with a contract connected to her: she froze. Betty did not remember you, Betty does not remember choosing you, and Betty was scared that she did forget. So, Betty ran away. Betty knocked you out to see if you really were an Archbishop or not. That was Betty’s first mistake. Her second mistake was letting you rot in a cell for two months, in fact. Betty was scared of losing the chance to see Bubby again, to turn the world against her on a whim. And Betty was scared that she was too late. But Betty realized: Bubby and the half-elf were just like her book, in fact. An excuse to delay action.”

Beatrice clung to the hem of dress. She wanted to die. She wanted to run and end it all. But she kept going. She needed to give her contractor at least something. Maybe closure. By finally being able to tell her to leave. And never come back.

“Betty hasn’t changed, but she still wants to try. Even if Betty might be wrong, even if you hate Betty for being late, for being slothful, even if Bubby and everybody in the world hates her: Betty still wants to choose you. Betty understands that she has already failed you multiple times, yet Betty does not want to give up anymore. Even if you never want to see Betty again, she will still help you until the day you die. Betty will not leave you alone ever again.”

Beatrice reached into herself and tore the remaining embers of the contract apart, right in front of Subaru, shocking him.

“Never again. Betty will not force you. Betty will give you the choice as well. Betty knows she can never fix this completely. But Betty will try. That is all she has left to do.”

“…”

“That is all Betty wanted to say.”

 

 

Within the brightest black star’s mind, he remembered his tumultuous time in Banan. He remembered the realities that no longer existed.

He remembered before his very last loop, as he laid on the floor, his guts hanging loosely while his lower half lay nearby, holding desperately onto the corpse of his pale light.

He remembered a girl, crying and desperately trying to ineffectually heal his torso.

He remembered the very last words from that spirit, “Betty is sorry. Please do not leave Betty!”

She choked as tears rained, “Please…live… don’t die… I wish I met you sooner… I’m sorry…in fact.”

He remembered not wanting to see such a sight again.

He remembered details that didn’t make sense at the time. But now they did with hindsight. He thought he was hallucinating. Why would Beatrice be here? Why would she care? Does he even want to see her? He hated everyone. For a time, he wanted them all to die. To suffer like he did. And another part wanted to forgive them. Understanding that it wasn’t entirely their fault. Just, bad luck.

Two warring versions of himself: One seeking revenge and one seeking forgiveness.

But then Subaru turned towards the one person who had been his guiding light since he left hell. The one person who chose to show him a different path. The one who reminded him it was okay to be selfish.

He looked toward Anastasia. Her face was masked in her usual steady merchant stoicism. But there were those little details Subaru noticed over the last few months: how she would always run her fingers over something when she was nervous, how her eyes would widen slightly when surprised, how her eyes would flicker and blink rapidly whenever she was excited.

Noticing his stare, she gave a soft smile, as if giving him the idea that it was his choice in the end. Her fingers running over her kimono at the same time.

 

He remembers what Anastasia once told him, when they first came to this festival, when Halibel and Tia were barely known to them. The past only he remembered.

“If you want something, go grab it. If you want something else, request it. If you want both, work for it. Be greedy. But put in the work.”

Now a third version of himself existed, born from the original two being combined with the lessons given to him. A greedy version of him that wanted both: revenge and forgiveness.

Maybe things could never be what they once were. But he’ll never know unless he gives it a chance. Unless he puts in the work.

 

 

Seconds passed in tense silence. Beatrice said her piece and taking the silence as answer, started to walk-

“You drained Felix’s mana.”

Beatrice, startled, looked back at Subaru who had an unreadable expression on his face.

“There were days where Felix would come in looking exhausted, with barely any energy to do anything to me. Only screaming and trying to reason with me. I thought it was because he spent it all trying to heal Crusch. Now I think I can guess what actually happened.”

Beatrice felt her heart squeeze.

“There were some nights where I would scratch my arms until they were a mess. I had dreams where someone was holding my hand but I couldn’t remember who they were. I woke up in the morning with all my leftover wounds healed. I thought I was either hallucinating or Felix came in early. I’m fairly sure what happened then as well.”

Beatrice felt her throat close, her mouth dry.

“…On the last day of my time in prison I woke up to half the guards, specifically those right next to my cell, knocked out. I know for sure what actually happened.”

She couldn’t believe it. She wouldn’t believe it! Not until he said it, she wouldn’t dare gain hope, only for it to die in grief.

Subaru took a deep breath, “Beatrice. I remember when we first met, you were cold and distant. I can’t count how many times you blasted me outside of your library. How annoyed you were that I kept finding your door no matter the location. The desperation and melancholy you had as the library burned around you. The joy and happiness you had during our partnership.”

Beatrice could feel it in her heart, there was no happy ending here, only remnants of a journey she cannot remember.

“When I saw you again at the end of the battle in Priestella, do you know what I saw in you on that day?”

Beatrice was on the brink of tears, “…A traitorous idiot who-”

Sob

“Sent you to hell, in fact?”

To Beatrice’s shock, Subaru just shook his head and gave a small sad smile, “No. I saw the same emotions you had on the day the library burned. The desperation and melancholy. As if you were trying to decide what to do.”

“Betty threw you away!”

“And yet you could have killed me. You panicked. But you only knocked me out. If it was the Beatrice I knew from the start, she would have thrown me away without a second thought and never looked back. But you did look back. You came, even if it was late.”

Beatrice was actively sobbing and threw her gaze to the floor, “Betty still left you to die.”

“You didn’t though. You kept watch. You tried, despite all rational reason telling you, that you shouldn’t. If you were wrong, you would have never seen Puck again, the brother you cherished the most at the time. If you wanted just a partner, you could have left to find another. Even if you think you haven’t changed since that day. I know for sure you did, all your actions since then prove it. And though you may not understand, I know you wouldn’t have let me die willingly,” at that point, Subaru’s eyes started to glaze as if he was remembering something from a long time ago, “I know that for a fact.”

“…”

“I’m not going to lie. It’s hard for me to forgive right now. The wounds and memories are still too fresh. But despite that, I’m still greedy. I don’t want to forgive you, yet I want to try.”

Beatrice froze and slowly looked up to see Subaru’s face. His face held no hatred, no animosity, no sense of deceit. He looked. He looked. He looked…

His sincere expression, his soft gaze, his body language welcoming. He looked as if he loved Beatrice despite everything. Everything she did to him. Her heart can’t handle this. She wanted to both run away from him and into his arms. She has to decide but she can’t. She hated that she can’t!

He knelt down on one knee, opening his arms up, “We might never get what we had before, but I still want to try. Can we try together?”

Subaru gave a soft, warm smile,

“Beako?”

 

 

Beatrice rocketed towards Subaru nearly knocking the poor boy over, “I’m sorry! I’m sorry! Betty is so so so so sorry!!!”

“I know. I know,” he patted her softly on the head.

“We’ll fix this. Together.” Subaru cooed at her as she wept and wept.

 

It was a scene that many could not help but awe at. Where an older brother was comforting their long lost little sister. Finally, together again.

Of course, not everyone cared about a crying child.

Tia walked over to Subaru and the crying spirit, “…So. You still want that contract Su?”

Subaru chuckled at his other spirit’s lack of tact, “…I think I will.”

Beatrice tensed and tightened her grip on her ex-contractor. Subaru returned the favor by rubbing her head.

“Beako. I want a contract with you as well. But I need some time. I don’t want to make the same mistakes again. So how about we work up our relationship once more. And then, when we are both in a good place, we can discuss and form a contract.”

“…Alright. Betty understands.”

“Don’t let that make you think you’re not important to me. Let’s get to know each other again. I’ll tell you all my stories, all the things we did together, and everything I like about you.”

Beatrice started to sob even harder, “T-thank you…”

Subaru patted his little spirit and looked towards his larger spirit, “That okay with you Tia?”

Tia shrugged, “Eh, as long as I get to be with Su, I don’t care. However, the little girl must know she is lower on the pecking order.”

Beatrice turned her head and started glaring at the bigger spirit, “Betty believes she should be higher than the one who started a tantrum because she lost her toy, in fact.”

“Huh?” Tia glared at the little girl, “You want to say that again?!”

Before Beatrice could retort, Subaru cut in, “Girls. Knock it off.”

They both flinched and gazed sheepishly at the floor.

“Sorry Su.” “Betty is sorry.”

Subaru sighed.

He heard the sound of light footsteps, he knew those sounds anywhere. Anastasia laid her hand on Subaru’s shoulder.

“You did a great job,” she said as she squeezed.

“…Really?”

“Why would I think otherwise?”

Subaru chuckled, “It’s a first for me. I thought about the many things I wanted, and I realized I wanted everything. For myself. Even if it would be difficult to achieve, I wanted to gamble for it. Thank you for that, by the way, I was inspired by you.”

He couldn’t see but Anastasia blushed when she heard him say that, she coughed, “R-really? I’m glad you are taking what you said to me seriously.”

She then looked down at the spirit, still held in Subaru’s hands, gazing specifically at the fox around her neck. She saw an eye peak out and wink at her.

“Let’s talk as well, I believe we are also due for a much-needed conversation. I apologize for the lateness as well.”

That is what Anastasia seemed to determine from how Echidna looked at her.

Anastasia sighed.

Now, it’s my turn.

Notes:

EN1: One of my plans, ever since the beginning, was to have Beatrice have an understandable reasoning for abandoning Subaru but also be completely in the wrong. In the best case scenarios, I always imagined that Beatrice would try to help Subaru or at least be curious about him. But that wouldn't cause the Re:Forgotten scenario to fully develop. So ultimately, I thought that the worst case scenario was Beatrice succumbing to her insecurities, especially without Subaru's influence. But I also didn't like the idea of Beatrice being thrown away. And I didn't like the idea of Subaru fully forgiving her. Both didn't make sense or gave a bad taste to my mouth. So, I wanted a story where both occurred. And I wanted to write a story where Subaru had a valid reason for it. And well, that led to me being inspired to write this story. It's one of the 6 moments that made me want to write Two Forgotten Stars. So I'm glad we finally got to this point. Hope you liked it or at least understood why I wrote it this way.
