https://x.com/MoneN78849/status/1930673876004159609

They show off how I describe Subaru and Anastasia's current designs. They look gorgeous. The kimono and haori look so much better than I could ever imagine. They shine. Please check their artwork out. They are a phenomenal artist.

Next is another fanart comic by the wonderful OBSERVER, showing off Subaru's taste tests with hot sauce and comedic implications of such experiments: https://www.reddit.com/r/Re_Zero/s/iEl0Ufthzt

The artwork is wonderful, hilarious, and god I love how they draw the expressions. Their comics always inspire me to implement those jokes in a later chapter.

EN3: Finally, more stories! If you couldn't already tell, I am now posting three stories every week, Monday-Wednesday-Friday. If you hadn't seen the other two, check them out on my profile. This will increase two-fold with another weekly Sunday fic and a daily webnovel with my own original story, so stay tuned for news about that! And thank you to everyone who have been very supportive about delays as well as my health. Rest assured, my health is always number one to me. I do not want to die or burn out so I am making sure this schedule doesn't kill me. But god am I having fun. Seriously, writing is such a drug.

Chapter 14: With Rain, We Begin Again

Summary:

Anastasia & Echidna have a talk. Later, Subaru and Anastasia go on a little date...

Notes:

Thank you for your wonderful support! This story and the other stories I have been writing have been getting so much love and attention, I am eternally grateful for being given the chance to entertain you all with my writing. Enjoy this chapter!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

After the fiasco, they decided to take a quick break back home, Halibel’s friends would occupy the stall while they were away. Subaru took Beatrice on a walk around the neighborhood so that they can talk a bit more. Halibel and Zarestia decided to grab food for everyone. That left Anastasia, who was now sitting in her and Subaru’s room, with her lost and now found, friend. Friend. What would you call their relationship? Friendship? Allies? Mother, daug-

No… not again.

For Anastasia, it’s been a whirlwind experience the last few hours. Setting up a trap to capture a demon out for Subaru’s blood, calming Tia down from either going into a bloodlust induced rage or from leaving forever, and Subaru having a talk with his ex-spirit who may have actually put Subaru through the worst experience possible because she was being stupid.

As for Anastasia’s opinion on Beatrice? Net negative. Sure, she understood. Sure, Beatrice was working with limited information and reacted decently well to what would essentially be a spiritual equivalent of a mindfuck. And sure, she did help Subaru out when she did figure out he was getting tortured.

But that didn’t excuse anything: Beatrice made so many mistakes and those mistakes cost Subaru everything. Subaru may be on the road to forgiveness but a part of Anastasia was wary and will probably always be wary of the little spirit. She didn’t blame him for doing so, his greed wanted everything, she could not fault him for forgiving someone he loved. But she felt the spirit got let off easy for so much. So, if Subaru wasn’t going to hold a grudge, Anastasia might just do it for him.

“Would you like me to start or shall you do the honors?”

Oh right. Now she needs to deal with this. Her ‘Beatrice,’ in a way.

 

She didn’t know how to think or act. So, she defaulted.

Anastasia gave a polite smile, “It would be rude of tis gal to take the spotlight when ya were the one who wanted to discuss. The floor is all yers.”

Echidna looked oddly sad, “…I see. It seems you are wary of me. I do not blame you given how you spent the last few months. Though I would like you to know, my sister and I do know your accent isn’t…necessary.”

Anastasia sighed and frowned, “So you both really did follow us and listen to everything.”

The fox chuckled, “Apologies. While we meant no harm, I doubt that would be how you would see it. Given how intrusive we were, we were practically right next to you every step of the way. Well, almost. We didn’t follow you anywhere inappropriate,” she gave a wink in jest.

Anastasia felt slightly relieved and slightly mortified.

On the one hand, thank Od they didn’t follow us into the bathroom. On the other hand, that means they saw everything else.

Including when Anastasia and Subaru would sleep in the same bed. Or when Anastasia would hold Subaru’s hand when he was having a nightmare. Or when Anastasia would stare at him in the morning if she woke up earlier. Anastasia was starting to have flashbacks to every possibly embarrassing moment in the last few months and felt incredibly horrified.

Echidna seemed to notice, “Don’t worry, we won’t be nosy anymore and will keep everything a secret. Though I will say, it is quite funny how often you trip when looking at the boy’s- “

Anastasia threw her hands over the fox’s mouth, glaring and blushing, “Please. Stop talking.”

Echidna chuckled again, “Apologies, I couldn’t help myself. If it makes you feel any better, the boy has done it himself as a well, looking at you.”

Her face darkened even harder, though Anastasia understood what her old companion was doing, “…You don’t have to loosen me up, I don’t hate you.”

Now. I think.

The fox’s face looked melancholic, “I wasn’t sure. You never talked about me extensively so I assumed I must have made a mistake before we got separated.”

Anastasia chose not to show any reaction, “How did you figure it out? Or are you like Subaru?”

The fox shook her head, “Unfortunately, the boy is too unique, though my sister has some theories. She won’t tell me though, so you’ll have to pry it out of her later. No, it was mostly through my own deductive reasoning. Some parts of what I remember do not make sense, especially when I delved deep into them. For example, my memory of the last decade was that I was a scarf that was passed around by employees of Hoshin Trading Company.”

Interesting, I originally thought Gluttony would have caused Echidna to forget her whole time with me or at the very least morph her memories into believing she was with another person this whole time. But it seems it’s trying to justify why she was in my company for so long.

Echidna continued, “But the more I thought about it, the more I realized how illogical it was. Sure, my justification for the memories was sound: I was hiding in plain sight and could get information through the company’s network, allowing me to hear if anyone was searching for a certain ‘spirit.’ However, why did I know such intimate knowledge of the people within Hoshin Company such as the Triplets? Sure, I am a curious spirit, but why would I ever know a lot about Mimi’s favorite dishes or Tivey’s favorite books or Hetaro’s favorite stories. Why would an employee be so intimately involved in that and why would I remember it so well? Even more interesting, my mind kept trying to justify it, rationalizing it often to the point I almost tried to ignore it. It was only when I discussed things with Betty constantly, finding contradictions, and connected it to your stories, that I realized that there was a high possibility that you and I were connected in some capacity.”

So, Gluttony tries to connect the dots between gaps in the memory. It doesn’t seem to make completely new memories but tries to mold logical connections wherever possible. So, does it affect the detection of any contradictions? It seems likely given how difficult it was for Echidna to dissuade herself. Maybe there’s a way to ‘cure’ the effects of Gluttony if we can figure out how it exactly works.

Echidna then shuffled her paws, “Finally, there were two pieces of information that made me almost assured my theory was true: your story of Ricardo experiencing betrayal and how you reacted to seeing me.”

Anastasia nodded, “The story’s date must coincide with when you joined Hoshin Company. And how I reacted shows that, if I was at the same place as you were, I should have been able to see through your disguise.”

It was interesting and incredibly funny to Anastasia that the one pro of having an inept gate, is that she could see through the disguise of one specific spirit. Life was funny in how specific terrible things can work in your favor.

Echidna smiled, “Precisely.”

“…”

“…So, what do you remember during the end of Priestella?”

Anastasia stifled a grimace, “We were trying to escape from the Archbishop of Gluttony. Unfortunately, I was a non-combatant, which made things difficult. In a last-ditch attempt, I asked you to possess my body and used the flow method to try outrunning him. Unfortunately, we failed. He took my name.”

For the next few seconds, they stared at each other in awkward silence.

Echidna broke it, “Do you believe I abandoned you?”

Yes.

“No.”

“…Unfortunately, I cannot recall what happened during the last hour of the battle, I only remember waking up in Betty’s room and how she found me.”

Well, that’s convenient.

“Don’t worry, it’s not important.”

Echidna looked at her and sighed, “Child, this is important.”

“Why?”

“Your eyes. They are on the verge of tears.” The words hit Anastasia hard. She quickly tried her best to steel her expression, chastising herself for letting her guard down.

 “…It has been a long day,” Anastasia did not know how to feel at this point. Emotions she pushed down since the end of Priestella were starting to boil back up.

Fear over what happened to Echidna. Doubt if she willingly left her. Regret over her hasty decisions that cost her. Resentment over everything. Loneliness. The loneliness persisted.

The merchant gripped her hand trying to calm herself as Echidna spoke again, “It has…do you wish me to leave?”

No.

“Yes.”

The fox stared blankly before seemingly becoming resigned by Anastasia’s response, “Alright. As you wish.”

Anastasia closed her eyes.

Maybe this is for the best… it’s not like I can’t figure this out later. I’ll take my time. Whether I want to believe her or not-

 

Anastasia felt something furry and soft rub against her body. Something very familiar.

Opening her eyes once again, she saw that Echidna did not leave but merely curled up next to her.

“…Why are you still here?” Anastasia asked.

“…I don’t know.”

Anastasia scoffed but before she could retort, Echidna gave an answer, “I just have a feeling. That I would regret leaving you here. Without even trying to connect with you.”

“…”

“…When Betty would talk about her plans for the future, it would always involve spending every moment with the boy. She wanted to make up for lost time and to make sure every moment she spends with the boy will be done in earnest. So that even if his life is short compared to hers, she’ll make sure he will have no regrets choosing her.”

“…”

“And when I thought about you, how you have so little life left. I knew I would regret leaving you instead of trying every moment to reconcile. I may not have memories. But the way you look at me. The way you act despite trying to hide it. How you rub the area around your neck, as if it is an impulse ingrained from years of comfort. It tells me our relationship was more than just a simple collaboration. I may not know it, but you cared. And I, most likely cared for you.”

“…”

“I don’t know how to fix this. I don’t know if my decision is correct. And I don’t know whether I can make up for all of the lost time, for all the pain you suffered alone. But I want to try. I would like to try, even if I were to fail.”

“…”

Anastasia thought of Subaru. She thought of how she wanted to have something more with him. How life felt more fleeting than ever. She remembered how much he has changed in such a short time. How greedy he has become.

In some ways, she has changed as well. Before, she would have scoffed at how open her emotions were. But maybe that was a good thing. Because Echidna chose to stay because she saw her hurting.

And maybe Anastasia was okay with that. Maybe, she will be a hypocrite and choose to let her pain go in pursuit of her greed. Just like Subaru did.

Maybe, it was her turn to try as well.

Echidna shuffled in surprise as she felt Anastasia close in on her slowly, into a hug.

The merchant’s voice vibrated within the soft cushion of the fox, “For a time, I hated you.”

“…”

“I thought you abandoned me. Left me in order to escape, because they were looking for a spirit. That while our relationship was friendly, you ultimately viewed it as transactional. And I lost value when I was captured…” Anastasia tightened her grasp slightly.

The fox kept silent, choosing to listen, “…”

“I understood. Survival was always a priority for me. I would have been a hypocrite to not understand. But I still hated you.”

“…”

“And for months I was scared. Scared of dying and scared that everything I had will never return…it made me resentful. Despite all that, and all my resentment, I still wanted you back. I wanted everyone back.”

Tears started to drop out of the merchant’s eyes, she put all of her effort to spill the last bits of her feelings, “I don’t know either. I don’t know what to do. It all feels so broken. So messed up. I feel so empty. Burning with anger that doesn’t know where to go.”

Sniff. Sob.

One last drop, “But I think I would regret it everyday, if I never tried to get you guys back. I-I want you back. Even if my anger still remains.”

“…I would like you back as well,” Echidna rubbed her face into Anastasia, “I will accept it all: your rage, your resentment, your fears. Everything.”

Anastasia was tired of waiting. It was finally time to take everything back. She isn’t going to stop here. She’ll never stop until her last breath.

 

 

After having dinner, they returned to the festival, only for Halibel to give the two stars the rest of the night off, “Yep yep, skedaddle! You both have gone through a lot today, so get some rest. My subordinates have everythin’ runnin’ like clockwork, so don’t worry and have some fun before the day ends.”

Subaru and Anastasia looked at each other before looking at their spirits.

Beatrice just gave a solemn smile, “Betty can help watch the stall, in fact.”

The little spirit looked like she wanted to follow Subaru everywhere, anxiously tiptoeing where she stood, but she seemed resolute to allow Subaru and her to take their time mending the bridge. Anastasia saw Echidna, who still clung to Beatrice’s neck, giving her a wink and a smile.

“Have some fun with the boy,” is how Anastasia interpreted it.

Tia was Tia, “The house is empty. Go do it in there.”

Anastasia was about to reprimand the spirit but was beaten by Beatrice who screamed, “Why are you like this, in fact?! Let Betty’s Subaru take his time.”

Tia scoffed, “They’re taking too much time. And what do you mean by your Subaru. He is my Su. I have the contract with him!”

Beatrice grumbled and pouted, “Stupid wind spirit, doesn’t understand that humans need time to court-HEY!”

Tia was now holding Beatrice with one arm while giving her head a rub with her knuckle with the other, “I’ll show you who is stupid you little fucking- “

“Girls,” Subaru gave a very chilling smile, “Knock it off.”

Tia froze and put Beatrice on the ground, “Sorry Su.”

“Sorry Subaru,” Beatrice then quickly ran over to Subaru giving him one final hug before whispering in his ear.

Anastasia could not hear the little spirit, but she could definitely hear Subaru’s response, “I love you too Beako!” He said as he spun her around.

“Too loud and too fast, I suppose!”

 

The two stars began to explore the different stalls, eyeing different foods and games they could play, the sun was setting in the background as people began to put up lanterns to light the paths.

Subaru quickly grabbed some meat skewers for them to eat while they walked, “So, how was your talk?”

Anastasia almost choked, “Y-you know about her?”

Subaru chuckled, “Kind of. I connected the dots as Beatrice talked about her new sister on our walk and well, she gave you her scarf which suspiciously looked like the one you always wore.”

Anastasia pouted, “…I was going to tell you later. I just wanted to introduce you when things were less hectic.”

Subaru poked her cheek, “I ain’t blaming you, I understand,” Subaru walked as he got this faraway look, “We all have our secrets, even ones we can never say.”

…One day I’ll find a way for you to talk to me about all of them. Even about what really is that ‘danger sense’ of yours.

She finished her skewer and took Subaru’s hand, “It was a good talk. I don’t think my relationship with her will be as it used to be. But we’ll see how it goes.”

Subaru nodded sympathetically, “I understand. Beako and I are the same. It feels just like old times but also strangely new.”

“…Do you really want to forgive her for everything?”

Subaru looked pensive for one second before becoming resolute, “I know it may sound insane to you, but I do.”

Anastasia looked at the crowd of people around, seeing kids tugging at their parents to play a stall game and couples walking hand in hand.

“…I told you I won’t judge you for your decision, but why? Most people wouldn’t. Especially after all you went through.”

Subaru rubbed her hand softly, “Thanks for not judging me… I guess I just want to enjoy my life rather than be bogged down with resentment and hate.”

While Anastasia wouldn’t judge him for his decision, she was going to judge him for his reasoning.

He chuckled as he saw Anastasia look at him weirdly, and continued, “I know. Most people would probably say that they can see the good in people and want to accept them despite their flaws. But I’m not that good of a person. When I came to Lugunica, I was so prideful, filled with dreams and delusions, and expected everything to work in my favor. And then, reality hit me like a truck.”

He started to laugh more as he saw Anastasia’s question, “Truck is a type of car.”

Anastasia’s mouth opened as a sort of, “Ah, okay.”

She then motioned him to continue, “I get petty, spiteful, and I want people to hurt just as much as I feel. I ignore my problems sometimes and get stuck in my head about how people feel about me. I tend to focus on my own perspective rather than how others would see the situation-ow, hey!”

Anastasia pinched him, “Is there a point to this or are you going to keep talking negatively about yourself? Because if it’s the latter, I’m going to shut this down very quickly.”

Subaru rubbed his head, “Sorry Ana. The point is, I know that I can be a terrible person too. I have the potential to do bad as well as good. Everybody I know can do good and bad. I can focus on how terrible those traits are, be petty and never trust anyone ever again. Or I can choose to enjoy my life, despite how terrible people were to me. Of course, I won’t let them walk all over me. But I’d rather move on from my resentment than let it fester. I’d rather enjoy my time with people, rather than hate them for possibilities that don’t matter. Because even people who I thought I would never come to like, ended up proving me wrong.”

He finished off his speech by squeezing her hand and smiling at her, making her heart skip a beat.

“So, live happily rather than let hatred control you. Is that what you’re trying to say?”

Subaru tapped his chin, “Ya know? You really know how to say things more eloquently and with less words than me.”

Anastasia puffed up her chest, acting haughtily, “You are talking to the greatest businesswoman of the west.”

Subaru snapped his fingers, giving off faux overexcitement, “Amazing! Incredible! Can I get an autograph?!”

“5 holy coins.”

“I’m broke.”

“Don’t just say that! Try to barter.”

Subaru whined and waved their coupled hands back and forth with exaggerated motion, “But Anaaaaa! We’re on break.”

She marched with exaggerated swagger, “No breaks! Business never sleeps!”

After a few seconds, they burst out laughing and began walking normally once more. Subaru spotted a familiar game, “Oh wait, let’s try that,” he said as he dragged her over.

“Hey, hey! No need to get so excited, I’m right here.”

The stall Subaru brought them to was a standard ring toss game, common in most festivals in Kararagi.

“Wow, I can’t believe you guys have this here too,” Subaru said while whistling.

Anastasia had to ask, “This a common game back home?”

“Yeah, we had tons of different games: ring toss, goldfish scooping, shooting.”

“Shooting?”

“Oh yeah, I guess that makes sense considering you guys don’t have gunpowder. It will take a bit to explain, so I’ll tell you later, but essentially it’s a toy weapon where you shoot little paper objects at toys to knock them down and win them as prizes.”

Anastasia stared at Subaru, “We should- “ “-Make that.” Subaru finished off for her as she smiled.

“Am I that predictable?”

“Only when you’re money hungry. Which is all the time.”

“Little shit,” she started playfully punching him.

Until someone interrupted them, “So, y’all goin’ to play or am I goin’ to have to watch y’all flirt all day.”

They both flushed and nodded. The stall owner held out five fingers, “Five copper coins per person.”

Anastasia was about to haggle but Subaru chimed in, “Ya got a couple’s discount?”

The stall owner sighed, “I’ll only go down to 8 copper for two people.”

Subaru tapped his chin, “Really? I heard the stall down the street was offering 6 copper coins for two people. Let’s go see if they are still offering that, Ana.”

Before she could respond, Subaru started dragging her away, only for the stall owner to yell, “Wait, wait! Alright, fine, 5 copper coins for two people. That’s as low I can actually go.”

Subaru smiled as Anastasia felt so proud of him, “Deal.” He handed the copper coins as Anastasia whispered in his ear, “How did you know there was another stall with the same game?”

Subaru slightly flinched but whispered back, “I guessed. I saw there was not that many people here but tons heading that way, so I made a gamble.”

Anastasia giggled, “How sneaky of you~. I really have infected you.”

He nudged her as he went to grab the rings, “Anastasia Syndrome is a slow and insidious killer. Now I’m all sneaky, soon you’ll see me swimming naked in coins.”

She swiped at him, he dodged, and then he threw the ring. The first one landed on a tower close to him. He threw the second. It also hit the same tower. He threw his last ring. Only for it to miss.

Subaru grimaced, “It’s been way too long since I’ve played.” His prize was a small wooden toy of Hoshin.

Anastasia rolled her sleeves up and smirked at him, “Watch a professional at work.”

Subaru smiled back, “Be my guest.”

 

She got all three rings in on the furthest tower, getting her the choice of the top prize.

Subaru’s jaw dropped, “So much for my masculinity.”

Anastasia pushed his jaw back up, “Was there every any there in the first place?”

Subaru pouted and then pinched her nose, “Loli-stasia.”

She poked him back, “Little shit.”

“Please. Choose your prize and leave.”

The stall owner looked like he was dying from watching them interact.

Anastasia relented and began looking at the different stuffed animals, there was an earth dragon, a bunny, a bird, and a dog.

“Hmmm, which one do you think I should get- “she paused as she noticed Subaru staring at the bunny one.

“Subaru,” she shook him out of his stare, “Do you like that one?”

Subaru blinked and quickly shook his head, “A-ah, not particularly. You can choose whichever you want.”

Her gaze went down as she saw his hand get clammy and shaky, gripping back and forth.

…I need to ask him later about that. For now, no rabbits anywhere near him.

She grabbed his hand, calming him down, and smiled before pointing towards the earth dragon, “That one please.”

 

They continued walking through the festival, checking out various stalls, eating food, and having a good time. Until, finally, they decided to rest by the benches, stuffed with food.

“You know, we could probably sell some of our sauces in batches to those food stalls. I bet they would love having new tastes to experiment with.”
Subaru messed with her hair, “I thought we were taking a break Ana.”

Anastasia flicked him on the nose, “Again. Business never sleeps.”

“Is your name business?”

“It could be.”

“Anastasia Business Hoshin. Truly, a name fitting for a merchant.”
“Damn right.”

They continued to banter until night fully arrived, bringing with it clouds.

Subaru frowned.

Anastasia was confused what changed his mood, “What’s wrong? Not a fan of rain?”

Subaru shook his head, “It’s not that. I just wanted to see the stars.”

“Oh, come now, we see them all the time, there’s always tomorrow.”

“Yeah, but I wanted to have them shining when I do this. Tsk. Oh well,” Subaru stood up and quickly spun, facing in front of her, and reached into a hidden pocket within his haori.

Anastasia was confused before her eyes widened as Subaru brought out a small box, wrapped with a bow.

“Subaru, what’s this for?”

He smiled warmly, “Happy Birthday Ana!”

 

Wait, I-what?

“W-wait it’s not my birthday- “

Subaru raised an eyebrow, “It’s in the fifth month of the rainy season, tenth day, right? Or I guess March 10th, back where I come from. That’s tomorrow.”

With everything happening over the past few months, Anastasia forgot. But Subaru didn’t, it seems.

Anastasia stared at him and nodded, “Yeah. That’s right. How did you know? I never told you.”

Subaru shrugged, “I remember Emilia told me once after one of her trips to the Royal Capital, I think you guys had a chat or something and it came up. I didn’t think much of it at the time, but I remembered a few weeks back.”

Anastasia kept staring at him, half in shock, half in wonder, “…You remembered my birthday, for so long.”

“Of course, it’s no big deal.”

It is a big deal! From how you talked, we were not close! And you still remembered my birthday!!

She didn’t actually remember her real birthday, given her status as an orphan, so she chose one based on when she chose her name: a symbolic birth for her. Something that she cherished for a while but neglected as she grew older. And this stupid boy managed to remember it despite having no obligation to.

Subaru gestured to the box, “Well, are you going to open it?”

Anastasia knocked herself out of her stupor and complied, pulling the ribbon and opening the box.

 

Inside were doll replicas of her whole camp: her, Julius, Ricardo, the Triplets, and even Joshua.

 

She didn’t know what to say. Actually, there was one thing she noticed.

“Where are you?” She blurted out without thinking.

Stupid. Stupid! That’s a rude thing to say to someone’s gift. And it’s not like he is a part of my camp…

Unlike what she expected, Subaru just gave a bigger grin, “Funny you should mention that.” He brought out a second gift, the same box and ribbon.

Two gifts?!

She grabbed it and opened the new box quickly: it was filled with dolls tailored after Subaru, Halibel, Zarestia, and Patrasche.

Subaru scratched his chin, “Unfortunately, I didn’t know Beatrice and her sister were going to join us until now, so I couldn’t make any dolls for them, but I’ll do it once I have some time and – Ana?!”

Subaru’s heart dropped as he realized Anastasia was crying.

…You stupid boy. You keep doing this to my heart. How do you keep finding ways to make me love you even more?

“A-ana are you okay? I’m sorry! I didn’t mean to- “

He was interrupted by Anastasia running into him for a hug, “Just shut up for a sec, you little shit. I’m not crying because I’m sad. I’m crying because I’m happy. Thank you. Thank you so much for the gifts.”

He quickly became relieved and patted her on the back, “Of course, it’s the least I could do for all you have done for me.”

She was about to tell him how much he had done for her, when she felt the small droplets of rain hit her hair.

Subaru raised his hand up into the air, grimacing, “Ah, well that sucks. Guess we should head back. Man I wanted to walk around a bit more.”

Anastasia began to remember a legend related to the festival. A legend that can only occur when it rains, and between two people.

I did promise myself, no holding back anymore.

The rain started to drizzle, “Subaru, I have something to give you as well, could you close your eyes?”

Subaru raised his eyebrow, “Wait, what for, it’s your birthday and mine is next month?”

She rolled her eyes, “Think of it as payment for the gift.”

“It’s free, you don’t have to- “

“Subaru.”

“Okay, closing my eyes.”

He complied.

 

 

Natsuki Subaru felt the rain hit his head and body, making him feel damp all over.

I wonder what’s taking her so long, is it really that big of a sur-

Subaru’s thoughts were interrupted by something warm and soft touching his lips. His eyes opened in shock as he looked into Anastasia’s eyes, which were closed right in front of him.

She was kissing him, passionately and slow.  Their lips parted. Her eyes were open, soft and gazing at him lovingly. Her cheeks red and rosy. Her hair was damp but shining under the glow of the glintstone lamps.

For a moment, Subaru was absolutely entranced.

Subaru reacted as expected, “Hubwah, uh, yuh, wha-huh?”

Anastasia giggled and continued hugging him, “That’s my first gift. And this is your second.”

She got close to his face again, “I love you, Natsuki Subaru. And I, Anastasia Hoshin, declare that you will be mine, even if I have to fight the world itself. I'll give you an offer you can't refuse.”

She kissed him again, as the rain continued to fall around them.

 

In the legends of Banan, there is a story of a star-crossed couple dating back to the aftermath of the Great Fire that ravaged the plains of pre-Kararagi. The story goes that the couple were a pair of enemies, scions of two warring households. However, when the Great Fire ravaged the land and destroyed all who lived there, it left the two as orphans. The last two living people of their desolate homes, they originally set out to end each other’s lives. However, through circumstance and conflict, they ended up falling in love with each other. Seeking to make amends and start anew, they declared their love for each other, and with their declarations, came the first rain and storms. This rain brought an end to the fire and restored the fertile land so that people were able to begin anew once more.

It is said that: if a person were to kiss their loved one during the Great Rain Festival, and while it is raining, their wish will be granted, and their love will be blessed eternally by the souls of the two-star crossed lovers.

May these two be blessed and be given a brighter tomorrow, as their story begins again, from zero.
