He could barely speak a word…is that a good thing though? They said it was a good thing. But what if they’re wrong?  And who the fuck says ‘cat got your tongue?!’  Did I even use that right?! I should have asked Subaru again before trying it?! What if I completely misinterpreted its meaning?! Ah, I’m so stupid! Stupid! Stupid! STUPID!

To make matters worse, she never really had a good motherly role model to help guide her on the path to womanhood. She mostly figured out everything on her own and by questioning some of the courtesans of Banan. As a result, her only methods of seduction included: lots of physical affection, double entendres, and very provocative teasing. All of which she could barely withstand herself from how embarrassing it looked and sounded to her. It took so much effort to prevent herself from screaming about how absolutely stupid she must look. Leaving for the bathroom was more of a tactical retreat for her than for Subaru to finally wake up.

“…Are you alright Ana?”

The merchant was startled out of her internal embarrassment, nearly tripped on her own feet, and quickly composed herself before turning to face the source of the voice: Echidna. She was sitting at the kitchen table, with a look of genuine concern on her face.

“Fine, fine. Totally, fine. I’m great… So great. Good morning, by the way,” she gave a thumbs up and a shaky smile before feeling embarrassed for being caught off guard so easily, “How are you Echidna?”

Echidna raised an eyebrow, “I am quite fine as well, though I do wonder if your definition of ‘fine’ is similar to mine considering you spent the last few minutes screaming into your hands.”

Anastasia’s smile cracked, “…Well you know what they say: words change with time! Ha. Ha! Ha.”

“…Right. Is this because of the boy- “

Anastasia quickly dove and covered her mouth, whispering, “Subaru could be coming down any second, I really don’t want him to think I’m talking about him behind his back.”

She also really didn’t want him to think she was this bad at romance. She needed to maintain the image of a ‘cool and experienced older woman.’ Not like Emilia, who, from how Subaru described her, seemed to be incredibly naïve romance-wise. Her gamble was such: show Subaru that she was interested, won’t make him wait for love and affection, and can offer him all the things those other girls can’t.

The fox quickly shook the merchant’s hand off of her, chuckling at the same time, “…And what would we be talking about behind his back? Perhaps your imminent plans to woo him?”

She blushed, “…”

“…Oh, you’ve went that far? Tia will be happy-“
“No!” She quickly looked around. Coast was clear, she went back to whispering, “I’m not baby trapping Subaru.”

“So, you have considered it?”

Anastasia looked mortified, “Absolutely not!”

It was hard to tell, but Echidna was grinning like a madwoman.

Anastasia did notice and promptly started pouting.

“Apologies, I always wanted to try teasing. I see why people like to do it.”

“…”

“…But tell me, what’s bothering you?”

“…Can we talk somewhere more private?”

Echidna nodded and jumped onto her shoulders.

 

 

“I thought you were going to grab a snack, in fact? Why did you bring the girl?”

Anastasia turned to the fox on her shoulders, “…I thought we were going somewhere no one else was going to be.”

Echidna jumped down, “Would you have preferred Tia or Halibel’s room?”

Anastasia stared, “You know what? Good point.”

She then looked at the little spirit, “Wait, I thought spirits don’t eat.”

Beatrice turned the page of the book she was reading, “We don’t need to eat. Doesn’t mean we don’t enjoy the taste, in fact. Now, why are you here?”

Anastasia tried to put on her normal façade, until Echidna responded and point blank blew it up, “Ana doesn’t know how to woo the boy.”

Beatrice looked up from her book, blinked, and then stared at the merchant, “You? Don’t know how? In fact?”

Feeling slightly betrayed, and her normal mask already destroyed, Anastasia glared at her old friend while gritting her teeth, “I didn’t even say anything.”

“Ana. Though I may not have my memories, you and the boy are not hard to figure out. You both do not have any relationship experience. It would be unrealistic to expect both of you to know what to do, especially in the beginning.”

“…” The merchant really liked pouting today.

Echidna ignored it, “And that is why I brought you to the best person who can help you.”

She laid a paw on Beatrice, the little spirit looked at her sister. Then back at Anastasia. Then quickly back at her foxlike sister, pointing a finger at herself, “Me?!”

Anastasia had a similar reaction, “Her?!”

“Should I expect a ‘you’ as well?” Echidna chuckled at her own joke as both girls glared at the fox, “Jokes aside. She is your best option, Ana.”

The merchant disagreed, “That is not true, there’s- “

She then paused. She thought about it. Tia would just tell her to jump Subaru immediately.

The merchant still slightly disagreed, “Okay, but there is-“

She paused again. She thought about it. Halibel was fine. But his last advice was to essentially wing it. Also, she was not asking a guy for tips on seducing men.

The merchant was neutral, “No, but- “

She paused for the third time. Her camp was out, for obvious reasons, but even if they were here, she wouldn’t ask them. They wouldn’t know what to do either. The only other person she could possibly think of was the miko. Yes. The miko she met literally a month ago. Absolutely not.

The merchant was having a slight crisis about the people she keeps around her, “…”

Echidna could tell what she was thinking, “And unfortunately: I do not have experience seeing many relationships blossom either. So, my dear sister may be your best bet.”

Beatrice looked like she wanted to be anywhere other than here, “I don’t think- “

Anastasia grabbed her before she could start leaving, looking slightly manic, “…Please.”

Beatrice looked into her eyes, and saw sincere desperation, she then sighed, “…Fine, in fact.”

Echidna clapped her paws, “Great. I’ll let you two have some privacy then.”

She then scampered away, out of the room.

Silence pervaded the air. Both of them realized what just happened.

Beatrice broke the silence, “…It seems sister decided we should get to know each other as well, in fact.”

Anastasia agreed, “…It appears so.”

“…”

“…”

“…”

“…Listen-“

“You don’t have to pretend to like Betty, in fact.”

Anastasia’s eyes widened, “You think I hate you?”

Beatrice shrugged, “If Betty was like you, caring about Subaru, and heard that one of the only reasons Subaru suffered was because Betty chose to throw him away and never saved him out of some stupid fear, then Betty would hate herself as well, in fact.”

“…It’s not exactly hatred.”

Beatrice raised her eyebrow as Anastasia explained, “I don’t really hate you. I dislike what you did. I don’t think you should be forgiven. But hatred isn’t my feeling towards you. It’s more akin to… frustration. I’m frustrated.”

“…About what, I suppose?”

“Subaru. He just let his malice go; he didn’t even flinch when you came back. And he let you back in. Sure, I asked him, and he says he hasn’t really forgiven you. And he also seems to hold some bits of a grudge. But compared to how much he suffered? It feels like he just ignored everything he went through. And simply chose to understand your position. As if that matters more than his own emotions. I know we’re different people. But a part of me feels like it isn’t really a personality aspect but rather…like he has to do so. As if it’s a habit.”

Beatrice began to understand, “As if he holds no worth in himself. Subaru doesn’t care because, why would he care about something that he thinks holds no value.”

“…It was worse during the beginning. He would hurt himself at the drop of a coin. Nowadays, he’s gotten a lot better, rapidly might I add. But when it comes to other people? He always puts them first.”

Even her. Anastasia’s heart felt warm that Subaru would prioritize her. But it also ached, seeing him care so little about himself. She loved that he was beginning to change, using her as a role model. But would he ever put himself over her? What if her love becomes a chain for him…she doesn’t want him to die for her. The possibility…no. She can’t even think of it.

Anastasia finished off her explanation, “So no, I don’t hate you. I am more frustrated by your presence. As it feels like Subaru is falling slightly back into bad habits, even though he has improved immensely.”

The room became quiet once more. Anastasia felt she said her piece. She waited until it seemed Beatrice gathered her thoughts and broke the silence herself.

“…Betty was jealous of you, you know?”

Beatrice looked like she was waiting for a retort. The merchant didn’t. Anastasia motioned her to go on. The little spirit sighed.

“Betty hated that you would always end up helping her contractor when Betty couldn’t. Escaping the Royal Capital, helping him with his panic attacks, giving him warmth and affection. Betty wished she could have been the one to help him heal. But that is a selfish and childish desire. Because Betty could have never helped him like you did.”

“…Have I helped him?” If Anastasia were honest, she feels like she has helped him a little. But also, she feels like she hasn’t done a single thing. Subaru sometimes seems like he took all those steps forward himself. She never told him how to improve. He just learned and became better without any intervention.

Beatrice snorted, “Humility doesn’t fit you. But Betty can understand if you have no confidence. It may not seem like it because you assume it is normal. Because it comes so naturally to you that you wouldn’t question it as special. Despite Betty not having any memories, she can deduce something that only you seem to have done for the boy: you listened.”

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, but Beatrice kept speaking, “You listen, ask questions, and constantly get Subaru to explain everything he knows. Betty knows the personalities of people back in that clown’s mansion. No one is as curious as you. So most likely, Subaru has never had someone this interested in his life. And it shows: Subaru looks like he enjoys speaking to you, every time. In addition, you are doing something to his confidence just by doing so, you are making it so that he feels valued. As if his words matter and have weight. Not just his actions, but what he talks about and what he believes in. Betty believes not many people have done such a service for him, only valuing him based on what he has done for them.”

Beatrice looked pensive before finally finishing, “Betty may not remember, but she believes the only people who may come close, would be Betty or the grey-haired idiot. The idiot would most likely be inquisitive, like your nature as a merchant. However, he would be too swamped in work and would be unable to do it often. Betty, on the other hand, would dedicate all the time in the world to her contractor. However, you have one thing over Betty: being human. Betty’s nature as a spirit makes her… nonconfrontational. Betty hates to admit but, Betty would not argue or challenge her contractor, unlike you. You have challenged him. You have tackled his beliefs. And you listen to his reasons. You try to understand but still offer counterpoints. You care. Betty believes that is your strongest point.”

Anastasia was astonished, “…Is this your way of telling me how to seduce Subaru?”

Beatrice gave a soft smile, “Betty thinks you are overthinking things. Subaru is simple. While I’m sure your seduction tactics have an effect, Betty believes the best way you can ‘win his heart’ over the other two, is by playing to your best attributes.”

Anastasia smiled this time, “So just do as I’ve always done. It sounds…stupid.”

Beatrice snorted, “Love always is. Toska was the same.”

“Who’s Toska?”

“…An idiot. Toska was a boy who thought he needed to prove himself to marry his childhood friend. Idiot didn’t even realize that she was head-over-heels for him because he saved her from a dragon, in fact. Even if he didn’t do such a thing, the girl already loved him for his kind nature. He didn’t need to be confident, suave, or cool: she loved him because he was genuinely heroic. Honestly, the boy needed better male role models…”

Despite her harsh words, Beatrice seemed to reminisce about the boy fondly.

Anastasia looked at the little spirit slightly differently now, “…Thank you.”

Beatrice didn’t look at her but simply nodded and stared elsewhere, “…Thank you as well.”

Anastasia could tell the spirit was thanking her for more than just the conversation.

 

Anastasia started to get up and walk towards the door, it was already time to get the day started and eventually go to the festival and start selling condiments once again.

However, she looked back one last time, “…Beatrice, I may be frustrated now. But that can change. I don’t think I can forgive you… but with time, I might be able to look past it.”

“…Betty understands. Betty can’t forgive herself either… even if her contractor might. Still, Betty wants to try.”

Anastasia nodded, she then smiled mischievously, “Should I call you Beako then?”

Beatrice smiled back, “Betty would rather die, in fact.”

The merchant laughed, “We’ll work on it.”

Anastasia didn’t expect it, but that conversation felt more worthwhile than she ever thought possible.

 

 

Beatrice didn’t expect it, but it felt like she might be able to get along with Subaru’s future lover.

She still sighed just as the purple-haired woman left, taking out her book once more to read.

…Now if only Betty’s Subaru could realize it himself. That girl is going to be fighting an upward battle, no doubt, in fact.

Beatrice heard the soft pitter patter of her sister’s footsteps come in, without looking up, “So you’ve finally returned, thankfully, your contractor isn’t as annoying as Betty thought- Sister?”

She caught a glance at the fox and noticed how absolutely terrified she looked. Her face looked twitchy, her eyes anxious, her body shaken. It’s like she saw a ghost or a monster.

“…” her legs were still shaking.

Beatrice stopped reading, her voice laced with concern, “What’s wrong? What happened?”

The fox didn’t even look at her sister, gazing downwards, “…Has the boy ever met our creator?”

Beatrice was confused before she connected the dots, He must have met that version of ‘Mother’ from Sanctuary.

“What did he say?” Beatrice was hoping that her sister’s relationship with Subaru wasn’t damaged. Especially after it seems her conversation with Anastasia went better than expected.

Echidna looked up, her mind stabilizing slightly, “…Don’t worry. The boy and I are fine. It’s just… I do not know what the creator did to him. But he was not happy hearing how similar I was to her, at first.”

“…Did he threaten you?”

“…Not necessarily. He was being protective,” she took a breath, trying to calm herself down, managing to get a small smile, “A part of me is happy Anastasia found someone who cares about her so much.”

Beatrice had a bad feeling, “And the other part?”

The fox’s smile dropped, her eyes looked like they saw the abyss, “The other part of me is scared what would happen if anything were to happen to Ana. And how the boy would react.”

 

 

“What did you say to her?”

Subaru flinched. They grabbed some leftover sandwiches they made last night for a quick breakfast and began heading out to the festival. Halibel and Tia had already left earlier. Anastasia passed by Echidna on her way to meet Subaru, and she looked positively spooked. She was going to check on the poor fox but the spirit just told her they can talk later, quickly running back to her room.

He looked very guilty, “Sorry. We had a bit of a misunderstanding… I may have lashed out at her by mistake. I’ll apologize to her later.”

Anastasia was surprised, Subaru wasn’t exactly the malicious or wrathful type of person, what would have caused such a reaction.

She motioned to grab his hand, holding it softly, “What was the misunderstanding?”

He flinched when she held his hand and seemed to hold it half-heartedly. Is something wrong with him?

Subaru furrowed his brow, “...She sounded like someone I knew. I thought maybe she was similar to her, but it doesn’t seem like she is. They’re completely different actually. Scarfdona seems… caring. Like she actually cares instead of pretending.”

She took note of who this ‘someone’ could be, but there was also another question she had, “Scarfdona?”

Subaru brightened up a bit, “You like it? It’s because she’s a scarf and her name is Echidna,” she noticed Subaru twitch when he said the name, “Scarf-dna. Scarfdona.”

…Note to self: ask Echidna and Beatrice about that.

She snorted and turned away, “Terrible. So terrible.”

He tried to poke her cheek, but stopped himself last second, “You know you like it.”

Anastasia did like it, she did have one problem though, “You know, I noticed you haven’t given me a nickname yet, despite everyone else getting one. Why is that?”

She expected Subaru to get flustered, but he actually looked genuinely distraught, “I-I didn’t mean for that. I guess I just, ya know- I mean-”

Anastasia tried to comfort him, but he let go of her hand, “Subaru that wasn’t- “

Subaru panicked, “No, you did nothing wrong. This is just a me problem. I just, sorry. I don’t want you to think I care for you less-”

Where is this coming from? It feels out of nowhere…

“…Subaru.”

He kept rambling, “Like I care for you a lot, it’s just I didn’t know if I should- “

“Subaru.”

“-give you one because I wasn’t sure if I could really give you what you want and I doubt I can because I’m so indecisive and you don’t deserve that-“

“SUBARU!”

He shut up quickly, “…”

“…What’s wrong? Why does it seem like you’re suddenly avoiding me? Did I do something wrong?”

He vigorously shook his head, both of them had stopped walking now and were standing in the middle of an empty street, “You didn’t do anything wrong. Again, this is a me issue. I just…”

“Just, what?”

“…I don’t think you should love me.”

 

What kind of dragon shit is he spewing right now?

“…Are you an idiot?”

Subaru looked at her like something was gnawing at his core, “Yes.”

She pinched her nose, “Actually, never mind, you’re not an idiot. This is just plain lunacy. Because why in the world would a rational person ever say such a thing.”

Subaru, for some stupid reason, agreed again, “I am crazy, but I know one thing, you deserve better than me.”

It’s been a while since she got so angry, but Anastasia was starting to remember that terrible conversation during their journey to Priestella. The memory was exacerbating her anger even more.

“Okay, then who do I deserve? Give me examples.”

“…”

“Come on tell me. If you know who can be a better fit for me, list them off.”

“…A merchant.”

“See? You can’t even list an actual person. And even if there was a ‘merchant’ you knew that could fit, I wouldn’t want them given that a lot of them are lying manipulative sacks of shit.”

She knew she was being hypocritical, but Anastasia was too angry to care.

“A knight or a mercenary, someone like Juli- “

Anastasia growled, “Don’t you dare finish that sentence. If I wanted Julius, I would have chosen him and made him mine when I first met him. Could there be sparks? Maybe. I don’t know and I don’t care. We are friends and he is my knight. That is all.”

Subaru looked slightly irritated now, “Then anybody. Anyone would be better than me!”

Her anger was skyrocketing, “You are not just anybody. I wouldn’t fall in love with some random person. I fell in love with you. What’s making you so adamant that I shouldn’t- “

“…Because I love Emilia and Rem still!”

 

He braced himself for her to be angry, closing his eyes. Only to open them and see Anastasia with her hands on her hips, eyebrow raised.

Rather than the rage she was exuding previously, she just looked slightly annoyed.

 

“So?”

 

Subaru was shocked, “That doesn’t bother you?!”

 

I mean, yeah.

 

“Of course it does, what woman doesn’t hate that the guy they like, loves another. Especially when he is in love with not just one, but two. But I’m late for the party so I can’t really complain. Even so, it doesn’t matter.”

Before Subaru could say anything, Anastasia continued.

“As Hoshin said, ‘love is like an auction, doesn’t matter who is first, just who wins.’ So, what if you love them? I’ll work my way into your heart too. Are they number one and two? I’ll find a way to overthrow them. You like spending time with them? I’ll make it so you enjoy my company way more. They make you happy? I’ll give you thousands of reasons to be happier with me. They may have certain assets I don’t, so I’ll just make sure you see the value in mine. Convince you that I’m better and more irresistible. Love is war, and I don’t intend to lose, nor do I intend to share.”

He looked so confused, genuinely baffled, “I’m not worth that much effort.”

She then tapped a finger on his heart, smiling up at him, “You can’t decide that. I can. I decide whether someone has value, and to me, you have the greatest value of anyone in the world. You’re smart, handsome in your own way, and kind. Above all: we get along better than any person I’ve ever met before.”

Subaru tried to step back, “You can meet someone better.”

She grabbed his haori, and pulled him back closer, face to face, “I don’t want someone better. I want you. I’m the greediest gal in the world, so I won’t stop until all of you is mine. My bid is simple: I’ll make you the happiest man now, and I’ll continue to make you the happiest man until the day I die. And unlike the others, I won’t make you wait, nor will I ever stop trying to be better.”

 

Her smiled turned resolute, eyes filled with determination, “Even if it takes days, months, years: one day you’ll say, ‘I love Anastasia, and she is the only one for me.’ And I’ll accept no less than that as a total victory.”

 

Subaru looked at her with both solemn resignation and admiration, he then looked away guilty, “…What if that never happens? What if I end up loving them still?”

Anastasia tipped his chin to her once more, and stared lovingly into his eyes, “Not possible. I can’t control how you feel but I won’t ever stop trying. Thinking of failure as a possibility has no meaning to me. The simple thing is: if you love me, and I love you, I’ll make sure nothing gets in our way.”

She then looked a touch vulnerable, “…Do you love me Subaru?”

…I can’t help it if he doesn’t. I won’t force him. But if there is even a chance…

He then hesitated, he looked like he had an answer he wanted to say, his eyes conflicted, until finally, “…I do. I can’t lie. I thought of it. Of saying I don’t. But my heart felt like it would break. It’s why I felt so terrible earlier. Why I ‘avoided you.’ I don’t want to treat you like an afterthought. You’re special to me. I just want to give you everything. Like you want. But I can’t. Even after everything, my heart still shares a space for them…I don’t want to give you hope. It would be too cruel.”

Rather than disappointed, Anastasia smiled, “And again, I’ve accepted that. But now I know there is a chance. And where there is a chance, there is a way to win. I promise you Subaru, I’ll win your heart and give you the happiest future possible.”

She then pulled him close, non-verbally asking.

 

Despite everything, he reciprocated once more, bringing his lips forward. She pulled his chin close, and she let passion take hold.

One.

Two.

Three.

Four.

It tasted sweet. Anastasia’s declaration was now officiated.

Five.

Six.

Seven.

Eight.

They separated, gasping for breath.

As they separated, Anastasia gave him a smile and wink, “Prepare yourself: this gal is going to take you on the best dates you’ve ever had.”

His cheeks blushed, his eyes finally looked relaxed, “…I’m looking forward to it.”

She took the chance to grab his hand once more, no more half-hearted measures, “Now come on, Poobaru, let’s not make the others wait.”

They began to walk towards the festival again.

Subaru’s eyebrows looked like they were about to go into the sky, “Poo-what now?”

“Poobaru. You know? Little shit. Subaru. Poo-baru. My little poo.”

“Absolutely not.”

“You love it.”

“…”

“…”

“…Ana-pop.”

Anastasia didn’t understand, “I was expecting something unoriginal like Ana-tan.”

He pinched her hand, “Hey, I can be original! Besides, you’ll like this, it’s named after a candy from my home.”

Her cheeks went pink, “Oh~, is it cause you think I’m sweet?”

Subaru smiled a shit-eating grin, “It’s called a lollipop.”

“…”

“…”

“…I’m going to kill you.”

“You can try,” he dodged a swipe from her, still holding onto one hand and laughing.

“Come here, my little Poo!” She sounded angry but her face was joyous.

“Mmm, nope! I don’t think I will Ana-pop,” he sounded mischievous, but his face looked like a weight was lifted.

Both stars continued their banter as they walked on, hand in hand.

And thus, Anastasia’s love assault began.

Notes:

EN1: Ah young love, I swear writing this chapter was too fun.

Chapter 17: Hate and Love

Summary:

We look into our favorite black star's mind a bit...

Notes:

Enjoy!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Natsuki Subaru is not an idiot.

 

Okay maybe he is an idiot. But he isn’t stupid. He isn’t dense. He can see where the cards fall.

Subaru knew for a while now about Anastasia’s growing attraction for him.

When she would linger at his touch longer than the previous. When she would watch him when she thought he wasn’t looking. When she would wake up in the morning and pretend to be asleep for just a bit longer, so that they can stay in each other’s arms.

And he knew about his own growing attraction for her.

When he would go looking for her whenever there was a moment of respite. When he would feel warm at her smile and giddy at her touch. When he would wake up from her movement and pretend he was also still asleep, so that he could continue embracing her.

He hated it. He hated this feeling just as much as he kept searching for it.

Because he didn’t deserve it. He didn’t deserve Anastasia. He declared his love for two women already. And look what happened?

One was forgotten and one had forgotten him.

He couldn’t fall in love again. Never again. Every time he fell in love. Everything goes wrong. He fell in love with one woman and sacrificed so much for her. He fell in love with another and she sacrificed so much for him.

What would happen if he fell in love with Anastasia? What would happen to her?


And what about Anastasia? She deserved better than…this! This disgusting waste of a human being. Someone who can barely function. Who can barely live without someone else giving him a reason. Someone who wears the mask of a normal person but is actually a powder keg on the cusp of explosion.

 

Natsuki Subaru hated one thing more than the Witch Cult: himself. He hated how weak he was. How stupid he was. How disgusting he was. He hated that he hadn’t learned a thing since he got here! He hated how easily he got caught. He hated how despite however many loops, he could never convince Felix to let him live. He hated that he could never consider him an enemy. He hated that he wanted Felix to be happy. He hated how much Anastasia had to suffer for him to get his shit together. He hated how often he dreams of his old camp, of Rem, of Emilia. He hated how often he dreamed of killing them. He hated how often he dreamed of reuniting with them. He hated how he dreamed of being in Emilia’s arms, sharing a kiss with her once more. He hated that he sacrificed so much for her, only to be discarded. He hated how he waited so long, only for any reciprocated feelings to never come at all. He hated how childish he was. He hated that he expected her to return his feelings. He hated that he was so entitled. He hated that he was so selfish. He hated that Emilia had such a worthless knight such as him. He hated how he dreamed of seeing Rem’s face smiling at him once again. He hated how she tortured him. He hated how he forgave her so easily. He hated how attached she was to him. He hated how much he came to treasure her. He hated that he regretted not leaving with her. He hated how he didn’t regret saving Emilia. He hated how he regrets not telling Rem how much he loved and appreciated her. He hated that he put her second to Emilia. He hated that Emilia had to deal with him loving another woman. He hated that Emilia never truly understood what he meant. He hated that he still loved her for it. He hated that Rem went along with whatever he wanted. He hated that he loved her for her poisonous devotion. He hated that he was so indecisive. He hated how often he had regrets. He hated that he got attached to people so often. He hated that he wanted his two loves to be happy without him. He hated that he wanted his two loves to be happy with him. He hated his two loves. He hated that he still loved them.

 

Ever since he left that prison, he has hated everything and everyone. He hated them. He hated that he still loved them. He hated that he cherished them. He hated that he still wanted them near him.

Hate is all he has left in this world.

 

No. That was wrong.

There was one thing, one person he could not hate. He didn’t like her. Now? He couldn’t help but… admire her. Cherish her. And from her, he began to cherish others again. To care again. Truly care, not…what he usually did. Halibel. Tia. Even Beako again. And who was that person?

 

Anastasia.

 

How ironic.

 

When he left that prison, he was prepared to embrace his hatred. To let the world burn. When he saw the merchant candidate, he was prepared to use her as a hostage. To let them suffer as he had. What did it matter anyhow? He was already abandoned by everyone, no one could save him even if they wanted to. He had to survive on his own. To die on his own. Just like always.

But that didn’t happen. She also suffered. She also was forgotten.

But why should he care? She never thought much of him, used him up and threw him away during the White Whale hunt. Everyone abandons him. Everyone uses him. Everyone hates him. That’s how it has always been. And that was always how it was going to be.

“I’m truly slothful ain’t I?”

…But how could he abandon someone when they looked like that? When they reminded him so much of himself. Of being lost. Of being forgotten. Of being alone.

Still, this was Anastasia Hoshin. One of the most greedy and selfish women he has ever met. Even though Priestella showed him new sides, it never changed his first impression. A woman who would never take a gamble for other people. She may not be heartless, but she never threw herself in harms way without having some benefit given to her. She would never care for him unless he could offer something of value to her.

“Trust me. Please.”

“Well then, I believe you.”

 

So why did she save him? Why did she take such a large risk to save him? Why believe in him so easily? What did he have to offer her?

 

Remembering her.

 

No. Even Subaru could not believe such a reason. What good would recognizing her do? He didn’t have money, power, or allies. All it would do was give her the presence of mind that she existed in the first place. That was it. A reminder. That’s what he was. That’s all he was good for.

Maybe that’s what he needs to do. He’ll keep her safe, he’ll keep her warm, he’ll be her knight. Until she doesn’t need him anymore…

“Don’t worry, nothing happened…”

Why? Why did she do that? She didn’t need to. She didn’t need to suffer for him. To debase herself to keep him alive. Those bandits. Those fucking bandits?! Why?! He didn’t do anything to merit such a thing. He didn’t help her! Why did she sacrifice herself for him?! This isn’t the Anastasia he knew…

“…Subaru, if we both go in the same direction, we’ll die. Let’s split up. There’s a chance one of us can make it.”

Why? Why not let him help her? Why act like this was a selfish decision on her part? Why does she keep being nice to him? He’s just a useless knight who can’t keep her safe.

“…please…save…me…”

That’s all he’s good for. He’ll save her. He’ll die for her. And then…he’ll make sure she’s safe. Find someone who can protect her.

“You are such a stupid, stupid boy. Thank you.”

He’ll help and save her. He’ll sacrifice everything. Make sure she’s safe. And then leave. He’s not necessary.

He’ll give you everything. Natsuki Subaru is worthless. He’ll give you everything of value so that he isn’t such a worthless piece of-

“Listen, I don’t know what made you so insistent about your own worth, but I’m not going to let you keep putting yourself down for no reason.”

Why? Why again? Why does she keep doing this? Why does she care? He’s terrible. He’s worthless. He could barely keep her safe just by killing himself.

Maybe he’s the problem.

Maybe he’s what causes her so much pain. Look at him. Natsuki Subaru is not okay. He needs to leave. She’s safe now. She can find someone better-

“… I was wrong to call you my knight. You’re my pillar of support. You’re someone I enjoy bantering with. You’re my…my friend.”

…Subaru was confused. So very confused. Nothing made sense. All he did was talk to her. He saved her once. And that was his fault. If he wasn’t there, she would have gone another path. Hired someone stronger. She was in danger because of him.

“Come on, you’ve been looking antsy all week, there’s a festival happening right now. It’ll take your mind off of things.”

He needed to be useful. He wanted to be useful. He wanted to help her. She sacrificed so much for him. He doesn’t understand. But he doesn’t need to. He’s an idiot. Of course, he can’t understand. He’s worrying her. He shouldn’t worry her. She had enough on her plate without him being a complete mess. He needed to be better. Keep her safe.

“Wait, where are you going? Are you okay?”

He’ll keep her safe. She didn’t need to know. She didn’t need to see him fail. She didn’t need to see him die. She’ll be safe. Only he has to suffer.

“Where have you been?! You don’t talk, you come home late, you leave early. And I come looking for answers and you say it’s for my own good?! You can’t just run off, expecting me to accept that! For my own safety?! What gives you the right to decide that? To leave me behind… just so you can die alone…”

 

…He failed. He tried to keep her safe. And she still suffered. He’s a piece of shit. He can’t do anything right. He needs to keep her safe. He needs to keep her happy. He wants her to be happy. How can he make her happy? What was wrong with him? Maybe…maybe he needs to change. But how?

“I lost everything! Everyone I loved disappeared. All my hard work was taken. My legacy is dead. You have all the time in the world to build back up. I barely have a few more years left in me, if I’m lucky! Do you think I want to make someone cherish me, only to take that away from them. Someone who has lost so much already! Do you think I’m such a cruel woman?!”

“I am cruel. I’m a terrible human being who manipulates others for her own personal gain. I know how messed up Subaru is and I would still use him to make a profit. I wouldn’t reconnect with my family because it wouldn’t be the exact same as before. I accept all of it. All of my sins.”

No. No she’s not. Why does she say that? She didn’t use him for profit. She never did. He was wrong. His first impression was wrong. So wrong. Even back then, she still helped him. She didn’t have to. But she did. She gave him what he wanted: a carriage. Why was she so cruel to herself? She was smart, dedicated, hard-working. He saw all of that during their first time in Banan. She worked so hard to get them a decent place to live, sacrificed all of her savings to get them jobs, and would act subservient just to give them an advantage. She was greedy but that was so beautiful. She never gave up. Was never satisfied with staying in the dirt. She was amazing. She’s not terrible. She’s not cruel. She needed to know that. Subaru wanted to be like her… he’ll take care of himself. He will be better. He will love himself. For her. Show Ana that her path is not wrong.

 

“I don’t need any pity. I’ve known my life was short ever since I was a child. And everyday I’ve lived it like it was the last. That’s why I always go after my dreams and ambitions. I take what I want, and I don’t care how others think. It’s how I lived my life and it being shorter doesn’t change that. It just means I’ll be making every moment of it worthwhile.”

He won’t pity her. He’ll never pity her. She was strong. So passionate. Underneath all of that cold, calculating, merchant persona, there was someone who cared. She really cared about people. Not everyone. But that was fair. People take advantage of you. Not everyone deserves a second chance. Despite how pragmatic she is, she’s so optimistic. She lives with a purpose that Subaru can’t help but admire. He wants her to keep living like that. To live as long as possible…he won’t give up. Even if it was ten years. That’s enough time to figure out how to fix the problem. He won’t stop. He won’t let her die.

“…I think I understand a bit now. Subaru, I’m glad we met.”

“You don’t have to explain anything. Just know, I won’t let you go back to that hell. Ever.”

Wait no. Why does she look at him like that?

He didn’t do anything special. So why does she look at him like that? Like…Rem did. No wait.

It wasn’t exactly like that. Rem looked at him like she saw a beacon of hope. Emilia saw him like a pillar of strength. Ana?

 

Ana looked at him like he was an idiot. Ha!

An idiot. She saw him for who he really was. An idiot. But she didn’t hate him. She never hated him. Not like he did. He hated himself for his stupidity.

But not her. She understood everything, questioned everything, asked everything. And despite looking at him like he was the stupidest person on earth, she gazed at him with such warmth and affection that even he would notice. How could he not?

 

…Did he look like this when he gazed at Emilia and Rem?

 

What should he do?

What can he do?

What will he do?

 

 

During the two weeks of preparation for the festival, he confided in Halibel. They were currently lazing around on the floor, relaxing after a day of hard work, both men laying on a bunch of pillows they brought in from their rooms.

“Ya know, Su-san? We could still blow up Lugunica.”

Subaru stared at the wolfman, “…Is Tia still going on about that?”

“Gahaha!” Halibel laughed, “Every once in a while. But in all seriousness, I am completely willin’ to go to war with them.”

Subaru tried to protest but Halibel’s faced was unreadable, “Listen, ya may think yer not worth the trouble. But I highly disagree. Tia would too. And Ana-bo? She would jump straight into hell for ya. And don’t say I’m wrong. We both know that’s a lie.”

The brightest black star looked pensive, before relenting and sighing, “…I just don’t understand. Why? Why me?”

Halibel snorted, “Ya askin’ why we care or why Ana-bo cares the most?”

“…Both.”

“It’s cuz we love ya, and Ana-bo loves ya the most.”

Subaru flinched, “Really? That simple?”

Halibel raised an eyebrow, “Yes really. Stupid questions get simple answers.”

“…It’s not that stupid,” Subaru grumbled.

The wolfman scoffed and threw his hand in the air, “It is when it comes from a place that doesn’t make sense. Ya really think you don’t deserve our love? Please. That’s not your decision to make. And even then, you are enough. Especially for our favorite little merchant princess.”

“But I haven’t even done anything! I’m just…me.”

Halibel sighed, “…Geez, Ana-bo’s work must be really cut out for her. Alright, let’s go over what you have done: you’ve entertained me.”

“…”

“…”

“…Aaaand?”

“Yeah, that’s it.”

“That doesn’t make any sense!”

“Heh. Friendship never does. Just like love, sometimes things just happen. Sometimes people get along well. Ya can’t expect everyone to value everything the same. Sure, others might need more. But I don’t. Neither does Tia if ya ask her. If there’s one thing both of us can agree on, it’s that you bein’ yourself, is enough. Fun, easy-goin’, and great to converse. What’s not to love?”

“…”

“…I’m guessin’ you disagree?”

Subaru scratched the back of his neck, “I just…it’s just. I.”

Subaru couldn’t get the words out.

“Didn’t  Ana-bo say you were working on lovin’ yourself more? That means ya gotta let other people love ya too. Friends, family, lovers. Ya can’t stop others from carin’ about ya.”

He noticed the boy flinch at lovers.

Halibel seemed to connect the dots on something, he pointed at Subaru lazily, “Hang on. I think I understand what’s makin’ ya so odd about this. You finally realized it.”

Subaru raised his eyebrow this time, “Realized what?”

“That Ana-bo really loves ya. Like not like a friend. But like-“

“Like romantically, yes I know,” the boy had his face in his hands right now, clearly embarrassed.

“…Well, I was goin’ to say like she wants to pin ya down and ride ya until the sun don’t shine but that works too-“

Halibel laughed as Subaru threw pillows at his face.

Subaru noticed ever since that conversation with the blacksmith. And as a result of that conversation, he kind of realized that there were many signs beforehand. Or maybe not. Honestly, he didn’t know if he was hallucinating or not. To be fair, Anastasia and his relationship was so weird and kind of fucked up. Like who begins their friendship by cuddling with each other? Or after one points a knife at the other one? Or feeds each other food like they’re dating when they’re not even dating?! Okay, that last one was his fault but sue him. He took one look at that emaciated woman and could not handle her just eating a pastry and coffee. Yes, he knows it’s coff. Fuck this world’s naming system its absolute bu-

Halibel threw a pillow back at him, “Ya spaced out again. Do it again and I’ll have to call Ana-bo to help keep ya here on the ground.”

Subaru looked away sheepishly, “…Sorry.”

“…”

“…Can I ask you something?”

“Ya already did.”

“Fuck off.”

“Hahaha! Seriously though, go right ahead Su-san.”

Subaru looked down before refocusing his eyes on his closest comrade at the moment, taking a deep breath, “What do you think I should do? With Anastasia, I mean. I don’t know what to do…”

Halibel stared back, “Su-san. Do you love her?”

“…I think I do.”

“Then just tell her you love her. And then love her with all of your heart.”

Subaru shook his head, “It isn’t that simple. I- “he swallowed, “I’m in love with two other people. Two women. She doesn’t deserve someone who can’t make up their mind.”

Halibel scratched his chin before asking, “Do they remember you?”

“…No.”

“Do you have an arrangement with either of them? Or both? Are you married, partners, courting? Did you promise them anything?”

Subaru shook his head again, more vigorously this time, “No. I only promised one of them that I would wait for them to figure out their feelings.”

Halibel blinked.

He then blinked again.

“Then what’s the problem? Just go after Ana-bo. Nothin’ stoppin’ ya.”

Subaru was shocked, “I-I can’t just throw away a promise like that! And even then…I can’t throw away my feelings as if they didn’t matter. Even if I wanted to…And what if our names come back? What if I see them again? What if I say my heart is only for Ana but it is actually shared with two others? I can’t do that to her!”

This time, Halibel shook his head in exasperation, “Su-san, perhaps it is because you are young, but you focus too much on possibilities and not what’s in front of ya. Life isn’t about lettin’ opportunities pass, it’s about seizin’ them just as they cross paths with ya. Ya can’t let your fears dictate your actions. Otherwise, you’ll never grow and obtain happiness.”

He waved his hand in the air, then emphasized his questions by pointing directly at Subaru, “Don’t waste time thinking of if’s, but’s, or why’s. Live life as you wish, it is our right as people who are alive right now to enjoy it. Will you wait forever for a possibility that may never happen? What if Ana-Bo dies before you make a decision? How are you so sure those other girls can make you happy? Is it because they came first? I can be the first one at the target, but it does not matter if I do not finish my work properly. Those girls may have come earlier but they wasted their chance. Don’t try to defend them.”

Halibel added that last part quickly as he saw Subaru try to retort, he then continued, “You can give as many excuses as you want: ‘they deserve all of the time in the world,’ ‘circumstances happened,’ ‘they told me they loved me.’ Doesn’t change the fact that life moves on. A farmer can’t waste his time, waitin’ for the perfect conditions, before harvestin.’ Just like you can’t. You can’t waste an opportunity for love. Ana-bo is right there, willin’ to make you the happiest person in the world. And you’re wastin’ it tryin’ to ruminate on possible futures? Do not think for them, they are their own people. They are responsible for their own lives just as much as you do for yerself. You have a responsibility as a man to make yerself and the ones you love happy. Do not let indecision prevent that.”

Subaru contemplated his words, “…So do I just, hide my feelings? Love Ana but wrap up the others like they don’t exist?”

The wolfman shrugged, “It’s ultimately up to you. But I don’t think it matters. We both know Ana-bo will notice and will probably drag it out of ya one way or another. One of these days, you should just tell her and see. While most gals may just kick ya in the balls, I doubt Ana is the same. She’ll kick ya in the balls and then claim ya!”

Halibel laughed as Subaru joined him, chuckling, “She probably would. I’ll think about this more…thanks Hal.”

“Anytime Su-san. Now, back to what we were discussin,’ I think we can do a preemptive strike by simply droppin’ Tia from the air. Thoughts?”

“Hal we are not carpet bombing Lugunica Tia-style!”

“Carpet-what-now?”

 

 

Speaking of Zarestia, she had her own view of the matter. It was during his impromptu haircut that she spoke her mind. He was currently sitting in a chair in the bathroom in front of a mirror. Tia was behind him, using her wind to sweep his hair and cut.

She used her wind to slice up some hair from the back, slowly trimming it to a reasonable length, “Su. When are you going to finally tell Ana you love her?”

Subaru choked, “I-what?”

“Ah maybe this is that human development thing again. Sorry Su. After you both mate, which will probably be soon, will you tell her you love her?”

Subaru looked at up her incredulously, “…Tia what the hell are you talking about?”

Tia stared back, eyes being the only thing visible, “…Su, what do you think love is?”

She cut some hair off the top of his head, “Love is…”

Subaru didn’t know what to say. He fell in love a lot. But he was never able to describe it well.

Tia seemed to understand as she lifted his bangs and slowly sliced, “Here’s a better question Su: Do you think you can always love someone?”

“…Yes.”

“Why?”

“Well, till death do us part you know?”

“I have never heard that but that is true. Death is the end. So then, why do you not wish to make the most of it by loving them right now? Why not mate with Ana and finally love her?”

Subaru blubbered and felt uncomfortable, “Well, I mean, you know, it’s just. I can’t. It’s not. I don’t… want Ana to suffer because of me.”

“…” The wind stopped, “Su. Are you dumb?”

The wind began again as Subaru felt embarrassed, “Yeah a little but- “

She started spraying some water on his hair to help cut, “Su. Humans don’t live long.”

The star closed his eyes, trying to block the droplets, “I know. But I can’t just decide these things so quickly. I can’t make the same mistakes. Not again.”

“Su, don’t be stupid. You are treating love like a chain. As if it is something that will last for eternity. It does not. Love dies. Everything dies. You can extend it. You can save it. But you can’t make it immortal. Love is like a storm: tumultuous, awe-inspiring, and can birth new life. Like a storm, it is your decision whether to let it pass or to enjoy it. Sure, you may die. Sure, a better rainstorm may come. It is your freedom to do as you please. Just as it is love’s freedom to do as it pleases. Embrace it or don’t, but don’t be a fool.”

Subaru absorbed the Great Spirit’s words, he felt like there was something more underneath it all.

“Tia…why are you telling me this?”

The wind swept through his hair as the spirit eyed it, “…I knew two humans. For a long time, they hated each other. But in actuality, they loved each other. I knew. They knew. They would tell me. But they could never because of their family. And some other bullshit that didn’t matter. Either way, they tiptoed around their love for so long… until I did something. It wasn’t on purpose, but the reason they couldn’t love was no longer a valid reason. And so, they finally got together. But then they didn’t.”

“…”

“The male died.”

“…I’m sorry Tia.”

Subaru couldn’t see her face, she was hiding behind his head, “…The female would tell me how much she wanted to have a child. She would make clothes and ask me for names. All of mine got rejected. I still believe Barestia and Bobtia were perfect,” she chuckled with melancholy.”

Subaru tried to turn his head, but Tia kept him forward, cutting some of the hair on his sides while waving the debris out, “What happened to the woman?”

“She,” Tia paused for a few seconds, the wind sped up for a second before dying down just as quick, “She died as well. Soon.”

“…Is this why you-“

“I tell you and Ana to mate. Yes. It is. Su, remember what I said. Love is like a storm. Do not waste the chance you get, or you may forever miss the rain. And forever substitute it with your own.”

“…”

They sat in silence until Tia finally finished, “There. You look much better. Less like a wild mutt and more like a respectable Su.”

He looked in the mirror and saw someone. A different Subaru. Not better, not worse. Despite it all, it was still him.

He was about to stand up when Tia put her arms around him, he then heard her whisper, “Take care of each other. Please. I do not want to say any more goodbyes.”

Subaru didn’t say anything. Only bringing a hand to slowly grasp hers, comforting her.

A few seconds passed in silence.

Tia then abruptly broke it, “Alright, now that that is over, let’s go see if Ana will stop being a coward or not,” she then grabbed his arm and pulled him quickly towards the door, intending to show off her work to the others.

It was only later during the festival that Subaru finally understood what she meant by goodbyes.

 

 

The blackest star was now sighing to himself. His mind was wandering through so much. Memories of their journey. Certain conversations. Ana. Meanwhile, he was currently brushing one of his favorite women in the world:

 

Patrasche.

 

Who was very much pleased by her favorite human’s care and affection. It was a nice gift, especially considering he was so busy lately. She nudged him softly, noticing his anxiety.

 

He smiled softly in return, patting her head, “I’m sorry girl. I just have a lot to think about. And unfortunately, I’m very stupid.”

She growled.

He rubbed his head, “Sorry, I meant that I’m being a little indecisive. You and Ana really like pointing out when I do that, ya know?”

Patrasche snorted, as if saying, The purple thing has only one good character trait: her taste in men.

“I know, I know,” Subaru rubbed her neck, “She’s too good for me.”

Patrasche stared at him before rolling her eyes.

“…I just. I don’t know what to do. I know what my heart wants. But is that right?”

A new voice came from behind him, “Maybe discussing it with someone would help? What does Ana say? Copper for your thoughts?”

Subaru flinched and felt anger rise when he heard that voice before quickly shutting it down, It’s not her. She’s different.

He then felt a rush of guilt for his previous actions, without turning around he said, “…Hey Scarfdona, how’s it going?”

“Quite well, how about you and I finally have a proper chat?”

Subaru was not looking forward to this conversation.

Notes:

EN1: Yeah Subaru is not doing okay.

Chapter 18: Paved with Good Intentions

Summary:

Subaru and Echidna have a talk, and finally, the stars go on their first date...

Notes:

Enjoy!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

“I’m really sorry for what I said.”

“Apology accepted.”

“…”

“…”

Subaru was awkwardly sitting in their backyard with Patrasche and Scarfdona. The area used to be just outside storage but was renovated by Halibel to keep Patrasche close to them. The reason for this was that Patrasche started throwing tantrums about being so far away from the little black star. She even attempted to barge into the tenement house and cuddle with Subaru in bed. Anastasia woke up that day to a face full of scales and rage. This was a nice compromise.

Though Anastasia still wanted to grilled lizard to this day.

There was a small stable for Patrasche to stay in that had all the necessities she needed: food, water, and a Subaru doll. The doll was a replica of the one he made for Anastasia because the lizard kept trying to take it from the merchant.

Subaru really didn’t understand why Anastasia said, and I quote, “That bitch can take it over my cold dead body.”

“…”

“…

This was really awkward.

“…”

“…

“…So- “ “I-“

They looked at each other and gave soft smiles, Subaru spoke first, “I really am sorry about what I did before…it wasn’t right of me to say those things.”

“Fufufu, I understand, considering what you must have experienced in Sanctuary, I doubt I can find it unreasonable.”

“…Beatrice told you, didn’t she?”

“Vaguely. She herself was not there, yet she did learn of the events from the others. A harrowing experience that they barely survived. The elf, the grey one, the angry yellow cat, and the oni. They were all able to pass the trials and safely made it home, with the clown at their beck and call. Or so she said.”

“…”

“…And I assume this was not the case for you, given that you were there at the time?”

“…It certainly was harrowing.”

Memories popped in from those hellish few days. The worst deaths he had ever experienced occurred then. At times, he felt like he only won due to luck. If Otto wasn’t there to knock some sense into him, where would he be now? Or if Emilia wasn’t able to pass the trials? Or if Ram or Garfield decided not to help them?

Would he have been under Roswaal’s thumb?

Would he have been abandoned just like now?

…Some days he wondered if he should have taken Echidna’s offer. It was an intrusive thought. An impossibility to him.

He hated her. For everything. For putting Beatrice in that situation. For putting Roswaal on his path. For manipulating him.

 

No. He might not hate her. Despite how he reacted, he did not hate her. Why could he hate her? He couldn’t understand her at all.

He can’t hate someone who he doesn’t understand.

 

On his worst days, when he felt like he was still drowning in that prison, he wondered if that offer would have been better. He wondered if he should have left with Rem on that day. If he should have left the mansion. If he should have never gone to the loot house.

Would it have been better than now?

 

Purple. White. And a smile that radiated his life. Those images flashed through his mind.

 

No…it doesn’t matter. Those thoughts. They don’t change anything.

“Subaru.”

He blinked. He shook his head, he was about to apologize for spacing out, when he heard a rather unpleasant sound.

“What will you do when Ana perishes?”

 

Subaru blinked. He looked at the fox with an unreadable expression.

 

“…Why did you say that?”

“Subaru- “

His eyes held barely restrained rage, “Enough. Why are you here? It doesn’t seem like you’re here because of what I said or to get to know me, so what’s your objective? You curious of something?”

“…”

“...Come on. Speak up. I’ll answer anything. That’s what you want, isn’t it?”

“You terrify me.”

 

His anger immediately froze. He did not expect those words. He expected something colder. Maniacal. As if she wanted to see how he would react. A trick. An illusion. A way to gauge his decision making.

No.

She was terrified. Shaking. It looked like she was trying her best not to bare her fangs at him.

Her eyes, her body language.

All scared of him.

He made the same mistake again. He thought she was just like her. Again.

Before he could apologize again, the fox continued, “Apologies, but I had a theory and I wanted to make sure. Your reaction back then, and now, you become intensely aggressive when it comes to Ana’s safety. You leak bloodlust. An incredible amount. Almost instinctually. Your initial reaction to me, I believed originally it was related to Sanctuary. Perhaps sourced from what my Creator did to you…but that wasn’t the case. When you naturally remembered the events, you did not react with fear or even dread. Rather, it looked like you were nostalgic. Which contrasts with what Beatrice told me about what happened there. No signs of your mind collapsing under the weight of the memories. No outward trauma. You didn’t even try to scratch yourself. Apologies, I don’t mean that I wanted those to happen, but I assumed they were a possibility, and I unfortunately gambled on them.”

The boy blinked.

He slowly pointed at himself in surprise, “I acted aggressively? Me?”

She stared at him.

“Subaru. What’s in your hand?”

He blinked. He looked down. His left hand was right there, pointing at himself.

She stared, “The other one.”

He looked to his right. And froze.

His hand was in a death grip, choking the life out of his knife, as blood seeped out of his palm. He quickly put the knife back in his secret pocket, sheathing it.

“I-I, didn’t. I didn’t mean to- “

“It’s alright. Trust me. I am not your enemy here nor am I here for apologies. I simply wish to understand you better.”

“…”

“Could you please tell me what you intend to do when Anastasia dies?”

“…”

“…”

“That’s not going to happen.”
“It will.”

“No, it won’t.”

Both the boy and the fox stared at each other. Neither backing down.

The fox sighed, “Do you believe you can prevent death?”

I’ve done it before…and I have time.

“Do you believe you are capable of preventing fate?”

No matter the cost.

“Are you this greedy or is this something else?”

I am greedy. Just like Ana.

“…”

 

The fox sighed again, “Please answer me this then: Will you join her when the time comes?”

“…”

“…That girl. She wants you to be happy.”

I know.

“Which means that if you think she’ll be happy that you both left this world at the same time, you would be mistaken.”

I’m not. I know what I’m doing. I won’t die. I won’t ever die.

“This isn’t a fairytale, don’t believe that just because you got lucky that you are incapable of failure.”

I know, I know, I know, I know.

“How would she feel if you- “

“I know!”

 

“…I know.”

Subaru was now lying on the ground, on his side. Subaru curled into himself. The fox gazed at him before creeping towards his body and lying next to him.

“I’m sorry- “

Subaru cut her off, “I know what you’re trying to do… you’re afraid that I’m going to do something drastic when Ana finally dies. That I’m going to kill myself out of grief.”

Silence persisted for a few seconds before leaving just as quickly.

The fox leaned on him as she spoke once again, “…I failed that girl.”

I did too.

“I understand.”

“You do not.”

Before he could retort, she cut him off and continued, “You remember her. I do not. My memories. They are gone. Where there should be fond memories of her, there is none. And the worst consequence of that horrible Gluttony, is that I cannot be sad about it. Why could I be? When my mind has logically connected the holes and sewn them up to the point that I barely knew they existed. Only when I rip them apart. Can I feel even a glimpse of the grief that was taken from me. And that is only when I talk to Ana, where I hear all the inconsistencies, when I understand where divergences originate from. I feel a sense of longing, a sense of irrationality, where I miss a possibility that did not ever occur to me…only now do I finally understand my sister. How she felt that very same irrationality, when she realized a part of her life was a lie. And I understand that overwhelming feeling of failure. Of failing someone you never knew existed. Of being the reason their existence became null and void.”

Subaru felt the warmth of Echidna, who was lying right next to his head.

He reached out and touched her fur, she reacted slightly but chose not to flinch. He brought her closer to him, hugging her while still curled up on the ground.

Patrasche, who had been silent and watching, sat down beside them wrapping her tail around to protect them, in a circle.

Subaru spoke softly, “…It’s hard for me some days. When I see her face, when I see how much she worries, I just want to take all of her pain away. I want to her to smile every day. I want her to be the happiest person in the world.”

“Even without you.”

“…Yes. Even without me.”

The fox nuzzled his chest, “The fact that you can even say that, is why I wanted to talk with you. I’ve noticed that, despite how eager you are to become someone as greedy as her, you fail to understand what makes her so greedy in the first place. Ana would rather die than hear you say such a thing.”

“I don’t understand.”

“You are willing to toss away your happiness to make her happy. You desire a future where the burden is only yours to bear. You see her as the lynchpin to your very existence at the moment. But when her existence is no longer there, you will fall apart. That, is what she despises. And not because of the responsibility nor the pressure, simply because you are disregarding what makes her happy.”

“…I am?”

“Her happiness, just as yours, is to see you happy as well. Right beside her. Living your life entangled with her. Not dragged, not enslaved, and not chained. Entangled. The difference is that you are woven into her life, and the idea that you can so easily cut yourself off, and expect her to be happy for it, is blindness on your part. You are blind to your effect on her, you see yourself as simply a pawn in her life when you are her queen. Maybe even king.”

 

Memories of his previous loops echoes through his brain. Of his time in Banan. Memories of his beloved angrily resenting his desire to keep her safe. He never understood it, despite everything. He thought she hated that he was babying her. Or seeing her as an object to be kept isolated. He hated himself for that. He made the same mistake as he did with Emilia. But this time with Anastasia.

 

But maybe he never truly realized what the problem was.

“…” his arms tightened around the fox.

She noticed and continued, “You have a habit of not seeing what good you already do. You value others as if they have qualities that surpass yours. Is that not why you originally tried to separate yourself from Anastasia back at the entrance to Priestella? Or how you seem to think you are not worthy of the girl simply because you still have lingering affections to two women? Or how you often seem to never put much value in your own life, constantly putting yourself at the mercy of danger for her? You need to be greedier child.”

He was more confused than before, “Have I not been greedy? Isn’t that the problem? I want what others have and want to keep everything I had before. That’s why I still like Emilia and Rem.”

He felt the fox shake her head, tickling his chest, “Child, you are mistaken. That isn’t greed, that’s-“

“Envy. In fact.”

Subaru lifted his head, standing in front of them, was his lovely former and hopefully future spirit, “What are you doing, lying in the dirt, I suppose?”

“…Scarfdona and I are having a heart-to-heart.”

“Betty does not understand what your hearts touching have to do with anything. Sister does not have a heart. She is a spirit, in fact.”

He forgot, “Oh, it’s a saying. I’ll tell you again later.”

Beatrice’s eye twitched and she visibly looked disheartened, “Betty sees. Betty will try not to forget this time.”

“Oh, no Beako- “
“It is alright, Betty is oh-kay. But enough about that. What Betty’s Subaru was describing, was envy, not greed, I suppose.”

Subaru raised his eyebrow, “Isn’t envy wanting to be someone else?”

Beatrice stepped over the circle of protection that was Patrasche, the lizard snorting as she did so. The spirit sat down and laid her back on Subaru’s stomach, sandwiching the fox between her and Subaru.

“It is. That is what you are doing, in fact. You want to be in others’ positions. Have their possessions. Live their lives. But there is another part of that, the part that makes one truly envious: blindness to oneself. One cannot covet others, without being blind to what you already own, in fact.”

Before Subaru could question further, Echidna continued, “You are blind to your own necessity in Ana’s life. Thus, you are willing to throw yourself in harm’s way and willing to throw away your whole life to make sure she is happy. You wish to be her hero. Instead of accepting you already are. You are blind to the happiness you can obtain, right here and now, which is why you still desire those two other women.”

“I guess I don’t understand what it means to be greedy…they kind of sound like the same thing.”

Beatrice drummed her fingers on her dress before speaking, “Subaru, would you consider Betty’s Mother greedy?”

Subaru didn’t even hesitate, “Yes. I mean, it kind of fits given her title and all.”

Beatrice nodded, “Have you ever seen Mother want to be anyone other than herself? Did she ever want to change herself? Did she ever value other’s traits as something she wanted to be, I suppose?”

“…No. I don’t think so.”

Betty’s eyes looked distant, “Even if the Mother you met wasn’t exactly Mother, their tendencies were the same. Mother was greedy. She wanted knowledge, wanted to know everything. Sure, she taught people, but the knowledge wasn’t exactly her greed. Mother had precious things she did not want to lose either, in fact…”

 

Before Subaru could question that, Echidna tagged in, “And what of Ana? Does she ever look like she is unsatisfied with her personality? Did she ever look like she wanted to change herself? Change her work habits, her lifestyle, her character. And I don’t mean for the sake of profit, that is different. I mean for the sake of changing herself for the better or worse, simply because she valued someone as better than her.”

“No, not really. Honestly, it seems more like Ana-pop just kind of looks down on people more than she looks up to them. Kind of like a tamer and less homicidal version of Pris.”

 

 

“Aldebaran. I would like foxes for dinner.”

“Princess. Please don’t call me that while I’m fighting for my life. Also, why foxes?”


“They are dead, it does not matter if they are still walking or not. And you shall do as I say, lest you wish to be like them, except in the ground like they belong. As for my preference, I simply desire the death and sustenance of a fox. I was reminded of a specifically greedy one. Find a white or purple one.”

“…Yes Princess.”

 

 

Beatrice shifted her body to be more comfortable, “Do you see what Betty and her sissy are trying to convey? Being greedy isn’t about having what others have. It’s about keeping what you already have. Recognizing the value of what you own and keeping it in a vice grip. And never letting go. Not letting others take it from you. No matter the cost.”

Subaru saw a flaw, “Wait then, what about my love for Emilia? And Rem? I want to keep those relationships. That’s greed.”

Echidna shifted herself so she could breathe easier, “That is also not exactly greed. It would be if you had those relationships. But you don’t. Not right now. Whether you like it or not, those relationships with those girls no longer exist. You are simply chasing your own ghost, your past self. You wish to be like him, having the affections that you had previously. In effect, you are still acting with the desire to be someone else.”

Subaru felt like his head was hurting, “I seriously don’t get it. I just think I’m a terrible person, for having so many girls in my heart.”

Beatrice stared at her favorite person in the world and then sighed, “Subaru… what do those two girls mean to you, in fact? The elf and the maid.”

 

“Well… I love them. Despite it all, I still want to give them the world.”

 

Even though he hated them, he loved them.

 

Beatrice laid her head on Subaru’s side, “But will they ever give you the world back, in fact? Subaru, how you feel for those two girls reminds me of Roswaal, with Mother.”

 

Subaru visibly cringed, “I’m not that obsessive am I? I thought I fixed that.”

 

She rolled her eyes, “No, the obsession is not where the similarity lies, it’s in the false hope. Roswaal hopes that his love will reach her, without ever thinking if that is what Mother will ever do back. Mother is dead, she has been dead for so long. How can he claim she will readily return his affections when she never did in life? How can you stand to push away her love when the previous ones never returned it? Betty knows you said the blue one returned your affections, but your stories always leave out any sign of you reciprocating. At least until the maid became comatose. Is it guilt that drives you for that one, I suppose?”

 

“… No. Rem, she helped push me to become who I am today. That’s why I love her. She was there for me at my lowest. Pushed me to be a hero like the one she believed I was.”

“So, she fed your desire to be someone else. She idolized you and you wanted to measure up, in fact. An idealized version that you would never truly be able to live up to.”

“That’s not!” Subaru paused, “That’s. Not…true.”

Beatrice gazed with care, “Betty knows they were important in your life. Betty knows you love them just as much as you do for Anastasia. But Betty believes there are differences. Differences between the girls that makes Betty trust Anastasia over the elf and the maid.”

Subaru was alarmed, “You trust Ana-pop?”

“Horrid nickname aside, yes, Betty does. Subaru, Betty only cares about your happiness. Betty does not care for anything else. If they do not relate to you being happy, then those things are irrelevant, in fact.”

 

Beatrice tilted her head back to look at the sky, “Which is why, Betty cares for Anastasia, I suppose. But not the half elf or the maid. Despite the arguments and banter, you make each other happy, I suppose. But the others do not, in fact.”

 

Her eyes reflected some of the clouds, “In part, it’s possible Betty’s lack of memories of your interactions with them causes me indifference, I suppose. But Betty is not an idiot. Betty can extrapolate from what is visible and verbally said to me, in fact. Subaru, what has your interactions with those girls brought you?”

“…Happiness.”

Beatrice frowned, “Truly? All of your stories point to you gaining more burdens than losing them. The Royal Selection? A burden you bare to win the half-elf’s love. The speech that maid gave you? A burden to be better that relies on her viewpoint rather than how you value yourself, a curse more than anything. The promises you made to them? Reminds me of how Betty would wait, trying to find that special person. How much will you bare to gain the loves of those who may never return it, whether due to circumstance or inaction? Do not waste your life, waiting for that special person to return for you, in fact. Just like you did for me, Betty wants you to choose the happiness that is right in front of you.”

 

Subaru didn’t know what to say, “Is that the right thing to do? Throw away Emilia and Rem because I can’t have them right now. It feels so… disingenuous. Like I’m throwing away everything we built together.”

 

“In another life, in another set of circumstances, those girls would have been perfect for you. But those are just what ifs, not certainty. They lost the opportunity, such is life. But the present is certain. Betty sees you happy, relatively happy, with a woman who genuinely desires you for you. Not a better Subaru. Not a knightly Subaru. Not a heroic Subaru. Betty knows what Anastasia thinks of you. She knows you are stupid, she knows you are kind, she knows you want to always be better. And Betty knows that she values you for who you are right now, than anyone you could ever be, in fact.”

Subaru was silent as he sat up and wrapped Beatrice with Echidna, “…Maybe. Maybe your right. I don’t know. Just like I don’t get this whole greed thing. What is greed then? What do I have to do to be greedy?”

Echidna nuzzled her sister’s cheek before speaking, “While your initial desire to follow Ana’s example is good, she and you are quite similar in some ways, I believe it is quite impossible for you to compare her greed to yours. It manifests differently for everyone. Everyone values things differently. Some keep hold of money, others keep hold of art, others keep people. What matters is this: what are you willing to give up for your greed? What doesn’t matter? What cost will you pay to get what you want? Everything has a cost, Su-bo, and everyone has a price they are wiling to pay to get what they want and keep it. Even the greediest people, who value everyone and nearly everything highly, have costs they are willing to pay, whether that is time, space, or money. The real question is: what’s yours?”

Subaru contemplated. He thought long and hard as the two spirits gave him time to think. Patrasche was comfortably dozing off as the sun hit them from above.

His thoughts ceased as a new figure approached and made her presence known, “Wow. No one invited me to a sleepover. How’s a gal supposed to not feel jealous when her man is with three other women?”

Subaru smiled and felt his heart warm and beat faster as he heard her voice, “Hey, Ana-pop. Just with three of my favorite girls,” he said as he squeezed two of them tight.

“Su…a…little…too..much….” Echidna choked out.

Beatrice on the other hand, “Betty…is…fine…I…suppose,” she said with a wide and satisfied smile. She didn’t really care that he was squeezing the mana out of her, she was just happy to be here.

Anastasia bent down, tucking her hair behind her ear, “Oh~. Is my darling little Poo getting along with Echidna finally?”

Subaru finally let the two breathe and brought up a finger, “Scarfdona. It’s better.”

“It really isn’t.”

Beatrice deadpanned from the ground, staring up, “And ‘little Poo’ and ‘Poobaru’ is good, I suppose?”

Echidna turned her head towards her sister, also lying down on the floor, “Oh come now, Sister. I think it’s lovely. Quite adorable actually.”

Beatrice turned her head and stared at her smart but stupid sibling, “And what do you think about ‘Ana-pop?’”

The fox snickered, “Lovely as well, though I’m not quite sure what the joke is.”

Beatrice grimaced before rolling over and whispering into her sister’s ear.

As Beatrice explained, Echidna’s face went from jovial to questioning to visibly cringing.

Beatrice finished her explanation, supporting her head with her hand and placing her elbow on the ground, and looked at her sister.

Echidna stared back, “…Really? Did I forget about that or something?”

“Yes. And no. You were sleeping as Betty’s Subaru explained it.”

Echidna then turned her head to Subaru, “Child, why?”

Subaru shrugged, “What can I say? She looks the part.”

Anastasia sat down in front of him and flicked his nose, before smiling, “What can I say, you also look the part as well.”

He tried to flick her back, but she jumped away, he then got up and started chasing her around the backyard, both stars laughing hysterically. Patrasche opened an eye, stared daggers at the purple thing before seeing Subaru smiling. She then snorted, satisfied, and went back to sleep.

Meanwhile, Beatrice was now laying on her sister, watching the young couple chase each other around, “…Did your talk go well?”

Echidna watched as Subaru picked up Anastasia and tickled her, the girl giggled as she was spun around, “I believe it did. I still have some fears, but I believe that they will be addressed in time. At the very least, our talk with him should hopefully help him realize what he wants to do. At least a little bit.”

Beatrice watched as Anastasia caught him off guard, kissing him, before tickling the boy back, as they fell onto the grass, play fighting, the spirit sighed with a mix of exasperation and satisfaction, “Betty feels more like a mother than a contracted spirit at the moment.”

The fox chuckled, “We’ll be what they need, whenever they need it. It’s our job to watch over them. What we always should have done.”

“…No matter what. Betty wants them happy. Even Anastasia, I suppose.”

“Oh, I guess your talk had larger ramifications than I thought. You actually seem to like the girl now.”

“Hmph!” Beatrice pouted and looked away, before hiding a soft smile, “Well maybe. Betty will see. Perhaps one day, I suppose.”

 

 

Anastasia was currently on cloud nine. She and Subaru were now on their first date. She picked out the perfect wardrobe, cosmetics, and even some ‘secret weapons’ just in case. She was prepared, everything perfectly matched.

She still had her hair in her usual side ponytail but was now wearing a more classic dress. It was reminiscent of her Lugunica style, a white dress that wasn’t exactly form fitting but did show off her assets quite well, her back was slightly exposed and it reached up to her neck in a v-shape. She wore a silver necklace along with matching earrings. She decided to forgo her hat, she wanted Subaru to focus on her other parts more and felt it would be too distracting.

 

And, well, judging by his reaction at the tenement house before leaving, he certainly liked how she looked. A lot.

“Wow, Ana-pop, you look…wow. Just, stunning.”

If she weren’t out in public right now, she would be jumping with joy. So, she settled for just skipping with jubilation while holding hands with the man of her dreams. She needed to calm herself down. Otherwise, her dreams might become more real and she may start jumping with a different kind of joy-

Bad. Bad mind. Stop. Not yet…though if the opportunity comes along, this gal ain’t going to waste it.

They arrived at a nearby café in downtown Banan, the city was bustling with traders and stores yelling advertisements from the streets. They got a table outside and were currently drinking tea while looking at the menu.

“Anything you want Subaru?”

“Mayo.”

“That’s obvious, but with what?”

Subaru tapped his chin. He was also dressed differently today. Not wearing his usual haori but a more casual suit. A white shirt and black vest combo with a dark green overcoat, black pants, and emerald tie. His hair was growing out more, becoming less white and more black with salt still peppered in. A lot of the whites were becoming just frosted tips. His hair was long at the back, put in a pony tail. His bangs were tucked to the side, almost covering his right eye.

 

Anastasia, to put it frank, almost dry heaved when she saw him at first. Apparently, Beatrice and Tia helped put together his outfit. Given how much they were screaming at each other in the morning, she kind of guessed there was a lot of discussion before settling on his look.

She really needed to thank them later because she can’t help but savor every part of him at the moment.

She needed to calm down.

“Well, it’s still the morning, what about breakfast?”

She smiled at his response, “Let’s get some eggs and sausag, get some mayo bowls as well.”
