He had to. All this time. Though his body remained the same.

His mind could not.

It had to change.

It had to get rid of all the unnecessary elements.

So, he can keep moving.

So, he can protect what he thought was precious.

 

…I need to remember.

I need to know… one last time.

He won’t run away this time. Or force her to go home quickly.

Subaru. Will have one last week of fun. Give her the time of her life.

Give him one last light to cling to.

 

And then, he’ll say goodbye.

So, he can fully commit.

To escaping this hell.

No matter what…I’ll save you.

 

And once more, Subaru did not hesitate and returned again.

 

 

And when he returned, he resolved himself to give her the best week.

So that he can finally say goodbye, to the him that loved her.

So that he can become, the man who saved her.

 

That was the plan.

 

“Don’t play it off like that. What’s wrong?”

 

But she knew. She always knew.

He could deflect. But she would bother him until he finally talked. Sit beside him, comfort him, until they could resolve whatever it was together.

He tested how much was needed for her to allow him some freedom. So that he can run around without her.

 

But he chose not to this time. He wanted to spend this week, with her, happily.

So, he walked with her to the hill he saw while on their sixth date. To sit. To perhaps calm down her nerves before going on their first date.

 

But he couldn’t.

He doesn’t know why.

He can’t.

Subaru can’t.

 

And he made a mistake, why did he ask her:

“Do you think we could have gotten together under different circumstances?”

 

It was stupid. This was supposed to be here time. His final time.

But the words kept coming out.

Ideas.

Questions.

Thoughts.

Everything he’s been holding in for so long.

Why?

After all this time.

Why now?

 

 

Oh.

 

That’s why.

 

 

“I’m afraid…of saying goodbye.”

 

 

 

He felt Anastasia wrap her arms around his neck, holding him closely as they silently sat beneath the bright sun. The clouds were drifting in.

He remembered. It always rained today.

He shuddered. Subaru rubbed his eyes, they were wet.

He hated that he couldn’t control himself anymore.

He felt so warm.

Her voice descended, sounding like heaven’s choir to his ears, “I still have some years left…”

No, you don’t.

He wanted to scream that at her. But he can’t. He would have to explain. And then he would have to watch her heart break. He would have to watch her cry in her sleep every night.

Not now. Not again. Not so soon.

So, he chose silence, “…”

Anastasia seems to have misinterpreted it, “…Let me tell you a story.”

He stayed silent. He hated this. He felt like a child. He felt so warm though. It’s been so long.

“…”

“This is the story of two lovers from ancient Banan. Pyra and Thebus. Children of two aristocratic houses, they were rivals since birth, constantly bickering and fighting and hating. It was in their blood. They believed that the other was a vain, cruel, selfish child of a family that had false claim over a piece of land that they both shared partial residence. In truth, the land was originally split between them for innocuous reasons, records state that both sides knew this, but the elders aimed to continue the strife so that eventually, one family would rule. However, things took a turn for the worse when the Great Fire struck.”

“…”

“…Their families perished. The story deviates depending on who and where you ask. Those in Banan say that the two became rivals even after the fire. Constantly fighting, aiming to kill each other to settle the blood feud. People from Fusumi say that the two were already in love since the beginning, consummating after their families could no longer hinder them. I prefer Kyo’s interpretation, Thebus saw Pyra was stuck in a blazing inferno, leg caught under rubble. And in an act of heroism, he ran into the fire and saved her, gaining her affection and later falling in love himself. In every case, they ended up falling in love. And with it, came the first storms that finally ended the Great Fire.”

“…And what happened to them after?”

He felt her grip on him tighten, “…Thebus got sick. They say the effects of the fire left a mark on his body that he couldn’t ever be rid of. Within a few years, he perished. Pyra. She was devastated. Despite all her efforts, traveling, asking for help, trying to save her beloved. It did not matter. He died in their home. Pyra herself, died soon after. Not because of the Great Fire. But…because of grief.”

…So that’s the two Tia cared for.

He hated this story. He hated what it meant. And he hated why she told it. He knew what she was about to say. He remembered each and every time she told him the same words, just as she was dying.

“Don’t tell me to move on.”

“Subaru- “

“Don’t!”

His anger boiling suddenly, he yelled as they still held each other close, “You can’t just tell me to…ignore this! Ignore that you don’t have long to live!! Or to move on as if this didn’t mean anyth-“
“Subaru!” He silenced himself as he heard her voice break and droplets hit his shoulder, “I’m not telling you to give up on me…I’m too selfish for that. I want to live too.”

You’re not. You’ve told me countless times. That you’re not worth it. You’re wrong.

“And I want you to remember me…it makes me sick to my stomach thinking of you being with another woman.”

You’ve told me to go find Emilia. Or Rem. Anyone. You’re such a fucking liar…

“But what makes me feel the worst, is you suffering for my sake without getting anything back…I don’t want you to suffer without me. Here, by your side, I can pay you back one hundred-fold. But dead? I can’t do anything…and I don’t want you to meet me again so soon.”

What worth am I alive?!

“You need to live a life without hardship. You’ve suffered enough. I want you to live well. Eat well. Be happy.”

I’m worth nothing! I can’t do shit. I can’t be a hero. I can’t save you! No matter what, nothing works…

“We’ll try our best. Together. Sharing the burden of responsibility. But, if we fail. You need to live, despite my loss. You don’t need me to be happy.”

…Why can’t I save you? I saved Emilia. Even if I died countless times, I was able to save her life. I saved Rem. I failed her but Rem can still be saved again. She’s still alive.

So, why can’t I save you like them?

Why can’t I be like who I was before?!

What makes you so different?!

What…

Different.

 

Oh.

 

Emilia.

Rem.

You.

 

Who am I?

“I want to be like you.”

What is it that I want?

“Is it a mental block?”

My greed?

“What are you willing to give up for your greed?”

Something. Clicked.

Within Subaru’s mind.

The time he spent in those countless loops.

Everything he experienced since leaving the prison.

The information.

The thoughts he had.

The questions he asked himself.

All came to a head.

And at the end of it all.

 

Was a feeling of…pure enlightenment.

 

He slowly lifted himself away from her body, still sitting but looking at her face now. Her makeup was slightly ruined, dried tear marks on her cheeks.

She looked so beautiful to him.

 

“Ana. I’m an idiot.”

Startled by his sudden statement, she automatically quipped, “You realize this now?”

He smiled as she giggled softly, it nearly brought him to tears.

Chuckling, “Yeah. I think I’ve just been trying to act like what I’m not. Not like who I actually am. I think…I’ve been lying to myself for a while.”

The clouds were covering the sky now, thunder rumbled in the distance.

Subaru grasped her hands and held them close to his heart, “For the longest time…I tried to be a hero. Someone who saves others. Despite my flaws and my lackluster traits. I wanted to strive towards that ideal so much. But the reality is simple: I’m not a hero. I’m not someone with great timing. I’m not someone who defeats the odds. I’m…Subaru. Just, Natsuki Subaru.”

His eyes widened slightly, “No. Even that’s wrong. The person I am today. Isn’t the person I was.”

Anastasia looked as if she wanted to ask a question, but he stopped her, he wasn’t quite done, “Ana. What I’m going to tell you. Is all true. Everything. And I want you to know something, all of it may not make sense. And if you were to ask those people, if my memories aligned with reality. They would say it didn’t. And they wouldn’t be wrong. And neither would I. But I want to tell you this. Because…I need to say it. So that I can finally tell you what needs to be done. What needs to be said.”

He felt his heart race. His instincts told him to shut up. To hold it in. To brace the world.

 

He told those instincts to bite it.

It was time.

Subaru took a deep breath, “A part of me died within that prison,” Subaru chuckled and shook his head, “Actually, no. That’s not right. I did die in that prison. The Subaru you know now, is not the Subaru from before. The one that you forgot in Priestella. I spent so long in there. Looking for hope. Begging for it. Wondering when the people I loved would finally save me once again. But deep beneath my despair, I already accepted it: no one was coming.”

He shuddered as he began to word vomit what he had been rejecting within himself, “The cruel reality I spent so long trying to refuse. That in the end. The kindness that I was given, ever since I arrived in this world, was just a simple touch of fate. I was not saved because it was some scheduled event. I was not saved because it was my destiny. I was saved not because of some loving heroine’s kindness. I was saved, because I just so happened to cross paths with her. For the longest time, I couldn’t accept that reality. That no matter what, my love was simply the byproduct of my loneliness. The grief of being lost, the agony of never being able to resolve my past sins, the bitter acceptance that I could never return home. All of it fueled me to love the woman who had been my guiding light. But the reality was that all effort amounted to nothing. That in the end…there was always a possibility that I would never get my reward. I accepted that. That it was childish to expect a reward in the first place. I thought I changed. But really? I was simply trying to ignore it. I didn’t change. I just thought I did. Chasing after bright stars, wishing to be like them.”

 

Subaru then softly said, “That was who Emilia was to me…the light that shines my path. Even if I never reach her.”

Her left hand left his, he felt Anastasia touch his cheek softly, her eyes held no malice, just warm acceptance, she said nothing.

So, Subaru continued, “And then I met Rem…she was someone I hated and then I grew to love. She never trusted me in the beginning. She killed me. Butchered me. Tortured me. All because I smelled like the Witch. She wasn’t wrong to be suspicious. But her rage blinded her. Made her cruel. I grew to understand her. Forgive her. To survive. It was the only way I could…and I really did want to. Because she ultimately wasn’t a bad person. Just a confused and scared little girl.”

He saw how Anastasia looked annoyed, “Haha, I know…it isn’t healthy. But I chose that path.  And I was rewarded with someone who genuinely loved me. I never expected it. And in the beginning, I honestly could never reciprocate it. But she was there at my worst. When I could barely move forward. Rem pushed me forward, to be better than who I was. Yet, still accepting me for who I already was. If Emilia was my light, Rem was my anchor, my compass. The one who believed in me when no one else did.”

He could feel Anastasia’s palm, her fingers, caress his cheek, before holding his hand once more, joining its other.

She still kept quiet, knowing innately, that he wasn’t quite done yet, “I needed them both. For so long, I needed them. Because I had no other purpose. Because…I would break without them. So, when I was in that prison. When I finally accepted I was abandoned. That the two I needed were no longer there to hold me up…I broke. My love…broke. I resented them. Hated them. Wanted to kill them. I had to. Otherwise, it meant that I no longer cared. My hate, sustained my love. So that I could keep loving them. It was stupid. Paradoxical. But it kept me alive.”

Subaru’s heart was racing. He didn’t know if any of this made sense, or if Anastasia was creeped out by his sudden confession of such details, but he needed to do this.

It was necessary.

So that he could say goodbye.

 

“And when you came into my life,” Subaru choked slightly, “I ended up substituting you for them.”

He looked down. He didn’t want to look into her eyes right now, only looking at her hands.

“I needed someone to be my light. My anchor. My compass. Because without one, I couldn’t function. I took advantage of you. You were the person that replaced them. So that I could eventually return to them. It’s why I got so attached to you. Willing to sacrifice so much for you. I wanted to be like you.”

He hated this part of himself. He felt disgusted. But he needed to say it.

To say what he kept within for so long, “I… fell for you because of that. I remembered their kindness, their faith in me, and when I saw similarities in you, I latched onto it. I’m sorry…I didn’t fall for you…for you. I fell for you because I missed them.”

He waited.

Her hands left his. He missed their warmth, just like always.

He expected her to slap him.

Hate him.

Find him disgusting.

But then, he felt the warmth return, holding his face with both hands and lifting it upward. So that he was forced to face her.

What he found wasn’t any rejection.

But pure love.

Her eyes radiated it. Along with understanding. Looking through him. Just like always.

Her words were like honey, sweet and golden, “I know. I had a feeling…I did something similar to you. You were a replacement for my family. Though it may not be the same, I loved and felt concern for you because you were the only person left who cared. Someone to hug and keep me warm, to fill the hole I had in my heart. I had no one else. But within time, I loved you. For you. The empty space was not only filled by you. You entered my heart in ways I never knew. To me, you are irreplaceable.”

 

He wanted to cry. He wanted to hold her close. Kiss her and never let go. But he needed to keep talking. Finish what he started.

Subaru responded in kind, “And me too. You were different from the beginning, despite my desperation for you to be a substitute. Caring, loving, kind. But also selfish, caustic, and wrathful. I hated you for those traits originally. But now…I began to love you for them. How you prioritize those around you over all else. How you banter and joke. How you bite back at injustice. You were a unique existence. Irreplaceable, like they were to me.”

His eyes shook, “But the problem was, I wasn’t willing to leave the past behind. I still wanted to be… the me before the prison. The one who saved the day. Was in love with Emilia. In love with Rem. I missed them. I missed my home.”

 

Subaru then held her face within his hands, “But I don’t need them. I don’t need that home anymore. You aren’t my light. My compass. You aren’t them.”

 “…You’re my home.”

“Someone who I feel most comfortable with. Where I can rest and relax. Where I can I live and walk, as myself. Not a hero. Not a knight. Just…me. Natsuki Subaru…Atlas.”

Flawed. Disgusting. Never meant for more.

 

But enough. Enough for her.

 

Enough for himself.

 

He could see her cheeks redden, tears springing up once more, one last sprint, “I need to say goodbye to the past. I need to say goodbye to the me that loved you, like them. To the me that hated you. To the me that idolizes you. And to the me…that cannot save you.”

Her eyes widened.

He expected thousands of questions after this, but it was time, he closed his eyes, “Goodbye to Emilia. Goodbye to Rem. Goodbye to the Subaru who I wish I could return to be.”

I loved Emilia. I loved Rem. I loved you.

 

But now…

“And hello, to the me that loves you, and only you. Anastasia Hoshin. I love you.”

It felt impossible to say before.

But now. It felt so free.

So, light.

As if the binds on his heart were never there to begin with.

His lover’s face was pink, flustered beyond compare, tears finally streaming down her face, makeup thoroughly ruined.

“…I love you too-MMPH!” He kissed her immediately.

She melted in his arms.

It felt like heaven. After so long.

Again and again. Separating briefly.

“I love you. I love the way you smile. I love how beautiful your eyes are, how radiant they are. I love how soft your hair is. I love how often you wake up early, only to pretend to sleep, to spend more time with me. I love how you skip every few steps while walking. I love how you always make weird food combinations. I love how you hum to yourself when bored. I love how your eye twitches along with your mouth when stressed or annoyed. I love how you’re such a Scrooge. I love that you remember me telling you about that. I love how embarrassed you get when I say these things.”

Anastasia looked like she was actively becoming a puddle, a very pink and red puddle.

Subaru laughed and hugged her close, “Now it’s my turn to tell you a story.”

“I-what, uh. Okay?” His sudden change of topic gave her whiplash, he could feel her heart racing. The girl felt like she was on fire.

So cute!

“Remember how I was telling you about my name?”

He felt her nod, and responded by nuzzling her neck, making her squeak slightly, he smiled, “So! My name comes from a cluster of stars called Pleiades, Subaru being the Japanese name, seven stars specifically. Maia, Electra, Taygete, Alcyone, Celaeno, Sterope, Merope. They were seven godly sisters in mythology. However! There are actually two stars that are right beside it, technically part of the cluster. Forgotten and ignored for years. They were only named recently. One was named Atlas.”

He felt her shuffle, “The name you chose.”

He chuckled, “You got it! Atlas was the father of the Pleiades sisters, a titan who held up the world on his shoulders…”

He originally chose it because it felt cooler than Alcor at the time…but now it felt very fitting. Weirdly fitting.

“What about the other star?”

He blushed a bit, thankfully out of view, “Pleione. Mother of the Pleiades sisters, married to Atlas, and symbolic for sailing and multiplication of flocks.”

“Interesting. But, uh, why now? It feels a bit out of nowhere for you to say it…”

He felt his cheeks burn red, “Okay so hear me out. Remember how we need a company name? And you wanted it to involve both of us?”

“…Okaaaay?”

“So, I was thinking,” he swallowed, he felt his heart thump in his neck, “We could call it Atlas & Pleione. And uh, I was thinking…I’m Atlas obviously…”

He whispered softly, “And well, you would. Be…Pleione.”

“…”

Now he felt like he was on fire. He didn’t know if that was her heartbeat now or his. Either way, it was beating like a death metal drum.

The silence was killing him. She still wasn’t talking as seconds passed.

Shit. Maybe this wasn’t the best way to-

“Subaru.”

He got startled, “Yes?!” His voice nearly went up an octave.

“…Is this a marriage proposal?”

He wanted to crawl away and die right now but he stood strong, “…Yes.”

“…”

Subaru immediately started rapid-firing, “Okay I know this is weird. But like I have a good reason for it. And I mean. I know technically this is still our first date. But like, I know it’s a bit sudden. And maybe I’m rushing. But I feel I can spend my whole life with you. It feels out of nowhere. But like, I’m dumb. And I listen to my heart. And I’m doing this for a bigger reason. And like, we can talk about it later if you want-“

She lifted him off of her, grabbing his face in both hands, staring intensely at him, “Subaru.”

They were two red tometos, sitting together without a care in the world.

“Yes?”

“Shut up and kiss me.”

“…Yes.”

And they did. Long and slow.

 

“So, is that a yes?” He said with a dumbass smile as they separated once more.

She smiled at him like he was a dumbass, “What do you think?”

“…Yeeess?”

She snorted, “…So, what now?”

“Now, I want to make a promise with you.”

Anastasia giggled, “Shouldn’t this have come before the proposal?”

He shook his head, “No. I need to do it this way so that you’ll know I’m serious. Anastasia. I want to make an oath. An oath that I’ll forever do my best to make you happy.”

Her expression became alarmed, “Subaru, why?”

“…I want you to know how much I care. Back home, we used to promise each other at the ceremony a set of oaths at marriage. I don’t how you guys do it here. But I want to do the same. And I want to do it now, because I don’t want to waste a single second making you happy.”

She appeared pensive, “…”

“You don’t have to answer me now. You can answer in a few days or near the end of the week.”

It looked like she was struggling, she scratched her head.

She sighed, “You idiot, I do want to do this. It’s just. Argh!”

She threw her hands in the air, “It’s just so frustrating how all my plans blew up! And I can’t understand what’s making you do all this.”

Honestly, I’m surprised you’re going along with my insanity.

For what felt like years, she would constantly go against his plans.

It felt nice and jarring for her to follow his words faithfully.

He felt touched, “I’ll explain soon, right after this.”

If I’m right, you won’t be as angry. Hopefully.

“…Screw it, we’re in this together, you little shit.”

Ah! I love you so much!

Subaru held Anastasia’s hands, and concentrated on her, the Authority of Greed resonated, and showed him her Od. It was small. Not yet cracking, but weak.

Here goes nothing, please work. I’ll try all week if I have to.

“Anastasia Hoshin. I, Natsuki Subaru, promise to always make you happy. That in sickness or great health, whether we are poor or healthy, old or young, I’ll always be faithful to you.”

“…Natsuki Subaru. I, Anastasia Hoshin, promise to always make you happy. That in sickness or great health, whether we are poor or healthy, old or young, I’ll always be faithful to you.”

…The Od showed no change. He didn’t see anything different.

Come on you shitty authority! What do you need for me to share my Od with her?!

Subaru pressed on, “No matter the challenge. No matter the struggle. No matter the situation. We’ll press forth and fight it together.”

“…No matter the challenge. No matter the struggle. No matter the situation. We’ll press forth and fight it together.”

Still. No. Change.

I know what my greed is. I don’t need Emilia. I don’t need Rem. I don’t need my name nor my reputation. I just need her. I’ll pay any cost. I’ll throw away everything.

 

…Please. I won’t give up on this life. I’ll protect what I have.  

Subaru had one last gamble, something he really did not want to do.

"Sharing the burden of responsibility."

…Fuck it.

“All my burdens. All my sins. All my flaws. I’ll lay bare to you. And if you are willing, I will carry all you lay bare. And you, the same for me. I promise, until death do us part. Always yours, Atlas.”

…Promises are a two-way street. Contracts are a two-way street. Maybe. You can’t pick and choose with allies. Maybe. You have give it all. Not just the good. The bad as well.

“…All my burdens. All my sins. All my flaws. I’ll lay bare to you. And if you are willing, I will carry all you lay bare. And you the same for me. I promise, until death do us part. Always yours, Pleione,” and with those final words from Anastasia, Subaru felt his heart drop more and more.

 

No ch-

Wait!

 

 

He saw something.

Please.

 

A flicker.

I don’t need RBD.

A bit of color.

I need you.

More. More color.

Let my greed run true.

The light was pulsating.

Let me covet the impossible.

 

Subaru pleaded with the world.

 

And the world finally responded, the Authority resonated.

 

 

It started small.

He saw the little white light glow and ebb.

Until finally, he saw it mold into a mosaic of colors.

Woah.

Vibrating through the spectrum of colors, he saw the little wisp extend a colorful tendril out to him, until it entered his heart.

Yes!

For a second, Subaru felt only elation.

 

And then. Pain.
“HNNG!”

Unbearable.

Unspeakable pain.

“Subaru?! What’s hap-ARGH!”

The boy panicked but he held firm, still holding onto Anastasia’s hands as they both seized up. It felt like pins, needles, and knives were shredding their muscles and bones.

He couldn’t hold it back, and neither could Anastasia.

They were screaming in agony.

It felt like their veins were on fire, their hearts beating in unison rapidly, their nervous systems screaming.

 

Subaru felt like his Od, his very being, was ripping apart.

 

And then.

 

All the brightest star saw, was black.

Notes:

EN: We are not done just yet. There is still more to see. This is not the end. We have a lot left to cover. Stay tuned for next week, where we find out what happened to our two stars.
EN2: A friend of mine's SO got in an accident recently, nearly dying. A part of me started realizing how often life can just...end. Out of nowhere. I think this story for me is not just about the romance, but also a reminder. Please. Go tell the people you love...that you love them. Not in the future. Now. Or else happiness will just be a regret, rather than a reality. And remember. I will always love you, my dear readers. Stay healthy, and stay safe.

Chapter 22: Melt My Heart, Set Me Ablaze

Summary:

The consequences of Subaru's choice, begins now...

Notes:

Enjoy!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

“I love you.”

 

Dark. Everything. Was dark.

 

“I love you.”

 

He remembers this place. He always did.

 

“I love you.”

 

It felt warm and cold. Free and suffocating. Twisted yet soft. This was where he always returned to. Where the abyss could no longer hold him.

 

“I love you.”

 

Formless. He had no form. No semblance of thought. His emotions a wild string of entropy that mashed against his entire being, flowing through the endless tapestry that was his existence.

 

“I love you.”

 

And that tapestry, that dissonance of reality, that he wished to rip apart every second. Was held lovingly, embraced fully, and worshipped by a ceaseless shadow that ebbed and flowed along his entire body.

 

“I love you.”

 

Enraptured. Engorged. Entrapped. Entranced. He had no will. He had no feeling. No place to go. This was his home. His tomb. Encased forever, within the embrace of boundless affection.

 

“I love you.”

 

He didn’t have a choice. This was all he knew. All he’ll ever know. Worshipped and adored. Within this shadow garden. Forever, and never, forgotten.

 

 

 

 

“..baru…Su…Baru!”

Or maybe not. The formless star heard it. Faint. Yet there. Calling to him.

 

“Subaru…”

The star knew it. Recognized it. Cherished it. Once hated, now loved. It needed to know. Needed to know where that siren call originated from.

 

“Subaru!”

The star reached for it. Wherever it was. But was hindered by one last obstacle.

 

The shadows that encased his heart.

 

“Subaru…where are you?”

The star whipped his head, the voice was close, yet far. He had to get to her. Her? Yes. Her. He. Him and her. He needed her. NO. He wanted her. He chose her. That was his choice. His essence. His other half.

His love.

His sanctuary.

His home.

 

The shadows clung harder to him. He rejected them.

“I love you.”

No. She was not her. This…prison. This was not his home. No matter the emotions nor the reality it tried to inflict upon him, it was not.

“I love you.”

Get away. The start writhed and pushed. It needed to leave. But the shadows clung harder.

“I love you.”

Stop.

“I love you.”

He does not.

“I love you.”

He never will.

“I love you. I love you.”

He made his decision. He will no longer be chained. Chained to the person he no longer is nor the one he never wishes to be.

“I love you. I love you. I love you.”

He has something to protect now. Someone. Someone he will abandon everything for. Someone who chose him. Just as he chose her.

“I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you.”

He was abandoned. Abandoned by everyone. It was not their fault. But still, he had no one. Just like her. They found each other. He does not need this prison no longer.

“I love you. I love you.” Let him leave. “I love you.” It won’t let him leave. “I love you.” It will never let him leave. “I love you.” She won’t. She never will. He was hers. “I love you.” She knew better. He was safer with her. More loved. Never forgotten. “I love you.” Never abandoned. “I love you.” Disgusting. These are not his thoughts. Never his thoughts. “I love you.” The memories of a dead concept, a dead reality he never chose. “I love you.” He can’t fight it. “I love you.” Hope. Salvation. Just out of reach. “I love you.” Maybe. “I love you.” It was better. “I love you.” To never. “I love you.” Dream. “I love you.” Of hope. “I love you.” Freedom.

“I love- “

“SUBARU!”

The voice echoed throughout the garden. The star looked up, his formless being barely able to move beyond the chains of hell.

 

A twilight shone upon him. Small. Effervescent. But there. Bringing warmth. Connecting to his absent heart, a bare thread. He could not reach it. But he. He could grasp the thread. He could feel it resonate. Feel it echo his will.

Formless he may be.

He had no mouth. And yet. He could scream.

 

“…Help me. Please.”

 

…And then, the light was gone.

 

 

 

Subaru woke up gasping. His eyes darting around the room.

His eyes settled on Beatrice, sleeping peacefully in a chair next to the bed he had been unconscious in. At first, they softened.

And then they widened when he realized, Where’s Anastasia?!

Just as soon as he thought, he felt something grip his left hand tighter.

 

He looked over.

She was clutching his hand. Sleeping peacefully. Breathing.

He didn’t hesitate, he concentrated his eyes focusing entirely on her.

 

 

 

It was there. It was shining. It was alive.

No longer small or on the cusp of burning out.

It was in fact larger than he had ever seen it before. Shining not pure white but an iridescent glow. As if it was changing rapidly before his very eyes.

 

It was beautiful.

 

Drip. Drip.

 

So. Beautiful.

 

She was alive. He finally won.

“You’re finally awake,” Subaru was startled as he looked towards the foot of the bed, a white fox stared at him with concern and a hint of relief.

He quickly rubbed his eyes, “…Eridna, what happened?”

“That’s what I should be asking you,” she walked over and sat on top of his legs, “One moment, sister and I are having a small ‘discussion’ with Tia over who will watch over you two on your next outing. The next, the wind spirit suddenly screams and bursts through the roof, flying towards your location. I believe she broke several windows on the way there given the amount of glass on the streets. And just as we are about to go after her, she comes back crying and holding the both of you with Halibel right behind her. It took some time to calm her down. It took even longer to convince her not to castrate the Admirer, thinking he was at fault for not watching over you both as closely as he should.”

Subaru stared at the fox before looking over to the fist sized hole in the wall, at a particular height, “…Is that why- “

“She missed. Luckily, Halibel jumped out of the way. He should still be able to have children.”

“Oh my god Tia,” Subaru rubbed his temples, grateful for his contracted spirit’s concern but exasperated nonetheless, “Where is she now?”

The fox grimaced, “…She and the wolfman left to…blow off some steam.”

“…”

“…”

“…They went to fu- “

“No. Fight. They have gone to fight so that she won’t spend the whole time pacing the room, waiting for you both to awaken.”

“…I was going to say that.”

“Do not lie to me boy, we both know how your mind works.”

Subaru chuckled, scratching his neck with his right hand, his left still tightly gripped by his lover. He couldn’t help but smile, watching her.

“We couldn’t pry your hands off each other,” Subaru refocused on Eridna, “Even while unconscious, you both wouldn’t separate no matter what. I’d call it romantic, but there is something…unsettling. Remove the covers from her.”

Subaru raised an eyebrow but obliged, using his free hand to take off the blanket surrounding them, his eyes bulging at the sight.

Anastasia was wearing what she wore during her date, but the clothing ripped, most likely from either Tia flying them or someone checking their body for wounds, Subaru’s was in a similar state. Usually, Subaru’s eyes would bulge from seeing Anastasia’s partially naked…assets. But that wasn’t the case here.

No. The reason for his surprise was what lay beneath the skin. Dark veins and blotches of black pigmentation stretched from Anastasia’s chest, specifically her heart, to her shoulder, then right arm, and down to her ring finger. The dark ‘ink’ created a sort of pattern, swirls of grey and black running up her arm and to her chest. Like a rancid tattoo, it almost looked beautiful if only the implications didn’t sicken him.

 

Subaru rolled up his own sleave, and then slid off his shirt partially. The same pattern.

One of his fears came true. He had given her everything.

“…Is that what I think it is?”

Subaru swallowed a dry cough, “…Yeah. It’s cursed blood. Straight from Capella.”

“Morbid, yet fascinating. Sister checked her condition and was surprised to find a familiar patchwork of curses within her body. Wolgarms.”

Subaru understood, “…Yeah. Just like mine.”

 

Subaru then eyed his own skin closer. He was missing a few scars. Eyeing Anastasia, those scars were then found, mirroring where they originated on his tissue previously.

 

Subaru felt a cascade of guilt. It was the price for using Greed. The ‘contract’ was all or nothing it seems.

“Subaru,” a new voice sprang up, Subaru averted his gaze reluctantly from his lover’s now sullied skin and looked towards his former contracted spirit, now wide awake, “Please. Tell Betty and her sister what happened, in fact.”

 

Despite the star’s hesitance, he obliged. He tried his best to recap everything, including some extraneous details so neither spirit was suspicious of his actions. Mixing truth and lies, he explained that he found out that Anastasia was dying from using his ability, that the ability came from the Witch Factor of Greed, and that he had an idea based on watching Regulus use his power and from talking to Beatrice before Priestella.

Their reactions were…poor to say the least.

“Of all the stupid…” Beatrice looked like she was about to blow a gasket, trying her best to yell at Subaru without waking up Anastasia, looking more adorable than anything, “Do you realize what you did?”

“…I know.”

“You know?!” Beatrice put hands over her mouth, counting to three before continuing, “Your Od. It is now weaker. Much weaker. Betty believes it is about half or a little over half of what it used to be, I suppose. You will die in around 30 years. 40 at most. That isn’t even counting what it could have done to the stability of your body. For all you know, your Od may crack from how much it has lost in such a short amount of time, in fact.”

“…But she’ll live as long as I will now.”

Beatrice was about to retort but Echidna cut her off, “This…ability. Do you believe you can replicate it in others?”

Subaru shook his head, “No. I don’t think so. It seems like the requirements are incredibly specific. And both participants have to be willing to an insane degree.”

He tested it on enemies, on witch cultists. Extensively. Only wounds are changed. Not Ods. It seems both ‘contractors’ have to be willing to sacrifice and share everything. Everything. A simple agreement to ‘fight’ doesn’t satisfy that condition. Or at least, that’s what Subaru can surmise.

The fox pressed, “I see. Then you cannot pull Od’s from others…”

Subaru put up his right hand, “No. I’m not going to do that. Ana would never let me do that.”

He tried. He really did.

Eridna raised an eyebrow, “And how would you know what Ana wants?”

He understood what she was implying, “I know…she’ll hate me when she finds out what I did.”

The fox stared at Subaru before looking towards her sister, “Has he always been this much of an idiot?”

“Hey now…”

Beatrice shrugged, “Betty can’t remember but a feeling in Betty’s gut says ‘yes,’ in fact.”

“Okay, I know I am one but-”

Eridna shook her head along with Beatrice, “It seems you will have a hard time once your memories return, sissy.”

“This is really feeling like déjà vu- “

“I suppose, I suppose.”

“Stop acting like Rem and Ram!”

Subaru felt Anastasia stir right next to him, before he could even react, she was no longer laying down. Subaru looked away before he could catch her eyes.

Could you blame him? Both Beatrice and Eridna got startled when looking at her expression, it made Subaru fearful for the time in a while.

“G-good morning Ana, I suppose.” “…It is good to see you awake Ana-bo.”

“…”

Anastasia didn’t say anything, but it seems she gestured in some way, causing the two spirits to slowly nod and leave the room.

 

At the sound of the door softly shutting, Subaru felt his throat constrict.

Why was he so scared?

“…How long were you awake?”

“…”

“…”

“…Since you woke up.”

That’s why. He could tell from the beginning. In the mornings, her breathing differs when asleep versus awake.

…Okay, that may sound creepy. But Subaru can’t help knowing these things!

Anyways.

The silence was pervasive, he didn’t want to look at her, afraid of seeing her so angry at him or crying or…disappointed.

So, he did the next best thing.

 

“I’m sorry!”

Grovel. He slammed his head on the mattress, right in front of her, bowing fully.

“I know you wouldn’t have approved. I could have told you, but I knew you would have said no. And I didn’t want to take any chances. I thought apologizing would be better than risking your life. I’m sorry.”

“…”

He felt tense, but pressed on, “…More than anything, I took that choice away from you. And I know you would have hated that. Hated me giving my life for you. Worst of all, I gave you, my curses. I didn’t even tell you about them. I didn’t want you to worry. I know. It’s not fair of me to do this either. I just…I don’t want you to think I did this without thinking. Everything. I thought of it. Weighed the options. And chose. It wasn’t out of nowhere. I take full responsibility for everything.”

“…”

“…So, if you hate me. Want to stop speaking to me. Or never see me. For however long you wish, I’ll do it. I won- “

“Subaru.”

He shut up immediately.

“…”

“…Was everything you said true? Before, when you talked about them.”

“…Yes. It was.”

He toed the line of the taboo with each word. He experimented previously. Tested what counted and did not count. It was a gamble. A major risk that could of killed her. But it was necessary. He needed to say as much as possible. Explain everything. That way the contract could go through. He needed to share all of his ‘burdens.’ It was worth the risk.

“You can’t explain more, can you?” He didn’t say anything, his silence being louder than mere words, Subaru heard her sigh, “Thought so.”

“…”

“…And what about the ‘proposal?’ Was that part of the plan? Was this all a way so you can save my – “

“No.”

He won’t let that ever be misunderstood.

Subaru continued before she could say anything else, he needed to correct this, “Never. In my life, will I ever pretend to propose to the person I love. I meant every word. Every emotion. Every piece of my heart I gave. Even if we weren’t in this situation, I would have done the same thing. I would have told you, from the beginning, that I intended to marry you. There is no one else in my life I’d rather have. Not anymore. And never shall that change.”

Silence returned. Subaru kept his head down. His curiosity beckoned, however.

He wanted to know her reaction.

“…Why? I don’t understand,” He heard her voice waver, almost croaking, and it made his heart crack, “Why now? Just the day before, you were so indecisive. You loved them. You didn’t know what you want. That’s what you told me. I…had so many plans. A dozen dates. Numerous ways to win your heart. I heard you say it. And it made me so happy…and so afraid. Because I didn’t know if this was a dream. If I would wake up and it would all turn out to be a figment of my imagination. I didn’t want to lose my chance…so, I said yes. So tell me, was it a dream? Was our love a dream? Something you did just to give me a few more years? Because you were grateful to me? Tell me. Please. What happened within one day to change your mind?”

…Everything.

When he woke up next to her, clinging to his side for dear life.

When she would spend her time writing letters to Julius, Ricardo, and the Triplets.

When she would ask him to comfort her at night.

When she would take every chance. Every day. Until the last possible second, telling him how much she loved him.

And dozens of more moments.

It was one day to her.

To him, it was infinite.

So yes, everything changed his mind.

He took a deep breath, “I loved you since the beginning. Not. Not the first time I met you. But when I saw you that fateful night. I was alone and scared. I had nobody. And I got attached to you, because you were the first person in so long who treated me with genuine kindness. And as time went on, I got to know all your good sides and bad sides. Truly know them.”

“…”

“I thought it was like before. I was grateful because you saved me when I had nothing. And I thought that for so long, it was just gratitute. Until yesterday, when I finally got it. It felt like I thought for…years about this. I ran through so many scenarios. So many thoughts. So many situations. And I realized something.”

“…What? What did you realize?” He could hear disbelief in her words.

“That you would do the exact same for me as I have done for you. If given the chance, you’d sacrifice yourself for me in a heartbeat.”

“You don’t know that- “

“Yes, I do.”

“No, you don’t!” He could feel her trembling, her voice sounding like it was on the verge of tears, he wanted to hold her close, but no, he needed to stay calm, choose his words carefully, “If you knew me so well, you’d know how selfish I am! I took you in because I wanted to take advantage of you! Not once have I shown you that I would prioritize you! That I would put you first!! All I’ve shown you is that I am attracted to you. Physical affection, words, and all that bullshit, that’s all I’ve shown! Nothing worth… this! This disgusting loyalty. I am not worth that! What if I left you after this? What if I tricked you all this time to steal your life force?! What if I didn’t ever love you?! What reason could you possibly- “

Nope, never mind, Subaru was not letting this go further, “You’ve given me ample reason you idiot!” Subaru sprang up, no longer prostrating himself, angry about her words, pointing at her chest, “You think you’re some clever manipulative person who can hide herself. Newsflash moron: You can’t hide shit! You say you act selfish, but you always look after me. You watch when I scratch myself, hell you know when I spiral, faster than even I can comprehend. You know who does that? Good! Selfless! People! Just like you!”

Subaru got a good look at her. Anastasia’s hair was disheveled, her dress in ruins, her face bare and tear-stained. God, she looked beautiful.

…But how can someone so beautiful be so stupid!

“That’s a load of dragon shit! Anyone can do that. I’m not special.”

“Well guess what? You’re wrong. It is special. Because not once have I had anyone check on me like that besides Beako. Everyone trusts me. Trusts me so much that they leave me alone when I obviously am not doing okay. And guess who doesn’t trust me for shit? YOU!”

She stared at him in disbelief, “…That’s a bad thing you fucking dumbass!”

Subaru stared at her back, “No it isn’t because I am fucking dumb! I don’t know what the hell I’m doing half the time. I’m just trying my best, working with what I got. Trying to steer this tram ride of hell that is my life. I’ll explain later, not right now,” even in this situation, he saw her eyes light up from what he said, God, he loves her, “You know what I need? I need someone who not only trusts me when I’m serious but also distrusts me so much that they make backup plans. Check on me. Discuss things with me. Problem solves with me. I need someone so paradoxical in nature, that they can somehow do both at the same time. Someone like you! A person who says they’re a logical person but ends up being the most emotionally charged person on the planet. You. YOU. DUMB. FUCK!”

“Don’t call me dumb, you fucking asshole!” The pale star scratched her hair in sheer rage, “Od, I fucking hate you sometimes. You make these dumb decisions for me thinking it’s okay. Well guess what?! It’s not! You using your stupid suicidal power to kill bandits. You leaving me alone so you can handle that whole Tia-two bullshit yourself. This. Whole. FUCKING! SITUATION!”

“But you accept that you’re dumb too, don’t you?!” Anastasia snarled at his words, looking like she wanted to tear Subaru limb from limb, Subaru didn’t care, “You know it! You are literally one of the most hypocritical women I know! If you were in the same situation as me, you’d do it in a heartbeat! Hell, I know for certain that, hypothetically, if we were in a life-threatening situation. And you thought you were slowing me down. You would sacrifice yourself for me. Or you’d sacrifice your dignity for me. Or you would try to distract a monster to save me. Or you’d tell me to move on instead of being with a dying woman. Or you’d tell me to find my own happiness. That’s you!”

“No, it fucking isn’t. I’ve never done those things!”

“Yeah, that’s why I said hypothetically, you idiot!”

“You’re the idiot!”

“No, you are- “

Subaru was tackled onto his back by a very pissed off Ana, pounding his chest ineffectually, crying nonstop, “I hate you so much! Why are you so difficult to deal with?! Why do you have to make this so confusing?!”

“BECAUSE I LOVE YOU!”

She stopped pounding and just stared, “…”

“…I love you so much that I would throw away everything just to be with you.”

“I can’t pay that back.”

“You don’t have to.”

“That’s unfair!”

“So, what if it is?! You don’t have to pay me back. But you will! Not because I want it, but because I know who you are. And I know who I am. We’re two idiots who would sacrifice the world for each other but don’t want the other to do the same. I’m hopeless, selfish beyond compare, barely functioning, insane, basically a waste of oxygen-”

“No, you’re not!”

“I am selfish and you know it! I didn’t save you because I wanted to be a hero. I saved you because I wanted you. I want all of you. I didn’t do it for nothing. I did it so I can spend so many more years with you. And what would you describe yourself?! Selfish, greedy, manipulative. You’re all those things and you’re also none of those things!”

“You’re so fucking stupid!”

“Yeah, well- “

They continued insulting each other for the next ten minutes.

Subaru and Anastasia ended their rants, gasping for breath.

“…Don’t insult yourself ever again. Only I can insult you.”

Subaru, arm over his eyes, smiled, “Yeah, well, same to you. Stop acting like you’re some megalomaniac. Even if you were one, you’d be my megalomaniac.”

Anastasia sniffled and giggled, before coughing. She then looked at his chest before deciding to lay on top of it.

Subaru felt warm, he motioned his arms over her, waiting a second, she noticed and frowned, “…You can hug me. You don’t have to ever ask. I’ll always say yes.”

He obliged.

“I know, I just…don’t want to do anything without your permission again.”

“…”

“…”

“…I trust you. Hug me, touch me wherever you want. I won’t ever say no.”

Subaru blushed, “W-well, I mean, that’s fine. But you probably won’t say yes to everything.”

“…”

Anastasia didn’t say anything. She just sat up and started straddling him, making Subaru blush harder, “U-uh, Ana-pop I- “

“One moment. Can you call Tia here with your contract?”

“Uhhhh, yeah. I think so?”

“Do it.”

Subaru was very confused, but he decided to just do as she said, concentrating on his connection to Zarestia.

A few seconds passed before,

BOOM!

They heard something crash into the ceiling in one of the nearby rooms, and then a flurry of stomps down the hall, getting louder, until,

“SU! ANA! Are you both alrig-“ Tia paused once she burst into the room, frantic at first, but her eyes laser-focused on the positions of her two wards, “…Is this? Are you?”

Tia didn’t have the words.

Fortunately, Anastasia did, looking deathly serious, “Tia. It’s time.”

“…”

Zarestia blinked.

Blinked again.

Once more.

And then it clicked.

Zarestia smiled.

Halibel rushed in right behind her, “Tia ya seriously need to use the door- “ he also paused like Tia, “Is this what I think-“

Zarestia didn’t even let him finish, punching him in the gut, and then holding him up by his robe’s collar, “We are leaving you pervy mutt. It’s time.”

Halibel, winded and out of breath from the sudden gut punch, looked from Tia to the two stars before the gears shifted in his head as well, “Oh. Ohhh. Su-san. Make me proud-AH! Alright, I’m comin’.”

Tia started dragging him out the door, the spirit slamming it shut with the wind. In the hallway, they could hear a muffled Beatrice, “Why is there a hole in the ceiling? Did you do this- hey?! UNHAND ME, IN FACT!”

And then a few moments later,

BOOM!

Another hole in the ceiling has been created. Property of Zarestia.

Subaru just stared at the door, “…What was that?”

He then refocused on Anastasia, however, he soon lost his breath.

She began untying her hair.

“First off. I’m still incredibly angry about what you did. You are not allowed to sacrifice yourself for me anymore. Ever. If I even hear you do something like this again, I’ll do the same immediately. Whatever you do, I’ll do. Do you hear me?”

“I- “

“Yes or no.”

“Yes.”

She let her hair loose, shaking it.

“Good. Second, don’t even think about leaving. I don’t care if you murder someone or commit treason or piss me off to the ends of the earth. You are not allowed to leave me because of some vague bullshit. If we have to, we’ll bury the bodies together. You’re stuck with me now. Okay?”

She began to slip off her torn dress, having trouble at first, before deciding to just tear it off piece by piece.

Subaru was transfixed.

“…Yes.”

“Finally, third. I AM selfish. Why? Because even if I feel like I’ll never be able to repay you. I’d still rather keep you for myself than let you find someone better. In fact, I’d rather let the world burn than have someone else take you from me.”

Subaru didn’t hesitate, “…There is no one better.”

“Good boy.”

She finished off by throwing the last piece of clothing on his face. He brushed it off and gawked.

She.

She was.

Artwork.

The most stunning piece of art he could have ever seen.

The merchant laughed warmly, “I knew it was a good idea to wear my favorite pair on the first date.”

“I uh, bwah, huh?”

“Shhh,” she brought a finger to his lips and leaned down to him, grabbing the edge of his clothing, “I got thirty or more years in me now. I’m going to spend it wisely.”

Subaru gulped, his face red. She grabbed his hands, warmth echoed through him.

He focused one last time on her.

It was still there.

Glowing in a myriad of colors, it flickered to life, a small strand of light connecting from it to him.

This was real.

All that effort…Worth it.

“Uh, Subaru,” he was knocked out of his Authority by her words, shaking his head he focused on the bright light once again.

Wait.

No.

He was not in his Authority anymore.

What was that light?

Her hands.

They were glowing. At the tips.

Panicking, he reentered his authority. But the Od wasn’t being used up. It was still alive. Glowing and staying the same. Nothing draining it.

Which meant…

“Ana,” the pale star nodded, already understanding herself, “I think…your gate is fixed.”

Notes:

EN1: Well, kind of. You'll see next time.
EN2: No lemons or smut for this fic by the way, at least not in this format.

Chapter 23: Some Stay the Same, Others...

Summary:

Changes and more changes...

Notes:

Enjoy!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

“Again, in fact.”

A beam of light shot from two fingers arcing past an appa hanging from a branch.

“…You are very bad at this, in fact.”

“Could you give this gal a break?!” Anastasia snarled at the little spirit reading a book next to her.

They were practicing magic in a park nearby. It was Beatrice’s idea. Test her limits given her newly rejuvenated magic ability.

Yeah.

Magic.

That was. New.

 

It felt.

Od. It felt weird.

Not bad. Good, definitely. New. And…well. Just, jarring.

So many changes. So much to process in just a week.

For starters.

 

 

“Stop mating so much-MMPH!”

Halibel slapped a hand over Tia’s mouth, “What she meant to say, is while it’s great y’all are being a healthy couple, ya need to calm down a bit.”

While both stars started to blush, Anastasia pouted and crossed her arms, “We are not THAT bad…”

Halibel stared at Anastasia, “Ana-bo. I have never met someone who can’t walk in the morning like you. Props to Su-san but, ya gotta understand that ain’t normal.”

The merchant gawked at the judgmental stares she was receiving.

What? Can’t a gal enjoy her newfound romance with her fiancé.

 

Just thinking about Subaru being her fiancé made her heart skip a beat.

Still, she kept pouting, “…”

Subaru fed her some daisukiyaki they made earlier. Her cheeks were still puffed, with good food and resentment.

Halibel sighed, “…I am not gettin’ those energy potions for ya.”

Subaru looked at Halibel weirdly, “Wait, what- “

Anastasia quickly stopped pouting and slammed her hands over Subaru’s ears, she glared at Halibel, “Can you please not say that out loud?!”

The wolfman deadpanned at her, “Ana-bo. You are plenty loud yourself-OW!”

Halibel rubbed where Tia bit his hand, as the murder spirit focused on the stars, “You need. To stop. Mating. Now.”

Anastasia shrugged her shoulders, “Yeaaaah. No.”

Tia snarled at her, but Anastasia just rolled her eyes, retorting, “Aren’t you the one who was always encouraging us to do the deed all the time? What changed your mind?”

“I haven’t slept for two days straight…” The spirit was death glaring her with malicious intent. Unfortunately, everyone in the house was now used to Tia’s bloodlust.

“Can’t you just move to another room, or cover your ears?”

Not breaking eye contact, Zarestia pointed at the wolf, “That mutt. Won’t let me switch rooms.”

Halibel shrugged, “Hey, ya chose it. Not my fault.”

She then pointed at Beatrice and Eridna who were sipping tea together, “…”

The two spirits didn’t say anything.

Tia picked up a pillow and threw it at them.

Beatrice stopped it midair and threw it back.

Tia cut it in half.

Halibel stared at his furniture being torn apart by two annoying spirits, he pinched his snout.

This was a usual occurrence. Halibel had to allocate a ton of the household budget to replacement furniture. On the plus side, they had a lot of firewood. On the minus side, all of the chairs and tables mismatched.

Tia looked at them, “Don’t you have anything to say?! You’re right next to them too.”

Beatrice shrugged, Eridna did her best version of a shrug, “We use a silencing spell.”

Tia stared at them, eye twitching, her bloodlust somehow rising another level, “…And you didn’t tell me this before, because?”

Beatrice looked at Tia like she was an idiot, “You didn’t ask, I suppose.”

“…”

Tia picked up a table and was about to pancake Beatrice before, “TIA!”

She swung her head towards Subaru, who was still having his ears covered by Anastasia.

He looked very disappointed, shaking his head, “Down. Now.”

Tia frowned, “But Su- “

“Tia.”

“…Okay.”

She put it down and pouted.

Anastasia laughed, getting another death glare from the wind spirit, “Karma.”

“What does that even mean?”

The merchant had a shit-eating grin, “Sorry, fiancé’s rights.”
“I hate you. So much.”

“Cry about it.”

“I swear, you’re making it louder every night just to annoy me!” Tia pointed at Anastasia, “See Su! Look at her face, she’s doing it on purpose.”

Subaru couldn’t hear but it seemed he could understand Tia’s facial expressions. Even though most of them were variations of frothing rage.

“Maybe, she’s got a point Ana-pop,” the black star said as he removed her hands and turned towards her.

Anastasia’s smile dropped, “Oh come now, it isn’t that bad- “

“Ana,” Subaru looked down, “I literally might have to make you a makeshift wheelchair at this rate.”

The woman wasn’t exactly standing but more limping, hanging onto Subaru for dear life. Anastasia’s legs were basically non-existent at this point, just flabs of meat. Honestly, she was afraid her hip might have broken last night.

 

Still, it didn’t stop her from enjoying herself.

 

“…Can’t a gal enjoy her new life with her man?”

Subaru smiled and kissed her cheek, “Course not, I’m just afraid I’ll have to carry you all the time.”

“I wouldn’t mind. Like at all. Carry me forever,” Anastasia spread her arms.

Subaru chuckled, “As you wish, my Lady!”

He then picked her up and spun her around, bridal style, both of them laughing.

In the background, Halibel mimed gagging as Tia just got annoyed. Beatrice and Eridna smiled as both of them took a nap. In reality, all four of them are happy for the two stars.

 

Tia just wants one night of full sleep. And she’ll get it, even if she has to toss Anastasia outside for a whole night. She can survive. Tia believes in her. Worst case scenario, she’ll just kill whoever touches Ana. Simple.

As Subaru spun her around, he kissed her neck and then her lips, before they both fell to the ground, smiling.

This was also a change. A weird but welcoming change. Subaru was much, much more affectionate with her.

He’d hug her every second he had the chance. They would sometimes slow dance with each other before bed, humming songs that Subaru taught her. He would kiss her everywhere or just hang around her body lazily.

Her daily routine changed as well.

He would give her a wake up kiss in the mornings. They would cuddle. They would…go further. Then they’d get dressed. Sometimes, they would get undressed again. Then they would go get ready, finally. Get breakfast. Work. Get distracted. Kiss. Work. Lunch. Distracted. Work. Distracted. Work. Dinner. Distract. Distracted. Distracted. All night, really distracted.

 

Anastasia loved getting distracted. It felt weird. New. She never desired this kind of life. She always expected that her work would take priority.

But no. Nowadays, her only priority was the love of her life.

She heard from Subaru that this was the ‘honeymoon’ phase or something.

That people eventually calm down and it becomes a routine.

That’s dumb. Those people are dumb.

Anastasia doesn’t want that. She’ll make everyday, until the very end, a honeymoon phase. She loves this. She loves her life right now. She loves all the people around her.

 

…She misses her family. She misses them so much.

 

 

 

“Alright, take a break,” Beatrice walked over as Anastasia sat down, gasping, “You weren’t even using your body physically, why are you so worn out?”

The merchant glared, “It…requires…concentration…plus…you’re…making me…do…flow.”

Beatrice shrugged, “Well, Betty expects you to do better, in fact.”

“…You’re so annoying.”

The little spirit rolled her eyes, “You chose this.”

“…”

Yeah. She did. It all started the day after Subaru and Anastasia had their first night together.

 

 

“Amazing,” Eridna and Beatrice checked their gates, curiosity dancing withing their eyes, “It is as if they’re gates have been…molded.”

Subaru raised an eyebrow, “Is that…gooooood?”

Eridna shook her head, “I do not know. Your gates are different now. It’s as if they are connected but not. The mana flows one direction. But not the other. And even then, well. Can you demonstrate one more time?”

Both stars nodded, they held hands, the mana flowing from Subaru to Anastasia as he concentrated his Authority. Anastasia began to channel the mana to her tips, the particles converting from Yin to Yang, and creating a light glow, the beginnings of a Jiwald.

Subaru himself tried to channel the mana.

 

And he couldn’t. His gate was still technically defective.

Well, both of theirs still were.

Eridna cocked her head, “So, Su can absorb mana, but Ana cannot. Ana can use mana but Su cannot. Su can transfer mana to Ana, but the mana cannot transfer back to Su…Sister, what are your thoughts?”

Beatrice was pacing a hole within their living room again.

She started to ramble, “Betty believes this is extraordinary. Subaru’s Greed Authority essentially linked the two’s gates. What Betty doesn’t get is why the gate was treated differently…the curses and Ods were shared in similar ways, but not the gate. Why was his broken gate not considered a ‘burden’ in fact?”

Beatrice theorized that Subaru’s Authority is based around the idea of ‘burdens’ or ‘responsibility.’

“Perhaps it couldn’t share his ‘burden’ as he calls it, because there was nothing to share. It could not repair the other without causing new damage… so it wasn’t sufficient for the contract. Instead, since the Od’s connected, it must connect the gates in some capacity as well. There is a link that tunnels from one person to the other, transferring whatever is needed, I suppose. But why does it not go from Ana to Subaru?!”

Beatrice rubbed her head in frustration, “ARGH! Authorities are so weird, in fact! They don’t work with reality, they bend reality. But there are limits! Is this a limit on Subaru or is it a limit on the authority, I suppose…”

This was something Anastasia couldn’t wrap her head around at first.

 

Subaru. Had an Authority. Apparently, a witch factor. Which apparently gave him world altering powers. And apparently, they were originally held by the Archbishops of the Witch Cult. And Witches throughout history.

 

Yeah.

 

She only threw up once when hearing that.

 

You can’t blame her. Even in Kararagi, the stories of the Witch of Envy and the Witch Cult resonated far and wide.

The fact that Subaru…got something related to them in him. Amazed her, intrigued her, and slightly terrified her. She had so many questions.

Especially when he kept acting like Subaru, she remembered his first reaction when she looked at him, concerned and rightly terrified for his well-being, “Well it isn’t that bad…”

She stared at him as he said that. Stared at him until he realized how stupid he was acting.

“Okay, it might. Just might…cause changes to my personality. Like…just a bit.”

 

…She almost punched him when she heard that.
That, stupid. Handsome idiot.

Beatrice kept pacing the floor muttering to herself before finally pointing at Subaru, “You said you had to promise each other to share ‘everything’ before the contract started to fulfill itself, correct?”

Subaru nodded, “Yeah, I framed it as marriage vows, that way it was easier to swallow.”

She glared at him, he sheepishly shrugged and smiled at her.

She was still pissed. Like. Immensely. Pissed. That he would do such a thing.

On the one hand, it was the dumbest thing he had ever done, and she had half a mind to put him on the couch forever for it.

On the other hand…she can’t help but feel grateful. Can you blame her? She has nearly as much time to live as she had before Priestella. Her gate was no longer a problem, she could simply get the mana from Subaru rather than the environment. And not only that, her beloved, who was previously struggling to choose her over two other beautiful women, somehow got an epiphany out of nowhere and chose to throw his whole life on the line to save her. And chose to save her by proposing.

 

It felt like it came straight out of one of Julius’s romance novels. She was sure if he was here, he’d be having a full-blown geek out, or however Subaru called it.

 

Anastasia sighed, “What am I going to tell our kids? That their father tricked their poor mother on the day he proposed…” she pretended to swoon dramatically and laid her head on his chest.

Subaru just gave her a look, “Technically. You tricked me the first time I met you.”

Anastasia looked up at him and smiled.

“Technically. I don’t remember that.”

He tapped her nose with his finger.

“Technically. You’re an idiot.”

She tapped his nose back.

“Technically. I’m your idiot.”

Beatrice barged in, squeezing both their noses, “Technically, we are still discussing how insane your situation is, I suppose!”

She grumbled as Eridna chuckled, “I find it quite fascinating. It reminds me of how my possession works. It’s as if your gates are pushing together. Yet they cannot, due to the fact you are still two separate people.”

Beatrice snapped her fingers, pointing to Subaru, “Perhaps that is it. They are separate people. Even if the authority can affect reality, it isn’t strong enough yet. It’s still one way. Perhaps, because Subaru has authority, it has always only flowed one way. From him to them. Sharing his burdens, or perhaps not even just burdens, but all conditions he has, in fact. Maybe, with enough time, he can figure out how to connect and take from people. Authorities have been known to evolve with time, becoming stronger with compatible users. Subaru is very compatible with Greed, in fact. Unlike his sloth witch factor.”

Anastasia rose an eyebrow, “Sloth, the one you got from the guy you killed with Julius.”

Beatrice flinched but Subaru quickly focused her attention on him, “Yeah. It’s not very compatible with me…making it less useful. I call it Invisible Providence. All it does is create an invisible hand that can interact with objects and things. It can even go through walls or flesh.”

“…So, you could possibly crush people’s hearts?”

“Okay, yes, but do you have to be so morbid?!”

Anastasia shrugged, “What? Can’t a gal figure out all the cool new tricks that her fiancé has in his pocket?”

Subaru blushed, even he can’t handle their newfound status, it was cute, “I mean yeah sure, I guess.”

She tapped her chin, “So, what are you calling Greed?”

“Well, I was thinking Cor Leonis, since it came from Regulus, but it kind of doesn’t fit the whole power and theme…”

Anastasia snorted, “Only you would care this much about naming a witch’s power.”

“Do you want me to call it ‘Poo poo lagoo’?”

“I retract my previous statement.”

“See? It needs to be aesthetically pleasing or else it just sounds dumb. Might as well call it something that fits the whole ‘burdens’ thing. I mean if I’m going for the whole Atlas theme, might as well call it ‘The World.’”

Subaru looked at Anastasia smiling which he immediately dropped as she appeared confused, “Right…I guess I didn’t tell you about Jojo yet.”

She raised her eyebrow as Subaru looked slightly depressed, he simply shook his head, “It’s a story from back home. I’ll tell you later. You’ll definitely love it.”

She smiled. Every evening, as they lay together. Right after making love but before journeying to dreamland, he would tell her stories from back home. This was a usual habit of theirs but nowadays it has become even more special.

Anastasia leaned onto his shoulder, contemplating, “Well… how about naming it something that doesn’t fit? You told me you figured out that dumbass archbishop’s weakness because of his name, right? What if that happens to you? Someone from your home could target you to and guess your power from the name. Make it something that fits but misleads.”

Subaru was stumped, he scratched his head, “Hmmm, even though it would be rare, you’re right, it’s still a possibility. But that just makes it harder.”

She grabbed his hand and held it, preventing him from scratching, “Well you said Cor Leonis was another name for Regulus, right? Any others?”

“…In Greek, the star was also called Basiliskos.”

Her eyes shined, “Similar to our company, right? Atlas and Pleione came from their religion or, what you called, ‘mythology.’”

He blushed, “Right…it also meant ‘little king,’ hence the connection to Regulus. Basiliskos was a serpent monster that could kill people by just looking at them, turning them into stone.”

She snapped her fingers, “Make it like that. If someone tried to guess your power, they’ll think you need to look at people to switch injuries. Or that the power comes from your eyes. You don’t need to have vision to do it right?”

Subaru closed his eyes for a sec, looking around, before opening, “Yep. If I concentrate, it doesn’t matter if my eyes are open or not. I can still people’s Ods.”

Anastasia got excited, “Pretend you need eyesight to do it. Then, when someone targets your vision, they’ll let their guard down. Allowing ya to switch the blindness to them.”

Subaru stared at his fiancée for a second before grabbing her face, “You are the smartest person in the world.”

She acted smug, “I know.”

“Also, the scariest.”

“That, I also know.”

“Alright,” he gave her a quick peck on her cheek before standing up, “It’s decided. I’ll call it Ops Basiliskos, ancient Greek for ‘Eye of the Serpent King.’ Honestly, it kind of sounds badass. My middle school self would be proud.”

Anastasia waved her arms out, gripping her hands rapidly, “And who do you have to thank for that?”

Subaru gave a warm smile before picking her up and bridal carrying the little lady in one motion, “My wonderful future wife.”

She giggled, “Well this wonderful wife would like to- “

“Hold it,” Beatrice held out a hand, “Before you start making Betty’s ears bleed, we need to discuss your newfound powers a bit more.”

The little spirit pointed at Subaru, “You need to figure out the limits of your authority, testing how this bond works and whether it can be replicated in others.”

She then pointed at Anastasia, “And you need to practice magic. Now that you’re able to take Subaru’s mana, having you proficient at casting spells would add another layer of protection. Plus, Betty has a theory, I suppose.”

The two stars cocked their heads as Eridna explained, “Sissy believes that there may be a way to fix your Ods. Well, two possible methods. Though one is more… morally complicated.”

Anastasia frowned, “Tell us the complicated one first.”

The little spirit sighed, “Betty believes that if Subaru can replicate the exact parameters of how he created a contract with you, then he could hypothetically do it again with other people. Essentially, if Subaru were to ‘marry’ other- “

“Absolutely not.”

“Let Betty finish!” Anastasia got annoyed but Subaru calmed her down by snuggling her from behind, “Geez, Betty is not advocating for Subaru to cheat on you! Betty is advocating for Subaru to try experimenting with people close to him to see what exactly allowed the contract to go through. To see if it is purely romantic or could be also platonic. For example, if he were to make a contract with Betty, then he could share my Od with both of you, in fact.”

Subaru seemed to understand, still snuggling a slightly peeved pale star, “I get what you’re saying…the complicated part.”

Beatrice grimly nodded, “You essentially have to accept that we are willing to give you part of our lives. An entirely different problem compared to giving your own, I suppose.”

Subaru’s hands were still wrapped around her waist, she grabbed one of them, “Subaru. I know you may have reservations…but think of how I felt when you did that to me.”

He flinched, “Betrayed…”

She pinched his hand, “More like annoyed that you went ahead without even asking me. The problem is that you expected me to just reject you outright.”

“…”

The silence was damning, “…I get it. Everyone shouldn’t sacrifice themselves for each other. It’s redundant. But if you’re going to be the type of person who will cut their life in half for the people you love. You have to expect that the people you love are willing to do the same. That not only me, but Beatrice, Halibel, Tia, and even Eridna, are all willing to give a part of themselves to make you happy. To make us happy.”

“…” his grip tightened around her.

She sighed, “It won’t be easy to get out of your mindset…but the fact that you were able to make a contract with me using Greed, shows that it is in fact possible.”

Beatrice nodded, “Ana is right. If it happens once, it can happen again. You just have to accept that it’s our turn to help you. Well, you and the girl, I suppose.”

Ana rubbed Beatrice’s head for that, the little spirit only frowned but didn’t whack her hand away like usual.

Subaru was silent for a second before shoving his face into Anastasia’s hair, though his voice was muffled, they could clearly hear him say, “…I’m very lucky…”

He popped his head out and clapped his cheeks, “Okay! Operation: ‘How the Hell Does An Authority Work?’ is a go!”

The three women laughed at his resolve. Beatrice then focused on Anastasia, “Now for the second method. Betty believes Subaru’s will be the easiest given that he has evidence of succeeding. You on the other hand, do not.”

The merchant rolled her eyes, “Gee thanks. So, what is it then? It’s not like magic can make us live longer.”

“…”

“…Beatrice.”

The little girl didn’t look her in the eye. Anastasia’s eyes widened.

“No way. That’s- “

“Impossible?” The little spirit finished for her, finally looking into the merchant’s eyes, her own holding hesitance, “Nothing is impossible, as mother liked to say. It just requires the right amount of effort and willpower, as well as the right materials. Luckily, you and Subaru are the correct materials, in fact.”

Anastaisa narrowed her eyes in confusion as Beatrice took a deep breath, signaling her sister, who promptly latched on and conducted possession, they spoke in unison, “Hypothetically. The problem with magic is that it is impossible to turn pure mana back into life force. You can draw life force from your Od to create mana particles, but there is no way to reverse it. In addition, even if you could potentially do so, a lot of mana is lost as heat as you cast a spell or when you convert it to different types, I suppose.”

Subaru seemed to understand, “Like entropy.”

They all looked at him strangely, he snapped his finger, “Ah. I forgot, physics isn’t as advanced here. So back home, scientists made a theory that chaos is simply the natural form of all. And that eventually, everything returns to entropy, or total randomness. In terms of thermodynamics, or at least how energy works, no matter what, you’ll always have energy lost when converting from one type to the other. It’s why perpetual motion machines, or machines that create energy for itself, are impossible. Or I guess in terms of magic, it’s impossible to have someone make mana from life force and return it back to life force without potentially losing some of it to heat.”

Beatrice nodded excitedly, “Exactly. However, mana itself cannot be returned to the Od as it is. It needs to convert into something else. Scholars have tried to figure that out for years, but have found nothing. The closest they’ve gotten is with water magic…and it failed, in fact.”

The girl shuddered, “Anyways, not important, the point Betty is trying to make is that it was thought to be impossible to turn mana into energy for the Od…until now, I suppose.”

Beatrice and Eridna channeled their mana from within. As they held out their hand, a small dance of a black sphere and white sphere twirled within their hand, “Subaru. Can you use your Authority to check our Ods?”

Subaru obliged, “…I don’t see anything.”

The little girl frowned and turned off the light show, “Figures. Betty theorized that if she channeled it, there could be a greater effect than simply shooting a spell. Back to the drawing board on that, I suppose.”

Anastasia still didn’t understand, “What were you trying to prove with this? You’ve explained Yin-Yang magic before, terrible name aside, it seems powerful enough on its own…don’t tell me.”

Anastasia’s neurons fired and connected as Beatrice confirmed, “You assume correctly. Betty has been checking her and her sister’s bodies extensively while experimenting, rooting out any possible flaws the magic may have, whether it is a detriment or poison to their body as a side effect. So far, Betty has found nothing. Well, almost nothing. One positive side effect, I suppose.”

 

Beatrice turned off the possession, and held her sister close, “Betty and sister’s Ods are now larger than they were a few months ago.”

 

 

“Jiwald! Shamak!”

A burst of light hit the appa on the tree while a small puff of black smoke billowed out in front, wisping into the air.

“Better, in fact. You were able to shoot off two spells of different affinity, though the Yin spell was incredibly weak.”

Anastasia was gasping right next to her, on her hands and knees, “Again…flow method…also…not good with Yin…”

The drill-haired child walked over with a bottle of water, “Yet you are able to use a lot more mana than before. The flow method is improving your body’s stamina while also getting it used to mana consumption. You’ll be a lot more efficient with this method, I suppose.”

“Yeah…I guess…Od…this sucks.”

“Stop complaining, you still aren’t done.”

Anastasia glared at Beatrice before sighing and complying. This was for her and Subaru’s happiness. She can’t be angry at Beatrice for that.

The merchant collapsed onto the floor, sitting up, and grabbed the water bottle with one hand while holding out her other, palm faced upward.

She then channeled her mana.

Right now she had two mana types swirling in her Gate. Yang and Yin. The Yang was from her gate while the Yin was from Subaru’s. Usually, having mana directly from another person could cause poisoning or rejection. Without a spirit fine tuning the mana flow, it could lead to the receiver becoming intensely ill. However, Subaru’s Authority seemed to subvert that rule, somehow. It didn’t remove all the side effects, nausea was still a factor, but it didn’t poison her body and make her want to expel the particles immediately.

She tried to imagine the two types bouncing off each other, willing the mana to constantly collide with itself so that it can create that ‘Yin-Yang’ effect or whatever it’s called.

Honestly that name sucks. Once she figures this out, and when she figures this out, she’s going to patent the magic and name it something cool.

…Oh Od, she’s becoming more like Subaru.

BANG!

Mana burst from her hand, exploding into a thin flash of light and concussive force, knocking her onto her back.

Beatrice stood over her, disappointed, “Betty told you to focus and not think of anything stupid, in fact.”

I was thinking of my future husband!

…Okay, point taken.

Anastasia groaned, “This is going to take forever.”

“Betty said that as well. Remember, you need to combine the magic types constantly. That way the resulting energy –“

“Could potentially be siphoned by my Od and extend its longevity. Yeah, yeah. I got it. For the billionth time,” Anastasia waved her hand in the air.

“Betty swears you are acting more like Subaru every day.”

“I’ll take that as a compliment, considering we both like that dumbass.”

“Hmph!” The little spirit pouted as the merchant giggled.

“…”

“…”

“…Betty. I have a question.”

“When do you not have a question, in fact?”

“I’m being serious. Something has been bothering me this entire week. Could you put up that silencing spell you invented?”

Beatrice stared at the girl before slowly nodding, sitting down next to her, she waved her hand in the air, “El Selin…there. Now speak. Betty will not judge whatever it is you have to say, I suppose.”

 

“Betty,” Anastasia gazed at the spirit with an incredibly serious expression, “I have a theory.”

 

“…I think Subaru can control time.”
