Chapter 24: Revelations

Summary:

Anastasia and Beatrice begin to unravel...

Notes:

Enjoy!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

“I’m being serious.”

“Betty is too. This is insane. You are acting hysterical.”

“I am not,” Anastasia gripped the little spirit close, “My mind is incredibly clear. This whole week…it’s felt off.”

The little spirit raised an eyebrow, “Off in what way?”

“Everything!” Anastasia’s eyes became slightly frantic, she quickly covered her mouth and calmed herself, “…My instincts feel like they are going haywire. It’s like…everything is too perfect. Like things are going so well. Too well.”

“Ana-“

“I know how that sounds but bear with me here. Subaru has been wonderful. I feel amazing every day. I have a loving ‘boyfriend’ or fiancé or whatever Subaru calls it. I should be happy…and I am. But something still feels off. Subaru’s mannerisms, his behavior as of late, it feels like something finally clicked within my mind finally. And I started to truly understand what’s going on.”

“…And you believe this is related to…time control?”

“Yes. Subaru has been telling me stories. Stories from these ‘movies’ or mahngah or whatever. Jojo, Back to the Future, Terminator.”

Beatrice looked slightly peeved, “You really just like boasting, don’t you?”

“Can we focus?! I’ll tell you the stories later, I just need to-“ Anastasia pinched her nose, her eyes were tired, “I need to give context. Subaru often would tell me these stories. But some of them would have this concept of time travel. Going backwards or forwards in time. Or controlling time. Or something similar. But he would always act a little off when talking about it.”

“Like how?”

“His words and voice gets a little stilted. Like he tries to be very careful about what he says. You could say that he is passionate about the subject and trying not to be wrong. But here’s the thing: he only does that in certain instances. When we are in danger, when he talks about certain people, or when he is about to have a panic attack. He shouldn’t act like this with those stories…but he does. And the correlating factor between all of them is there is some sort of time related plot device.”

Beatrice didn’t look convinced, “Be that as it may-“

“He knows how to cook daisukiyaki almost perfectly.”

Beatrice stared at her, “Okay, now Betty thinks you are reaching, in fact.”

“No, you need to understand. He did it almost perfectly. Which was strange because we never made it before. I had a plan to make it for one of our dates last week, but it got cancelled because…well, you know.”

The proposal.

Anastasia continued, her eyes narrowing, arms crossed, her hand tapping her forearm repeatedly, “Yet he was able to cook the recipe nearly perfectly. I assumed that maybe Subaru had experience cooking it back home. Subaru also said he tried it back in Priestella. However, the recipe I gave him was one of my special ones. The one I usually made. It’s hard to do because you need to cook the seafood just right, or else you either burn the batter, or the meat gets too raw. Yet, he did it almost perfectly the first time I gave it to him.”

“…Subaru could be just a natural cook.”

“Possible but doubtful, his stories say otherwise. Subaru is not good at cooking without practice.”

“Maybe he had a similar recipe back home.”

“Also unlikely, Subaru said the ingredients here are slightly different. Even in the most unlikely probable situations where everything aligned perfectly, I would still see him make mistakes given that it is his first time and he is not a professional.”

Beatrice tried to retort but Anastasia didn’t let her, constantly rambling a word train, her eyes trailing to the ground slowly, “When we were exploring some of the areas I wanted to show him, he initially acted like he didn’t know Banan that well. But when I took him to some of my childhood haunts, his behavior was strange. There was a park that I used to hide in when I was a child, and it had a massive hill with a tree. The hill has a small staircase where one of the tiles was loose. If you stepped on it, the thing made a loud ringing sound. I would go into that tree and hear if anyone followed me by using that tile as a doorbell.”

Her eyes refocused on Beatrice, manic, “…Yet Subaru avoided it.”

It was creeping Beatrice out, “Maybe Subaru was lucky.”

“Again, possible but unlikely. It’s the first step. That staircase has large gaps between each step.  The only way to get past it is to make a large jump from the bottom to the very next step. No one does it because it’s inconvenient. I do it because I’m used to it. But when I asked Subaru to go first, he ended up doing what I usually do. As if…he saw it before.”

Anastasia’s eyes became frantic, vomiting out theories that she’d been keeping within for a while, “There are other oddities as well. Subaru acts differently. He’s more affectionate, which is nice, but it came from out of nowhere. In addition, when I talk to him about Emilia or Rem, his reactions became a complete 180. I don’t mean that he hates them now. No. Instead… it’s like he doesn’t care anymore. Which is weird. I don’t believe someone can get over their past flames that quickly. I don’t care what Subaru says, he isn’t the type of person to do that. He’s passionate, loving, and loyal beyond fault. He wouldn’t ignore them completely unless something were to provoke that out of him. It’s only been over a week since I last saw him speak so passionately about those two. Now? The fire is gone. Not even embers remain.”

She began to frown, “He’s also…more comfortable with uncomfortable topics. Before, he would squirm or reject any of my more unsavory ideas. Now? It’s like he completely accepts my pragmatism. Hell, one time, when I was explaining how we could corner the market by running every single one of the local stores out of business with his condiments, he didn’t bat an eye. No. He even added onto it. Saying that he could flood the market with hired experts and citizens who would praise our goods but criticize the locals. Subaru would normally argue with me that we should try to recruit the local stores first. I mentioned it as a joke so I can teach him more about basic merchant skills. But that didn’t happen. He took it 100% seriously. It’s as if his moral compass is slightly off now…and again, it happened out of nowhere.”

Beatrice was reaching for straws now too, “Maybe… maybe he changed after accepting his love for you.”

Anastasia started to smile softly before immediately her face turned pensive, “Impossible. Though it makes my heart flutter, this isn’t a romance novel. Subaru isn’t someone who gives in like that. He’s a very moral person. I doubt he could change that easily off a whim and certainly not off of love…he would need a very good reason to do all that.”

“Ana. Betty understands that you have worries, in fact,” she placed a hand on the merchant’s shoulder, “But this doesn’t explain why you are acting incredibly hysterical. You look…scared, I suppose.”

Anastasia was quiet for some time before her eyes stared into the little spirit’s, almost on the verge of tears.

“…I’ve also been having dreams. Weird dreams.”

Her eyes reflected the abyss, “Dreams where I’m in some dark place. And I feel so alone. But not alone. Like there is something there. Watching me. And I also feel something else. I feel like…Subaru is there. But he is not there. It’s like he’s somewhere far but close. And the problem is I feel like he’s in pain. Like he’s suffocating. And I don’t know why I know that. But I do! And it makes me so scared and so angry. So, fucking angry. Because he’s hurting but I can’t reach him. But he’s right there! In front of me. I keep moving but I can’t go. I keep trying to say anything, but nothing comes out. It’s like I’m trapped in a swamp. And he’s right there–“

“Ana!” Anastasia stopped rambling, her eyes widened looking at Beatrice, the little girl’s expression drowning in concern, “…Stop, in fact.”

Confused, she followed Beatrice’s gaze.

 

And immediately became alarmed.

Without even thinking.

Without noticing.

She was scratching herself on her forearm. Not enough to cause bleeding…but enough to leave a nasty pink mark.

 

It reminded her of Subaru.

“…That’s not normal.”

“You think?!” Beatrice started to heal the girl, allowing the marks to fade, “Betty knew Subaru was too hasty…there must be other side effects to his authority. There always is a drawback, in fact.”

 

Something clicked in Anastasia’s mind.

 

She gripped the spirit’s shoulders, startling the poor girl, “B-betty. I need to know. This whole, authority thing. It…scares me. The more I think about it. The more I wonder if it isn’t possibly poisoning Subaru. Or if it’s changing his personality. Or if it has a cost that we don’t know. Or…Subaru has a power that he doesn’t want to share. Because-”

She choked, the idea making her feel nauseous.

“…Because if Subaru has the power to control time. And if it comes from an Authority. What is the drawback? What ‘payment’ does he have to give to use it? What makes him so scared beyond having people target him? What makes him choose his words so carefully that he looks like he’s on the verge of a breakdown?”

And if he could time travel, what are the limitations? What’s stopping him from going back to Priestella?

…Anastasia had theories. None of them she wanted confirmation. Because the very idea that it could be true, may break her.

Beatrice gazed at the girl for a second, before taking her hands off the spirit’s shoulders, holding them close, trying to comfort her “…Betty wishes she could say that these are all baseless. That all of this is simply some paranoid fantasy that you pushed onto yourself. But Betty would be lying if she did so…because your words make some modicum of sense, outlandish they are, in fact.”

The merchant sniffed, her panic attack slowly dissipating, she rubbed her tears with her shoulder, “…I don’t know what to do Betty. I feel like I’m in the happiest time of my life. But everything feels…wrong. Like something isn’t right. I thought it was missing my camp. That I wanted them here. So, we can all be happy together.”

“…But?”

“…But I think the real reason is that I’m scared of what Subaru experienced. He said my Od was breaking. He said that I could have died by now…what did he see? Did he see me die? How many times did he see me die? What did he sacrifice to travel back? How many times has he done this before?! What is stopping him from talking about it?! Is the cost silence? Or is it something more sinister?”

Anastasia shivered, a lot of the pent up paranoia she’s been keeping under everything crept up, lately her emotions have been running haywire, she doesn’t know exactly why, there are times where her mind goes on tedious ramblings and long-winded thought trains that never cease. The dreams weren’t helping.

She gulped, her throat dry, “…I just wish I could have my memories of him back. I met him before…if I could see how Subaru acted during certain moments, I can get a better understanding. I could talk to other people, interrogate his former camp- “

“And get Betty’s opinion on whether your theory runs true or not,” Beatrice interrupted, understanding dawning on her.
“…Yeah. If I’m correct, you were the closest to him, based on his stories. If anyone could know if I’m right, or hell if anyone probably figured this out, it could be you.”

“…”

“…”

Beatrice swallowed, her own guilt eating her up from the inside, “Betty cannot tell you now, obviously. However, Betty has had some observations on Subaru’s actions,” Beatrice’s brow began to furrow, “During his activities when initially entering Banan, Subaru’s actions showed complete confidence in navigating the city, finding that wolfman, and how that doppelganger was searching for him. That level of knowledge could only be possible if Subaru experienced that himself, in fact.”

Anastasia nodded vigorously, “So you agree that he must be experiencing some sort of version of these events. At least prematurely. And then experiencing them again through his Authority or whatever.”

“Yes. Betty will concede that your theory holds the most weight. As for the cost, Betty surmises that abilities such as those that could literally rewrite history or fate, would have an incredible price, I suppose. Mother paid her cost dearly as well and so did Guese…”

Beatrice began to also word vomit, “The Witch of Wrath could heal anything and anyone, at the cost of causing equal amounts of carnage somewhere else in the world. The Witch of Gluttony could make hundreds of mabeasts and make anyone feel endless hunger…at the cost of experiencing such a fate herself. The Witch of Lust could make people see their most cherished loved ones, which made her a target for many people while also causing those very same people to stop breathing, in fact.”

Anastasia nodded even more, the dots connecting, “So, Authorities often have a cost that are not necessarily direct, but more indirect. Wrath had a cost that was not apparent initially. Gluttony had a cost that was self-inflicted. And Lust had a cost that made her own power detrimental to those around her.”

Beatrice put it nicely, “A natural consequence, a side effect, and uncontrollable power, I suppose.”

Anastaisa no longer felt like she was on the verge of the abyss. Instead focusing on logic, “In that case, let’s see which one fits Subaru’s dilemma. His Greed Authority for example is a ‘natural consequence.’ Subaru must inflict his own wounds on himself to use it as a weapon.”

Beatrice added onto that, “Betty remembers that the Greed Authority often makes the user hyper-fixate on certain ideas…a side effect of the power, I suppose. Sloth was the same, usually pushing the person to be as lazy as possible. From what Subaru says, his side effect was more related to incompatibility. The nausea and corruption he felt from using Invisible Providence most likely stems from the pieces not aligning correctly, rather than any direct contribution from the Authority’s power.”

“…And the third ability. Time travel. What could possibly be the costs?”

“If we go by natural consequence, it could be that Subaru remembers all the pain he suffers during that period all at once. The second he transports, his mind can’t handle the sudden influx of information…causing Subaru to react badly, I suppose.”

Anastasia held her face within her hands, she ran her fingers through her hair, “That would explain his odd behavior at certain times. Back when we just left the Royal Capital, when we arrived at Banan, and recently on our first date. He suddenly had an odd spasm or a weird reaction that made him stop mid-conversation. Those are probably when he suddenly transported to that time…”

Beatrice started pacing again, tapping her chin, “That’s one possible cost. What about a side effect? Is there something that could cause Subaru to be unintentionally hurt by the power, in fact?”

“Well besides the memory influx, the only thing I can think of is that Subaru has to do a lot of…things…again,” her mind started to rapid fire, “Depending on how long Subaru went back, perhaps he’ll have to redo everything again. Recreate relationships. Foster trust. Go through the motions. Experience everything once more.”

That would explain how he was able to negotiate with Halibel so quickly.

Beatrice was confused, “Is that bad, in fact? It just sounds tedious?”

Anastasia started scratching her head, “Of course it’s bad. Subaru is experiencing more life than most people. He could be experiencing more in one day than most people do…he’s getting older faster than others. His mind has more memories. He’s on a different timescale than us. Maybe the unintentional side effect is that Subaru doesn’t age normally, skipping years ahead, depending on how much he does so.”

Beatrice narrowed her eyes, “Plausible. It would explain Subaru’s sudden mood or behavior shifts. Perhaps he experienced so much that his morality or opinions changed. He can become a different person within just a moment. It would be natural for him but unnatural for us.”

“…But that doesn’t explain why he can’t tell us this himself. He can talk about Greed. He can talk about Sloth. What is causing him to not tell us?”

Beatrice paced for a while still thinking.

 

Until finally she stopped, “The third cost. Uncontrollable power, I suppose.”

Anastasia’s eyes widened, “Maybe he can’t control it. Maybe if he says certain things about it, it causes him to go back unintentionally, causing him to have to redo everything once again. Then what are the parameters? It feels so unreliable if he can’t control when to return. It’s as if it wasn’t intended to be like that in the first place.”

“…Maybe it wasn’t supposed to be like that, in fact.”

Anastasia looked at Beatrice, “What do you mean?”

“Think about it. Subaru’s Greed Authority switches wounds and allows Subaru to see people’s Ods. He can make contracts with people…but does that mean it was supposed to be used for combat? No. Subaru uses it because that’s all he has. And even then, the drawback comes from its own method of power. He has to injure himself to use it as a weapon. Most people can’t do that because they aren’t suicidal or can harm themselves that easily.”

Anastasia felt her body chill, her spine was shivering.

 

Something clicked again in her mind. And then unclicked.

 

No. People can’t come back from that. That would be insane.

 

This time, she didn’t know if she wanted to say it out loud.

She remembered how Subaru would act. How he was so nonchalant about near death experiences. How he was so quick to hurt himself. Stab his own body in order to switch injuries. Hell, when he got an arrow to the throat or an ice spell to the heart, that would be an instant kill for most. Yet Subaru was able to power through.

Is that because he has the willpower…or is it a side effect of something else?

 

He can time travel.

He’s used to getting hurt.

He suddenly comes back, in pain.

 

…Why would you need to be scared of death if you always came back before it happened?

 

Anastasia had a very plausible theory, “Perhaps. Subaru’s power wasn’t meant for direct time travel. If it’s like his other Authority…maybe his power was meant to protect him. Like a failsafe. Maybe. If he gets into a life-threatening situation, he goes back. Right before the end. It knows. Or if he is in a situation that could turn life-threatening, he turns back. Or if he says anything that could threaten his life, he turns back.”

Which meant…if he wanted to use it proactively.

If he wanted to use it for other people.

If he needed to save her life.

“Then Subaru would need to harm himself in order to go back in time…in fact.”

“…”

“…Anastasia- “

“No. Don’t try to sugarcoat this,” Anastasia’s hands were in her hair, gripping it tightly, “I don’t…I can’t. If what we’re saying is true…that means Subaru has been harming himself for everyone’s sakes. He’s been putting himself in danger, risking his life. Causing himself pain. Just to save me. To save others. To help his camp!”

Anastasia smashed the ground, viscerally angry, “Those absolute bastards! Did they not notice?! How could they not notice?! Was Subaru hiding it that well?! I doubt it considering he was an absolute wreck when I found him. And how he said no one notices him as much as I do! I can’t, no. I’m going to kill those bastards. I swear to Od- “

“Ana-”

The merchant suddenly stood up, tears streaming down, rage exhuming out of her, “I’m not going to calm down! Do you know what this means?! He’s been putting himself at risk this entire time! What if his power failed? What if something went wrong? What if it was too late?! Hell, getting hurt is the main thing! He stabs himself. Hurts himself. Knows the limits. That’s inhuman?! The only type of person who could do that is someone who does it nearly everyday! Do you know how messed up that is?! I-”

“It was my fault then, I suppose!”

Anastasia paused looking over at the little spirit, who was crying and prostrating on the ground, sobbing immensely, “W-wait Betty- “

“I-if you are correct, Betty was right next to Subaru the whole time…and she couldn’t do anything to help him. M-maybe Betty didn’t even notice. Maybe Betty chose not to notice. Either way, it seems Betty has failed Subaru even before Priestella, I suppose.”

“Betty that’s not-“

“It is! It is, it is, it is!” The child was rubbing her head into the floor,  “Betty was supposed to be Subaru’s contracted spirit. His confidant. His most trusted person…and Betty failed. B-betty saw Subaru’s pain and most likely never helped him deal with it. Betty was selfish. Betty took advantage of Subaru. Betty never treated Subaru well for all he did for Betty. Subaru saved Betty from that fire…and Betty never paid him back. Only became one of his burdens, I suppose.”

“…”

“…Please kill Betty. So, Betty can no longer be a problem-”

“Shut up.”

“A-ana-“

“Shut up!” Anastasia was crying, looking down at Beatrice, “If you want to act like that, then I should die too.”

“But you helped Subaru!”

“And I was probably a burden for him too! Did you see how he acts nowadays?! He’s almost completely different. What did he see back during our first date? How much time did he go through? How many times did he hurt himself to help me? Have you seen what he’s been telling Halibel?!”

Beatrice looked at her confused, “I-what?”

She grit her teeth, “Subaru’s been going behind my back, telling Halibel all sorts of stuff. Apparently, the Fujogeki company has been in league with the Witch Cult this entire time. They’ve been strong arming the Miko temples and holding their family hostage. Subaru told him to gather a team and wipe them out, that’s why he’s been gone all this week. I only know because I woke up in the middle night to one of their discussions and forced Halibel to explain to me in the morning. Do you know what else I found out? Subaru has intimate knowledge of Witch Cult strongholds in Gusteko. All over Gusteko.”

As Anastasia said those last words, Beatrice connected the dots, “…How many times-“

“Too many. We’re so far from Gusteko. Weeks away. And it would take months to scour it. Given that he couldn’t go back before Priestella, it most likely has a limited time span. Maybe a day or two or three. How much did he experiment? Did he torture the cultists for my sake? Who did he kill? I wonder, if I showed Subaru someone getting brutally killed, will he even flinch? I-what-I…”

Her hands were shaking.

She looked down at them and glared.

She nearly slammed them into her face, her body shuddering, crying and groaning as her body felt like it was about to break down. Her brain was working in overdrive. Understanding dawning on so many levels. She wanted to stop. But she can’t. It all made too much sense. She wanted to tear out her hair, scream, anything.

 

How long? Maybe he took advantage of Tia and used her wind magic. That could get him there in a week or less. But based on how my Od was described, it was on the verge of collapse. Would I have lasted that long? No. Maybe a few days. A week and a half tops. Did he leave me then? Go alone. No I would have noticed, especially if he took Tia. Does that mean I let him leave…Does…that mean. No. NONONO. I let him leave! I let him go. Or maybe. Or maybe. I-I-I-I…I went with him. I wouldn’t have let him go alone. I know that for sure. So I went with him. But we couldn’t have gotten across the border easily. Not without hurting the guards, or maybe even killing them. Was I that desperate to live? NO…I…could have. I was desperate. Subaru wanted to help. I got greedy. We both went to Gusteko. We went there. Most likely countless times, given how extensive his knowledge was. But what could be in Gusteko? What could…Archbishop. We gambled on an Archbishop. And if Subaru got it…and an authority that could help my Od…I could have been saved. Meaning…meaning. I knew Subaru would do anything to help me.

Meaning. I took advantage of his love for me. I let him help me…I made him do this.

I must have. I made him… break. I broke him. He’s…did he give up the others, not because he loved me more…but because I made him obsess over me.

Because he needed to save me. I must have guilted him. I must have told him to save me. To help me. To do anything.

I let him do this. To himself. I must have. I would have noticed.

 

And I did nothing.

 

I…I…

 

“Remember child, the greatest asset, is anyone who truly loves you…because they’ll give you everything they own. All of themselves. And leave nothing. How droll, a slave, without a collar. Isn’t that right?”

 

…

 

Seconds passed as neither girl was willing to say anything, only shaking and silence.

 

 

 

Until finally,

 

“…FUCK!”

 

The sudden screamed startled Beatrice who was fixated on the young woman, swearing up a storm out of nowhere,

“Fuck, fuck, fuck, fuck, fuck!” She was hyperventilating, “If-if….shit…I…I’m going to…”

She was about to tear her hair apart, her hands ripping through her scalp, her mind firing rapidly without a break.

Gasping for breath, “He’s all I have…I can’t…and I did…I don’t…fuck. Please.”

Her heart was beating quickly. Her brain was malfunctioning. She was remembering. Her childhood. Her mistakes. Everything.

She needed to…she didn’t.

She needed.

Subaru.

Now. Subaru.

 

Please.

 

Anastasia slowly let her hair go, strands falling .

She blinked.

“…Betty.”

She couldn’t see Beatrice, but her tone was afraid, “…Are you okay, in fact?”

 

“…No. I’m not.”

 

She blinked again.

 

“…”

 

“I’m,” she swallowed, her throat felt like it was bleeding, “…I’m going to see Subaru.”

“Wait, Ana- “

 

“No. I’m going to see him. Now.”

 

Before she could say anything else, Anastasia channeled all the mana within her body to flow to her muscles.

 

And then she took off sprinting.

 

 

She didn’t look around.

Didn’t care to look behind.

 

 

 

Didn’t even stop.

 

 

Everything flashed around her.

 

 

 

 

Until.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

SLAM!

“Woah, what’s got you all…Ana-pop? What’s wrong?”

He was there.

Standing there.

Just like always.

Subaru.

Her Subaru…

 

Sharp eyes, black hair with some strands of white, bangs covering one eye, the rest slicked back into a ponytail.

Wearing a casual black kimono for home use.

Standing there as if nothing was wrong.

As if he didn’t experience so much without her ever knowing.

For her.

Subaru. The love of her life. One of the only people she truly cared for.

Who gave everything up for her.

Because she asked him to save her.

 

Ha. It’s so funny…I'm just like her. I'm just...just...

 

Anastasia finally decided what she was.

 

A disgusting freak.

 

Someone who would take advantage of someone down on their luck. Just because it would benefit her. Using love like a chain.

 

Just like the one who raised her…before Ricardo.

 

Revulsion echoed through her soul, seeping through every inch of her body. She was gasping for breath. Sweating out of her mind, her muscles roaring from the pure adrenaline and mana pushed into them.

She wanted to tell him…she didn’t know what to tell him.

She wanted to say something. Anything.

Whatever it took to get all of this disgusting feeling out of her body.

 

But she couldn’t, she didn't know how.

 

But her body knew, and it complied.

 

And so, Anastasia vomited onto the floor.

 

And everything went black.

Notes:

EN1: If you're wondering why the taboo isn't murdering Anastasia, try to guess. There's a reason.

Chapter 25: Chapter 25: Purgatorio I

Summary:

Look into the abyss...

Notes:

Sorry for the lack of chapters last week. Been dealing with real life stuff. Realized something.

I don't want to ever stop writing. So. I'm going to lay the foundations, so that I can do this full time. No matter the cost.

Wish me luck.

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Darkness.

All darkness.

All she could see was darkness.

A thin veil that cascaded through her mind.

She had no body, no soul, no mouth. Yet she could feel, touch, taste, and smell the abyss around her.

It was suffocating. Yet liberating.

As if she was surrounded by abject nothingness while also being unbound by the earthly desires of reality.

A paradox within this isolated squall of darkness.

Shadows ebbed and flowed periodically with dashes of light. As if the stars were streaking through her soul, rivers of starlight, and torrents of darkness raining down on her every second.

 

It was beautiful.

“…ve…”

There.

She moved her head slightly.

“u…o…u”

There it was again.

Like a low rumbling. Faint, and ever present. But only reaching clarity within her soul every once in a while. It was odd.

It was…new.

This whole place…new.

It felt wrong.

Yet right.

As if this world, this pocket universe, existed since eternity. But only came into her purview recently.

How strange.

It-

“o…I…”

There.

Again.

Why? Why does it keep coming in and out? Is it trying to drill into her skull? Invade this sanctuary of hers?

…She didn’t like it.

The pale star peered around with her formless eyes.

 

 

 

Nothing. There was nothing.

But she could hear it nearby. Far but near.

 

A presence.

 

It’s like…it was looking at her. But not. Eyes everywhere. Like she was out in the open.

 

But it didn’t care. Like she was an insignificant gnat in the grand scheme of reality.

 

She moved, or tried to move, her formless body. It was like swimming in honay. But she couldn’t move any further or move any-

“…you...”

The pale star flinched.

 

It was clearer. She heard a word this time. Why? What changed? Was it how she moved?

 

She tried to move her arms, they flowed all around her, scouring and trying to find the difference.

 

“lov..ou...”

There.

One more.

“I..lo..”

That.

 

Barely visible but it was there.

A thin strand of pure light.

Attached to her heart.

 

She could see it connect all the way to somewhere, someone far away.

 

…Someone?

Who? Wait, no. She. Who? Why did she think of someone?

 

She grabbed at the string. It felt…warm.

 

Familiar.

 

Close.

 

And yet so-

“I love you.”

 

The pale star startled, the voice it heard was almost right next to her ear.

What was that?

Who was that?

Was that the someone? The someone she thought of?

 

…No. No her gut says no. Her instincts scream no. Whoever that voice was, it wasn’t him.

Him?

 

It was a him!

Him.

Yes. Him.

She looked towards the light again.

 

Him. It helped her remember him. For whatever reason, it connected her to him.

 

She didn’t hesitate. She grasped the light with both hands once again and felt the warmth brush through her soul.

 

It was…like heaven.

Pure. Blissful. Loving.

 

“I love you.”

 

…But that voice. It unnerved her. Overwhelmed her. Made her want to vomit. Made her non-existent heart squeeze. It was unnatural.

“I love you.”

The pale star shuddered. It felt disgust on an incredible level.

She wanted to stop. Stop hearing it.

 

But she can’t. She was getting closer. Getting closer to the one she loved.

 

Yes. Yes! She loved him! He made her feel warm. Made her feel whole. More than whole.

“I love you.”

Despite the sheer apprehension she felt, the pale star pushed forth, still clinging to the strand of starlight that shined brightly.

 

Brighter than before. It was bigger. No longer a thin strand but more like a thread.

“I love you.”

The voice was getting louder.

Echoing throughout her whole body.

She hated it.

Hated every second of it.

It felt like it was invading every particle of her formless body. Infecting it.

She felt an intense loathing.

“I love you.”

Stop. Stop it. She rejects these words.

She only has one lover. One person she loves. And that is Subaru.

 

Subaru?

 

Visions of a boy. Of a man. A man with dark hair, sharp kind eyes, and a loving smile dripped into her mind.

 

Subaru!

“…!”

She tried to scream.

Yell out into the void.

But nothing came out.

She had no mouth.

No semblance nor way of transcribing her thoughts into words.

 

“I love you.”

Shut up. Shut up! Rancid.

She needed to think. Where was she? What was this? Why does she not remember much?

 

…Where is Subaru?

She needed him. She wanted him. Wherever he was, his spot was by her side.

 

She wasn’t going to lose him. Not like everyone else. Not like her name.

 

So, where? Where?! WHERE-

“…p..se…”

Her form whipped towards the origin of that voice.

It wasn’t disgusting.

It was heavenly.

Where?

 

There.

Right there.

 

Where the string led to, into the abyss.

The string had become a rope. Tethering her to wherever her beloved was. And will be.

 

She clung to it. Like it was her last lifeline.

“…!”

She tried to scream once more.

But no sound came out.

Frustrated.

She swam towards the voice, the entropy around her felt like water, grabbing and pulling at the rope each second.

It was solid. Like a lifeline that could never fade.

“I love you.”

“sa…m…”

The voice.

It sounded so desperate.

As if it was on the edge of this abyss.

Clinging onto sanity barely.

 

The pale star got furious, swimming faster and faster. Tugging the rope with all her might, the starlight line shimmering brighter the more distance she carried.

“I love you.” “…please…”

She didn’t care anymore.

The other voice was screaming in her ears at this point.

She was not stopping.

She had no mouth.

No.

That doesn’t matter.

She’ll make one.

If one doesn’t exist, then she must build it herself.

Pushing all her will, all her thoughts, the pale star brushed the tides of shadows to her skull, molding and sculpting lungs, vocal chords, and a tongue.

The star was just a fragmented corpse, floating darkness in the shape of respiratory organs.

 

But that’s all she needed.

Just enough,

“Su..uu…” her voice was fragmented, etched into the dark without a care, a torrent of scrawls and intonation without form.

“I love you.”

Rage billowed, she pressed forward, pushing her body forward, solidifying the organs that became more and more alive, more bright.

“Su…baru…Sub….aru!”

Almost.

Almost!

“help…m…”

She will!

She’s coming.

She won’t stop.

 

She’ll never stop.

 

“Su…baru…Subaru! SUBARU!”

“I love you.”

Not you! Never. Get away.

The voice pounded in her lungs, threatening to pop them.

As if her very presence, her very existence, was an affront to that disgusting voice’s intentions.

That only made the pale star even more furious.

Spite filled her breath, and it billowed through her words, she fought through the imaginary pain and entropy,

“Subaru! Where are you?!”

The disgusting pest could go to hell, for all she cared.

It will not get in her way.

“Please…help…”

There!

His voice.

She remembers him.

How they first met.

How they held each other close.

How they fell in love.

How they kissed and made love.

How they promised to share all, burdens and all.

Everything.

 

She moved faster and faster, a tidal wave approaching wherever her lover may lay.

“I love you.”

 

That voice. It was as loud as Subaru’s. Both drilling into her brain, one carving into her neurons while the other lit them ablaze.

 

It was a threat.

Those words weren’t for her, were they?

They were for…they were for…

 

Him.

 

There.

 

There he was.

Floating.

A mass of nothing.

Nothing except the rope that bound her heart to his. His beating center, the pulsating star within the galaxy of his body.

 

He had no face, no limbs, nothing.

 

But that was him, she knew it was him.

 

“I love you.”

 

…And that voice, that other voice.

 

What the hell is that?

 

A form. It looked…familiar. But not. Like a caricature of a person. It made her stomach scream, as if whatever she was looking at should not exist. It had no eyes, no mouth, no features. Yet, the pale star could see that whatever that thing was, it could see, hear, and breathe. And it was using all those biological paradoxes, those scars on reality, to grip the soul of her lover with shadows of pure ecstasy.

 

The hands, these ebony limbs, caressed his very existence each second.

All originating from a vacuum of sheer malice, at the center, a semblance of creation, a mockery of reality. A mirror…that reflected innocence. A silver scar amongst the sea of darkness.

 

The pale star hated it.

Loathed it.

Disgusting.

Hands off.

But as the pale star tried to swim closer.

 

The silver scar blinked.

 

“…Leave.”

 

Lungs. Chords. Tissue. In the blink of an eye, all gone.

 

The pale star felt her existence start to collapse, the echoes of entropy dissolving her very soul. She was being dragged back to the origin.

 

Away from the silver scar. Away from her star.

 

Away from Subaru.

No.

It won’t. She won’t let it.

 

Her mental mindscape was burning, the organs she made were being plucked, and devoured by the abyss.

She didn’t care.

This…thing!

Could do whatever it wanted to her.

But the mere fact it was touching her star.

Coveting him.

Imprisoning him.

 

It was the most vile act committed against her very existence.

 

She didn’t hesitate. She gathered her fragmented consciousness one last time, constantly reforming, ignoring the pain,  pushing the boundaries of her momentary invasion, she clung to the edge with incredible rage.

 

It gave her only one moment, one last hurrah.

 

With one last breath, she screamed into the endless purgatory, “SUBARU!”

 

Her gambit worked. Suddenly, the area surrounding her shook, tremors cascaded around her.

 

The black star woke up.

 

She could see him. Formless, but identifiable.

 

And he was looking right at her.

 

His soul lost, tormented, tired.

 

As if he was-

The silver scar stared into her soul.

 

The pale star blinked.

 

“…!”

Her lungs were gone.

Her body was gone.

Everything was finally gone, torn asunder.

Her mind shredded, her very essence fragmented into nanoparticles of pure nothing.

 

She couldn’t think. Couldn’t talk.

 

But she could hear.

 

Hear one last plea.

 

From the center of this accursed galaxy.

 

“Please. Help me.”

 

…No…matter…the cost…

Wait for me.

I will save you…

 

 

 

Anastasia woke up, her heart racing, her body shivering. She was in her white nightwear kimono, drenched in sweat.

She looked around, scared.

 

What was that?!

Her brain tried to process the nightmare she saw.

Of Subaru crying as Anastasia died in her arms, before his ribcage ripped open, placing his heart within her dead corpse.

 

She then disappeared into darkness, feeling ever present eyes watching her from nowhere. And always having the intense feeling that her lover was just around the corner, out of reach.

The first part was new. The second part was a recurrence, a plague on her soul.

She wiped her brow and sat up.

 

She was in bed, in her and Subaru’s room.

No one was around.

Where was-

Creeaaaak!

Her head whipped to the side. Subaru slowly walked in with a tray, a bowl of what looked to be soup along with a sandwich and two glasses of orage juice.

Subaru didn’t look surprised seeing her up, his eyes were filled with concern, “You’re finally awake…how do you feel?”

He placed the tray near the bed before sitting down next to the girl, using his hand to brush the merchant’s messy bed hair back.

 

Anastasia, to be frank, felt like shit.

Her body had chills, her head was on fire, and she was 80% sure that, even though she felt nothing in her gut, she wanted to vomit.

“…I’m okay.”

“No. No you’re not,” Subaru shook his head while rubbing circles on Anastasia’s back.

For some reason, it made her feel better.

“…”

“…Beako came back soon after you did. She looked awful too. I asked her what was wrong…but all she said was that you overworked yourself, and that you ran back here trying to use the flow method. As a challenge or something.”

“…”

“…While I’m honestly happy that you and Beako are getting along well enough to keep secrets from me, that doesn’t mean I’m not going to be worried nor am I not going to be a little intrusive when my future wife got knocked unconscious in front of me. After spilling her lunch.”

“…”

He kept rubbing her back, Anastasia not saying anything, just…blinking.

“…I won’t push you to tell me though, either way. Much as I want to, I trust that you will come talk to me about it when you’re ready, whatever it may be.”

“…”

“…” Subaru sighed before he smiled and wrapped an arm around her shoulder, pushing her head onto the crook of his neck, sitting side by side while he caressed her arm.

“…”

“…Are you feeling hot? Is this uncomfortable for you?”

“…” She didn’t say anything, simply shaking her head slowly.

“That’s good. Just let me know, and I’ll stop.”

“…”

“…I’m guessing you’re wondering how I knew you woke up. Because it would be weird how I knew to bring you some food right this moment, right? Well… I don’t know actually. I just had a weird feeling that you’d be awake. And that you would probably be hungry. So, I went to go grab something, a little for me and you. And when I got back, I was right. It’s weird, I think my Authority bonded us more than I thought.”

“…”

“I haven’t really made any headway on it by the way; I’m still confused on how it exactly works. Tried it with everyone. Tried fake proposing, tried telling Halibel I was madly in love with him, tried doing the same stuff I did for you. Didn’t work, unfortunately. I think it requires something more. Something that ties me to them or something. Something unique that I can’t have with anyone else.”

“…”

“…Anyways, in other news, I’ve been experimenting with those new sauces. I know you really didn’t like the hot ones but I think you’ll like this one. It has a bit of tang and sweetness and honestly-“

“Subaru.”

The black star gripped her tighter, “Yeah, Ana-pop?”

“I…”

What was she supposed to say? Tell him all she knew? That he could turn back time? Whenever he's near death? Or...

Is it:

Hey Subaru, I’ve been currently trying my best not to think about the fact that I may have screwed you over by falling in love with you. As a result, I haven’t heard a single thing you said in the last few minutes. You know what’s messed up? If it wasn’t for me, you’d probably be living a normal and good life, away from people. Because you probably would be living in a nice place out in the countryside with someone who didn’t have a terminal illness. Probably the only thing you would have to worry about is farming and paying taxes.

Or how about:

The more I think about it, the more I realize how much I’ve taken advantage of you. I literally dragged you to Kararagi in order to start a business. And as a result: you were attacked by some rabid animal, had to deal with a Witch Cultist scheme, and also watched someone you loved die in front of you. And I’m guessing it happened several times! I really don’t want to think about how you went back in time, if my theory is correct, because that would mean you threw yourself into danger every time I died. Or worse. You did it yourself. And I try really hard not to think about that possibility. But I can’t help it, honestly. My brain makes the logical connection and all I want to do is bash my skull open. Or just make myself forget. Forget the fact that you sacrificed however much time and pain for me. And the fact that I even thought about desiring that, makes me want to vomit immediately.

 

But this one, this one is her favorite:

You know what’s absolutely awful? I don’t regret a single thing. I saw you and I thought, ‘this was all worth it.’ And you know what’s the worst part? I truly believe it. I hate that. I hate that part of me so much. I hate that at the end of the day, I don’t regret meeting you. And it makes me a vile piece of shit. Because it reminds me so much of her.

…When she died, I promised I would never be like her. I promised I would be better. That I wouldn’t take a blind eye to inhumane cruelty. But guess what? I did the same to you! I did it to you. I took in someone who I was fond of for ulterior motives. Ended up getting attached. And used you to improve my own life at the cost of yourself. How! Super! Ironic! Wow. I just. Wow. It totally doesn’t make me want to slit my throat and die. Or choke myself to death. Out of sheer disgust. God I’m disgusting. A disgusting pile of waste who made you suffer for my sake, and who doesn’t even regret it.

 

Not even in the slightest!

 

However, she instead chose:

“…I think you should lay off the hot sauce or I won’t be able to kiss you anymore.”

Because, how could she say any of that?

“…Ha, I guess you would hate that.”

“Right? Remember when you gave me some earlier, I felt like I was dying.”

If she explained all her worries, every theory that was rolling around in her brain, every single thing plaguing her mind, would he go back? Would that be enough to trigger his ability? 

“You really did… you really did.”

“Yeah. We should start thinking about our next moves. Now that our company is finally making it big in Banan we can think about expanding. I’ll set up some meetings, see if we can send samples and create exhibitions in the neighboring cities.”

How far would it send him back? What if it sent him back to before he made the contract with her? She couldn’t do that to him. She can’t ever do that to him. She could wait, but what would that do? Subaru would most likely figure out a way to avoid speaking to her about it after resetting. Or maybe try to deflect her reasoning, slowly push this away as a paranoid fantasy…maybe that’s what she should do.

“I can…set up some if you want. Make a batch of new products to… entice… people…”

“Oh, don’t worry. I think we should be fine. I have full confidence in our current lineup. Maybe we’ll add some of those hot sauces you keep testing, it would be a waste not to.”

Just…let it all go. It’s not her problem. It’s Subaru’s. He dealt with it for so long, why try to intervene.

“Ana…”

“Though maybe you should add some variety. See if you can have a hot sauce and a semi-hot sauce. That way some people can enjoy it with others, could make a killing by selling them as a pair.”

Especially since…since she can’t do anything about it.

Yeah. Nothing. What could she do? Tell him to not use it to save people? It’s his choice. His right.

She had no business here. She had her strengths, he had his. He can deal with it on his own. And she’ll make sure to pick up the pieces of his fractured sanity.

Just wear her mask again. Keep up the façade. They were having fun, right? She was happy. She wanted to keep being happy. She wanted him to be happy. This was all just some paranoid fantasy. Subaru can deal with it. He always dealt with it.

 

All alone.

He was used to it. Bearing it all. Everyone not caring. Or maybe, trusting him to deal with everything. Trusting that he would call them if he needs them. He’s strong. He can do it.

 

He’s Subaru.

 

“…”

She ignored the pain in her heart, “Yeah. I think that will work. I can…I can work with that. T-that. Won’t. Be too…hard.”

She ignored how her guts were writhing with rage.

She felt his other arm wrap around her, “…”

“N-not hard.”

She’ll ignore everything. Just like how everyone else did. Because they trusted him. She trusts him.

“A-at,” she swallowed but her throat was dry, she could taste salt in her mouth, “a-all.”

 

She forced the words out, “I-“ it hurt.

“I…” everything hurt.

“I!” And what hurt especially was her heart.

 

Her heart was breaking. How to help him. How to save him. How to be someone that was worth all of this pain.

 

“…I can’t,” she started to sob, her body shaking, her blood ran cold, “I CAN’T!”

 

It was impossible.

 

But what can she do? She can’t think of a solution. No matter how much she thought. There was nothing. She can’t help him. He can’t talk to her. She can’t tell him to never use it again. He would just hide it from her as best as he could. He can’t share this with her. This was his burden to bear…forever.

“…”

After all this time, she can’t hold up her end of the deal. She can’t share his burdens. He was alone.

“…I…I…” the words could barely come out, her heart beat like a drum, tears have been streaming out of her eyes for however long, “I…I’m sorry. I’m sorry!”

All alone.

Subaru held her close as she continued to hysterically apologize, her tears endless, clutching his chest, sobbing.

“I’m sorry, I’m sorry! I’M SORRY!”

I’m worthless. I can’t help the one I love. I can’t help myself. I can’t help anyone!

Subaru kept hugging her, she could feel his heart beat, a slow drum.

And all she could do, was continue to cry, because that’s all she was good for.

 

Useless. Until the end.

 

 

Elsewhere.

 

Hundreds of miles away from our two stars.

 

[Reinhard van Astrea has died.]

 

[Reinhard van Astrea has died.]

 

[Reinhard van Astrea has died.]

 

A war waged between two beings.

Chapter 26: Chapter 26: Purgatorio II

Summary:

Subaru checks-in on everyone...

Notes:

Enjoy!

Chapter Text

“How’s Ana-bo doin’?”

“…Not great.”

It has been two days since Anastasia had become bedridden. Subaru was currently wracked with worry, wondering if this was a side effect of his Authority or something more sinister. Despite numerous attempts to pry, and multiple checks with Ops Basiliskos showing no changes to her Od, he had no idea what was afflicting her.

“Seems she caught the same thin’ as ol Beako. Given how both of them look like they are bout to pass out any second.”

Subaru brushed his hair back as he chewed on a piece of toast, “Has she said anything to you? Either of them?”

Halibel shook his head, sighing to himself, “Nope. Tia got nothin’ either and Eridna’s got tight lips. Ya can try, but she told me herself, ‘Sister needs someone to confide in right now, I won’t betray that trust.’”

Subaru felt his insides wrench.

So does Ana. But she won’t confide in me at all!

…Is it because of me?

But what would…no. That…no. That’d be impossible.

Before the thought could even occur, he threw it away. Because if it did happen, he would know.

He touched his heart, where the black dragon’s blood now festered.

He would definitely know.

Subaru sighed, picking up his plates and walking them to the sink, “Well, let me know if anything changes. How goes the chore I gave you?”

Halibel chuckled as he smoked, leaning onto the wall next to Subaru, as the black star washed the dishes, “Fine. A bit of Green-Sun cleanin’ was due in Banan anyway, so I appreciated the motivation. The bugs have been neutralized and I sent some exterminators after the sources. Might not be able to get all those nests ya told me bout, but most of them will perish.”

Subaru hummed happily, “And what about some of the victims’ families? No bugs in their beds?”

The wolfman blew out a puff, “Took a bit of time. I sent Tia after them.”

Subaru glanced at Halibel, “Hal.”

He waved his hand in the air, “I know what you’re goin’ to say. But trust me. Tia’s more precise than ya think. She got back a few days ago and was able to save a good bunch. Unfortunately, not all of them made it. Those sick bastards mutilated them beyond measure.”

Subaru hummed boredly, “At least there was some to be saved. And that wasn’t what I was going to say,” Subaru started to wash some other dirty plates as Halibel stopped smoking, eyeing him from the side, “I was more concerned about Tia getting overworked. I already asked her to check the border of Vollachia for me.”

Halibel stared for a second before taking a big puff, “…That makes sense. Ya know, Su-san.”

Subaru stopped washing, Halibel’s tone getting his attention, not sharp, but a little on edge, “Yeah?”

“I’m not questionin’ this whole situation. Honest. I already grilled ya back when ya first told me all this shit was goin’ down in my city. But a part of me is still curious…how exactly did ya find this all out so well?”

“…”

“I know ya told me it’s classified. That ya got sources. Ya have this odd instinct. Danger sense. Whatever. That ya did things like this back in Lugunica, and that’s how ya were able to get so much done. But ya gotta understand, Su-san, I’ve been guardin’ ya all this time. And it just feels odd. Now, I ain’t goin’ to pry any more. I trust ya. But just want to let ya know that there are people out there who, when push comes to shove, might have smarter ways of figurin’ out how ya do all this. At least better than me.”

Subaru connected the dots, “…Ya don’t say?”

It seems Halibel got more information out of Eridna than he’s letting on. Ever since Subaru asked for Halibel’s help in eliminating the whole Witch Cult from Kararagi, they’ve gotten used to this new dynamic. Hidden messaging. This would be a lot more difficult if he hadn’t gotten used to it in that hell loop.

Subaru started washing again, “I’ll keep that in mind, thanks for the advice, Hal.”

“Of course. Oh! And just before I forget,” he brought out two containers, one filled with brightly colored rocks while the other was filled with wrinkled purple fruits, and placed them on the counter, “Yer shipments of lagamite and bokko fruits came this mornin’. I’ll store them in a warehouse nearby.”

Those should help if another emergency comes up. And if Beatrice was able to finish the task Subaru gave her earlier this week, then they should have all their bases covered. No more situations like last week.

Ever. Again.

Subaru turned off the water and wiped his hands dry, “Thanks again Hal. Truly. I really appreciate all the help.”

The wolfman just smiled and extinguished his pipe, waving his hand in the air as he opened the window and prepared to jump out, “Thank me by inventin’ some new sauces.”

He then stopped just as he put a foot out the window, looking back, “But no more of those tabasco whatsits. That stuff was terrible, had the worst shits a man could ever dream of.”


Subaru chuckled, waving him away, “Y’all just have bad taste. But I get it. No more hot sauces. I’ll prepare something nice for you. Back home we call it Tonkatsu sauce. Trust me, you’ll love it.”

Halibel gave a thumbs up before jumping out, towards the roof of a neighboring house.

The black star sighed as he walked over and closed the window, muttering, “We have a door for a reason. He could at least close the window on his way out.”

After checking that there was no lit fires and double checking window locks, he then went through his mental checklist before going back to his room. On the way out of the kitchen, he grabbed some appas, a plate, and a knife. He went down the hall and arrived at his door.

Knock Knock!

…Hearing no voices, he opened the door slowly and walked in, the room was dark except a dim lagamite lamp in the corner. The room was a bit of a mess, some clothes strewn about, with a large lump in the middle of their bed, hidden under tons of blankets.

He walked over and gently placed the plate on the table.

He bent down and placed his head near the lump, whispering, “Ana…Ana? Are you awake?”

He waited a few moments, expecting a shudder or some sort of response. Only to hear a soft, barely audible snoring.

He sighed in relief.

At least she finally fell asleep.

She barely slept the last two days. Spending the first day constantly crying and clinging onto Subaru for dear life. She wouldn’t even eat until Subaru begged her to.

He slowly took the covers off, peeling them one by one, until getting to the core.

His lovely Anastasia.

Who was curled up like an armadillo.

He then grabbed her body and placed her in a more comfortable position.

The second day wasn’t that much better. When she would sleep, Anastasia would be in a deep trance, barely affected by anyone touching or moving her. Only waking up if you shook her or slapped her. When she was awake, she would be in a haze, speaking minimally and mostly with Subaru.

It made him feel sick. But he needed to be patient. From how the doctor described her, she was actually in peak physical condition. Her problems seemed to be mostly mental and emotional. It felt like the complete opposite of how she usually was.

Subaru brushed her hair with his hand, her hair was all over the place, frazzled and barely straight. Her face was a mix of eyebags and tear marks.

She was the most beautiful person in the world right now, just as always.

After running his fingers through her hair for a few seconds, he sighed before grabbing an appa and beginning to peel and cut as he sat right next to her.

What could be causing her so much distress?

He narrowed it down to two possibilities: His Authority and him.
Those were the only conclusions that made sense. The bond between them must have transferred more than just physical attributes. Mental and emotional scars must have also been shared.

…Which made him feel absolutely ill to think about.

Did she get any of his memories?

No. Otherwise, he would know more about Anastasia’s past. But he didn’t.

But what about his traumas? The pain he felt from all those loops a year ago. Even if she doesn’t have the memories, did the mental wounds take hold in her too? Does she feel the intense phantom pains he always does? How much? What kind?

He eyed her arms, covered in her kimono.

A part of him wanted to check.

To see if she scratched herself like he did.

But he shouldn’t.

Not yet. Not when she’s asleep.

He’ll ask her when she is awake again. Or when she’s calmed down a bit.

If the Authority is causing her distress…that means it’s my fault.

On the one hand, she’s alive because of it. On the other hand, she’s basically experiencing a cascade of all of Subaru’s terrible experiences in one sitting. Possibly.

He really didn’t understand how this power worked.

Subaru concentrated and saw her Od again. It was still bright and shining, iridescent and strong. He could now see a thin thread of light connecting from her Od to what was most likely his, barely visible.

He turned off his power and continued cutting the second appa.

I’ll have to think of how to get her to cope with the stress. But how? I could barely keep up with it besides pushing them all deep down. Which, wasn’t a smart idea, to be honest. But I’m not exactly the healthiest person, mentally.

Subaru suddenly frowned and rubbed his temples.

“…I guess I didn’t come out of this unscathed either,” he muttered as he went back to peeling.

He wasn’t an idiot. This whole situation. How he dealt with it. How he’s dealing with everything nowadays. He had changed.

He was still him. But not him. Like a weird new version of himself that felt oddly foreign.

He just didn’t know how much.

And whether it was because of the time he spent trying to save her. Or if it was some byproduct of the bond. If the bond had shared some personality traits. Which Subaru didn’t mind personally, he would love to be more like Anastasia.

Unfortunately, he felt the opposite about her being more like him.

Subaru shook his head vigorously.

Self-love Natsuki. Self-love. You promised yourself and her that you would be better.

He started to slice the appa into little animals, he was halfway into making a bunny, thought about it for a moment, and then decided to make it into a hedgehog.

And then there’s what Hal said…

“That there are people out there who, when push comes to shove, might have smarter ways of figurin’ out how ya do all this.”

…It couldn’t be.

Otherwise.

Otherwise…he would be dead. Or she would be dead. Or his heart would feel like it would be getting crushed into a million pieces by some psychotic personality of an otherwise, charming girl.

Though he still has so many questions about why she looks like Emilia. He should really get on that some day. Why is it that they look so similar? Are silver-haired half elves all like that? Why does she love him? He never met her in his entire life. It feels odd that she’s so fixated on him. Maybe she’s a version of Emilia that time traveled from some weird timeline where they were in love.

Nah. That sounds dumb.

Sniff.

Subaru’s eyes looked over to his lover, her eyes were starting to glisten again.

…Surprised where all this water comes from. I should remind you to drink some more when you wake up.

She muttered in her sleep, he could see her breathing quicken, “Su…baru…where…are…you…?”

He smiled softly as he grabbed her hand, whispering, “I’m here, I’m here. I won’t ever leave your side. Never again.”

He won’t be leaving her side for a while. The last time she woke up and he was gone, it was not pretty. He came home to Anastasia breaking down on the floor, screaming about where he was, with Halibel not knowing what to do.

It’s something else. It must be. Maybe she’s seeing my weird behavior and is thinking this is all some sort of weird influence from my Authority. I should try talking to her about it. See if that soothes her worries.

Or maybe it was from worrying about him telling Halibel to completely dismantle whole companies overnight. The wolfman told Subaru that Anastasia confronted him once, about it. He didn’t blame the poor guy for caving in. Anastasia was terrifying when she was angry.

It’s why he was expecting her to confront him about Subaru’s recent actions any day now.

She’s usually the inquisitive sort. Probing him for info at all times. He loved that about her.

But she didn’t. Not recently at least. For some reason, things were going well up until she had that major freakout.

Subaru noticed her breathing slow down, going back into some kind of deep sleep. He lifted his hand from hers, already missing it. He bent down and gave her a little kiss on the forehead before putting some of the blankets back on, just a few so she didn’t overheat.

He placed the plate of sliced appa hedgehogs on to the table. Hopefully, when she woke up, she’ll be happy to see them.

He tiptoed his way out of the room and went towards his next objective.

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Knock! Knock!

…

Nothing. It seems Beatrice was either out cold or out with her sister.

The little spirit was doing better than Anastasia. But her reactions to him were the near opposite of Ana’s, she would end up crying whenever she saw him, avoiding him like the plague. It made his heart hurt as he couldn’t really fathom what was causing her distress.

Was it his weird behavior? Was it how he hasn’t discussed having a contract with her yet? Was it because…did she remember him?

The thought came back. It was one of his first thoughts when he saw how Anastasia reacted. He thought there might have been some sort of reversal of Gluttony. The sudden onset of old memories clashing with the new, leading to some kind of odd dissonance. That was his theory. That Beatrice and Anastasia experienced Gluttony backlash.

It got soundly debunked when he talked to Eridna, who couldn’t remember him or Anastasia at all still. Meaning this was entirely separate from some outside source. He was the cause. He just didn’t know why, and no one was willing to give him a straight answer.

“Sister has gone on a walk with Tia. While my sister has her reservations, I think a chat with the wind spirit would work wonders on her health, currently.”

The black star was startled as he heard a voice from his side, the white fox smiling mischievously at Subaru’s reaction, “Gah! You really gotta stop doing that hiding and appearing stuff. You’re going to give me a heart attack one of these days.”

The fox’s smile just got bigger, “I will. Once your reactions become less entertaining.”

He frowned as she walked over to his legs, pawing them lightly. He rolled his eyes and picked her up, holding her close, “You’re too spoiled. I should drop you on the floor.”

Eridna nuzzled his neck, tickling him, “For shame. You wouldn’t hurt your mother-in-law, would you?”

“I would if she was being incredibly annoying.”

“Touche.”

He walked over to the kitchen again and placed her on the counter. Subaru reached up and unlocked one of the cupboards, grabbing a small vase and taking out two cookies, giving one to the fox.

“How’s Beako?” He munched as Eridna ate hers in one motion.

After swallowing, “She is doing better. Her emotional state is much better. I believe she will be able to talk to you without having a nervous breakdown soon.”

Subaru grimaced and sighed, “Well…that’s good.”

“You aren’t going to ask me about why she is going through such an experience?”

Subaru shrugged his shoulders, “I want to. I really do. But I’m not going to intrude when I know it won’t make a difference. Tell Beako that I’ll wait until she’s ready but that I am worried about her.”

The fox cocked her head at him, “That is surprisingly mature of you.”

Subaru glared, “When have I not been mature?”

“From how you tell your stories, it always feels like you have a childish side to you. Which isn’t bad per se, however, I’ve been seeing this other side more frequently recently.”

Subaru swallowed, “Yeah. I guess that makes sense.”

“Hmm,” she brought a paw to her chin, trying to act cute, “Perhaps that saying is correct. ‘A man who becomes married grows older by 20 years.’”

Subaru nearly choked, “There is no way that is a saying. And if it is, it’s probably told by bitter husbands about how their wives annoy them all the time. And that marriage is a sham and you should never do it.”

“You aren’t annoyed by Ana?”

“No, I am. She’s probably the most annoying person I’ve ever met,” he waved his hand in the air, his warm smile exposing his true feelings, “But I’d rather die than say that I’d never marry her. Even if the world ends or someone holds a knife to my neck, I am marrying her and living a long happy life with her. No matter what.”

Eridna, somehow, began to clap slowly with her paws, “How wholesome.”

Subaru then pointed at her, “By the way, that saying doesn’t even work for us. We’re betrothed. Not married yet.”

The fox shrugged and lied down on the counter, “If you ask anyone who witnessed the entire development of your relationship, they would all say, ‘I assumed you both were married the entire time.’”

“No, they wouldn’t. We literally met under knifepoint.”

“All great romances begin with danger.”

“I don’t think one of the romantic leads should be causing the danger.”

“Read some more romance novels. You would be surprised.”

Subaru shuddered, “Why the hell would anyone like someone who hurt them or was about to kill them?”

His brain then paused.

Okay, I might be a hypocrite for that one. I’m just going to shut up now.

Before the fox could retort,

Knock Knock!

They both looked towards the source of the disturbance, at the front door. Eridna turned her head back towards Subaru.

She raised an eyebrow, “Are you expecting someone today?”

Subaru eyed the clock on the wall, “In an hour. Crap. I should have expected he would be like his brother.”

Subaru shook his head as he walked over to the door, Eridna disappearing from his purview.

He grabbed the doorknob to the front entrance, and was greeted by a familiar face, a soft nervous smile paired with a monocle covering one of a pair of golden eyes, and violet hair, “Greetings. I presume you are Atlas of Atlas & Pleione Trading Company?”

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

“Tea work for you?”

“Yes,” Joshua Juukuulius shifted in his seat and adjusted his monocle, “That would be lovely.”

Joshua was an oddball in Subaru’s eyes. He reminded Subaru of Julius.

Which was a bad thing.

Okay, maybe not that bad. But honestly anyone with the Juukuulius surname was on Subaru’s shitlist automatically.

Okay, not actually. But honestly, it’s too funny for Subaru to just stop having a feud with Julius out of nowhere.

The black star brought out two cups of tea, a variation of some kind of jasmine that Subaru came to enjoy during his time in Banan.

Joshua took a sip and noticeably grimaced at the taste.

You’re on thin ice Julius 2.0.

Subaru just chuckled, “Not your taste? It’s fine. It’s a traditional Banan strain. You must be new here.”

Let’s get this negotiation started.

Joshua flinched, “A-ah, not quite. I’ve actually been here sometime. Nearly four months now.”

I know. You told me before. Sorry Joshy, but I’m going to be giving you a hard time today. No hard feelings.

Subaru put on a cheerful smile, “Really? How are you liking the area?”

Joshua tried to give a polite smile, but his inexperience showed, looking more like a nervous grin, “I am pretty enamored by the culture of Banan as well as Kararagi as a whole. I would not mind living here for the rest of my life.”

That’s a lie. I know you miss home dearly. But you don’t want to disappoint your brother.

Subaru kept up his practiced business smile, “Well that is wonderful. I wouldn’t mind showing you around sometime. There are some wonderful places that many tourists and visitors miss, even after so many years.”

The young man’s eyes widened, “O-oh, you are a local then, I presume?”

You gotta work on your expressions there bud. Was I this bad too? Probably, considering Anastasia always hounded me during our first weeks in Banan.

Subaru waved his hand in the air, “Not really. I only arrived in Banan recently, but I’m actually very familiar with Kararagi itself. My family has ties to its origins.”

Not a lie technically. And if I’m correct-

Joshua got startled but quickly reoriented himself, “T-that’s incredible! I did not know I was in the presence of someone with such a bloodline.”

“Oh please, you flatter me. Especially considering your own bloodline’s extensive family history, I doubt I could compare.”

The boy’s eyes sparkled, “I see! You are a very knowledgeable man. I am grateful that you are aware of my family’s incredible achievements over the years.”

That’s it. Getting closer. Now…for the bait.

Subaru laid it on, thick, “Of course. The Juukuulius bloodline has spawned countless heroes and knights, worthy of praise. Though I haven’t been that up to date on Lugunica news, has there been someone who has recently taken up the mantle of chivalry?”

Ugh. It’s shoddy work but this is the best way to goad the kid. And if I’m right…

Joshua scratched his neck in embarrassment, “Ah apologies, unfortunately there has been no recently noteworthy members of our family.”

…What?

“It is a bit of a shame. While I would, my constitution is ill-suited. Though perhaps- “

Joshua continued to blather on about his family line as Subaru tried his best not to appear shocked, his eyes slightly widening.

Underneath however,

No. What?! That doesn’t make sense!

Subaru’s mind raced.

This was not what was supposed to happen. Joshua was supposed to start rambling about his brother. And then realize that Subaru should know about his brother. Given that the boy knew ‘Atlas’ was secretly an escaped Archbishop from Lugunica. That his brother requested him to look into Subaru and create a friendly relationship. Subaru was banking on his reaction being similar to before and then using it to get them a way back into Lugunica in the future.

But that’s not what happened!

He’s acting like-

Shit.

“Joshua,” Subaru cut off Joshua’s lore dump of his family history, “Does the name…Julius Juukuulius ring a bell?”

Subaru waited with bated breath, his heart pounding.

He had an idea.

And he really did not want it to be confirmed.

“…” Joshua looked at him strangely.

Subaru pressed him, “Any at all?”

Joshua continued to stare at him before finally answering,

“Of course, he’s my older brother. The famous Finest of Knights.”


Subaru’s heart stopped. His mind froze. He was…incredibly confused. It wasn’t the answer he dreaded.

“Wait,” the black star eyed Joshua closely, “Didn’t you say that there was no noteworthy people in your family recently?”

Joshua cocked his head, “I did? Apologies, maybe you misheard me. I said there was no other noteworthy members besides my brother.”

I-what? That’s not what he said! What the hell is going on?!

 

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Miles away. Far, far away from our two stars’ story.

“Juuuuuliusss~.”

The Finest of Knights held his breath. He did not recognize that voice.

“Juuuuulius. Oooooh Juuuulius. Come out, come out, wherever you are, tsu.”

He felt his heart pounding. That voice was so familiar. He remembered it clearly. A dear friend who would always invite him to drink after every mercenary mission.

“Come oooon! Juli-chan! Play with us! Just like always. Mimi really wants to play with you, tsu!”

That was not Mimi. That thing is not her! It’s wearing her skin. Trying to coax him out of his hiding spot.

“You can hide Julius. But you can’t run. So come out. We’ll find you eventually. And when we do. We can all go find Otto. It’s his birthday soon, ya know? Let’s celebrate it. All together. As a family.”

Julius grit his teeth. That wasn’t Tivey. That wasn’t…whoever looked like Tivey but wasn’t. He can’t remember. His mind was a mess. His memories were a mess.

He needed to find Otto. Make a plan. Something!

SHINK!

A blade got shoved into the wood next to him, nearly perforating his shoulder, it then quickly got pulled out.

“…Aw. I was really hoping that you were there. That’s fine though. We got all the time in the world to find you. You only have a few chances left Juuuuulius. Make em count, tsu~.”

…Julius Juukuulius was afraid.

Chapter 27: Chapter 27: Purgatorio III

Summary:

Take a glimpse into the mind of a lost soul...

Notes:

Enjoy!

Chapter Text

“You wanted to see me, Roswaal-sama?”

Otto Suwen took a step inside the Margrave’s dilapidated room within the Mather’s Manor in Costuul. Ever since they had returned from Priestella, Roswaal Mathers had been slowly becoming more and more of a recluse. A part of Otto believed this was a long time coming. For such a man, who was used to being in direct control of everything, only to now be a tool for the one who he used to looked down upon, would bring anyone to the lowest of lows.

Otto nearly tripped on an empty bottle, one of countless scouring his humble abode. Books, liquor, trash. All made refuge within this small sanctuary of depression.

“Yeeeeesss, it is good to see you Otto-san, it has been sooooo long,” Roswaal said with his usual drawl. The clown had seen better days. What was once an incredibly well-kept mage of the arcane arts, had become an emaciated wreck of a person. Baggy eyes, sunken cheeks, unshaven beard, hair was a complete mess.

He didn’t even wear any of his iconic makeup nor his usual getup. Instead he opted for long, dark red robes that covered his whole body. Evidently, it seems the man slept on his desk more than his bed.

Otto grimaced, the mage has been constantly disappearing. Otto could barely catch him on a normal day, it was only by luck that he was able to finally get a meeting with the Margrave, “It has been quite a while. Have you looked at the documents I gave to Ram?”

“I have, I have. Quite the amount of resources you will need in the next few months. It seems you have taken my recommendation to tackle the Sage’s tower to heart,” Roswaal took them out from under his desk, holding them in front of Otto, before burning them immediately with a small Goa, smiling with pure malice, “But what would it matter for me to know such things? I gave you complete financial control. Use it.”

“Roswaal-sama-“

“Oh, please. We both know such honorifics are only used due to your innate politeness. You could care less about respect in regards to me. You are only doing so because you wish to retain some semblance of decency in our relationship. That way, if and when this whole camp burns to cinders, you expect that such kindness will convince me that it would be worth saving.”

“…Is this why you wanted to see me?”

Roswaal laughed, it sounded hollow and wrong, “Hahahaha…no, of course not. Reminding you of our situation is barely needed. We are already one step away from exploding.”

“We are not. May I remind you that we were able to save Priestella with the help of the other camps?”

“And may I remind you of what we lost? Sure, we have indeed struck a great blow towards the Cult. The death of Greed, the capture of what seemed to be Pride and Wrath, as well as confirmation of the remaining bishops’ identities. However, our ally Crusch Karsten is on a time limit. You all barely survived with your lives thanks to luck. And we were unable to hold complete responsibility for any of the victories.”

Otto blurted out, “That’s not true! Emilia-sama played a great part in Greed’s defeat. Without her help, Reinhard-sama would have been unable to neutralize the Archbishop.”

Roswaal just gave Otto a sneer, “A victory that she could not explain in any logical way. From how she surmised, she seemed to have ‘guessed’ that Greed’s power was ‘somehow’ correlated with his wives. That a man wouldn’t have that many wives without good reason. She then thought freezing them would be enough to negate his power, leading to his demise by the Sword Saint. Tell me Otto Suwen. How in the world could such a victory be replicable in any logical sense?”

Otto stood strong, “Emilia-sama has incredible battle instincts. Even if you were to infer that her strategy was completely based on luck, you cannot deny that the results were clear. Her intuition was true, and Greed is no more.”

Roswaal waved his hand in the air, “Indeed. Now let us see what happens next. Let’s see if her ‘intuition’ will prove correct once again. Perhaps when she sees Gluttony, she’ll find out that he is susceptible to food poisoning. Or choking. And what about Lust? Perhaps she figures out the cure to Lust’s incredible psychopathy was a healthy dose of pure love and friendship. Perhaps the real apex of magic, was family love and camaraderie~.”

Otto had enough, “What is it that you want, Roswaal?!”

“What I want, deaaaaar Otto, is for you to accept the reality of our situation,” Roswaal slammed the desk with both hands, and stood, eyes manic and filled with pure rage, “We are barely scraping by, without any knowledge of what we are doing nor how to actually achieve our goals. You, the captain of this sinking ship, cannot even fathom the depths of this abyss that you are leading us into. Do not jest me with the idea that Emilia is the forerunner of this malarky. You hold the reigns. You hold my leash. You were the one who defeated me despite all the odds, yet you refused to accept the panacea in front of you that could solve all of our problems!”

Otto resisted the urge to grasp at the nearly restored Tome of Wisdom that he kept with him at all times, “I don’t know what you’re-“

“You know exactly what I’m talking about! Do not take me for a fool, Otto Suwen. You may have bested me within my own machinations, but you would be an idiot to think I have lost my edge in the slightest! You have my book. I can tell given your constant investigations into my archives as well as Clind. You know that with my help, we can fully repair it. And with its use, we can forge a path towards victory with the least possible complications! Our luck will no longer be random, but it will instead be predetermined! Our vision clear!”

The head court mage spread his arms out, acting as if he was preaching their salvation, and not leading them back to damnation. Otto hesitated. Despite knowing how such a tool could be insidious, the offer was tempting.

“…And what would you want in return for such assistance?”

“My freedom. This oath mark will no longer bind me,” before Otto could interject, Roswaal rolled his eyes, “Do not expect me to be so witless that I would choose to betray you all.
