The path forward will require more than just me, even I can see that now. People have the capacity for change, even changes that I could never predict. However, the book will allow us to avoid the worst of possibilities. Give us a future that can be favorable to everyone within this little camp of yours.”

We would no longer have to be running blind. Roswaal would also perhaps turn from a resentful helper into an active advisor.

Still, Otto shook his head, “You know better than I do how such proclivities led to your defeat. Your overreliance on the book was what caused your downfall. How could you be so sure that you won’t return to such bad habits. That we ourselves would not fall into such vices.”

Roswaal glared at him, “Then that is it?! You will damn us on a path where our carriage is kept together with rags and spit. Where every passenger barely knows how to drive it nor how to get past all the bumps and curves that we will face? All because you do not believe that any of you are incorruptible?! You will be damning us to hell Suwen. A hell that we could have easily circumvented. What if on your journey to the Augria Dunes, you face monsters and challenges that you could never hope to solve? What then, Suwen? What then will you do when nothing you have nor prepare, can even hope to solve such problems?!”

“…I’ll have my friends beside me. I may be unable to solve everything on my own, but the others will make up for my faults.”

“…Then you have doomed us all,” and with those words, Roswaal slumped back into his chair, the life gone from his eyes once again, “I do not care anymore. Just know that I have given my opinion, and that once this trembling house of cards finally falls, that I will laugh at your hubris. Go. Travel to the Sage’s tower. Die. In the end, none of it matters. My goal is more out of reach than ever before. I shall not be the Mathers that accomplishes my family’s dream…and I accept that. Just as you should accept your fate as well.”

Roswaal didn’t specify what ‘fate’ he was alluding to for Otto, but his silence and demeanor meant that this discussion was at an end.

Otto bowed slightly before leaving. However, just before he exited the door, “Though you may not realize it, there was a time that I and the others were starting to warm up to you, despite your schemes. During the last year, when you earnestly guided Emilia in her studies, advised Garf on how to improve his combat skills, and for clearing my debt. We were willing to let the past, truly stay the past. Might I ask, what changed?”

“…I realized that our efforts were for naught. No matter what, without something to make our victory assured, we will only blindly writhe in the muck of despair. Trust me. There is nothing worse of a feeling, than realizing that you have no hope of winning, no reward in sight, despite aaaaaaall of your hard work. Give up. It is worth more than dying as a fool.”

“…” Otto didn’t say a word more, he didn’t even expect Roswaal to say much more. However, that last bit, along with the rest of his speech, struck a chord with the advisor of the Emilia camp.

He exited the room, contemplating if he made the right decision. Every ounce of his body was screaming at him to take the deal. To let this farce of a coalition be finally led with real purpose instead of some idealistic nonsense. Even he barely believed in his own words.

…But what else could he do? Give up? No. If he gave up now, that would spit on all of the efforts of everyone who had gotten this far. He needed to do it for them.

Even though he doesn’t realize who they are anymore.

-------------------------------

“Otto-san.”

“…”

“Otto-san?”

“…”

“…”

Garfiel’s voice rang true, “Here, let me take a crack at ‘em.”

Said voice was followed up by a sucker punch to the face, sending Otto sprawling onto the ground as Reinhard and Julius stared at the sheer audacity of the Emilia Camp pair. Otto, meanwhile, sat up, nursing a bruise on his cheek with death in his eyes, “What the hell was that about Garf?!”
Garfiel snorted as he pointed a thumb at the two knights next to them, “Ya were spacin’ out like a wolgarm in Blue-sun. Ya didn’ even know the Knight bros were tryin’ to get yer attention.”

Otto looked towards the two knights, along with the Iron Fang who were awkwardly sitting far behind them, polishing their weapons or resting.

He grimaced and stood back up, brushing his robes, “Apologies. I’ve been trying to think of a solution to our problem.”

Said problem, was some kind of trial for the Pleiades Tower, situated right on the third floor, Taygeta. Which they were completely unable to figure out how to solve despite being here for nearly a week. After months of preparation, traveling, and fighting, they were finally at their limit, their supplies were running low.

Despite numerous tests and experiments, the group was unable to make any headway on the trial. It didn’t make sense, even after touching every single monolith clone, there was no difference. The trial was virtually impossible.

“Touch the brightest of the hero destroyed by Shaula.”

It didn’t make sense. There was no historical evidence of a hero being defeated by the great Sage Shaula. The sage wouldn’t answer any of their questions either, ignoring them entirely or just whispering, “Not yet.”

Otto sighed as he rubbed the back of his neck, “Unfortunately, I am still drawing a blank on what could be the answer to this riddle.”

Both Reinhard and Julius looked at each other before Julius stepped forward, “If I may, it might be wise of us to simply…cut our losses.”

That made Otto flinch, “No, we can’t just leave now.”

“Otto, please. We have made great strides in the investigation of the Pleiades Tower. Far more than any other explorer in history has. While I understand your frustration, we have reached a limit. It would be more tactical to return to the Royal Capital and discuss this trial with the Sage Council. Perhaps they can illuminate our path, even though we remain clueless.“

No. We can figure this out.

“Please just give me some time. I’m sure the answer is just on the horizon.”

“Otto-“

“Just,” Otto stammered before bowing, deeply, “One more day. Just one more day.”

His voice felt coarse, rough, and filled with regret.

“…Our excursion here is coming to an end Otto, whether we like it or not, we have failed,” Julius said, despite his eyes showing complete sympathy.

Otto didn’t say anything still bowing, before quickly turning around so no one could see his eyes, “…I’ll be on the fourth floor if you need me.”

“Otto, we can’t do this forever.”

The advisor ignored his friend’s plea, leaving without another word.

Julius motioned to go after him, before Garfiel stopped the knight, slowly shaking his head.

Otto descended to the third floor. His thoughts in disarray.

“Are you sure you don’t need me or Ram, Otto?”

“Emilia-sama. I think it would be best if we split our efforts. Garf and I should be enough, given that the Sword Saint and Royal Knight Julius will be accompanying us, there should be minimal difficulty in traversing the Augria Sand Dunes.”

“Still…it’s not right that you both are doing this for my sake, and I am not there to shoulder the burden.”
“Please, do not worry. While we are gone, you will have the important job of making connections with more of the noble houses. While I am grateful for Felt-sama lending us Reinhard’s help, we need to take advantage of the situation. She already has a large following in the commoners. And with Crusch-sama out of commission, that means we have the unique opportunity to draw the nobles to our side.”

“…That doesn’t seem all that fair-“

“Emilia-sama. Ram thinks you should just let Bottoto take care of things. He always gets the job done. Despite his lackluster attributes.”

“Hey!”

“As for what he said, Ram agrees. This is a competition. Even though we are on friendly terms, only one candidate can win. Do you really think ‘fairness’ is an excuse if you lose the Royal Selection? How would the elves from the Elior Forest feel if you abandoned them for such a reason?”

“Ram! That was uncalled for!“

“No…Ram is right. I don’t know what I was thinking. I would like to apologize to you both, for not taking this as seriously as I should. I was being naïve…I’ll believe in you Otto. Just as you believe in me.”

“You heard her Bottoto, make us proud. We’ll hold down the fort here.”

“…But look at me now,” Otto whispered to himself as he finally arrived at Alcyone, “So close and yet so far. Only to return with nothing but information, not even any that we could use to improve our standing by a large margin.”

He looked around, trying to find a place to ruminate in peace, only to notice a figure in the distance, sitting on the edge of a balcony, gazing off into the desert.

Deciding against his better judgement, he made his way over. The cool breeze brushed over him with every step closer, until he was finally outside. It was night, the stars were shining brighter than ever.

He glanced over at the figure, the Sage known as Shaula.

She was a beauty beyond any measure. Her outfit was practically a death sentence for any man’s heart. But her demeanor or character was a mystery to everyone. Barely a word spoken to any of them, only gesturing and guiding them when they first arrived.

“…It’s quite cold tonight.”

As always, Shaula was quiet, only looking towards a place that neither Otto nor anyone else could ever understand, “…”

But for some reason, Otto felt chatty today, “Perhaps it is rude of me to ask, but my curiosity still troubles me. What exactly are you waiting for?”

“…”

“…You mentioned once the words, ‘not yet.’ Which means that you were waiting for something. Or someone. You need not answer, but I’ve always been curious about what exactly it is that such a wise Sage such as yourself is searching for.”

Her hair and cloak blew with the wind, but her body and expression were stationary, never moving from her spot.

Otto persisted, “Are you searching for someone special? Someone who can give you the knowledge that you seek? The person who could solve this tower’s trial? Or maybe…it is purpose that you seek.”

The advisor looked out into the distance, viewing the stars in all their glory, “Just like all of us…looking for purpose.”

Otto Suwen did not know what his purpose was anymore. When he first joined the Emilia camp, everything felt so clear. His debt was no longer an issue. His goal was to make sure that Emilia became the next queen no matter what. And despite everyone’s problems, the people around him were a cohesive unit, ready to take on any obstacle in their path.

But now? He didn’t know. The path forward was vague. It felt like…he no longer had a star to follow. Even though such feelings did not make sense in his mind. His emotions were still there.

He was lost. With no idea what to do.

He muttered to himself, “Maybe it’s not even just a purpose. Maybe you’re looking for a reason to go forward. Something to guide you once again.”

Silence invaded the area, only the howling wind breaking up the monotony. Perhaps tonight will be just like every night.

Or perhaps not.

“…Master,” her voice was soft yet clear. Filled with yearning and heartbreak.

Otto flicked his head towards the Sage, her only spoken word for weeks hitting him out of nowhere.

Only to see that she disappeared just as fast. She was gone. Her presence no longer next to him.

He felt the last of his composure fall apart, realizing that his gambit failed, and the Sage was still far from ever being reachable.

Otto slumped forward, resting his head and arms on the railing of the balcony.

Perhaps it really was over.

“Oi, Brotto, gettin’ some clean air?” Otto didn’t even raise his head, as the familiar brotherly voice came from behind him.

“…Hey Garf.”

Otto could hear the boy’s heavy footsteps walk confidently before feeling the vibrations of Garfiel’s back hitting the railing, most likely leaning on it with his whole weight.

“So, ya think wer screwed?”

Garfiel’s bluntness barely fazed Otto, “…Yeah. That sounds about right Garf.”

“Hmph,” he could hear Garfiel blow air between his lips, “Alright then, I guess we failed.”

The words pierced Otto’s heart, causing him to raise his head and look at Garfiel with complete indignation, “How can you say that so nonchalantly? As if us failing isn’t a massive cataclysmic event?!”

Garfiel simply cocked his head in confusion, “It is?”

“…Yes! Yes it is! Do you know how bad our position is currently?! We are halfway into the election and we barely have any victories to our name! And now, we spent an incredible amount of resources and time, only to fail miserably! We’ll be an absolute laughing stock! Emilia’s reputation will be in tatters! All because I made the stupid decision to try conquering a tower that no one else could before!”

Otto was panting, his cheeks flushed with rage and embarrassment, as Garfiel just looked at him and smiled, “Ya feel better now that ya got dat all out of yer system?”

Otto felt his blood pressure spike, “No! I don’t! I just-“

He slapped his hands over his eyes before falling to the ground, laying on his back, sulking.

“…I don’t know what to do.”

He took his hands off his eyes, slightly stained with the tears that came out from his outburst, as he saw Garfiel kneel down and lie on his back right next to him, “Yeah. I don’t know what to do either.”

Otto stared at him, “Great. So, we are both idiots.”

Garfiel chuckled, “Yep…so then what’s next?”

Otto kept staring at him, “What’s next? What’s next?! We failed Garf. What’s next is that we go home and report to Emilia that we are utterly incompetent.”

“Are we?” Before Otto could retort, Garfiel kept talking, “Cuz, from what I can see, we ain’t too bad. Look at how far we got. Unlike everyone, even the Sword Saint on his own, we got to the tower. We confirmed dat the Sage is alive. We know that there is some secret trial or some shit in order to access the rest of the tower. It’s a lot more than most people ever achieved.”

“…But we still failed. We’re hopeless.”

“And I don’t really know where ya got dat idea from. Think about it Brotto. Look at what we’ve accomplished. Ya were able to figure out how to get through Sand Time with just yer brain and yer Divine Protection.”

Otto was stubborn, “Anyone could have done that.”

“Nah, at least, I don’t think so. Dat shit was difficult to understand. Hell, the Sword Saint and the Finest of Knights couldn’t think it through. But ya could! Dat’s somethin’ ya can’t just ignore. Hell, remember Priestella? Sanctuary? We got so much done despite all the odds against us.”

Otto looked upward, staring at the stars once again, “…It was all luck. None of it was anything we could have accomplished with just grit.”

“So?” Garfiel laughed at Otto’s reaction, “Come on Brotto. So, what if it was luck? That just means we capitalized on our good luck. Not everyone can do dat. Just like Hoshin’s gamble with Ford Lugunica, ‘the real test of skill is those who use every ounce of luck, no matter what.’ Sure, we could have lost horribly. And things might seem unclear right now. But are we really just goin’ ta give up just cuz we failed once? After all dat?”

“…No. I guess not. But what if we make a bigger mistake? What if we die for it?”

Garfiel sat up and put his arm on his bent knee, “Then we die. It’s better than just sittin’ somewhere, doing nothin’ but stagnate.”

“…”

“…If there’s anythin’ I learned back in Sanctuary, it’s that doin’ nothin’ is worse than going out there and doin’ something. Sure, we might fail, fall into various pits. Maybe the people we love will suffer for it. But ‘d rather live mah life, moving forward, than stay fearful any longer.”

Garfiel looked towards Otto and held out a hand, “And ‘d rather die with a brother by my side, towards a goal worth fightin’ for, then runnin’ away just cuz thin’s were lookin’ tough.”

Otto stared at the outstretched hand and saw the various calluses and scars on the boy’s hand. A fifteen year old boy who left the shelter he once lived in since childhood, and not only a year later, he defeated the reanimated corpse of a legendary warrior.

…How could Otto be so foolish?

He grasped his brother’s hand tightly, the sound of their locked hands echoing throughout the night, “It wouldn’t hurt to die as a fool.”

Garfiel chuckled as they both got up, the young teenager wrapped his arm over the shoulder of his now rejuvenated brother-in-arms as they both made it up the staircase, and back towards the rest of the group.

As the duo arrived in the white room, they saw Ricardo and the Triplets trying to work on the monolith.

Mimi noticed them walking up and bounced with excitement over to them, jumping onto Garfiel, “Did you guys beat each other up?!”

Otto looked at her as if she was insane, “Why in Lugunica would Garf and I fight each other?”

Mimi put a finger on her chin, “Mimi remembers you saying that friends need a punch every once in a while, to get their head on straight.”

Otto grimaced, “If Garf actually punched me, for real, I would die.”

Ricardo walked over with the two other Triplets, putting his arms around Garfiel and Otto, “Ah don’t know, ya seem like ya took that punch earlier pretty well. Might as well see how durable ya are.”

Garfiel grinned maliciously at his now—absolutely scared as shit—brother, “We never did get to spar Brotto.”

Before Otto could give all 101 reasons why that was a bad idea, Julius and Reinhard appeared from behind the monolith and walked over.

Julius looked regretful, “It seems you are now in better spirits, Otto. I apologize for my words earlier. They were rather blunt-“

Otto cut him off, “No. I think…I think you were right. We’re wasting time here. We’ve done enough, it’s time to head home.”

Julius perked up, “That is quite wonderful to hear. Let us make haste then-“

Julius was cut off once again, but this time because of Reinhard’s hand which was raised in front of him.

Julius glanced at Reinhard, confused. The Sword Saint was acting strange. His eyes were fixated on a spot on the wall. His body tense and his demeanor was now incredibly alert.

The rest of the group noticed as well. Otto spoke up, “Reinhard-san? What’s wrong?”

“…”

Reinhard didn’t speak at all his eyes searching for something. Something they all couldn’t see. Seconds passed.

Until finally, he yelled out, “Everyone, please get down!”

Just as he yelled, the spot where he was fixated on, burst. Shadows and dark hands twisted with miasma, climbed through the opening, just as more holes were created from above and below.

They all clustered together, in the center of the white room, just as Reinhard gripped the sword at his hip, shadows surrounding them.

To Otto’s horror, he saw the sword break free from its scabbard.

The Dragon Sword Reid had finally found a worthy opponent.

-------------------------------

Anastasia felt sick. Her eyes fluttered open and she barely had a second before she started to dry heave into the nearby trash can.

Thankfully, she had nothing left in the tank for her to vomit. Unfortunately, that also meant that she was incredibly hungry.

She lifted her head and turned in surprise as she noticed a plate of freshly cut appas. Sliced into various animals, including a spiked one that reminded her of that one story of Subaru’s.

Sonic, right?

She felt warm. The only warmth left in her heart.

A part of her felt thankful for Subaru’s presence and love. That despite having no idea what was afflicting her, he was still trying his best to help, not even prying into her mind for a solution.

It both made her feel safe and disgusted. Not disgusted at him. But of herself. For still taking advantage of someone with such a kind heart.

…It wouldn’t be good to waste them.

She promptly took off the covers and blankets that surrounded her and grabbed the plate from the nearby table, slowly popping slices of appa into her mouth.

They were sweet, slightly tangy.

Subaru said he wanted to make something called an appa pie. Maybe I’ll ask him if he still wants to make it this week…

Sure. Ask him to do more for you. How selfless of her.

Anastasia shivered, her guts were twisted once again, she had to use all her strength to force the appas back down.

She sighed before taking another bite.

“This can’t go on,” she muttered to herself.

Anastasia didn’t know how to move forward, however. She could say this was all just a random sickness, a side effect of his Authority, or that she was pregnant.

…Okay, that was a horrible joke. Anastasia would never lie to Subaru about that.

Still, every logical part of her mind said this had to end somehow. And perhaps, the only solution that would make everyone happy, would be to simply… move on.

Yeah.

If Subaru can bear the burden of his power, she will bear the burden of knowing. She’ll work from the shadows. Guess and infer from his reactions. Help him but never tell. It’s the least she could do. The only thing she could do. Despite how worthless such a gesture was.

“…It’s time to face the music, as he says,” she smirked, though the smile quickly died. She wanted to see him now, to give her the courage needed to return to normalcy.

Anastasia stood, wobbling slightly due to the sudden movement, and made her way to the door.

Just as she was about to reach for the handle-

Subaru ran in, eyes bewildered and his expression was on edge, when he caught her eyes, he pursed his lips, “Ana. We need to go back to Lugunica. Now.”

…Oh no.

Chapter 28: Purgatorio IV

Summary:

Subaru starts prepping while Anastasia finally talks about her feelings...

Notes:

Enjoy!

Chapter Text

“Subaru…why is Joshua unconscious?”
Anastasia was currently staring at her knight’s brother, who was lying face first on the ground.

Her darling husband-to-be, meanwhile, was feverishly combing through their stuff taking out various objects, bottles, and tools. He didn’t seem to notice what Anastasia said.

“…Subaru. Please tell me why you knocked out Julius’s brother. I understand you don’t like him that much but-“

“Ana, quick question: how many Pearlbatons do you know?”

Anastasia looked at him like he was insane, “One? There’s only one that I know, and his name is Hetaro.”

Subaru stared at her, “…Shit. Oh, this is really bad.”

Her nerves started to fire once more. She was already on the verge of another breakdown but seeing Joshua knocked out took the wind out of her sails. Now the winds were on full blast, and a storm was coming.

Anastasia went up to Subaru and grabbed his sleeve, her eyes manic, “Subaru…please. Tell me what’s going on.”

Her tone of voice finally made Subaru stop rummaging around the house, focusing on her, his eyes filled with regret and sadness. He put down the pouches he took out from a cupboard and put them on a table, gently grabbing Anastasia’s hands.

“We need to go back to Lugunica. If I’m right about this…your family is in danger. Gluttony is eating their names as we speak.”

Her blood froze, “…What?”

Her mind was about to collapse.

Subaru grabbed her cheeks with his hands, they felt warm to the touch, “But they are not going to get away with this. We’re going to Lugunica and we are going to fix this. Now.”

He then gave a her a quick peck on the lips, before going back to rummaging throughout the apartment, grabbing more and more ludicrous things, hidden all over. Packages of lagamites, bokko fruits, various crystals of different sizes and colors in bottles with labels that Anastasia could recognize as ‘Japanese,’ and what looked to be a small cylindrical object with a string attached to it. One side of it was closed while the other was open.

Subaru grabbed the cylinder and placed one of the crystals inside before running to the nearest window and peaked his body out.

He then positioned the cylinder upward and pulled the string. The resulting sound was almost like a mini cannon, shooting out a small bundle of light into the sky.

Anastasia was shocked, “Did you just shoot out a night banisher?!”

Subaru pocketed the mini cannon into his pocket before going back to rummaging, “Yeah, I had Halibel get me some during the last week. Don’t worry, it’s only a less concentrated version, it will stay up there for only one-third of the time and with less power. As for how I made it, remember those guns that I told you about from back home? I had an idea for a possible prototype and got close.”

Anastasia could only gawk at the absurdity of this situation, “Y-you made a gun?”

She had only been told a few stories about some of the most dangerous weapons from Subaru’s home. He always talked about them with caution. How they were loud, explosive, but effective. That you could kill people within just a second of firing it and with little practice or skill. From distances that you couldn’t even see with the naked eye. The idea made her shiver when listening, she wasn’t a fan of arms dealing but she could see how lucrative it was. The potential for selling these weapons was incredible.

But Subaru never liked it. Vehemently denying any sort of explanation of how they worked or how to even make them. Just saying that he didn’t know much and could never reconstruct one. Underneath, she could see how uncomfortable the idea of having these weapons here made him. So, she never pressed him.

Subaru kept grabbing more objects: a couple of knives and kunai stashed in random places, a few more of those cylinders, and some more crystals.

“I’ll tell you more about them later. I was meaning to explain earlier but…so many things happened that I decided to push it off. I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to keep this a secret.”

He seemed to be misunderstanding what she was so shocked about, “Subaru…could you tell me why you made such a thing?”

“…Not to hurt anyone. But I knew there could be scenarios that it would be possibly useful. It was better safe than sorry.”

She felt her gut twist and writhe at such logic, “Scenarios such as?”

Subaru pursed his lips before answering, “Wrath. If Sirius ever got out, I could use a more advanced version of it in order to kill her from a long distance. I don’t know her exact range, and while I don’t want to ever test how far it can go, this could help with neutralizing her if I reach her theoretical limit.”

That answer was too quick. Too precise. She knows exactly why he made it.

He made it for her.

He must have been desperate. If he was looking for an Authority to save her life, Sirius was the only Archbishop they knew the location of. The only problem was killing her without her power causing everyone around her to die.

Hence the weapon.

“…Could you at least tell me how you made it?”

Subaru hummed as he unscrewed a bottle and smelled its contents, he then continued around the room, grabbing similar bottles, “Minerals here are more diverse than I once thought. I thought I had to recreate gunpowder, but it would take too long and require way too many resources. However, grounded up pyroxene crystals is a decent substitute. It’s not as efficient, nor powerful, but it gets the job done. The only problem was making it so that the container could handle the explosion. After finding out how night banisher and magic stone cannons worked, I was able to guess and design a miniature version. The casing is lined with Anti-Magic crystals that help dampen the expulsion of fire mana and redirect the energy forward, causing propulsion. Unfortunately, the damn things are still not perfect, they break after a few uses and can malfunction easily.”

Experiments. He must have experimented countless times. Failed a large percentage of them.

She wondered how many of those experiments caused him to go back.

Just as she was about to ask another question, someone slammed into their wall, breaking it apart upon entry.

It was Tia. Holding a very scared and manic Beatrice.

Subaru glanced at the two spirits, still preoccupied, “Hey Tia, sorry about the-“

“Subaru!” Beatrice cut in, practically tackling Subaru as he almost fumbled some jars of liquid, barely catching them, “A-are you hurt? Is everything alright? Betty is sorry! Betty should have been here! Why did you use the emergency signal, in fact?!”

After gently putting the bottles down, he cooed and patted the little spirit in order to coax her anxieties, “I’m fine, I’m fine. Everything is okay. Okay, maybe not totally okay. Gluttonies are back in Lugunica-“

“What?!”

“And it’s eating all of our friends, possibly. By the way, how many people are in Anastasia’s camp?”

Beatrice looked at him confused, “T-three, I suppose?”

“Okay we are still good. I think. Ana-pop, every five minutes, could you please list all of your camp’s members? Please and thank you.”

She understood what he wanted, “Julius, Ricardo, Mimi.”

His eye twitched, “Okay, I think I’m starting to understand what’s going on. Maybe.”

Tia was just staring at Joshua, who was still blissfully sleeping on their floor, covered in debris from the broken wall, “Su. Why is there another purple thing on the floor? It doesn’t look like you or Ana, so it’s not your child. Should I kill it?”

Subaru stood up and started bouncing Beatrice in his arms, trying to still calm her rapidly beating heart, “No, even though he looks like Julius, he doesn’t deserve to get swatted like a fly. He’s pretty cool. As for why, I kind of panicked.”

Tia started poking Joshua with a stick, “Panicked?”

“I may have thought he was Capella in disguise for a few seconds. Clocked him in the face. After making sure he wasn’t faking it, and checking using Ops Basiliskos, he was already unconscious.”

“Ha. What a weakling.”

She then glanced at Anastasia and narrowed her eyes. Tia threw the stick, it ended up hitting Joshua in the head, and she walked over to the little merchant, eyeing her closely.

Anastasia tried to meet her eyes, but found it difficult, “…I’m fine.”

Besides the fact that her camp was slowly getting eaten from existence and the fact that Subaru changed his whole morality for her, she’s doing fine.

Tia sighed, “Did not even ask. And you are not. We need to talk later.”

“No, I don’t.”

Tia shoved a thumb towards Beatrice— who despite acting annoyed about Subaru treating her like a baby—was actually looking calmer than ever, “That one said the same thing. But a talk with me cured some of her sickness or whatever. You are talking with me later, and that is final.”

Before she could retort, someone broke the window and jumped in.

It was Halibel, “Is everyone alright?! I saw the light and came back as soon as…why is there a child knocked out on our floor?”

Said child had some pieces of glass laying on him, thankfully none of the shards seemed to have pierced his clothes or skin.

Subaru pinched his nose bridge, “Seriously. We have doors. Why is no one using them?!”

Halibel brushed some glass off of his shoulder and then immediately shrugged, “Doors are just concepts. Anyways, dats not important. What’s the emergency and what do we need to do Su-san?”

Subaru managed to calm Beatrice down and motioned towards Joshua, “Long story short, we have a situation: Gluttony is currently eating Ana’s family back in Lugunica. And maybe more. We need to go save them. Now.”

Anastasia spoke loudly, “Julius, Mimi, Tivey.”

Subaru’s eye kept twitching, “They’re either having indigestion or messing with someone. My guess is the latter.”

Halibel stared at Subaru before picking Joshua up and slinging him over his shoulder, “You’re awfully calm when describin’ possibly the worst situation that could ever happen. Also, what do we do with this guy?”

Subaru shrugged as he grabbed a backpack and started arranging all of his materials into it, still holding Beatrice with one arm, “There is no use panicking when I could be doing something about it. Also, technically not even the worst possible situation I imagined. As for Joshua, we’re going to take him with us. Send a message to Hoshin Company that Joshua has a family emergency and requested the help of the Admirer. At the very least, they’ll know where he is. We’ll need him to go inform his family of what’s happening. Maybe he can get the knights to back us up. Could you explain everything to him once he wakes up?”

Halibel nodded as he whistled. Suddenly two ninjas appeared from outside, climbing into the broken window. He started whispering to them instructions.

Subaru then finished packing up, his moves efficient and quick, before slinging the bag on his back, he looked at Beatrice, “Sorry about this Beako but I’m going to need your help expediting that project I gave you. How far into it did you get?”

Beatrice’s eyes widened as she realized what he was referring to, “A-ah! So that’s what you want to do, in fact! But the mana cost-“

“Can be dealt with, I have an idea. If it can work, we could possibly shave off a lot of time. But we’ll need to go to a spiritually rich place.”

Subaru grabbed Anastasia’s bag and threw it over to her, she nearly fumbled it as she was in the middle of processing everything, finally realizing, she said, “We need to go to the Miko Temple.”

Subaru snapped his fingers at her, “Bingo. It’s the only place with potentially a high number of spirits for our purposes.”

But Anastasia didn’t understand one thing, “But what are we going to do there?”

Subaru just smiled confidently, “We’re going to make an intercontinental Door Crossing.”

------------------------------------

“Let’s talk.”

Anastasia eyed the wind spirit with annoyance, “Does it have to be now?”

Tia waved her hand around them. Their arrival at the Miko Temple was met with a warm welcome, many of the priestesses thanked the group for their help with the Witch Cultists and allowed the group to use their main auditorium without a second thought. Subaru and Beatrice were currently drawing symbols on one of the doors. Halibel was talking to a, now awake, Joshua who quickly went from scared out of his mind to deeply concerned about his brother. Meanwhile, Tia and Anastasia were in their little corner, watching everything unfold.

“We’re about to go into a life-threatening situation. This is no time for you to be in some weird mindset,” before Anastasia could argue, Tia glared at her, “Su looks like he has half a mind to leave you here. But I know who you are, and I know you would rather die than let him go at this alone nor be the only one who stays while their family is in danger. So, we either talk this out or you get left behind. Your choice.”

Anastasia held her tongue and instead grit her teeth, “Fine. So what? Is this just going to be like before?”

Anastasia expected a possible verbal fight incoming. It was a good guess considering who Tia was. What she didn’t expect, was the wind spirit’s eyes to go soft and her face looking incredibly concerned.

“…Do you hate yourself?”

Anastasia didn’t know how to answer that, “…”

Tia sighed, “So you do. It’s just like that little brat. For some reason or another, you are blaming yourself for something you can’t control. And you’re slowing killing yourself as a result.”

A pang of guilt and rage spiked into her soul, “That isn’t it.”

“It is that. People like you, who can solve most problems with their mind and intellect, crash and burn when faced with a situation that is literally impossible. Where the only choice is to accept the results because any further action will just make things worse. You hate yourself because of your weakness. Because there is nothing else left to do.”

Anastasia gripped her hands, so tightly that it threatened to break the skin, “So what do you suggest I do? I would take any advice at this point.”

“…I don’t have anything.”

“So, this conversation is pointless then!” Anastasia threw her hands in the air, her body shaking, “Nothing can change! I can’t do anything. You can’t do anything. No one can. No one but-“

“Subaru.”

That name made Anastasia’s blood freeze, she gripped the spirit’s shoulders suddenly, “How much did Beatrice tell you?”

Tia shook her head, “Nothing. But it doesn’t take a genius to figure out that you both are at a crossroads because of Su. Ever since last week, it’s as if you’ve been slowly pushing everything down until finally exploding. Like a volcano.”

Anastasia looked away, towards Subaru who was guiding Beatrice’s hand as they drew more symbols together, hand-in-hand, “…So you noticed he was different too then.”

“What? No. Su is the same as always.”

Anastasia whipped her head back towards the spirit and looked at her as if she was stupid, “Are you blind? Have you seen how he acts?! Halibel, Eridna, Betty, me. We all noticed. How did you not? He’s basically a different person.”

Tia looked at Anastasia as if she was stupid, narrowing her eyes, “He isn’t. He’s the same Su as always.”

“How?! Have you seen how he acts? Subaru has knowledge that he never had before.”

“So? Su knows a lot about stuff I never can understand. Nothing different there.”

Her anger was rising, “How about how his morality? Subaru is barely phased by anything at this point. I bet if you killed someone in front of him, he wouldn’t even react.”

“Wrong. Su is kind but that doesn’t mean he has to be open about it. He’s prioritizing. Most humans care about death because it’s a natural instinct. Su cares because he is Su. It’s just that Su doesn’t act like a baby about it anymore.”

“Then what about his love for me? Just two weeks before, he was hesitating all the time. Now, I’m all he can think about!”

“Isn’t that a good thing? Didn’t you want that? You wanted all of him.”

“But I’m not enough!” Her outburst made her quickly look around, try to see if it got anyone’s attention. Until she realized that Tia was using her magic to deafen their conversation, a thin veil of constantly vibrating wind preventing any noise from coming out. It was extremely exhausting mana-wise to keep up. Tia herself was blocking everyone’s view of Anastasia.

Anastasia realized how seriously Tia was taking this conversation, the spirit’s eyes all but confirming it. The merchant’s eyes teared up.

Tia was confused, “What do you mean?”

Her throat was constricting, Anastasia felt sick, “I can’t give him something equal. I realized…he gives me so much. More than I could ever pay back. Not now. Maybe not ever.”

“That doesn’t matter to Su-“

“It matters to me!” No longer constrained by the thought of drawing attention, Anastasia let out all she was holding back, “I’m just like everyone else. Subaru gives me so much and I can’t give him an ounce back. I want to be there for him. To be right beside him. To hold everything up with him! All his problems, all my problems. Shared equally. How can I do that if I can’t even hold them in the first place?! How can I even compare to him?! I’m useless! I’m terrible! I can barely think of a solution, all I can do is reap the benefits! I’m a piece of shit who can only take advantage of people! A bastard who only knows how to gain, and gain, and gain! I’m a greedy girl who doesn’t know when to stop. I took everything from Subaru and gave him nothing back! A disgusting, worthless, mess of a woman! Who am I compared to Subaru?! I’m nothing! I’m…nothing.”

Her last words were just sobs. All the disgust had left her stomach, leaving only the hollow feeling of being worthless.

“…”

Every breath felt like five, her body shuddering, “What am I supposed to do for him? When all he does is give to me.”

Tia gazed at her with pity, “…Would you do the same for him, if you had the choice? Able to give him back just as much, when given the chance.”

“Absolutely. What kind of question is that?” Anastasia couldn’t help but laugh at the absurdity of such a question. She’d go against the whole world, if it would even pay a fraction of what she owed to him.

“Then that’s all that matters.”

“That doesn’t mean any-“

“It does though,” Tia cut off anymore interruptions, “You act as if you won’t get the chance to ever pay him back. The problem with that mindset is that you’ve essentially given up before even trying, you pansy. So what if you can’t do anything now? A situation will come where you can. But that will never happen if you keep moping around, thinking that you’re a waste of space. All you’ll really do is add on more burdens to Su. Is that what you want?”

“No! I don’t…I want to help him with everything.”

“Then do that. Get your shit together and be there with him. Be someone he can rely on. That he can look towards for guidance. And you’ll get all the opportunities to pay him back. Some small. Some big. Maybe never like he did for you. But it can be enough. You can be enough.”

“…”

Perhaps she was right. Anastasia can’t do anything now. But an opportunity will come.

“…”

And maybe that was enough.

“…Thank you, Tia. I needed this. This…talk,” Anastasia didn’t feel all that better. But her mind was less cloudy. And her guts felt less rancid.

Tia rolled her eyes, “Yeah, you did, you stupid lame moron. Now come on, Su looks like he is losing his mind over there and he could probably use your advice right about now,” Tia pointed behind her with her thumb. Anastasia peered around the spirit’s body and saw Subaru frantically going through his bag, pulling out various fruits and stones.

She smiled softly and whispered, “…That idiot.”

She then walked past Tia, just as the wind barrier dropped down.

Tia watched as Anastasia walked towards Subaru and Beatrice, whispering to herself, “Not happening again…not on my watch.”

She then joined everyone, Halibel and Joshua seemed to have also finished their discussion.

Subaru was pacing back and forth, thinking and muttering, biting his thumb, “It’s too much, even with the bokko fruit and hexcel drugs. We need other sources of mana…”

Anastasia chimed in, “The Door Crossing requires that much?”

Subaru looked in surprise, noticing how his fiancé had a slightly different demeanor now, and smiled, “Yes. The problem is that Beako is tapping into a familiar area from an unfamiliar location. Theoretically possible but the mana requirement is humongous, especially considering that we have to carry several people at once. I originally asked Beatrice to slowly link a door in our house to a door in Lugunica. It would require a lot of mana as well but with more time, she could have slowly done it with ease. Now, we are basically forcing a hole through space to get across half of the continent.”

Anastasia bounced ideas, “How about draining the mana from us and asking some of the spirits here for help? That’s why you brought us to the temple in the first place.”

Subaru shook his head, “We don’t have enough. Banan isn’t that spirit dense compared to Lugunica and Gusteko. I was wrong. There aren’t as many spirits as we need. And we can’t drain all of our mana, we’ll be arriving in a location that could have enemies, I’d rather not arrive without any of us being able to fend them off. That’s not even adding onto the fact that we still need to make our way to the Sage’s Tower.”

Subaru then held out jars of Bokko fruit and hexcel drugs, Anastasia’s face went pale, “Subaru, that’s a terrible idea.”

He shrugged, “I know. But it was something I had just in case. Even then, the math doesn’t check out. Beako doesn’t think it will be enough.”

Anastasia thought for a moment, until her neurons fired a brilliant idea, “Maybe-“

Her brilliant idea was completed by an outside source, “Let us help you, Subaru-sama.”

Many Mikos appeared from the main door, the fox demi-human Miko in particular was leading them from the front.

She bowed in front of the group, along with the others, saying, “Apologies for our rude interruption. We did not intend to eavesdrop. However, we saw how frustrated our savior looked, and many of us would rather be rude than ignorant. We wish to offer our mana for the ritual. So that you may save your family, as you saved ours.”

Subaru and Anastasia were stunned. Subaru got shaken out of his shock first, stepping forward, “I appreciate you offering, but I did account for you guys as well. I actually wanted to ask for your help as it seemed like the most rational option. Even then, it still wouldn’t be enough.”

The Mikos all stood up, the fox Miko’s lips curved into a smile, “Then it is good that we are not the only ones offering assistance.”

Suddenly all of the doors around them sprung open, as hundreds of people poured in.

Everyone in the group was stunned.

Even Halibel who whispered, “Moving people without saying a word…”

The miko gestured to everyone, “These are our families, relatives, and friends. As well as whoever we could get our hands on at the moment.”

A man limped forward, he had an eyepatch and a deformed arm, twisted into the shape of a bug’s pincer, his right leg a wooden prosthetic.

The fox miko took his deformed hand, holding it lovingly while helping him stand, the man smiled at her as he took his eyepatch off, revealing a more disgusting mutation: his eye was like a weird fusion of a fly’s and a human’s.

He bowed his head towards the group, his voice stuttering but filled with conviction, “T-thank y-you. W-without y-you, w-we w-would h-have n-never s-survived. P-please…”

He took a deep breath, concentrating all his will, “Let us be of service to you.”

The miko looked proud at her husband before refocusing on the group, “If this is not enough, wait. We will bring hundreds more. All our connections, our money, our mana, our bodies. None of it can repay a fraction of the debt we owe you all. Without us even asking for help, you came and freed our loved ones. You gave our temple hope, when we had none.”

Subaru, Anastasia, Halibel, Tia, Beatrice, even Joshua. Not a single one of them could speak.

Until Subaru stepped forward. Anastasia saw his movement and followed. He then bowed almost ninety degrees, filled with reverence, “Thank you. Truly, thank you. We will never forget this favor.”

Anastasia bowed as well. Halibel next. Tia and Beatrice too. And Joshua, when the two spirits pulled him to the floor.

The crowd copied Subaru’s action, bowing in reverence, “And to us, the same. We will honor our debt to you, until the end of our days. For now, this is all we can offer you.”

All of the people started to line up in front of Beatrice as she siphoned mana from each of them.

Subaru and Anastasia stood off to the side watching, Subaru whispered, “Incredible. This never happened before…”

Anastasia looked at him, “You didn’t expect this?”

He shook his head, “I expected the Mikos maybe. But not this. There’s more coming in too. It’s as if all of Banan is coming here.”

“You should be proud,” the duo turned their heads and saw Eridna walking up, she had been absent from the group after reaching the temple, “Your act of kindness created waves. That is a rare occurrence in this world.”

Subaru had a sneaking suspicion, “Did you do something to cause this?”

Eridna scoffed, “Oh, not really. Though I may have left the doors a tad open, right as some random passersby heard you mumbling to yourself aloud. Everything else was their choice.”

He smiled as he picked the fox up and petted her head, “Thank you.”

The fox purred, “You are not alone, child. There are people out there who will move mountains for you.”

At her words, Subaru felt a hand touch his, the warmth and texture were so familiar, he didn’t have to even look.

Anastasia held his hand and looked forward, “She’s right. Not even mountains. Worlds would move for you, if they had the chance.”

Just like these people, I’ll have my chance. Just you wait, Subaru.

------------------------------------

“Thank you everyone, once again.”

The fox Miko waved her hand in the air, as everyone else waved goodbye, “Please. We should be the one expressing gratitude. Good luck on your journey.”

Subaru looked at his group, “Everyone ready? Good. Beako, tell us when to run into the door.”

Beatrice nodded and began channeling mana while being held by Subaru.

The crowd watched as Yin magic poured from the little girl, covering the door in a thin layer of shadows, before solidifying into a dark mass, like a black hole in the middle of reality.

Beatrice’s voice sounded strained as she shouted, “Go! GO NOW, I SUPPOSE!”

The group then rushed forward, diving into the black hole all at once.

…And then breaking through the other side, out of a burnt door that lay next to some rubble, they tumbled out onto a bunch of dirt and grass, trees and shrubbery surrounding them.

Subaru rubbed his head as he got up, helping Anastasia to her feet as everyone groaned in pain, “Everyone here?”

“Yeah, Su-san.” “Su. I hate Yin magic.” “Betty can’t believe that worked, in fact.” “That was incredible, Atlas-sama!”

Subaru nodded as he recognized that everyone got through unscathed, “Awesome. Now if I’m right, we ended up near the old manor. Or what’s left of it. Huh. I thought Ros-chi would have started rebuilding it the moment we moved.”

“That was the plan. Unfortunately, other priorities got in the way,” the unknown voice, tired and confused, made Halibel and Tia get in front of the two stars immediately.

Beatrice stumbled to her feet, mana almost all drained but still willing to use whatever’s left, she channeled the mana within her and Eridna, who immediately possessed her.

Joshua hid behind the two stars peering over their shoulders.

Everyone’s attention was focused on the source of the voice.

At least until Joshua spoke with alarm, “Margrave Mathers?!”

Subaru looked back before looking forward once again, shock evidently on his face, “So this is where you were…no wonder I couldn’t find you. What happened to you, Ros-chi?”

“…I lost. Now, who are you~? And how do you know me?”

Roswaal L. Mathers. Current incarnation of Roswaal A. Mathers. Master of the arcane arts. Current holder of multiple color titles. An incredible tactician and manipulator of the highest degree.

 

So, why was said person currently dressed like Gandalf?

Chapter 29: Purgatorio V

Summary:

The stars finally meet Roswaal Mathers...

Notes:

Enjoy!

(See the end of the chapter for more notes.)

Chapter Text

Roswaal Mathers.

The greatest mage of his generation.

Master of several magical elements and considered the pioneer in recent metia innovation and has published numerous papers on new magicology.

Was currently wearing a dirty rag of a robe, covered in multiple stains, and had a beard that went down to his chest. His hair was ratty and filled with gunk and random bits of food. He was practically filthy and smelled like he hadn’t washed in weeks.

Many of the individuals in the group, besides Tia, were gob smacked by the current state of the head mage of Lugunica.

He was sitting on a log, nursing a bottle of liquor. One of several, given that there were many empty surrounding him.

Subaru gazed at the mage with genuine pity, “You look awful.”

Roswaal took a long sip. “…And you are trespassing. It seems we both can point out the obvious.”

Roswaal glanced to the side, his eyes slightly widening, “It seems this is where you have been, Beatrice. Has your journey for self-fulfillment found fruit or have you returned to join us as fellow failures?”

Beatrice gazed at the clown, her eyes sullen, “Betty has…”

Her eyes darted to Subaru quickly before returning back to Roswaal, “Betty has found her person.”

The clown looked genuinely surprised, “…Well, how surprising. I am happy for you Beatrice. Truly. At the very least, you have found your way despite all that has happened. Perhaps Teacher has not forsaken us, after all.”

Anastasia’s mind was trying to rapidly connect the dots. Subaru had been incredibly vague about his relationship with Roswaal. Only that Roswaal was obsessed with a witch and had been at odds with the rest of the Emilia camp, once upon a time. However, this was apparently all resolved before Priestella, and the clown was considered a staunch ally. Subaru even stated that Roswaal was someone he can trust.

Though Subaru’s record of ‘trustable allies’ has always been questionable, me included.

Roswaal bowed slightly, “Well then, let me introduce myself, though it seems you already know me. I am Roswaal L. Mathers, current lord of the Mathers Domain and Head Mage of Lugunica. Make yourselves at home in my humble abode.”

He waved his hand at the mountain of garbage and rubble next to them.

Subaru gawked at the sight, “…Why are you here and not at your actual mansion?”

Roswaal tried to take another sip but then realized his liquor ran dry. He then shrugged, threw the empty bottle behind him, pulled out another from his robes, cut the top with a small blade of wind, and started chugging once more.

He then realized Subaru asked a question, nearly spilling, “Well, I like to come out here to reminisce and contemplate in peace.”

Subaru kept staring, “What about Ram? There’s no way she would leave you here alone.”

Roswaal stared back, “…She’s preoccupied at the moment.”

Subaru’s face morphed into shock, “You didn’t…did you?“

Roswaal’s brow furrowed, “If you’re asking me whether I have killed her or not, I haven’t. It would be a gross misunderstanding for me to be so cruel for no reason. I’ve been simply giving her errands. Constantly.”

Roswaal’s eyes were now intensely analyzing Subaru, something Anastasia quickly noticed, she intervened immediately, “It is quite nice to meet you, Roswaal-sama. But we must be leavin’ soon. We were just droppin’ by Beatrice’s old home before makin’ our way to the next destination.”

Roswaal didn’t stop looking at Subaru, his eyes getting more manic and intense, “You haven’t answered me yet. Why are you here and how do you know me?”

Anastasia spoke, “I already-“

“No you haven’t,” the air got tense as Roswaal ignored the bottle in his hand, letting it drop to the ground, as he stood abruptly, “You don’t think I didn’t notice? The abrupt intensity of magic? The odd clothing? The presence of a Great Wind Spirit and the Admirer? Or the fact that you look like a certain Archbishop who escaped a few months back?”

That got everyone to start bracing themselves, Halibel readying several kunai behind his back and the wind beginning to howl around Tia.

“Guess the lame clown has a brain?” “Su-san, it might be time to let us handle the talkin’.”

Roswaal didn’t even glance at them, only staring at Subaru, mana beginning to concentrate around him, “But I could care less about any of that. None of that matters. What does matter, is how you know about my dear maid and your odd reaction to her whereabouts. As if the idea that I would kill her was a plausible possibility to you. As if…you knew how she and I are. Adding onto that, your relationship with Beatrice. Your odd casual tone with me…”

Anastasia readied her hand, lights starting to flicker at the tips, she grabbed Subaru’s hand, ready to leave at a moment’s notice.

Subaru gripped her hand back, softly whispering, “Calm down. I have an idea.”

She whipped her head at him, “Are you crazy?!”

He didn’t answer her, only keeping eye contact with the mage.

Joshua kept his distance, correctly deducing that his situation was completely out of his league, as Beatrice stepped forward, angrily stating, “Don’t do anything rash, I suppose.”

Roswaal ignored her, just looking forward, his mind racing, magic pouring out of his body, “…But I don’t know you. So either you have been monitoring me without my knowledge, which I am extremely doubtful. Or you have some other way of knowing me. Perhaps an ability of some kind. Or perhaps my memory has been tampered with. Either way, you cannot leave.”

Beatrice started channeling, “You-“

Subaru brought his hand out, making her look at him confused, he only shook his head before refocusing on Roswaal, “You’re putting together the pieces. Come on. Think a bit more. You’re almost there. Why exactly do I know you so well? Why did we come back to this place specifically? Why would Beako trust me so easily?”

Roswaal narrowed his eyes, deep in thought, before they widened, “…Gluttony.”

Subaru gave a solemn smile, melancholic and filled with regret, “Nice to see you again Ros-chi.”

Roswaal looked as if his brain was on fire, his eyes spacing out, “Wait a moment…if that is the case. You were probably in our camp. Which means that you had a high possibility of being there. Back then. But why would…were you…no. What if…”

Subaru spoke tersely, “Ros. Whose name is on the binding oath you made after the Sanctuary incident?”

Roswaal’s gaze locked back onto Subaru, “You know that as well. So you were there. And given Beatrice’s attachment to you, were you the reason she left the library in the first place? I always wondered-“

“Focus Ros-chi. The oath.”

Roswaal sneered, “You know exactly whose name is on the oath. That irksome pest, Otto. The man with no fate. A blank spot within my Teacher’s writings. The reason for my enslavement to such a miserable goal that has no possibility of being accomplished. Do you really expect me to-“

Subaru interrupted again, “Look at it. Check the name.”

“Why would I do that-“

“If you do, I’ll tell you how I know about Echidna,” Roswaal’s whole body began to tense, “How I know about the other witches. How you lost so easily.”

“…You can?”

“One simple look. That’s all I ask.”

Roswaal contemplated before begrudgingly accepting, “Alright, but I do not understand why you are so adamant…so…so…”

The mage’s eyes started to waver, his face becoming just as pale as it usually was with the makeup. The magic began to dissipate, his hands no longer tense but loose. His eyes were now beginning to bulge, sweat already streaming down his neck as it seemed like his mind could not comprehend what he was seeing.

Roswaal stared off into space, muttering, “Why is it blank?”

At his reaction, everyone began to calm down and instead their anxiety was replaced with confusion.

Halibel smirked, “I think ya broke him Su-san. How did ya do it?”

Subaru kept watching Roswaal, waiting, “I’ve been thinking a lot about Gluttony for the last few months. Ever since I got imprisoned. Did you know that Ram still uses her sister’s recipes? All of the written documents by Rem disappeared with her name. Yet the knowledge remained. So why wouldn’t Ram get confused about where such recipes came from?”

Anastasia understood what he was explaining, “It’s because Gluttony twisted the memories. Made it seem like she memorized them herself. Tried to connect the dots in the most plausible way for her not to question it.”

Subaru nodded, “Exactly. But that doesn’t explain why Ram still wouldn’t question certain things. Like how she was able to clean a whole mansion by herself, nearly spotless, despite her own laziness and lack of energy. For months. Or how there was a whole room filled with extra maid outfits and a mace she doesn’t use. Or the presence of a woman who looked exactly like her. Ram barely reacted to her sister falling into a coma. But imagine being in Ram’s position. Imagine finding someone who looked almost exactly like you, only with different colored hair and eyes. Wouldn’t that rub you the wrong way? Give you an existential crisis? But for some reason, she barely cared, at least until I pointed these things out to her.”

“…You think there is something more than just the loss or change of memories, that’s what you’re implying, isn’t it?” Anastasia held his hand tighter.

Subaru pursed his lips, “It’s like there is some kind of filter in their brains. As if some kind of fog now exists over those memories, making it all hazy. The filter is actively preventing them from asking the right questions or even dwelling on the absurdity of some of them. At least, until something concrete shatters that filter.”

Subaru looked towards Beatrice, who couldn’t return his gaze, keeping her eyes on the ground, she softly added, “Like Betty…”

Subaru sighed before reaching down and patting her head, “Beako. I know you blame yourself. But I don’t blame you anymore.”

“You should, in fact.”

“I don’t. Because I realized something. That filter isn’t just there to make Gluttony more insidious, it’s there to protect you.”

Beatrice finally looked up, guilt mixed with vague hope danced within her expression, “What do you mean, in fact?”

“I don’t know if it’s Gluttony or something else. But that filter keeps you from becoming a nervous wreck. Imagine realizing that everything was a lie. That your memories were completely fabricated. The mind wouldn’t be able to handle that kind of comprehension. Ignorance is preferable so the filter allows you to simply ignore the inconsistencies. It even works when you see the missing person themselves. Even if they give you good logic and reasoning, countless evidence to the contrary, they will be unable to comprehend that their memories are different.”

Beatrice began to understand, “So when Betty was faced with an undeniable fact…the contract. The filter broke, I suppose.”

Subaru kept patting her head, “And your mind panicked. Contracts, like oaths, are unable to be removed. Even if the name is gone, it seems they still remain. Ros-chi made a bet with me a year ago and I won. One of the results was that he made an oath tied to me that would force him to support Emilia’s candidacy for queendom. He even did it voluntarily, but it seems Gluttony twisted the memory towards an involuntary promise with Otto. It was probably one of the more logical ways for him to have even done such a thing without my presence.”

The others were confused by Subaru’s words, wondering why his lack of presence would change everything so much. Anastasia was not confused.

…Because without Subaru and his power, it would seem like they bumbled their way into a victory. Subaru knows how things were going to play out. But the others didn’t. At least, from Roswaal’s perspective, it seemed like the group made all of the correct decisions purely on luck. But if Roswaal was completely willing to submit to Subaru, someone who at the time was just some no-name commoner, then that means Roswaal knew Subaru was someone who he could trust.

Because he knew Subaru could time travel.

Something clicked within Anastasia’s mind, something that she would return to once their names returned. The resolution of that certain something may result in a very dead Margrave.

Subaru continued explaining, “I always thought it was odd how little we knew about Gluttony, especially if contracts are not broken by its use. Wouldn’t there be a ton of people or spirits out there with missing names in their oaths or contracts? You could argue that the Gluttony Archbishops didn’t eat anyone with contracts. But that’s bullshit. Those guys lack any kind of restraint. So my theory led to the possibility of a filter. That it not only makes it so that everyone doesn’t question their new memories, it also makes it so that people don’t even acknowledge the contract at all. It’s why Beako forgot about it so easily despite contracts being important to spirits. It’s why Ros-chi didn’t question the emptiness of his oath.”

Beatrice spoke up, her voice more relaxed and playful, reflecting Eridna’s mannerisms, “Su. If that is the case, it explains my lack of decorum during that one conversation.”

Subaru rubbed Beatrice’s head more, “Yeah, sorry about that again. I couldn’t connect the dots that time because my mind was such a mess.”

Eridna tapped his hand, “Do not apologize. We both were not in the correct headspace, technically.”

Anastasia leaned in, “Wait, what are you both talking about? What conversation?”

Subaru glanced at her and rubbed her hand with his thumb, “It was right after the fight with Tia-Two. A few days after, she and I talked. It wasn’t…pleasant.”

Anastasia wanted to ask more but was interrupted by a sudden bout of hysterical laughter. Coming straight from the clown’s mouth.

The mage was laughing to the point of tears, as they started streaming down his face. A feral grin stretched across his face as he couldn’t help but giggle like a maniac. His hands were trembling as he covered his face, as if he was trying to prevent the world from seeing his image.

Tia raised her hand, “Su. Let’s just kill this guy.”

Subaru put her hand down, “Not yet. We still need him for now.”

The laughter finally died down as Roswaal’s hands fell to his side, his eyes were red and puffy, but they looked more alive than ever before, focused solely on the star in front of him, “Subaru…you were the one who defeated me. Weren’t you?”

Subaru looked down, as if contemplating, before responding, “Yes and no. It wasn’t just because of me that you lost.”

“Irrelevant,” the clown chuckled once again but stifled it just as quickly, “Yes, yes, I know. The others all had their moments or whatever but you. You! Youuuuuuuuu.”

Halibel side-eyed Beatrice, “Is dis guy always so creepy or is dis just an off day for ‘em?”

Beatrice sighed, “He has always been like this, I suppose. Ever since he fell in love with my mother and spent four hundred years body hopping like the world’s most disgusting parasite.”

“Yep, yep, I guess dat makes sense.”

Halibel nodded as the logic was sound.

His eyes then popped open, and he turned his head towards Beatrice, “Wait what did you just say?”

Beatrice ignored him as she watched her pseudo-brother act like he was witnessing her Mother for the first time, again.

Roswaal pointed at Subaru, “YOU! You were the key. The lynchpin. The catalyst. You were the reason why everything worked out so perfectly. It all makes sense now!”

Anastasia glanced at Subaru, “Are you sure this was a good idea?”

Subaru smiled, “Just give him a minute,” he then reoriented himself towards Roswaal, “Why do you think that?”

Roswaal studied Subaru before answering, “You lack any sort of physical attributes that could challenge my magical capabilities. Perhaps you are a mage of a higher caliber or perhaps…”

Roswaal’s eyes drifted towards Beatrice and Tia, both spirit’s cocking their heads and lifting one eyebrow at his gaze, he smiled as if the picture was all coming together, “You are a Spirit Art’s user. A very skilled one at that, given how you not only seem to have contracted with Beatrice but also the Great Wind Spirit of Murder.”

Tia narrowed her eyes at him, “Have I met you before?”

Roswaal chuckled, “Not me. But Teacher has. She described you as a malevolent ball of pure rage and malice. A murderous reaper that’s bloodlust could not be sated no matter how many bodies you threw at her. Well, at least until now.”

Tia responded by unleashing some of said bloodlust out into the open, “Just be glad Su doesn’t want you dead.”

Roswaal barely blinked despite the wrath of the Spirit brushing over him, only staring straight at Subaru.

Throughout all of these interactions, Anastasia kept her face passive, but her mind was beginning to unravel what exactly was about to happen.

He’s assuming a lot. Trying to exactly pinpoint Subaru’s expertise. Some of this seems to be him genuinely figuring out what Subaru’s role was in everything, and the other half is testing the waters. He’s trying to bait out info from Subaru’s reactions.

Unfortunately, Subaru’s face was ironclad, not one single accidental emotion was leaked out. Not even from the beginning of this whole encounter.

Subaru simply nodded along to Roswaal’s assumptions, “You’re not wrong.”

Roswaal’s brows furrowed, “But I am not exactly right either. You have more than just brute strength under your belt. Perhaps I am looking at a genuine tactician.”

Subaru laughed, “You’re flattering me too much. Get to the point Ros-chi. You’re obviously using all of this as a precursor to your real theory.”

Roswaal smirked, “You…have an Authority, don’t you.”

“Two in fact,” as Subaru lifted up two fingers, Anastasia and Beatrice followed Subaru’s lead, keeping their expressions tight, “You could say they were they were partially the reason why I was able to gain the upper hand against you.”

Roswaal’s eyes danced with pure glee, “That’s how the book was defeated. It was not because of some pointless drivel like ‘pure luck’ or some insanity like ‘the magic of friendship!’ You have the power to literally change fate, you must!”

Subaru closed his eyes, smiling like a cheshire cat, “You could say that.”

“No wonder I admitted defeat so easily. Unlike the book, which only gives me vague preparations towards my goal, you are more definite. If someone was on our side, someone with the ability to redirect all routes towards our final destination, then I would have gladly placed all of my bets on such a person. Why bother when a jackpot is all but predetermined? My behavior during the last year…of course I would have been so complacent. There was nothing to worry about. Nothing at all. But then why…?”

Roswaal’s voice drifted off as confusion settled in, Subaru took the initiative, “Why would I, someone with the ability to change fate, decide to get their name consumed and be treated as an Archbishop? Why indeed Ros-chi?”

Roswaal thought for a moment before snapping his fingers, “You planned this. All of this. That’s the only logical conclusion.”

Subaru didn’t acknowledge anything, just continuing to smile.

Anastasia tried her best not to have her eye twitch.

Subaru replied, “I’ll be honest, not everything has gone to plan. I was originally going to return at a later date, when the time was right. I didn’t even expect to find you here. But the circumstances are forcing my hand. I’ll need your help Ros-chi.”

Roswaal raised an eyebrow, “Something even you can’t change with your Authority?”

Subaru shook his head, “Getting things back to how they should be is my main priority right now. Something is happening at the Sage’s Tower and it’s not looking pretty. I think Gluttony is making the rounds there as we speak. Tell me Ros-chi, how many people in the Iron Fang joined Julius and Otto on the expedition?”

Roswaal raised an eyebrow, “The Iron Fang? I wasn’t aware any of them were still in Lugunica.”

Subaru winced, “Shit. Ana-pop? Roll call?”

Anastasia gripped his hand, “Julius…”

Subaru pinched his nose bridge, “I’ve wasted enough time. Ros-chi, I need you to help us get to the Augria Sand Dunes as quickly as possible. Is there any way you can do that?”

Roswaal hummed at the request for a just a moment before responding, “I may have an idea, but we will need to return to my mansion. There is someone there that can provide you with what you need. For the right price.”

Subaru didn’t hesitate, “We’ll take it. Let’s go now. Time is of the essence.”

The clown didn’t argue, leaving his bottles behind and pointing towards the gates of his old home, “While I flew here by myself, there should be some workers nearby that can provide a carriage. They’ve been slowly removing all of the burnt rubble over the last year, so they should have a spare earth dragon. Let us make post-haste.”

He walked forward letting the group follow along cautiously.

Anastasia prodded Subaru’s hand with three pinches, a silent message.

“We need to talk. Something feels suspicious.”

Subaru pinched three times back.

He then used his free hand to head pat Beatrice one more time, poking her head three times as well.

Beatrice had already learned their silent communication techniques and promptly put up an El Silen barrier around the group.

Anastasia immediately voiced her concerns, “I don’t trust him. He’s been way too cooperative. Even if you think otherwise, my instincts are telling me that he has something up his sleeve. Either he is waiting for an opportunity or this is all a trap.”

Subaru nodded and glanced towards Beatrice, “Beako, what do you think?”

Beatrice folded her arms across her chest, “Betty knows the clown well enough that he is probably scheming something. If not now, he will definitely try something later at home, in fact.”

Subaru sighed, “My thoughts exactly. To be honest, this is all just a gamble. I’m banking on Ros being so desperate for a way forward, that he would try to help me, believing this would further his plans as well.”

Anastasia walked closer to Subaru, “And if the gamble fails? If he realizes that we are more desperate for his help than he is of ours?”

Subaru let go of Anastasia’s hand and wrapped his arm around her body, holding her close as they walked, “Then I’ll do whatever it takes to get him on our side.”

A part of Anastasia felt relieved by Subaru’s words while the other felt immense guilt.

In Subaru’s embrace, her body was covered in warmth, bolstering the relief.

Despite that,

Whatever it takes, huh…

Tia shrugged as Halibel took a puff from his kiseru,

“I’ll just threaten to cut his family jewels off.” “Worst case scenario, ya just have me aim a kunai at his balls.”

Tia and Halibel turned towards each other in surprise, before nodding in solemn agreement for clown-related castration.

Beatrice nodded while petting Eridna on her neck, “Betty will make sure the clown doesn’t ever reproduce again. This will be the end of the Mathers bloodline, in fact.”

Anastasia giggled, some of the guilt being relieved by the group’s banter, “Okay, okay. I’ll trust you guys to take the lead if all else fails.”
Subaru held her tighter, “We’ll save your family. I promise.”

…My new family helps save my old one. I’m truly blessed.

A tender moment for the Banan group.

Meanwhile, Joshua walked along beside all of them, within the bubble of El Silen, thoroughly horrified by their explicit plans.

He muttered to himself, “Brother, I may have joined a group of utter psychopaths…”

Hopefully, the cost Roswaal mentioned won’t be too steep.

-------------------------

“To reach the Sage’s Tower, you must give up something you cherish the most.”

 

Perhaps not.

Notes:

EN: If you haven't already guessed, Gluttony works a little differently here. This...filter is what I thought of to explain some of the more confusing aspects of Re:Forgotten's premise.

Chapter 30: Purgatorio VI

Summary:

Subaru and Anastasia have a little talk while traveling to the mansion...

Chapter Text

Roswaal was able to persuade some of the construction workers to lend them a carriage and an earth dragon. Subaru and Anastasia sat inside with Joshua and Beatrice while Halibel distracted Roswaal from the front and Tia sat on top, speeding up the carriage’s velocity using wind magic. They turned off the earth dragon’s Divine Protection so that Tia can actively control the carriage and dragon herself.

“Beako, you mind giving me and Ana-pop some space?”

Beatrice was about to cast the spell when Joshua shuddered and exclaimed, “I-I won’t say a single word of what happens in this carriage! Please don’t throw me out!”

Subaru squinted at Joshua, “…Dude. We’re not yakuza or anything. I just want to have a private conversation with my fiancé. Beako will talk to you while we’re busy. She won’t bite.”

Beatrice eyed the boy beside her while sighing and casting the spell, “If you bother me or do anything funny, Betty will actually throw you out this carriage, in fact.”

Subaru couldn’t hear Joshua’s response, but the boy’s horrified expression spoke volumes. Subaru face palmed, “Beako. Come on, I said don’t scare the kid.”

He then focused on the beautiful woman beside him, his lover, the most important person in his life, Anastasia Hoshin.

The same Anastasia Hoshin who was currently fidgeting in her seat and not making eye contact with him.

“Ana-pop?” Subaru scooted closer to her as she flinched, “Is everything alright?”

“…Yeah, I’m fine.”

Shit. It must be worse than I thought.

He originally planned on leaving her in Banan with Eridna, he didn’t want to risk her breaking down when they would most likely be going into imminent danger. But somehow, whether because of Tia or otherwise, she managed to pull herself together in some capacity. A part of him still wanted her somewhere safe. But the other part knew she would never accept that.

Because she never did before.

Subaru wrapped his arm around her and rubbed her head while pulling her close, “…You know, I’m pretty scared myself.”

He felt her tense up and immediately grab his other hand, she spoke softly, “Is it because of Emilia?”

Subaru hummed.

…Surprisingly, no. Yes and no. But that’s not what I’m particularly scared of.

He felt the carriage jump and tousle as it accelerated into speeds it was never used to. It was surprisingly easy to convince Tia to reduce the wind resistance of the whole carriage to almost zero, allowing it to go Mach 6 with some added propulsion from her magic. Subaru felt slightly disturbed by how easily Tia agreed to things nowadays. Maybe she wasn’t joking about nuking Lugunica.

Anyways, not important. What was important, was getting to the bottom of his fiancé’s troubles.

Subaru finally answered, “Ha, well, not really.”

Anastasia nestled her head into the crook of his neck, right at home as always, “Why? I thought…wouldn’t you be…at least a little sad?”

Subaru rubbed his cheek into her hair, “Why would I, when I have you?”

That didn’t seem to have the intended effect as he felt her shudder, Subaru raised an eyebrow, pulling her closer and asking, “What’s wrong? Did I say something wrong?”

Anastasia didn’t speak for a few moments, making his anxiety start to slowly rise.

She then spoke in a stilted manner, “I just…I don’t…”

You don’t…what? Did I do something wrong?

She took a deep breath, “Why? Why don’t you feel anything for her anymore? It hasn’t been that long. And, I get it, why am I so interested in this? Shouldn’t I want you to get over her as quickly as possible? But it’s just…I don’t…”

I-what? I don’t understand. Where is this coming from?

For once, Anastasia began to fumble her words as Subaru couldn’t follow her train of logic or thought. But innately, he had some understanding.

She must be confused why I got over Emilia and Rem so fast. Is that why she’s been acting so weird?

…No, it can’t be. Her reactions are too extreme.

Must be something else. Something more sinister.

Pushing down possible theories, he focused on what was in front of him, he spoke with a tone that was equal parts nostalgic as it was lethargic, “If you want to know why, it’s really simple. I moved on.”

“…How could you move on so fast?”

“Because I can’t hold onto possible futures that might never happen.”

Anastasia scoffed, “But…you loved her. Emilia. Rem. Both of them.”

Subaru frowned.

Why does that matter to you? Do you think I would leave you just as quickly?

“But my love died,” he noticed Anastasia shifted uncomfortably and sighed, “Ana. That’s not going to happen with you.”

She froze and slowly turned her head towards him, “What?”

Subaru stared at her, full eye contact, “I love you. And that’s never going to change.”

Anastasia stared back at him for a full five seconds before blushing, “I-what?”

Subaru didn’t even blink, continuing, “You probably think I’m going to do the same thing to you. Move on without a care in the world. But that’s not going to happen. I know it seems like this came out of nowhere but my love for them was real. I loved Emilia. I loved Rem. I imagined my whole life with them. I pledged my life for them. I would have done anything in my life for both of them.”

“Subaru-“

“But I didn’t move on because I found a new person. I didn’t move on because I got bored-“

“Subaru!” She interrupted him immediately, his eyes squinted in confusion as she held his hand tightly, “I didn’t…I didn’t mean that. I know. You would never move on without good reason. And I know. You aren’t going to leave me.”

Subaru still couldn’t understand, “Then…what’s the problem?”

“The problem is….is…” her voice trailed off as her eyes wavered, her body was shaking.

“Ana? Ana what’s wrong-“

“The problem is me!” Anastasia awkwardly yelled, her voice breaking.

Subaru’s jaw dropped as he couldn’t comprehend what she just said. Those words. Individually he understood them. All together? Not comprehensible.
