Subaru stared at her incredulously, “What?”

Anastasia’s voice became a whisper as she could no longer look into his eyes, her gaze quickly darting down at their conjoined hands, “I’m…not good for you. I’m not. I-I realized that.”

That’s. I. What?!

“Ana-pop, you’re completely fine.”

“I’m not. Please!” She shouted as she saw him open his mouth, “I know what you’re going to say. That I’m fine…but I’m not. Because at the end of the day our relationship is too unbalanced.”

Unbalanced? You do so much for me. Am I not doing enough?

“…What do you mean?”

Anastasia looked as if the words were being choked out of her, “I haven’t given you anything. But you’ve given me everything. I’ve realized that now. All this time, you’ve been following me selfishly. Us building a company. Moving to Banan. Living our lives there. All of it was selfish on my part. I should have…did more for you. I didn’t. I didn’t think of a way for you to reunite with your camp. I didn’t think of a way to help clear your name. And I didn’t think of how to help you at all. I…owe you so much. So I want to help you. Whether it is talking with Emilia or Rem or whoever, just to get some closure. Or maybe even just to get everything settled. I’ll do it. Whatever it takes. I’ll be there for you.”

“…”

“…”

The silence crept in as Subaru processed her words.

The silence was immediately kicked out with two simple words.

Subaru spoke them bluntly, “That’s stupid!”

He threw his hands up in the air, as Anastasia almost leaped back in her seat.

Subaru pointed his finger at her and spouted, “Is that what has been going on in your head this entire time?! You think you owe me something? That I’ve been constantly giving and giving and you’ve been just taking? You know how utterly stupid that is right?!”

Anastasia was bewildered by his reaction, automatically responding, “But it’s true! You’ve done so much for me this entire time! Haven’t you?!”

Subaru held back his wince as he remembered the countless loops and deaths he experienced during his time in Banan. He regretted not a single one of them.

“Sure, I have! I’ve done a lot but so have you!” Before Anastasia could retort, Subaru lifted up his fingers, “One, you took me in when you had absolutely no reason to trust me. Two, you constantly looked after me mentally and emotionally. Don’t even argue that it doesn’t count! I was a complete wreck back then and I only recovered because of you! Three, you were the one who taught me so much about negotiation and how to talk to people.”

He finally lifted his fourth finger, “And four: I’m an idiot and you’re super smart!”

“…” Anastasia was absolutely flabbergasted, her eyes bulging at his last statement, “What kind of answers are those! One, I was taking advantage of you! Two, of course I didn’t want someone who is an emotional wreck, I can’t do anything with that! Three, I barely taught you anything, you learned way too quickly! And four: how the hell is you being an idiot related to this?!”

Subaru started shouting back, “Who cares if you were taking advantage of me?! You barely did. Honestly you were probably lying to yourself that whole time, you absolute tsundere! And you didn’t have to take care of me so well! You kept checking up on me! That’s going above and beyond! Also, maybe you’re just a really skilled teacher, ever thought of that! Finally, I am stupid! I need someone to help me because I’m so stupid! I can barely do anything by myself, even with trial and error. YOU’RE THE REASON I PROBABLY HAVEN’T DIED BY NOW!”

For some reason, that set Anastasia off, “That’s bullshit and you know it!”

------------------------------

Meanwhile, Beatrice and Joshua were sitting outside the El Silen bubble, awkwardly trying to pass the time. Beatrice was reading a book, slowly reading each page before turning so Eridna could also read, while Joshua fidgeted in his seat glancing everywhere. His eyes finally settled back on the two stars, widening slightly.

“Um, Beako-sama?”

Beatrice turned a page without looking up, “Betty told you not to call me that, I suppose.”

Joshua flinched, “Uh, but you told me not to call you Betty.”

Beatrice sighed, “…Just Beatrice, in fact.”

“My apologies, Beatrice-sama.”

Beatrice turned another page, “So what is it, in fact?”
Joshua pointed forward, “I believe—apologies if I am misunderstanding this— but are Anastasia-sama and Subaru-sama…alright?”

Beatrice still didn’t look up, though her eyes noticeably became slightly tense, concentrating on the book more, “Betty believes they will be fine. Anastasia is simply having…problems that need to be resolved internally rather than externally. Subaru cannot help with that. However, when the girl finally figures everything out. They will be fine. Betty believes so, in fact.”

Sister. You should talk to him as well.

Betty will. It’s just…not now. Anastasia needs him more right now, in fact.

“I see. Well, I guess I am unaware of how romance and partnerships are supposed to progress. As I was never aware it involved a lot of grappling.”

Beatrice blinked once.

Then twice.

And then three more times.

She then slowly turned her head towards Joshua who was still pointing forward.

She then finally looked at the El Silen bubble and did a double take.

They were indeed grappling each other.

Violently.

Both stars yelled at each other without any noise coming from their lips. Beatrice could barely tell what they were saying just from lip movement, and she counted several expletives.

“Beatrice-sama,” Joshua stared as Anastasia put Subaru in a headlock, “Is this normal?”

“…Yes it is, in fact,” Beatrice sighed as she pinched her nose.

------------------------------

“STOP BEING AN IDIOT!” Subaru exclaimed while getting put in a headlock by Anastasia.

Anastasia screamed back, while getting her cheeks pulled by Subaru, “SAYS THE IDIOT! ADMIT I’M TERRIBLE!”
Subaru struggled but her flimsy arms were unable to choke him effectively at all, “NEVER! YOU’RE SO GOOD TO ME! WHY IN THE WORLD WOULD YOU EVER THINK THAT?!”

“BECAUSE I’M WORTHLESS!”

Subaru froze.

He felt moisture hit his hair.

Subaru stopped pinching her cheeks as he looked up at her, tears slowly dripping from her eyes, “Ana-pop…”

She stopped trying to choke him, bringing an arm to her face and rubbing her eyes, the tears weren’t stopping, “Shut up… Just. Shut. Up. You’re so kind to me. So nice. So loving. I’m worth none of that.”

The words felt so familiar to him.

Because he used to say those exact same words all the time.

…I gave her this, didn’t I? Basilisk Ops. It gave her that.

His self-hatred.

His lack of self-esteem.

His uselessness.

That must have been considered a ‘burden’ by the contract.

He felt his insides twist. Perhaps…that was why he felt so odd nowadays.

He felt confident in ways he did not expect. At first, Subaru believed it was just because the worst was over. That nothing else could faze him. And maybe it was a part of that. Or maybe it was all a consequence of losing that self-hatred.

Subaru brought his hand back to Anastasia’s face, her arm lowering and slowly revealing the teary eyed merchant, sniffling above him. Her cheek felt so warm, pink and covered in tear stains. Each and every time he saw her. He couldn’t help but fall in love with her looks, again and again.

How soft her face felt to the touch. How her eyes sparkled like sapphires. How her hair glowed under the sunlight. How he couldn’t help but stare at her constantly. How could someone with such incredibly beautiful aspects ever think of themselves badly? That she was worthless? How could she ever believe such a lie was true?

…Perhaps he was a hypocrite.

Subaru asked a prominent question on his mind, “Ana. Do you love me?”

Her eyes widened, her face was etched with pure outrage, “Of course, I love you! What kind of question is that?!”

Subaru smiled warmly, caressing her cheek, “I don’t ever doubt that. But if that’s the case, why do you not deserve the love I have for you?”

Her eyes wandered, not willing to look at him directly, only responding by grasping his arm with both hands and leaning into his palm, her eyes finally closing, “…Because that would mean I was someone who had done something worthwhile. Something that deserved such love.”

She trembled in his hand, whispering, “I’ve done nothing. Absolutely nothing.”

He frowned at her words, “Ana-pop. You don’t have to do anything for my love.”

She didn’t open her eyes, “But I want to…I want to do something for you.”

“That isn’t what I want though. I never needed something from you in the first place.”

Anastasia wasn’t listening just holding onto his arm like it was a lifeline, “I’ll do it. I’ll find a way. I promise.”

Subaru felt his heart squeeze. It reminded him of something. A blast from the past. Around a year ago. At the capital.

“Ana-“

He was interrupted as he felt the carriage suddenly stop and the bubble pop, the rush of sound from outside coming in all at once. He heard the screech of the earth dragon as their claws grinded to a halt, the carriage itself tumbling and cracking from how much force it was put through in the last half hour.

His gaze wandered to the side as he saw Beatrice look at both of them with concern. Joshua was awkwardly holding his hands to his ears and not even looking at the two. It seems the young lad was trying his best to give them space in his own ways.

Beatrice calmly stated, “We have arrived at the mansion. You both should get ready.”

Before he could react, Anastasia let go of his arm and turned away from him, evidently trying to wipe away the tears that have become so common for him to see in the past few days.

Subaru got to his feet and began double checking that all of his essentials were still with him. However, his gaze kept wandering towards Anastasia.

The door opened before he could say anything more, Halibel’s voice rang out clearly, “Yup, yup. Come on out y’all. Time’s a tickin’ and we got places to be.”

Beatrice leaped out of her seat and tugged on Joshua’s sleeve, allowing the boy to finally open his eyes and ears. He looked around vaguely before settling on the two stars, waving awkwardly at Subaru.

Subaru couldn’t help but chuckle at the poor kid, obviously out of his depth and only tagging along because the Admirer suggested him to come with them. One couldn’t really argue with an over six-foot wolf demi-human who could easily make you disappear without even thinking.

Beatrice exited the carriage with Joshua in tow.

Anastasia was about to step out, but Subaru stopped her, grabbing her hand as she finally looked at him. She still radiated an odd sense of desperation, only making eye contact for a second before her eyes shifted away.

Something began to gnaw at the pit of his gut.

A vague of sense of dread crept in.

He needed to say these words before anything else.

“Ana. I love you. I will always love you. I will never stop loving you. So please. Stop. You don’t have to pay me back.”

Anastasia stood there, motionless, staring at him, her lips wavering. She finally forced a small smile, “…I know.”

She smiled at him, eyes closed.

Despite her words, he didn’t feel that much better.

 

Subaru finally stepped off the carriage, helping Anastasia down the steps. The carriage was almost completely run down, battered from Tia pushing it to the limits. The earth dragon looked absolutely winded. They were in front of the Mather’s mansion in Costuul, out in the courtyard. His vision wandered, settling on every familiar detail.

He could see the vague outline of the parkour obstacle course that he and Garfiel built together.

He could see the flowers that he and Ram planted together, blooming in the distance.

He could see the small outhouse where Frederica and him used to hang out around and eat sweets without the others knowing.

He could see the swing set he built for Petra.

He could see the path to the forest where he and Emilia would sometimes go for dates.

He could see Rem’s room, the morningstar that he used to polish every day reflecting sunlight through the window.

He could see the window where Otto’s office sat, where he would often bother the poor advisor whenever possible.

He could see the uneven dirt caused by Roswaal’s magical experiments on the courtyard grass.

He could see the gardens that he and Beatrice would frolic and play in.

He could see the grassy hill where everyone sat, admiring the night sky, on the day they made a star for him. On his birthday, which was just a few weeks away.

Home. The home he missed so much. He was back. Finally.

He had longed for this day.

To return.

To be reunited with everyone.

He missed them so much.

And yet, today was not for them.

In the future, he’ll be back at that grassy hill, talking and bantering with everyone.

Subaru felt Anastasia’s hand still closed around his, rubbing his thumb with hers. She said nothing, giving him space. He tightened his grasp.

…I’m already home.

It’s time to save those closest to his home.

He walked across the courtyard with everyone, he and Anastasia were at the back with Tia, Beatrice, and Halibel surrounding the pair, watching all around them. Roswaal was way ahead of them, walking with unusual fervor and gusto. As if he was on a mission.

They reached the mansion, the head mage threw open the doors and strolled straight down the hallways, the rest followed suit.

Tia and Halibel looked around, analyzing the area. Beatrice strutted without care, her eyes wandering every once in a while. Joshua nervously walked right behind the stars.

The two bodyguards slowed their pace, protecting the group from the back.

Tia scoffed, “I like our home in Banan better. This place sucks.”

Halibel chuckled, “What’s got ya so disgruntled? This is a noble’s house. Ya can’t get finer digs than this.”

The wind spirit waved her hand nonchalantly in the air, a lantern and vase near her shattered into pieces, “It’s not cozy. The walls feel all close. The lighting is lame. I hate it.”

Halibel lit his kiseru again, smoking it eagerly, “Ah come on, it’s Su-san’s old home. We gotta be courteous. Don’t act out so blatantly.”

He puffed the kiseru and let the smoke drift out all over the hallway. Usually, he would use the scentless medicinal versions. However, today he was using incredibly smelly herbs. The ones that stuck to fabrics and materials for years. And you can’t wash out no matter how much you tried.

“Tia. Hal.”

The spirit and Admirer turned their heads to Subaru, only seeing the back of his head as Johsua awkwardly looked back and forth between the bodyguards and their wards.

Subaru didn’t look back, but his tone was stern, “Stop it.”

The two blinked before both of them side eyed and clicked their tongues, “Tch.”

“Sorry Su.” “I’ll stop Su-san.”

Tia waved her finger in the air and the shattered objects clumped together in a ball and sat near the wall while Halibel snuffed out his pipe.

Anastasia looked around, her vision taking everything in, as if constantly searching for something.

Subaru thought it was adorable.

Even when she’s acting weird, Ana is still Ana. She’s probably trying to find some kind of hidden bit of info or trying to memorize the place in case something goes wrong.

Subaru’s staring must have caught her attention as they locked eyes, making her glance away before looking back shyly, “What?”

Subaru smiled at her with fondness radiating from every inch of his face, “Just admiring how cute my fiancé is.”

Anastasia blushed bright red before looking away and squeezing his hand softly, “…Thanks.”

Subaru’s smile slightly drooped.

It’s cute. But usually, she would say something snarky or try to pinch me. Or even just try to make me blush back.

He felt a tug from his other hand and looked down.

Beatrice was holding his finger gently with her small hand, not looking at him but just staring ahead.

He smiled as he wrapped his whole hand around hers. She wouldn’t look at him, but he could tell she was smiling.

His heart warmed back up.

Well, at least Beako is getting a bit better. She was finally talking to me back at the temple. Still stuttering one-on-one. But better than before.

His thoughts stopped as Roswaal entered his office, everyone crowding around the door and looking in.

He saw two people inside: a maid he didn’t recognize and Clind.

The two barely reacted to the Margrave’s presence but Subaru could see the slightest bit of surprise from the maid, her eye’s shifting slightly and focusing on the group for just a half second before focusing on her master.

The maid’s voice spoke with poise and careful wording, “Roswaal-sama. Welcome back. Should I notify the staff to arrange a meal for you? Or would you like to join the others in the dining hall?”

Anastasia’s hand tightened around his. He held it just as tightly back.

I’m not leaving you. I promise.

Roswaal’s voice bellowed, “Sylphy-chan. Tell the others that I have a meeting with some…old friends. Let no one bother us for the next hour, we have business to discuss and time is precious.”

She bowed gently, “At your command, Roswaal-sama.”

She walked towards the door and passed everyone, her eyes flickering between Subaru and Anastasia for a brief second before leaving.

Subaru cocked his head. She seems familiar but I can’t put a finger on why.

“Subaru, come right in. Close the door behind you please.”

The group funneled in, the door slamming shut just as Joshua finally squeezed in. Roswaal was now lounging behind his desk, his elbows on the desk and his head resting on his hands. The man was smiling ear to ear, a genuine smile that made Subaru shudder.

Subaru walked up to the mage, “Alright, so why did you bring us here? Is there a magical device or something that can help us get to the Tower quickly?”

Roswaal gestured to Clind, who stood smiling right behind his master, “Not exactly magical. Clind here has a power that can transport you all to the Augria Sand Dunes in an instant, close to the tower’s entrance. This shouuuuuld solve your little travel predicament.”

Subaru perked up, “That’s great! Let’s get this show on the road then!”

Internally, Subaru had questions.

What’s the catch Ros-chi? I know you’re thinking of something here. Come on. What do you want out of this?

“Not so fast Subaru,” the black star internally rolled his eyes, the clown didn’t care to notice Subaru’s disgruntlement and continued speaking, “Don’t you think such a loyal ally such as myself deserves a rewaaaaaard.”

Subaru’s eyes hardened, narrowing onto the clown, “What is that you want?”

Roswaal laughed sincerely, “Straight to the point are we? You are already proving to be much more fun than dear Otto~. But I digress, what I want is simple: a promise.”

Subaru raised an eyebrow, “A contract? Like an oath?”

“If that is necessary, though your word is simply enough. I can already tell that you aren’t the type to betray your promises. All I need from you…is to accomplish my dream. Help me. Truly, help me. So that I may accomplish my goal and finally revive my dear Teacher. And if you do that…Clind’s power is yours.”

Subaru scoffed, “You’re seriously trying to negotiate now?”

I don’t blame you. I would probably do the same.

Roswaal shrugged, “It seems your time in Kararagi hasn’t changed you. You haven’t obtained that mercantile spirit yet it seems. Please, Subaru. I would be an idiot not to take advantage of the situation. You give me what I want. And I’ll give you all the support you need. A fair trade I must say.”

“Tch,” Subaru clicked his tongue.

This is reasonable. I knew Ros-chi would probably try this, though I’m kind of surprised how blunt he is here. Guess he really is that desperate. Can’t believe my absence would hurt him this badly.

Subaru already considered this as a possibility. He was already ready to take the offer, but he needed to make sure this was the only offer. A contract or oath was fine; he’ll figure a way out later. Anything more that bound him was not.

Subaru gave a faux glare at Roswaal, “I always hated this about you, Ros-chi.”

Roswaal smirked, “You are not the only one~.”

Subaru rolled his eyes and gritted his teeth, “Fine I’ll-“

“I’ll take the oath,” Anastasia stepped forward, letting go of Subaru’s hand, alarming him incredibly.

WHAT?!

“Oh~? It seems your lover has more courage than you, my dear Subaru.”

Subaru’s eyes darted back and forth between Anastasia and Roswaal. He then steeled his expression and walked forward, holding his hand on her back and smiling proudly, “Well I can’t just let her take it alone, we’ll both do it.”

Meanwhile, Subaru’s fingers were silently communicating with her.

“What are you doing?! I had a plan! You don’t need to do this! Stop. Stand back.”
Subaru kept inputting messages into Anastasia’s back. Messages that she was ignoring given that she chose to keep her own hands firmly at her side.

Externally, he was smiling sunshine. Internally, Subaru was sweating bullets and questioning what Anastasia was planning.

Roswaal clapped his hands, “Excellent. Now that we have that settled, we can continue to consider the most important topic: the cost of transportation.”

Subaru and Anastasia both raised an eyebrow at him, the merchant asking, “The cost?”

Roswaal smiled maliciously, “You don’t think such an incredible feat of teleportation would come without a cooooooost?”

Roswaal snapped his fingers as Clind stepped forward, his expression not changing once. The butler spoke politely, “My ability allows me to compress the distance between one point and another, effectively allowing you to experience instant teleportation. Unfortunately, such power requires you to give something in return. It can be physical, mental, emotional, or conceptual. As long as it is something you value. To reach the Sage’s Tower, you must give up something you cherish the most.”

Subaru’s neurons fired.

I don’t like that. What’s the exact requirements?

Before he could ask any questions, Anastasia spoke quickly, “Do we all have to give something up individually? Or can one take the burden for everyone?”

Clind hummed, “Hmm, you should be able to do either. Depending on what you relinquish, one person may bear the majority of the burden.”

Subaru’s heart stopped. The gut feeling he had was roaring from below. He knew what was about to happen. Despair was clawing at him. He needed to stop her right now.

“Ana-“

She didn’t even hesitate, stepped forward even more, her eyes slightly manic, “I’ll bear everything, I’ll pay the cost. For everyone. I’ll give everything up.”

He reached his hand out to her.

Subaru felt goosebumps. Everything was spinning. His throat closed in on itself.

Not because of what she just said. But because of her next words:

“My body, my emotions, my future…even my love. Take it.”

Chapter 31: Please Don't Leave Me Alone

Summary:

Subaru confronts Anastasia...

Chapter Text

“Oi, Ana, what the fuck are you-“

“Tia. Not now. I’ll do it.”

“Su-“

“Tia,” Subaru’s eyes were cold as he locked onto the Spirit’s gaze, “Please.”

The spirit stood quietly before finally acquiescing.

Subaru sighed before pinching his nose bridge, he then finally spoke, “What do you think you’re doing?!”

Subaru’s voice echoed through the room. He was furious. The second Anastasia proclaimed what she would do, Subaru immediately asked for a ‘timeout’ so they could discuss things properly. Funny enough, Roswaal easily obliged and handed them the room next door. Which Beatrice and Tia immediately scoured for any sort of magic, just in case the clown was trying to eavesdrop. Some quick spells to dampen the noise and they were ready for a shouting match.

Anastasia calmly talked back, “Listen. There is not much I can do, at least in relation to combat. If we are going to ‘pay the cost,’ it’s better that I take the frontload of it.”

“That’s bullshit!” Subaru couldn’t control himself, anger coursing through his veins, “What would be the point of this then?! Your health and safety matters more than just a quick teleportation spell or some shit. You didn’t even barter with him. We don’t even know the exact parameters of the cost! Didn’t you tell me to always think before speaking?! Are you even thinking at all at this point?!”

Anastasia’s face was steel, her merchant mask fully back on, “…I’ve calculated all the necessary risks. This will be better for the long run. Think about this rationally: we barely have any time, and we can’t just slow down our pace by trying to ask unnecessary questions. The more we try to find a loophole, the more time is wasted. It’s better to simply choose a necessary sacrifice and continue on our journey.”

This isn’t like her. Not at all.
Subaru stared at her with increasing horror dawning on his face, “A necessary sacrifice? Is that how you see yourself? You haven’t thought at all, have you? This…you…”

Subaru grasped his face, as if trying to figure out the absolute absurdity of this situation, he muttered to himself, “I shouldn’t have brought you…”

Anastasia’s eye twitched, “I would have forced myself along anyway-“

“No, I should have knocked you out and tied you down in Banan,” Subaru’s eyes were blazing as he walked over to her, “You are not thinking rationally, despite whatever arguments you’re probably scavenging for in your head. You are not paying the cost. You are going to stay here and wait until we return and that is final.”

Anastasia’s eyes narrowed, her mask cracking, “You can’t just expect me to accept that. Treating me like some piece of cargo or some…pet that needs to be kept on a short leash.”

Subaru shook his head, “You’re not changing my mind. Don’t think I didn’t notice you’re using that inflammatory wording with me. This isn’t up for debate. You’re not mentally or emotionally well.”

It cracked even further, “You don’t understand…this isn’t just about me. We have an opportunity here to fully get rid of Gluttony. We can solve our missing name problems! We can get our lives back. Why risk us being weaker? I’m the weakest link…it won’t cause any issues.”

Subaru stared at her, “Your body, your future, your love. What did you mean by those?”

She couldn’t look him in the eyes, “…”

“…What. Did. You. Mean?”

She still couldn’t look, only glancing at the floor, hands gripped at her sides, “…Isn’t it obvious?”

“We just got your Od stabilized. You want to undo all that?”

“…”

“Our company. Our ability to make money. That too?”

“…”

“…You’re love for me? Is it worth that little to you?”

“No!” She couldn’t stay quiet anymore, “It’s worth everything! That’s why I can use it for the cost. I just…I can’t…”

Hot emotions were running wild within Subaru’s mind; cold logic was trying to finally pinpoint what was wrong with his fiancé.

Subaru decided to gamble, the anger was pushed down for just a moment, “Please, just tell me.”

Subaru grabbed her hands and spoke softly, “What’s wrong? You can’t just expect me or anyone else here to accept this. Give us a reason. Something logical. This…whatever this is. It isn’t like you. You’re acting like…”

Like me.

Anastasia was silent.

And then she slipped her hands out of Subaru’s, speaking cold, “I’m acting sane. This is the best-case scenario: I take the burden of teleportation. We go to the Sage’s tower. We kill Gluttony. Our names return. We get our lives back. You get your camp back. Everyone’s happy.”

“But not-“ Something stood out from her words, Subaru locked onto that discrepancy, and his eyes widened, “Ana. How many people are officially in your camp?”

Ana cocked her head, “What do you mean? My old company is full of people. You have to be specific.”

Subaru sweated, “No I mean…the closest people.”

“Well besides my secretary…I guess there is Joshua.”

Joshua’s face morphed into confusion as Subaru’s morphed into dread. The black star grabbed Anastasia’s shoulders, “Julius. Ricardo. Tivey. Mimi. Hetaro. Do any of them ring a bell to you?!”

Her confusion increased, “Subaru, who are you talking about?”

He then looked around and flinched, “Everyone. What was our purpose in going to the Augria Sand Dunes in the first place?”

Halibel raised his hand, “You realized some people everyone knew, suddenly got their names disappeared. So, ya got the idea that we could kill Gluttony since those people were rumored to be at the Tower.”

…That fucking filter!

Subaru shook his head and refocused on Anastasia, “We are going there to save the people you love. The people you care about. Your family.”
Anastasia looked at him as if nothing made sense anymore, “Subaru. We were going to the tower so we can get our names back. Don’t you remember? I’ve been an orphan my entire life. Once we get our names back. You can become a knight again. I get my company. Everything is as it should be. That’s the plan, isn’t it?”

Subaru rage peaked, “Then why sacrifice yourself?! I get it. Gluttony fucked with your mind so now you think we’re going to the tower just for our names. That’s obviously the most logical thing for that stupid power to connect the logic on. But why would you ever think that sacrificing your own health and safety was a good idea. To take everything on by yourself?!”

Anastasia stared at him before suddenly blowing up also, “What do you mean?! You don’t get to…you. You. You!”

She scratched her head before screaming at Subaru, “This is for you! This whole excursion is for you! I don’t need my name! I can get my wealth back myself. We were doing fine in Banan! You were the one who wanted us to leave and save some nobodies! I’m just making sure this goes smoothly! So that you can finally get something out of all of this!”

Subaru couldn’t believe what he was hearing, “Is that what you remember?! That I wanted to become a knight again or do something so dangerous for strangers?! I don’t need you to do that! I have everything I ever wanted!”

Anastasia’s eyes became cold as she narrowed in on Subaru, “So why are we here then? Why did we come all of the way here? If you’re so satisfied, why come here?!”

He was about to spew venom at her but quickly halted his tongue. He needed to calm down. This was Gluttony’s fault, no one else’s.

Subaru chose his words very carefully, “We came here to help you. To save the people you care about.”

Anastasia waved her hand wide, “…The only people I care about are in this room. The only person I care about from Lugunica: Is you! I’m doing this to save you! To save the life you deserve to have! Where you don’t have to be perceived as a fugitive!”

Goddamnit!  She thinks that this whole thing is for my sake while I know this is actually for her sake. The filter is preventing it from going through her thick skull. Unless we can get undeniable proof, the filter won’t break.

Subaru shook his head, he knew what needed to be done, “You know what? It doesn’t matter. You just need to understand this is for your own good. We’re going to save your family. We’re going to get their names back. And you’re going to stay here where it’s safe. End of the conversation.”

Subaru turned but was immediately stopped by Anastasia’s hand gripping his wrist tightly, “You’re not leaving me here.”

Subaru glanced back and glared, “You don’t get a choice.”

Her eyes were still cold but manic, “I do. If you leave me here, I’ll…I’ll…” her eyes darted around.

Subaru didn’t hesitate, “Beako.”

Her eyes widened as she turned to Beatrice gliding over to her in the air, hand outstretched, “Do not hate me for this, I suppose. This is for your own—”

Beatrice stopped as her eyes glowed slightly, her hands stopping a few inches from Anastasia’s neck, her voice changing to a more even tone, “Apologies Sister, but this is not right. We should discuss this more—”

Beatrice’s body twisted, fighting itself, “You little! This is mut—”

“Just listen and—”

“Unhand me, in—”

“You can’t just listen to Su—”

“The girl is unstable—”

“Pot, ket—”

“How dare you—”
Beatrice soon started to wrestle herself, her arms fighting each other.

Anastasia seemed to realize Subaru’s plan as she quickly tried to let go of Subaru’s arm, only to then notice he had already locked his grasp over her wrist now, keeping her in place as he glanced at their two bodyguards.

Subaru spoke quickly, “Hal, Tia. Knock her out.”

Hal was about to step forward when Tia raised her hand in the air, the wolf demi-human eyeing the Spirit confused, “What’s the matter with you now?”

Tia glared, “We shouldn’t keep Ana here.”

Halibel opened his eyes, “That’s odd. You aren’t the type to refuse a request from Su-san.”

His tone was drenched in bewilderment.

She kept her gaze on Halibel, “This is for Su and Ana’s own good. They’re just too stupid to realize this whole argument is idiotic.”

Halibel put his and into his other sleeve, “Stupid or not. We have a job to do. And Ana-bo ain’t in the right headspace for making decisions.”

Tia growled, “This isn’t a discussion. Let this play out.”

Halibel pointed a kunai at her, “You’re right, it isn’t. But I ain’t lettin’ ya endanger her life for that vague of a reason.”

The wind blew through the room, a nearby closet door opened and closed rapidly as Joshua hid behind a nearby sofa.

Subaru raised his hand in the air, “No, wait, stop! We shouldn’t be fighting, this is not the time!”

His vision caught a bright light in the corner of his eye. It was from Anastasia’s finger pointed straight at his body, a Jiwald pointed at his chest.

Subaru was stunned, “Ana-pop?”

Her mask was cracking fully, no longer steel, but melting with guilt, “Subaru. Let me come. Please. I-I know. This escalated more than I wanted to, but we can stop this. I’m not going to hurt you. I would never hurt you! Just. Let me come with you.”

Subaru stared, “Why go this far? I don’t get it. I seriously don’t! This isn’t like you. The past few days. That whole conversation we had in the carriage. This whole bullshit! What happened to you? What happened to the girl I fell in love with? The greedy girl who would do whatever it took to claim what she wanted. This isn’t you!”

“What good is there about me?!”

Subaru flinched at her words, “W-what?!”

The mask was gone. Leaving only a crying and broken girl who had no idea what she was doing anymore.

Through the tears, her voice strained to get out every word. Subaru tried to hear as Tia and Halibel fought each other in the background.

She whispered, “…What good is there about me? A greedy girl who constantly takes what she wants and doesn’t think about giving back once. I’ve done nothing for you. Nothing. You know better than me, but you refuse to see the facts. I haven’t…died for you. I haven’t sacrificed anything for you. I haven’t lived my life for you. All I’ve done for you is what others already have. Love. Affection. Promises. Just like the others. Emilia. Rem. Me. We’ve done nothing worthwhile for you. Guiding you? Acting as a pillar for you? A…home?! What good is any of that if we can’t help you in the ways that truly matter?!”

Subaru’s throat felt constrained, her words choking him, “I don’t need anything more-“

Anastasia’s voice cracked, broken and ready to finally fall apart, “But I want to be more! I want to be more than some shitty greedy merchant! I want to be someone who can stand by you, side by side. Not someone who waits at home. Not someone who lets you figure everything out. Not someone who follows your every word. I want to be someone who actually…who actually…”

Her eyes glanced elsewhere, everywhere, darting around the room, as if trying to find exact words. She then finally made eye contact with Subaru. And for some reason, whatever she saw, made her brace herself.

She closed her eyes.

And when she opened them, her voice exploded, “Someone who actually fucking matters! You’re the only one who matters here! What good am I if my husband, the person I love more than anything, suffers for us! For me! And I can’t do shit about it! I can’t hear everything you do! I can’t see what you do! I can’t be there for you every step of the way! What good am I if I can’t return with you?!”

Subaru’s heart froze. He felt his blood run cold.

Subaru shook his head slowly, “Ana…please…don’t tell me.”

She smiled, not warmly, but as if nothing mattered anymore, “I’m sorry. I’m so, so, sorry. I couldn’t control myself. I’m sorry for being such a worthless lover, I can’t even suffer alone like you could. Bearing everything, like you. Please, when you return to the past, don’t leave me alone. Don’t leave me in Banan. Don’t leave me here. I want to be with you, even if I have to sacrifice everything. Even if I have to sacrifice myself…don’t let me go. I’m scared. If I can’t be of worth to you, what good am I compared to the others? I know you say you would never abandon me. But if I’m not special, then why would you only choose me? Why not have more worthless lovers? Why not pick someone stronger or more capable? It’s stupid. I know you wouldn’t. But I’m scared. I’m scared of even the smallest chance of you abandoning me. Am I too greedy? Do I really ask so much? I just don't want to be alone. I don't want to be alone… Is that so hard to understand?!"

Her voice echoed as she fell to her knees crying, hands covering her eyes as she hyperventilated, “Please don’t leave me alone…I can’t be alone…not anymore…please…please…please…”

Subaru couldn’t find the words, his mind racing, his breathing rapidly increasing in pace and volume.

She knows. She knows about Return by Death.

Why? How? How did he mess up this bad?!

Did he let it slip?!

He quickly looked around, expecting shadows or a hand to reach out and break his heart or destroy hers, shielding her from anything that could approach. All he saw were his companions staring, who all finally calmed down and watched the stars quietly, evidently realizing that this wasn’t the time for a brawl.

But nothing came.

But…no. She said return to the past? That means…maybe…does it not count…does it…

Subaru had a nasty theory.

He quickly turned on Ops Basiliskos. Locking eyes onto Anastasia’s form and putting all of his intent into switching any fatal wound on her with him. A part of him knew this was a bad idea but the other part needed to know. Desperate to know.

If she dies, I’ll take it instantly. Don’t fucking try me Satella. Just me. Just tell me…that it’s still there. I don’t care how much it hurts. But don’t you dare fucking touch her!

As Anastasia sobbed, he tensed his muscles and whispered a barely audible, “I…can Return by Death.”

A second passed. His body went stiff.

Another second passed.

And then another.

Another.

And another.

For nearly half a minute, nothing happened.

As if…it wasn’t there. The taboo wasn’t there.

Subaru’s mind blanked.

“I can Return by Death… I can Return by Death…” He repeated it several times, just as audible as before. Yet nothing still happened.

Subaru couldn’t believe it, his voice getting progressively higher, “Oh my God…oh my God!”

He laughed hysterically, causing everyone in the room to flinch, “I can’t believe it! Is it gone?! Is this…am I?”

Subaru didn’t understand, his emotions were running high. Fear, joy, rage, curiosity, concern. A full spectrum of different feelings rushed through him.

He was free. Maybe. Maybe not. But for a second, besides that horrible time just last year, he realized how great it felt to no longer be bound by a horrible curse. To be allowed to at least say the words he always wanted to say.

Wait. Why is it gone?

Subaru suddenly felt pure dread pour into his stomach. Was Return by Death no longer working correctly?

And maybe-

Ana.

His eyes widened. This wasn’t the time. He needed to focus on her.

No wonder she was going crazy the last few days. She must have realized something…she must have gotten so close to the truth.

And it made her go insane.

They needed to talk about this. Now.

Subaru looked down at his fiancé.

Only to find her gone.

NO!

Subaru panicked and quickly looked around, only to find Tia and Beatrice were missing as well.

His confused expression was corrected by Halibel as the wolf Demi-human walked up to him, concern etched across the wolfman’s face.

Halibel said, “While you were havin’ a crazed fit, Ana-bo took the chance and scurried off. Little girl used the Flow Method fully and sped right out the door. Was about to chase after her but Tia and Bea were faster, yellin’ at me to keep you safe. Speakin’ of, what the hell was that about? One moment you looked like ya saw a ghost and the next it looked like ya were in the heavens above.”

Subaru was filled with relief that the two went after her but also tremendous guilt as he realized how that brief distraction led to his fiancé running away.

“Hal, let’s follow them. I think…I finally know what’s been bothering her for so long.”

He needed to talk to her now. Set things straight.

Halibel perked up, “You do, huh? Well, maybe this drama play can finally be over. Alright then, what are we waitin’ for-“

The door creaked open, and the person Subaru wanted to see the least walked in.

Silver hair. Beautiful. Iridsecent. Shining.

Innocent curiosity and concern radiating from her.

“Um, is everything alright in here?” Her voice was like cold sugar.

Subaru swallowed.

It was Emilia.

--------------------------------------------

Death.

That’s what she heard.

Almost completely inaudible. But she heard it.

Ever since they shared Ods, it was as if she could hear Subaru so clearly compared to the others. So, when he whispered those words and nearly broke down laughing. She finally realized it. Everything.

He died. He died for me.

Not near death. Not because he got injured enough. No threshold to reach before it activates fully.

No, the condition was clear. Subaru needed to die.

Subaru died for her.

Countless times.

So, she ran.

She wanted to run away from it all.

Because it was all so much worse than she ever realized.

She ran out of that room even as two of her spirit companions screamed at her to stay. She needed to run.

She needed to get away.

She was a plague.

A disgusting wretched disease.

Festering on her beloved. Forcing him to die to sate her Greed.

She needed to get away from him.

To leave and never come back.

That was how he could stay safe.

How she could pay him back.

Because ever since she came into his life, she made him suffer.

Might as well cut the disease from the source.

She slammed her back onto the door and curled her body inward, ignoring the yelling from the two Spirits as they pleaded with her.

Anastasia just tuned them out, covering her ears and sobbing.

She was a coward.

A worthless piece of shit who ran away.

Because she couldn’t handle this reality.

The reality that her worth was even worse than the bottom.

When she was a hyena, she was nothing.

Now she was worse than nothing.

A black hole. Devouring Subaru’s happiness and kindness until there was nothing left.

An eternity passed.

…Did they give up?

It seemed against their character to do so but perhaps she had run their compassion dry. Maybe she wasn’t worth it anymore. Not worth kicking the door down.

She lifted her head and looked around.

Anastasia wasn’t picky when choosing a room to break down in, simply running into one at random.

It was a nice and well-kept room. Not a spot of dust or dirt to be found. No shelves of books but there were several cleaning tools stored and safely kept next to the closet. A desk, chair, and bed were the only other furniture.

And for some reason a spiked mace was kept on a podium right on top of the desk.

Anastasia kept forgetting how weird the Emilia camp is.

Though I’m the weirdest since I fell in love with their knight.

She shuddered as she slowly got to her feet and walked over, her eyes glancing at the desk first.

It’s a morningstar. Not a mace. Why is it so shiny? Has someone been polishing it?

She then peered elsewhere and was rightly surprised by what she discovered.

A beautiful woman with short blue-hair dressed in a gown was quietly sleeping in the bed next to her.

She knew who this was.

Rem.

The second woman her lover fell for. A complicated woman from how Subaru’s stories painted her. But an overall caring, loyal, and supportive person.

How many times did you die for her? How much did she hurt you?

Her neurons kept firing, connecting and disconnecting theories over the course of the day. His twitches. If those are related to his ability in any capacity, then perhaps those people didn’t just hurt him…they killed him.

And if that’s the case, Rem was a prime suspect. Subaru’s stories had too many plot holes. There was too much missing information.

And now she understood why.

His reaction to saying the ability, complete joy after the intense fear that permeated his expression beforehand, implied that he wasn’t able to say such words before.

Meaning for some reason or another, he could never explain that he returned by dying. Intentionally or not.

So, he always chose his words carefully to avoid any topics related to him dying.

And what topic did he dance around the most?

Rem. Especially when it came to how they met and got to know each other.

The constant twitches and phrases such as, ‘we didn’t get along that well in the beginning,’ cemented that Rem killed him or led to his death in some way. Plus, given that she was apparently an Oni, just like Tia-Two. Who could smell Subaru’s scent. A scent associated with Witch Cultists. Who were responsible for the maid’s tragic past.

Even an idiot could surmise the most likely scenario.

And it’s why Anastasia had half a mind to make sure this woman never woke up again.

Her hand hovered above Rem’s throat, several lights glowing at her fingertips.

A quick slash and everything would be fine.

…But Subaru wouldn’t like it. Even if he didn’t love her anymore, Subaru still thought of Rem fondly.

The glow stopped and she brought her hand down.

You’ll get your punishment eventually. Everyone will. Even me.

Anastasia didn’t know when such murderous thoughts were so prevalent in her mind. It started off as a preemptive measure, a way to prioritize people if any bad situations occurred. But as Anastasia began to realize how much her lover suffered. The person she valued above all else.

The list of names quickly became a hit list.

Anastasia sighed as she rubbed her temple.

What is wrong with me? Am I insane?

“Hmm~. I wouldn’t say you are insane. Your loyalty to your future spouse and dedication to keeping him safe is quite beautiful. I applaud you, all things considered, Mother of the Taijitu.”

Anastasia whipped her head to the source of the voice.

Confusion muddled her mind as she gawked at the person sitting in front of her.

Well, not a person. A bird in fact.

A very beautiful silver bird with feathers that puffed and shined in the sunlight. Blue eyes that radiated and pierced her soul. It was mesmerizing.

But why was it crying?

Chapter 32: A Deal with the Devil

Summary:

Anastasia meets a peculiar individual...

Chapter Text

A crying bird was not on Anastasia’s list of ‘things I expect to see in my entire life.’

She didn’t even know birds could cry. Or talk. Or look so majestic.

Like a prized species.

The bird spoke despite no mouth or beak movement, only cocking its head, “How complimentary. Unfortunately, despite my appearance, I am not a bird. I am in fact, a person, speaking through this animal as a conduit.”

And apparently it could read thoughts.

Anastasia started to straighten her body, moving slightly backward, cautious, “Who are you?”

The bird preened its wing, “Does that matter?”

“…It ain’t good to negotiate unless the other party is forthright with ya.”

A wonderful laugh echoed through the room, piercing through Anastasia’s skull, making her wince, the voice of the bird was rapturous, “Hoshin’s proverbs are ever-present. Do feel free to relax. I mean you no harm.”

Anastasia tried her best to retain a smile, broken and heavy as it felt, “I can see dat, given how ya got my attention rather than takin’ me out when ya got the chance. So? Who are you? Why are you in the Margrave’s mansion? And what’s somethin’ interestin’ like you got to do with someone like me?”

And what was that about callin’ me the ‘Mother of the Taijitu?’

The bird cocked its head back and forth, a small melodious hum cascading through the air, making Anastasia feel like her eyes were heavy.

She had to pinch herself to stay awake as the bird spoke softly, yet clearly, “Pandora. My name is Pandora. And I am interested in you, Anastasia Hoshin. And your story as a whole.”

Anastasia rose an eyebrow, “My story? What’s dat got to do with ya? Ya lookin’ to write my autobiography?”

The bird…smiled? Anastasia could feel it smiling despite no movement of its beak. It was strange. She could almost imagine a beautiful woman sitting in front of her, effervescent. There but not there.

The bird’s voice called, “Your love. It is…incredible.”

Each word the bird spoke was genuine. Pandora. Her voice. It was as if she held reverence for the very essence of love. For her. For whatever Anastasia represented.

Anastasia felt seen. Heard. Understood on a level that she couldn’t quite believe.

Anastasia’s mouth felt dry. She couldn’t swallow. She could barely look away.

“…Why me? I ain’t special. My love. It ain’t special. I haven’t done anything special.”

Pandora cooed, “Do you really believe that? That your love holds no value? That you are a lesser mortal for lacking some secret substance that makes your love more profound? Tell me, what makes you so deserving of such self-hatred?”

“I…I…” Anastasia’s lips wavered, her mind screaming at her to shut up, and failing, “…It is because I have no value.”

“Hm?” Pandora flapped her wings and edged closer to Anastasia.

The words tumbled out of Anastasia’s mouth without a care, “I’m not someone worthy of it. Of love. Of the love I want. I want…to love equally. But I haven’t done so. I can never. I could not be the person worthy of…him.”

“I see, such a considerate disposition. Your lover must be quite wonderful to have such lofty expectations of yourself. Tell me about him.”

Everything cascaded from Anastasia’s lips, nothing restrained, “…I thought I wanted so much in the world. Wealth, status, power. I just wanted it all. I didn’t care for love. None of it. Because what does love matter? It doesn’t bring me anything. I wasn’t going to be like her. Never like her. I could get it anytime. I could find it anytime. I had suitors and beautiful people surrounding me. I’ll get it later. I have time. I had time. I even thought someone like Julius could hold that place in my heart. Because I deserved someone with high specifications: beauty, background, talent. I deserved someone worthy of me.”

The bird edged closer, “But?”

“…But I was wrong,” Anastasia laughed with melancholy drenched in every inch of her tone, “So wrong. I didn’t know anything. I should have known. The first time I fell in love, it was because someone gave me kindness. It wasn’t because of some grandiose actions or because that person was beautiful or impressed me with their intellect or anything fucking normal! I just…I can’t help but fall in love with kindness.”

“Oh child, that is such a wonderful reason for love. But what does that have to do with your lover?”

Anastasia rubbed her arm with her hand, trying her best not tear through her clothes and break the skin, “Subaru is…nothing I wanted before. An idiot who barely has any talent. He didn’t understand how to negotiate. He had no wealth, no family connections, and he wasn’t even that handsome. A bare-bones boy with nothing to offer me. I would have barely cared for him before I lost everything. All he was, all he ever will be, is a kind, selfless fool.”

“But now?”

Anastasia grit her teeth, a part of her mind knew something was wrong, but everything else was lulled into this siren’s call, wanting to whisper the deepest recesses of her mind for all to see, “But now…he’s everything. He’s everything to me. I don’t care about money. I don’t care about my company. I don’t care about being a queen or even just living forever. I want…him. I want all of him. I want to wake up in his arms and laugh my cares away all day and night. I want to be the only one he thinks of. The only woman he could ever even possibly consider beautiful. I want to be his everything. Just like he is to me.”

Pandora was practically right next to her. Why was she on the floor now? When had Anastasia fallen to her knees?

The voice silenced such questions, “But isn’t that already true? He already considers you his world? Why don’t you believe in his love?”

“I do!” Anastasia shivered, her head downcast and her body wanting to close in on itself, “I do…but am I worthy of it? Have I done enough for him every day that can compare to what he has done for me? He…his power…he has done so much for me that I can’t come close to what he offers. If I can’t match that. If I can’t be the only woman in his life. If I can’t be his everything…than what is the point of me?! I’m nothing compared to him! Nothing! Less than nothing! Worthless fucking garbage!”

Everything felt so claustrophobic. She hated it. She hated crying. She hated how it made Subaru sad. She hated being so powerless. She hated how much pain she made him go through. She wanted it all to stop. To end. To end this miserable existence of being alone. She didn’t want to be Anastasia Hoshin anymore.

And then, Anastasia felt the soft touch of feathers wrapping around her body, warm and comforting her very soul, “There, there. I understand. Truly, I do. You, who wishes to love so purely. To give and receive just as much love. To be frustrated by your inability as well as the world. You, who loves so genuinely. I applaud you, Anastasia Hoshin. The you, who learned to love the one who never said goodbye. A beautiful, pure, sanguineous love.”

Anastasia looked up and gasped.

No longer was she being held in the wings of a shining bird, but rather the arms of a woman, with platinum hair and piercing blue eyes. Beautiful, pure, ethereal. Such words could barely describe the masterpiece of humanity right beside her. That very rendition of perfection was crying for her. Crying for her woes. For her love.

Anastasia needed no tears, for the woman named Pandora cried for her.

Anastasia’s lips moved before her thoughts, “…Thank you.”

Pandora’s smile never ceased, “I should be thanking you. For allowing me to listen. For telling me all of your worries and tribulations. To bare one’s soul is a gargantuan task. I applaud you once again for your resolve. For your love is not wrong.”

“I…yes.”

Anastasia’s mind was a canvas. Barren, stripped of whatever plagued her. Ready to be painted on by the right artist.

Pandora’s voice was a splash of colors, “Child. Anastasia Hoshin. What if I could offer you a way forward? A path that will allow you to achieve what your heart truly desires. Where you no longer have to feel such emotions. Where you can become who you truly were meant to be? Someone who deserves to be loved. Someone who gives love freely. A truly happy and satisfying ending. It will satiate your Greed.”

Anastasia felt the colors cling to her body, staining her, “…Do you really mean that? What…are you exactly offering?”

Pandora smiled, despite her lips already curving upward this whole time, the smile had appeared as if it was never there to begin with, “A merchant until the end it seems. How quaint. But yes, I do mean it. Your story will no longer have to journey through Hell. No longer bound. The path forward will be treacherous and laid in thorns, but it will be worth the effort. Take my hand. And I shall be your guide, into the salvation of Heaven.”

Anastasia blinked. No longer was Pandora surrounding her, but instead in front of her. The sun shining through the window behind her. Wings coveting the goddess’s very body, an amalgamation of an avian and a beautiful woman. Anastasia could barely understand or tell where everything began and ended. Where to look. The eyes of Pandora constantly shifted and spread all around. Her smile cascaded throughout the room.

Rapturous.

Disgusting.

Neither.

Both.

And more.

But Anastasia could tell. A hand, the handle of a door to her salvation stretched towards her.

“Take my hand. Open. Let your true story begin here, in earnest. Do not fear. Do not weep. Tomorrow, you will be with me in paradise. Your love awaits you. Away from the rot of Purgatory. From the burdens of Hell.”

Paradise. Love.

The colors shifted in her brain, in Anastasia’s brain.

I can be with him. Truly, with him.

Kneeling before Pandora.

Standing side by side.

She stood with one foot, one step forward, alone.

Together, forward.

Anastasia’s hand reached out, wishing to hold what she desperately wanted.

Forever hand in hand.

Never one without the other.

Never alone again.

Just as she was about to touch the hand, the door slammed open behind her.

----------------------------------------------

“Um, is everything alright in here?”

Subaru stared at her briefly before looking away, “…Yeah. Everything is okay here.”

“Oh-kay?” Emilia looked around and blushed slightly, “Ah, I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to intrude. I heard some loud noises and thought someone fell. Are you both Roswaal’s guests?”

Subaru hesitated as Halibel’s voice sprang from his side, “Yep, yep. We were just havin’ a little chat here is all. Our business with Ros-san is a bit important, ya see? Can’t really rush that kind of stuff. So, if you don’t mind, we’ll go find our other associates and get this negotiation all sorted.”

Emilia brightened up, “Ah, if you wish, I can help you find-“
Subaru cut that off immediately, “We’ll be fine. We wouldn’t want to bother you.”

“Are you sure?” Despite being rejected, Emilia still shined brightly, “This mansion is quite big and navigating it is reaaaaally cumbersome.”

Subaru immediately muttered, “Who even says cumbersome nowadays?”

“Hm? What did you say?”

“…I said I understand. We’ll be careful. See you later,” Subaru moved to go past her and through the door, only to be surprised by another familiar face.

A specifically clownish face.

“Oh? It seems you have met my waaaaard,” Roswaal Mathers looked inside before Subaru tried to move past him, stopping his movement with one shoulder grab, “Not so fast. Have you made your decision?”

Subaru shoved his hand off and glared, “Not right now. Hal, let’s go.”

Subaru’s mind was solely focused on finding his wife and settling her mind. Nothing else mattered at the moment. He needed to make sure she was safe.

I can’t believe she figured out RBD. How? You know what, it doesn’t matter. We need to talk and I need to answer any of her questions and try to see what exactly about all of this is bothering her. Is it because she’s scared that I’ve been manipulating our relationship? That I’ve been lying to her? But based on what she said…does she think I’m just using her? No…I need to tell her everything.

After that, he’ll figure out what’s going on with Return by Death. Is it malfunctioning? Is something going wrong with Satella? Will he die permanently?

While ruminating, he ended up nearly colliding into Clind, glaring at the butler before back at Roswaal who was smiling beside a confused Emilia.

Subaru glanced at Halibel who shrugged, the wolf demi-human will follow his call.

Subaru sighed, “What do you want? If this is about our deal, I said we can talk about it later.”
Roswaal kept on smiling, “I insist that we accompany you. You are my guests after all and while I’m suuuuuure you can find your way. It would be discourteous of me to not guide you as a rule of hospitality.”

He obviously wants to keep watch of me. Probing for something. I doubt Ros-chi hasn’t figured out everything about me now. Explains why I so happened to run into Emilia.

Subaru narrowed his eyes before nodding, “Fine. Just don’t slow me down.”

Subaru began to walk forward once again with his trusted bodyguard and unwanted entourage. His footsteps echoed in the hallway, eyes glancing anywhere and everywhere for any sign of his other companions or his lover.

“Are you alright?” He was nearly startled out of his concentration again by that sweet voice he used to love, her eyes filled with genuine concern as she walked beside him, “You seem…troubled.”

Subaru tried his best not to frown, opting for the most neutral expression, “…I’m fine. Just trying to find my fiancé.”

Emilia perked up, “Oh? Congratulations!”

“I, uh…thanks,” Subaru scratched his neck awkwardly, not expecting this kind of response.

Emilia matched Subaru’s pace naturally, “How long have you two been together? When’s the wedding? What do you love about her?”

“Um…about a few months now. I have no idea but hopefully soon. And uh, a lot of things but it would take forever to list.”

“Wow! That’s amazing, you must reaaaaally love her to get married that soon.”

“…I do,” Subaru didn’t know where to look or what exactly to say.

Emilia put a hand over her mouth, “Oh. I must be making you uncomfortable with all these questions. I didn’t mean to pry.”

Subaru stared for a moment before chuckling, “No, you’re alright. It’s just…nostalgic is all.”

At Emilia’s confused expression, Subaru laughed more, explaining, “Sorry, sorry. You just remind me of someone is all. From the past.”

Emilia frowned as she looked closer at Subaru, making him lean away.

Emilia then blushed in embarrassment, “Ah! I thought you seemed kind of familiar too. You remind me of someone as well.”

“Really? Who?”

Emilia hummed, “I’ll tell you if you tell me about who I remind you of.”

“I…sure. It’s a deal.”

Emilia clapped her hands, “You remind me of my Mother. She had the same type of eyes as you. A little scary but super kind.”

Subaru’s lips pursed.

I remember you telling me about Fortuna.

In the past, it made him incredibly happy that Emilia described his eyes like that. Now…it was just a nice compliment. Nothing more. Nothing less.

Subaru spoke softly, “I see. She sounds like a wonderful person.”

“She was,” Emilia spoke with reverence before glancing at Subaru again, “Now it’s your turn.”

Subaru dared not to look her in the eyes, “…You just remind me of someone I admired before. I wanted to devote my whole life to her. She was very kind to me. One of the first people who was kind to me when I came here. She made me happy.”

He glanced over at her.

Emilia’s eyes shined with compassion, “What happened?”

“…Life did. Some bad things. Some good things. And after some time apart, I ended up falling out of love with her. It wasn’t her fault.”

“I’m sorry,” Subaru’s eyes widened as he saw Emilia clutch her chest, her lips wavering as she spoke, “I’m sorry that happened to you.”

“…It wasn’t your fault. It was no one’s fault.”

“If no one was at fault, you still deserve an apology. No one deserves to suffer for that.”

Subaru smiled, “I guess so…thank you.”

Emilia’s smile returned, “Thank you as well. I’ve been wanting to learn more about love and what it means to be in love.”

“…Really? That’s…great.”

“Mhm. Granted, I haven’t fallen in love with anyone yet. But…I don’t know why but this last year, I’ve wanted to understand it. I wanted to see what it’s like to love someone. It’s why I asked those questions. I’m curious about love and how people can so easily find it.”

Subaru bit his lip, “I see.”

“…Do you mind if I ask you a small question?”

Subaru tried his best to hold his emotions in, “…Sure.”

Emilia looked at him oddly, “You don’t have to answer if you don’t want to. You seem stressed.”

“I…” Subaru sighed before calming himself, “I’m good. Again, just worried about my fiancé is all.”

Subaru’s answer seemed to make Emilia smile even brighter, “Ah, well. If you don’t mind then, could you tell me what love is to you?”

Subaru thought for a moment, “…It’s the warmth you feel when you see a person smile. The happiness you feel because they are happy. Sadness when they are sad. Anger when they are mistreated. Love is that feeling when you come home, after a long day, and you see them, and realize everything is worth it. It’s when everything you ever do is brighter with them. And everything you ever will do is darker without them. Love pushes you forward as much as it slows you down. And above all, love is…a home. Where you feel the most comfortable.”

He finally looked at Emilia once again, only to see her eyes shining, “…What a wonderful way to describe love. Your fiancé is a lucky woman.”

Subaru blinked before smiling, “I’m a lucky man for having her.”

Emilia skipped forward, hands behind her back, “Thank you for telling me. I feel…a little closer to my goal.”

“I’m glad. Truly. I hope you find that special person as well.”

And I’m sorry I can’t be that person for you anymore.

Before any more conversations could occur, Subaru noticed the presence of his two Spirits ahead. Except…why were they standing in front of a door like that? Not moving or talking at all?

“Beako! Tia!” Subaru rushed over as quickly as possible. He checked the two motionless Spirits as the others arrived.

Emilia was alarmed, “Oh, so Beatrice returned! Is she alright?”

Halibel crept over and waved a hand in front of both of them, they didn’t even blink, “Well that’s odd. Really odd. What’s the matter with them?”

Subaru couldn’t tell. He didn’t have time for this though. He grabbed both of them, Tia by the shoulder and Beatrice by the head, and shook them awake.

This did the trick as both suddenly started glaring at the source of their rude awakening before their eyes softened.

“Su? Where did you come from?”

Subaru pointed at them both, “Down the hall. I’m more worried about you two though. What happened to finding Ana? You guys were spacing out here in front of this door. Where is she?”

They both blinked at him before looking at each other and then at the door.

Beatrice spoke next, “That’s…not right, in fact. We were both slamming on the door, trying to coax Anastasia out. Nothing was working and she wouldn’t answer our calls. And then you appeared right beside us, Subaru. Sister, am I getting anything wrong?”

Beatrice clutched her scarf. Given how Beatrice nodded, it seemed Eridna agreed.

Subaru frowned, “Something isn’t right. Tia. Cut open the door now.”

Tia didn’t hesitate; a slash of pure wind slammed into the door.

And then bounced off right behind her, cutting a gash into the wall.

Everyone gawked at the sight, Roswaal especially.

The Head Mage immediately began looking at the door, his eyes peering over every detail, no longer smiling, “That is interesting.”

Subaru walked over to him, “This isn’t you?”

Roswaal didn’t look away, “You really believe I would have something strong enough to deflect a Great Spirit’s wind?”

Subaru shrugged, “To be fair, you want to kill Volcanica using Ram. I’m assuming you have invested in something that can deflect Dragon-level weaponry.”

“…Fair enough.”

Subaru then narrowed his eyes and focused on the door, Basiliskos Ops opening his vision beyond the door.

He could see a bright iridescent light. Ana. Sitting right in the middle of the room.

And…what is that?

It’s not…it’s…what…I…

)*$&D!)&$!)$&$&!$@O@@@@@@@@@@@@N@@@@@@@@$&#$12307123078T23071230782P3071230782307123078230712E3078230712307823071230782307123E07823071afhilaodsfayfd;ayfdsaop;uygpyi9753K492475081[uyt;uhohg;osuy9auyp98y9p8ufay[8[[8yq[y8yaf8y[y

“Su-san?!” Subaru was now suddenly laying in Halibel’s arms, Beatrice over him with her hands radiating healing magic, as Tia growled nearby, her fists slammed into the door every second.

Subaru rubbed his face and was shocked to see blood staining his hand, “W-what the hell?”

Halibel took out a handkerchief and wiped Subaru’s face, “You started bleedin’ out of nowhere. Your eyes went bloodshot, and your nose was gushin’ red like no tomorrow. What did you do?”

Subaru felt his head spin as he tried to stand on his own, almost falling to his knees without Halibel holding onto him, “…I tried using Basiliskos Ops to see if Ana-pop was in there. And she was. But something else was there too…I don’t know what that thing is, but it isn’t normal or of this world.”

Subaru glanced towards the door. Tia kept angrily hitting it, trying to crack the damn thing open while Roswaal and Clind were discussing something to the side.

Emilia herself was helping Tia by punching alongside her, not making a dent either.

Tia ran her hands in her hair, angrily shouting, “What is with this door?! It’s harder than my light sphere.”

Subaru couldn’t wait any longer, his instincts were screaming that Anastasia was in danger and he needed to get to her now.

Subaru turned to the butler and Margrave, “Clind. What cost would it take for you to put me in that room right now?”

Clind rubbed his chin, “Teleportation? Something substantial. However, that is not necessary. I believe if you give up something small, like a couple of favorite foods, and I will be able to open this door.”
Subaru didn’t hesitate, “Deal. How does this work?”

“Simply-“

Roswaal cut him off, “Remember Subaru. I won’t let you use Clind-“

Subaru didn’t hesitate, “I’ll do it, whatever, now tell me.”

Roswaal was caught off guard, “Do you not understand what you just ag-“

“I don’t care. None of it matters. What matters is right behind that door, most likely facing something completely out of this world, alone! So, either tell me how to get in there or I will have Halibel and Zarestia slaughter every single person in this mansion.”

Roswaal was stunned silent, a quick glance to Tia and Halibel’s stances answered any lingering questions, “…Clind. Tell him the requirements.”

The butler obliged, “Simply tell me what you are willing to give up, and I will use it to bypass the spell on the door.”

Subaru didn’t hesitate, “Ketchup, mustard, ranch. I will never eat them again. Done.”

Clind’s eyes glowed before he then channeled whatever power was given to him by the cost, holding his hand out as the door in front of them slowly started to splinter before getting crushed and blown open.

Subaru got to his feet and ran through the open doorframe, eyes panicked, “Ana! Where are you?!”

His eyes widened as he saw her, the love his life, on her knees, holding her hand out to a…bird?

A silver bird that had striking blue eyes and a presence of aura that made Subaru’s spine shiver.

Ana.

The bird didn’t matter. What did matter is that it was obviously a danger to her. To his wife.

Subaru tried to move closer but before he could even take a single step, he saw Anastasia’s hand reach out and touch the wing of the silver bird.

And then he heard its voice.

“Magnificent. Anastasia Hoshin. I wish you a wonderful journey.”

Anastasia looked back, guilt-ridden and filled with regret, whispering, “…I’m sorry.”

And then he heard a voice.

“Anastasia Hoshin is not here. She is in the cradle of souls, where the dead may begin again. May your love forever move the Sun and the other stars. Good luck.”

She was gone.

Just as soon as Subaru realized her complete absence from reality.

A blade of wind shot into the room and cut the bird into pieces, shredding it without remorse, before tearing into the window of the room, creating a hole in the wall.

“NO!” Tia screamed from right behind Subaru as he stood motionless, staring into the now completely vacant room.

No blood.

No flesh.

No Anastasia.

His connection with her…was gone.

No.

No. No.

NO. NO. NO.

NO. NO. NO.

NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO.

NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO.

NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO. NO.

Everything was too loud.

-------------------------------------------

Roswaal L. Mathers had no idea what just occurred. The woman who seemed to be the lover of his key, had just disappeared in the blink of an eye thanks to the power of some avian creature.

He needed to figure out what that was and how it was easily able to enter his home without anyone noticing. That fact that it could cast a high-level defensive spell on his door and put two Great Spirits into a trance unnerved him without compare, on the level of his first encounter with Hector all those years ago.

He glanced towards Clind, who had an especially nasty frown.

It seems he knows what exactly that was. Curious.

His ears perked up when he heard his dear sister Beatrice mutter to herself, “Sister? What’s wrong, in fact? Why are you so afraid all of a-“

Her words were cut off just as Roswaal felt…

Felt.

Felt…

Bloodlust.

Raw. Pure. Bloodlust.

And just as suddenly he was choked slammed into a nearby wall, Zarestia’s hand tightening its grip on his windpipe as he quickly processed what had just happened.

A quick scan of the room showed that he wasn’t the only one, Halibel had several clones pinning Clind to the ground, kunai barely piercing his flesh, as Beatrice cast hundreds of Minya spikes aimed right at Emilia.

Each one of his key’s companions were dripping with malice so dense that he could taste it through his pores.

Roswaal assumed the bloodlust was purely from the Great Spirit of Murder.

But no.

As the Head Mage finally began to analyze his surroundings more thoroughly.

The bloodlust originated not from the Spirit known for slaughtering countless populations for centuries. Nor the assassin known for hundreds of successful murders. Nor the artificial Spirit with power comparable to the Beast of the End.

No.

It was from his key. The key to his Teacher’s salvation.

Standing there, motionless, without a word, with his back turned towards them.

Natsuki Subaru. His black and orange garb flowing like water as wind poured in from outside, through the open wound on the wall.

“Subaru-“ Roswaal was barely able to strain his name out before the man in question spoke softly.

Yet his words were loud and resonant, carried by the wind with malevolence, “Quiet…you’re going to tell me what that was. What happened to her. And you’re going to speak the truth. Otherwise, I will break your body into pieces before having you watch me cast your Teacher’s mutilated corpse into the streets where everyone can see. Am I clear?”

Hell was open once more.

Chapter 33: The Pursuit of Happiness

Summary:

Subaru wants it all to end...

Notes:

(See the end of the chapter for notes.)

Chapter Text

Basiliskos Ops.

The Authority of Greed.

Natsuki Subaru did not exactly understand how it worked. However, his subconscious did.

All Authorities operate on three known aspects: an extension of the user and their Od, a trait that defines the Authority as a whole, and the ability to warp the World around them.

For the second, Basiliskos Ops shares the ability to create contracts, similar to the abilities of the previous users, Regulus Corneas and Echidna.

The third aspect, the ability to warp the World around them, allows Natsuki Subaru to transfer injuries, emotions, mana, and Od with those around him as long as they are a ‘consenting’ party. Consent involves the alignment of both parties’ purposes and goals for one another.

However, the third level’s full potential is still unknown to Natsuki Subaru consciously.

His understanding is that he must define the terms of engagement, in order to truly make full use of his power. That his power works differently for allies and enemies. That the contracts he makes require specific terms in order to be more powerful.

That he was only able to create a contract with Anastasia Hoshin, failing to do so with Halibel, Zarestia, and Beatrice.

This is false. In truth, the only pieces he has assumed correctly are that the contracts differ based on his perception of the person and that the recipient must consent.

Similar to Regulus Corneas, he is the King of his Domain.

And in his specific Domain, there are Roles and Rules.

The Roles include: a Queen, Knights, Citizens, and Enemies.

The Queen shares the ‘life’ and ‘burdens’ of the king.

The Knights share the ‘goals’ of the king.

The Citizens are ‘taxed’ by the king.

And the Enemies are ‘sacrificed’ by the king.

Subaru found his Queen, and in turn, found his Knights.

Subaru assumed his Knights would share their Od, Gate, mana, or injuries with him. This was a misunderstanding.

In truth, their level of trust was already sufficient to become Subaru’s Knights. However, the benefit they got was quite specific.

Basiliskos Ops allows their minds to…sync. Less of a hivemind but more than a simple mental connection. Emotions, complicated sets of information, and thoughts are all conveyed. In less than a fraction of a second, Subaru can give orders to his Knights and they in turn can coordinate with each other and consent to the action. Such orders come instinctually, rather than clearly defined messages. All done through the connection of their Ods to Subaru’s. Their hearts metaphorically become one with his.

As for the first aspect, an extension of the user and their Od:

…Basilisk Ops was a cry for help.

A wish for someone to understand him.

A desperate cry for the world to lift his burdens instead of being burdened by the world itself.

----------------------------------

“Do not be so rash, dear Subaru,” Roswaal chafed under the Spirit of Murder’s grip on his throat, “We are allies here.”

“…You haven’t answered my question, Roswaal,” his voice brought chills down Roswaal’s spine.

It wasn’t like the voice was particularly different. In any other situation, it would sound as whiny and annoying as he initially thought. But…the tone. The sheer…boredom he conveyed.

It was as if Roswaal’s life mattered nothing to Subaru at this very moment. It felt like he was negotiating with a monster rather than any human.

Roswaal chose to not gamble quite yet, “I have no idea who that was. You have as much knowledge as me in that regard.”

He could hear Subaru hum, “…You don’t know anything. But I am guessing Clind does.”

Roswaal’s eyes flicked to his butler, who was now getting pressed deeper into the ground.

…If I were to use that magic…no. Even if I were to get Clind free and he were to use his full power, this whole situation would be catastrophic. My key to salvation has already returned, I cannot let this chance go to waste.

Despite Clind’s hampered position, his eye was able to catch Roswaal’s.

Tell him. We shall adapt to how the situation progresses.

Clind’s voice was muffled. Halibel grabbed his hair and pulled him up violently, the wolf demi-human was eerily silent, his many clones just watching the butler carefully while pinning all of his limbs to the floor.

Clind coughed before speaking, “Whoever that was, it was most likely the current user of the Authority of Vainglory.”

Roswaal’s eyes widened.

Interesting. Teacher always said that Vainglory had disappeared for years, though stories of it have surfaced throughout the centuries. To have appeared right now…

Subaru stood motionless, though his bloodlust increased in intensity, “…And what does she have to do with my Ana.”

Clind frowned, “I have no idea. If I were to guess, Vainglory saw something special within your lover and opted to take her for a specific purpose. Most users are quite…delusional in their beliefs. But I have no idea why they would take such a girl in the first place.”

Roswaal noticed a discrepancy.

How did Subaru know it was a ‘she?’

The voice they all heard…it had no gender. He then noticed his ward act strange. Her eyes wide and her face pale.

Emilia spoke aloud, “U-um! I think I may know the reason!”
