Beatrice stared emotionless as Emilia continued, surrounded by Minya crystals, “I know who that is. If it’s the same person who had Vainglory…it was Pandora. She’s a Witch who has ties with the Witch’s Cult. She’s…horrifying. The most horrible person you could ever meet. She…I don’t know why, but she wanted me to open something for her. Something reaaaaally bad. That’s not all…”

Emilia nearly chocked as she finished her explanation, “…She made Guese into a monster.”

The mage ignored how those last words made him feel, opting to focus on the situation at hand.

Roswaal’s curiosity began to spike, So, Vainglory’s user has history with our dear Emilia. And given how well she knows about her. The fact that Subaru knows her gender…

The pieces in Roswaal’s mind began to form into a nice perfect picture. It all made sense now. Emilia and Subaru’s conversation, his reaction to Emilia, Subaru’s longing gaze at the mansion when they first arrived, the reactions of his companions, the argument that Roswaal was able to spy on despite their precautions, Subaru’s knowledge of Pandora, and Subaru’s overall demeanor.

I must have used Emilia as a honaytrap. If I knew of Subaru’s existence, I would have used her to coax him into loyalty…have his fate tied to me through a hostage or through common goals. So, he must have been close with her. In love with her. Close enough to learn of Pandora. But…he fell out of love. Found another.

Roswaal held back a frown.

And now that lover has found herself in the jaws of the enemy. Perhaps if Pandora is truly in league with the Witch’s Cult, they are looking for a new potential Archbishop.

His eyes locked onto Subaru’s form.

Or two.

“...I see,” Subaru still did not move, his haori flowed as the wind blew in, “So, at the end of the day, it all comes back to me…and my sins.”

Roswaal took the chance, “As you can see, we have no relation to what just happened. In truth, we are allies in this regard. That witch has invaded my property without my consent and has stolen your precious lover away. Wouldn’t you say this gives us ample reason to tie our hands together and hunt down such a monster in a mutually beneficial alliance? You have already promised to help me in my quest, and I am not one to leave my benefactors wanting. You have my word; your wife shall be rescued in due time.”

Subaru didn’t respond to Roswaal’s offer, only shifting slightly, “Clind. You have an Authority, don’t you?”

Clind didn’t respond, neither reacting nor saying a word, “…”

Subaru hummed, “I see. It doesn’t matter. I know you have it. That level of power is not possible with just magic. Beatrice couldn’t sense it…but that doesn’t prove anything. Pandora had no miasma either. So, yours and hers must be special.”

…Was he always this perceptive? He’s getting too close to the truth regarding Melancholy and Vainglory. I was hoping to use that information later. Depending on what he knows, he might wish to eliminate Clind. He already has two Authorities, what would prevent him from wanting a third?

“Roswaal. You probably can guess what I’m thinking. Care to elaborate on what my decision might be?” Subaru’s words broke Roswaal out of his musings.

Roswaal glanced around before shaking his head, as best as he could within such a tight grip, “Unfortunately noooooot. You seem like a reasonable man, however, my lack of knowledge due to Gluttony is neutering any sort of correct analysis. Care to illuminate us?”

His former lover is here. His former friends are here. He yearns for this place. I have the ad-

“I’m considering whether to slaughter you all or not,” Subaru’s tone was like someone pondering what meal they should eat for lunch, nonchalant and filled with zero concern.

…This was not what Roswaal expected.

------------------------------------------

Natsuki Subaru felt numb.

Well, not exactly.

He felt guilt, rage, sadness, and longing in droves.

But overall, he felt numb.

Everything was too loud.

The people around him, loud.

His inner voice, loud and rambling.

Noisy.

Annoying.

He wanted it all to stop.

He just wanted one voice, and not all this discordant sound.

But she was gone.

…He’d prefer the silence.

Subaru hummed, “Was that not what you were expecting, Roswaal?”

The mage only smiled but the slight twinge of his upper lip betrayed his true emotions, “Not at aaaaall. Though, I do consider it to be such an extreme decision. Our deaths would equate no benefit.”

“Hm, not quite. The benefit is that I don’t waste any more time on nonsense. Don’t worry, I’ll still keep my promise and help you. Once you’re in a new body.”

He’ll kill everyone in this mansion.

And then, figure out where Anastasia is.

And then everyone between here to her will die.

They either get out of his way.

Or die.

Simple and effective.

Roswaal tried to keep up the charade, “You would benefit more from us alive than dead. Think about it: a royal candidate, a mage with unequivocal arcane power, and much more. Such allies will bring you enormous benefit! Your goal, my goal, both can be obtainable. Will you really throw away such pieces on a whim?”

Subaru shrugged, “…I don’t care.”

Roswaal’s mask fractured, “You-“

“Roswaal. You seem to be misunderstanding me. Which is fine, many people do,” Subaru sighed, “You don’t realize what I’ve been through. What I care about. What I want. You assume a lot. You think people will always stay in their niche. It’s a bad habit of yours that hasn’t changed since a year ago.”

The wind howled through the gash in the wall; Subaru glanced to the side. He saw Rem’s Morningstar. He remembered polishing it all the time, thinking about her. Before that, he used to be afraid of it, the rumble of its chains always made him flinch with nausea.

Now?

…He didn’t care.

He saw himself reflected on the Morningstar. His hair was now longer, the white barely present besides a few strands here or there. His eyes no longer shined.

He glanced over to the other side.

Rem.

Fear. Rage. Sadness. Forgiveness. Love.

All feelings he once felt for her.

…Now nothing.

Subaru spoke with poise and care, “You are probably thinking I’m angry because of Gluttony. For being forgotten. Betrayed. That I want to burn the world down for it and everyone else can go to hell. That’s not true. In reality…nothing matters to me now. I don’t hate you. I don’t hate Emilia. I don’t hate Rem. I don’t hate anyone. Fact of the matter is…none of you mean anything to me anymore. I gave it all up, because it doesn’t matter in the long run. I don’t care about any of you. Anything or anyone. The only thing that matters…is her.”

Subaru was running out of time.

“…You are making a mistake,” Roswaal almost sounded pleading, “Do not be so rash. Your chances of her returning to you safely will increase with our involvement. Be reasonable!”

“I am thinking rationally. Every second I waste here is a second that Ana could suffer longer. I came here to save her family. To make her happy. I won’t let anything get in the way of that. In some ways, I think I can understand you a bit more…Roswaal.”

“What do you mean?”

“Your goal. To bring back the person you love no matter the cost. Before, I thought you were insane. That you were obsessive. That you were an evil piece of shit. Now? Well…”

Gone was the boy who arrived in Lugunica with delusions of grandeur.

Gone was the self-proclaimed knight who wanted to become someone important.

Gone was the man who would make Emilia the queen.

All that remained was the star who entered Hell willingly…and returned as a monster.

Subaru turned his head, his eyes finally reaching Roswaal, “…You and I are more alike than I once thought. We both fell in love with greedy people. We both chose to dedicate ourselves to those people. And we both would do whatever it takes to bring them back.”

His eyes stared into Roswaal’s soul, unflinching.

Roswaal could only stare back, wide eyed. He blinked.

…Zarestia. Halibel. Beatrice. It’s time. Anastasia awaits.

A cascade of conversations occurred within his Od between the three and their King. Within mere moments, they all consented to the order and were now primed to execute.

Subaru’s Od felt twisted. He never realized Basiliskos Ops could be used in this way. Authorities were more nuanced than he expected. Unfortunately, his body felt strained from its usage. He needed to settle all of this fast. Gain Clind’s Authority. And sacrifice everything between here to Anastasia. Time was ticking. He had no idea if Return by Death will work, he can’t risk perma-death and leave Anastasia alone. No looping until he understands what’s happening.

He remembered some of her last words to him, “I just don’t want to be alone.”

Roswaal. Pandora. Volcanica. It didn’t matter. Everything will die if it has to.

…He’ll make sure she never feels like that again.

He can’t make any mistakes here. No hesitation.

Subaru turned back to the opening in the wall, the wind soothed him, its roar blocking out the screams and outrage behind him. He could hear Roswaal’s bargaining and Emilia’s cries for Beatrice, fade away in his mind.

Soon. All the noise will be gone.

“…Boy…Boy!”

Subaru grasped his head, a sharp pain followed the voice that screeched in his head, he whispered to himself, “Echidna?”

“You fool, in your insanity, have you already forgotten me?”

“…Eridna,” Subaru pursed his lips, “I was wondering why I couldn’t hear you.”

“…Unlike Sister, it seems we have not bonded. Though at the very least, my connection to her Od allows me to speak to you.”

I’m surprised…though maybe I still consider you as a substitute for your mother. I’m sorry.

“If you are truly apologetic, stop this farce. This is not like you!”

…What do you know about me? I am not a child. I am not some lovesick puppy. Nor am I some kind of honorable knight…I haven’t been any of them for a while. A long while.

“…I know. But you aren’t like this. You aren’t a murderer. What would Ana think if she saw you as you are now?”

Subaru snarled in his head, Ana isn’t here! She’s gone!

Subaru’s hands gripped inward, drawing blood.

…And it’s all my fault. If only I was faster to notice. If only I got to Gluttony in time! If only I stopped getting distracted!

Subaru let the blood drip from his hands and onto the floor.

No more. I’m too slow. I have no time. I need to-

“ENOUGH!” Before Subaru could retort, Eridna’s voice startled him due to its intensity, “Ever since Ana started deteriorating—no—even before that, you have been acting irrationally impatient! You rushed all of us here without a thought or a plan! We barely just recovered from Ana’s near-death experience! Your constant desire to search for a solution has caused us issues. Instead of truly talking with Ana, all you did is push her into a corner, making her act hysterical.”

Subaru grit his teeth, She wouldn’t talk to me! What was I supposed to do?! Just let her family die?! Get forgotten into nothing?! Let her come with us when she is not mentally sound?! I can’t do that to her. I didn’t want to push her. I have to make her happy. I can’t let her get hurt. Not when she just got healthy. I don’t want her to cry all the time…

The numbness became worse.

…I don’t want her to suffer any more.

Eridna’s voice was drenched in empathy, speaking softly to him, “…Child. Please. Think. Take a step back. Take a breath. Ask yourself. What is it that you want?”

I already told you. I want Ana-

“No. What do YOU want? Not what will make Ana happy. What would make you happy? What is it that you are fighting for?”

…What do I want?

“Please. Su, just think of it. Remember what this was all for.”

I…I…

And then, Subaru remembered. Back during that week after Hell.

----------------------------

“My little Poobaru~!” Anastasia grabbed Subaru’s arm and held him close.

Subaru’s eyebrow twitched as he grabbed her body and spun her around, “My sweet, adorable, Ana-pop!”

Despite Anastasia’s wide smile, her upper lip was also twitching.

They were twirling down a busy street as many onlookers gawked at the sight. Old women snickered and smiled, men looked in disgust, and women smacked their boyfriends while pointing at the two stars being all lovey-dovey with each other.

“Hey Subaru? Do you know how much I love you?”

Subaru looked down and cocked his head, “Hm?”

She then let go of his arm and stretched her arms out, “This much!”

Subaru’s eyebrow kept twitching, he then did an exaggerated pose as he pretended to have a heart attack, “Ah! You’re too cute! My blood sugar! I’m practically getting diabetes!”

Anastasia’s eye was twitching like a madman as she ran up to hug him, “Well I got the cure for it right he-WOAH!”

Subaru interrupted her by quickly picking her up into a bridal carry, her eyes darted everywhere just as Subaru spoke low, looking into her eyes, “…Careful. Don’t want ya to fall out of heaven again, honey. Or I’ll end up falling in love with you. Again.”

Anastasia stared at him speechless before her face turned blushing red. Subaru chuckled as a passersby mimed vomiting in the background.

Anastasia ineffectually pounded on his chest, pouting, “…No fair. It’s cheating to use the ‘L’ word.”

Subaru laughed, as he kissed her forehead, “You snooze, you lose, Ana-pop. I won the game.”

Said game was one concocted by both of them. They would try to act as cringe and love-dovey as possible to get the other to fold. Whoever lost would have to follow the other’s date plan for the day. The winner also got bragging rights.

The added bonus is that both of them found the reactions of the people around them incredibly hilarious.

Subaru skipped with happiness holding his fiancé while she kept pouting with her arms crossed, “I swear, you were never this smooth before.”

Subaru gave her a cheeky smirk, “I think you have bad memory. I’ve always been this smooth.”

“Tch. Just you wait, the next date is mine.”

Subaru rolled his eyes playfully, “Whatever you say Ana-pop.”

She started swiping at his face as he spun her around, dodging her hands while laughing like a maniac.

Her eyes started to spin, “S-subaru!”

“What? Can’t hear you! Ya gotta speak up!”

Anastasia narrowed her eyes. She grabbed his face and immediately kissed him on the lips, stopping the boy in his tracks.

Instead of getting embarrassed like she expected, he instead fully reciprocated the kiss…deeply.

It immediately made her separate from him, blushing madder than before, “W-wait, wait, wait!”
Subaru put on the puppy eyes, “You didn’t like it?”

Anastasia’s face paled, she then shook her head rapidly while waving her hands, “No, no! That’s not-I mean. Yes, I did like it! It’s just…people. People are everywhere and I mean…”

Anastasia stopped talking. She squinted. Subaru was smiling like an asshole.

Anastasia muttered, “You are such an asshole.”

Subaru accepted his assholery, shrugging, “I’m your asshole. Though not actually. I’d smell like shit.”

Anastasia stifled a laugh, punching his chest, “Gross.”

“Can’t a guy be a little crude with his wife.”

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “We’re not married yet.”

“We’re basically married at this point.”

“I want a divorce then.”

Subaru nuzzled her neck, “Unfortunate. I’ll be taking the house then. And Halibel. And Tia. And Beako. And Scarfdona.”

“…So, you’re taking everything then.”

“Hey, you taught me to be greedy.”

Anastasia sighed, “I’ve taught you to well it seems. Well, I guess we should stay together then. Not like anyone else could stand your personality, unlike me.”

“I feel like that’s what I should say.”

She swiped at him, he dodged, “Dick.”

Subaru raised his eyebrows seductively, saying quite loudly, “…I mean if you really want to, we can just head back hom-“

She smacked his chest this time, blushing for the third time in the last hour, she whisper-shouted, “You idiot, we are in public!”

Subaru just hummed as he kept bridal carrying her through the streets, “And? Let the world be graced by my love for you!”

Anastasia visibly shuddered, “Romantic as that was, please don’t say it like that again.”

“You’re right, I was channeling too much of Julius there.”

“Julius is not that cringe.”

“Agree to disagree. Also, great use of that word I taught ya.”

Anastasia hung her arms around Subaru’s neck as she looked forward, “You’re not the only one who is learning quickly. By the way, what’s the date plan?”

Subaru adjusted his grip, “I’m thinking we just head to the river and relax while eating some of the snacks and lunch we brought with us.”

He nudged his head to the bag hanging on his back, containing some drinks and rice balls.

Anastasia laid her head on his chest, “That simple?”

Subaru shrugged, “…I guess I just want to take it easy for a bit. Just hang out and talk with you all day. It’s…been a while, you know?”

Anastasia looked at him oddly, “…Okay. Ah don’t mind talkin’ with ya forever.”

Subaru grinned, “Don’t tell me your bringing back the accent for today.”

“It is a classic.”

“If you do it, I’ll do it. An’ aie don’ta think y’all like-“

“Okay, okay! Nope! Vetoing that!” Anastasia cupped her hand over his mouth, “Remind me to teach you how to do a proper Kararagi accent later.”

Subaru snickered, “Can’t wait Ana-pop. I always liked your private lessons.”

Anastasia ignored him and simply pointed forward, “Alright, enough innuendos, march on my noble steed!”

Subaru rolled his eyes, “I’m not an earth dragon.”

Anastasia looked at him with a smug expression, “But I do ride you all the time~.”

Subaru choked, blushing, “T-that was a cheap shot!”

Anastasia waved her hands in the air playfully, “You snooze, you lose, as you say.”

Subaru spun her around in retaliation as they both giggled their way down the streets, in their own little world.

Subaru carried her the whole way to the riverside park. The place was pretty popular, multiple families and couples were already there to relax under the sun, having picnics or going on walks, some were even swimming. The river was quite small, leading to a pond which then led to a series of canals that stretched towards the Great Waterfall.

Subaru brought Anastasia to a nearby tree and sat down quickly, leaning onto it, with her still in his arms.

“Oh!” Anastasia spoke with alarm, “Subaru. You could have just let me down beforehand.”

Subaru smiled, he winced through the ass pain, “Hey, guys get a plus ten to their strength ability score when carrying a beautiful lady. It was easy carrying you the whole way.”

Anastasia stared at him, “I meant when we arrived. You nearly broke your butt.”

Subaru’s smile became more sheepish, “Ah. Well, okay, yeah you got a point.”

She smiled back at him before tapping his cheek softly and then sliding down to rest her head on his thighs. Along the way, she spoke, “Don’t do it again. What would I do if you lost one of your greatest assets.”

Subaru ran his fingers through her hair, evidently feeling nice as her smile got even brighter, “Pfft. Nice wordplay there.”

She laid there, using him as a lap pillow contently, “You should catch up. Otherwise, I’ll be the one winning the future contests.”

“Mhm, mhm,” Subaru hummed as he took out some onigiri from the bag and started feeding some to Anastasia, he held it as she took a bite, “But it’s not like I’ll need it until I’m a Dad.”

Anastasia raised an eyebrow as she chewed and swallowed, “What do you mean by that?”

Subaru bit into his own onigiri, “Well, back in Japan, we have a thing called Dad-humor. Mostly involves wordplay that makes you cringe. So, when you get a kid, you have to start getting good at making those bad puns all the time. My dad used to say them to me when I was younger.”

Subaru shivered from all the Pokémon related puns his dad would tell him. Subaru never liked them. He was more of a Digimon fan, unfortunately.

Anastasia giggled, she then thought for a moment, “Hey, Subaru?”

Subaru took another bite, “Yeah?”

“How many kids do you want?”

Subaru immediately choked, “W-What?”

Anastasia grinned, “How. Many. Kids. Do. You. Want?”

Subaru’s eyes darted around, “…How many do you want?”

“This ain’t a trick question you little shit,” she opened her mouth.

Subaru stared for a second before his eyes widened. He gave her another bite of the onigiri.

Subaru answered while she was busy devouring the riceball, “Well, if I had to choose, maybe two?”

“Hm, why?”

“…Well, if we ever get busy. I’d kind of like them to not be lonely.”

Anastasia giggled, “I like that answer.”

Subaru scratched his neck awkwardly, “So how many do you want?”

“One is perfect for me. Maybe two. I don’t want too many. I think I might die.”

Subaru saluted her, “Well I thank you for your future service.”

Anastasia sat up and crawled next to Subaru, putting her head on the crook of his neck while Subaru put his arm around her naturally, she spoke softly, “Well don’t thank me just yet. We still have to go through the process.”

Subaru chuckled, “You’re right about that…do you know what names you would want?”

Anastasia put a finger to her chin, “Hm, I’ve never thought of that actually. Maybe…Nikolai?”

Subaru gave her a look, “How is it that you know so many Russian names?”

Anastasia also gave him a look, “Russia? Is that a place near Japan?”

Subaru waved his hand in the air, “Kind of. I’ll explain later. They’re kind of complicated. But there is a famous person who has the same name as you from there.”

Anastasia perked up, “Oh really? What are they famous for?”

“…On second thought, I’ll also explain that later.”

Anastasia pouted, “Dangerous?”

“Eh, more. Just not really a good story for a date.”

Anastasia nestled closer to Subaru, “Fine, fine. But how about you? I know for certain you’ve thought of this before.”

Subaru rubbed her arm, “You know me so well. But yeah, I have. I’ve always been partial to Spica or Rigel.”

“Star names, right? Are they related to ours?”

Subaru thought for a moment, “…No. They’re not. Actually, that’s a good point. Maybe we should continue the theme.”

Anastasia giggled, “So, are there any mythological children of Atlas and Pleione.”

Subaru reached deep into his astronomical knowledge, “Well, besides my name, there were two other groups of stars—or I guess— children. The Hesperides and the Hyades.”

Anastasia frowned, “Is there any way we can make it sound better like yours?”

Subaru also frowned, “Maybe. We can shorten Hyades to Hya, which means rain. As for Hesperides, we can turn it into Vesper, a more Roman Version. It means ‘the evening star.’”

Anastasia nodded in approval, “I like them. Hya if we have a girl. Vesper if we have a boy.”

Subaru felt warm, “…I can’t wait.”

They both sat under the tree as people walked by them, warm breezes drifting by.

“…Hey Subaru.”

“Yeah, Ana-pop.”

“I love you.”

“…I love you too.”

Anastasia’s voice was soft but music to his ears, “So, my wonderful Poobaru. What’s next on the agenda?”

Honestly, Subaru just wanted to sit here and chat. But there were so many other possibilities. So many ideas he had.

All he could say was, “I have no idea. Too many to choose.”

She tapped him on the nose, “Well, its not like we have only today to do them. So come on. Tell me what you want to do. You earned it for winning the bet.”

He did. He really did win, didn’t he? Won despite the odds.

His thoughts drifted to the many hopes and dreams he built up from the time he spent in that Hell loop.

Natsuki Subaru knew what he wanted.

The noise…most of it was gone.

Back in the present, his lips moved without him thinking, “I want…

-------------------------------------

Roswaal Mathers was grasping for straws, trying to dodge Zarestia’s attacks as he now covered himself in a barrier of stone and wind, her wind blades getting deflected as she tried to cleave right through him.

He needed to calm the boy down. He can’t have Subaru kill everyone here.

Out of the corner of his eye, he could see Emilia pleading with Beatrice while covering herself in ice armor, breaking any Minya crystals with a staff of frost. Clind was able to keep up with Halibel’s clones, only barely dodging the killing curses. The butler could easily match the shinobi if he let loose…but it was too soon. Despite the kill order, it seems the three companions of Subaru were holding back. Beatrice wasn’t spamming nearly as much magic as she potentially could, the main body of Halibel was simply observing, and Zarestia could easily shred this whole mansion, only releasing a few wind blades and a bundle of bloodlust.

Either the three are playing with their food or something is going on with the boy.

He needed to find a way to prevent the mansion inhabitants’ deaths. It would be…inefficient. Yes. Inefficient. He still needed Ram. He still needed Emilia. He still needed them all.

His death wouldn’t matter, Annerose was primed for his transfer at any time.

…A pity. He did not want Annerose to have her childhood end so early.

His sins are endless it seems, too entwined with his desires.

Speaking of, what could calm Subaru down? What is it that the boy wants exactly? The fact he didn’t immediately order a mass killing. The fact he took the time to explain to Roswaal his reasoning. The fact the three power companions aren’t going all-out. It doesn’t add up.

Roswaal took the direct approach, “Subaru. This is an extreme reaction. There are numerous alternative solutions to your predicament. Tell me: what is it that you want? You say you do not have a grudge nor a reason to kill, then you should just leave! If it’s a time issue, then you are already wasting it! You do not even know where she is, so this is pointless! So, tell me, what do you truly wish to gain from all of this?!”

A reaction, a twitch, anything, he just needed a way to gain some leverage and information.

I’ve already surmised he has an ability to return back in time based on that argument of theirs. But when has he used it? How many times? Has this whole scenario been played out already? Is that why the three are being cautious? Perhaps we won beforehand. Now, they are trying to find a way to-

Suddenly, the noise of battle ceased. Zarestia’s wind calmed in an instant.

Roswaal, confused, lowered his barrier slightly and saw…nothing. The three companions of Subaru had stopped fighting, all turning towards their leader and staring at him with different expressions. Halibel’s was unreadable, Tia’s was morose, and Beatrice was sobbing.

Before he could even say anything, before Emilia or Clind could break out of their astonishment, Subaru spoke clearly.

“I want…to go on a date with my wife.”

…What?

What?

“What?” “What?” “What?” Roswaal, Emilia, and Clind said in unison.

The star’s haori flowed, slowly, the wind blowing like a calm breeze, “I want to go on another date with Ana. A fifth. Sixth. Seventh. Eighth! I want to go on hundreds of dates with her! I want to go eat and share ice cream. Not just ice cream. All kinds of food. Okonomiyaki again. Sushi. Yakiniku. Everything I can ever remember. I want to relax in a library, wrapped in blankets, and fall asleep next to her while we talk and read. I want to tell her about all the stupid manga I read: Dragon Ball, One Piece, Bleach and more. I want to tell her all the dumb jokes I made up in the last week. All the puns I’ve been thinking of. I want her to laugh. So that she can smile more. I want to wake up every morning to her smile. I feel like a flower when it comes to her bright smile. I want her to smile on her wedding day. I want to have Ricardo take her down the aisle, the Triplets as the ring bearers, and…even Julius as one of my groomsmen. I want to burn her image, wearing a wedding gown and dress, into my mind so that I don’t ever forget. I want to have two kids, so that they won’t ever be alone if Ana and I aren’t there. I want Beako to spoil them rotten. I want Halibel and I to have a drink while I complain about how my kids are growing up too fast. I want Tia to complain to me about my kids being lame and how she’ll kill whoever touches them. I want the two to grow up healthy and happy, finding their own purposes in life. Fall in love. Make their own families. I want to tease Ana about her gray hair, while she teases me back that I’ve always had it. I want to remind her how beautiful she looks even as we both wrinkle into old age. I want to die, hand in hand with her…and then. When we are reborn, I want to fall in love with her all over again.”

Roswaal could see something drip onto the floor.

It was tears.

Subaru was crying.

----------------------------------

How long has it been since he cried?

Actually cried.

Years? It felt like it.

Subaru brought a hand up to his cheek. He looked at his wet fingers. He remembered the tears coming out when he proposed to Anastasia. But those were happy tears. This? It’s been years since he felt so melancholic. Because sadness didn’t prevent death. Only action.

The words kept spilling out, none of it organized, all of it from his soul, “…I want to go home. I want Ana to meet my parents. My mom would probably get along with her immediately. My dad would probably tease me about her, relentlessly. I’ll get annoyed by them monopolizing my wife. I’ll get embarrassed. I’ll get jealous. I’ll be…normal. I want things to be normal, for once,” Subaru chuckled sadly as he tried to imagine it all.

It was so hard. Because it felt so unrealistic.

He wishes he was normal again. He wishes everything was less complicated. He wishes…he met Anastasia earlier. He wishes he was someone she could love back then. He knows she wouldn’t fall in love with who he was before. It scares him. Because Subaru knows he would have fallen for her immediately. It doesn’t matter either way.

Because he can’t change the past.

This was his life now. A broken mess of a person who somehow was able to save the love of his life. Only for tragedy to strike him again and again and again. He can’t ever catch a break. He can’t ever be happy. He didn’t even want to leave Banan.

Subaru couldn’t stop the cascade even if he tried, “…If I could spend forever just being with Ana, I would take it in a heartbeat. No Gluttony. No Royal Selection. No worries about the Cult or some fucked up hidden conspiracy. Just me and Ana spending our lives together with the people we love. That’s all I want…the only thing I want.”

Because even whatever remaining time they may have left in their short lives, isn’t enough. He wanted their love to last…forever.

He was greedy…so greedy.

Subaru almost glanced over his shoulder.

He didn’t know how, but Subaru could feel like Emilia was trying to walk up to him, only to be stopped by Beatrice.

Good on the little Spirit. Whatever comfort Emilia could provide would never work on him anymore. He was tired. Tired of this whole journey. Of suffering. Of sacrifice. Of everything.

He just wanted to take his fiancé and leave all of it behind.

He wiped his tears with his hand.

…I’m sorry…I guess I’m just tired. I don’t want to do this anymore. I just want this to be all over. Quick. So, I can finally rest.

Eridna’s own melancholy echoed through him, “…I am sorry too, Subaru.”

Don’t be.

He could feel Roswaal motion forward, behind him, and try to open his mouth.

…Only for nothing to come out.

Subaru nearly laughed out of absurdity.

Speechless, huh? I guess you’re disappointed your ace in the hole is a broken mess who wants something so stupid.

“Um…” the voice made Subaru glance to the side. He poked his head out the door and saw a familiar face down the hall.

Sharp teeth, calm but concerned demeanor, and a professional attitude.

Frederica stood there slightly confused, “…Would our guests like to have some tea?”

Subaru looked over at everyone.

The hallway was a mess, the walls and floors filled with gashes and holes from the short fight, debris scattered everywhere.

Halibel was helping Clind up from the floor while Tia walked over to pick up Beatrice. Emilia stood nearby, awkwardly healing some wound on her arm, her gaze darting to Subaru every once in a while.

Roswaal seemed to be deep in thought. Most likely thinking of a scheme or something.

Subaru then turned back to Frederica; he tried to smile in order to calm her nerves.

It seemed to have done nothing but Frederica still tried to smile back, polite as always.

Subaru sighed, “I think some tea and…a chat would be nice.”

Notes:

AN: 33 chapters! Ah, so exciting. If anyone here hasn't been reading my updates on my social media, this story is around a little over halfway done. The max chapters I have planned are 50-60, give or take. It might extend or shorten depending on the pace i want. It feels insane to me that its been nearly six months since I started, and so many of you have enjoyed it!

I want to say thank you again for supporting me this whole time, your comments as well as your love have been one of the greatest motivations for me to continue this story. I'm sure a lot of you have felt like this story beats you over the head with angst, sadness, and emotional mayhem. The cliffhangers don't help either. But I want you all to know...I'm glad you are able to feel the emotions I wanted you to experience. To feel how Subaru feels. To be angry, sad, tired, happy. One of my biggest goals in writing is to have all my readers connect with the story on a personal level and want to see and root for the characters every step of the way. So thank you all for sticking by and enjoying my work. I hope you will enjoy as this story reaches its climax and as I get to the moments I've been planning since the beginning. Stay tuned for more!

Chapter 34: I Choose to be Kind

Summary:

Subaru and Roswaal have a talk, but first, Subaru needs to confide in his friends for once...

Chapter Text

“Would you all like anything else?”

“…That will be all, Frederica,” Roswaal waved his hand as Frederica bowed and left them all to their business. Emilia had already absconded earlier, taken somewhere safe as she had no purpose in their discussions, only dragged into the situation by circumstance.

…Not the kind of reunion I wanted.

Before Frederica left she looked towards Subaru, “By the way, Joshua Juukuulius is currently being occupied in one of our other rooms. I found him looking quite disheveled earlier and I gave him some refreshments to calm his nerves. Would you like me to escort him here?”

Subaru blinked. His eyes then widened as he thought, Oh shit! I forgot about Joshua!

The poor boy must have been still hiding behind a couch when he and Anastasia were having a fight.

Subaru grimaced, “No. I think he doesn’t need to be here. We’ll go find him before our business finishes…thank you Frederica. It was very kind of you to do that.”

Frederica smiled a toothy grin, though she quickly hid it with her hand, “Think nothing of it. It is a maid’s duty to serve their guests as best as possible.”

Subaru tried to refrain from retorting, Tell that to Ram next time she ‘disappears’ when we have people over.

Subaru blinked. We…right. Not we. You all. Not me.

The sound of the door closing refocused Subaru’s attention on the two in front of him. Roswaal Mathers sat casually with his hand resting on his face while Clind sat next to him, back straight and hands placed neatly on his lap.

Subaru tapped his foot, “So…what now?”

“Now we…” Roswaal seemed to be still at a loss for words, “We talk.”

Beatrice sat on Tia’s lap, sitting right beside Subaru who was wedged between the Great Spirit of Murder and the Admirer. The companions chose to keep quiet, letting Subaru take the reins of the conversation.

Subaru eyed the mage suspiciously, “About what? I’m surprised you’re even letting us sit here in the first place.”

Roswaal rubbed his throat, still slightly bruised, “Would you expect me to simply throw you away? It would be illogical. Despite your noticeably volatile emotional status, I still believe an alliance would be fruitful.”

The clown smiled as if Subaru hadn’t just threatened to murder everyone with extreme prejudice.

Subaru lifted up a cup of tea and started to drink, his other hand felt cold and empty. The tea felt familiar. It was the good blend, the one Ram kept hidden from him after Subaru took it one too many times. Nostalgia radiated his bones.

Clind spoke next, “If you are worried about your wife, I would not be so rash to believe her whereabouts are impossible to uncover. Vainglory may seem all-encompassing. But it has limits. She cannot do the impossible. Sympathetic.”

Roswaal added on, “And given her exact words, ‘the cradle of souls,’ I have an inkling of an idea of where she might be.”

Subaru almost spilled his teacup, his arm almost reflexively tossing it at the person in front of him. All of Subaru’s instincts were firing. He wanted to throttle Roswaal and make him spill the truth. It took all of his willpower to calm down. It was not the time.

…I really am messed up.

Subaru grit his teeth, “I’m guessing you’ll want us to make an oath, a more strict contract so what happened last time doesn’t happen again.”

Roswaal smiled, shrugging with exaggeration, “You cannoooooot blame me for feeling a little betrayed by your actions.”

To be fair, Subaru fully intended on fulfilling Roswaal’s goal and reviving his beloved Echidna. It’s just that Subaru would only do so after getting Anastasia back. By paving a road of corpses.

“That’s fair, but what is it that you exactly want? Is this a contract where you have complete control over me? A contract where my allies and I have to follow your every word?” Subaru motioned towards his friends.

Roswaal cocked his head, “It seems my past self has made quite a bad impression.”

“You did try to corner me and make me submit to following your fake gospel like it was God.”

The clown chuckled, his eyebrow twitched slightly, “And I can imagine exactly how that turned out. No. Nothing like that. The contract will replace the original I placed onto myself. The parameters will be simple: we shall support each other’s goals and be unable to actively hinder each other in anyway. Conscious or otherwise.”

There’s probably more to it than that. I wish Ana was here. She could probably go through the whole thing and point out any loopholes…

Subaru thought for a moment, “…Do you mind if we get some time to think?”

Roswaal waved his hand to the door, “Feel free to use any of our rooms.”

Subaru glanced at his companions, “Actually, I think we’ll just stay in the room and huddle in a nearby corner.”

“Hm, well. Whatever makes you comfortable~,” Roswaal picked up his teacup as Subaru and his three companions stood and walked to a corner in the room.

Beatrice quickly put up an El Silen bubble.

Tia crossed her arms, “So. We killing them or not?”

Subaru shook his head, “No. I wasn’t thinking straight. We need their help if we’re going to go save Ana. I was too overwhelmed and made you guys follow my rash decisions.”

Tia looked straight at her contractor, “So what? We had to get Ana back. It was their fault that they let some asshole into their home and took her. It would be better to kill them all than anything else. I wanted to kill that clown since the beginning. His smell, the alcohol, his stupid beard. Disgusting.”

Tia clicked her tongue in irritation. Subaru had felt her irritation gnawing at the back of his head for a while now, he’s grateful that she has been learning to rein in her bloodlust better.

Subaru sighed, “It’s not that simple I…”

I don’t want to be responsible for making you all into monsters like me.

He almost choked on his words as Tia put a hand on his shoulder, “Su. We will follow whatever you decide.”

That made him actually choke, his voice breaking as the words tumbled out, “…That’s the problem. I don’t think you should follow my every word.”

“Su-“

Subaru grabbed her hand and let it gently down as he continued, “This isn’t about me. I’m not okay. I’m not okay at all. I don’t know what I’m doing. I have no idea how to get Ana back. I barely understand why the Witch Cult wants her or who the fuck this Pandora person is. I’ve been scrambling to figure out solutions for so long. I’m just. Tired. So…tired. I don’t think you should trust me to make rational decisions right now…so I’m going to let you guys decide.”

I still don’t understand why you guys trust me so much. I haven’t done anything to earn it.

Throughout all those countless loops. He never questioned it. Their loyalty. Why they would follow a loser like him. He was too focused on the goal. On saving her. And now?

 

He didn’t know what to do.

Tears dotted Subaru’s eyes, he wiped them quickly and finished what he needed to say, “I shouldn’t be leading you guys anymore. I’ve been just throwing shit at the wall, just to see what works. And look what happened because of it? Sure, we got here faster than ever possible. But I ended up ignoring Ana’s mental wellbeing. I ended up ignoring everyone else’s wishes. And now we are worse off than before, I don’t even know what’s happening with Julius and the others. I’m not smart enough for this…”

He felt so lost. His eyes were firmly planted on the ground, not wanting to look any of them in the eyes.

Seconds passed as he expected them all to finally tell him their grievances, cursing him out for being such a pathetic waste of a person.

Only for Halibel to ask him an odd question, “Su-san. Do you remember what I told ya when we first met?”

Subaru looked up, brows furrowed, “You said that I have a natural disposition for gettin’ mugged.”

Halibel blinked and then laughed, “Seems we have a different way of rememberin’ thin’s. What I said was that ya have haunted eyes but a kind heart.’ A rarity in this period of time.”

Subaru flinched, forgetting that both were technically true. They were both phrases that were first told to Subaru when he met the Admirer just a few months ago.

Halibel didn’t seem to notice or simply let it pass, “Most people I know with such eyes don’t have such proclivities. Their heart, their soul. It gets corrupted. They get stuck in the mire of revenge. Twisted. Wanting to ruin the world for ruinin’ them. And based on yer stories, I could hardly blame ya for wanting the same. But you didn’t. And so, I used to admire ya for such a trait.”

Subaru knew what was coming, “And now?”

“…And now I admire ya for different reasons. I admire how straightforward and casual ya can be. I admire how lively ya are despite all that happens. I admire how ya quickly made sure Tia felt safe in our house, gettin’ rid of any and all alcohol when you noticed how she hated it. I admire how yer so forgivin’ ta those that hurt ya, ta Beatrice, despite how easy it would be to hate. I admire how ya thought I was flirting with women every time I complimented them. I thought that was hilarious.”

Subaru’s eye twitched. He recently learned that all those people in Banan, even that one married couple, were familiar with Halibel. None of them took his flirting to heart, or at the very least they did not take it as sexual or romantic. They took his flirting, his admiration, as harmless. Because it was pure. The Admirer loved the people around him, and they in turned loved him equally.

Subaru couldn’t help but laugh, “To be fair, you can probably tell I’m not that experienced with women.”

Halibel chuckled in agreement, “And yet, you were able to still attract the attention of ole Ana-bo. That’s a mighty feat given how you both have such different personalities on the outset.”

“…I still don’t understand really. Even now. She deserves better. There are others that fit with her better or compliment her personality more.”

Halibel shook his head, “Maybe so. Maybe there are better matches for her. Perhaps. Perhaps not. Who cares? I told ya Su-san, those are just possibilities. Not reality. We can argue semantics forever but what matters most is what has been done. At the end of the day, Ana-bo chose ya. And yer heart chose her. Yer heart chose her over kindness.”

Subaru felt his guts twist, “But isn’t that the problem? I’m so laser focused on her. I ended up tunnel visioning and messing everything up because of it. I nearly made you guys kill a whole mansion of innocent people because I couldn’t be bothered to wait!”

Halibel shrugged, “And?”
Subaru stared at him, “You should be telling me I’m insane! That I shouldn’t be making such decisions in the first place!”

Halibel motioned towards Tia, “You expect a Great Spirit, specifically one with more bloodlust than the most deranged serial killers in history, to believe yer insane for wanting to kill a bunch of people she doesn’t care about.”

Tia nodded, “Just say the word and I’ll paint the walls red.

He then pointed at Beatrice, “You expect an artificial spirit who doesn’t care about anyone other than her previous contractor to have any sympathy for the people that also abandoned ya.”

Beatrice looked away, “…Betty would do whatever it takes for her Subaru, I suppose.”

Halibel then pointed to himself, “And you expect me, an assassin, to value others over my own wards. Wards I’ve sworn to protect under all costs.”

Subaru hesitated, “…We never discussed extending our agreement.”

“Because I never intended on endin’ it,” Halibel raised a hand, seemingly expecting Subaru’s response, “I ain’t doin’ this out of obligation. Nor am I doin’ this because you did somethin’ stupendous or awe-inspiring to garner such intense loyalty.”

Halibel walked over and placed his hand on Subaru’s shoulder, eyeing him straight, and speaking softly, “I’m willin’ to do this because I like ya.”

Subaru gawked, “…That’s it?”

Halibel smiled, his irises peaking through his eyelids, warm as the lazy summer sun, “There is no greater reason. Can’t a man want to help a friend in need?”

Subaru was speechless.

He was reminded of a time where a another loyal friend of his gave him a similar speech…and a punch to the face.

Halibel patted him on the shoulder, “This road may be bloody. It might be twisted and filled with turmoil. But it ain’t one I regret takin’. Talkin’ with ya, watchin’ ya grow with Ana-bo, seein’ how life is with everyone here. I don’t mind just relaxin’ in Banan with ya until death do us part. So, stand proud with us. Don’t fear takin’ a step forward. We won’t abandon ya. Even if ya can’t tell us everything, we’ll carry your burdens. Until the future is as bright and shinin’ as before.”

“…Is that really what you all want?” Subaru looked around to the others.

Tia sighed, “Su. You think too much, like Ana. I’m not here to just kill. I’m not here because I owe ya for saving my light ball. I’m here because I like being around you. It’s why I made a contract with you. I could easily sever it anytime, but I don’t want to. Because life would be boring without you and that little greedy gremlin…I don’t want to go back to just killing all the time. I want to kill and be with you all. No matter what.”

“But there are tons of other people who can do the same thing-“ Subaru’s words were stopped by Tia’s fingers, clamping his mouth shut.

Her brows furrowed with irritation, “I swear, you infected Ana with this annoying self-hatred didn’t you? You need to shut up and accept that I have free will! I don’t need to find someone better. Or have you convince me to stay! I do what I want. I am free to do as I please. And if that is choosing you, then you better just accept it! Stop second guessing yourself or thinking I deserve better! It’s the same problem as Ana; you both don’t realize that life isn’t about doing what’s perfect. It’s about choosing and believing and accepting. I want to be with you and these other dumbasses. That’s it. Nothing else. Nothing more. Understand?!”

Subaru stared into her frustrated eyes before nodding slowly, not able to properly respond.

Her rage disappeared as she smiled happily, taking her fingers off.

“Good, now stop being stupid and address the little idiot finally,” with those words, Tia stepped back and in the same motion, pushed Beatrice forward with her foot, making the little spirit panic visibly.

Subaru looked down at Beatrice, “Beako.”

The little spirit flinched, “Yes, in fact?”

“…You know what Ana knows, don’t you.”

“…Yes, in fact.”

“…”

“…”

“…I’m sorry.”

Beatrice nearly stumbled back, “Wait, no-“

Subaru got on one knee, “Please. I want to apologize. I know you don’t want me to. That you don’t deserve it. But I need to.”

“…Okay, I suppose.” Beatrice grabbed the hem of her dress, nervously.

“I’ve been neglecting you,” Subaru’s eyes started to water as he saw Beatrice looked to disagree, “I have. I’ve been so focused on everything. So focused on trying to help with the new company, dating Ana, trying to survive. I haven’t tried to reconnect with you as much as I should. And it’s not for any good reason.”

“…”

“Beako I…I don’t want you to feel hurt anymore. I forgive you. And it’s not your fault-“

“Please don’t say that,” Beatrice’s voice wavered.

“Beako…”

“Betty doesn’t want to hear that!” Beatrice’s throat was hoarse, as if every word was choked out, “Betty…Betty knows how you are. Betty can guess…so much.”

How Subaru might have used Return by Death, or at least what she thinks it is. How often he did it. Beatrice isn’t stupid.

Beatrice continued, “Betty knows, and Betty can guess how much pain you’ve been through. Before, during, and after the prison. But Betty doesn’t want pity, in fact. Betty…wants to be worthy. It’s not realistic. It’s not what you want. But Betty wants to feel…proud to stand by your side. Please don’t forgive Betty, I suppose. Ever.”

He held out his hand, she hesitated, her hand shaking, as she reached out and touched his.

Her hand.

It was so small when compared to his. He kept forgetting. Despite how old she may be, that Beatrice was still like a child in so many ways.
“Then tell me. What do you want Beako?”

“…”

Beatrice was silent. It seems she herself didn’t know.

However, an idea struck within Subaru’s mind.

As if a thought occurred that he never realized until now.

He knew. It’s just he never was able to put it into words.

Ana hating herself.

Subaru hating himself.

Beatrice hating herself.

We’re all the same aren’t we. Trying to chase happiness. Trying to live up to that ideal we set ourselves out to be. Trying to be someone worthy of others. And they’re love. It’s a never-ending cycle.

“…Beako. We can’t live like this,” Subaru sat down and crossed his legs, trying his best to be on the same eye-level as his little spirit, “Ana. Me. You. We can’t…live like this.”

Roswaal. Felix. And so many others. We’re all the same.

Beatrice looked up, trying to form words but not knowing what exactly to say, “…”

“Are we just going to constantly hate ourselves for existing? For being…human. For not being perfect. For making mistakes. Is that our wholes lives? What is it worth? Are we just going to choose to be unhappy?”

“Subaru…”

Subaru held her little hands tenderly, “We can’t Beako…we just, can’t. We can’t live like this forever. And I don’t want to anymore. I don’t want to suffer anymore for the people around me. I don’t want to suffer and go after some stupid vague happy ending. I don’t want to be anyone else; I want to be me! The me who is here, right now, happy with you all.”

Perhaps this didn’t make sense to anyone else. But it made sense to him. And perhaps that was enough.

He just wished he could tell this all to Anastasia.

Subaru tried his best to keep the tears in, “…I want to love. And be loved. I want to go on dates. I want to laugh and play around with you. I want to hang out with Halibel. I want to cook food with Tia. We can’t live on this guilt anymore. We have to be…kind. Kind to ourselves for once.”

No more. It was time for him to finally take on the task he originally set himself out to do. For Anastasia. For himself.

Subaru wiped his eyes and spoke his final words, “Don’t focus on what is or what isn’t. Tell me. What do you want?”

Beatrice’s eyes widened. Her butterfly irises flocked in every direction, trying to find the solution to the question he had given her. Only to refocus finally on Subaru.

“Betty…” Beatrice swallowed, tears dripping out slightly, “Betty wants…I want. To be loved. I want to be loved too. Betty wants to love you. And be loved by you. Even if you never forgive me. Even if Betty never forgives herself. I want to…choose you. I want to choose you again. In spite of Betty’s sins, Betty wants to always choose you. Until the bitter end, in fact.”

Forgiveness. Right and wrong. Revenge.

It all doesn’t matter. Not anymore.

Subaru…wants to be happy.

He’ll choose to be happy.

Subaru smiled, “…Then I’ll choose you. And you’ll choose me.”

Beatrice sobbed, nearly wailing, “…Subaru!”

Running into his arms and hugging him, as he hugged her back, he patted her head softly.

When this is all over…I’ll find a way to make a contract with you. Both you and Tia.

Despite having her around, it never felt like they could truly go back to the way things were. But maybe that was okay. Maybe they were going about things the wrong way. Maybe it was time to move forward, instead of being stuck in the past.

He could feel Eridna connect to him through physical contact.

…Am I making the right decisions?

He could hear her soothing voice, “Child. If Ana were to see you now, she would be immensely proud.”

Subaru felt his heart feel so warm, I don’t know what I’m doing.

“Does anyone? What matters is that despite how many times you have fallen, you still try your best. You seem to have forgotten why that girl loved you so much. Your ability to be kind within the muck of despair. Do not ever doubt who you are in the dark.”

Subaru could feel two hands on his head, one rough and furry while the other soft and ethereal. Both warm. Pleasant. And somehow…it felt like they’ve been at his side since forever. Even though they only met recently.

Halibel’s voice reverberated, “When we felt yer emotions rush into us…I realized one more trait of yers that I admire.”

Subaru looked up and saw Halibel’s cheeky grin.

“…Yer weak. But you still keep tryin’. You don’t know what to do. But ya still try. Yer clueless. Yer stupid. Yer a loser. But you still try. Can’t help but admire a fool who still gives their best effort despite everythin’ in the world tellin’ ya otherwise. Fools with kind hearts have the greatest ability to shake the world. Because they don’t give up, when all else fails.”

Tia’s voice was soft, despite her ever-present bloodlust, it felt like a calm breeze in a maelstrom of violence, “Even I want to try. Because if someone lame like you keeps trying, why shouldn’t I? I can’t give up…because you and Ana didn’t. You both never give up.”

She never did, did she? Anastasia Hoshin. Even when Subaru saw her at her worst, she was still scrounging to survive. In Lugunica. In Kararagi. In every loop he ever saw her. He couldn’t help but admire her for that.

…He wants to tell her that.

Subaru began to stand up, “Thank you guys…I think this was good. I think I needed to take a step back and just…talk.”

Halibel chuckled, “We’ve been waitin’ for that. Just wanted you to make the first move.”

…Ha. Maybe I haven’t learned a thing. Not since Sanctuary. Not since I came to this world. Here I am, ignoring the love of people around me. Just like I did with my parents.

“So, what are we going to do about them?” Tia pointed a thumb at Roswaal and Clind, “I still think we can just kill the both of them and move on. They both give me the creeps.”

Tia shuddered as Subaru thought for a moment.

“…We’ll take the contract. Despite how I think we might get screwed in the fine print, I’ll just have to try my best. We need fire support and resources. If Ros-chi can supply those, it will make getting Ana and her family back much easier.”

Tia cocked her head, “We still trying to save those guys? Aren’t they…”

Tia, thankfully, seemed to have learned a bit of tact, trying not to state the obvious.

Subaru sighed, “No. I don’t think so. Gluttony are a bunch of insane monsters but they don’t necessarily kill or put people in deformed states. We just need to find a way to get them to vomit everyone’s names. But first we need to get to the tower and secure their bodies.”

Halibel clapped his hands, “Alright then. It seems we know that ta do. Let’ get started.”

Subaru whispered into Beatrice’s ear, “Do you need a minute?”

Beatrice rubbed her head into his chest, muttering a muffled, “No, Betty is fine, in fact.”

“…Okay. Just let me know if you want another hug again,” Subaru’s words made Beatrice tighten her grip on him, before loosening.

Subaru patted her head.

Just before he put her down, Beatrice reached over her shoulder and took off her fox scarf, she then wrapped it around Subaru’s neck.

“Fufufu, it seems Sister believes you need me more than she does.”

Subaru looked Beatrice in the eyes, “You sure?”

Beatrice rubbed her pink eyes and smiled, “Betty can part with Sissy for a while. Besides, you will need her for the negotiation, I suppose.”

Subaru returned her smile, “Thank you Beako.”

He then put her down as the El Silen bubble popped.

It seemed Roswaal noticed as his voice rang out, “Dooooone? Have you all made a decision?”

Subaru glanced at his companions who all gave their approval: Halibel giving a smirk, Tia giving a thumbs-up, and Beatrice smiling brighter than she ever did before.

Subaru then turned towards Roswaal, “…We have. But first. I want to talk to you.”

“Aren’t we already doing so?”

Subaru rolled his eyes, “A one-on-one talk. No bullshit. Just us.”

Roswaal’s expression didn’t break, he simply said, “Alright…Clind. Leave us alone. Take Subaru’s companions somewhere nice. Perhaps take them to the dining room? They must be awfully famished. It would be good for them to have some dinner before leaving to the tower.”

Subaru’s stomach grumbled slightly. They really did need to take a small break. As much as Subaru’s instincts still wanted to go find Anastasia immediately, they needed to be more strategic about this.

Subaru watched as Clind got up from the couch and began to lead everyone outside. Everyone except Subaru and Roswaal.

Roswaal waved his hand towards the couch in front of him, “Take a seat.”

Subaru sat down as Roswaal eyed him closely, most likely trying to guess his next move. The clown always had a habit of doing so, too bad Anastasia taught Subaru everything she knew. He wasn’t perfect but he could at least guess when someone was sizing him up.

“I’m ready to accept your offer. I’ll create an alliance with you. One where we both go towards our intended goals without either of us getting in the other’s way and where we both support each other as much as possible. It will replace the old oath. You no longer have to support Emilia, though I doubt you’ll abandon her so easily given how much investment you put in.”

Roswaal was beaming with delight, “My, my~! It seems we have finally overcome our greatest impasse. But now I am more curious, if you intend to accept my offer, pledging our loyalties to each other, then what is this conversation supposed to entail. What purpose does it resolve?”

“…I want to talk to you. A real conversation,” Subaru’s words made Roswaal narrow his eyes.

“That is what we are having. This is a real conversation. Frankly, I do not knoooo-“

Subaru rolled his eyes. Enough was enough.

No more games.

“Ros-chi!” Subaru interrupted him mid word, “Can we just be… normal. Have a normal conversation. None of this manipulation. Or weird social dynamic stuff. Just…talk. And be real with each other, just this once?”

Roswaal cocked his head, “I do not understand. This is my normal.”

Oh, if he’s going to play it like this, I’ll just do what I always did to get Ana to stop being annoying.
Subaru pointed at him, “No it isn’t. I call bullshit. You know what your problem is?”

“Ooooh~? Do tell?” Roswaal seemed genuinely intrigued by where this was going.

“Your teacher is stupid.”

“…What?” Roswaal didn’t expect this, as noted by his genuine surprise.

I’m going to piss him off.

“Like genuinely stupid. I know you told me that version in the tea party was different but honestly the real one must be even more stupid given how everything turned out.”

“Subaru.”

So bad.

“Because if I think about it enough, isn’t it kind of stupid she made you go through all of that nonsense, only to get thwarted by me and Otto. Like I wasn’t even that big of a presence, Otto did most of the work.”
“I know what you are doing, Subaru.”

You haven’t experienced what I put Ana-pop through nearly every day.

“400 years of constant planning and manipulation. Only to get upended by two idiots and their earth dragons. People call us stupid but if you lost to us, what does that make you? Given that Echidna must be way older than that, she must be going senile in her old age. Actually, now that I think about it, you were super young when you both met, like 12 right?“

“This isn’t going to work. Such childish insults will not-“

“Doesn’t that make Echidna a pedophile?”
“Teacher is not a pedophile!” Roswaal yelled as he stood up, furious beyond compare.

Jackpot.

“…Did you really have to call my mother a child predator?”

Sorry Eridna! But we both know Ros-chi would never get mad if I insulted him directly. If he’s anything like me, insulting the person he loves the most would be a one-way ticket from zero to pissed in less than a second.

“I’m just glad Sister is not here.”

Subaru refocused on the very angry clown in front of him, thinking, Now I just gotta wove in some of Ros-chi’s insecurities and some truth.

Subaru raised an eyebrow at Roswaal, smiling, “Are you sure about that?

Roswaal glared but then quickly closed his eyes…opening them once again to smile, “Subaruuuu~. While I understand what you are insinuating, such a term would-

Subaru immediately interrupted him, “Be perfectly fitting for her, given that she basically groomed you into being her lapdog. I mean, obviously you’re happy with it, but God. I can’t believe Echidna is into children.”
“She is…” Roswaal stopped himself, trying his best calm himself, though now his face looked like it was having a stroke, “not like that. I was not twelve, mind you. I was an adult, above the age of fifteen-“

Subaru interrupted him, raising his eyebrow and smiling, “Are you sure about that?”

“…Yes. I am,” Roswaal said through gritted teeth, “Teacher may have her flaws, but she is not to be described in such a disgusting way-“

Again, Subaru interrupted him, “Actually, that means I have to be more careful once we revive her. Can’t let Petra near her. Or Meili. Or even Schult. I should send a letter to Priscilla sometime. Warn her before it’s too late.”

Roswaal was visibly shaking, “Now you are being absurd. We both know that she has no romantic or sexual interest in any- ARE YOU A CHILD?!”

Subaru was halfway raising his eyebrow and smiling when Roswaal blurted out his frustrations. Subaru didn’t even say anything, just making that same expression.

“…”

Roswaal huffed, “…We both know that she has no romantic or sexual interest in any person. Her only goal is to secure knowledge and only knowledge. Teacher may have her flaws, but I will not have you slander her with such baseless assumptions.”

“…”

“…”

“…”

“…Are you just going to keep making that face or will you have a normal conversation with me, as you asked?!”

For the whole time since Roswaal screamed at him, Subaru locked his expression. One eyebrow up, smiling.

“…”

“…Alright then-“

Subaru interrupted, fifth time in a row, “I guess I know why Echidna wanted me so badly. She thought I was a child, just like you thought.”

“You pompous little-“ Roswaal started muttering profanity at a high velocity at Subaru.

“Quite a talent you have there.”

Thanks. To be fair, Ros-chi doesn’t look like he’s been taking care of himself all too well. I’m sure in any other situation, he’d be able to deal with this much better. Good sleep and water are the greatest defenses towards ad hominem.

“Is this all a joke to you?” Subaru’s expression was all Roswaal needed to know, the poor mage looked like steam was popping out of his ears, “Are you an idiot?! What good would aggravating me do for you?!”

Subaru stood up and patted his chest with pride, “I am an idiot. It’s why I had to do this in the first place.”

“To what end?! What do you want from me in the first place that I haven’t already offered you?”

Subaru looked Roswaal directly in the eyes, “I want to know what you truly desire.”

Roswaal’s expression shifted from rage to confusion, “…I have already told you my goal.”

Subaru sighed, “Yes. Your goal. But not what you want. You say you want to revive your teacher. You say you owe her everything. But what do you get out of it?! What is it that you want when all is said and done!”

Roswaal’s eyes shifted to the side before answering, “The goal is all I want. Her revival. Whether I die or not, means nothing.”
“You didn’t answer me. What do you want? What do you want to do? What do you want to be once this is over? What was this all for…beyond what would have been good for your beloved?”

“…”

His silence was damning. Familiar. Roswaal’s eyes were now stuck downward, deep in thought.

Subaru touched his scarf, Eridna’s presence warming him, keeping him calm despite everything.

He smiled slightly.

I guess I know why you touched Eridna all the time, Ana-pop. It’s nice.

His eyes widened. Subaru thoughts of Anastasia gave him an idea.

Always inspiring me, aren’t you?

He knew what he needed to do.

He wanted to be kind. He wanted to connect with Roswaal for once. Genuinely.

And the only way he could do it was the same way Anastasia did with him.

Time to gamble.

Subaru took a deep breath, “Ros-chi.”

Roswaal looked up, his eyes no longer glued to the ground, “…”

“…I don’t know what your assumptions about me are. But I’m not who you think I am.”

“…”

“I’m not…smart. I’m not some tactical genius. And no matter what you think my power is, because I know you definitely have some idea, I don’t abuse it. I don’t use it efficiently. I’m not some grand schemer. I’m just…Subaru. Currently Natsuki Subaru, future Hoshin Subaru.”

“…”

Subaru raised his hands in the air, “I’m dumb! I take risks all the time. I get super arrogant when I get ahead in life and I also keep wanting more and more. I don’t like myself all too much, but I want to change that. But it’s hard because I’m dumb. I don’t understand things easily. Hell, I have to constantly ask people for help because I can’t do anything by myself. I broke my gate before because I kept thinking I was some stupid fantasy hero. I called Emilia, Satella, out in the middle of the streets when I first met her because I didn’t stop to think that she would lie to me! I have been in so many life-threatening scenarios because I kept acting suspiciously when I first came to your mansion! I got my ass beat by Julius, a royal knight, because I proclaimed I was Emilia’s knight without even thinking! At the Royal Selection’s ceremony of all times and places!”

Roswaal just stared, “…Why are you telling me all of this?”

Subaru slowly put his arms down, “Because…I’m tired. I don’t want to do this stuff anymore. I don’t want to play these games. Go through these loops. These constant back and forths. I don’t want to get broken down only to build myself back up again. I’m done. All I want to do is get married and go on fun dates with my wife all the time. I just want a simple life. No more of this, any of this, nonsense. It’s not worth it to me anymore.”

“…”

Subaru swallowed, his throat felt hoarse, “And I want to know what you want. Because at the end of the day, I can’t help but feel like you and I are the same. We both fell in love with greedy people. We both want to throw everything away for love. And we both are narrow-minded fools who can’t help but ignore the happiness that is right beside us. I want to be kind to myself for once. And maybe, just maybe, helping you would be a start.”

“…”

“…”

“…I don’t know,” Roswaal took a deep breath, and sighed, his eyes looked heavy, his beard and robes accentuating his exhaustion, “Whatever idealism you spout, it does not matter to me. The path I paved cannot be undone. I have taken too many lives, too many sins to count. I do not deserve redemption. Nor pity. Or absolution. My fate is to finish what I started and to let the world move on. That is all I shall ever be, a footnote in history.”

Subaru locked eyes with Roswaal, “…Maybe you don’t deserve a second chance. Maybe you think your sins are too many. But just giving up every other option is cowardice. It’s cowardly, and an insult to those who love you.”

“…No one-”

Subaru knew what Roswaal was going to respond with, “People love you! Have loved you. If Ram could love you, then anyone can. Maybe you and Ram may never work out. Maybe she deserves better. But at least, just for her sake and yours, could you at least consider what it means to be truly happy. What you really want, that isn’t tied to making someone else happy?”

“…”
Subaru saw Roswaal look down at the ground again. The star already said what he needed to.

Certain thoughts flowed through his head.

This was irrational. This was a waste of time. This won’t help him save Anastasia.

But everything Subaru ever did was irrational. Stopping and checking if a manipulative merchant, who Subaru barely cared for, was okay during that night was all of those things and more.

And if Subaru never regretted helping her on that day…he won’t regret helping Roswaal. Nor anyone else, from this day forward.

Subaru walked over to the door, just as he reached for the doorknob, he said one last thing, “I’ll help you achieve your goal Ros-chi. But please, think about what I said.”

He then twisted the knob and exited the room, leaving Roswaal to ruminate on his past four hundred years of hell.

Subaru braced the back of his head against the door, trying not to hurt Echidna who was hanging off his back, slowly sliding down while sighing deeply.

…God. I’m way in over my head.

“Has it ever been any different?”

Subaru shrugged. No, I guess not.

“Dear guest, will you be needing directions to the dining room?”

Subaru whipped his head to the source of those words. Someone he really didn’t want a reunion yet either.

Ram stood there, stone cold expression, but her eyes sharp and judgmental as always.

She tapped her foot on the floor, stating with a slight tinge of irritation, “Well, will you be needing Ram’s help?”

Chapter 35: Love Doesn't Last Forever

Summary:

Subaru faces more problems before his final negotiation...

Chapter Text

“So-“

“Would our esteemed guest like the full course tour before entering the dining room?”

Subaru narrowed his eyes, “Uh-“

“Or would our esteemed guest like to have a scenic walk outside through the courtyard?”

“Well-“

“Or a bath and a nice glass of our finest wine?”

“Ram-“

“Oh you know my name, am I to assume you are interested in the maids of this domain, how scandalous.”

“…”

“Cat got your tongue?”

Subaru’s eyebrow twitched. He decided to keep silent since it seems Ram’s whole goal was to piss him off as much as possible. He doubts it was out of some vendetta. Most likely she is trying to figure him out. See what his deal is.

“Quite a mouth on this one, I dare say she can run circles around you, on par with Ana.”

Subaru heard Eridna laugh within his mind.

…That’s Ram for you. Good to know she’s still the same as ever. She even used the phrase I taught her.

“You said that this girl is in love with that clown? Do you believe she could help us with turning the terms of the contract towards our favor?”

I doubt it. As much as I want to say Ram would love to help us, her loyalties are towards Ros-chi first.

“But your objective would align with hers. She wishes for his love while you wish for the clown’s happiness. Complimentary goals in many aspects.”

But she most likely heard about what I did. Would you really trust someone who nearly killed two people you care about?

“I feel I do not have to remind you that love makes you stupid.”

…Fair point.

Subaru could not get used to Eridna’s mental laughter. It was like an echo that bounced around his head. Not exactly unpleasant but a completely new sensation.

“But on a more serious note, your lack of willingness to ask for her help does not stem from a lack of trust. Am I wrong?”

Subaru bit his lip.

I…Was I right to say those things to Ros-chi?

“You believe you made a mistake?”

More like I don’t know if that was the right time to say all that. My goal right now is to secure his help without screwing myself over. Yet I basically made some Naruto level Talk-no-Jutsu friendship speech because…I felt bad for him. I feel like my priorities are all over the place.

“Was that another reference to that one story you told Ana? The one with the nine-tailed fox and the boy who keeps talking about the power of belief.”

I’m surprised you can remember which one. I’ve told her a lot by now.

“Quite a fun story. Though I am surprised that the boy likes the pink-haired one instead of the angry one.”

You would love the internet back in Japan.

“Tell me more about that later. But going back to your worries, while I will say such a speech came from nowhere, your intentions and results may be more positive than you think.”

What do you mean by that?

“I have witnessed many people in my lifetime. Geniuses, egotistical maniacs, shrewd businessmen. Yet, despite how often they are wary of each other, they are often blindsided by blunt, straightforward kindness.”

Sounds cliché.

“And yet it happens. People often expect the worst out of others. Believe others are smarter than they actually are. Trust me when I say that your decision had more impact than any political or logical maneuver you could ever think of.”

That sounds like something Ana would tell me.

“Fufufu, while I am quite adept at masquerading myself as others given my power to possess, Ana and I already share many fundamental beliefs. One of those beliefs is in your ability to shake the status quo by being sincere.”

Hard for me to agree but I’ll take your word for it.

“Believe it, as that one boy says.”

I…thanks, Eridna.

“Is our esteemed guest not going to answer Ram’s question?”

Subaru was shaken out of his internal discussion and back to his external conversation.

“Uh,” Subaru’s eyes bounced everywhere, “Could you ask it again? I wasn’t paying attention.”

Ram sighed, “I see. Well, Ram will be courteous and repeat the question. Do not make me do so a third time.”

“Okay nee-sama.”

“Yes, yes you-“ she paused and turned her head slightly to Subaru, “What did you just call me?”

“I, uh. It was a force of habit. Not actually…what I meant to say was…could you just tell me the question? Please.”

Subaru wanted to curl up into a ball and die.

Ram looked at him awkwardly, “…Alright. Well, my question would be if you have any aversion to certain foods.”

“Oh, well, not really.”

“Good, in that case,” they finally arrived at the dining room, Ram opened the doors and allowed Subaru to enter, “Ram hopes you enjoy your meal.”

Subaru tried to smile, “Thanks Ram.”

“…Sure.”

Her response confused Subaru, but he chose not to question it. He instead walked into the room towards where his companions were sitting, they were already eating the food. It was a nice spread of typical Lugunican food. Roast poultry and bovine dishes with some vegetable stir fry here and there. There were loaves of bread with cream soups to pair. Baked tatoes and fried sliced tatoes as usual. Lastly, there were some nice spring beverages, citrus juices along with some condiments placed next to them.

Halibel waved at Subaru as he walked over, talking with a relaxed tone, “Hey Su-san. Good to have ya back. Negotiations go well?”

Subaru shrugged, “As good as it could be.”

Halibel tore some bread and handed half to Beatrice who sat in between him and Tia. Tia was playing with her meat, slicing it with her wind every other second, she only brightened up when seeing him. Joshua sat next to Tia, anxiously partaking in the feast. He did give an awkward wave to Subaru.

Beatrice stood up in alarm and dropped her bread onto the table. She immediately got out of her chair and pulled it out, gesturing for Subaru to sit down.

Subaru smiled, “Oh Beako, I appreciate it but you didn’t have to do that.”

Tia scratched her ear, “Come on Su. Let Bea be helpful, she’s been annoying as ever this whole dinner, constantly fidgeting while waiting for you.”

“Betty was not fidgeting!” The little spirit yelled as Tia grinned, flicking a piece of meat onto Beatrice’s hair, she screamed, “Ah! You crude Shinigami!”

“Yep, yep, she’s our resident Shitigami, Bea-bo” Halibel dipped his bread into the soup and took a bite, “Not bad, not bad. Can’t fault them for the food at least.”

“Shut your mouth Hal or I’ll shove this knife up your ass,” Halibel just laughed at Tia’s threat, then adding, “And we can definitely fault them for other stuff…”

Subaru chuckled as he walked over and patted Beatrice on the head, taking off the piece of meat and eating it before picking the little spirit up and sitting down in the chair with her in his lap.

Beatrice preened in silent joy.

“Thank you again.”

For what?

“For helping sister.”

…It was the least I could do.

The countless loops where Beatrice gave her all to help Subaru at a moment’s notice. She barely needed a second thought and was constantly making sure he was okay. While Halibel and Tia would sometimes argue with Subaru, something he needed on occasion, Beatrice would follow every plan no matter what.

Subaru forgot she never experienced all of those moments. Where they would talk about authorities, science and magic, as well as tactics. Bond over many things. Some repeatedly, some not. He had long forgiven her for what she did back then.

He spent so long with her in those loops that he never realized his current experience with the little spirit was too little. Subaru planned to rectify that starting now.

I never hated Beako. I just needed time to let the wounds heal.

Subaru patted her head as he grabbed a plate from Halibel and Tia started floating pieces of food onto it.

As they did so, Subaru glanced beyond Tia, “You doing alright Joshua?”

The boy in question flinched, nearly dropping his fork, “A-ah, I am, Subaru-sama! S-sorry for leaving you like that.”

Subaru felt bad, “To be fair, it was our fault. Didn’t mean to drag you into this. The plan was to get you a carriage back to your home so you can send help to the sand dunes. Sorry about scaring you with all this nonsense.”

Joshua looked slightly touched, which seemed to be overwhelmed by his fear considering he was sitting next to Tia. Subaru and the others were already used to her bloodlust, but Joshua was just some normal guy in comparison.

“I-it’s fine, it’s fine! I’ve already received confirmation from the Margrave that I will be supplied with transportation. So, I shall travel to my home post-haste after this meal.”

Speaking of meal, Tia stacked his plate high. It was practically a tower of meat and carbs.

Subaru dug in voraciously, hungrily.

Halibel drank from his glass of lemomade, “I think we needed this. We didn’t even eat lunch before leavin’ Banan.”

Tia twirled a knife in her hand while she leaned onto the table, bored, “Should have brought that earth dragon with us. Could have ate her as a last resort.”

“We are not eating Patrasche, Tia. Ah, speaking of, she must be worried sick,” Subaru rubbed his temple with one hand while still eating.

He was definitely getting the silent treatment when they returned.
