“Don’t you worry Su-san, she’s in good hands. Had my people make sure she is given the premium treatment while we’re gone. Besides, it was an emergency,” Halibel shrugged as he covered some meat in tartar sauce, “By the way, ya didn’t tell me ya sold yer sauces ta Lugunica already.”

Subaru flinched, “…I didn’t.”

“He’s right,” Ram’s voice chimed in from the side next to Petra, both standing nearby in case the guests needed anything. Petra stood petrified while Ram stood with an annoyed look on her face, “This was a product of our household. While flattering, it would be ill-advised to steal our idea and sell it in another country. Quite the nerve you have.”

“Quite the nerve you have too, oni dog,” Tia sneered at Ram.

The pink maid narrowed her eyes, “Excuse me.”

“You got wax in your ears or are you just deaf and dumb like that one in Banan?”

Ram eyed Tia suspiciously, “You know other onis?”

“Yeah. From my experience, that oni was an annoying idiot who chose to die on a hill of lies and revenge, like a dumbass. You remind me of her.”

“And from my experience, spirits are supposed to be majestic and honorable creatures. You remind me of neither,” Ram bit back.

“Dumbass.”

“Moron.”

“Loser.”

“Tramp.”

“Washboard.”

“Fatass.”

“Your master is a clown who looks like he touches kids. And that bimbo you call a Lady sucks and looks like she has nothing going on in that skull of hers!”

“Don’t you dare disrespect Roswaal-sama or Emilia-sama like that! Who do you think you are?”

Ram glared as Tia’s eye’s narrowed, the wind howled through the windows outside, slamming on the glass. Subaru placed his hand on her shoulder.

“Tia,” Subaru tried to keep his voice calm, “This isn’t worth it.”

“Like hell it ain’t. These assholes think they can just be annoying for no good reason!”

Ram scoffed, “Oh please, we shouldn’t be even giving you the barest amount of respect given how you made a mess of our hallway and nearly killed our master and Lady. The least you could do is apologize.”
Tia just glared, locking eyes with the pink oni as if she was an insignificant insect.

“I’d kill you for that, but I won’t considering Su would be sad. But I’m not apologizing. You and everyone in this mansion are all responsible for Su. And you failed him.”

“Tia!” Subaru gripped her shoulder tightly, the spirit was no deterred, “Enough!”

Tia didn’t stop, “I won’t! Ever since we entered this place, you’ve been feeling sadder than ever, not even from just that whole mess with Ana. You’re hurting and I hate anything that does that. And I hate these pieces of garbage the most because of that. I’d bludgeon them to death if I had the chance.”

She glared at the two maids; Petra hid behind her mentor as Ram returned the glare defiantly.

 “Ram does not even know you nor your contractor. It’s more than likely you are both mistaking me for someone else.”

Suddenly the doors to the dining hall swung open, “They’re not.”

That cold but sweet voice again.

Subaru only glanced slightly back as he saw Emilia waltz in with Frederica in tow. Her wounds were now healed, not a single scar or blemish to be found.

The half-elf looked troubled, her eyes held determination but there were evident confusion and guilt painting her expression. Frederica was as professional as ever, only slight tension marking her brow as she seemed uneasy with her master’s actions.

Emilia strode forth, stopping only a few feet from everyone at the edge of the table.

Subaru felt a sudden transfer of emotions. His eyes rocketed from Tia to Halibel to Beatrice.

They were all different. It was hard getting used to this new form of Basiliskos Ops. If Subaru could explain how it felt, it was like feeling different bodily sensations that weren’t exactly words but expressions.

For example, Tia’s emotions felt like the wind: sometimes a cool breeze, other times a raging maelstrom, most of the time a torrent of wrath with a calm eye in the middle of the absolute hurricane of bloodlust.

Halibel’s was like resting on a soft meadow, sometimes ticklish, sometimes prickly, but a nice sensation of calm and earth. Though there were times that a little prick or bite was involved, out of nowhere and mixed with precise dread.

Beatrice was like a children’s book. Or books rather, a different one every day from a library of emotions. Sometimes the heaviness of a historical retelling of events unforeseen by anyone else. Other times the soft whimsy of a child’s happiness. And the melancholy of loneliness tinged every spine and page.

Despite the differences and complexities, Subaru understood their intentions immediately.

And every single one of his companions asked the same thing,

“Do you want us to intervene and get you out of here?”

Subaru smiled internally. He sent out a response, claiming he was alright and that such a confrontation might be good, albeit painful.

“You do not have to deal with this today. You are already dealing with a myriad of problems at the moment, I would advise you to not be overwhelmed.”

Subaru chuckled in his mind at Eridna’s warmth, Don’t worry. I’ve been preparing for this day to come and we are already waiting for Ros-chi. Might as well rip the bandaid off this fiasco before my name comes back.

“…You are too nice for your own good.”

Ana-pop says that a lot.

Subaru turned around, patting Tia’s shoulder to let her calm down the bloodlust, the wind no longer bombarding the walls and windows.

The Spirit of Murder clicked her tongue and pointed her fingers at Ram, miming that she would keep an eye on the oni.

Ram only responded with a confused grimace and an eye roll.

“Hey Emilia,” Subaru chose to strike first.

Emilia’s eyes widened, “I see. I never told you my name. Unless Roswaal or someone else told you, you must have heard from it elsewhere. I am a royal candidate, after all. But that’s not right either, isn’t it? The way you look at me. How you look so guilty and tired just from speaking with me. I assumed it was because of your missing fiancé. But it isn’t just that.”

Emilia’s voice came out low, “We knew each other in the past…didn’t we?”

Subaru swallowed a dry cough, “…Yeah. We did.”

Emilia paused as if bracing her mind as she closed her eyes for a few seconds.

“…Subaru. That’s your name, correct?”

“Yes.”

“And we…when did we meet?”

Subaru hesitated but chose to answer truthfully, “Around a year and a half ago. It was during the summer, when you and Ram visited the Capital. You…met Felt and Reinhard. Got into some trouble with the Bowel Hunter.”

Emilia flinched, “I…”

It was obvious she was hit with a mental blow. She was probably considering if she met him while trying to retrieve her insignia. The level of information Subaru had was concerning.

“Don’t worry about it,” Subaru didn’t want to stress her, “I don’t blame you for forgetting.”

“…No. That’s not fair to you,” before Subaru could stop her, Emilia leaned closer, “We were close, weren’t we? If you knew about what happened with Felt, you must know why I was running around in the first place. And if you knew that, then I must have trusted you. But if I don’t remember…then it must be something worse than just me being an ignoramus. Are you…like Rem?”

She was connecting the dots better than he expected.

Subaru got a sudden flashback.

“I’m reaaally sorry. I don’t recognize you. I wish I could offer you anything. Please, just tell us about the cult and this will all be over quickly. I promise you.”

Subaru held back his wince, that memory didn’t sting as much as before but it always was a sore spot to him.

Why couldn’t she believe him so easily back then? Was there too much going on? Was Gluttony’s effect harder to sift through depending on how recent it was?

…It doesn’t matter. The interrogations never happened in this timeline.

Subaru tried to keep his voice steady, “I was a victim of Gluttony, if that’s what you’re trying to imply.”

“…Then you must have been part of my camp,” Her eyes drifted to Beatrice who was most likely looking away out of shame, “At Priestella. We lost you at Priestella, did we not?”

This short conversation felt draining already to Subaru. But he had to continue. It was the least he could do for not choosing her.

“Yes. Gluttony got me right near the end of the assault. I got separated from you all and ended up paying the price for it. Got mistaken for a cultist. Got taken to the prison tower. Got…tortured.”

Subaru grimaced as he saw Emilia’s face wracked with guilt. She seemed to be grasping at words and thoughts that most likely could not be said sparingly. Despite not knowing who Subaru was, she must have felt responsible for him. His disappearance without anyone knowing, at the very least she could imagine it, and how lonely it must have felt.

Empathetic as ever, Emilia.

When was the last time he used that special nickname for her?

It felt like years. It felt wrong to use nowadays. Never rolling off the tongue like Ana-pop’s now did.

“How did you not go unconscious like the others?” Ram’s voice pierced the awkward veil.

Subaru could feel Tia’s bloodlust spike, but he chose to answer without turning, “It seems Gluttony can take your name but not your memories. Just like how Crusch lost her memories but not her name, I had the inverse. If you lose both, you end up like Rem.”

“…I see,” Ram was despondent. Most likely trying to grasp at a thread to recover her lost sister.

It was a nice change of pace given how Ram’s reaction initially was indifference to Rem’s condition.

Maybe the filter really does try to reject the impossible as much as possible in the beginning. It would make sense given all the examples I’ve seen now.

Gluttony seemed fairly simplistic but powerful in its range of effects. It only seemed complex on the outset. Though to be fair, Greed revealed several interesting facets, both Subaru’s and Regulus Corneas’s versions. Perhaps Gluttony is the same.

Subaru’s brows furrowed.

Does that mean Invisible Providence is more than just an extra hand? It hurts to use but the fact that I can phase it through solid objects has always been useful, especially with fighting Regulus. Maybe if I train it I can get more hands. Or perhaps it has more uses than I think?

“From what Sister surmised, there is the factor of compatibility. You have more compatibility with Greed and thus can access more of its potential. Though I do believe it would be wise to experiment.”

He already experimented quite a bit during his time in Banan. He tried everything to save Anastasia. Enough to know that they only work well if Subaru truly is ‘greedy’ or ‘slothful.’ It doesn’t make sense, but it seems they need proper intent rather than just a base desire. Subaru couldn’t just sit around doing nothing, expecting Sloth to become stronger. He needed to embrace the sin, just like he did with Greed.

“Who was I to you?” Emilia said with wavering eyes as Subaru was broken out of his musings, “I must have been someone important to you. Given all the evidence. I can’t begin to express how sorry I am for abandoning you to your fate. But…I want to know at least what I meant to you.”

Authorities could be dealt with later; he needed to focus on how to deal with his greatest challenge, yet. Dealing with his ex-love.

“I…” Subaru hesitated.

But what could he say? What was good to say? He didn’t hate Emilia. But he also didn’t love her anymore. What was the right decision?

“Please. I won’t push you. But I don’t want to leave this alone. I can’t,” Emilia seemed oddly desperate. And confused about her desperation.

As he heard her, a single image came to his mind. Of the day he and Anastasia met in the Royal Capital, where she saved his life, and his mind.

He swallowed. He got up from his seat and put Beatrice gently down onto it. He stood behind the chair and turned towards Emilia. Both of them were very uncomfortable, given their expressions.

At the end of the day, what always worked was laying out my heart. As cruel as it might be.

Subaru braced himself, trying to push out what he threw away so long ago.

“I…loved you. I was your knight. I was someone who pledged my life to you.”

Subaru couldn’t bear to look at her, choosing to instead look downward, holding his hands close and tightening their grasp on nothing.

It hurt to speak but he needed to, “I loved you like you were the only one who mattered. I loved you like there was nothing in the world that could deter me from being with you. I loved you because life would be that much dimmer without you in my life. I loved you because you were the one shining beacon of hope when I felt like I was a nobody. Because I was one. I was stupid, vain, self-sabotaging. But I wanted to be someone better, someone worthy, for you. Because you were worth all of that time and effort. I went through so much: assassins, monsters, insane cultists. Just so I can see you smile. And the funny part…I never regretted it.”

“…” Emilia stood silent as Subaru tore out the final vestiges of his past flame.

He chuckled, but it was a sad dry chuckle that held no warmth, “Love does that to a guy. You would go against the whole world just to see the woman you love safe and sound. Smiling like always. And I wanted to keep doing that for you, forever. Even if you never responded to my love, I knew you felt something similar for me. I knew there would come a day where you’d be comfortable enough with your feelings, confident enough that you—yourself—were enough. Because you’ve always been enough for me. I would have waited forever contently, because there would be no reason for me to doubt your sincerity.”

Subaru grimaced. All of these words came from the heart. From the thousands of thoughts and emotions he felt through all of those loops. They were real. His feelings for Emilia. His feelings for Rem.

He never wanted to give them up…until now. Until he saw Anastasia’s Od break apart in front of him. Until he realized those emotions were meaningless in the grand scheme of things. When he needed to choose. Choose the present over the past.

“…But life isn’t fair,” Subaru spoke with melancholy, “You can’t expect it go the way you want. You can’t expect yourself to always be the person you always are, even if you pray to God everyday that you could return who you once were, because the current you disgusts your soul to the point of absolute insanity. You can’t. You just…can’t. I wanted to love you. I used my love for you and Rem as an anchor because that was the only thing I had left in that Hell. I loved you. But I also hated you. Irrational as it was, I couldn’t help but hate you for leaving me again. You left me out of compassion before in the capital but this time you left me out of indifference. I don’t blame you for Gluttony, but I couldn’t help but feel…like the only reason you cared for me back then was because you had nobody but Puck before. Now you had a camp, people to be responsible for, a goal you couldn’t just throw away for anyone. I know you probably had more reasons, but I can’t help how I felt! I lived everyday like nothing mattered but survival! I wanted to stop seeing all of your faces looking at me like I was insane! Out of pity! Out of fear! Because that damn filter wouldn’t let you see me as anything other than someone who could never be a part of your lives! I wanted to be Natsuki Subaru again! Not…this!”

He waved his hands out, ashamed by his current visage.

He didn’t want to be anyone else, other than himself.

Not an Archbishop. Not a monster. Not a nobody.

Not a knight. Not a hero. Not someone important.

He just wanted to be a boy again.

That same boy who came into this world with wide eyes and an honest desire to be someone cool and loved. As lame as it felt to him now, he’d rather be an immature brat than some messed up old man.

Subaru’s voice felt hoarse, he was choking and barely keeping himself together. He had so many emotions he kept close to his heart all this time because there was no way to vent it out. The only person who knew even a glimpse of what he felt, was the woman he cried his heart out to on the night he escaped that infernal prison.

But she wasn’t here right now. And he needed to settle his past, so he can embrace the future.

Subaru continued despite his heart tearing at itself, “I wanted to be the person you loved again…so badly. I wanted to be the person who was in your life again. Your lives. You, Rem, Ram, Garfiel, Otto, Frederica, Petra. I wanted to be that person you guys cared for. I wanted to be your friend again!”

His arms fell to his sides.

His voice broke, “…But again, life isn’t fair. And I couldn’t wait forever. Not in that prison, not in my current life, not ever again. I can’t wait to be happy anymore. I can’t wait to be someone who I no longer am. I can’t be a hero anymore! When I was in that hell loop, the one no one will ever know because it is the burden I shall forever bear alone, I could barely think of anything else than moving forward. Because the one person, despite acting like a selfish greedy egotistical woman, who still cared for me despite the risks. The person who nearly sacrificed her whole livelihood just to save me, when she barely knew me. The person who constantly put herself in all those dangerous situations we kept getting into, just to be by my side. The person who saw me as…Natsuki Subaru. Not a hero, a knight, or someone special. Just Subaru. That person was going to die. And I couldn’t cling to something vague anymore. I couldn’t cling to the idea I could ever be anyone else, anyone before. I couldn’t cling to your love. To Rem’s love. Because you weren’t there! Like always! I had to deal with everything myself! I had to be the person who chooses! And I chose…her. I chose Anastasia. Because despite what could have been, I can’t keep chasing a hopeless dream. I want…to be happy. I could have been happy with you and Rem. But I made my choices. And I’ll die with them. And I’ll make sure it is a happy one. Hand in hand with her.”

Subaru was panting. His throat was dry. He felt like he had been talking so much in the last few hours.

“…”

Emilia was still silent. Was she confused? Angry? Annoyed? Sad? Guilty? Regretful? Subaru didn’t know. And he really didn’t want to know.

He cleared his throat, “…I’m sorry. I know this is all confusing. I know I sound like a piece of shit who’s throwing this all onto you. You don’t understand any of it. But I couldn’t hold back. For me…and for you. Because I can’t give you some kind of cruel hope. Not again, not ever again.”

When his name comes back, when everything returns to ‘normal.’ Subaru would rather she believe he’s become an awful person and move on, than have any vague possibility of him being who he once was. It’s been too long.

He’s no longer Natsuki Subaru, the self-proclaimed knight of Emilia.

He’s Natsuki Subaru, future husband of Anastasia Hoshin.

He may be a monster, but at least he’ll be her monster.

His hand felt cold.

He pet Eridna’s paw for comfort, choosing to not look at Emilia’s face, like the coward he was.

“You did a good job.”

I don’t feel like I did. I sounded like some depressed child having a tantrum.

“Children have tantrums because no one will pay attention to them otherwise. You are no child, however. Just someone who wants to be heard.”

Subaru sighed.

Subaru thought this trip would be a quick in and out. Go save his wife’s camp. Kill Gluttony. Ask for her camp’s blessing. Return to Banan. Have a wedding. Deal with consequences later.

Now, however, it’s been an emotional roller coaster that seems to have no intention of stopping anytime soon.

It has been approximately one hour, 35 minutes, and 42 seconds since Anastasia was no longer next to him. And life has been awful ever since.

He felt Beatrice’s hand on his as well as a torrent of reassurance from his companions, flowing into him through his Authority.

His mind was a mess, his emotions were tapped out, but at least his heart was still warm.

At the very least, he wasn’t alone.

“Subaru-“Emilia’s words or speech was interrupted.

Subaru looked up as the doors slammed open once again.

In walked Roswaal L. Mathers.

Except he looked a little different.

No longer looking like a ragged Gandalf, he wore his usual mage garb mixed with noble wear. His beard was not present, though some of it was left over as a sharp goatee mixed with his mustache.

Interestingly enough, he wasn’t wearing his clown makeup, his face bare for the world to see.

His expression was complex. Subaru couldn’t really tell what the man was thinking or feeling, there was an odd sense of foreboding. His smile…it was weird.

Roswaal’s voice rang out through the dining hall, “Apologies for the intrusion my dear guests, I am here to discuss the last details for our contract.”

Subaru felt his spine tingle.

It was time for the final negotiation.

 

 

Chapter 36: A Fine Problem Emerges

Summary:

We take a look at a certain Finest Knight's situation...

Chapter Text

Julius Juukuulius was in a literal and figurative hell.

 

Figurative since he was not in fact in an area filled to the brim with fire and brimstone. Literal in the fact that there were actual demonic creatures prowling about the tower, hoping to slowly drive him insane with torture. Demons that looked like people he should know and should cherish, but don’t exist anymore. He knows he should feel something for them. He knows they were important to him. But he doesn’t remember any of it. And it was frustrating.

 

It all started when…the Witch of Envy started tearing the tower apart. Julius recalled Reinhard’s sudden mood shift when the assault started. He quickly drew Reid and began shouting orders with an intensity unforeseen before. Thinking back to that moment gave Julius intense shivers. The fact, the mere idea, that Satella had breached her confinement, nearly shattered whatever composure he could have had. Nearly everyone was brought to their knees from her presence, the miasma in the air was suffocating and maddening. It was only due to Reinhard’s intervention that they survived—at the cost of everyone getting separated.

 

Julius sat on the floor, exhausted, taking another cursory glance of his surroundings. He was currently in a small enclosure—his designated safe house—that could only be found by taking a specific blank book from a specific shelf of the Taygeta library. This tower was strange, the immediate second the tower was attacked, it changed shape. Numerous new hallways, rooms, and areas had materialized into existence. Not only that, traversing the place was a nightmare, numerous hallways that stretched infinitely, rooms that—when entered— would exit into a completely different location, and turning a corner could teleport you to the other side of the room. At first, he thought it was illusions, but after some rumination, he was sure this was some type of advanced yin magic at work. Julius had a theory that the Sage implemented this system in the chance scenario that the Witch was freed, trapping her within the tower itself.

 

Julius glanced to the side and eyed the three dormant bodies: two identical children and a large wolfman. He…he knew their names. Maybe? He doesn’t know. Tivey? Heta? Richard? It was hard. He’d…forgotten. He remembers hearing names but were they theirs? He knows he forgot but he doesn’t know what and it made his brain bleed from trying. Everything…he needed to stop. The more he did, the more he wasted time. They were the only ones he was able to find in this accursed place. He pinched his nose, thinking back to what that monster told him days before.

 

“We want to play hide and seek, tsu~! A little game, a way for you to get a chance at survival while we get some fun! You try to find your missing friends, their bodies, while we chase you. You only get five chances, tsu~. Make them count.”

 

Whoever that was chose not to mention that he would be hunted not only by the other Gluttony Archbishops, but also the people he was trying to look for in the first place! That was how he had lost the first time. He had encountered one of the twins next to him, alive and walking. He assumed this was who he was supposed to find. Only to be surprised by sudden physical contact, and the jarring feeling of his insides feeling rancid. It was nauseating. He didn’t understand what they just did and he didn’t like it.

 

“Oh, that’s interesting, tsu~. That…hm. Well, whatever, we can work with this. Four chances left, tsu~.”

 

Julius gritted his teeth. He already lost four times now. He only had one chance left. He didn’t know why they were toying with him nor what their words meant. He needed to find the rest soon or else they’ll all be comatose here, wasting away while Reinhard was battling with the literal incarnation of evil. He had a vague idea that there should be only five people he needs to find…but the only one he could remember was Otto. That gave him some hope. Otto must be still surviving like he was, evading these cultists better than he could ever do.

 

Julius sighed as he gripped his sword in one hand. He was supposed to be the Finest of Knights. He was supposed to be protecting the honor of Lugunica. He was supposed to be protecting his friends and family! But he failed…these three were proof of it. They were taken while he was busy trying to navigate this endless vertical labyrinth, such a failure he was to let them suffer alone. He needed to save them.

 

…I need to find Otto. Two heads are better than one and he could possibly have a better idea or plan for this. We can’t just keep playing their game, who knows how long Reinhard can last against her?

 

Find Otto. Secure a plan. End the Gluttonies. Find a solution to the Witch of Envy within this tower. There must be something. The Sage dealt with her before, he must have notes on how to deal with her again. The tower is already keeping her in a deadlock with Reinhard, it must be, it’s the only logical reason for them not dying immediately.

 

Julius slipped a hand under his coat and grabbed a book from his inner pocket. A book he found within one of the drawers of the desk inside this very room. Julius theorized this might have been a personal refuge for the Sage, somewhere he did his hidden studies given the bed, desk, and numerous writing supplies. He brought it closely to his face and eyed its cover for what was probably the fiftieth time he had done so:

フリューゲルの日記

女子はお断り！

特にドナ！

It was illegible.  Written in a language that seemed oddly familiar. It looked like the texts of Hoshin, given to him through various trade deals that he had no interest in investigating when he came upon them. Julius was interested in ancient history, but the Royal Selection took priority, he had no time for the past at the moment. But now he cursed his lack of foresight. Alec Hoshin knew the Sage! He must have. If Julius had even tried to translate these texts, he would be able to uncover the treasure trove of information within this tome and get even a hint towards what the Sage’s research was for.

 

Julius opened to a random page, trying his best to understand what was written:

サテラたんは世界一可愛い。あぁ！大好き！明日のデートはどこに行こうかな？オッドグラスに会いに行こうかな。オッドグラスはいつもあの大きな赤ちゃんを抱っこするのが大好きだったから。

 

まずはシャウラの気をそらす方法を考えなきゃ。邪魔されたら大変だから。うーん、パトラッシュの掃除を頼んでみようかな…

 

パトラッシュはシャウラが全然好きじゃないから、二人とも一日中気をそらせる。

 

あぁ！でもドナも気をそらさないと。なぜかずっと一緒に行こうとするから。彼女の気持ちを傷つけたくないから。後で一緒に遊ぼうって約束しようかな。何か楽しいことを考えなきゃ。みんなで楽しめることを。

 

リードはもういいよ。あの野郎はサテラにキスしようとして、それで済むと思ってるみたいだけど…

 

Nothing, not a single thing he could understand! This could be the answer to all his problems! A way to seal the Witch again, or maybe an advanced spell that could eliminate the Archbishops with ease. But he’ll never know due to his negligence. How truly slothful of him…

 

Julius took a deep breath. He closed the book quickly, with a snap. No matter. Wasting his time on possibilities solves nothing, only action will. He placed the book within his coat once again and stood up slowly, brushing himself off. He grimaced at how unsightly he must look, his clothes were becoming rags with each passing day, and he hasn’t showered in weeks. How repugnant. If only there was a bathroom in this whole tower-

 

…He heard the click of a mechanism; he knew that sound. It was the prelude to the next sound.

 

 

There it was. The sound of gears turning. A hole should appear in one of the corners of the library. A hole that led straight to this room.

 

Someone found this area. Who?

 

Julius could only assume the worst. He unsheathed his sword and bounded toward the wall. He quickly maneuvered to the ceiling, using the desk as scaffolding, and with a quick call to Iku, he created pockets of earth on the ceiling to hang off. His feet and one hand were encased, allowing him to peer downward by looking over his shoulder, his remaining hand on his sword’s handle and ready for action.

 

Julius heard the approaching footsteps from the narrow passageway leading up to the chambers, they weren’t soft nor were they heavy, not rapid nor did they have any indication of a limp. They were not some warrior’s rhythm, often a confident march, nor someone with a lot of weaponry, the lack of any additional noise supported that. A slight nervousness, the footsteps were uneven, as if they were checking where they were walking or looking back once in a while. Familiar. It must be…

 

The door opened, ever so slightly. Julius’s eyes widened as his assumptions proved true. Grey hair mangled and unruly without his hat to keep it stable. A green robe paired with a brown coat, a demeanor that was equal parts skittish and wary.

 

Otto Suwen had somehow made his way to Julius after days of searching.

 

Julius’s eyes narrowed. It felt too convenient. Was this a ploy? It could be one of the Gluttonies, obfuscating as the advisor. But it wouldn’t make sense, Julius still remembered Otto. Unless there was something about their powers that Julius could not understand, he assumed they needed the person’s name to impersonate them. He needed to be sure.

 

Julius fell to the ground, slipping out of his earth mounds, aiming for just behind Otto.

He quickly heldhis blade against Otto’s neck and yelled with ferocious intensity, “Hands in the air!”

Otto screamed, making Julius flinch, “W-wait, wait, wait!”

“Do as I say or I shall slit your throat in one fell swoop!” Julius ordered, the second time seemed to have been processed by Otto, as the advisor immediately followed the directive.

“I-I,” Otto stuttered before he seemed to realize something, “Wait…Julius is that you?”

That was a good sign, but it did not prove anything, “You will answer all my questions, and you will not move a single muscle unless I tell you to. Otherwise, I will kill you immediately.”

Otto tried to nod but immediately felt Julius’s blade pull closer to his neck, he paled and immediately spouted, “Y-yes!”

“Good. How did we first meet?”

 

While Julius spoke, he had In and Nes concoct a secret Nect between Julius and Otto.

 

“U-um. You saved me from some Witch Cultists during the expedition to slay Sloth!”

Correct. In reality, the questions meant nothing. The Nect spell was the real test.

Julius pursed his lips before speaking once more, “Alright. Why did I invite your camp to Priestella?”

“I-it was to improve the relations between all camps! You also wanted to offer help to Emilia-sama to locate a stone for her contracted spirit!”

 

Julius had read the reports on Gluttony. They stole people’s names and given how they were able to know key details of individuals after doing so, they had the ability to retain the memories of each victim. This meant any and all questions about a specific person were meaningless. What mattered…was the Od.

 

“Good, last question. When is my birthday?”

“…A-are you serious?”

No. But he needed more time, the Nect was almost finished.

“Answer the question or I will bring your neck a swift end.”

Otto flinched visibly, “I, uh…”

“Well?”

“…Um.”

Almost there. The connection is nearly stable, his spirits just have to fine tune it.

“…Otto.”

“…”

“…”

“…Uh.”

“Did you forget?”

“No!” Otto’s voice cracked.

“…Then why are you not saying anything?”

“…Dramatic effect?”

Julius’s eyes narrowed, he was now more convinced this was his friend.

“I am deeply hurt that you forgot.”

“W-wait! I think I remember!”

“…”

“…The third of Marshba?”

“…It’s Jularm 7th.”

“…”

“…”

“Please don’t kill me.”

Julius sighed, it was him, “Luckily, I have already confirmed you are indeed the Otto Suwen I know.”

Julius lifted his blade and sheathed it, allowing Otto to turn around, rubbing his neck, “How could you tell?”

“In and Nes confirmed it. I used Nect to connect our Gates, allowing me access to your Od as well. The Earth magic affinity was a good sign but the two confirmed your Od as familiar. It may not be exactly foolproof, but it is the best I have at the moment. Apologies for the rude greeting but you understand why. It is wonderful to see you again, however,” Julius offered his hand out.

Otto looked down and smiled before grasping it firmly, “I do. Don’t worry Julius-san, I would have done the same in your position. It’s good to see you too. How have you been since I last saw you? And…who are they?”

Otto pointed to the three people lying on the bed, making Julius grimace, “They are the people that came with us. Gluttony got them before I could and well…I’ve been trying to find them and gather our forces. Specifically, you.”

Julius began explaining his experience over the last few days, constantly dodging the imposters and trying to find his way around this absolute labyrinth. How he tried looking into the books and was surprised by what they held. The memories he saw.

Otto gripped his own hands in anger, “A game huh, those monsters really treat this situation like it’s nothing to them.”
“It’s to be expected. I am quite surprised; did they not do the same to you?”

Otto sighed, “Fortunately, I was never given the chance as I kept running and hiding from them the second I saw. I guess I got lucky because I was able to recognize one of them, Lye Batenkaitos, before seeing him morph. After that, I assumed everyone who I couldn’t recognize was a threat.”

“A necessary precaution. I only threatened you as I was unfamiliar with their ability, not knowing how it exactly worked, and whether they could impersonate you without devouring your name. I’m glad I was wrong.”

“Again, would do the same thing in your position. As for what we should do now,” Otto looked around, “I think we’ll need to try something drastic.”

Julius raised an eyebrow, “What do you mean? We do not have the combat potential to go against them in a head-to-head battle. I am not at my peak condition, and neither are you, I’m assuming.”

Otto nodded, “I didn’t intend on that. Rather, I believe we can take an indirect approach. This floor may not have anything of value besides the library, but the next floor may differ. During my investigation around this place, I found that there is a staircase to the next floor. And you’d be surprised to find what I uncovered…I found Reid.”

“Reinhard’s sword? Did he lose it during the clash?”

“No. The first Sword Saint himself is here. In the next floor.”

Julius stood dumbfounded, “You are not kidding are you.”

Otto shook his head, “I wish I was.”

“How?”

“I barely understand myself. All I know is that the spirit of the first Sword Saint is anchored to the tower, challenging anyone who wishes to proceed forward. I came upon him getting fought by one of the Gluttonies, Roy Alphard I believe. The Archbishop was soundly defeated with ease.”

“Hm. It is not like I wish to doubt you Otto, but are you sure that is the same Reid of legend?”

Though to be fair, they have been seeing quite a number of baffling things lately, the soul of Reid being bound to the Tower of the Sage seems par for the course.

Otto didn’t even blink, “Red hair. Boundless strength. And an aura exuded from him that could only be described as power, in it and of itself.”

“Appearance matches but that doesn’t mean-“

“I saw him use a pair of small wooden sticks to defeat the Archbishop in only a few moves.”

“You are kidding.”

“…”

“…Oh my Od, you are not.”

Otto shrugged, “I would if I could, he seems to be the real deal and most likely is both our path forward and our trump card against the cultists. If we can get ahead of him, maybe the cultists won’t be able to follow, that should give us some freedom and possibly more access to the tower’s resources.”

Julius bit his lip, “I was unable to defeat Roy in combat myself. I do not think I will be able to defeat the legendary Sword Saint, even with your assistance.”

Otto smiled, “Who is to say that we need to defeat him in a normal manner? From what I could hear, the spirit simply wishes for you to make him move at least once. It seems his role is to be a challenge for us, just like the monolith from this floor. So, all we need to do is find his weakness and force him to take a step forward.”

“Still a difficult task, I’m afraid.”

“I know. But feasible compared to outright beating him in combat. On a related note, how did you feel when reading the books in this library?”

Julius eyed Otto in confusion before answering honestly, “…Like my mind had morphed into that very person. It was as if those memories firmly planted themselves into my mind as my own. It felt…jarring.”

 

The one book Julius read was of Fourier Lugunica, the deceased prince of the Royal Family. It caught his eye while hiding from Lye. He had only met the prince a few times, but the prince left an incredible impression on him during the Argyle incident. On some days, he wished the man would still be alive, as he would no doubt be leading the country better than anyone else. But after reading his book, seeing his memories, feeling his emotions…

 

“Cr…lo…no…sorry…Fe…”

 

Julius flinched and looked behind him. The whispers died once more.

 

…The impression the late prince left on Julius was now more haunting.

 

“Julius-san, are you okay? Did you sense something?” Otto’s voice was filled with concern.

Julius caught his breath and tried to calm his heartbeat, it was just nerves acting up, “I’m fine. I believe being in this tower has not helped my mind. I feel as if I am being constantly watched, and perhaps I am, given our malicious neighbors.”

Otto put his hand on Julius’s shoulder, “You should rest.”

Julius shook his head, but patted Otto’s hand in gratitude, “I appreciate the concern. But I’d sooner feel comfortable being in a safe position than forcing myself to sleep. Please, continue what you wish to say.”

Otto stared for a few seconds but obliged, “Alright. But don’t push yourself too hard. As for what I was saying, if the books allowed you to see and feel the memories of those who died, then perhaps it can reveal more than just a late-night dinner or a childhood memory. Perhaps one can also know the strengths, weaknesses, and habits of said person. And if said person is the dead Sword Saint?”

Julius immediately understood, “Then we can know a possible way to defeat Reid by finding his book. An excellent idea.”

“Who knows, if the book can give you the memories of the individual, it might even imprint their skills and abilities. At the very least, it is worth a try given our options are either to make Reid move or to kill the Gluttonies. Both impossible, but one not nearly as much as the other.”

“I agree,” Julius looked towards the exit, “Now the only issue we have is finding the book within this whole library. An incredibly difficult task. Akin to finding a specific flower in an entire garden.”

Otto chuckled, “I might have the solution for that. But we’ll need to return to the library floor to do so. Up for another excursion into Witch Cultist infested territory, Julius-san?”

Julius smiled, “Delighted. Truly unfortunate that I did not pack Cultist pesticide for this journey.”

 

They both laughed. Julius felt much better about their situation. While the odds were stacked against them, it felt less daunting with a friend at your side.

 

“Ah, Otto,” Julius reached into his pocket and brought out the Sage’s book, “I found this in the nearby desk. I believe this might have been a secret refuge for the Sage and this book may contain some of his knowledge. Unfortunately, I am unable to read it.”

Otto’s lips tightened, “I might have the same luck as you I’m afraid, judging by the cover. But I can try to see if I recognize any of the characters.”

Otto took the book and opened it to a random page, Julius looked over his shoulder as they both read:

寒いのも嫌い。暑いのも嫌い。昼間は暑すぎるし、夜は寒すぎる！ なんで砂漠の真ん中にこんな馬鹿げた塔を作ったんだ？

 

エキドナのせいだ。逃げ出さなきゃ！ 彼女はただ実験がしたいだけなのに。ああ、子犬のような目で見られたらこうなるんだ。私はそういうのに弱い。

 

ここにGoogleがあればいいのに。そうすればエアコンの作り方が調べられる。精霊を使えば…炎の魔法が一番いいかもしれない。うーん、質問は後でしよう。

 

どっちにしてもどうでもいい。ヴァをどうするか考えなきゃ…

 

Otto blinked three times, “…I have no idea what any of this says.”

“I expected as such. It seems we will have to decipher this once we return to Lugunica, for now, let us proceed with the plan as you suggested,” Julius led the way towards the door, opening it and traversing the narrow passageway once more, Otto in tow.

 

They finally reached the dead end, the only way out being upward, as Julius brought out both Iku and In. The earth spirit created little steps on the wall for them to climb while In lit their path vertically with a bright light. They climbed until there was nowhere else to go, Julius looked towards the side and found a small divot within the wall. He put his fingers inside and pressed forcefully, this caused the entrance to reemerge, a large hole replaced the ceiling, leading to the brightly lit library. Julius grimaced before taking a leap upward, he hated this part the most.

 

As he leaped, he suddenly felt an odd sense of vertigo, and then suddenly fell flat onto the ground, forward. He brushed himself off as he turned around and quickly grabbed Otto’s hand, pulling him out of the now horizontal hole. As Julius looked around, he was once again amazed by the state of the library. It felt like something out of a storybook. Floating books and bookshelves dotted the air, staircases covered the walls and ceiling, leading to nowhere and possibly everywhere. Julius could see random hallways near the walls, that led down areas that should not exist given how wide the tower was from the outside, they looked like they went on forever. The previously open floor was now a labyrinth of bookshelves, the shelves creating intricate artificial halls that twisted and turned endlessly. Trying to climb the bookshelves was not always good, sometimes they would allow you to climb, other times they would shift your sense of gravity, sending you to the wall or ceiling.

 

Otto peered back as the hole soon disappeared, returning to its original state as an ordinary bookshelf, “This place is incredibly confusing. How in the world did we go up sideways?”

Julius shrugged, “The Sage must have been a skilled Yin magic user. From what I recall, Beatrice-sama had similar magic.”

“Yes, but this level of spatial magic is absurd. It feels like this whole tower is just a treasure trove of secrets.”

“Then it will be worthwhile to bring some scholars next time. Perhaps they can illuminate this tower’s capabilities with more precision than us. For now, let us make haste to Reid’s book. You said you had a solution to locating it?”

 

Otto nodded and smiled; he then began to say some gibberish into the air.


A second passed.

 

And then another.

 

And then hundreds of Zodda bugs began to pour out from nearby bookshelves, leaving Julius gawking.

 

Otto chuckled, “Surprised?”

Julius was, “I did not know you brought this many bugs with you.”

“I didn’t. They were actually from this tower to begin with. Turns out, some snuck in before the tower became isolated. Zodda bugs are much more resilient than you’d expect.”

“I see,” Julius was both amazed and incredibly grateful that Otto was on his side, “So your plan is to use the bugs to find the book.”

“Exactly,” Otto started speaking in their language once more and then smiled excitedly, “They know where it is!”

“Good, but you must please be a bit quieter, we have no idea where the Gluttonies are this moment,” Julius reprimanded Otto as the advisor paled.

“A-ah, sorry, my mistake. Actually, let me ask them something,” Otto had a quick conversation with a nearby Zodda Bug, “Hm. That’s interesting.”

“What is it?”

“They haven’t seen anyone else on this floor for hours. It’s quite possible they are searching on another floor at the moment.”

Julius narrowed his eyes at that, “That…hm. Alright. Then let us finish this quickly, who knows when they’ll return.”

Otto nodded in agreement as he then led the way, both of them running down the path and turning wherever Otto deemed fit. Something was still nagging in Julius’s brain. But he can’t quite figure out what. It felt like he was missing something. Missing something important. It felt like the onset of a migraine.

 

“Ju…sh…ca…O…no…”

 

Julius winced again, choosing not to react as explicitly.

 

The longer we stay in here, the more I feel my mind becomes scrambled. I’ve always heard isolation can lead to hallucinations, auditory or visual. Hopefully with Otto’s presence, it will fade away.

 

They kept turning and running. From what Otto said, it should be a book that was right next to them, positioned just on the other side of the left-hand bookshelf, just as they left their hideout. Unfortunately, turning a corner led to them being teleported on the other side of the room. Several times. After numerous trial and error, they were finally able to find the book.

 

Julius looked towards it. It had Reid’s name plastered all over the binding. Reid Astrea. No ‘van’ it seems. Questions for later, however. Otto gestured to the book.

“Would you like to do the honors?”

“…If you’ll allow me,” Julius waited for Otto’s confirmation before moving towards the book slowly.

 

However, just as he did. A bright light flickered from its position, blinding them both.

 

Just as soon as it began, it ended. Julius blinked, rubbing the spots out of his eyes and refocused forward-

 

Who was that?

 

A beautiful woman with purple hair, a yellow star pin on top, wearing a white kimono with several stars with wisps embroidering it, was now on the floor, groaning in pain.

It…

It…

It…

She was familiar. No. Something clicked within Julius’s mind. That nagging feeling. It was no longer there. Replaced with a clarity that Julius could not understand, yet it pierced his mindscape and revealed something that he had missed dearly. Something he had been missing for months now but never realized until now.

 

Julius’s mouth felt dry, “…Anastasia-sama?”

Chapter 37: Who Are You?

Summary:

Julius begins to realize why everything has been so off...

Notes:

My internet has been cut off and it was a struggle trying to find a way to access and post this chapter. Luckily, life finds a way! Enjoy!

Chapter Text

 

“Julius-san.”

“…”

“…We should talk about this.”

“What is there to talk about, Otto?” Julius said as he put Anastasia down gently on the bed, next to the others. Julius kneeled right near the edge of the bed and stared at her.

 

His brain. It was going mad. Too many thoughts. Too many ideas. But above all. There was an unyielding force of disgust and regret swarming within him. He remembered. Why is it now that he remembered? Remembered his greatest failure.

 

Otto pursed his lips, “How long has it been since we last saw her?”

“…Ever since Priestella,” Julius’s hands gripped themselves.

 

It all made so much sense now. Why he suddenly was given a company from Kararagi. How could he believe it was just a gift from a random benefactor? There must have been some reason for it. Gluttony. They must have some secondary effects. He had heard of the Emilia camp’s maid going through a similar fate. How her disappearance altered the world. When Anastasia was lost…

 

His participation in the Royal Selection.

 

His reason for being friendly with the Iron Fang.

 

Their presence in Priestella.

 

It all changed. Her disappearance actively put him at the forefront of all of her achievements. Because…that must have been the only way for the world to adapt to it. The only way it would possibly make sense. How cruel. How disgusting. How demeaning. To have everything you ever worked for be thrown away, tossed to someone who does not deserve it. He did not deserve it. All he deserves is damnation for his sins.

 

“…What if it’s not her?” Otto’s question was met with an incredible glare from Julius, “Julius-san, be reasonable. Do you really think her arrival here makes any sense? Right as we are trying to accomplish our goals?”

Julius’s glare faltered as he glanced at his Lady, “…I do not know why she is here. Or if this is some elaborate scheme to coax us. However, what I do know, is that my Lady has been gone for months. And I have done nothing about it.”

Otto tried to put his hand on Julius’s shoulder, “It wasn’t your fault. Gluttony-“

Julius brushed his hand off, “Absconded from me!”

Julius’s voice wavered as his hands nearly tore into his legs from gripping his pants, “I was supposed to be the one to have apprehended him! He was my opponent! And I let him escape! And if Anastasia-sama was taken from us and we had no idea, not even a concept of her existence or absence…”

“…Then I was responsible for her being forgotten by the world,” Julius’s head hanged low.

“Julius-“

Otto was again interrupted by the downtrodden knight, “Please do not insinuate that I am not at all responsible for this. I am a knight. My duty was to my Lady. And as we can see, I have failed. There is nothing else to say.”

“Julius!” Otto was finally able to get Julius to look at him, sighing, “It is your fault. But what will saying such a thing prove exactly?”

Julius kept glancing at Anastasia’s unconscious body, her breathing all that he could hear, “…The beginning of my penance.”

“…I understand wanting to make things right. I don’t know what I would be thinking or feeling if I was in your position and Emilia-sama was in hers. But you have to think clearly,” Otto pointed at Anastasia, “Why would she be here and why would she appear from Reid’s book right as we arrived? It couldn’t be a coincidence.”

 

Julius struggled to follow that train of logic as his emotions were too on edge. Still, he tried, at least for Otto’s sake.

 

Julius began to think out loud, “…There are a couple of possibilities I could wager. To begin, Anastasia-sama is possibly a trap laid by the Gluttonies.”

Otto nodded, “It’s highly probable given what we’ve experienced.”

“But that does not explain why I or you can remember her,” Julius turned his head towards Otto, “Why release her name for this specific purpose? Why not pretend to be her instead?”

“She could still be an impersonation. Have you checked her Od?”

Julius bit his lip, “I have…”
“Julius?” Otto raised an eyebrow.

“It is hers…but not hers. When I used Nect on her, as I did for you, my spirits recognized her, they confirmed who she was. But…her Od is much stronger than before. It feels different.”

“Different how?”

“…As if something else is mixed in there. Something foreign.”

Otto visibly tensed, “Julius, that’s bad.”

“Before you assume anything, “Julius raised his hand, “I can still verify that she is indeed my Lady. Her gate is…different compared to others.”

“Julius. You can’t just expect me to trust that without extra information,” Otto pleaded.

Julius bit his lip, “Apologies. But I have already failed enough. I will not spill her secrets while she is unconscious. She trusted me with them. All you need to know about my Lady is who she is, and her gate proves that. Please, trust me my friend.”

Otto clicked his tongue before pinching his nose, “…Fine. I will. But all this points to the fact that Anastasia-sama isn’t exactly as she was before. Whether it was due to the influence of Gluttony or not, we can’t take any risks. We should at the very least bind her just in case.”

Julius couldn’t look Otto in the eyes, “I can see your point. I truly do. But you can see as I do that something else is clearly different about her.”

“…Julius.”

“Otto, please. Look at her. Her clothes. She wasn’t wearing those before. They look fairly new. Not only that,” Julius carefully lifted her hair and revealed the ribbon tied to her ponytail, “Look. Doesn’t this seem familiar.”

 

It was an orange ribbon, with a picture of a kitten demi-human, looking almost like the ones sleeping right next to her. Julius gently let it fall back down. If his suspicions were true, if the demi-humans were all once part of her camp. And given he has no memory of Anastasia having this ribbon on her in Priestella, then that just supports one of Julius’s greatest fears, that he never knew existed until just now.

 

Otto paled, “…You’re implying she was awake. But her name was gone. The exact opposite of Rem-san.”

Just like the Archbishop that escaped. Julius wanted to tear his throat out at the mere thought, “Kararagi clothes. The ribbon. Her existence here. Is it…possible that she lost her name in Priestella and was left all alone?”

Otto shook his head, “That doesn’t make sense. Even if that were true, wouldn’t her first reaction be to return to you all. Why would she go to Kararagi? It just doesn’t make sense. Julius?”

 

Otto stared as Julius’s eyes glazed over. His mind began searching through his own memories. To Otto it wouldn’t make sense, but Julius understood his Lady. He understood who she was. She was strong. Someone who would never give up on the people she cared about. She was a natural born leader who understood the plight of the people, especially those under her.

 

…But she was also someone who could not let go easily.

 

“Otto,” Julius’s voice was pensive, melancholic, and nostalgic, “This is not the first time I have seen my Lady with such clothes.”

Otto nodded slowly, “In Priestella, correct?”

Julius chuckled, “No. Before. During my time with her after the Royal Selection began, there was a time where my Lady took me shopping, hoping to get me some new apparel for the season. It was during a stressful period of my life as we were training a new batch of knights. I appreciated the moment of reprieve. My Lady also indulged and bought herself several new dresses. Her desire for new clothes is unmatched.”

Otto couldn’t help but smile, “A true fashionista it seems.”

“Indeed. But there was something I realized as we returned home…her closet had no more space.”

“…”

“…”

“…Julius, I swear to Volcanica, what was the point of that story?! Are you just saying Anastasia-sama buys too much stuff without thinking?!”

Julius couldn’t help but laugh at Otto’s reaction, though it sounded a bit hollow, “No, no. Let me continue and you may understand. Her closet was filled to the brim with clothing. From every nation, from so many different designers. She had dresses in every color and nearly every style in existence.”

“…” Otto stayed quiet, opting to let Julius finish before reacting.

“And she had dresses from years ago. Many years. As I helped her unload many of them, there was one in particular I noticed. In the back of her closet, kept safe within a secure compartment. A dirty, worn out, stitched up, kimono. A dress from Kararagi. It was far too small for Anastasia-sama. A child’s size.”
“…”

“…When I asked Anastasia about it, all she said was, ‘ta remind me of where I started, so I don’t forget how far I’ve come.’”

 

Julius said those words with such reverence that he could almost feel himself tear up. It was one of the many moments that inspired him to work harder. To reach the expectations of others. To reach the expectations of his Lady. To remember his origins, and how much he has worked to get here. How he should cherish his memories of hardship. How a life filled with comfort is not as satisfying as a life filled with purpose.

 

“…I see. She’s that type of person,” Otto kneeled down next to him.

Julius smiled, but it was brittle, “The type of person who cherished what she had.”

“…”

His smile dropped, “…Could you imagine how she must have felt when she saw me, saw everyone she knew, and tried to reach out for us. Only to be met with nothing. Absolutely, nothing!”

 

Julius felt, for the first time in a long while, tears begin to well up, as his imagination spiraled, his memories beginning to form connections once more.

 

Julius muttered solemnly, “I was there. I…was helping people evacuate. Helping many people find their families. And I remember seeing this poor woman. Dressed just like my Lady. Who looked just like Anastasia-sama. Who talked like Anastasia Hoshin! Saying my name with such familiarity that I should have had some vague suspicion that she must be someone important! But I didn’t! I didn’t express concern, like one who cares for their most important person! Like one who cares for their liege! Like one who has known someone for nearly two years!”

Tears began to fall, he wiped them quickly as his guilt overwhelmed his pride, he muttered softly, “…I acted like she was a stranger. Like a knight who must protect the common people. Like she was someone I would forget only a moment later. Do you know how that must feel to someone who couldn’t bear to throw away their childhood clothing?”

Otto hesitated as he hovered his hand over Julius’s shoulder, “…She must’ve have felt like the world was shattering right in front of her. Especially, if everyone she ever knew, forgot.”

“…My Lady is strong. She is someone who I know who would not give up without a fight.”

“…”

“But she is also human. She must’ve-” Julius choked, “…She must have left in order to spare herself from the pain. She left us. Returned to Kararagi because it was familiar. And began again.”

 

A part of him began to hurt as an intrusive thought came into being. Did she leave because she could not bear the pain of no one knowing her? Or did she leave because she felt betrayed by Julius’s failure? That Julius was the cause of her downfall because he let Gluttony retreat. That his failure cost everything she ever owned and loved. She lost her home, her connections, her company. Everything.

 

…If Anastasia were to wake up and exact vengeance upon him, he would not dare to refuse nor run away. This was what he deserved.

 

Otto’s voice chimed in, “…What a horrid existence those Archbishops are.”

Julius’s own rage began to rise, but he kept a pin on that for now, “Yes. But you can see what I am trying to say.”

“Yes, I believe so. Anastasia-sama could have possibly ended up here, perhaps searching for Gluttony herself or through other means. Either way, despite how low the chances are, there is a possibility that she isn’t here directly as a trap but perhaps as a consequence. Which only leaves one question.”

Otto looked towards Anastasia and finished his thought process out loud, “Why is it that her name returned only now?”

Julius thought for a moment, “It could be that she was successful in getting her name back.”

“Do you really believe her to be capable of that?”

“My Lady is capable of anything she puts her mind to,” Julius said without hesitation.

“…Your confidence aside, it doesn’t explain how we were unable to find her before this, nor the fact that she appeared out of nowhere in a flash of blinding light.

“This place is rather attuned to spatial magic, are you sure that wouldn’t cause such odd occurrences?”

“Julius, I understand that you are feeling a tremendous amount of self-reflection at the moment, but we can’t let it drive us away from the bigger picture, “Otto pleaded, “Think rationally. My Zodda bugs were unable to notice her despite being able to find one book out of what could be possibly millions of others. I do not believe her presence here is beneficial for us. It all smells suspicious. We should focus on putting her in a safe, but bound, status so there is no risk involved. Then, we should prioritize our current plan of getting to the next floor.”

Otto took out Reid’s book and handed it to Julius, Julius was hesitant, “Otto, you must understand-“

“I do understand! I do! If someone that important to me was returned out of nowhere, I would be in your position, most certainly. But I am not. And therefore, I must play the villain here. We have to be vigilant. We can’t let something emotionally debilitate us, especially during such a key moment in a crisis. It is now or never. Reinhard is knee deep in a battle that he may or may not win. I will not risk the people we have around us on any possibility. If you won’t stray from your Lady’s side, then at the very least, watch over me as I delve into the book. I’ll find what we need and report back to you.”

Just as Otto was about to take back the book, Julius grabbed the other end and spoke calmly, “…Otto. I apologize. You are right.”

 

Julius felt worse than before. This whole nightmare of a situation was confusing him. He wanted to protect his Lady but he needed to do his job. People were relying on him. Even if he failed, he shouldn’t let that persist and cause more failures to occur.

 

Otto raised an eyebrow, “Are you sure?”

“I am,” Julius said resolutely, “I was being selfish. I wasn’t considering where I was or what was at stake. I…will not let everyone down.”

Otto smiled and let go of the book, “Good, then let’s get started-“

“Urgh…” They were interrupted by a groan from the bed.

 

 

Julius nearly dropped the book as he crawled closer to Anastasia’s side, all thoughts discarded besides helping the person he had abandoned.

 

Julius felt anxiety creep up his spine, “Anastasia-sama? Are you alright?”

“Ugh, who…what?” Her eyes fluttered open, glancing around groggily before focusing on both Julius and Otto, “…Otto-san?”

Something about that unnerved Julius, though Otto responded faster, “Anastasia-sama? Is it really you?”

She blinked before raising her head, staring at Otto with incredible intensity, “…You remember me?”

Otto’s eyes widened, he whispered, “So it is true, you did lose your name…”

Anastasia looked around nervously, “Where…where am I? Where is this place?”

Julius felt his nerves firing, he spoke quicker than he wanted to, “Anastasia-sama. You are currently at the Sage’s Tower and in a safe room away from danger. We found you when…you appeared after a blinding flash of light.”

Otto chimed in, “Yes. How is it that you appeared here out of nowhere?”

Julius wanted to glare at Otto for pushing Anastasia too hard with questions, but Anastasia’s brow furrowed before he could get the chance, her voice coming out low and confused, “I…don’t know. I remember bein’ in Lugunica one second and the next bein’ here. Yer guess is as good as mine.”

Otto murmured, “I see. Hm, perhaps there is more to this than we once thought. Anastasia-”

Julius intervened, “Anastasia-sama. I must apologize…this must be disorienting for you. To wake up in an unfamiliar place with no idea what is going on. Would you like a second to rest before we continue?”

Julius ignored what was probably Otto’s annoyed gaze as Anastasia smiled at him thoughtfully, “I appreciate the concern Sir Knight, but I think it might be best to get my bearin’s as quickly as possible.”

“I see. I am quite impressed by…your…fortitude,” Julius’s eyes narrowed, “Apologies, my Lady, but what did you just call me?”

Anastasia cocked her head in confusion, “Sir Knight? I’m assumin’ yer a Royal Knight, given yer apparel. Though I’m quite sorry for not recognizin’ ya.”

“…” Julius’s head began to spin as he tried to stand up before nearly falling to the floor.

Otto caught him but was struggling to hold him up, “Julius?! Are you okay?”

Anastasia’s eyes narrowed ever so slightly before widening as she exclaimed, “Is he alright?!”

Julius couldn’t stop staring at Anastasia, his mind reeling as he tried to comprehend what was happening, “…Anastasia-sama. Do you not…not recognize me?”

Anastasia’s eyes widened as she looked to Otto and back to him, “Oh no. I’m so sorry.”

Julius couldn’t believe what was happening his eyes flickered from Otto to Anastasia, back and forth, “I-It can’t be…”

Otto quickly cut in, “Now wait just a moment! Anastasia-sama…this doesn’t make any sense. How is it that you are unable to remember Julius, but I can?! Are you…who are you?”

Anastasia kept her face neutral as she sat up, “Are you implyin’ I’m not who I say I am Otto?”

Otto stood his ground, “Apologies, but I have to. You cannot expect me to believe you have forgotten your own knight. Unless Julius’s name was taken from him, which does not make sense given that I myself can still remember him. Therefore, either you’re not Anastasia-sama or-“

“I have memory loss,” Anastasia finished for him as she raised her hands in the air, “I understand what’s happenin’ here. Listen, I’ll cooperate. But I am who I say I am. I don’t understand why exactly I’m here, but it seems there is a predicament goin’ on, I take it. Could you at least tell me what’s happenin’ for you to be so on edge?”

“…” Otto hesitated to say anything.

But Julius didn’t, he regained his composure and began to stand on his own, walking a bit to the side after patting Otto on the shoulder, “We are currently being assaulted at all sides. Reinhard is keeping the Witch of Envy at bay while the rest of us have been dealing with the Archbishops of Gluttony, who have taken the names and existence of those sleeping beside you.”

Anastasia looked to her side, “I see…wait. Witch of Envy?”

Anastasia’s head whipped back to both Julius and Otto, her voice wavering as she spoke, “What do you mean by that?”

Otto glanced to the side before returning his focus on her, “…The Witch of Envy has escaped her seal and is now hellbent on destroying this entire world. Reinhard is the only one keeping her at bay right now. We need to traverse the tower, avoid Gluttony, and find a solution to her.”

“…Oh my Od,” Anastasia looked shocked beyond compare.

“A natural reaction,” Julius grimaced, “We found you right as we were in the middle of finding this book.”

 

Julius revealed Reid’s book within his hand, though his hand shook from a mix of fear and anxiety. The knight still couldn’t comprehend his situation. That Anastasia, the woman he swore to protect and ultimately failed, now no longer was able to remember him when he could finally remember her. What a cruel twist of fate. Was it really just a memory problem on her end? But it wouldn’t make sense otherwise, Otto could still remember him. Otto was trustworthy. Julius checked his Od and found that it was recognizable by his spirits. It doesn’t make sense…wait a moment.

 

Julius spoke quickly, “Otto. I have a question.”

Otto peered over towards Julius, Anastasia also glanced towards her former knight, the advisor spoke inquisitively, “Uh, sure, go ahead, Julius-san.”

“Those Zodda bugs, you mentioned you should have been able to find Anastasia-sama easily if she was in this tower, correct?”

“Yes? It’s true. That is partially why I’m suspicious of you, Anastasia-sama. No offence,” Otto gave a sheepish smile towards Anastasia.

Anastasia just gave an unamused look, “I understand but I can’t help but feel a little hurt.”

Julius ignored that and continued staring at Otto, “If that’s the case, Otto. How is it that you were only able to find me now?”

Otto blinked, “…What?”

Julius’s hand was now gripping his sword’s handle. He was now a small distance away from both Anastasia and Otto, his back towards the door of the room, “The Zodda Bugs. You should have been able to find me. Quickly. The fact that you didn’t. The fact that I know for certain you, Otto, would have been able to discern me from those monsters, concerns me. Who are you?”

 

Julius sweated as Otto’s eyes widened, Anastasia keeping a neutral expression but her eyes shifting between them.

 

Things got a whole lot more troublesome.

Chapter 38: A Stab at Diplomacy

Summary:

Julius has no idea what is happening anymore...

Chapter Text

Julius’s innards twisted, his brow moist with sweat as he now had his sword fully out and pointed at the two of them. How could he have been so naïve? This was a situation where he could trust no one outright. These Archbishops defied reality. So, any notion that he could figure this out with straightforward logic should be thrown down the gutter. He needed to be more careful, think outside the normal scope of reality, if he is going to get out of this alive and save the people he cares for.

 

Julius’s eyes flickered to Anastasia, the source of most of his inner turmoil. He so desperately wanted to know if she was real or not. His brain buzzed as the memories that once were gone came back in full force. Where did she go? How has she been? What has she done? Does she hate them? Does she hate him for failing her? What troubles has she gone through? Why does she look so different? She looks healthier and less healthy at the same time? Does that make sense? Does any of this make sense?

 

“Do…t…ust….an…Ju…”

 

Pain rocketed through his skull as the whispers returned, getting clearer by the second. Who was that? Is he going insane? He needed to deal with all this quickly or else he’d no longer trust anything or anyone. No. He may no longer even trust himself.

 

Julius pursed his lips as he stood firm, “Explain yourselves. I have no reason to trust either of you given what is at stake.”

“…” Otto was now giving his full attention to Julius, as Anastasia glanced back and forth between them.

Anastasia tried to intervene, “Now hold on, let’s not get too hasty. We don’t need to escalate this. Let’s just all calm down and talk this through.”

“I am calm, my Lady,” Julius said while now aiming his sword directly at Anastasia, “If that is truly you. However, I have no evidence to trust your identity.”

Anastasia’s face did not flinch, only having her eyebrow lift up barely, “Hmm, just realized, Mm Lady? Ya call all women that or am I to assume we were close?”

“…We were. And it is odd you do not know me, yet Otto does. Either I am being affected by the powers of Gluttony, and I am no longer of this world, making Otto the prime suspect for impersonation given he has knowledge of me. Or you are lying, trying to incite tension between Otto and I for nefarious reasons.”

 

Julius wasn’t quite sure about the former theory. While Otto was suspicious, it did not explain why he could still feel his spirits. They should have forgotten him, but they haven’t. Meaning, he must still have his name. Right? Julius wasn’t quite sure, but he wasn’t taking any chances.

 

Surprisingly, Anastasia nodded at that, “I can see yer point. If I was in yer shoes, I’d think the same. And it is odd how ol’ Otto couldn’t find ya despite his hand little Divine Protection.”

Julius’s eyes narrowed as he turned his attention to Otto again. I knew I felt something off earlier.

Julius was now gripping his sword handle tightly, his instincts now firing at all cylinders, “I was hiding and running through this whole area for days. How is it that, given the sheer magnitude of bugs under your control, were you unable to pinpoint my location and meet me so much earlier?”

“…Julius, I understand how this looks. But you have to understand, I had to make sure you were not one of them,” Otto put his hands in the air, “I know what you must be thinking but I am telling the truth. This place is not normal. Time and space feel so off. I’ve been trying to find you, honest, but it feels like I’ve been running circles in the same area for days on end. I only just recently found you.”

“…Be that as it may. How does that explain you finding the book so quickly?”

“Julius, you saw how long it took us to find it!” Otto yelled in outrage, “And if you must know, I have no idea! The book was easy but for some reason, you were not. No matter what, you were always out of reach no matter how many times those bugs tried to find you! I took a gamble trying to find this place and only found you by pure luck!”

Julius’s eyes narrowed, “Nothing you do is based on luck. We both know that is true.”

Otto stared back, eyes nearly bulging out, his arms falling to his sides, “…What do you mean by that?”

Julius was now more suspicious, eyebrow raised, “The Otto I know is responsible for many accomplishments and has a sharp mind unmatched by any other tactician. You always think before acting and you never take any risks. You are not someone who would go into an area without a plan, not the type of person to trust anyone without fully understanding them and being incredibly on-guard with every piece of personal information you have. Do you really expect me to think that someone like you, the strategist who helped defend Priestella and was responsible for many of the victories for the Emilia camp, would come into an area without any recon or planning?! You must have known I was in there, that would be the only reason you would even think of entering!”

 

Julius felt awful interrogating his friend, but it made no sense to him. Otto was cautious, incredibly paranoid, and the type of person to always have backup plans upon backup plans. He would never take any risks without thinking it through. Otto reminded Julius of Anastasia. Perhaps that was why they got along so well in her absence. The two merchants were both cunning, mercantile, and perceptive. Fiercely loyal to those they care for and kind at heart. But not the type to make decisions without some sort of backup plan.

 

Otto kept staring, his eyes haunted, “…Shut up.”

Julius raised his eyebrow, “Otto- “
“I said shut up!” Otto pointed at Julius fiercely, eyes manic and filled with unyielding rage unforeseen before, “What do you know about me?!”

“I-“

“You think I’m some kind of God or something! That I’m some kind of manipulative villain who thinks twelve steps ahead of everyone! Do you think I’m someone who can’t make mistakes?!”

“Uh- “Julius’s eyes rocketed towards Anastasia who looked incredibly uncomfortable.

Otto wasn’t done, he snarled at Julius while continuing to point his finger with emphasis, “I am the unluckiest person in the world! I nearly drowned when I entered a bath for the first time in my life! My Divine Protection was absolute hell to get used to! I got food poisoning from drinking alcohol! ALCOHOL!”

Anastasia’s eyes kept darting between Julius and Otto, she opened her mouth as if to say something, then clamped it back shut when she heard Otto continue, “…”

“This whole situation is awful! We came here looking for answers, only to end up flailing around for weeks, met a Sage that doesn’t care about us, and now the Witch of Envy is breathing down our necks! I don’t even know where Reinhard is or even if he’s okay! We’ve been stuck here with no source of food or water; I’ve been rationing as best I can but I’m practically starving at this point! And I am not looking forward to scavenging for insects! You think eating bugs are bad?! IMAGINE HEARING THEIR SCREAMS, BEGGING FOR MERCY WHILE YOU STRUGGLE TO SURVIVE! This place is an absolute hellhole! I can’t even go to the bathroom because the toilet keeps teleporting! I was stuck circling the same hallway for eight hours! I am hungry, thirsty, too cold at night and too hot in the day, tired, sleep deprived, and I think I’m hallucinating! And you’re really expecting me to be so sane and rational enough to plan everything out perfectly?! ARE YOU MENTAL?!”

 

Otto was now yelling at the top of his lungs practically foaming at the mouth, walking in circles while ranting. Julius and Anastasia side eyed each other. Julius could see her eyes dart from him to Otto and back to him, before nudging her head at the poor advisor with a hint of concern. Julius gave the slightest hint of a shrug as he started to realize this might actually be Otto. Only Otto would be this exasperated with everything.

 

Otto kept spewing venom, his focus back to Julius, making the knight flinch, “And what do you mean I’m responsible for the camp’s success?! Do you really think we’re all that capable?!”

Julius did not expect Otto to be this forward with his problems, he lifted his hand up, “Otto, you musn’t-“

“The rabbits? We barely got out of that situation alive, and I was not planning any of that! I burned down our mansion to make a distraction! We were running around with no idea what we were doing at Priestella!”

Julius stood back in alarm, “Wait, Otto please calm down. Choose your words carefully-“

Otto stomped forward and nearly got into Julius’s face, only stopped short by Julius’s sword nearly an inch away from Otto’s heart, “No! I don’t care anymore! I’m sick of this! I’m sick of tiptoeing around everything and acting like everything is going well! IT’S NOT! Ever since Priestella, I’ve been getting closer and closer to losing my mind! Everyone keeps acting like things are normal, but I can tell! Something is wrong! Emilia-sama keeps getting more and more distracted every day, as if she’s trying to find something! I don’t even know what that whole ‘find love’ thing is about or where it came from! Beatrice-sama stopped talking to us and basically disappeared! Roswaal hates everything and everyone and has been drinking himself into a drunken stupor that makes me look like a lightweight! Meili keeps trying to escape every day and I’m really getting sick of having to live over some psychotic child who keeps trying to stab me every time I sleep! Ram is Ram, except worse somehow, I don’t even know how that is possible! And I can barely keep the estate together! I am trying my best to wrangle everyone and keep things cohesive but none of it works! It’s like we’re friends but I keep forgetting why we are friends in the first place! I’m tearing my hair out trying to make sure we win this selection but none of it is working! The nobles hate us still, Roswaal not talking with any of them for months just made it worse! We have no official knight! Our only win at Priestella was Emilia killing Greed, by somehow guessing how to defeat that Archbishop BY PURE LUCK!”

 

Otto was gasping for breath, red faced, struggling to keep his eyes focused, his voice came out hoarse and sullen, “And every day we somehow win or get out of a horrible situation by the skin of our teeth, is a day I lose hope. Because that just means when we fail, we are going to fail spectacularly. I can feel it. We are on the precipice of the abyss, and I feel like I’m the only one who can see it. And that scares me more than anything. Knowing that all of the friends I made and care for will all suffer and die if I’m not careful. Emilia-sama. Ram. Rem. Frederica. Sylphy. Petra. Everyone. All of them could die and I’ll have no way to stop it. And look around us. This is the exact situation I’ve been dreading. Stuck in a position where we can barely see a way out. Having to act like everything is okay or act like there is something we can do. When really? We are well and truly fucked. And you know what? I’m tired of acting like I know what I’m doing. I feel like a joke. A fraud. An idiot who is in way over their heads. I hate the fact that people keep praising me for situations that I had no control over and no confidence in ever succeeding. I do not know what I’m doing. I am barely understanding our next move. The book with Reid. Going up the tower. Trying to find something to deal with the literal Witch of Envy. None of it matters because we are all going to die here.”

“…Otto, I-“

Julius was interrupted for the fifth time as Otto blurted out, “Stop. Don’t. Just…don’t.”

“…”
