“…I’m sick of hearing people try to encourage me or give me some inspiring speech or say that I am better than I think,” Otto stood motionless, still breathing heavily but now his eyes looked defeated and tired, “I hate it. I know who I am. I understand what I want. I don’t need support. I don’t need people to pity me or offer condolences or give me hope. I don’t…”

 

His voice petered out as Otto looked to the side, contemplative. Silence persisted as he stood there, legs looking ready to collapse and his lips wavering with emotion.

 

“… I don’t need any of that. What I need. Is a reason to keep going,” Otto weakly cried out, “I don’t know why I’m doing this anymore. I care about my camp. I care about my friends. But working this hard, struggling for everyone’s sakes. It feels…empty. It’s been empty for a while and I don’t know why. I just. Don’t. Know. Why!”

 

Otto stomped on the ground with that last word, before becoming silent. Otto stood motionless as he simply stared at the ground, unresponsive and radiating melancholy. Julius didn’t know what to say. And it hurt him tremendously when he realized how inept he was. He was aware that Otto was stressed out but he did not realize the depths of his struggles. It reminded him of his mistakes with Felix. How he let the poor healer fester in his own fears and emotions, until he made terrible mistakes, hurting an innocent soul that he would have otherwise not done in any other situation. His heart burned. Julius began to regret his actions and how callous he was with his friends’ inner turmoil. And yet, Julius still couldn’t find the words to help Otto.

 

It seems Anastasia was different, however, walking cautiously up to Otto and peering around his side to meet his eyes. Otto’s eyes widened before looking away from Anastasia, seemingly embarrassed.

 

Anastasia’s face was neutral but showed some compassion and concern, “Ya feel better gettin’ that all out of yer system?”

“…Not really,” Otto said as he chose to look anywhere else than the other two.

Anastasia sighed, “I understand. Been in the same position but bein’ honest about how shitty everything is, is a good step forward.”

Otto gave a sad wheeze, “Is that supposed to make me feel better?”

Anastasia shrugged, “You said you didn’t want pity. And I understand. Pity ain’t necessary for people like us. Understanding, comfort, relief. But never pity. I’m just tryin’ to say that what yer goin’ through ain’t special. Not in the sense that you don’t matter. But in the sense that ya ain’t alone.”

Otto’s brow furrowed, “…You seem very different compared to Priestella.”

Anastasia shrugged again, “People change. When I lost my name, I was so lost. Bein’ on my own for a time. Tryin’ ta understand my purpose here. It’s all somethin’ ta think about. And I had a lot of time ta think. And because of that, and some fateful meetin’s, I’m not really who I was anymore.”

“…Are you really Anastasia Hoshin?”
Anastasia smiled, “In a way, not really. Would it matter if I am or not?”

“…Well, I guess not. Even if you tell us stuff about yourself that only we should know, it won’t matter given the Archbishops can take your memories. At the very least, Julius deserves to know for sure. It’s only right given your two’s history,” Otto nudged his head towards said knight.

Anastasia glanced over to Julius who awkwardly laid his sword lower, her smile became much more melancholic, “I’m guessin’ you and I know each other?”

“…Yes. I was your knight,” Julius looked pained by the lack of recognition, “I inducted you into the royal selection and was by your side since the beginning.”

Anastasia’s smile slightly wavered, “Well I’m sorry bout my reaction then. It always hurts not havin’ people recognize ya. Especially when you do but they can’t.”

Julius felt even worse, “Anastasia-sama. I…I’m sorry.”

Anastasia raised her eyebrow, “For what?”

He put his free hand on his chest, “I failed you, didn’t I? Your name was lost. You were alone for months. You had no one by your side. I essentially abandoned you.”

“I guess I’ll take that apology but it’s hard for me ta really process. I don’t really feel abandoned. Sure, I lost my company and all I had but…from my point of view, there was no one I really cared for to lose. It feels weird. I know that I should feel terrible, that someone close to me forgot about my existence. But because I don’t remember ya, I don’t feel it. Quite odd to feel and think about,” Anastasia looked sympathetic at Julius.

Julius’s lips thinned, his guilt worsening, “…Even so, my mistakes have caused you to suffer. And for that, I must apologize and seek penance. In whatever way you see fit.”

Anastasia cocked her head, “You believe I’m who I am?”

Julius shook his head, “Perhaps, perhaps not. Ultimately, my sins still exist. If you are truly my Lady, then I deserve punishment. If you are not, then that means my Lady must be dead or suffering a worse fate. As such, I still deserve a swift execution for my failure.”

“…” Anastasia sighed before muttering to herself, “Feel like I’m gettin’ déjà vu.”

“Hm? Day Jah Voo?” Julius said in confusion.

Anastasia shook her head, “Nothin’. Just somethin’ I picked up. As for what you said, I forgive ya.”

Julius was taken aback, “Surely you jest? Are you being merciful to me because of your lack of memory?”

“No. While it does take away the sting, I know myself enough that I wouldn’t really blame ya. I’d be sad, regretful, and miss ya dearly. But I wouldn’t have blamed ya for it.”

“…” That somehow made him feel even worse.

“Besides, it wasn’t all bad.”

“How so?” Julius was curious of the silver lining, as was Otto given the advisor was now glancing at their conversation instead of looking so downtrodden.

“I got married,” Anastasia said with no hesitation, “Well, more like engaged I guess but at this point it’s basically marriage.”

“Ah well, that is wonderful…to…hear,” Julius started processing what she just said.

 

Otto’s jaw dropped as Julius’s eyes started to bulge out of his skull.

 

Julius stuttered, “C-could you say that again? I believe I misheard something.”

Anastasia smiled, “I’m getting married.”

“…What?”

Anastasia snickered, “Is it that hard ta believe?”

“I-what-who-where-why?” As Julius was short-circuiting,

Otto chimed in, “Apologies, what he means to say is while you getting married is believable, you getting married in less than a year since you disappeared is incredibly absurd and surprising.”

Anastasia began to laugh, “Fair enough. Even I would be surprised hearin’ this from me as it wasn’t expected.”

“…What happened, Anastasia-sama?” Julius said, genuinely curious.

“I fell in love,” Anastasia said as her eyes seemed to dance with delight, “It’s really as simple as that.”

“I see…does he make you happy, Anastasia-sama?”

“He does, to a surprising degree. He makes me laugh, feel safe, feel warm, and feel loved. Even though I lost everything. Suffered through so much. I don’t regret any of it. Because at the very least, I met him. It’s why I don’t blame ya Julius. At the end of the day, this all led ta me finding happiness in a different way.”

“…I am truly happy for you, Anastasia-sama,” while it hurts Julius to hear that he missed such an incredible event for his Lady, the way she speaks of love moves his romantic heart.

 

The way she looked as she spoke, the way her demeanor feels a tad different, the way she seemed slightly saddened when reminiscing. It reminded him of those romance books he often read in his younger years.

 

“Anyways,” Anastasia seemed slightly embarrassed, realizing what she said, “Let’s focus back on the topic. It seems we all can’t trust each other 100% as there is no way ta fully disprove or prove our identities. So, I suggest a compromise. Let’s use an oath.”

Otto’s eyes widened, “Are you saying we should make a magically binding contract to prevent any future conflict or betrayal?”

“Exactly. We can’t just stay here with knives and swords pointed at each other. From what you say, we are approachin’ a deadline here and it ain’t like we can escape by ourselves. So let’s make a contract that will allow us ta not worry about each other and accomplish our goals step by step,” Anastasia offered.

Julius nodded hesitantly, “A superb idea. However, what would be the terms of the contract.”

“Nothing too complicated, as we do not have the time nor the brain power ta accomplish somethin’ like that,” Anastasia tapped her chin in thought before snapping her fingers, “How bout this? We all promise ta not harm each other directly and ta work together until the crisis that is currently befalling us is concluded.”

That sounded great to Julius, but it seems Otto had other ideas given his interjection, “Why ‘directly?’ That added stipulation could allow us to hurt each other indirectly.”

Anastasia pondered before answering, “Hm, I guess I was trying to make sure we don’t accidentally kill each other by violating the contract. It would bind our souls so I was preferring one that wouldn’t kill us by technicality. Such as one of us tripping and hurting the other accidentally.”

Otto grimaced, “I did not know magical oaths worked like that.”

“It seems you’ve never done business with any mages, Otto. A lot of them often have secrets that they never want ta leak to the public. Makin’ very particular magical oaths is how they prevent any secret spillage. I myself took part in some many years ago,” Anastasia started lecturing to Otto about magical business 101.

 

Julius, meanwhile, began to get distracted by something. While his mind was starting to warm up to the idea that these two were the people he knew and cared for, his body thought differently. For some reason, his instincts were blaring danger at him loudly and it was making him incredibly uncomfortable. His gut, it was screaming at him about something he can’t quite grasp. Like an itch that would not go away. It has been like this for quite some time, and he does not know what to do.

 

“…oo…ow…r…”

 

Julius whipped his head to the source of the voice but found nothing again. It was maddening. Was he going insane?

 

“…us….ow…”

 

Julius grit his teeth. The voice was getting more and more clear. Making his brain pound. And this incessant itch in his gut! Both were making him feel nauseous. He needed them both to stop, now! He couldn’t even focus on the conversation in front of him.

 

“Show…her…”

 

Show her? Show her what? Who are you? Why does your voice sound so familiar?

 

“Show her the Sage’s book.”

 

Julius’s eyes widened. The pounding and itch stopped. Julius peered down and noticed that his hand was in his coat pocket, directly above the book filled with strange writing, right next to Reid’s. He didn’t even realize his hand had moved in the first place. He sheathed his sword.

 

“Julius? Is somethin’ wrong?” Julius blinked at Anastasia’s words, turning his head slowly towards his Lady.

 

He blinked again. The gut feeling was now raging at him to act. No reason. Just instincts.

 

And despite every logical part of his brain telling him it was absurd, he weirdly trusted said instincts. He shouldn’t, but he does. He trusted the voice. He trusted him. It didn’t make sense. A voice that felt so distinctly regal yet so far away. And yet…

 

“Anastasia-sama,” Julius lifted the diary out of his pocket and presented the cover to Anastasia, “Before we make any decisions, I was curious about something I found within this very room. This book contains scriptures that look oddly familiar to Hoshin’s writing. I was wondering if you knew what it said.”

Anastasia lit up when she heard Julius’s words, walking closer to see, but her brow furrowed when she focused on the cover, “Flugel’s…diary?”

 

The exact second Anastasia said those words, the exact millisecond she touched the book, the room started to rumble.

 

“What’s going on?!” Otto cried as the room began to glow red. Lines of glowing magical energy appeared on the floors and walls as the Sage’s room roared with noise.

 

And just as suddenly as it occurred, the three were now flying mid-air, teleported somewhere else without notice. Julius reacted quickly and called on Aro to use wind magic to hurl himself towards Anastasia, catching her in freefall in his arms while he then pointed at the ground and used another Fura. The wind spirit heeded his call and slowed their descent as he and Otto fell to the ground seamlessly. Well, not ground. They actually landed on a table in what looked to be some sort of dining room, looking oddly familiar to the one he saw in the lower floors.

 

“Uh,” Julius blinked as a voice called out right in front of him.

 

He then realized that they landed right in front of a group of mostly unfamiliar people. A white- and black-haired man in a black haori with orange stars, wearing a familiar white fox scarf of his shoulders. A tall wolfman in a black kimono with white wolves strewn about its cloth, a satchel over his back, smoking a pipe with a kunai in his hand. A positively terrifying white-haired woman dressed in a white and green kimono. And, for some reason, the Emilia camp’s Great Spirit Beatrice. All staring with varying levels of confusion and surprise at their sudden arrival.

 

The man in particular’s face shifted multiple times. From pure surprise, to confusion, to joy, to confusion again, to suspicion, to horror, and then finally, the most terrifying glare Julius had ever seen. Even compared to the woman literally dripping in bloodlust naturally, right next to the man, that glare nearly made Julius falter.

 

“Julius. Put her down and step away,” the man pulled out a knife and pointed it at him.

Julius’s eyes widened in alarm, wondering why the man was acting like that and how he knew him, only to get his questions answered directly from the woman in his arms, “Subaru?!”

 

Julius looked down at his lady and saw how she looked directly at Subaru. Her eyes shined just like it did back in the room. When she talked about being in love.

 

Julius blinked. He then looked at Subaru who was glaring at him wildly.

 

He then blinked again and looked back at Anastasia, whose expression was a mix of joy and something else he couldn’t put his finger on. The same woman who he was holding, bridal carry style.

 

Julius then blinked and stared off into space. It didn’t take him long to connect the dots.

 

Julius then whipped his head towards Subaru and yelled, “Wait it’s not what you think-“

“Julius. Put her down now and get out of the way!” Subaru yelled back, not letting Julius explain himself.

 

The poor knight grimaced and quickly obliged, putting his Lady down gently before taking a few steps back, trying not to accidentally walk backwards off the dining table, nearly running into Otto. He really hoped that he didn’t make a bad first impression on his Lady’s future husband.

 

“Subaru…” Anastasia, however, was solely focused on the person in front of her, “I-“

“Julius. Otto. Get over here now,” Subaru said, motioning them with his other hand to his location.

 

Julius looked at Otto in confusion, Otto returning a similar look. Julius then refocused on Subaru. He raised an eyebrow before noticing. Subaru was still glaring and pointing his knife. However, it was not pointed at them.

 

But at Anastasia.

Chapter 39: ______ For Climate, Hell For Company

Summary:

Subaru confronts Anastasia (?)....

Chapter Text

“Subaru, what are you doing? Don’t you recognize me?” Anastasia looked hurt, pleading at Subaru.

But Subaru’s glare only grew fiercer, “Don’t you fucking use her voice like that. The fact that you’re trying to use her body and voice makes me sick.”

 

Subaru was an idiot. He knew this to his core. But he wasn’t some gullible fool anymore. The impersonation was almost perfect. Nearly identical to how Anastasia would act and talk, her mannerisms down to even the most finite of details. But again, it was only almost perfect, and it would have fooled anyone besides Subaru. He was sure Julius could have sniffed out the obfuscation if the poor guy wasn’t affected by Gluttony.

 

How did he know? Because Subaru memorized everything about Anastasia Hoshin. Her breathing patterns, the way she walked, the way she moved, every single habit. Even down to the intervals of her blinking and the exact cadence and tone shifts every time she spoke. Subaru memorized it all during his time in Hell. During the last nights, when he knew Anastasia’s moments would be her last. Right before he would kill himself, he would spend all the time he had left searing her very existence within his mind. Just so, if he ever failed, he would never ever forget her.

 

And the fact this monster was wearing her skin, acting so familiar with him and Julius, looking at Subaru with eyes that were filled with so much love and devotion. It sickened him to his core. Who was this? Was it Pandora? Was it Capella? One of the Gluttonies? It didn’t matter. What mattered is that whoever this was, it was using her visage in some disgusting attempt to impersonate her. And whatever it was needed to die screaming.

 

He quickly sent out the information to his companions, alerting them that the Anastasia in front of them was an imposter. Only to get back something even stranger from two of them.

 

From Halibel, he got a nostalgic smell of grass that was filled with both a tinge of bitterness and fond sweetness. From Beatrice, he got the brief chapter of a certain fox and her schemes from Priestella. Both had the same message.

 

“We remember her.”

 

Tia also sent a message, though it was more akin to a slightly pissed storm cloud that grumbled jealously that the other two recognized Anastasia from some forgotten past, but she didn’t.

 

It filled Subaru with both delight and dread. Anastasia’s name was back. Subaru was ecstatic because that meant his lover’s exile and longest source of misery was finally gone. That once this was all over, Anastasia could finally return to her camp. As for the dread, that originated from one single question: why would her name come back at the same time someone was impersonating her? And what did that mean for the person in front of him?

 

Subaru’s use of Basilisk Ops did not help, the Od looked exactly similar to Anastasia’s, an iridescent light. It should have filled Subaru with joy but her slightly off mannerisms made him viscerally nauseous and angry beyond belief. He needed to figure out who this was, pronto.

 

Anastasia looked sincerely hurt but Subaru wasn’t convinced, “Subaru. Don’t do this to me. You know me.”

“Yeah, I do. And whoever you are, you’re not Anastasia.”

“What about me makes you think I’m not who I am?!” Not-Anastasia said in dismay.

Subaru sneered, “For starters, everything.”

“You…you!” Not-Anastasia’s face was practically trembling with shock and embarrassment.

Subaru didn’t back down, “Julius, Otto. That isn’t Ana.”

Julius looked alarm, the poor guy must be completely flummoxed, “How can you tell?”

Subaru blurted out, “She’s breathing every 2.7 seconds instead of 2.3. Her blinking is also off, Ana has a habit of blinking every 1.5 seconds, but she tends to double blink randomly. Also, she usually has a habit of wiggling her nose every few minutes or when a breeze comes, doing it when no one is looking.”

“…”

“…What?” Subaru looked around when he realized everyone staring at him, “What did I say?”

Otto yelled out, “Sorry but that was the creepiest thing I have ever heard!”

Halibel just started laughing hysterically as Tia muttered, “That is weirdest thing I have ever heard you say. Which is an accomplishment, Su.”

Beatrice’s face was in her hands, “Betty’s Subaru is going to be on a watchlist, I suppose.”

“They have a point Subaru. What you just said is borderline psychotic.”

I didn’t mean it like that! Besides, aren’t you supposed to know the person you love so well down to the most minute detail?!

Julius chided Otto, “Nonsense, I believe it is quite romantic for a person to know their partner that well, as strange as it might sound.”

…Okay, maybe I am a creep.

Anastasia was the only one taking such accusations seriously, sighing to herself, “I should have known…we were hoping this was going to be easier, tsu~.”

 

As she said so, two shadows dashed in from the ceiling, blades clashing with both Halibel’s kunai and Zarestia’s wind, knocking the two shadows back, both landing next to Anastasia. Julius swiftly dashed with Otto next to Subaru’s group, sword now pointed firmly at Anastasia and the two new and familiar assailants.

 

“Ah, how magnificent! How tantalizing! How delectable! How excellent! How truly awe-inspiring! To think that our actions at Priestella have concocted a most exquisite dish! Look at you, Subaru-kun! You have become my greatest masterpiece! My magnum opus! You are now made of the finest ingredients ever conceived! Terrifying aura. A mindset bordering on insanity. Experiences and knowledge far surpassing any known person in just the briefest amount of time! You…are a dish best served maliciously, I am looking forward to finally devouring you!” Lye Batenkaitos screamed with pure ecstasy.

Subaru visibly cringed, “Urgh, I feel like I’m being looked at like a piece of meat.”

Roy Alphard, standing next to his brother, sighed, the boy’s face was tinged with pure disgruntlement, “How tasteless. Such scraps of meat could have been gorged on earlier for little to no difference. We could have eaten them all and more at Priestella but you had to have your way.”

Lye chastised his brother, “You talk of taste when you have no sense of decorum. You lack the eye and tongue to see how delicious he has become! His eyes, his demeanor, the very way he barely flinches when he sees us! All of it shows how monstrous he has become! And that does not include how you, yourself, gave up a meal for our sister. And look how wonderful that turned out! She has been freed from her prison and can now partake in the feast with us all, in person!”

Roy sneered, “That was not intentional in the slightest! I fully intended on gorging on the little merchant. I have no idea why I wasn’t able to feast on everything, it made no-“

 “Shut up! Your ruining dinner with our guests,” Not-Anastasia glared at the two brothers, her hand on her hip.

 

Surprisingly, the two quieted down, though Roy had a permanent frown on his face while Lye muttered something about ‘little sisters going through puberty.’

 

Not-Anastasia then coughed into her hand and spoke with poise and an odd softness, “Apologies for that my dear Subaru. Unfortunately, we did not plan for your arrival so quickly, we had hoped this would be all over soon so that our family could have a nice reunion.”

Subaru nearly gagged hearing her speak so affectionately about him, “Stop talking like that. You’re going to make me hurl.”

“Oh~. But Poobaru~,” Subaru felt his bloodlust rising as she spoke, “Isn’t this your beloved talking? Didn’t you want to reunite with her and bring about her greatest dream? To have her family all together and have a grand banquet? All so you guys can finally be happy and be married? You wanted that, didn’t you?”

Subaru narrowed his eyes, trying his best not to grind his teeth, “Don’t talk like you know.”

“But~. We~. Doooo~,” she said in a sing-a-long voice, “We know how much you love her. How much she loves you. We know how much she longs to see you. How much she treasures you. How much she thinks about you. How much she agonizes each day, wishing for you to be happy with her despite being so inept at doing so. Her memories of you. Her love for you. Her pure, unadulterated, joy when she sees how happy you are. All of these would make such a delectable meal when it comes to finally devouring her.”

“You-“ Subaru’s snarl was cut off by Not-Anastasia’s words.

Anastasia’s eyes narrowed in disgust, “But we didn’t. We didn’t eat her because it doesn’t matter how much she loves you. How many memories she has or how wonderful her life was. What matters most is the fact…that she has you. She has you. She has Julius. She has Ricardo. She has Mimi. She has Hetaro. She has Tivey. She has Echidna. She has Joshua. She has all of these wonderful people in her life that she can dine with.”

Not-Anastasia’s lips thinned into a line as she spoke derisively, “And she squanders it. Like a petulant child! So greedy and yet she doesn’t take advantage of how wonderful it was! She could have had a wonderful relationship with any man or woman but chose to never give into romance, even once! She had someone as high-end as Mr. Finest Knight over here but chose to let things be. And guess what? Despite never being interested in romance. Despite never caring for the idea or thought of being with another person intimately. Despite being so focused on other desires and worldly possessions. Her greatest joy was falling in love with you: Natsuki Subaru. Her greatest regret was never meeting you earlier. And you know what’s so funny about that? She in fact did. She met you nearly a year and a half ago, during that meeting between all of the knights and candidates and wise men. And her first thought about you was a simple two-word description: loudmouthed idiot. Isn’t that funny?! The mere idea that she, someone who looked down on you, ended up falling head over heels for you. If she even tried to get to know you earlier, we are sure she could have had some inkling of who you are and possibly even became close friends with you. Getting a hint of that happiness she could so easily obtain. But you know what’s even funnier? That version of her would never have tried to deepen your relationship, even if that was the case. She’d flirt, tease, and give you some interest. But her personality would never try to attain happiness she could never imagine. Why? Because she’s so greedy but has no interest in going past her bias. Why should she? When all she has done and experienced gave her no reason to push past her boundaries? She has always been rewarded for her thinking. She always finds a way out of every situation. Always knows how to barter her way out. She has faced challenge after challenge but was never punished in a way that makes her think of more. To think outside the box. Only when she lost everything, did she really understand what it meant. What she wanted and had always wanted. Something that she so desperately craved since childhood, since her first parental figure ingrained it deep into her psyche: to not be alone. She wanted love. She wanted to be loved. And she wanted to give love back. She desperately craved it, and it evolved into her desperate wish to keep the people around her close as much as possible. She doesn’t want anyone to leave her. She hates the very notion that anyone would leave her. But she hates the idea of forcing anyone to stay. To her, it matters not if someone stays if they are staying without wanting to do so in the first place. She is so greedy in that way, wanting and craving as she sees fit without any thought behind how difficult it is to achieve. She squanders it! Squanders it! SQUANDERS EVERYTHING SHE COULD EVER HAVE! It is like we are seeing someone constantly be offered a high-quality meal, only to throw it away simply because they cannot see that their greatest desire is right in front of them. And the worst part is that she knows the value but does not truly understand it! It is as if she is both perceptive and blind. Truthful yet hidden. Greedy yet wasteful. Anastasia Hoshin, if we were her, should have talked to you Natsuki Subaru. She should have noticed your various oddities and reached out after the Whale Hunt. She should have understood you more. She should have put in more effort. But she chose to instead constantly seek other avenues. To never think of you as anything more or less. And as a result, she threw away an early path to true happiness. She is someone who benefits well from a romantic relationship. She is not someone who needs such a relationship but would find themselves passionately involved in one. And yet she never once thought to do so! That is why we consider her to be lesser. To be suboptimal. Because such mistakes didn’t happen just once, twice, or thrice! It happened consistently! She could have been happy with Julius but chose to focus on acquiring a kingdom. She could have been happy becoming a queen but chose to take riskier ventures and ended up losing her name. She could have been happy with you but chose to delve into knowledge and thoughts that revealed truths she should have never known! Choosing to dance around the idea instead of confronting it and returning to her happiness! She is wasteful. She could have been satisfied, satiated, given a happy life. A life that anyone and everyone dreams of having! But no! She chooses to never be satisfied. She chooses to chase a perfect relationship with you because she can’t bear the thought of it being one-sided. She hates it. The very idea of never being able to pay you back for all of your love. That she herself could never come close to it. Which would leave her on the same level as those you previously loved. And it infuriates her to her core. Because if she hated those people for failing you, then what makes her so different? So. Greedy. Wanting everything you are and wanting you to desire all of her. And she ended up pushing you away anyway! In her pursuit for happiness, she burns any possibility of it occurring due to her negligence. Incompetent. Idiotic. Brainless. Moronic. But not us. No. Not! Us! We will not be like her. If you are going to waste your life, then give it to us! Dig in the trash and wallow in your self-pity for all we care! We will take your tossed scraps and make a fine dish! We will attain her happiness because we are better. We know what we want. And we will get it. We will become happy! We see her life, and we know how close she has always been to happiness! And we know that the key to happiness, here and now…is you. Natsuki Subaru. We will have you. And then we will have your family in Banan. Julius. And everything else. We will have the joy that you and everyone else in this miserable rotten waste of a world constantly waste with abandon. Because we, Witch Cult Sin Archbishop representing Gluttony, Louis Arneb, want to become happy. And if we have to devour and shit out every single one of you until there is nothing left, building a staircase to the heavens above, off your corpses and bones, all so that even a single morsel of pure unadulterated happiness can be obtained. Then we shall.”

 

It was in those words that Natsuki Subaru finally understood what was going on. It wasn’t that this woman was playing pretend or acting like his precious fiancé. No. Louis Arneb was trying to become her. She was…

Subaru spoke with every ounce of killing intent he could muster, “Get out of her body.”

“Oho~? So you finally figured it out, hm?” Louis said with a saccharine smirk.

“I don’t know how you are possessing her, but you are not having her. She is not yours. She is not anyone’s!” Subaru said with fierce determination.

“He’s right,” Julius said as he walked up with his sword now pointed at the Gluttony trio, “You will not have our Lady.”

Halibel patted Subaru on the shoulder from behind and spoke nonchalantly, “It’s bad manners ta take a man’s wife. By the code of brotherhood Su-san taught, that means I gotta kill and castrate ya. Sorry.”

Tia was on Subaru’s other side, glaring daggers and adding a heavy air of bloodlust to the surrounding area, “You all talk too much. Stop ranting like a lame insect and get the fuck out of Ana. Or I’ll tear you apart and hang you using your entrails.”

Subaru in one swift motion took off his fox scarf and wrapped it around Beatrice. The little spirit’s eyes flickered, her cadence now matching Eridna’s as she spoke, “Sister and I only have two people we wish to see happy. If that means tearing down your happiness, then so be it. Monsters like you three deserve none.”

 

At their responses, Louis just grinned widely, the smile ominous on Anastasia’s face, “That’s what we want. We want that camaraderie! That sense of family! That pure fulfillment that can only be achieved by those who truly love each other. Ah. We can’t wait to have it all and more. It’s a shame you weren’t able to receive your prize, Julius.”

Julius’s eyebrows rose, “My prize?”

“For winning the hide and seek contest. We were hoping to guide you to your salvation, to be the new you. Give you a party for your new life. But alas, you ended up coming right as poor Anastasia was just coming out to greet you. So, we had to adapt. But don’t worry, we can celebrate the party right here. Right now,” Louis-Anastasia smiled and snapped her fingers.

 

Subaru was confused by what she meant, until he heard the tearing of flesh and creation of magic. His head nearly snapped as it turned to the source of the sound.

 

“…!” Subaru heard Julius’s gasps and moans, seeing the poor knight spurting blood from his mouth and from the now punctured hole in his chest, occupied by a summoned piece of stone. A book was sent scattered to the floor, landing right before the dining table. Subaru’s eyes widened as he realized the source of the Dona: a horrified Otto with his arm held up, twisted forward without his consent.

 

“I-I, I didn’t want to do that! That wasn’t me-I-AH!” Otto screamed.

 

Before the poor man could explain his actions, his body started to twist and bend unnaturally, blood began to poor out of nearly every orifice: his eyes, nose, ears, and mouth. All of it bled as his body’s bones and muscles seemed to crack and move as if something was taking it over by force, marionetting his body with invisible strings and pulleys. His face cracked into a vicious smile as his eyes became withdrawn and haunted. Halibel quickly ran and recovered Julius while kicking Otto away. The possessed advisor barely flinched, rolling onto the ground and quickly standing up, his body bending upward first rather than his legs.

 

And then he started to sing.

 

Otto’s voice opened despite blood dripping out constantly, “H-happy b-birthday to you~.”

 

And then more people began to crawl from openings all around them, bursting from the ceiling and crawling like spiders down the walls. Each one recognizable by Subaru: Ricardo, Tivey, Hetaro, Mimi, Garfiel. Nearly every single one was bleeding just like Otto, and every single one was singing.

 

“H-happy birthday to you,” their voices in unison but all jangled and stuttering, as if their bodies were constantly fighting the urge, “Happy birthday to youuuu~! H-happ-y-y birthday dear Julius~!”

“…Happy birthday to-HELP ME! HELP!” Otto began to scream once again.

 

Subaru paled as the rest also screamed, all around them their voices echoed with despair and agony. Their eyes no longer glazed and now rapidly shifting with lucidity. Their hands quickly grasping at their fur and hair or trying to wipe away the endless leakage of blood.

 

“Stop it, stop it, it hurts!” “You monsters, let the kids go!” “I don’t want to be here anymore, I don’t want to be here anymore!” “Why are you doing this?!” “You bastards! I’ll kill ya all!”

 

And just as suddenly, they were silenced, every single one of them stood at attention, in-sync and bowed while speaking in-stereo, “Witch Cult Archbishop representing Gluttony, Louis Arneb.”

 

Subaru and the rest were horrified, Beatrice and Halibel applied first aid to Julius who was on the ground struggling while Ana-Louis started to laugh hysterically, “Congratulations~! Congratulations!”

The possessed people applauded as she spoke, “It’s a shame their bodies reject us so much. It isn’t perfect like this one’s. But it’s fine. They should survive long enough to recruit you all as well. So, what do you say, want to join the family?”

 

Subaru’s hands shook as he yelled, “You disgusting monster! I’ll kill you for this!”

Ana-Louis smiled, “Thought so. Oh well, it isn’t a choice though.”

 

And then all of their former companions lunged, every single possessed body ran on all-fours and sprinted like wild animals at the group. The possessed would have reached them if not for the sudden wind dome that suddenly surrounded the group, courtesy of Zarestia, blocking any of the bodies from getting in.

 

Subaru quickly sent a thank you to Zarestia through their connection before simultaneously asking for situation updates with Beatrice and Halibel. Thankfully, Julius was alive. The Dona nearly pierced his heart, but it seems they were aiming to simply put him out of commission, given it somehow hit none of his internal organs. Beatrice and his water spirit helped him heal. Either Julius was very lucky or Louis really was planning on inducting them all into this weird, twisted family of hers.

 

The only problem was, how was Louis doing this? Subaru looked through the dome of wind. It acted less like a solid construct and more like a constantly swirling foggy maelstrom that deflected any and all attacks, sending bodies that tried to get in hurtling in opposite directions. At the very least, Subaru could see through it and understand what was happening. For some reason, the three Archbishops were simply choosing to watch rather than join the fray. Either they were conserving their strength or devising a plan. It did imply one thing; however, these archbishops were different.

 

Greed, Sloth, and Lust were all strong, with incredibly broken abilities. However, they were not super creative, simply focusing on using their abilities in the most straightforward method they could concoct for maximum lethality. The Gluttonies, however? They were definitely smarter. Based off Priestella and Subaru’s more focused insight, he could tell they were the type to think things through rather than just brute force everything.

 

The problem was Subaru needed a plan and he needed a plan fast, Tia could keep the dome up for a long period of time, but the possessed bodies were hemorrhaging and hemorrhaging quickly. Subaru did not want to risk them dying from an extended fight.

 

He channeled Basilisk Ops and began using his connections to create high-speed discussions in seconds.

 

Any ideas on how she is possessing the bodies? Technique? No, there is none known besides Eridnas. Magic? Not possible, Beatrice would know. Authority? Possible. Gluttony seems to be much more variable in its effects. But why did they not use this before? Are there any drawbacks preventing them? Or maybe it’s because they never thought they could do this before. And why the bleeding? Are their bodies rejecting it? If so, then why is Anastasia not bleeding. Is she more compatible? Wait. No. Not all of them are bleeding. A quick scan showed that Ricardo, out of everyone, was the only one besides Anastasia who wasn’t bleeding. Which meant there was something about both of them that was allowing them to survive it easier. That was a clue.

 

And Subaru knew who to ask to clarify such a clue. He quickly ran over to Julius and saw that his wound was nearly patched up. Subaru kneeled down and caught Julius’s attention.

 

Subaru snapped his fingers in front of Julius’s face, “This is going to sound out of nowhere but I’m going to need your help with something. Do you know what Anastasia and Ricardo have in common?”

Julius looked incredulously at Subaru, pain still obviously radiating through his face, “Is this really the time?”

“Yes. I’m trying to figure out what’s allowing that asshole to possess everyone. I need your help with this so can you please answer the question?”

Julius’s face shifted to a more determined expression, “I-I see. Very well, Anastasia-sama and Ricardo are generally very different individuals. The only thing I can surmise as a surface level similarity, is that both are from Kararagi and neither have a Divine Protection.”

Subaru’s hand laid on his chin as he began to contemplate, “And given the Triplets are getting affected, it’s probably not the former. Then it’s the latter. But why would a DP matter and-wait a minute. Do you remember Ricardo?”

Julius stared for a second before his eyes widened, “I do…I do remember him!”

“What about the Triplets? And what about Garfiel or Otto?!”

“Yes, I can remember them all but…Otto never got his name taken.”

“He didn’t?” Subaru started to connect the dots.

 

The Divine Protection is the only significant commonality they can think of for the two people not suffering from the bleeding effect. Otto not losing his name means it isn’t an Authority’s effect. And the fact that all of them now have their names and, most likely, memories returned, definitely takes out any relation to the Gluttony Authority. Then why-

 

“It’s the Witch Factor, in fact,” Beatrice said out loud, her brow furrowing, “That’s the only reason Betty can think of. Witch Factors and Divine Protections cannot coexist in the same body. They reject each other.”

Subaru didn’t understand, “But how? How can they have so many Witch Factors on hand? It’s not like they can just make some out…of…nowhere. Petelguese.”

 

He remembered a certain conversation with a Greedy Witch.

 

Subaru’s mind began to shift to his encounter with the Sloth Archbishop and how his Witch Factor was spread between his fingers, Subaru began to mutter to himself, “That might not be exclusive to him. Maybe Gluttony can split itself. They’re splitting up the Witch Factor and using it to possess everyone. But that still doesn’t make sense, how is it that the Witch Factor itself can control people? Is it…alive?”

The implications of such a thought made Subaru’s gut wrench. Beatrice shook her head, “Betty does not think so. Witch Factors are more complicated than that, I suppose. Either way, it does not matter. We know what the source of the trouble is.”

“Now we just need to get rid of it,” Subaru nodded as he thought for a moment, “Hang on, what if I can take it out of them?”

Beatrice stopped working on Julius’s wound and stared up at Subaru, “How would you do that, I suppose?”

“Back when we were fighting Greed, I was able to take out that bastard’s weird heart thing from Emilia’s heart using Invisible Providence. Maybe…maybe I can do the same thing here, but with the Witch Factor. Do you know where the Witch Factor can be located?”

Beatrice struggled to think, “…Betty does not know. It is theorized it could be found in the Od or the soul. Or even both, in fact.”

“I’ll just have to trust my gut like before then,” Subaru then peered over to the trio of cultists, “I also might have an even stupider idea.”

 

Everyone looked at Subaru. All of them except Julius were sent information that sent them into a frenzy of reactions.

 

“That is a stupid idea, Su!” “Su-san, are you sure this is wise?” “Betty cannot allow that, in fact!”

 

Julius was thoroughly confused as his eyes began darting between them all, “Apologies. But I appear to have missed what the idea was.”

Subaru glanced down and scratched his neck in embarrassment, “Ah yeah. I’m starting to get used to communicating in my head at light speed. That’s my bad.”

Julius’s face could only be described as, “What?”

“Long story. I’ll tell you once this is all over. Anyway, I’m going to go save my wife now,” before Julius could respond, Subaru gave him an embarrassed look, “And…when you finally remember me. Come talk to me. And don’t apologize. You’ll probably be blaming yourself for a lot of things. Don’t. Okay, Julius?”

“I…Oh-kay?” Julius didn’t seem to know what to say, only nodding and responding hesitantly.

 

Subaru clapped him on the shoulder, making the poor guy wince, and walked towards the edge of the dome. With each step, multiple conversations rocketed between him and his companions, making his brain feel like it was bleeding. Halibel quickly slipped Subaru a kunai into his hand as he walked by, patting him on the back for support.

 

He waved his hand at the trio of Gluttonies. His nonchalance must have confused Louis as the assault on the wind bubble immediately stopped. With a quick word to Tia, a small pocket of air opened, allowing sound to get through. Subaru walked up and cupped his hand over the opening and yelled clearly.

 

“I have a proposition for you!”

Ana-Louis raised an eyebrow, “Well this is odd. Giving up already?”

Subaru waved his hand in the air, “Kind of.”

 

Subaru can already imagine Julius losing his mind behind him as Ana-Louis stared at him for a few seconds before laughing hysterically.

 

“Hahahaha! We knew it! You are necessary!” Ana-Louis squealed with glee, “So what exactly is your proposition?”

Subaru smirked, “Simple. You want me, right? Then let’s make a trade. You take me. You let the rest go.”

“…Why in the world would we take such a terrible deal?”

“Because you know my power.”

Ana-Louis flinched, “…”

Subaru spoke calmly, “You’ve seen Ana’s memories, so you have some idea of how it works. You’ll get me and it. I feel that’s a fair trade for letting everyone go.”

“…Why would you even offer such a deal? You gain nothing.”

“I do. I get to be by Ana’s side.”

 

Ana-Louis was stunned by his words. Because despite his plan, Subaru’s words were completely sincere. In the worst-case scenario, he won’t let Anastasia suffer through this alone, even if they both become puppets for some madwoman.

 

Lye, standing right beside her, shivered with delight as he couldn’t help but drool, “Ah~, he really has become more magnificent. Better than my hero, he has become his greatest self, tsu~.”

Roy rolled his eyes, venom tinging his every word, “Even an idiot like me can see this as a trap. Don’t choke on your meal, dear Sister.”

Lye chuckled, “Brother. It is through experience that we can achieve the finest forms of ecstasy. Let our sister find her path.”

Ana-Louis paid neither of her brother’s any mind, only focusing on Subaru as she smiled an eerie grin, “You and her really are a match made in Hell together.”

Subaru couldn’t help but agree, “If it means being by her side, anything is worth it.

“Hahaha! Fine, fine, we agree to such a deal,” Ana-Louis then took out the book she had just picked up from the floor, “However, two caveats: one, you must read this book with me. And two, drop that kunai you are hiding behind your back.”

Subaru outwardly flinched and waved the kunai in the air nonchalantly, “Can’t blame a guy for trying.”

“You have nothing to fear. My brothers and I would never harm an invited guest at our dinner table,” she then snapped her fingers as the shambling figures of their former camp members started to line up, one by one.

 

A bleeding corridor created from the barely standing bodies of their former comrades stretched between Subaru and the Gluttonies, who still stood high above on top of the dining table. Subaru couldn’t help but feel his temper flare at their mistreatment. Tia carved an opening through the wind orb to allow Subaru an exit towards his possible undoing. Before he could step forward, he heard Julius’s voice cry out.

 

“Subaru-sama!” Subaru cringed hearing that unexpected additive, praying to himself internally that Julius never calls him that again, “Do not read that book!”

Subaru turned his head and frowned, “What do you mean?”

Julius was still on the floor, struggling to lift his head as he no doubt was still exhausted from his injury, “Anastasia-sama appeared from there. I do not understand how she is connected to Reid’s book of memories, but it reeks of sinister intent! Please, do not do this! There must be another way!”

 

Subaru eyed Julius closely and saw how desperate he looked. Subaru struggled to understand exactly why he was acting like that but surmised something simple.

 

He must think Subaru is an idiot for going headfirst into a trap. Of course. It makes sense. Julius lost his memories of Subaru, so he obviously forgot one simple fact.

 

Subaru turned fully towards Julius, leaving his back exposed to his enemies and gave a cheeky smile. He pointed towards his chest with his thumb and spoke without hesitation.

 

“Sorry to disappoint ya Julius, but I’m a love-sick idiot!”

Julius stared, “…Huh?”

Subaru chuckled, “I’m not someone smart. Or strong. Or cool. Or brave. But I can’t help but follow my heart. Even if it means walking into Hell itself, I’ll always find a way forward. And you want to know why?”

“…” Julius raised an eyebrow.

“…Because I love Anastasia. And that’s all I need to take a step forward.”

 

Subaru turned back towards the Gluttonies, but he caught a glimpse of Julius’s expression. The poor man looked shocked beyond belief, though Subaru didn’t understand why the guy was on the verge of tears. Perhaps all the stress got to him. Maybe the guy will end up being more exasperated once Julius finally remembers Subaru.

 

Subaru waved his hands in the air, one already holding the kunai, and dropped the weapon to the ground before kicking it away. He kept them in the air as he walked forward slowly. His footsteps echoed through the room, the only other sound the dripping of blood.

 

First there were the brothers of the triplet pair.

 

Hetaro. Tivey. Ana told me a lot about you guys. Once this is over, I’ll spoil you both with gifts.

 

Then there was Mimi and Ricardo.

 

Hope you guys approve of me. Maybe I can convince Mimi with snacks, but Ricardo may be a bit tougher.

 

And finally, Otto and Garfiel.

 

…Despite everything, I hope you guys still want to be my friends. Even though, I can never return to the camp as I was.

 

Subaru looked up at the Gluttonies, peering down at him from above. Distant lamps in the ceiling shined behind their heads, nearly blinding his eyes. Cruel, disgusting, wretched. All qualifiers that described the three perfectly. Qualifiers that he would describe himself as well. He peered at the image of Anastasia who bore an uncharacteristic smile, bordering on malice. His hands gripped at his sides.

 

Ana. I’ll save you. And even if it takes everything in the world, I’ll convince you that you are enough. That I will never abandon you. Nor fall for another person. Nor return to somewhere I can no longer call home.

 

Ana-Louis held the book out, “So, are you ready to join us, Subaru?”

Subaru loosened his grip and smiled, lifting his hand towards her and gripping the book at its other end, “…Ready as I’ll ever be.”

 

Let’s go home Ana-pop.

 

Before she could let go, he pulled her towards him, using the book as a connector. Her face was filled with surprise and glee, reflecting the expressions of her two brothers who immediately dived at Subaru. It seems all three were expecting him to launch an attack, poised to incapacitate him at close range since the beginning. However, what they did not expect, was that Subaru wasn’t alone. As his hand on the book revealed three strands of gray fur.

 

The strands shined as they popped into existence three Halibel clones, each one taking on an Archbishop. One clone wrapped around Anastasia’s body, restraining her arms. Roy plunged his fist into another clone’s body, only for the fist to get stuck within its torso as the clone grabbed his body and tackled him to the side. One tried to kick Lye, only for the Archbishop to teleport behind the clone and quickly plunged his dagger towards Subaru’s neck.

 

It hit its mark. But not the intended mark. Another clone’s hand, as a fourth clone popped into existence in between Subaru and his blade. Lye seemed to grin ecstatically as he noticed the bits of fur found on Subaru’s back.

 

Throughout all of this commotion, Subaru took advantage of the seconds the clones bought him. The Gluttonies would not be staved off for much longer, the clones barely being a match for two. Subaru was thankful that Anastasia’s body was still physically weak, otherwise restraining her would be a much harder task.

 

Ana-Louis growled with irritation, “You will only delay the inevitable!”

Subaru ignored her as he reached deep within himself and prayed that his impromptu plan would work. He couldn’t rely on Return by Death for a quick redo, not knowing where the checkpoint would be or whether it even still existed in the first place. So, he had to rely on something he gave up on using ever since his imprisonment.

 

“INVISIBLE PROVIDENCE!” Subaru yelled furiously as he felt the usual nausea and corruption, though it felt oddly…different this time.

 

The black hand reached forth from his navel and quickly flew straight to Anastasia’s chest and entered it without any hinderance. Instinctually, Subaru felt the hand travel to where Anastasia’s Od lied and grabbed at…something. Her soul? The Witch Factor? Subaru did not know but his instincts yelled that he grabbed the correct object.

 

And then his body began to feel like it was on fire.

 

Unbeknownst to him, the Sloth Witch Factor had indeed grabbed the split Gluttony Witch Factor. But not alone. The Hand of Sloth had become intwined with the thread connecting Subaru’s Od and Soul to Anastasia’s Od and soul. The thread made from the Greed Authority during that fateful day. So, when the Hand of Sloth had made contact with Gluttony, a spiritual reaction occurred between all three Witch Factors.

 

Gluttony tried to devour Sloth. Sloth tried to crush Gluttony. And Greed.

 

Greed tried to claim ownership of both.

 

Connecting its threads to both Witch Factors. The three eldritch pieces of illogical sin chased each other, each vying for control and dominance, to extend its Authority over the other two.

 

Fighting. Gnashing. Devouring.

 

Until finally, the three’s eternal struggle created something new.

 

Within that microsecond between contact of the three Witch Factors, Roy and Lye dealt with their clones and were rushing to save their sister.

 

Within that microsecond, Halibel’s clone knocked out Anastasia’s body and pushed it towards Subaru.

 

Within that microsecond, Halibel pulled the metal thread he attached to Subaru’s back and launched both of his wards to him, the two stars soaring through the air.

 

Within that microsecond, the rest of the Louis-possessed humans rushed at the stars with animalistic fervor.

 

Within that microsecond, Subaru’s scream was snuffed out as he was overwhelmed with sensations never felt by him before, darkness taking hold of him, and still clutching onto Anastasia for dear life.

 

And within that microsecond, both stars were plunged into a new world from within.

 

Trapped within a Purgatory of their own making.

 

-------------------------

“…Ugh,” Anastasia moaned as she tried to open her eyes.

 

Only to see absolutely nothing.

 

She blinked her eyes.

 

…Where the hell am I?

 

Everywhere she looked, there was pitch black darkness. Why was she here? She remembered talking to someone. But everything was so bright before. Why was it the opposite no-

 

Her prayers were answered as everything nearby became a blinding light, causing her to cover her eyes and scream in agony.

 

Until she realized her eyes were not burning. She blinked them open.

 

The room was no longer dark like before as Anastasia now could see her own hands. And the fact that she was lying on the ground. Well, some weird ceramic floor that felt smooth and clean in the weirdest ways. She looked around and was perplexed by her surroundings. The walls looked odd, white and stonelike. She seemed to be in some kind of hallway, with doors dotting the walls in even spaces. The place was eerily dark but softly lit by strange contraptions stuck in the ceiling. She was about to question what that weird wind-like sound was when she heard something even more peculiar.

 

Someone crying. Specifically, the light whimper of a baby. Coming from the door right next to her, opened ajar with fragments of light piercing through the dark hallway. She felt drawn to it. She hesitated for a second before picking herself off the ground and slowly sauntering toward the source of the sound.

 

As she got closer, tiptoeing lightly, she began to hear voices. And just as she touched the door and started to push it forward, those voices became even clearer, the crying much louder.

 

“-crying too? It’s been a while since I’ve seen you cry, Kenichi~,” a soft and kind voice said.

A deep but whimpering voice responded, “I-I can’t help it! Just…look at him! He’s so…so…”

“There, there, it’s okay. I know. He’s beautiful.”

“…Are you comforting me or our baby?”

“…Both?”

The deep voice chuckled at that as the crying became louder, the man quickly said, “Don’t cry…or is crying good? S-should I keep crying with him?!”

The soft voice giggled, “The nurse said it’s normal. It means he’s alive. And he’s happy to see us.”

“…Hope he doesn’t take after me.”

“Kenichi. He’ll be fine. Stop worrying so much and hold him.”
“I-I don’t-“

“Hold. Him.”

“…Okay,” the deep voice said.

 

Anastasia was enthralled as she pushed the door further, allowing her to see the two voices in all their glory. They sounded so…loving. Tender. Fearful. Sad. Scared.

 

…Hopeful.

 

Her eyes fixed on both individuals: one on a bed and the other sitting right beside her in a chair. The one in the chair had black hair that slicked back but was noticeably disheveled with bits clumping and spiking in odd places, reminiscent of the patchwork found on his face and chin. The man’s eyes looked stern but tired, large bags drooped under them. The guy’s fashion was a disaster, a mix of different apparel ranging from a jersey to sweatpants to mismatched socks, as if it was all haphazardly put on in a hurry. The guy was carefully holding a bundle in his arms, his eyes solely focused on whatever was held within. The woman on the bed looked haggard, her auburn hair in a ponytail but all frazzled and twisted. Her attire was simple, what looked to be some kind of greenish-blue robe. The woman’s eyes were distinct, sharp and quite terrifying but holding a unique sense of soulful kindness. They too were tired but focused solely on the bundle the man was holding.

 

Anastasia blinked again as she quickly panicked, hoping that she hadn’t just disturbed the couple. Only to realize that they hadn’t even noticed her entering, still only having eyes for the one within that cloth.

 

The crying was beginning to quiet as Kenichi, who Anastasia surmised was the man, spoke softly, “…I can’t believe he’s here. I-I remembered being prepared for this. Having so much I wanted to say! But now…now…”

The woman put her hand on his arm and spoke just as softly, “…Now you can’t find the words, right?”
“…Yeah. Yeah, I can’t.”

The woman smiled, “…There are two words we should say though, given it’s his first day with us.”

Kenichi looked at her confused, “Uh…can you remind me which ones, Naoko?”

Kenichi looked sheepish as Naoko playfully slapped his arm, “This isn’t a quiz! But here, let me give you a hint.”

 

She then motioned for him to lean his head forward as she whispered in her ear. Anastasia slowly walked towards them, her presence causing no disturbance. It was as if she wasn’t even here. She should leave. This wasn’t for her. For anyone but the couple. But something was drawing her to them. As she got closer and closer, she finally was able to see what Kenichi was holding within his arms.

 

A baby. An ugly baby. Pink and with eyes that were absolutely frightening like his mother’s. Black hair like his father’s. A face that only a mother could love despite being so adorable.

 

And Anastasia couldn’t help but shudder when she saw him, tears threatening to spring out as she saw the couple each hold him together, supporting one another, leaning their heads over him. Both Kenichi and Naoko spoke almost in unison as Anastasia finally realized where she was.

 

As they spoke words that were said with love that could not ever be measured.

 

“Welcome home, Subaru.”

Chapter 40: A New ______ and A New Earth

Summary:

Anastasia begins to see the life of Natsuki Subaru...

Chapter Text

“Here come’s the airplane~!” Naoko said in a sing-along-voice, making a brrrr sound with her lips as she slowly waved a spoon towards Subaru’s mouth.

 

The little baby giggled as he opened his mouth and ate the spoonful of mushy apples with cheer and excitement befitting of a three-month-old baby. Some bits of apple were spilled all over his cheeks as he ate happily.

 

Apples. Not appas. Apples. How strange. Just one of many differences that Anastasia was slowly getting used to. This world, this place. She sat right next to baby Subaru’s stool as she leaned on the table lazily, watching as Natsuki Naoko took care of her son daily, happily humming to herself a random JPOP song that she had heard on the radio.

 

Anastasia watched as Naoko took a napkin and wiped her son clean before moving to clean up some dishes, leaving the baby to play happily in his seat, ignorant of Anastasia wistfully trying to pinch his cheeks. She frowned as her hand phased through his skin, completely missing any solid contact. She then eyed some of the leftover apples smudging his seat and curiously dipped her finger into the mashed fruit, lifting her now stained finger in the air, and eyeing it suspiciously.

 

The fruit was on her finger. It was there, physically. Not some mirage or illusion. She narrowed her eyes and then popped her finger into her mouth.

 

Sweet, fruity, and a bit of tang. It tasted like a normal appa.

 

Anastasia was confused, her right hand naturally floated back to baby Subaru as she once again tried pinching his cute baby cheeks. Only to fail miserably once again, much to her frustrations.

 

…I don’t understand how the rules here work.

 

She can touch certain things: food, objects, and people. But only after a certain time has passed. And not all objects. No obvious consistency in what she is allowed to touch and sense other than that it can only be done after Subaru experiences it himself. And even then, not everything is interactable. She can interact with her surroundings but never people. She can’t feel Subaru’s clothes or touch his parents, despite both being technically in close proximity with him at all times. The rules of this place were odd and confusing.

 

Not only that, but she could also barely understand what this place is. Obviously, she was currently witnessing the life of her lover, starting from birth. But the why and how are absent. Not only that, but her memory also felt untrustworthy. She remembered escaping from Subaru’s disappointment and the debilitating reality of his situation. She remembered running away and hiding within Rem’s room. She remembered… a bird? But after that, it became fuzzy. Anastasia knew the bird made a deal with her, and she for some reason accepted, and then she ended up somewhere completely different. But it doesn’t make sense how deals with birds lead you into the memories of the people you care about the most.

 

…Anastasia realized how absolutely insane her life has become in the last few months.

 

Or six months? Anastasia had no idea how long she has been here relative to the outside world. She knew, intrinsically, that three months have passed since the happy couple left with their newborn baby boy from the hospital. She experienced everyday since. And yet, it doesn’t feel like she has. She remembers every day with clarity that rivals how her mind currently feels, clear of all the emotional tar that she was feeling previously, and yet it doesn’t feel like time had passed at all. Three months here felt like only a few minutes. And yet, it has been three months. How strange and jarring.

 

Anastasia sighed as she leaned back into her chair, her movements causing light scuffing and screech, caused by the scraping of the floor from the legs of the wooden chair. Her eyes peered over to Subaru, ignorant to everything she does.  Just happily, innocently, waving his feet in the air, his eyes constantly drifting towards every new sight and sound as if it was the most amazing thing in the world. She couldn’t help but smile at him. How could she not?

 

He wasn’t like her Subaru yet. Filled with trauma and grief untold. Never tortured. Never hated. Never suffered. Not yet. He was still happy.

 

She rubbed her eyes before the tears could spring out. No. No more. She had cried for days on end before she came here. And look what it brought her. Tears solved nothing. Nor did acting like some emotionally debilitated teenager help you convince your fiancé that you are mentally stable enough to be with him. Anastasia’s cheeks burned red as a mixture of guilt and embarrassment rushed up to her neck and pooled into her face. She rubbed her temples, biting back however many scathing comments she had for her own recent lack of decorum. After the initial shock of seeing her beloved as a literal baby wore off, she ended up spending most of the time here until now, hopelessly chastising herself for her behavior and how she almost ruined their relationship and lives by acting so out of norm.

 

Anastasia blinked as she stared upward. No. This was not exactly out of norm. In some ways, this was just who she was. In most cases, she was absolutely a monster of logic and efficiency. But when it came to the people she loved and the mere idea that she could lose them…

 

Anastasia peered at baby Subaru and stretched her hand towards him once more, still feeling that bitter annoyance stretching through her chest as she couldn’t reach his cute face, having to make do with watching the little toddler coo at his mother as she walked by. As she continued to phase her hand in and out Subaru’s face, her mind began to wander, a habit she started to pick up recently given how monotonous the Natsuki family’s life was.

 

…I need to find a way out of here. I need to get back to Subaru. I need to go save my family. I need to apologize to Subaru. Apologize to everyone. Try to…talk. Figure out a way for us to move forward.

 

A part of her had accepted that Subaru’s life would never be fully shared with her. That ultimately, he would be burdened by a nightmare that she could never fully comprehend, nor could she ever save him from. He will forever bear his wounds alone while Anastasia could only hope to soothe his lingering scars. And Anastasia will have to settle for that. Settle with the idea that she was no better than anyone else.

 

She hated it.

 

She pretended to run her fingers through Subaru’s small amount of hair, whispering softly, “I guess I’m just like the others. I’m…not someone special to you. Just someone who will watch you get hurt and suffer while I reap the benefits. Like everyone else in your fucked up life.”

Subaru giggled in happiness, making Anastasia smile, her head cocked to the side as she stared longingly, her finger ineffectually trying to tap his nose, “…I wonder if our children will look as cute as you were. I know you wanted a daughter first, as cute as me. But I wouldn’t mind having a son who was as adorable as you, Subaru.”

 

Her eyes drifted to the side, hearing the clatter of porcelain dishes hitting metal, and the pitter patter of water washing the stains off each plate. She couldn’t help but admire watching Naoko work. The woman worked nearly every second, every day, to make sure the house was clean and tidy, all while making sure her baby was properly cared for. The woman barely got any sleep and yet she tirelessly made sure her husband and son were given as much as affection and joy as she could, always having a smile plastered on her, admittedly, scary face. Anastasia couldn’t help but gape in awe, her hand clutching her chest, right above her heart. Her other hand was still trying to reach for Subaru’s face and failing.

 

…I never realized how hard motherhood was. Or I guess, will be. I always assumed it would be just like raising the Triplets but honestly, I never really had experience with babies. I wonder if I’ll be a good mother.

Her jaws tightened at the thought, her hand gripping her kimono fiercely. At the very least…I’ll be better than her.

 

She will be. She’ll make sure of it. Anastasia’s eyes drifted back to Subaru, her face crinkling into a natural smile, seeing the boy knead his hands over the back of Anastasia’s hand, enamored by her fingers. Anastasia giggled at the touch.

 

…The touch?

 

Anastasia blinked. Her eyes focused on baby Subaru making contact with her hand. Physical contact. After months of no success at it.

 

Her mind scrambled just as she heard the unlatching of locks at the entrance, coupled with a loud and booming voice, “Naoko! Subaru! I’m hooooooome~!”

 

Before Anastasia could even process what just happened, Naoko snatched Subaru out of the chair and started walking briskly towards the door without hesitation. Anastasia scrambled out of her chair, slipping on the smooth wooden floor, as she quickly ran after Naoko. She breathed heavily as she slid to a stop at where the Natsuki family congregated. Anastasia quickly tried to hold Subaru’s face in her hands, only for her body to once again slip through reality, as she phased through him and kissed the floor with her face, groaning in pain. She quietly got up as the young couple ignored her existence, speaking to each other openly.

 

“How was work?” Naoko asked while trying to keep Subaru from eating her hair.

“No success!” Kenichi said proudly, giving a thumbs up while his smile wavered slightly, he sighed when he realized his wife’s deadpan expression, “…They told me I won’t need to come back tomorrow. So, I’ll have to look for a new job.”

Naoko frowned, “But they promised you would shift to full-time?”

Kenichi grimaced, “Unfortunately, they changed their mind.”

“I should give them a piece of my mi-“

Kenichi interrupted his wife’s angry protest, his cheerful tone reinforcing his words, “It’s okay! I’ve already looked around and found another job. The fact that they didn’t want me back was a blessing, if you think about it, saves me having to quit because of their terrible work conditions.”

“Kenichi.”

The man scratched the back of his neck and kept trying to smile, “Don’t you worry, just focus on taking care of Subaru and we’ll-“

“Kenichi!” Naoko raised her tone, shutting him up.

“…”

“…You don’t have to pretend to be strong about this.”

“Naoko,” Kenichi’s voice broke slightly as he tried to keep his smile up, “I’m fine.”
“You are not,” she raised her hand to hold his face, “Don’t lie to me.”

“…I’m sorry. I just. I don’t want to break my promise with your parents,” Kenichi said as he finally dropped his smile, his mood becoming downcast.

“If you are worried about promises, then focus on the most important one we made.”

Kenichi raised an eyebrow, “To always have a bottle of mayo on hand at all times?”

Naoko smiled and rolled her eyes, “The second most important promise. The one you made on our wedding day.”

Kenichi’s eyes widened, he bit his lip but spoke reverently, “…I, Natsuki Kenichi, promise to always make you happy. That in sickness or great health, whether we are poor or healthy, old or young, I’ll always be faithful to you.”

Anastasia’s body flinched as Naoko’s smile became even brighter, “No matter the challenge. No matter the struggle. No matter the situation. We’ll press forth and fight it together.”

Anastasia’s mouth automatically matched Kenichi’s as he finished the full vow, “All my burdens. All my sins. All my flaws. I’ll lay bare to you. And if you are willing, I will carry all you lay bare. And you the same for me. I promise, until death do us part. Always yours, Kenichi.”

The two looked at each other with rapt affection, Naoko caressing Kenichi’s cheek with boundless love and attention, “We are in this together. Every step of the way. Don’t ever act like this is your struggle. This is ours. You and I. I won’t ever let you decide to carry everything alone.”

Anastasia struggled to bite back the tears as she saw Kenichi wrap his arms around his wife, resting his head on her shoulder, “How could I forget? I guess…I just wanted you to rely on me a bit more.”

Naoko chuckled, “Oh, you idiot. We all have our strengths and weaknesses.”

“…Like when you almost got tricked into a pyramid scheme?”

Naoko pinched his ear, “That was one time!”

Kenichi laughed through the pain, “More like three.”

Naoko pouted, “…They were very convincing.”

Kenichi cooed at her response, “Still, it’s because of those assholes that we met.”

Naoko blushed as she pinched his mouth shut, “No swearing! Honestly, what if Subaru’s first word is something outrageous?”

Kenichi laughed even harder, “You worry too much Naoko, he’s only three months old. It’s not like he’ll learn how to-“

“Ahoole!” Subaru popped up between the two, sandwiched in their embrace and smiled a non-toothy grin. He smacked his hands on both Naoko and Kenichi’s faces.

“…Kenichi,” Naoko’s voice turned bloodthirsty.

“Hey! Anyone up for ice cream?!” Kenichi yelped, sweating profusely.

“…We are talking about this afterwards.”

“Of course! But first ice cream! Sweet, non-violent ice cream!” Kenichi said as he quickly turned and marched out the door, Naoko sighing with both exasperation and fondness at his antics. She kissed Subaru’s cheek as he babbled nonsensically at her before tracing her husband’s footsteps.

 

Anastasia slowly followed them until they reached the street. The young couple and their baby walking together, holding each other close, as they walked to the nearest ice cream parlor. Anastasia stared at them, her heart squeezing with warmth and envy. Her hand stretched out towards their figures as they walked down the streets, shadows growing under the evening sun. For a brief second, Anastasia could imagine their features as another family. One with a mixture of violet and black hair.

 

A possible future.

 

Her hand faltered as it returned back to her side, cradled by the other.

 

…Even if it might be impossible, I still want to try.

 

She needs to return to Subaru’s side. She wants to hold his hand again. She wants to find a way forward.

 

She took a deep breath, before stepping forward, quickly catching up to them.

 

On that day, Anastasia made a silent promise to herself.

 

And on that day, she discovered the taste of vanilla ice cream.

 

---------------------

Anastasia raised an eyebrow as Subaru carefully wiggled his way out of his father’s grasp and tip toed away, the sounds of Kenichi’s snores and the static of the TV muddying his soft footsteps and the creak of the wooden floorboards. She was amused as Subaru tried his best to be as quiet as possible. Though not quiet enough that when he heard his favorite Super Sentai show’s theme music, he automatically posed out of habit, pointing his finger upward. The poor boy flinched as he quickly swerved his head towards where his father lay on the couch, only relaxing as he heard his quiet snores. Anastasia could barely hold in her laughter at the boy’s precocious actions.

 

She followed him as he made his way to the front door, pulled out a step stool and pressed on the door handle. Within moments, Subaru snuck out the house and was running free down the streets of the neighborhood, Anastasia walking briskly right beside him. The sun rising in the background as the cold morning air brushed against his skin. His mother was currently visiting family out of town while his father was at home, making sure Subaru wasn’t causing a ruckus like he was currently doing right now.

 

Natsuki Subaru is now four years old.

 

Anastasia’s eyes peered down the familiar streets as she kept pace with Subaru, counting the streetlights and parked cars out of habit. In the last few years that she has been watching Subaru grow, she has learned a lot about Japan as well as his world as a whole. A migraine started to form at the ideas that bounced in her head. She still can’t believe that Subaru doesn’t just come from beyond the Great Waterfall. He comes from beyond her plane of existence.

 

For starters, apparently Subaru’s world is round and circular, not flat like hers. It was jarring to realize that all of those globes she saw represented his planet. Planet was also a word that she had to get used to, along with several other terminology. The fact that stars in this world were not bundles of mana but were actually hot pockets of gas was hard to wrap her head around. As well as the fact that magic just didn’t exist here, leading to her to have a slight existential crisis at the fact that Subaru was surviving without mana, despite having a Gate or Od. Or the fact that he possibly didn’t have either but somehow gained one when he moved to Lugunica.

 

Anastasia was having multiple crises almost every day from the constant influx of new information during the last few years, and she honestly was enjoying every single one. Anastasia knew a lot about Subaru’s home from all of his stories. Yet, stories could only do so much. It was a completely different experience seeing everything in person. She ran her hand over the hood of a car, enjoying the glossy feeling of her fingernails scraping the metal. Subaru’s descriptions of cars were accurate, but it was incredibly exhilarating to see them in action. She remembers staring with her jaw dropped as the dragon-less carriage ran on its own, powered by gasoline, which she originally believed to be some type of oil.

 

Oil. Japan didn’t need that much or at least didn’t use it as a substitute for magical stones like back home. Electricity and technology, something akin to metias, were plentiful and everywhere. The buzzing of the streetlights overhead cemented such a fact. Her eyes peered upward at the empty sky. The stars are noticeably gone, yet Anastasia does not feel uncomfortable by their absence. She long since realized that they were just hard to see, overshadowed by the countless man-made lights that dotted Japan’s streets. Televisions, radios, electrical heating and cooling. Her mind whirred with possibilities, wanting to replicate them back home in some capacity. Oddly enough, Anastasia felt some pride in Subaru’s homeland, their technology making up for their lacking physiology, constantly pushing forward out of a sense of progress and survival.

 

I wonder what it would have been like if I was born here?

 

Her eyes caught sight of a passing store’s sign.

 

ケンスケのラーメン

 

Kensuke’s Ramen. Anastasia did not waste any time while watching Subaru’s childhood, becoming fluent in Japanese by the end of the first year. She already learned a lot from Subaru’s brief teachings, her proficiency increasing so fast that Subaru was always complaining about her being a genius. However, with three years of added practice, she not only could read and write Japanese katakana, hiragana, and kanji. She also had a basic grasp of English. It was illuminating to realize how many different languages existed in Subaru’s world, being flabbergasted the first time she heard a tourist try to ask Naoko a question in French. She was equally flabbergasted, doing nearly a triple take, when she heard someone speak in a Kararagi accent. Apparently, it was called a Kansai dialect here, making her head spin at the implications.

 

Anastasia’s musings drifted as she saw Subaru’s feet grind to a halt as he found something incredibly peculiar. A bunch of people standing outside as a voice sprung from a nearby radio, they were all lined up down the street, listening to its words. Subaru, however, chose to cut through the static.

 

“Hello!” He waved slowly in the air, making Anastasia laugh at how adorable he looked, “My name is Natsuki Subaru! Nice to meet ya!”

 

Subaru then struck a dumb pose, reminiscent of his Super Sentai shows, causing all of the people, who on closer inspection were fairly elderly, to smile and snicker at his behavior.
