Subaru beamed proudly as one of the older men waved him closer, the little boy skipping happily towards the man. The old man leaned down and whispered, “Nice to meet you too, young man.”

Subaru smiled and then his eyes widened, smacking his hands over his mouth as he whispered, “Do we have to be quiet? Did I do something wrong?”

The old man chuckled, “No, no. You are just in time actually.”

“Just in time for what?”

“For morning calisthenics. Here, watch,” the old man said as he pointed towards the others, a twinkle in his eye.

Subaru was confused for only a brief moment as he heard the radio cry out, “Tokyo Calisthenics Number 2! Bounce on your feet to loosen up your body!”

 

Just as the voice announced the maneuver, everyone around him started to bounce on their feet. Anastasia nearly died of cuteness overload as she saw Subaru replicate their movements, albeit awkwardly and with way more energy than the old people could muster. After a minute, Anastasia couldn’t help but follow along, copying the movements that Subaru did, movements that were familiar to her from another time.

 

So, this is where you learned how to do those exercises, Subaru.

 

Not winded as she usually would be, Anastasia was able to keep up with the others until finally they all raised their hands in the air and yelled, “Victory!”

 

Anastasia coughed in her hand in embarrassment. Despite how fun it was to do with her fiancée, doing it out in public was a bit much. Thankfully, no one could notice her presence.

 

Young Subaru, however, couldn’t contain his exuberance, “That was so fun! Can we do that again?”

The old man from before smiled and patted him on the head, “We sure can. But tomorrow, okay? You got strong legs but us old folks, we got creaky old knees. Can’t use them too much, otherwise they’ll break.”

Young Subaru blanched, patting his own knees, “I like my knees. I hope they don’t get creaky like Mom and Dad’s.”

“Your parents also have weak knees?”

“They complain about their knees all the time! And their bed! It’s so creaky! Creaky weaky! Especially in the morning,” Subaru’s blunt words made Anastasia and old man choke.

“I-I see. Well, speaking of your parents. Let’s take you back to them. Can you tell me where your home is?”

Subaru put his finger to his chin, thinking really hard, “…”

“…”

“…” He then plops his fist on his hand, “I have no idea!”

 

The old man nearly doubles over as Anastasia tries to swat Subaru’s head, missing entirely.

 

Subaru laughs as he scratches his head, “Sorry! I forgot!”

The old man couldn’t help but join him in laughing, rustling Subaru’s hair, “In that case, let’s go look around. I’m sure if we find some landmarks, you’ll be able to remember where you live.”

“Mmm, okay!” Subaru said with a thumbs up, before taking the old man’s hand, he then waved to the others as they walked back down the street he came from, “Bye bye! Thank you!”

The other elderly waved back, all bright and cheerful at the youthful display. The old man guided the boy and spoke softly, “You express gratitude so easily, child.”

“Yep! Dad says you have to always say please and thank you! Especially after you have so much fun,” Subaru swung their connected hands widely, marching without a care in the world.

“Your father is a wise man.”

“He is! Dad is super cool! He’s good at everything! One time he was able to fix my toys with just a screwdriver! And another time he- “Subaru rambled proudly.

Anastasia walked beside the two, her own thoughts starting to assess Subaru’s words, So you say. But honestly, Kenichi doesn’t seem all that cool to me.

 

Anastasia respected Kenichi. He was Subaru’s father and someone who dearly loved and cared for her fiancé. That was more than enough for Anastasia to consider him someone important. But that did not mean she had as high of opinion of him as Subaru did. Subaru’s stories painted Kenichi as a man who was not only good looking, but incredibly well-loved and talented. A high-quality man, akin to Julius. Someone to be admired and adored. Yet, Anastasia’s own perspective painted him in a different light.

 

Anastasia agreed that Kenichi was good looking. But talented? Well-loved? Top tier? Kenichi was anything but. Kenichi was a hard worker, that she was sure of. But he had no skills that he was an expert for. It’s why, despite however many jobs he has held in the past few years, none stuck. He’d be contracted for a few months before having to move on. He’d get along with everyone around him. Make countless friends. Be praised for his diligence. Often recommended by everyone. And yet, he was never the best. And because of that, he was never kept for longer than needed. Always someone else was better. If there was one thing Kenichi could be applauded for, it was his unwavering optimism despite however many failures he came across.

 

Anastasia observed Subaru’s eyes sparkled when talking about his father and found herself amused by a sudden epiphany.

 

…You’re more like your dad than you think, Subaru.

 

“Subaru! Where are you?!” The two suddenly stopped walking as they heard a loud booming voice from around the corner.

The source of said voice, with an unkempt beard and wearing pajamas and mismatched sandals, nearly tripped as he rounded the corner, his eyes locked onto Subaru before barreling towards him at Mach speed. Subaru waved his hand, “Papa! I just did calis-uh. Cali. Cala. Calithonic. Cali-“

Kenichi scooped Subaru up into a hug as the boy kept trying to stutter his way to completing his sentence. Kenichi hugged him tightly, making him squeak, as Kenichi cried out, “I thought I lost you! How many times have I told you not to leave the house without us?!”

Subaru patted his dad’s face, before counting on his fingers, “Uh…eight times!”

Subaru’s proud expression did not mirror his father’s exasperation, “…What am I going to do with you?”

The old man chuckled in the background, “You have quite a spirited son there.”

Kenichi nearly flipped when he realized they weren’t alone, too focused on his son to notice beforehand, “A-ah! Sorry! Were you-did you. I…thank you for keeping my son safe. My name is Natsuki Kenichi.”

Kenichi stretched out his hand towards the old man while keeping Subaru close with his other. The old man eyed his hand for a second before clasping it in his own, “Kensuke Taro. A pleasure to meet ya.”

“A pleasure. I’m sorry for my boy causing a disturbance, no doubt. It won’t happen again.”

Taro raised an eyebrow at Kenichi, “It’s quite alright. You a working man?”

Kenichi tried to hide his wince, scratching his neck awkwardly, “Uh…I’m currently between jobs.”

“I see. Your son was talking all about you before you arrived. Says you’re quite the handyman.”

“I dabble,” Kenichi said without trying to seem too arrogant.

“Hm. Well it just so happens, I’m currently looking for someone to fix our stoves and heaters. Got a couple of stores that are experiencing some electrical issues. Think you can stop by and take a look at them?”

Kenichi stared at the man for a second before sputtering, “I-I would be happy to. I just have to ask…why me?”

Taro stared at Kenichi for a few seconds before walking up to him. He then patted Subaru’s head before speaking fondly, “No reason. Just looking for someone to fill the position. You just so happen to be available. Or am I wrong?”

Kenichi quickly shook his head, “N-no! I mean, yes! I mean…I am completely available. I would be happy to help you with your business’s problems.”

Taro laughed and gave a final tap to Subaru’s nose and walked away, “Good to hear. Store opens tomorrow at 7 am. Look for Kensuke’s Ramen. After that, I’ll guide you to the others. I’ll see you then. Don’t be late.”

Kenichi blinked several times before bowing deeply, “Thank you! I won’t ever forget this favor!”

Subaru did not understand but quickly dropped down to the ground and copied his dad, “Thank you Mr. Kensuke! I’ll see you tomorrow at calisthonas!”

Taro ignored Subaru’s mispronunciation, not turning his head and choosing to just wave his hand in the air.

 

Kenichi stood upright once more, smiling as if he was on top of the world, he then took Subaru’s hand and spoke softly, “What do you want to eat for breakfast, Subaru? I’ll make you anything you want.”

“Really?!” Subaru preened at the notion, “Can I have pancakes with mayonnaise?!”

Kenichi chuckled, “Of course! I’ll make as many pancakes as you want!”

 

The two began to walk home, both ecstatic for different reasons as Anastasia watched, walking slightly behind them. She couldn’t help but share their good mood, happy to see that Subaru’s childhood was happy and safe. Happy to learn so much about him, his home, and everything in between.

 

Maybe one day, I’ll get to meet your parents too. I hope they don’t mind giving their blessing. If they don’t, I’ll just prove to them I can make you the happiest in the world.

 

Anastasia skipped as the sun rose above her. Despite her desire to find an exit, she couldn’t help but enjoy herself. She could only hope that wherever Subaru was right now, he wasn’t worried sick about her.

 

------------------------------

Deep within the bowels of Banan’s underbelly, in the slums of their most wretched hives, a lone cry echoed throughout the desolate streets.

 

As the stars hanged overhead, illuminating the garbage and scraps that lay about the cobblestone roads, one man stood motionless, staring at one particular area.

 

Natsuki Subaru had woken up without any knowledge of what happened to him or where he exactly was. The only thing he remembered was trying to reach for his beloved’s soul before everything went dark. But that did not matter. What mattered was what was before him: A baby.

 

A lone baby, with mauve hair peaking out from her blanket, crying. Crying as no one cared for her. Crying for anyone to care for her.

 

Alone, amidst the trash and dirt of Banan’s slums, the one who would become Anastasia Hoshin solemnly cried beneath the black star’s gaze.

Chapter 41: ______ is Under Our Feet and Over Our Heads

Summary:

Subaru goes down memory road, and witnesses the first moments of who would become Anastasia Hoshin...

Chapter Text

It has been approximately two hours since Subaru arrived in this hellhole.

 

Actually, hellhole is not an apt description. This street was more akin to a waste dump, where the only objects and landmarks you could see were trash piled high as far as the eye could see. From corner to corner, the only objects plaguing this part of Banan were bundles of trash, discarded food scraps, and randoms bits of gunk that Subaru really did not want to dwell on. What made this area particularly hellish was the mere fact that a baby’s cries could be heard echoing throughout this lonely street and not a single person has come to investigate. Oh, there were people passing by. But no one cared enough to check. Some brief glances. Some slightly pitiful expressions. But nothing more, and usually everything less.

 

Subaru’s hands were bleeding from how tightly they gripped themselves. Fucking bastards. It’s a child! You can’t just-

“Uaugh…” Subaru stopped and immediately knelt down, instinctively, trying his best to reach out and softly caress the baby’s cheek. Only for his hand to phase through her body. He nearly pounded the trash beneath her in frustration.

 

All Subaru could do was ineffectually coo at the child, hoping that somehow he could communicate any of his presence to her, “It’s okay. I’m here. You’re going to be okay. I promise. I…no. Someone. Will come. Someone will come to save you.”

“Augh…UAHHHH!!!” Unfortunately, the baby’s crying continued, much to Subaru’s dismay.

 

Subaru glared as he whipped his head around, trying to find anyone. Onto his feet in a matter of moments, he sprinted to the edges of the street, screaming at a passersby, “Are you fucking deaf?! There’s a baby crying in a shitload of garbage!”

He gasped for breath as the man continued walking without a care. Frustratingly, Subaru reached out with his hand, trying to grasp the man’s collar, “You bastard, I swear to God! I-what?”

His hand phased through the person, just as the person disappeared out of reality. Not some kind of shimmer or phasing out. The person literally was there and then in the next second, absent. Subaru held his hand in front of him, folding his fingers back and forth.

 

There was no marking or blood from his self-inflicted wounds earlier. It was as if the wounds never happened. He then saw the next person pass by and, right as they reached the wall of the alleyway, they too disappeared. Subaru then peered out from the entrance of the alley, to look at the other roads making up the intersection and was stunned by what he saw.

 

Nothing. Absolutely nothing. Just a blank canvas that stretched on and on forever. He turned his head to the other side and saw the same thing. It was strange. From where the alley spilled out, Subaru could see the perpendicular dirt road parallel to the wall of an old Edo style building, some flowers and plants growing within the cracks. But they suddenly disappeared right as they reached an invisible line, unfolding into pure white nothingness. Not only that, people appeared out of nowhere, crossing the road until disappearing as if they never even existed.

 

…Where the fuck am I?

 

Subaru could not ruminate on his surroundings anymore as he heard the rustle of garbage from behind him. Quickly spinning around, his eyes widened as he saw a dirty, rag wearing woman with long brown hair looking at the mauve-haired baby before slowly reaching down and picking her up. Subaru’s muscles relaxed at the sight before quickly becoming stiff.

 

Wait, no. What if they try to hurt her?

 

His feet moved faster than his thoughts as he quickly moved to reach the woman. However, she was much quicker, seemingly having an objective as she dashed out of the alleyway and ran down the maze of alleys, not even looking behind or turning her head to path find. Baby wrapped tightly within her arms. Subaru was way behind her, not fast enough to catch up but was at least able to keep pace. After a myriad of turns and streets, she finally stopped at a decrepit house in the bowels of what seemed to be Banan’s slums, slamming her fist on the door as fast as possible. Just as Subaru slid towards her, phasing through her body, and tumbling onto the ground, the door opened, revealing a tall rat demi-human. Subaru’s head slowly lifted in pain to see the rat demi-human blink before looking down at the raggy woman, his eyes narrowing.

 

“Danzi. What the fuck are you holdin’ right now?” The rat man asked.

Danzi looked down. Then up. Then down again. And then up. Down. Up, “A baby!”

“…Yes. Just,” the rat man pinched his between his snout and his eyes, “Tell me why you have a baby in the first place?”

Danzi looked down once more, the little baby babbled beneath her head, stretching out its little arms towards her face, “I found it!”

“…Where?” The rat man looked incredibly concerned.

“In the trash.”

“Oh, in the trash, alright,” for a second, he relaxed and waved his hand in the air, “Then put it back.”

Danzi’s face turned downcast, “Put it back? But we just got her!”

The rat man’s eyes narrowed, his face scrunching as if disgusted, “Danzi.”

“Turrel?”

“We can’t take care of a baby. It will ruin us,” Turrel closed the door as if that was the end of the discussion.

Danzi put her foot in the door, “Are ya sure? Are ya really really sure we can’t?”

Turrel didn’t budge waving his hand through the opening, “Look around. That child is more likely ta die in our hands than without. She won’t live long enough for…any use.”

He tried to close the door, but she was adamant, stubbornly keeping her foot within the doorway, “B-but-“

“No buts. I ain’t takin’ responsibility for some child when we can barely survive on our own. It won’t be worth the trouble. You’ll get attached.”

“I can take care of her!”

Turrel poked his head out and squinted, “Her? Ya checked? And for that matter, ya can barely take care of yerself! What makes ya think ya can take care of some baby?”

“I can take care of her! Please! It ain’t much trouble!”

After some more back and forth, Turrel finally agreed, “Fine! Ya can keep it! Don’t even try to name it though. And don’t expect any help from me. If it dies, it’s your problem.”

Danzi cheered, nearly dropping the baby. Subaru jumped forward to catch her but was thankfully not needed as Danzi held onto the baby’s dirty blanket by a thread, “…So, what do babies eat though?”

Subaru and Turrel both facepalmed.

 

----------------------

Despite Turrel’s reservations, Danzi wasn’t that terrible of a mother. Sure, she often didn’t quite understand the baby’s needs initially. Trying to feed the baby alcohol was a prominent example. But she learned! Especially after Turrel begrudging taught her some of the basics: milk, mashed food, changing diapers, and helping the baby pass gas.

 

“The brat is fuckin’ loud,” was usually his excuse, followed up by genuinely helpful advice. Subaru glanced over at the empty bottles of milk that always showed up full on the kitchen table in the morning.  Somehow, two years passed by, and the little baby has been growing semi healthily. As best as the child could within the impoverished environment she was currently growing up in.

 

“Buah!” The little baby exclaimed, waving her spoon in the air while she sat at a small table that had no chairs and was basically a former stool with its legs shortened.

 

Subaru sat next to her and ineffectually kept trying to pinch the baby’s cheeks or to try twirling his finger through her soft mauve hair. He tried not to fixate on the baby’s meridian blue eyes nor the fact that her cute face was so familiar to him.

 

…Who am I kidding? It’s obvious.

 

This was Anastasia. His Anastasia. For some reason, the culmination of his encounter with Gluttony sent him back in time as some kind of ghost or something. A ghost that was witnessing Anastasia’s life from beginning to whenever. Subaru frowned as his fingers kept phasing through her cute chubby cheeks.

 

The world hates me. I have the most adorable baby in the world, right in front of me. And I can’t even pinch her soft cheeks. When this is over, I am tackling Ana and squeezing her face for hours.

 

Subaru’s frown deepened. He had mostly made peace with the fact that he was on some kind of obligated amusement park ride through Anastasia’s memories, but it still irritated him that the love of his life was being possessed by some disgusting monster while he was stuck here. He didn’t even know what exactly happened. Was this an effect of Gluttony? Or was this some weird reaction when he tried to grab the Witch Factor? Is he technically inside Anastasia’s mind? How does this exactly work? Does his presence change the past at all? Can he even change anything or is he stuck just watching?  What exactly will he see? Because he’s basically seen every moment these last two years and he really doesn’t want to see every time Anastasia has to take a shit-

 

“Ehehe~,” Anastasia babbled and giggled as she smacked the end of her spoon on the surface of the table, happy as can be despite being dirty and covered in a rag. Her hair was starting to lengthen and was getting to her neck, not as long as it was present day.

 

…Would our kid look like you? Act like you? Talk like you? Smart as you? Kind as you?

 

Subaru thought for a moment before smiling, Definitely would be as adorable as you.

 

But I really hope not. Because if she’s as precious as you are right now, I might die.

 

Subaru blew his hair out of his eye, Or maybe that would be a worthwhile death. Death by cuteness. Though technically…it is a pretty fitting name for that one time I got eaten alive by rabbits. Urgh.

 

As Subaru tried to categorize every horrible death he faced by some kind of catchphrase, Danzi came back with a large plate in her hands, “Hello, my little sprout! Are you ready for breakfast?!”

“Bau-ba!” Little Anastasia cried, her little hands waving rapidly while she kicked her feet under the table.

By the time Subaru recalled his accidental death by Reinhard, calling it Death by Emotional Damage, Danzi slammed the large platter of food onto the table. Well, really it was just one clump of food. It looked like a giant green onion pancake except instead of green onions, it was tons of different foods mashed together into fried dough. Peas, bananas, what looked like bacon, cheese, pears, apples, some weird fish thing, and potatoes. Subaru was 80% sure this was all from the garbage.

 

Danzi clapped her hands, “Dig in! I found a nice spread from that one restaurant ya loved so much! They had a huge buffet due ta the rain festival and threw out a ton of food!”

 

Subaru blinked. He was joking. Is that where she was getting all of the food from this entire time?

 

Anastasia clearly did not care as she quickly dug into the giant pancake of questionable origin and had the happiest expression on her face, nearly radiating pure sunshine. Subaru couldn’t help but smile at that.

 

Guess your weird taste in food never changed. Though I’m not someone who can talk. I’m really craving mayo right now.

 

Subaru then squinted at the food as Anastasia kept gorging herself. Subaru reached out, briefly hesitating, before he snagged a piece and plopped it into his mouth. He chewed slowly.

 

I mean…it’s actually pretty good?

 

Salty, sweet, crunchy, soft, savory. Literally the whole spectrum of flavor and taste. Could be better though. At the very least, Anastasia was enjoying it.

 

Subaru took another piece as Danzi patted Anastasia on the head, the little girl preening at the touch, making Subaru a little jealous. Danzi smiled happily, “I can’t wait until you grow big and strong little sprout.”

 

Subaru swallowed as something bitter started to creep up his throat.

 

Ana never told me about these people. She did tell me about that woman, brief as it was. But not these two who took care of her. That and the fact that Anastasia hasn’t been named yet…

 

Subaru shuddered; he had a very bad feeling for what was to come.

----------------------

“The wolgarm jumps over the fence!” Anastasia shouted with glee while sitting in Danzi’s lap, reading a worn out book in her hands.

“There you go little sprout! You’re learning so quickly!” Danzi clapped.

 

Anastasia giggled while Subaru sat nearby in pure awe. Learning quickly was an understatement. Anastasia was only around two years old, and she learned how to read I-script, Ro-script, and Ha-script in less than a few weeks. And that wasn’t even counting how fast she was able to do simple math and addition. Nor the fact that she could memorize directions, figure out small devices, and knows how to open everything in the house with enough effort. She was a natural born genius as far as Subaru was concerned.

 

Subaru could hear Turrel exit his room, his door creaking as it usually does, and heading straight for the nearby kitchen for a snack. Danzi waved at him, which Anastasia copied after a few seconds, “Turrel! You should hear little sprout, she can-“

“I don’t give a shit,” Turrel said as he rummaged through the cabinets, “And what did I tell ya about teaching it that stuff.”

 

Subaru flipped Turrel off from the corner where he sat.

 

“But…but…if she doesn’t know how to read. She won’t be worth much-“

“Not our problem. Stop it. Ya’ll only make it harder for everyone,” Turrel said as he grabbed a bowl of dried meat.

 

He then trudged back to his room and slammed the door shut.

 

Danzi looked pensive for a few moments before her focus was taken once again by Anastasia clapping her hands in the air, always so cheerful despite everything around her. Danzi smiled down at her and patted her head, “Thanks little sprout. You’re such a good girl. I’m proud of you.”

“Ehehe!” Anastasia giggled.

“…One day. You’ll grow up into a mighty fine tree.”

----------------------

“Ya little bastard! Stop drawing on the walls!”

“Ehehehe!” Anastasia giggled as she ran through the hallways without a care in the world.

 

Subaru’s heart felt warm. It was the greatest sound in the world.

 

“You little fuckin’-OH SHIT!” Turrel slipped and slammed his head into the wall, making a new face sized hole for rats to poke their head through.

Turrel’s moans of pure agony were Subaru’s second greatest sound.

----------------------

Turrel entered the door, exhausted after spending the whole night working. Subaru had no idea what his job was but it didn’t take much brain power to at least make a good guess. The dark clothing he wore. How he constantly came back with trinkets or heaps of gold coins. He was either a thief or a ninja.

 

Subaru’s head turned as he saw part of the roof fall to the floor, making Turrel wince as he decidedly ignored whatever problem just popped up. It seemed he subscribed to the idea of ‘if I ignore it, it will go away.’

 

Turrel walked through the house and continued his subscription by blatantly ignoring Anastasia who was up bright and early and staring happily at Turrel. Danzi had left earlier on some kind of errand, leaving Anastasia to be by herself. She stared intensely at him from her little table. He kept ignoring her and walked silently to the nearby cabinet, reaching up and extracting a beer from deep within before uncapping it by using one of the hinges as leverage. He then turned around and was nearly startled by Anastasia being right behind him, holding up a piece of paper to his face.

 

Subaru tiptoed around and looked over Turrel’s shoulder as the rat man narrowed his eyes. It was a child’s drawing of three stick figures. A stick figure with brown hair and a smiley face. A triangle headed tall stick figure with a frowny face and whiskers. And finally, a small stick figure with purple hair and a very big smile that nearly ran off her face. Contrasting the simple art style was the almost perfectly legible script writing next to each figure, besides the little one which was noticeably absent.

 

Subaru couldn’t help but coo at the drawing while Turrel frowned just as badly as his caricature. Subaru glared at Turrel, “You better compliment her or I swear to God.”

Turrel rolled his eyes and pushed Anastasia aside, making his way to his room. Subaru flipped him off again, yelling, “You fucker!”

But the rat man only made it halfway to his room before he stumbled, looking backward to see what exactly stopped his movement. It was Anastasia. Who was clinging to his leg and pouting. He grimaced, “What do you want, brat?”

Anastasia flicked out the paper from behind her and waved it furiously at him. He raised an eyebrow, prompting her to point her finger at the two names. And then point at herself.

“…You want me to name you?” Turrel asked.

Anastasia nodded vigorously, “Yeah!”

“…”

“…Yeah?” Anastasia cocked her head at his silence.

“No,” Turrel viscerally recoiled as he saw Anastasia’s eyes well up, “Don’t you dare!”

Anastasia flinched, tears starting to form, “B-but-“

“We’re not family! I’m not your fucking dad or whatever you think Danzi and I are! So, stop acting like we are!” Turrel snarled trying to shake off Anastasia, “Now let go!”

“No!” Anastasia stubbornly clung onto him.

“I said let go!” Unfortunately, Anastasia was still just a child, and Turrel was easily able to pry her off, flinging her across the floor.

“You bastard, she’s just a kid!” Subaru yelled, trying to punch Turrel, only for the hits to miss him completely, “Of course she’ll get attached to you! Just…what is wrong with you?!”

Anastasia sobbed on the floor, looking up at Turrel without any words, “…”

A flash of guilt struck his expression, before Turrel fiercely swore, “I knew Danzi shouldn’t have taken you in. We can’t…Oddamnit!”

Turrel didn’t even finish his thought, never daring to look at Anastasia once more as he ran into the room, slamming the door.

Anastasia sat there sobbing and nursing her bruises. Subaru knelt down next to her, not knowing what to do and his heart breaking at the fact that he was incapable of even doing anything, “It’s okay…he’s just an idiot. You didn’t do anything wrong.”

Without hearing anything, Anastasia only sobbed harder, “I’m sorry…”

After a few minutes of crying, she wobbled as she stood on her little legs. She sniffled and rubbed her eyes as she stumbled back to her room, constantly glancing at Turrel’s door.  She slowly entered her room, practically a closet, and crept on top of her makeshift bed made of boxes and pillows. She closed in on herself, huddling under a dirty rag and continued to sob, not saying another word.

 

Never noticing Subaru sitting right next to her, desperately whispering assurances to her that would never reach her.

----------------------

Anastasia woke up to hear shouting outside her room. She rubbed her eyes, slightly pink from all the crying. She sniffled and blew her nose on her pillow. Anastasia tiptoed her way around the clothes and small bits of trash that lay about the room. Just as she reached the door, the shouting stopped and she heard a loud thud just outside. Subaru’s heart sank as he desperately crawled towards her.

 

“Ana, no! Stop, don’t look!” His cries went unheard as Anastasia peaked out the door before suddenly screaming in horror and falling onto her bottom. The door slowly creaked open, revealing Turrel gasping for breath, his back turned towards her.

 

And a bloody Danzi laying beneath him.

 

Subaru tried to hold his hands over Anastasia’s eyes, but she quickly phased through them, getting onto her feet and walking out the door. Turrel did not react, continuing to take deep breaths, his fist caked in blood. Anastasia walked slowly towards Turrel as Subaru pleaded for Anastasia to run away.

 

Despite her instincts, she got closer and closer to him until-

“Get back!” Turrel finally noticed her and pulled out a knife, turning to face the child while making her freeze in place just a few feet away from him, “You…you need ta leave.”

Anastasia was confused, “What?”

She took a step towards him, making him flinch and point the knife at her, “I said leave! Before they…no. Just go!”

Despite his threatening aura, Anastasia still crept closer. Turrel glared, “What the fuck is wrong with you?! Are you insane?! Can’t you see…I killed her. Your mother or whatever the fuck you thought of Danzi, you…take another step and I’ll kill you too!”

 

Subaru panicked, his heart wrenching from what he was seeing. He clutched his chest. He felt disgust. Hatred. Concern. Incredible worry. Curiosity.

 

Wait…curiosity?

 

Why are you lying?

 

Subaru blinked, that was Anastasia’s voice. He could tell immediately. He crept around to get a better view of her.

 

Why do you keep lying?! The voice cried out. But Anastasia’s lips did not move, her cries echoed through Subaru’s head. It reminded him of how Eridna sounded when she would try connecting to him.

 

Subaru didn’t understand and neither did Turrel it seems, it didn’t seem like he could hear the voice. The rat man was shaking, “I’m not jokin’! One more step and you’ll die!”

 

Anastasia didn’t listen, still walking forward but not saying a word externally but her mind was racing.

 

Face is red. Red and won’t look at me. Red and won’t look means he lies. He always lies! He looked at me when he said ‘leave.’ Why? I don’t know. I’m scared. Danzi is hurt. Turrel looks scared. I can’t leave. Turrel. Turrel needs me. I need Turrel. I need Danzi! I can’t. I won’t. I don’t want to go. I don’t…

 

Anastasia took one more step forward and reached her hand out.

 

Turrel clicked his tongue and briefly hesitated before swinging his knife. Subaru, out of pure instinct, reached for Anastasia’s collar trying to pull her out of the way. Desperate despite knowing it would not work-

 

But it did. He somehow pulled her back, the knife narrowly missing her hand and landing right next to her foot. Subaru blinked in surprise, his heart jumping out of his chest as he blurted out, “How did I do that?”

 

Subaru looked down at his hands as Anastasia whipped her head behind, scanning her eyes around but not looking directly at Subaru.

 

“You get it now?!” Turrel screamed, waving his knife like a maniac, “Leave!”

Anastasia whipped her head back towards Turrel, “B-but-“

“Leave! Or I’ll fucking kill you!” As Turrel stepped forward, Anastasia blanched and scrambled to her feet, running towards the exit as fast as possible. She burst out the door and ran through the streets as the morning sun rose in the background. Running and running. On the bare dirt road. Running past all the people who drifted without a purpose. Running without even looking back.

 

Subaru was right behind her, and he could hear Turrel’s voice get quieter and quieter, “Don’t ever come back! You fucking…monster…”

 

Anastasia sniffed, confused and shocked. She didn’t know what to say or do. All she could do was run. She couldn’t stop running. 

She ran.

 

And ran.

 

And ran.

 

Not knowing any alternative.

----------------------

“Are you ready Subaru?” His mother asked him.

Subaru appeared anxious but he still tried to smile, giving a thumbs up, “I’m okay!”

Naoko giggled, mimicking Anastasia’s, “Alright…then let’s go before we’re late!”

 

Natsuki Subaru was six years old. And today was his first day of class.

Chapter 42: Earth Has No Sorrow That ______ Cannot Heal

Summary:

Anastasia begins delving deeper into Subaru's childhood...

Chapter Text

The years drifted by like flashes. Colorful flashes, painted with happiness. If Anastasia could describe Subaru’s younger years, it would be purely blissful.

 

Anastasia sat on the open fields of a grassy hill as she watched a young boy, pure of heart and uncontaminated by the cruelty of the world, run happily with friends in tow, playing a simple game of tag. The boy was surrounded by many friends, people who all admired and loved him. Cherished. Cared for him. He laughed happily as Anastasia was only meters away, twirling a piece of grass between her fingers.

 

He looks so happy.

 

Anastasia frowned.

 

When was the last time I saw him so happy?

 

The only moment that could come close was… when he proposed. When she nearly died. And even then, his happiness was more a mix of pure relief and joy. Rather than the pure innocent joviality she was witnessing now.

 

It was interesting. She never expected Subaru’s childhood to be like this. Compared to hers, his was largely uneventful. Surrounded by so many novelties and raised with love and care. It was something Anastasia could only dream of as a child. And speaking of dreams, this world and its technology was pure fantasy. Cars, planes, rockets. Radio, television, internet. Manga, anime, and merchandise. So many concepts that Subaru explained to her with the best of his abilities. And now Anastasia truly understood what he was talking about. Her mind was whirling with possibilities, every year came with new ideas, and with it, she couldn’t help but plan for a wonderous future. Where she will be implementing all of these concepts in some capacity, to expand her company, to create a lasting memory on her own world. The name Hoshin will not be synonymous with solely Alex, it will be surpassed by the one named Anastasia.

 

…And yet, despite being in literal Heaven, where her previous self of just a year ago would be salivating at all the possible innovation, she couldn’t help but feel unsatisfied. Has she become greedier?

 

Anastasia’s frown became deeper as she glanced at the blade of grass and let go, sending it flying away. But something caught her eye, she peered at her hand. Flexing it back and forth, rotating it slowly, she peered at a particular finger, her index.

 

Didn’t I have a scar there-

 

“AH!” Anastasia was thrown out of her thoughts by a sudden yell, her attention drawn to a child groveling on the ground.

 

As the group of children ran across the park without a care in the world, one brown haired child tripped and fell behind the rest. Tears began to well up as the little girl silently held her breath, wincing from her bruised knees and scraped skin. No one in the group had noticed her lag, her separation. Her growing isolation brought further tears, streaming down her plump cheeks. Until a shadow grew beneath her, followed by a hand.

 

The little girl looked up and blinked, as a boy with sharp eyes and a warm smile kneeled down and offered her a hand. She hesitated for just a moment, before taking it, wiping her tears, a smile returning just as quickly as she was pulled up. She flinched as her legs limped, struggling to walk. The boy noticed, frowning at her sudden disability. She seemed to be on the cusp of crying yet again…

 

Until the boy gently squatted and positioned his back for her to latch onto. The girl seemed flummoxed, wavering whether to accept his offer. Though such hesitance was quickly dashed by the boy offering another smile and a thumbs up.

 

“Hahahah!” The girl and Subaru laughed as he ran with her as fast as he could catching up to the rest of the group, the little girl struggling to hold on but feeling so elated by the rush of movement and freedom. The group now noticed their absence and reappearance, jumping for joy and racing with Subaru, some getting on each other’s backs to simulate their leader. The status quo returned, no, was reinvigorated, all because of one single child.

 

Anastasia gazed thoughtfully at the group as her mind wandered to a conversation she and Subaru had one blissful night together.

 

“I was popular as a kid.”

“You trying to brag or something?”

“I was! Well, kind of. Everyone liked me because I was super-fast and confident and smart. You know how kids are. They follow whoever does the best.”

“…Yeah. I guess they do.”

“Like my Dad. Everyone loved him because he was so cool and dependable. He was charisma incarnate. I wanted to be like him. And for a time, I was. Everyone liked me, just like they loved my dad.”

“…”

“…But I guess I wasn’t that cool after all.”

“Subaru-“

“It’s okay. I’m just saying this because…I wouldn’t mind our kid being lame. Or not that smart. Or not that strong. Or not a social butterfly. No matter what, no matter who they are, I would love them just the same. So don’t…worry.”

“…I don’t want them to be like me.”

“Ana. If they could be anything like you, I’d love them. And even if they aren’t, I’d still love them. Because at the end of the day…they’ll be our kid. No matter what.”

 

Anastasia watched as Subaru tried his best to carry the girl, despite his notable exhaustion, and his eyes constantly watched everyone, roaming especially towards the back. Like a guardian overlooking his herd, he never ignored a single person.

 

Anastasia curled up and wrapped her arms around her legs, her head tucked in but still gazing upon Subaru, as always.

 

…I hope our children are as kind as you.

----------------------------

And yet happiness was not forever. The colors began to mold. Their brightness dulled, slowly. Except a flicker of one particular hue.

 

Green.

 

Because as Subaru grew older, as his perceptiveness increased, as his eyes constantly kept watch of the group. He began to notice changes.

 

Some of the kids were getting faster. Stronger. Smarter. One of the kids became the fastest at running. Another of the children became the greatest at playing hide and seek. One of the children was amazing at science. Another math. Another spelling. English. Japanese. And more. Children were improving. Children were growing up. Everyone was changing.

 

…Except him. Subaru’s eyes kept watch of it all. As he slowly drifted and lagged behind everyone else. And before he knew it, he was the one watching from the back.

 

The colors were melting. Slowly replaced with the tint of green.

 

Green with envy.

----------------------------

“Are you doing alright, Subaru?”


“Yep, yep! Totally fine Teach!”

 

“…Are you sure?”

 

“I mean,” Subaru’s eyes flickered to the side, “Why? Do I look like I’m not?”

 

The teacher sighed, “It’s not that you look unhealthily. I just wanted to check in, is all. Your grades are starting to fall behind the rest. This is not like you. So, I was wondering if there was something going on at home.”

 

Subaru hummed, hands in his pockets, “Nah. Mom and Dad are same as always.”

 

“I see. Well, do be careful with your studies then. If you’re wanting to go to a good high school, it wouldn’t be good to slack off.”

 

Subaru saluted at the teacher while Anastasia sat on a stool nearby, trying her best not to flip off the 30-year-old man, as she muttered, “Subaru. He’s calling you lazy.”

 

Subaru could not hear her words as he simply said, “Thanks for worrying about me though.”

 

“Yes. Well, your dismissed,” the teacher waved him off as Subaru waved back in an exaggerated fashion.

 

He then marched out of the office, Anastasia in toe, before closing the door behind him. Subaru’s eyes glanced around quickly, finally relaxing as no one was nearby. He leaned his back onto the door, tired, his body slowly drifting towards the ground, his hand rubbing his face and forehead, before being run through his hair, “I’ve been trying my best though…”

 

Anastasia gazed at him with concern, trying to brush his hair away from his now closed eyes, and failing. She frowned. She had been experimenting for years on how to replicate that one moment. Where she was able to touch Subaru. She wasn’t hallucinating. She felt his presence that day and he acknowledged her. But no matter what, she couldn’t replicate it. What were the conditions that could allow her to intervene in his memories?

 

“Subaru-kun?” Subaru and Anastasia startled in unison as a voice sprung next to Subaru, making the poor boy fall onto the floor, “Subaru-kun?!”

 

“Argh…” Subaru moaned in pain as the source of the voice hovered above him. It was a girl with brown hair wrapped in a ponytail, eyeing him with concern.

 

“Are you okay? I’m sorry, did I scare you?” She offered him a hand.

 

 

Subaru gazed at the hand longingly before he hesitated. He quickly bounced to his feet, leaving her hanging, as he posed dramatically, “I’m completely fine! Was just thinking about something dumb is all!”

 

The girl blinked before chuckling, standing straight once more, “Is that so? How have you been? It’s been so long since we last talked.”

 

“Fine. Super fine, actually!” Subaru rubbed his neck before giving her a thumbs up, “You’re looking spiffy though!”

 

The girl cocked her head, “Spiffy?”

 

“Yeah, spiffy! You know, that slang Americans use?”

 

“I…see?”

 

“Yeah…”

 

“…”

 

“…” Anastasia was too busy cringing in the corner, deciding whether it would be better to slam her head into the wall or throw herself out the window.

 

“So…why were you at the Teacher’s office?” The girl finally cut the silence off.

 

Subaru grimaced, “Oh well, you know how it is.”

 

“…Uh-“

 

Subaru quickly added, “I-I was just getting lectured about my future opportunities! You know, because, well. We’ll be graduating soon. So gotta prep for high school as much as possible. And well, I’m not the best at studying so it’s always good to, you know, start. And study better. And stuff.”

 

The girl stared for a moment before stifling a laugh, and brushing her hair behind her ear, “Yes, I know that feeling. I have to also start going to cram school soon. It’s going to be a tough year ahead of us.”

 

“…Yeah, so. That’s that, I guess,” Subaru said, rubbing his neck nervously, “Anyways, I’m going to-“

 

“Subaru-kun.”

 

“Yes!” He squeaked.

 

“If you aren’t too busy, would you…like to study with me on the weekends?”

 

“I-well-“

 

“Not alone!” She tacked on quickly, blushing slightly, “With some others. I have a study group, and I think it would be really fun if you joined us. If you want.”

 

“I…” Subaru didn’t know what to say.

 

“Subaru. You should accept her invitation,” Anastasia urged. Despite the slight jealously creeping up her spine, she knew he would benefit from this. A way to reconnect with his old friends. A way for him to relax and socialize after so long.

 

“I-I…” Subaru struggled, his eyes dashing all around before he finally, “I’ll definitely let you know if I’m free!”

 

He did another dramatic pose as the girl awkwardly said, “Uh…okay?”

 

Subaru gave a thumbs up, “Cool! See you later!”

 

He then ran away without another word as the girl reached out and tried to get his attention, “W-wait, I didn’t-“

 

But he was gone.

 

“…I don’t have your number,” the girl muttered as the world began to fade around her.

 

Anastasia stared as the girl’s features became muddled before disappearing into whiteness. The world suddenly shifted to where Subaru was now, racing down the hallways. Anastasia did not have to move at all as the scene kept shifting, of Subaru running down the halls of the empty middle school, the afternoon sun his only friend, peering through the windows. Running and jumping downstairs. Until he finally burst out the main doors, tripped on his own feet, and fell to his knees, gasping for breath.

 

The scene finally shifted, placing Anastasia right next to Subaru. Her eyes widened as she tried to kneel down to him, instinctually reaching out, only to startle backwards as Subaru pounded the ground with frustration, tears dripping onto the pavement.

 

“Why did I…?!” Subaru nearly screamed before getting onto his feet and running away again.

 

Running.

 

And running.

 

Always running away.

 

By the time he got home, his tears dried up, and the mask of Kenichi’s son returned once more.

 

Smiling as if nothing was wrong. A smile that reminded her of those days when he would lie about the pain. As he drifted off into sleep next to her.

------------------------

That festering green continued to grow. As Subaru’s middle school years slowly came to an end, he got more desperate.

 

“Wow, he’s just like Kenichi-kun~!”

 

He would take more outlandish actions. Act like a clown. Push himself to be daring. Make himself the center of attention as much as possible.

 

“Keep it up! Make your parents proud!”

 

He would try to study. But fail. And opt to make himself the class clown to make himself feel better.

 

“Oho~. You’re just like your father!”

 

Try to act charismatic. Confident. Try to make everyone laugh at his jokes. Take dares on a whim. Hot sauce challenge? Done. Jump out the second floor window? He’ll easily do it. Confess to a girl that was out of his league? He’ll do it for 2000 yen. And it kept escalating. And escalating. Until finally:

 

“…Dude. Stop.”

 

No one wanted to be around him.

 

“No, it’s just…look. I’m only inviting a few people. Don’t want it to make a big deal, you know?”

 

Everyone saw him as passing entertainment. Someone to laugh at for a little bit before moving on.

 

“It’s okay. Take it slow. Everyone has their own pace.”

 

No one expected anything from him anymore. No one wanted anything to do with him anymore. No one cared about who he was anymore. He wasn’t Kenichi’s son. He was…Subaru. Just Subaru.

 

Nobody special.

 

…He didn’t know if that was a blessing or a curse.

 

“It’s me! Natsuki Subaru!”

“…I’m sorry, have we met before?”

 

Even the people who cared for him once, no longer remembered him. Too many missed opportunities. Too many times, he ghosted them out of anxiety. Too many times, he gave them excuses.

 

Until eventually the invites stopped. The moments were gone.

 

And all Subaru had…was nothing.

 

And what did he do when he started high school? A fresh start from his previous blunders?

 

No. Nothing changed. It was the same old thing. He emulated his father. And the cycle began again.

 

Laughter. Awkwardness. Isolation.

 

No friends. No one who really knew him. Anyone who did, still called him Kenichi’s son. Only cared because of that association. He hated it.

 

He wanted to be Subaru. Kenichi’s talented son.

 

Not Subaru, Kenichi’s son. Not Subaru, the nobody.

 

Natsuki Subaru. Someone people cherished.

 

But he couldn’t, and so one day, he stopped going to school. One day became two. Two became three.

 

The days stretched on as Subaru became a recluse.

 

“Subaru…is everything alright?” His parents one day asked, concern etched over their faces.

 

Subaru had missed one full week. His eyes widened as Anastasia gripped her chair tightly, “W-what do you mean?”

 

“…We’re just concerned is all. You know you can talk to us about anything, right?” Naoko said soothingly.

“Anything at all,” Kenichi added.

 

“…I’m okay. Just, tired is all. Trust me. Everything will be back to normal soon!” Subaru said with a thumbs up, his tired eyes trying their best to seem exuberant.

 

Anastasia smacked her foot into Subaru’s chair leg, “You idiot! Tell them the truth!”

 

“Are you sure?” Naoko said. Both of his parents didn’t seem to believe him.

 

“Yep! But I’ll definitely let you know if something is wrong!” Subaru lied. She knows he’s lying. She can tell.

 

Anastasia did not stop, trying to smack his chair or do something to get his attention, to no avail, “Liar! You…stop looking like that!”

 

Stop looking like those men and women who wasted their lives, lumbering and complaining while doing nothing about it. Those vagabonds from the slums of Banan who would rather seek pity, seek someone to save them or give them a reason to live, instead of changing their lives for the better. The vagrants who gave up instead of fighting tooth and nail for a chance to really live.

 

“Okay…we’ll always be here for you, Subaru,” Kenichi said, his constant smile seeming less sunny than usual.

 

“That’s not what he wants!” Anastasia yelled, pointing her finger at them, “Look at him! He’s…he doesn’t want this. He wants someone to smack him. Punish him. Call him all the terrible things he always thinks about himself.”

 

“…I know, thank you,” Subaru said with a smile that made Anastasia want to vomit.

 

She pounded the table furiously, “You…you…”

 

…Why won’t you seek help? Why do you not want to talk about your pain? Is this why you don’t talk about everything you’ve been through? Is it because you don’t think we’ll understand you?! Do you not want to burden your parents so much that you’d rather waste your life doing nothing?!

 

Despite Anastasia’s words, and despite how much his parents yearned to help him, Natsuki Subaru chose to close himself off from the rest of the world.

---------------------------

And now, he had been absent from school for nearly 3 months.

 

Secluding himself in his room. His parents never confronting him, only trying to get him to open him up every so often. Trying not to intrude on his personal space despite how desperately he seemed to want them to. Anastasia knew. She knew Subaru so well at this point. How he acted. How he hid. How he hated.

 

How he hated himself so much.

 

Hated himself but did nothing. Nothing but playing video games in the dark safety of his room, submitting himself to stupid fantasies of other worlds and adventures beyond his wildest dreams. And all Anastasia could do was watch, sitting on his bed.

 

“…Tsk, how cliché,” he muttered to himself as he played some RPG, “Look at this asshole. How in the world do all the girls just like him without even trying? It’s not realistic. I can expect it if the guy is some ikeman or handsome guy. But no. He’s so…bland.”

 

Anastasia couldn’t help but nod along. These stories were pretty trash in her opinion. And for some reason they made all the women scantily clad for some bizarre reason.

 

“Women don’t just fall for you like that! You can’t just be nice or kind and suddenly they are all over you…” he grumbled.

 

Anastasia was about to agree in her head, until she paused.

 

…Maybe there is some truth to that. It’s not like she fell just because Subaru was nice to her, but his kindness was partially responsible for it. She didn’t really fall immediately either but like-

 

She shook her head in exasperation. I really don’t want to agree with some trashy Isekai harem trash.

 

She chuckled to herself. Wait until that idiot hears her say all this slang she learned. He won’t be able to hang such information over her head anymore.

 

Subaru continued to talk to no one, “Such wish fulfillment bullshit. It’s not like you can just die and everything gets better automatically. You gotta actually try and improve yourself.”

 

Anastasia grinded her teeth, You hypocritical idiot! If you’re going to criticize some terrible game, use that energy for yourself-

 

“…Maybe I should just die.”

 

Her thoughts stopped. Her heart skipped a beat.

 

…What?

 

Subaru chuckled to himself, “Maybe I’ll get sent to another world if I do.”

 

“You…you!” Anastasia’s heart burned, she clutched her chest with her right hand and stood up, slowly walking towards him.

 

“…I won’t have to deal with any of this. None of this anymore-ARGH!” Subaru’s self-deprecation was interrupted by a sudden slap to his face, as his eyes nearly bulged out of their sockets at the sight of Anastasia standing over him, fury pouring out of her, “W-wait, who are-“

“Take it back.”

“Wha-“

“TAKE IT BACK YOU ASSHOLE!” Anastasia grabbed him by the collar, shaking him, “You wanna act like an idiot? Fine! You wanna be some self-pitying recluse? You’re an even bigger idiot than I thought but fine! But you…if you ever even joke about that again.”

“I-I don’t-“ Subaru looked scared out of his mind but Anastasia was too angry to care.

“I’ll die with you,” Anastasia stared into his soul as every word slipped out of her lips, “Do you hear me? You die and you’re going to end up killing us both.”

“What?!”

“Not so fun hearing it from someone else huh? Imagine what your parents would feel. They love you, you absolute moron. They care about you. Have you ever thought about how they would feel if you died? That their precious son died before they did!”

Subaru’s expression morphed into guilt. And then suddenly into a reflection of Anastasia’s pure rage, “Then what am I supposed to do then?!”

Subaru glared as he continued to speak, “I’m not great! I’m not someone they can be proud of! I’m barely a human at this point! What worth do I have other than being their son?!”

“That’s all you need!”

“…What-“

“You fucking dipshit,” Anastasia felt a migraine form, her potty mouth tended to emerge whenever Subaru did something dumb.

 

Which was all the time.

 

Anastasia continued, “You really think they needed any other reason? They didn’t have you because they wanted some perfect specimen. Nor did they want someone to be like them. Nor did they want someone who wasn’t you! They wanted Natsuki Subaru!”

“…”

“And all his flaws. All his virtues. They don’t need anything else.”

Subaru retorted bitterly, “But I want to be someone else! I want to be someone they can be proud of!”

“They are already proud of you!” Anastasia let go, causing him to fall on his ass, “How many times has your dad introduced you as his ‘beloved son?’ Or how many times has your mother told you how much she loves you?!”

“But that’s what they have to say! They’re my parents, they have to say that!”

“You little…do you really think that?”

Subaru’s eyes changed from rage to a soft sorrow, “…I don’t know. I just. No one looks at me. They always see my dad but not me. What if one day…my parents realize they’re right? That I’m a nobody. A regret. Someone they would rather not have.”

“…”

“…”

“…Tell me about your dad.”

“I-what?” Subaru gazed at her with confusion.

But she was adamant, “Describe him to me. Why do you admire him?”

“Well…he’s dad. Everything he does. He does well. He’s talented and liked by everyone I know. Everything he does, he gets a laugh out of everyone. Everyone talks to him or speaks to him like he’s their friend. Like he can do anything. They come to him whenever they have problems and he solves every single one. He’s…amazing.”

Anastasia stared at Subaru, “Yeah. Well, I disagree. Kenichi’s a loser.”

Subaru’s face molded back into rage, “You-“

Anastasia held her hands up in exasperation, “I don’t see what is so great about him. Sure, he’s handsome. And sure, he can make people laugh. But that’s normal. You act like he’s some type of God or second coming of Alex Hoshin but he’s anything but.”

“Alex Hoshin? Who?”

Anastasia ignored him, “Did you know he dropped out of college?”

Subaru flinched in alarm, “He did?! I thought he never went…”

Anastasia rolled her eyes, “Of course you don’t remember. Or at least, you do but you blocked that memory out given I saw it. You heard it when you were a child. He was drunk and apologizing to your mother about how much of an idiot he was, regretting not taking his studies seriously. He dropped out of college because some friend of his convinced him it was a waste of time. That they could start a business without it. And guess what happened: it failed miserably. It didn’t help that your father is street smart but the worst book smart possible. He can barely do any math above high school level. He can use what he knows well but anything beyond and he flounders.”

“Hey, he’s not that bad!”

Anastasia didn’t stop, “Do you know why he kept getting fired all those times? It’s because he let people walk all over him. How many times do you think someone said something wrong and he just let it go? Or how many times has someone asked him for a favor and he can’t say no? Too many. It’s why everyone likes him. Because who wouldn’t like a guy who says yes to everything and ends up somehow figuring it out? But it’s also why he couldn’t keep a job. Because so many people took advantage of him and threw him to the curb after using him up. Hell, it’s why he has all those high school girls’ email addresses on his phone.”

“…I thought it was because he liked the attention,” Subaru said.

Anastasia shook her head, “Oh please. We both know the only attention he wants is from his wife. But he doesn’t have the heart to say no. He’s gotten better from what I saw but he is far from the perfect human being of pure talent you keep describing him as. In fact, I can make a good argument that he’s an absolute loser.”

“…Take that back,” Subaru glared at Anastasia.

“Nope. He only recently got a stable job and that was after years of mucking about. Hell, I’d wager you were partially the reason for him getting the job in the first place. And he only recently started getting some backbone. And it’s sad for someone like him to use those exaggerated gestures all the time. He looks like a kid who never grew up. He should have gotten a good job to support his family, but he was only able to barely scrounge up enough savings to buy this house, half of it being paid off by a loan from his in-laws in exchange for a promise to take care of your mother. He’s been tripping his way to victory and only knows to be optimistic to cope with it all.”

Subaru stood up, pointing at Anastasia’s chest angrily, “You don’t get to say that! He’s a good dad and he tries his best every day!”

“Then why do you get to demean yourself?! How is it okay for others to be flawed but you can’t?!” Anastasia pointed back at Subaru.

“…” Subaru tried to speak but the words wouldn’t come out, his eyes couldn’t hold contact with Anastasia, wavering before looking down at the floor, his knees buckled as he fell down once more.

Anastasia’s eyes softened, along with her tone, “…Why don’t you love yourself like we love you?”

She could see Subaru shudder as she kneeled down in front of him, taking his hands into hers, he wouldn’t look at her, but his voice breaking was all she needed to know, “I don’t deserve it.”

“You do.”

“I don’t.”

“Yes. You do.

“I don’t!” Tears streamed down his face, he choked on his words, “I’m not worth any of this! I’m not good enough! I don’t try to make up for my flaws. All I do is wallow in my own pity! I’m…worthless!”

“You are worthy,” she slowly wrapped her arms around Subaru’s shivering form, as he wept and choked, “You’re worthy of so much. Of our love. Of your parents’ love. Of my love. Of everyone’s love.”

“…Why do you love me?”

“Because you are kind.”

“…Is that it?” The pure disbelief in his tone was laughable.

In fact, Anastasia gave a dry laugh, “No, you idiot. There are so many things I love about you. I love the way you care for people. How you always choose to be there for others. How it never even crosses your mind that others don’t matter. How you’re talented at the strangest things. How you can talk so passionately about topics you know about. I love the way you laugh. The way you smile. The way you scratch the back of your neck when you’re nervous.”

“Gee,” Subaru’s ears began to turn red as she felt his body warm up, “You keep talking like that and I’ll fall for you too.”

She giggled, unfolding her arms and allowing him to face her, despite how much she missed his warmth, “Don’t treat yourself like nothing. Because to us, you’re everything.”

Subaru’s face was red, whether from embarrassment or the tears she did not know, but his voice was calmer, “I’ll…try. I’ll really try.”

“Good,” and as Anastasia stood up, her mind finally caught up with her emotions, her eyes now widening as she looked down at Subaru with incredible intensity, “Wait a minute, how can you see me?”

Subaru blinked as he stared up at her before looking around lost, “Where did…you go?”

Anastasia’s eyes widened as she quickly went to grab Subaru’s shoulder, only to miss him and fall to the ground, as her body became incorporeal once more, “How did-what? Subaru, can you hear me?”

He in fact couldn’t as he kept looking around, eyes vaguely paranoid before looking down at his hands, muttering, “…Was that all a dream? Was I hallucinating?”

“No! No it wasn’t!” Anastasia kept trying to make physical contact with him, only to fail as she flailed around ineffectually, “You-Oddamnit! Subaru, love yourself! Please! Just, please! If there is anything you take from this, love yourself!”

Subaru flexed his hands before closing his eyes. Seconds passed before he reopened them, walking forward to his door, speaking with newfound determination, “Thank you…whoever you were.”

Anastasia scrambled to her feet and quickly followed him down the stairs, as he stood motionless in the living room, staring at his mother who was quietly cutting some vegetables in the kitchen. For a moment he hesitated before walking towards her.

 

Yes!

 

He then veered off the direct course to his mother and went straight to the sink.

 

No! Anastasia face palmed. Though when she peaked through her fingers, she was happy to be proven wrong, as the sounds of running water and the clutter of ceramic contrasted Subaru’s soft voice.

“Hey Mom?”

Naoko seemed slightly surprised but smiled lovingly at her son, putting her knife down on the counter, “Well this is a surprise, what brings you down here Subaru?”

“I…just wanted to clean up before I go out.”

“Go out? It’s already sundown.”

“I know, I just wanted to grab a snack from the convenience store before coming back. But I was wondering…” Subaru struggled to finish his sentence.

Naoko, blessed Naoko, chose to stay silent in order to let Subaru find his words, “…”

“…I want to talk to you and Dad. Once I get back.”

Naoko’s eyes widened slightly before she smiled even brighter than before, “I would love that.”

Subaru blinked before returning her smile, “Yeah. Do you need anything from the store?”

Naoko thought for a moment before shaking her head slowly, “No…I have everything I need here. Well, once you’re back home, I’ll have everything.”

“…Okay. I’ll be back soon then,” Anastasia heard the sound of the faucet turning off coupled with the racking of a mug on the drying rack. Subaru then turned towards the door and walked a few steps before stopping. He then turned suddenly and ran towards his mother, hugging her tightly.

“Subaru?” She said quietly.

“…I love you, Mom. I’ll always love you and Dad. No matter what,” Subaru’s hold tightened on his mother.

Naoko took a second to process those words before returning his hug, just as tightly, her eyes wavering and on the brink of tears, her voice cracking but filled with so much affection and love, “I love you too, Subaru. Your Dad and I will always, always love you. Always and forever. Until the heat death of the universe.”

Subaru hugged his mom for the next ten seconds, lasting almost an eternity, before finally separating. But just as he was about to turn, Naoko gave him one last send off, “Take care.”

Subaru’s eyes watered as he smiled exuberantly, “I will!”

 

Anastasia couldn’t help but rub her eyes at the scene as Subaru made his way to the door. However, as she opened her eyes, she noticed something odd. A thin thread of iridescent light wrapped loosely around her right hand. She lifted it outward slowly and saw where it connected: from her chest all the way to Subaru.

 

What in the world?

 

It flickered in and out of existence before finally disappearing, leaving nothing.

 

Anastasia couldn’t wrap her head around that, nor the implications of what she just did that began to settle into her mind.

 

Was this Subaru’s memories? Or was this actually the past? She knew things that Subaru did not. Or at least, he did not consciously know. But if it’s the case where she has physically traveled to the past, as a ghost or otherwise, then…

 

Would her actions change the future?

 

Anastasia’s brow sweated.

 

Would Subaru’s life change?

 

Her heart beat quickly.

 

Would Subaru…never meet her? Would they never fall in love?

 

Her heart burned once again.

 

But then she heard the sniffling of Naoko, as the world began to fade to white, signaling the transition of the scene to where Subaru now was. But just before everything changed, she could see Naoko’s bittersweet smile, her eyes wet and tender, and her voice muttering with pure happiness, “He finally reached out…”

 

And with those words, and as Anastasia’s location shifted towards Subaru walking down the street, happily smiling like he was eight years old again, nothing mattered anymore.

 

None of her worries mattered. Because at the end of the day, Anastasia only really had one wish.

 

I want you to be happy, Subaru.

 

…Even if that means I never see you again.

---------------------------

Subaru did not know what to do.

 

“…Cold.”

 

He hated this. He hated everything. He hated the circumstances that led to such a situation.

 

“…so…cold…”

 

If he could, he’d burn the world. Tear this whole city apart, piece by piece. And light it ablaze.

 

“…I’m sorry…please…don’t…” her soft, aching voice slowly drifted into silence.

 

…If it meant Anastasia could be warm for just one moment, he would do anything.

 

But he couldn’t.

 

All he could do was stare and watch. As Anastasia shivered within a dilapidated box that was slowly caving in under the weight of the rain, in complete darkness. Within the depths of Banan’s slums.

 

No one around. No one to love her. No one to save her.

 

Only the sounds of her pleas and a black star that was too far to reach her.

Chapter 43: Tears for ______

Summary:

A glimpse into Anastasia's childhood...

Chapter Text

The years drifted by like flashes. Bloodstained flashes, painted with desperation. If Subaru could describe Anastasia’s younger years, it would be a survival horror.

 

Subaru could barely keep his mind at ease, his foot tapping on the dirt road as a young Anastasia picked the lock on a bakery door. Her eyes were bloodshot with bags that only began to droop. Her body was covered in scuff marks, dirt, and grime from living out in the streets for months. Her hair a ratty mess, her body basically a skeleton, a thin layer of skin barely attached. She was a walking corpse waiting to happen, a hyena as they so aptly called these orphans within Banan.

 

And despite Subaru’s hatred for the moniker, he couldn’t help but agree with the identification. He has seen Anastasia scrounge through the trash for morsels of food. Bread or rice festering with maggots. Rotten fruit and vegetables. Fish that was all but bones. These were the best of what she could scrounge up. Because the worst was nothing. To go through all that effort, to cut your nails and pierce your skin as you dig through pieces of glass and metal so haplessly thrown away without a thought. To feel disgusted with yourself, only to ignore such disgust in favor of that hopeless hunger that seeped into your very bones.

 

Subaru shuddered, slamming his fist into the wall. His eyes held hope, only for what little was there to be dashed by Anastasia’s ignorance of his existence, still single-mindedly picking the lock. He wanted to hold her close. Comfort her. To give her some kind of support for the absolute loneliness she was currently enduring. But he couldn’t. He was useless. A simple observer, always watching. Never interfering.

 

He held his hands close, slowly gripping them tightly, Why can’t I do anything like that one time? What are the parameters? What is it that allows me to make physical contact with her? I just don’t understand.

 

He gripped his chest before slowly reaching down to try patting Anastasia on the head. He frowned as his hand missed again, phasing through her.

 

I wasn’t mistaken. I really did pull her back, and it was after I held my chest. I’m missing something, but what?

 

Subaru stopped ruminating as he heard the lock finally give, allowing Anastasia access to the bakery. She didn’t hesitate, tearing the door open and silently tiptoeing her way in. It was early morning; she had scouted the place beforehand so there shouldn’t be anyone occupying the premises. But it didn’t hurt to be careful. And Subaru knew Anastasia was rightfully paranoid. Hyenas were never welcome and the death toll was nothing to scoff at.

 

Subaru entered after her; yeast, wheat, and the scent of dough filled his sinuses. He saw Anastasia creep along the wooden floors, testing the sound of each floorboard before putting her full weight into each step. Her eyes scanned the premises, searching for loot. She ignored the sweet confectionaries and fruity pastries on display, no matter how much her mouth watered, opting to go deeper within the building. Passing the ovens and various appliances, she made a beeline to the corner, where a large pile of misshapen bread was tossed haphazardly into a barrel.

 

These were the products that were either too ugly, too stale, or too soft. Instead of throwing them away into the trash, they were often sold in large batches to neighboring restaurants for recipes such as Kararagi’s version of katsu or karaage. Subaru thought for a moment and squinted. Why isn’t Kararagi’s main cuisine karaage? It just fits better and- you know what? Not the time to think about that type of stuff.

 

He watched as Anastasia untied a piece of cloth that was wrapped around her waist, acting as a makeshift skirt, and untied the dirty gnarled string in her hair, loosening her ponytail. She began to place as many of the discarded bread into her cloth before wrapping it and tying it tightly with the string. As she lifted the sack of goods onto her shoulder, nearly tumbling backwards from the weight, she eyed what remained in the barrel. For a second, she hesitated, glancing back and forth from the barrel to the exit. She greedily reached for the pile and grabbed two more pieces, putting one in her mouth while having the other remain in her free hand as she slowly retraced her steps back to the door. Subaru grabbed one of the breads and plopped it in his mouth, grimacing at the flavor. It was tough, cracking in his mouth and hard to bite. Whoever made this batch added a little too much sugar, making it taste more like a miniature dessert than actual bread. He smiled when he saw Anastasia realize this herself, as her smile grew big with the bread lodged in her mouth.

 

It was the little things.

 

Once she returned to the door, she slowly closed the entrance and relocked the door. Once she made sure everything was secured, she absconded down the streets and alleys, not looking back once. Her destination was obvious; she had no reason for a detour. And yet…her eyes wandered and caught sight of something peculiar. Someone peculiar.

 

A child, about her age, laying on the ground, gasping for breath. He or she, it was hard to tell given the malnutrition, looked absolutely famished. Their green hair dulled and tangled. Barely able to move, either because of exhaustion, lack of sustenance, or complete unwillingness to go on. Anastasia frowned at the sight, but her eyes couldn’t move from the spot. Staring for what felt like eons but was just a few moments. She made her decision.

 

In one quick motion, she tossed the bread in her hand over, making a perfect arc. It landed right next to the child’s face, their eye opened and locked in on what should have seemed like a delicacy from the Gods. Only for their iris to lock in on Anastasia’s form, who simply nodded when they made eye contact, before sprinting off to her original destination. Subaru quietly watched this all happen, his mind reverting back to a memorable night with his lover.

 

“…I don’t want them to be like me.”

“Ana. If they could be anything like you, I’d love them. And even if they aren’t, I’d still love them. Because at the end of the day…they’ll be our kid. No matter what.”

“That’s not what I meant. I don’t…I don’t want them to have my gate problems.”

“Ana-“

“It’s a bloodline problem. I was born with it, Subaru. No matter what I do…I’ll pass it on.”

“…”

“…We shouldn’t have children. I’m sorry-“

“Do you not want children?”

“…I just told you-“

“You said ‘should.’ I want to know what you want.”

“That doesn’t matter-“

“It does. Tell me what you want. You’re greedy, right? Tell me your desires, even if it’s impossible.”

“…”

“…Please.”

“…I want them. I want kids who look like us. Who I can spoil and scold and love. I know how hard it is. How hard the nine months will be. I know how hard raising them will be. I know how many mistakes they will make. I know. I know! I KNOW!”

“…”

“…But I want them. But I shouldn’t. But I want them. But what kind of parent would bring their child into the world, knowing that they would be cursed since the beginning? I can’t. I want to. But I just can’t.”

“…Ana. We’ll figure it out.”

“How do you know?”

“We just will.”

“…”

“…I want them to be just like you. As kind as you. As cute as you.”

“…Heh. I can allow cute, but kindness? Not mine. Yours. But not mine.”

“There’s a difference?”

“Yes. Yours…is everything. Mine…has a price.”

“I don’t understand.”

“And I hope you never will. Kindness has a price. Always has a price. Some know it, some don’t. But it is always paid.”

 

Subaru watched as Anastasia arrived at her little makeshift hideout, which was really just a bundle of planks leaning onto each other with a small tarp over the top to prevent rain, it dug into a small crevice in a deserted building, a blanket acting as the door. Anastasia got on her knees and crawled inside, pulling the sack of bread within. Subaru followed, feeling claustrophobic as the scent of wet moss and damp cedar entered his nostrils. Anastasia’s new home was what remained of a supply closet, the door to the remaining area of the building was latched shut, blocked by whatever lay on the other side. There were various knickknacks and pieces of garbage strewn about. A rough and muddied cloth lay on the ground, a garbage bag filled with wet books and paper lay on top acting as a substitute pillow.

 

She dug into her new sack of treats without remorse, stuffing her face and celebrating with every bite. It was the happiest Subaru had seen her ever since she ran away from her adoptive parents. Parents? Were they her parents? Subaru’s eyes darted to one, very clean, area. There was nothing in that area except for a sole artifact. A picture of a tall rat stick figure with a triangle head, a short purple haired child, and a moderate sized woman with long hair.

 

…Despite everything, they were the first ones. And that was enough.

---------------------

Anastasia woke up in the middle of the night to a flurry of violence. Her foot grappled and her body torn from safety, dragged out into the middle of the night as her eyes tried to make sense of the madness. Her vision adjusted under the moonlight as she quickly felt it darken and turn double as pain rocketed from her nose to the back of her head. Repeatedly. Someone was punching her without remorse. Just as she moved her arms to block the pain, her throat began to collapse as two rough hands aimed to choke the life out of her. Panicking, she tried to pry off the hands with no avail, they continued to tighten around her esophagus.

 

She was going to die. No, she will die. In the next thirty seconds, she will lose consciousness. If she does nothing.

 

…Why?

 

Why should she do anything? Her grip slowly loosened.

 

Why was she fighting? Her hands began to fall to the sides, almost lifeless, she felt the brush of a rock on her knuckles.

 

She had nothing. No reason to go forward. Everything was suffering.

 

Perhaps this was enough. Her end. It might be nice. It might be…

 

Her eyes glanced to the side as her ears heard a voice not hers.

 

“Holy…look at this! She had so much, just like you said!”

“Did you get it all?”

“Yeah, I did. Just finish up. And we’ll have a feast back home.”

 

Her eyes finally flickered into clarity, despite the dark spots creeping in from the edges, she could clearly see. A child with gray hair was pulling her sack of bread out from her makeshift home. The bread. Her bread. The ones she worked so hard for. The ones that tasted like Danzi’s celebratory daisukiyaki.

 

…No. Her hand gripped that loose piece of stone and clutched it so hard she could feel it tear into her skin.

 

No. She slammed it into her assailant’s head, voices rang out from around her, but her ears were closed off.

 

No! She didn’t care. The voices did not matter. She won’t listen. She doesn’t who care they are. She doesn’t care who this is. She won’t beg. She won’t give in. She won’t let herself just die. Her hand struck true, her limbs flailed as she grabbed hair and kept striking, practicing the motions of striking flint to start a fire. The motions Danzi taught her. Her lessons. This was hers. Her fire. Her home. Her life!

 

She kept striking, even when more arms grappled her from behind. There was just more areas to hit, to butcher. She would not give in. If they wished to take away from her, take what was hers, they can pry it from her cold dead hands! But until then! She will not let them take away what is hers ever again!

 

Her food! Her home! Her life! All hers!! Die! Die! DIE!

 

She kept striking, kept pulling, kept biting. Never stopping. Hitting, kicking, scratching. Even as they screamed, she would not stop. If they wanted to take what was hers, so be it. Let them choke on it. Choke on what they could never comprehend! She won’t die! She will never die! She will live until her last breath, clinging to whatever she had until nothing remained. They will not remain! SHE WILL REMAIN-

 

“Please…stop…please…” a voice weakly groaned. Anastasia blinked.

 

She looked down, her vision wavering, as she saw what became of her assailant. A bloody mess of scratches, teeth marks, and indented punctures. What remained of their hair, green and ratty, was caked in blood. The same blood that was splattered all over the floor. The same blood that tasted of iron within her mouth.
