The same blood, when she lifted her hands in front of her, stained every finger and every inch of the rock that was still held with a death grip within her right hand.

 

“…” Anastasia had no words. She could not speak. All she could do was stare. Stare at the misshapen form of the hyena that had assaulted her. Wheezing slower and slower with each passing minute. Her own breath trying to match the rhythm, but failing, and instead inversely quickening. She could only stare and watch as the life slowly bled out of every orifice she had made and finally drifted from the light of their eyes. And even long after, she continued to stare. Not knowing how long. Not caring. And only when she heard the chirping of the morning birds did she finally blink again.

 

She slowly turned her head to the bag of bread that had spilled all over the ground, dirty and covered in mud. She slowly marched to it, pushing all the bread back in before dragging it back to her little hole in the wall. Her eyes caught a trail of blood that absconded to the depths of Banan’s slums. There was another one. They must have ran away. Or…not. There was a figure lying on the ground in the distance, some birds poking it. Was that them? Did…did they? She did not know. Anastasia did not know.

 

All she knew, was she was alive. She dragged her bag of bread into the hole and looked around the decrepit room. Everything was a mess. More than usual. The little toys, small pieces of reading, and bottles she collected were all thrown about from their usual spot. They must have torn apart her room to find the bag, which she stored under the loose floor boards. Which were now no longer on her floor but thrown to the side. She looked to where they landed and almost fell over. The picture.

 

She dropped the bag and fell to her knees. She slowly crawled towards it, throwing the rock she still carried to the side, not caring where it landed. All she cared about, was right here. She lifted the paper, torn and crumpled from the previous carnage. She could barely make out the image, but they were still there. Turrel and Danzi. What remained of them. They were still there. She slowly held the picture close and didn’t even notice when her body fell to the side, closing in on herself. She didn’t notice when she fell asleep, too exhausted to care about the dried blood covering her body. She didn’t notice the invisible man, crying silently as he watched over her.

 

Not knowing the constant words that echoed through his mind,

 

“Kindness has a price.”

----------------------

The bodies were still there.

 

She didn’t look at them once.

 

Not one bit.

 

She took what she had and left.

 

Never looking back.

----------------------------

From then on, Anastasia never stayed in one place. She was constantly moving. Constantly scavenging. Constantly fighting. Never looking back. Never letting her guard down. Never stopping to consider.

 

Eating whatever she could with abandon, never leaving any behind. Leaving scraps is meaningless. She needed nutrition. But more than anything…it was hers. She wouldn’t let anyone have what she had. No more losing. No more hurting. No more giving. It was all hers, and she will make it so.

---------------------------

Slavers. There were slavers prowling the streets. She needed to be careful. Several hyenas had disappeared. They were always the first to go when the traders are looking for more stock. Just have to hide.

 

Hide and ignore everything. Ignore the screams. Ignore the begging. Ignore the voices. It was all a trap. If she goes out there, she will be taken too.

---------------------------

The bakery knows. How does she know? Well besides the obvious trap hidden just a few meters from the door, she could smell fresh bread already. They never make bread that early or late. But no one is in there. Which means they know. They know she enters. They know she goes for the bread in the corner. They know. So, she can’t come back. She can’t. She’s smarter than this.

---------------------------

Another hyena was found dead. She knew this one. He also ran solo like her. Never going near the others. Never trying to make groups. Groups were lethal. Someone always was going to betray the other. A quick slit to the throat meant another meal for the next day. Everyone thought the same. But this hyena was alone. His lips were stained with white cream, remnants of a rare pastry he must have stolen from a child. He took one bite…and died. He died from lack of food and too much food. She noticed this before. If you do not eat for weeks and suddenly eat, your body rejects the food. And you die. That’s bad.

 

This is why she eats whatever she can. No matter what. No matter the day or time. She will eat it. Even if it’s covered in dirt, feces, or maggots. She’ll eat it. And survive. Keep moving. One step at a time. Never look back.

 

The pastry tasted sweet.

---------------------------

She found more books. A rich child threw them away while a carriage passed by. More for her. She’ll learn. Maybe there will be something useful. Maybe there won’t be. But at the very least, she won’t be bored.

---------------------------

She was wrong. They were all some weird novels about princes and knights and some weird stuff that made no sense. There was a story about a girl who was all alone until she made a friend with a monster. A dark monster made of shadows. The monster was hated by everyone. But not the girl. The girl and the monster were friends. They did everything together. Played together. Laughed together. Ate together. The girl loved the monster. And the monster loved the girl.

 

…The girl got sick. The monster went on a journey. The monster fought other monsters. The monster found a flower. The monster came back with the flower. The girl was cured. The girl was so happy.

 

But the monster had to leave. The monster had to pay a price for the flower. The monster had to return to the shadows.

 

And the girl…had a choice. To stay. Or to follow the monster.

 

The girl stayed. She was afraid of leaving. So she stayed. The girl grew up. The girl married. And the girl died old.

 

And at her grave, there was constant rain. Only her grave.

 

…She hated that story.

---------------------------

Anastasia made a mistake.

“How much do you think, we’ll get for her?” a gruff voice said.

“Hmm,” a more light and coarse voice replied, “No idea. She’s nothin’ but bones but that don’t dissuade all of em’. I’ve seen some folks prefer em’ thin. Not my cup of tea but hey, I don’t judge.”

“Gross.”

“It’s what it is. This is our line of work.”

“I know, but I ain’t gotta like it.”

She felt nauseous. This was it. She was about to be sold into slavery. All because she slept at the wrong place at the wrong time. She hated this. She wanted to leave. She needed to leave. She won’t have her freedom taken away so easily! She would rather die!

 

“Oi, hey, hey!” Anastasia felt something slam her head, causing her head to spin, the gruff voice exasperated, “Stay still ya little brat! Don’t make this harder for us.”

“Easy on the merchandise. If we lose any value on her, we’re takin’ it out of your cut.”

“Alright, alright, I get it. I, uh-“

“Excuse me gentlemen,” a sultry voice flooded Anastasia’s ears, “May I ask what you are doing~?”

“Oh…well, we’re just transportin’ goods.”

“Hm~, goods?” Anastasia couldn’t see but the rustle of movement suggested whoever was talking was pointing right at her.

The coarse voice coughed, “Yes. Goods. Which we really should be-“

“I’ll buy her.”

“Excuse me?”

“I said,” the melodious, sultry, voice unnerved Anastasia, “I’ll buy her. How much?”

“…30 divine coins.”

“Done,” the rustle of coins sounded nearby, most likely in a pouch. At the same time it landed in someone’s hands, Anastasia was gently placed to the ground.

“…Is it all there?”

“…Yep. She actually paid us 30.”

“Hoshin’s balls.”

“So, do we have a deal?” The melodious voice asked.

“…Gojo. Give the lady what she wants,” the coarse voice said.

Gojo obliged, taking off Anastasia’s blindfold. However, right as he did so, Anastasia scrambled forward, dashing with all her might. She was not going to get sold to some random rich woman. She will not have her freedom taken so easily.

 

“Oh no you don’t~.” Unfortunately, the woman was quicker and more agile than she thought, as just as Anastasia got three steps in, she was hoisted into the air, hanging by her tattered robes, angrily snarling and trying to make herself seem as rabid as possible. Her cheeks were grabbed by the softest hands she had ever experienced, tilting her whole face towards the source of the melodious voice.

 

And it was the most beautiful woman she had ever seen. Pink hair, blue eyes, and smile that made Anastasia enraptured. Dressed in the most exquisite pink and blue kimono, she was a sight for sore eyes. A dazzling woman covered in makeup and radiating sex appeal. She smelled of flowers and sweets to the point of nausea.

 

But despite it all, Anastasia couldn’t help but be afraid.

 

“You are quite the feisty one…I am going to enjoy having you around, my little dove.”

---------------------------

“Just you wait…I’m going to…”

Anastasia stood motionless.

Not knowing what to say. Not knowing what to do. Not even knowing how to breathe.

All she could do was watch. Watch as her future lover bled out on the floor, deep within the slums of Lugunica, trying to desperately hold the hand of someone she held nothing but contempt for.

Whispering a promise—no— a curse, that would be forever etched in both his heart…and hers.

 

And then the world began anew.

 

Chapter 44: What's a ______ For?

Summary:

Anastasia witnesses Subaru's deaths and reacts with grace...

Chapter Text

Have you ever seen someone die in slow motion?

Subaru has and Anastasia was right there to witness it with him. The poor boy had stolen his father’s laptop and scoured YouTube looking for something entertaining, back when it was first released on the web. And after a dozen pirated anime compilations, he finally found a horrific video of a slow-motion car crash. The person in the front seat became a tangled mess of blood, guts, and metal by the end of it. It was horrible and frankly not appropriate for a thirteen-year-old boy to watch. But there was something about it that you couldn’t really look away from. There was no terror, no disgust, or physical revulsion. All you could do…was watch.

Ever since Subaru entered this world—her world—she has barely reacted. Her brain, the logical part, was actively working overtime to process every piece of information. Her emotional side? It shut down the moment she realized he merely blinked and was immediately transported here. There was no fanfare, no information that preluded the transfer, no semblance of what happened to him. To Subaru, in one moment he was walking back from the convenience store. And the next, he was gone. To Anastasia, everything went white. Then black. And then like a pop, the world became familiar to her once more.

And then Anastasia saw how Subaru reacted, expecting him to be scared, thinking that reality would hit the boy and he would be intensely worried for his own safety, his parents, and perhaps the existential idea that there are other worlds different from his. But no. He did not react as she wanted him to. He reacted as her logical side knew him to: with joy. Elation. Despite showing signs of surprise and slight fear, the boy was more-or-less ecstatic that he had transitioned from his boring misanthropic life into the fantastical land of Lugunica.

And that was when Anastasia’s emotional side shut down. Like it always did. She was a merchant at heart and ever since she was a child, her logical side always took over. Being emotional was never good. Getting attached was never good. It never helped her. So, she always tried her best to use her logical side at all moments, locking her feelings deep within a vault where they wouldn’t influence her. The vault had been gone for some time, but it returned to her once more, as the years watching Subaru grow up peacefully allowed her once perforated emotional mindscape to finally heal. She allowed her emotions to run rampant…until now. She needed to understand what was happening, gain information, pinpoint an exact time where her intervention was most likely to cause the most ripples. Her now fully intact mind raced with calculations and possibilities.

Subaru’s parents must have believed he either ran away or got kidnapped. There is no way they would…no. They might have considered the possibility that he killed himself. But if that were the case, they would have found his body. So, the former two are their most likely thoughts. If time runs concurrently with my world and his and given what I know about his appearances in Lugunica along with Subaru’s own testimonies, that means he has approximately been away from home for around a year and three-quarters. His parents must be worried sick.

As she watched Subaru gaze in admiration at the wonderous sights, her mind continued to work. Subaru wandered the streets, getting into all sorts of hijinks. Falling into water, getting in trouble with the locals, trying to get information. Subaru is coping with the fact that he is no longer home by trying to comprehend this like a typical Isekai adventure novel. He assumes that there is some glorious reason for his arrival here, which is why he is searching for some sort of…starter quest. A guild, an indication of purpose, a quest.

“I will not stand by and watch any more of your wrongdoing. That is enough,” a saccharine voice laced with silver cried out.

…A cute summoner.

She watched as Subaru was saved by Emilia from three unnoteworthy thugs. She saw Subaru’s expression, how his face flushed, how his eyes nearly became saucers. She saw the moment Subaru fell in love. A beautiful girl, radiant beyond all measure, coming to the aid of a poor boy after being alone for so long and thrust into an unknown world with danger around every corner? It made sense now. Subaru falling in love so easily made so much sense. He was practically enthralled by her. And why wouldn’t he be? He was starved of social connection, of affection from anyone other than his parents who he intensely felt guilty for. Subaru would have fallen for anyone at that moment, especially a physically attractive and kind woman such as Emilia.

“…Satella. I don’t have a last name, so you can just call me Satella.”

The vault cracked open slightly before being locked even tighter than before. It wouldn’t be good to react like she did before. Whatever was influencing her in the days leading up to her transportation to this domain, was absent. Her mind was clear. She could think rationally once more. She’s testing him. Subaru is reacting positively to Emilia, unlike virtually every other person in existence when they see a silver-haired half-elf. Subaru is practically an anomaly to her. She’s both suspicious and elated to meet someone like him. She probably thinks he is someone trying to take advantage of her, so she is using the Witch of Envy’s name to test the waters. See if he actually knows nothing or is hiding something. How cruel.

There was no need for further commentary. Her own feelings on the matter will not help. The vault needed to stay closed. Her emotions needed to be tightly shut. Nothing can open it.

“Now feast your eyes on this magnificent notched ten-yen coin!”

…Nothing here can open it.

As Anastasia saw Subaru and Emilia take the little girl back to her parents, hand in hand, her heart burned with bitter resentment. Before being squashed along with the others and thrown into the vault as well.

---------------------

“…What’s wrong, kid? You’re staring off into space.”

“…Huh?”

Anastasia stared off into space. Her heart beating quickly. Her mind was blank besides one single thought.

Subaru had died.

 

 

 

 

The vault nearly burst at the seams. It took all of Anastasia’s willpower to keep it closed, leaving her despondent, as she crushed whatever emotions leaked out of it. She needed to stay calm. No weeping, no breakdowns, nothing. No more. Not now, she needed to think. She knew…no she theorized this was possible. She just didn’t want to accept that this was the truth. That…Subaru needs to die in order to turn back time. It’s not just a time travel power. Nor does it have some sort of trigger word. The trigger is his death. He…needs to die. He feels it. It isn’t like some kind of vision. It’s real. He died there, slowly, painfully. I saw. The blood was pouring out of him. He can’t control it other than dying.

She sealed the next leak of emotion that resulted from that final thought. No use speculating on that possibility. Subaru…no. No. No. Stop. He wouldn’t. Would he? He…could. If put in a situation where dying was better than living, he could choose. That was the only way he could control his power, is it not? The only sense of control he could ever have…

Anastasia’s thoughts froze. Wait a minute. If that’s true, then why can’t he talk about it? I thought he was scared because it would send him back in time. Is it a trust issue? No…he looked like he was scared every time he drew near that topic. So maybe it isn’t him exactly, but…the power itself?

“My name is Natsuki Subaru, the ever-busy and never-free wandering vagrant…”

Anastasia was broken out of her musings as she realized Subaru had quickly recovered from the mental shock of dying and went off to find Felt and Rom’s loot house again. No. That isn’t true. He didn’t recover. He’s just coping and buffering the realization by pushing forward. Trying to solve the problem: Emilia is in trouble. He did not realize he died yet. As Subaru conversed with Rom, and eventually with Felt, Anastasia dived back into her mental world again.

Subaru’s terrible negotiation skills aside, everything almost lines up with what Subaru told me about this very day. He ended up in Lugunica, he met Emilia and fell in love, and he got involved with the Bowel Hunter when they met Felt. But the little details, details Subaru chose not to tell me or at least didn’t see the significance of, are what’s most important. Emilia lost her Insignia this day and given that Felt was the one who stole it and ended up as a Candidate, I can easily guess what happened. But the problem lies in Emilia.

“The reason I stole the badge in the first place is because someone asked me to…in exchange for ten holy coins,” Felt’s voice bounced in Anastasia’s head, making her grit her teeth.

Are you an idiot or do you not realize the ramifications of losing your insignia? Besides the fact that you would have blatantly lost the Selection before it even started, there is an undeniable fact that an information leak is present. Someone close to you was targeting your right to the throne or is at the very least responsible for someone else having that knowledge. But Subaru never mentioned you dealing with this…meaning it wasn’t important enough of an event, you dealt with it behind the scenes, or you’re actually an idiot and never considered this possibility.

The former two would lead to a reanalysis of Emilia and who she is. The latter…Anastasia hoped it wasn’t the latter. She watched as Subaru chatted away, giving away too much information to both of the vagrants, until finally…the Bowel Hunter made her second appearance. Subaru was cagey about her. While he readily admitted her role in nearly killing him several times, which made Anastasia rancid at the implications, his only significant note about her was her demise by Garfiel Tinsel. But he never stated the reason why she and Meili targeted him and Emilia again and again. Once is happenstance, twice is coincidence, thrice is a pattern.

“…Oh, I was planning on returning it to its owner,” chills ran down Anastasia’s spine. He…oh no.

Stay calm.

She watched as the Bowel Hunter nearly took off Subaru’s head in one swing. Felt’s quick thinking and reaction time was the only reason he stayed alive.

Stay calm.

 Rom put up a good fight but barely made a dent into the Bowel Hunter, taken down with little fanfare.

Stay calm.

Felt died just as easily. She wanted to die with her loved one. Anastasia understood.

Stay calm.

Subaru…

Anastasia slapped herself. She needed to watch. No crying, no vomiting, nothing. She needed to see all of it. To watch as Subaru was slowly played with by Elsa. She could have killed the poor boy instantly but decided he was worth a few minutes of her time, elbowing him and throttling him just to get a reaction. She taunted him. Subaru’s legs were shaking. He was trying to stand but every part of him was screaming fight or flight, his nerves firing on all cylinders. Struggle as he did, it did not matter as Elsa cleaved his torso open, rending his intestines open for the world to see.

Keep watching. Don’t forget a single moment.

Her hand unconsciously reached for her chest, trying to grasp the thread that may already be connecting the two. But she consciously shut that action down. It would do nothing. She could not save him. Not right now. She didn’t even look down to check, the temptation to be there for him, to hold his hand while he dies, would be all that was needed for her to act. So, she watched. She watched as his guts spilled out and his blood seeped out to the floor, as he fell to the floor, gasping for breath and reaching out for one last attempt at salvation. Only to find Elsa’s foot, and her cruel words, “Slowly, slowly, slowly, ever so slowly your body will lose its heat, and you will go cold.”

And Anastasia memorized every second. Every twitch. Every moan of pain. Every soft plea that barely escaped his dying breath.

Just watching.

As her beloved died once more.

-------------------

Subaru died a third time. In the very alley he was saved by Emilia. Only this time, he was spurned with vitriol simply because he called her ‘Satella.’ The name she gave to him in the first loop because she didn’t trust his intentions despite all signs stating otherwise. And so, he was left with no one, left to die as one of the three thugs shanked him on accident.

Anastasia memorized their faces. She knew who they were. She’ll remember. As for Emilia…she had every right to react as she did. Emilia did not know Subaru. So, his careless use of the Witch of Envy’s name led an appropriate reaction. Emilia did no wrong, logically. Emotionally…Anastasia threw that line of thinking in the ever-growing vault. Not yet. Not now. She’ll process that later.

It wasn’t important. She needed to keep watching. For a moment where everything can change. Where she can pay him back by preventing all of his suffering in one fell swoop. She watched as the life drained out of Subaru’s eyes, as the world shifted into the next.

“How many times have you seen my face so far?” Subaru asked Kadomon

Kadomon eyed him as if he was insane, “What do you mean, ‘how many times’? I haven’t seen you before in my life. The way you stand out, I don’t think I’d forget you and that awful expression you’ve got if I’d seen you before.”

“I didn’t need to hear that last part about my expression, you know? Anyway, what’s the date today?”

“It’s Tammuz the 14th. At this point, according to the calendar it’s halfway through the year.”

“Huh. I see. Tammuz, huh.”

“So anyway, kiddo. How’s about buying an appa?”

“I’m sorry, but I’m as broke as the sky is blue!”

Anastasia tried to smile but the emotions were absent. It was fine. She’ll smile once all of this was over. This was why she was here. She was here to correct the past. It’s why she was brought here. To save Subaru once more.

“Whenever I die, I start back at square one in my initial state. At least, that’s the way it seems.”

Anastasia blinked. This was it. He’s realizing his situation. He’s compartmentalizing his experience, rationalizing what is actually happening. This was the perfect time. She just needed him to connect the right dots.

“I guess I’ll call it ‘Return by Death’… The fact that it’s a power that assumes you’re going to lose really makes it fitting for me, doesn’t it?”

…You’ve always thought you were a loser. Did my words mean nothing? How much do you need to change to finally accept your worth?

“Still, dying three times in only half a day is just way too high of a rate.”

Her heart was now racing. Yes! That’s the correct thinking! This is what I needed. She gripped her chest, right where she did previously, she looked down, her eyes hopeful. All she needed is the thread to appear. Then she can intervene and help Subaru. Tell him to leave this all behind. That he isn’t responsible for any of this. That nobody would blame him for running away. That all he needed to do is inform a guard or knight and simply live a quiet and safe life away from all of this nonsense. She ignored the pain in her heart, the very idea of Subaru never being with her is a moot point, she’ll just tell him about herself. Be better than Emilia ever was in making him feel seen and loved. He’ll fall for Anastasia no matter how long it takes.

“The second time is simple. I was already with Rom and Felt when negotiations broke down…To be killed twice by the same person…Is Elsa the kind of character that when you run into them it means certain death?”

…Why isn’t it appearing? Why? Why? WHY? She slammed her hand onto her chest, willing for the thread of fate linking her and Subaru to appear. Was I wrong? It’s been some time. So, there isn’t a problem with a time gap but conditions. Did she misunderstand the conditions? No. She knows how she felt. She wanted to reach Subaru. She wanted to be there for him. Those thoughts should be the key. So why wasn’t it working? What was she missing?

“Well, it’s about time I got moving. Fortunately, I know that I can turn my cell phone into cash, so I’ll just amass some funds, and live a good life using my modern knowledge. It’ll be full of dreams! Don’t you think, old man?”

Yes! Go! Leave! Subaru…I’ll be right there. You just need one more push. Come on…just…come on! WHERE?! Why are you not…responding?! What do you want?! Anastasia’s panic grew more and more, her hand hurt as she pounded her chest ineffectually, grasping at a thread that would never appear.

“But you see, there are some people out there who, even if it puts them in a tight spot, can’t help but help other people out.”

Anastasia stopped mid-movement, her hand right above her heart. She whispered a very faint, “No.”

“But you know, I hate it. It feels terrible. I know those two are far from being saints, but knowing that someone you know is going to be killed…that’s just impossible to ignore,” Subaru spoke, determination etched across his face.

“No, no, no!” Anastasia gripped her chest and lunged at Subaru, phasing through his body. She tried again, and again, and again, “Stop! That isn’t your responsibility! This isn’t what you need to do. You need to live a good life! Prioritize yourself! Think of your parents! Think of what you deserve!”

“And of course there’s also Satella—I mean, that girl. I just can’t just abandon her like that,” his eyes were starry, as if that girl was everything to him.

“She doesn’t deserve you! She can take care of herself! She’s the idiot who lost her insignia in the first place! Subaru! A woman is not worth all of this effort! You won’t get anything out of this!” The vault was pounding, her emotions leaked out. Her cries were unheard, her logic not heeded. The thread would not appear.

He pounded his chest, “In that case, I guess I’ll just have to work hard enough for her to actually give me her real name this time.”

“That wasn’t because of you! You were enough! She wasn’t! She wasn’t trusting you and that isn’t your fault! You tried your best!”

Subaru posed, “There’s just sometimes where a man’s gotta do what a man’s gotta do! Right, old man?”

“NO!” Anastasia tried grabbing an appa, only for her hand to phase through as well.

Kadomon was irritated, “Yeah, yeah. That’s exactly the way it is. Totally agree. So go on and get outta here!” He waved Subaru away. Subaru ran off, happily, to find the loot house once more. Anastasia could only watch, her breathing becoming more rapid, her heart syncing with her breathing, and that vault was screaming to be let out once more.

She watched him as he ran off to the Hell of his own making.

--------------------

He won. Through a timely intervention from the Sword Saint, Subaru was able to survive his encounter with Elsa. He’s alive. He’s still breathing. He didn’t die a fourth time.

“Come on. Come on!” Anastasia spent the whole time Subaru was battling the Bowel Hunter to try every possible theory she had on how the thread worked. Was it the result of an Authority? If so, it must be related to a carnal sin, as Beatrice described them. Is it Gluttony? Is it Greed? Is it Sloth? Those are the only ones she can think of that could have possibly led to this situation. Lust was too far. Unless…her brain scrambled to reach that empty spot. That empty period between being at the Mather’s Mansion and appearing here. There was something she saw before disappearing. A…bird? Yes, it was a bird. But how…it must have something to do with her being here. The bird must be a clue or…she does not know. Something must work!

She still had time. If she can figure this out before Reinhard leaves, Subaru just has to travel with him towards the Astrea Estate. Reinhard could protect him better than Emilia or anyone else can. Subaru will be safe. Subaru will have an invincible ally. He’ll be okay.

-------------------

…She failed.

Subaru was taken by Emilia, not Reinhard. He awoke in the Mathers Mansion with bright eyes and a sense of fulfillment. He wanted a job. He got a job. He worked hard. He tried to befriend everyone. He looked…happy. But then he died again. In his sleep. She tried. It wouldn’t appear. She could only watch as he woke up again to the twin maids who eyed him suspicion.

She failed.

-------------------

Anastasia stared at Rem.

Subaru’s second death was gruesome. Bloody. She recognized those chains. That Morningstar. She remembered. As well as the overwhelming feeling of contempt Anastasia had as she hovered her hands over a sleeping blue oni.

Anastasia stared at Rem.

-------------------

Subaru did not deserve this.

He’s being tortured. Healed and tortured for a crime he didn’t commit. By someone he once saw as a friend. Who he still sees as a friend, despite their cruelty.

Anastasia failed. She failed every second as Subaru’s screams were singed into her mind.

Subaru did not deserve this.

-------------------

“I want to ask you for a favor…don’t have anything to do with me,” Subaru told Emilia as fear crept into his heart.

…He can’t tell her. He never could tell her. He didn’t have a choice. This wasn’t a power, it was a curse. But by who? And who does she need to kill to free him?

-------------------

“I’m sorry.”

The feathered pen stabbed into Subaru’s hand. Anastasia curled up next to him.

“I’m sorry,” she whispered.

He stabbed himself again, the faint noise of it hitting his muscles, splattering blood all over the sheets made her tense.

“I’m sorry.”

-------------------

All because Subaru smelled bad. That was it. Such a stupid and asinine reason. Anastasia was happy when Rem died. She deserved to die. An annoying, emotional pest that would rather act with malice than actually think through her actions. Subaru was suspicious. But that did not mean he deserved such a fate. But Rem deserved to die.

“I’ve finally found you—you will go no farther,” Ram pulled out her wand, glaring at Subaru with intent to kill. They stood on the rocky cliff, face to face, Beatrice by Subaru’s side.

This was the end of the current loop it seems. Subaru will die to Ram and will then figure out how to survive the twins in the next life. Or perhaps he’ll die again. This was his fate. She…can’t stop it. She used up the last of that power it seems. She wasted it as he still ended up in Lugunica and suffered because he had no self-love, clinging to this false hope that he could be of some worth to people who would never care for him. Even Emilia was useless, an idiot who was never of any help while Subaru was being slaughtered within her own residence. Whatever. It did not matter. Hopefully Subaru’s death is quick-

“Not exactly. More like…I decided to do something,” the tone of Subaru’s voice stopped all of Anastasia’s mental faculties. Her head turned slowly towards him, her voice ragged and broken, “What?”

She mirrored Ram’s own confusion as Subaru stepped forward, making both girls tense. He scratched his neck awkwardly, “Sorry. Because I was sloppy, I brought you girls so much sadness.”

Ram’s glare intensified, “So, you did do something to Rem?!”

“No, sorry, but I honestly don’t know. There’s so much I don’t know. But…I think I know one thing now.”

No, she knew this tone. It reminded her of the fools who would act all hysterical one day before disappearing the next. This isn’t determination.

“What’s the point of this nonsense?!” Ram slammed her foot on the ground, kicking up dust, “Rem’s already dead! There’s no taking that back! What good is it that you know something now?!”

Subaru shook his head, “I’m not gonna say I can do anything. It’s because I couldn’t do anything that things ended up like this. I know more than anyone that’s not gonna convince you guys.”

Nor some sense of enlightenment.

“…And what is it you know about Rem and me?!”

“…You have a point. I don’t know any of the important stuff between you. But…” Subaru wavered for only a moment before steeling his resolve, “There’s no way you girls knew this, but…”

He’s suicidal. He’s going to-

“What…” Ram couldn’t find the words, too confused.

“I! Love! Both of you!” Subaru cried out as he quickly spun on his heel and raced past Beatrice.

As reality hit Anastasia, as Subaru was just about to enact his plan, her logical side raced. He’s going to kill himself. He’s come to the conclusion that his life is worthless and that the life of Rem, who barely showed him any kindness and ripped him apart at the first chance she had, was worth more than him. He…loves them. He genuinely loves them. And for that love…he’ll…he’ll…

Her voice echoed through Anastasia’s mind once more, “Remember child, the greatest asset, is anyone who truly loves you…because they’ll give you everything they own. All of themselves. And leave nothing. How droll, a slave, without a collar. Isn’t that right?”

…You fucking monsters.

The vault’s door unlocked. The emotions poured out. Her heart burned with rage.

You, Anastasia’s eyes drifted to Ram, Each and every fucking one of you, but were caught off guard by the appearance of what she wished for this entire time.

The thread was there, glowing vibrantly, floating in front of her.

It was her chance, and she was going to take it.

She didn’t even think, grabbing the thread and then lunging towards Subaru’s location. The boy had already ran past Beatrice and was about to reach the edge, Anastasia was hot on his trail. She didn’t know how, or why, she just needed to reach him. “Subaru!”

He had already jumped when she screamed, turning around as he locked eyes onto her, “You?!”

And then he fell.

Anastasia jumped towards him, reaching out her hand to grab whatever she could.

 

She made it. Her hand was barely able to grab his as she dangled right over the edge, she saved him. She won! She can change things; she isn’t too late. If she can pull up Subaru, Beatrice can keep Ram away as he escapes. He can live. He can get away. This was why she was here. She smiled triumphantly. This was her chance to pay Subaru back-

“It’s you,” Subaru voice was filled with disbelief as he hanged onto Anastasia’s hand, “I remember you now.”

Now?

No, it didn’t matter, she didn’t have that much time, the thread was still wrapped around her arm and connecting their hearts but it could disappear any moment, “Subaru…that doesn’t matter, let’s get out of here!”

“…” Subaru just stared at her.

“…Subaru?” Anastasia’s smile dropped, “C-come on. This isn’t worth it! They aren’t worth it!” Her lips snarled, “They tortured you! You owe them nothing! You saw how you died last time; Ram killed you! They aren’t good people; they don’t deserve to live!”

“…”

“…Subaru please. You need to live. Please just…just let me save you. I can do this. I can be someone more. I can be better. So just live. Please. Please. I can’t watch you die again,” her voice was breaking as tears streamed down her face, dropping onto his, “Not again. Once is one too many. You died more times than anyone deserves. You deserve rest. You deserve happiness. You deserve…love. But not this kind.”

“…”

“Say something! Anything!”

“You’re from the future.”

Anastasia felt her body slip forward, “What?”

Subaru’s eyes looked pensive, “I…remember you now. For a long time I didn’t, but when I saw you, I remembered talking to you. And then I remember talking to my mom, cleaning my cup, and hugging her before saying goodbye.”

“…That was real. I was there. I’m from the future and I’m here to save you,” Anastasia tried to smile but she could feel her anxiety rise as her body was unable to grip onto the stone cliff, inching ever closer to the abyss.

“But you can’t,” Subaru’s smile was melancholic, “That wasn’t what actually happened that day. I didn’t talk to my mom. I didn’t clean my cup. I didn’t say goodbye. That day…I only had regrets.”

“Subaru please, let’s talk about this later!” Anastasia was nearly off the ledge, “After you’re safe, just…help me save you!”

Subaru slowly shook his head, “There’s no point. This isn’t like some time travel movie where you went back in time to change the future,” Subaru’s other hand lifted the thread that connected them, his eyes sparkling as it glowed, “Our connection grows stronger, but the past is the past. You can’t change it. All you can do is watch, understand, and lessen the pain. Heal my regrets.”

Anastasia didn’t understand, “What? I don’t…you’re not making sense. Subaru-“her body fell forward, “NO!” Both Anastasia and Subaru were in free-fall.

They hurtled towards the rocky terrain, Subaru clutching her body close as her mind panicked for any solution. The air bristled against her skin as they were headed to certain death. If I can use magic or maybe push us towards the trees, maybe we can survive. No, if Subaru can at least survive, maybe there is still a chance-

“Thank you.” Subaru spoke softly, his voice vibrating her hair, “If there was one regret I had about this day, it was dying alone and being so scared despite my resolve. Thank you for caring about me.”

Anastasia felt her blood run cold as Subaru pushed Anastasia away, as he plummeted faster than her to his death. Anastasia wanted to look away. She didn’t want to see him die again. But she couldn’t. Her eyes locked onto his form as always.

Have you ever seen a person die in slow motion?

It was horrifying. But there was something about it that you couldn’t really look away from. There was no terror, no disgust, or physical revulsion. All you could do…was watch. Anastasia watched as Subaru’s head smashed into the hard ground, the iridescent thread still connecting them.

And all she could feel, was pain.

 

Chapter 45: ______ Polishes Its Jewels

Summary:

Subaru's viewing of Anastasia's life continues as she begins to learn under her new 'Mother'...

Chapter Text

Subaru hated this. He hated all of this. He hated every second that he was in this fantastical simulation of horror, strapped to it like an automated theme park where all he can do is watch his lover suffer on a constant basis for nearly four years. She had ran away from her initial caretakers right around her third birthday. Which meant she spent most of her formative years stealing, begging, and scrounging whatever morsels of food she could get from wherever she could. As a result, Anastasia Hoshin was a bare-bones child who barely grew. She was thin, short, and weak beyond compare. No wonder she was so pint-sized as an adult. Yet her mind was still as sharp as ever, as Subaru witnessed Anastasia always push forward, never letting the idea of death or starvation phase her as she did whatever she could to survive.

She’d memorize store patterns, mercenary patrols, and celebrations. She would dig through the trash during festivals or special events where food waste was plentiful. Anastasia had a photographic memory. Whatever books she could find, however rare they were, she would read them quickly and memorize whatever she could. She could do calculations in her head, easily understanding basic arithmetic and logical puzzles. If Anastasia had been born in Subaru’s world or with any sort of educational support, she would have been a genius applauded as one of the greatest in history. Subaru was sure of it. He was biased but he knew how talented his future wife was.

…Which is why Subaru could only curse her early life. Compared to him, someone blessed with good parents and a safe childhood, Anastasia had nothing. She was a survivor, doing whatever she could to take another step through life and live another day. Barely even thinking of any problems like self-esteem, the worth of her own existence, or how people viewed her. All of Subaru’s problems felt non-essential compared to Anastasia’s, and he hated how spoiled he must have seemed. How spoiled he must have sounded when he regaled her with some of his deep-seated insecurities that she continuously uncovered despite his reluctance. She wanted to know. She always wanted to know. And Subaru obliged because he couldn’t help but love that constant curiosity. That desire to understand Subaru on a level beyond normality had touched his heart deeply in the little time he spent with the woman.

“I like hearing you talk.”

And he loved hearing her voice, how she sounded, how her eyes lit up with each word he spoke. Despite how boring he must have come off, she still loved to hear him, and despite how little he understood, it was enough for him. His home was warm, his home was happy, and that’s all he needed.

But to see his home brought to her knees, to see her bloody and mistreated, to see her fight and kill for her own survival. To any other person, they would be horrified. A child in the midst of the impoverished districts of Banan would only inspire pity and outrage. Especially from someone like Anastasia, who outwardly was a calm and rational person, this level of violence would practically be unimaginable. Subaru hated it all. But he did not pity her nor was he surprised by the depths of cruelty Anastasia was capable of.

Why would he be?

He had seen her at her most vulnerable. During their initial stay in Banan, before Halibel or Tia had become attached to their lives, when Subaru was still struggling with the traumas he endured during his confinement, he had seen her best and worst attributes. Just like how he saw them during that hellish week. He had seen her desperation, her resolve, her subdued acceptance of imminent death. Her primal greed that she barely revealed to anyone. He’d seen all of her. He burned every part of her into his mind. And despite it all, he only loved her more. He accepted all of her.

“Now child, I would suggest putting the knife down,” the beautiful courtesan said, not a hint of fear etched on her face.

As a result, Subaru really wasn’t surprised by Anastasia’s current actions.

“…I’m not going to be your slave. I would rather die,” Anastasia said while glaring ferociously. Both hands clasped over a dagger, pointed directly at the courtesan. It had only been roughly twenty minutes since Anastasia was bought and dragged into the courtesan’s abode. As soon as the courtesan let Anastasia go, the little girl took out the concealed weapon she hid within her clothes, wrapped around her torso with a dirty rag. It was dull, rusted, and could be barely considered a weapon. But it was enough. Her initial plan was to stab the slavers who caught her and make a break for it. She did not expect any of this. Despite conviction coloring her words and posture, she was shaking beyond compare. It was obvious she was scared and it was obvious that despite her courage, she had no idea what she was doing.

She won’t kill herself though. She isn’t the type. Not even passively suicidal.

Subaru tugged at his chest, disappointed by the lack of glow. He was still confused about how he could actually intervene. Was it Greed that was allowing him to do this? The iridescent thread was familiar. If it was Greed, why won’t it activate? He knows what he wants. He wants to share Anastasia’s burdens. Be there for her. He is wishing for this with all his might and yet still, it will not answer. Is it because this is a simulation? He knew this wasn’t the actual past, this was most likely a result of his Authority or Authorities (whichever they were) and akin to what he saw in the Castle of Dreams. Despite how little his presence would matter in the large scale, Subaru could give less than two shits. This was his Ana. She was suffering. And he’d be damned if he couldn’t provide a small portion of the comfort she gave him daily.

The courtesan tapped her chin, “Now why would I do that? I did not set you free just to put you back into chains.”

Anastasia blinked, “…You bought me.”

“Yes, I did.”

“Then your intentions are clear. You want a slave.”

“Oho~? Quite verbose and logical for your age. I like that.”

“What are your intentions for me?!” Anastasia shook violently, her bare feet must have felt cold on the wooden floor, “Stop playing around bitch! I’m not some doll you can play with!”

“And quite a mouth too,” the courtesan giggled. She slowly sat down, face to face with Anastasia. Not even caring for how the knife’s tip was inches away from her left eye. “Tell me child. How old are you?”

Anastasia was confused by her actions, taking a notable backstep at the extraneous question, “I-I don’t…I don’t know.”

“That is a lie. You do know. You just don’t wish to tell me on the off chance it can be used to correctly calculate how much you would cost on the slave market. Am I correct on that?”

“…”

The courtesan cocked her head, “And now you’re scared. Not knowing how to respond lest your position becomes more tenuous than before.”

“Stop fucking around!” Anastasia panicked, inching the blade closer to the courtesan’s skull, “I-I’ll kill you!”

Yet the courtesan still stared straight forward, not blinking despite the danger present, “That is not how you negotiate.”

“…What?” Anastasia was bewildered.

“Negotiation requires more implicit rather than explicit offers. Too much honesty spoils the deal as Hoshin once put it. Your direct offer of violence does not have much worth here. Sure, my own life being at risk provides me with an innate desire to survive, which tips the scales towards you slightly. Motivation to not die has more merit than you think. But it’s such an all or nothing gambit, that honestly you are hindering your own position when committing to such a maneuver. Because at the end of the day, such an action implies you have nothing else to offer. And that is the worst mistake any self-respecting Kararagian can do. Because you must always offer something of value lest you wish to be devoured wholesale.”

Anastasia blinked, repeating her earlier question, “What?”

“You are Kararagi born, correct? Your lack of accent aside, which we should thoroughly fix might I add, you definitely do not act like an orphan of Lugunican, Vollachian, or Gustekan origin. That carnal desire to survive no matter the cost is frankly a staple of our culture. The only factor you lack is that essential mercantilism that Hoshin so thoroughly beats into our skulls with all his memoirs and stories.”

“…”

“…Do you not know who Hoshin is?”

“I do!” Anastasia protested. Subaru knew the truth, however. Anastasia only tangentially knew about Hoshin. Turrel and Danzi were not native born Kararagi citizens. They often tried to obfuscate such knowledge by pretending to take on the accent but were inconsistent. Subaru noticed their accents slip all the time. Not only that, but they also barely talked about Hoshin and whatever knowledge on the man was learned from whatever books Anastasia could scrounge up. And unfortunately, Anastasia was unlucky enough to never get much more than an anecdote or two.

The courtesan smiled, seemingly noticing something that Subaru did not, “Really? Then you would not be interested in this?” She slipped her hand into her kimono and pulled out a small red book. In golden glyphs, its title was ‘Hoshin’s Fables.’ Anastasia couldn’t help but gawk at the book. “Seems you are.”

Anastasia noticed how she stared longingly at the book and quickly shook her head, returning her attention to the courtesan, “No. I’m not. I already know enough about him.”

“Then tell me one thing.”

“…He was a man of great renown. Hoshin of the Wilderness is what people called him.”

“Yes. A man who founded our great nation by uniting the many small city-states and settlements littered throughout the wildlands. He survived with nothing, thrived despite the challenge, and succeeded where many others fail. A shining role model for any Kararagian citizen, especially those who relate to his origins,” the courtesan said.

Anastasia understood what she was implying, her hands still death-gripping the dagger, “Why show me this?”

“Simple. I would like to make a trade,” the courtesan gently laid out both her hands, her right still holding the book, “Give me the dagger. I shall give you the book. A fair exchange.”

Anastasia narrowed her eyes, “But what’s the catch?”

“The catch is that you shall inevitably return to my home.”

Subaru wasn’t expecting that. Usually the answer would be ‘no catch.’ Yet the courtesan blatantly stated her real intentions. It not only left Subaru flummoxed but Anastasia as well. Anastasia sputtered, “W-what do you mean by that? I’m already here.”

The courtesan only smiled as a response, gesturing towards Anastasia with both hands. Subaru could see Anastasia’ breath quicken, her eyes darting around as if there was some sort of trick or a shadow out of place. She was checking for some kind of sneak attack. Perhaps someone was waiting to strike and this was all some incredibly long illusion, meant to keep her distracted. But despite however long Anastasia waited, nothing happened.

All that was in front of her was a choice. A fair exchange. Anastasia eyed her knife. Subaru could guess that she had no attachment to said knife, stealing it from a corpse just a couple days ago, but that it was her only way of protecting herself. Was it really worth throwing away for a book that may or may not be a fake?

Anastasia immediately tossed the dagger at the courtesan’s chest. Subaru sighed as he realized Anastasia’s only answer to most things nowadays was violence.

It bounced effortlessly off, its blade too dull to leave a scratch. The courtesan continued to smile even as Anastasia snatched the book out of her hand and sprinted towards the exit, not even looking back. Subaru watched as the courtesan didn’t react. Not a single blink. Only speaking with that light sweet tone as always, “See you soon, my little dove.”

Anastasia ran out the door and onto the streets, barreling past carriages and roaming merchants as she navigated the alleyways. The scenery shifted around Subaru as he watched her pass several buildings, shops, and bridges. Until she finally arrived at a familiar park: a lone hill with a staircase leading up to a large tree. Already sprinting, she jumped over the first step and onto the second, climbing the hill as fast as possible before reaching the base of the tree and sliding into the small alcove within its trunk. A niche habitat that used to be home to some fairly large animal before being vacated decades ago. Anastasia sought refuge here as it was far enough from the rest of the city but close enough to her usual targets of theft.

Subaru followed her footsteps, taking a wide uncomfortable leap to avoid the first step. Once he got to the peak of the hill, he saw Anastasia hungrily break open the book, scanning it for information. A part of him was genuinely happy to see that Anastasia’s love of Hoshin was as consistent as always. It was not something she was taught or given to by others. It was simply the direct result of her hunger to survive and finding a relevant role model for it. A smile broke over her face yet her eyes continued to dart towards over the hill, expecting that loud creak of the steps or the crown of someone’s head to peak over the grass. Yet nothing came and soon enough, her hunger to learn took all of her attention.

Subaru frowned as he looked over the hill, his gaze centered on that wooden brothel where Anastasia’s soon-to-be mother figure lived. The other part of him was anxious. Restless. He knew how Anastasia felt for that woman. He remembered what she said. He expected the worst to come. But there was something else that was occupying his mind.

For what reason did Anastasia return to that woman? Why trust her eventually? She was obviously suspicious, so what would make someone so rational as Anastasia, become overtly attached to that woman? Subaru could only guess as the sun slowly dipped into the horizon.

The sun distracted him from noticing the faint iridescent string materialize and dissipate once more.

-----------------------

“So, you have finally returned.” The courtesan spoke softly, brushing her hair back over her ear. She lay sideways on an ornate bed centered within a beautiful Japanese-style living room with paper walls and incense burners laid all over the floor. The smell of honey, jasmine, and vanilla invaded Subaru’s nostrils. She waved away the servant who brought Anastasia in from the front entrance. Anastasia angrily glared, no longer shaking with fear but resolve. The courtesan cared not, only lazily leaning onto a pillow, “To what do I owe the pleasure?”

The little girl whipped out the book from within her sleeve and opened it for all to see, “The pages. Where are the rest of them?” The book had been defaced, half of its contents ripped out from the spine, leaving only jagged edges of torn paper.

Subaru facepalmed in the background, muttering to himself, “I almost forgot. You’re like seven. Of course you’re going to be angry someone duped you…” And go into the obviously creepy courtesan’s house in order to get your missing pages that you so rightfully deserve. Anastasia wasn’t stupid, she held herself back for days but her greed eventually won out.

The courtesan fanned herself, “It seems you have lost them.”

Anastasia grinded her teeth, “You tricked me.”

“I did not such thing. I offered you the book and all that it held. You gave me your weapon. Not only that, but you also intentionally tried to wound me with said weapon instead of gracefully giving it to me. Frankly, I should be angry at you rather than the inverse as you so selfishly declare. But given how magnanimous I am, such crimes shall be laid to rest. Be grateful for what you have already received.”

Anastasia pouted, looking away, “…It wasn’t going to hurt you. It wasn’t on purpose.”

“And I ‘forgot’ that the book contained only half its contents. See? We both made mistakes and we both shall hold no grudges for it.”

“…”

“…”

“…”

“…Would you like to make another exchange?” The courtesan lazily held up several pages taken from her sleeve.

Anastasia perked up. Before quickly trying to act disinterested, her face trying to restrain the giddy excitement she had from just seeing more of Hoshin’s stories. “Not…really.”

The courtesan smiled, “As Hoshin once said, ‘Do not let them see your desire, your interest, or else-“

“-you will begin with a major disadvantage.’” Anastasia automatically finished the proverb, blushing at her response.

The courtesan laughed, “Do not be so embarrassed child. I applaud you for already implementing Hoshin’s lessons. I knew my intuition was correct. You are quite a fascinating little girl.”

Try as she might to hide her reactions, Anastasia couldn’t help but preen under the praise. “So…what do you want for the pages?”

“Good. You even understand that there is no such thing as a free meal in this world. Whether that be food or knowledge, to devour such contents requires the willingness to give value. Now tell me child, what value could you give me?”

Anastasia frowned, obviously ruminating on what she could offer for more of the pages. She made a show of going through her pint-sized rags, trying to fish out something. Only to then light up as she held up the book once more. “What about this?”

The courtesan blinked, “Child, I do not need that book. I have memorized its contents thoroughly. Try again.”
Anastasia pouted, making Subaru giggle. To see his lover struggle with basic negotiation as he once did was too adorable to not laugh about. Anastasia squirmed, her hand scratching her hair in frustration. She then seemed to realize something. “…I’m not giving you my body.”

The courtesan snorted, “How many times must I tell you child, I have no intention of chaining you in such a way. Practically, you have no value to me as a physical worker. You’re too small, too young, and definitely too weak for me to gain anything. Now try again, what can you offer me?”

“…Knowledge?”

The courtesan shifted, sitting up straighter, “There we go. Now what knowledge could you offer me?”

“Umm,” Anastasia struggled, her brain working on overdrive. Subaru could imagine little gears in her head spinning out of control. “Well…do you want to hear about the Princess & the Shadow?”

The courtesan cocked her head, “I know of that story. Quite a romantic tale.”

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “Romantic?”

“Yes. A story where a young girl and a monster fall in love. The monster sacrifices his freedom to save the one he loves and the young girl repays his devotion by living an honest and good life thereafter. Quite sweet.”

“…But the monster is all alone. And the girl abandons the monster.”

“Is that not what the monster wanted? They are too different. One being from the shadows while the other flourishes in the light. The princess would only suffer in the shadows. The monster knew that. He saved her life. Why should she sacrifice herself? To suffer along with the monster? It would be a waste of his own sacrifice.”

“But they were in love!” Anastasia cried out.

The courtesan sighed, “And such a pitiful fate that love brought. Remember this child: love is a tool. One that many become ensnared by when they least expect it. Even if you are aware of its effects, conscious of what one is doing to you, it will still act as a crutch for those who desire it the most.”

“But…” Anastasia wanted to argue more but found no words to continue, “…Was that enough for a trade?”

The courtesan stared for a few moments before flicking her wrist and sending the papers flying. Anastasia rushed for them, plucking them from the air. She counted the papers she caught and frowned at their number.

“This isn’t all of them,” Anastasia said.

The courtesan snickered, “Of course. Such information is not worthy of more than a few proverbs. Be grateful I handed you such a large bounty for a measly story that I was already aware of. Though I will say, such discussion did bring meager entertainment. For that, I shall thank you kindly for. Now leave. I shall see you tomorrow at the same time.”

Anastasia stared at her, “Why do you think I’ll come back?”

The courtesan yawned, her lips always tilted upward, “Because a hungry hyena like you would never be satisfied with such a small taste.”

Anastasia’s lips thinned before she spun on her heel and exited the room.

Subaru frowned as he analyzed the courtesan. Why are you teaching her? What purpose do you have to do this? Why do you seem so…normal?

Subaru only knew as much as Anastasia told him. This was the woman who mistreated Anastasia, showered her with affection, and mutilated slaves as a pastime. But seeing how the courtesan acted, he honestly expected her to be more cruel and insane, similar to the Archbishops. Subaru was equal parts curious and dreading what was to come.

Chapter 46: All Fools Go To ______

Summary:

Anastasia is not okay...

Chapter Text

“Emilia-tan! Super cute! Super beautiful! Super amazing!” Subaru yelled out with as much mirth as he could muster.

Emilia portrayed herself as unamused, “Subaru! You can’t just compliment me so you can get out of trouble. Don’t be a nincompoop!” Yet, to anyone who had an above-average brain with eyes, it was obvious Emilia was enjoying herself. Her eyes lit up with the same joy as Subaru, perhaps even more, strengthened by her warm tone and gaze towards Subaru despite her words and body posture.

“Who even says nincompoop these days?” Subaru chuckled before getting smacked on the head with a broom by Ram, “Hey what gives?!”

Ram sneered, “It’s rude to slack off while your superior so graciously is offering assistance, Barusu.”

Subaru looked around, “Weren’t you literally taking a nap a minute ago?”

“You saw wrong. Check your eyes and find some way to improve them,” Ram squinted, “On second thought, ignore Ram. You’d only use such superior vision for perversion.”

“Even if I did, you’d be the furthest thing on my list of objects to see.”

Ram was about to smack him again, angling her broom in the air, only for Subaru to graciously avoid further violence by using Rem as a meat shield. He cried, his voice light and girly, “Save me Rem-rin!”

Rem blushed at the sudden physical contact, his hands so preciously touching her shoulders, his pinkies nearly grazing her bare skin. Rem chose not to focus on such intimate contact and instead spread her hands out, “Do not worry, Subaru-kun! Your Rem is here!”

Subaru gave a cheeky grin as Ram chastised her sister jokingly for protecting such a useless waste of space. Rem protested such a designation, though she did not deny Subaru’s uselessness, while Emilia pinched Subaru’s cheek and scolded him. Such was a normal everyday experience for those who lived in the Mather’s domain. To any normal visitor, this would be a scene of genuine warmth and bonding. Where those of different backgrounds have found mutual ground and respect to forge the beginning of lifelong relationships.

“…Why are you acting like that?” A broken voice whispered nearby.

Unbeknownst to the rest of the inhabitants, Anastasia sat on the ground, curled up. Her hair was a mess and her eyes were bloodshot. Yet despite her condition, her eyes were ever-locked onto Subaru’s form. Never looking away. Never wavering. Never blinking. Such was the constant state of the pale star ever since the events that unfolded just a month ago.

---------------------------------

Pain.

That was all Anastasia felt in that brief moment. Everything was slow at first. Her eyes could clearly see Subaru’s descending form rupture as it splattered all over the stone floor. She could remember each piece of viscera, brain matter, and bone layer the ground like a morbid jigsaw puzzle. And as her mind could barely process what happened to Subaru, in that brief moment, the world went dark.

“…cannot…meet…not…” Anastasia ignored that irritating voice. She couldn’t focus on it. Not in her current state. Pain. That was all she could feel.

Not a general feeling. A very specific experience. As her head hit the ground, she could feel the skin indent, her skull rattle before bursting, her brains leaking. A burst of visceral sensations that spread its infections from her head to her torso. And just as the sheer agony was too much to bear, there was nothing.

 

 

Absolutely nothing.

 

 

That was the scariest part. Not the pain, not the fear, not the understanding of dying. It was the pure nothingness that couldn’t be described as your brain ceased to function and your existence was wiped. There was no after. No existence after the end. No acceptance. There was nothing. For most, that would be it. Nothing was all they saw and will ever see and will ever comprehend. But for the one named Natsuki Subaru, the end was only an interlude. A partial step before waking up to a brand-new day. A solo that only he knew. No one else could fathom such a possibility.

Until now.

Anastasia could only scream, clutching her head and writhing on the ground in a panic. Her mind only focusing on the occurrence of death while her body already returned to normal function. She could still feel the echoes of what just occurred to both her and Subaru, like a phantom that whispered in her head, reminding her that she was an anomaly to the throes of the living. That she shouldn’t exist in this brief moment. That she died along with Subaru. That those pains, those emotions, that fear. They were only supposed to be experienced once and only once. It was maddening.

“Whew…I’m back,” Anastasia’s mind grounded in an instant as she heard his whispers. Her head still clutched within her hands, nearly ripping out her hairs as she staggered and turned her head slowly to Subaru. Who like her, just experienced their entire being become extinguished. Only to stand up like it was nothing. Easily chatting and putting on airs with the two maids who were responsible for his cruel deaths just moments and days before. He looked relatively fine. His face a little flushed, his body notably stable, no explicitly visible sign of fear.

“No…no stop. Is that why you hide it so well?” Anastasia croaked, her voice stricken by the tightness of her throat, “The taboo. I thought that was just the reason. The sole reason. You didn’t…you couldn’t…you only had one choice.”

Survive.

Her hands fell loosely to her side, covered in hairs that would no doubt disappear soon and return to her head. To anyone else, Subaru had just came back to life without any care or worry. He looked normal. Acted normal. Spoke normal.

But he was anything but. His eyes glance around too much. His breathing is erratic and staggered, as if he is trying his best to keep himself at a certain pace. He flinches ever so slightly when it looks like either of the maids make a move near him. His face twitches. That same twitch. That fucking twitch! It was there since the beginning. Since here. He must have not known but it’s there when he is reminded. His movements are a little too stilted as if he is trying to copy what he once saw which was already natural. He isn’t looking at them directly in the eyes. Slightly off. As if he can’t focus on them for too long or else something will bring him back. He…he…

----------------------------

Natsuki Subaru was not okay. Anastasia could see it clearly as she sat a few meters away from what would become the foundation of the Emilia camp. This past month, she had seen Subaru persevere and convince the maids that he was no enemy to them. In fact, he went above and beyond, striking a nice sibling dynamic with one while the other became head over heels. Subaru fully embraced the former while unconsciously and consciously ignoring the latter, settling on his attachment to Emilia over all else, the only thing left to ground him. Such anchoring facilitated his current demeanor: a hapless idiot in love. His façade was perfectly crafted. A mask of an idiot, a fool, that would protect him from the world as well as his own insecurities and fears.

“Subaru, are you alright?” Emilia whispered to Subaru’s ear, making him shudder.

Subaru flinched as he processed what she just said. He then quickly responded, “Aww, Emilia-tan, I love that you worry about me so much!”

Emilia pouted, “That isn’t what I-“

“E.M.T!” Subaru continued, hopelessly love-bombing Emilia as his eye twitched.

Emilia, exasperated, accepted all of his compliments and simply moved on. Just like she always did this past month. She would be the only one to notice how stressed Subaru was, besides Rem on occasion, and subconsciously understood his emotional state was in the throes of a breakdown. She would offer him ‘help’ in the only way she knew how: lap pillows, small dates, pampering. Comforts that could stave off his growing anxiety that was always present and never satiated. She never pushed him, never understood (despite wanting to) and was always aware. But she simply accepted it. That Subaru was just like that. Happy-go-lucky, naïve, idiotic. Like how someone treats a child. Or… like a dog.

Anastasia scratched her head, her logical side trying to maintain control over her increasingly erratic emotions. She needed to calm down. The vault was open but that couldn’t be allowed. Calm down. Think. Do not succumb to your emotions like a child. It solves nothing. Settle the emotions and then compartmentalize them again. Lock them tighter than before.

That isn’t fair to Emilia. From what Subaru told me and how I’ve seen the others treat her, she was always isolated. Always treated like fragile glass. She was someone to be protected and kept away from the madness of the real world. Perhaps at this point, that’s all she knows.

Anastasia stared at the half-elf with a mix of contempt and pity, whispering to herself, “And perhaps that’s all she’ll ever know. Why try to escape it when such happiness is blissful? Why run away from what feels good, even if it’s a prison of your own making?”

A core memory arose within her mind and immediately was squashed. She ignored that flickering rage that still burned through her every time she glanced at Rem or Ram. Her hatred of them was meaningless at the moment. It was all based on simple emotional attachment to Subaru. He suffered. She hated them. Simple. Her mind knew better. Rem was a terrible, emotionally charged, moron. But she wasn’t wrong objectively, as much as that made Anastasia disgusted to think. Smelling like a Witch Cultist and acting irrational and suspicious? Rem was someone who had suffered from the Witch Cult. Why risk your sister dying for someone you barely know? And for Ram, Beatrice, and Roswaal. Why intervene or keep him safe when you barely knew him? It all made sense in her mind. These weren’t kind people.

“…Which is why you had to convince yourself. They aren’t kind like Emilia, but they are capable of good. Of normality. You’ve seen them and how they are. All their facets and sides, you understand and know. Only you bear it all,” Anastasia continued to mutter to herself as she gazed longingly at Subaru, “…How lonely that must be.”

She slammed her head onto the wall behind her. There was no pain. She stared at her hands. No matter how much she scratched or picked or pulled or bent. The skin and bone would not break. Her head was clear. She looked behind herself briefly before slamming her fist into the drywall with increasing ferocity, her face still blank and contemplative. No matter how much she tried, her fist did not bruise. She frowned as she waved her hand and clutched her kimono, right where her heart lay below.

No pain. So it must have been the thread that connects me to Subaru. It not only allows me to touch and interact with him, but also it allows me to feel what he feels. Understand what he thinks.

She remembers it clearly, not only the death and pain, but the emotions and stream of thoughts that came with it. He was resolved in his commitment, yet it all was tinged with fear and loneliness. And shame. So much shame. He felt ashamed for feeling such a human emotion in such a situation. His standards for himself are so high, yet for others, so low. It’s disgusting. How they take advantage of it. How they see his pain and let it fester. They don’t understand. Don’t try to understand. Sure, they’ll push a little, but when it gets a little difficult, they let him be. Because he can handle it? Because they trust him? Is that all he is to you?! A doll or baby?! A pawn?! You fuckers! IS THIS ALL HE IS WORTH-

Anastasia breathed in deeply.

Calm down. Keep it together. You’re better than this. You are- I’m better than this.

Anastasia Hoshin is better than this.

Her heart glowed and the thread that began to coalesce, dissipated into bright motes. She barely noticed.

Anastasia counted to ten and let the emotions halt where they stood. Pushing them down would only ignite them once more. Let it be stable. That’s all she can do now. Just like when she was alone. Always, when she is alone. Push forward. Don’t settle. Survive at all costs. Work towards a solution. Step by step.

She looked one more time at Subaru.

…I’ll find a way.

Whatever that way was, she’ll find it. To the future she so dearly desires.

-------------------------

Days, weeks, one month.

Subaru enjoyed himself despite the lingering trauma that lay underneath. He reinvented mayo with Rem. He helped Emilia with her studies. He would banter with Ram. He and Roswaal maintained a cordial but friendly relationship. Beatrice would keep him at arms-length yet never fully reject his constant visits.

Rinse. Repeat. Maintain status quo.

They had a snow festival. It was quite relaxing, despite how much Subaru was still on edge.

The tub. That existed and wasn’t a joke. How in the hell did that maid make so much mayo?! Anastasia did not want to think about it.

It was interesting seeing all of Subaru’s stories in-person. She remembered those days of just asking him endless questions. A simpler time. When she was just beginning to get unhealthily attached to him.

And soon enough, the day of the Royal Selection drew near. The beginnings of the Emilia camp’s alliance with Crusch were underway. Wilhelm and…that one’s visit, was all theorized by Anastasia. She knew their relationship was already set in stone early but didn’t exactly understand why. Now she knew better. It was all because of Subaru. Emilia knew something was wrong. But she didn’t know exactly what. Anastasia could give her points for trying, given how she seems to naturally believe Subaru isn’t okay and is constantly trying to keep him safe. Hell, putting herself out there and asking Crusch for assistance with his gate was a pretty ballsy move given how most people perceived her.

But Anastasia was spiteful.

She watched as Subaru and Emilia waded through the Royal Capital, their hands wrapped around each other, her body tense.

Emilia was worried about Subaru, thinking he always finds trouble no matter what like a danger magnet. Subaru is worried about Emilia, knowing she ends up in horrible life-threatening situations that she can’t necessarily deal with on her own. The seeds of an eventual misunderstanding based on miscommunication was blatant to Anastasia. She’d seen it countless times. The greatest failures of any business or even just relationships between like-minded people were a misinterpretation of each other’s desires and perceptions.

For example, Emilia sees Subaru as a child. Subaru sees Emilia as a romantic prospect. The problem is obvious. Subaru blushes as he feels the warmth of Emilia’s hand while Emilia takes it as a sign that he is embarrassed or perhaps annoyed about holding hands in public. And neither of them, despite whatever they say, can understand the other. Sure, with time, these issues can be resolved as they talk and adapt. But for now, these ideas that they convey to each other will never fully transmit and will eventually tumble down into a festering explosion waiting to happen.

Anastasia felt nothing as Subaru glanced at Emilia like she was the prettiest person in the world. Why should she feel anything? This was the past. Subaru was his own person. He deserves to fall in love, be happy, and whatever comes with it. At this point, Anastasia would be in the capital making some last-minute business meetings come to fruition, trying to see if there was any opportunities to be found in the Karsten domain. No chance of her meeting him until the Selection begins. She was nothing to him. And he was nothing to her. The closest romantic prospect at this time, and for a long-time, would-be Julius.

“—My, it is not often I meet an acquaintance in a place like this. It has been some time, Lady Emilia. You have not changed at all since then,” speak of the devil, as Julius stepped out of the garrison to greet Emilia. Subaru bristled seeing him. Anastasia sighed as she realized Subaru wasn’t downplaying how bad their first impressions were of each other. Subaru was blatantly jealous of the man, thinking Emilia would swoon over him compared to himself. Which was stupid. Emilia barely gave a second thought to Julius while whenever she looked at Subaru, there were so many emotions running through that poor girl’s head. A romance between Emilia and Julius here was even less likely than a romance between Anastasia and Julius now.

And even that would not possibly come to fruition so easily. Not because she couldn’t ever see herself and Julius together. She could, once upon a time. Julius was handsome, diligent, and honorable. She admired him for those traits. But she had no interest in starting a relationship beyond flirting here and there. Perhaps if she never experienced Gluttony, she could see her heart opening slowly to Julius. It would take years, but a quiet romance would have been nice. She could also imagine Subaru slowly letting Emilia come to terms with her feelings. Anastasia knew the girl hadn’t made a decision yet about what love is. But from what Anastasia saw? Emilia didn’t fully grasp it, but she was already on her way to becoming head over heels for Subaru. She could see it in how Emilia cared for Subaru, looked at Subaru, desperately tried to understand Subaru. All Emilia needed to do was get over her odd perception of him.

“You lie. Do not make me laugh. Appas are white, understand? I have never seen a fruit such as this before,” Anastasia did not linger on Priscilla’s apparent ignorance of the true form of appas. She also only judged Subaru a little for still agreeing to Priscilla’s bet in exchange for the opportunity to touch the Baroness’s chest.

…Okay, she judged him a lot, actually. Still, the idea of ignorance was interesting.

Anastasia could easily say that she loves Subaru and would choose no one else given the chance. She can guess that Subaru would maybe say the same. But…would that be forever? Just like how they were once ignorant of each other, couldn’t such a possibility occur again. What if Subaru falls out of love? What if she hurts him. What if she forgets him. What if Subaru doesn’t trust her either. They were happy during this time, at least compared to their post-Priestella states. Maybe even happier. And wouldn’t Subaru prefer to be with either Emilia or Rem-

Anastasia slapped herself. No pain. But the motion was enough.

Anastasia stopped that intrusive thought immediately. Ignoring the hijinks Subaru and Priscilla were getting up to, she tried to focus on different topics. Like how Subaru is on his way to a meltdown. It’s obvious given the clues. His insistence to be with Emilia all the time, his obsession with her, his slowly rising paranoia regarding his role in the world and in her heart. He’s one step away from crashing. And isn’t that so familiar? Didn’t she, just recently, do the same? How fun. She let her own insecurities fester until Subaru thought of her as a burden. Hell, she was worse. Subaru was actively trying to save her family, which Anastasia couldn’t remember. And all she could think about was failing him. She hated her emotions.

Anastasia grit her teeth, her hands habitually scratched her body, her head, and her arms. She hated this. What was wrong with her? Why does she keep acting like an emotional wreck?
