Didn’t she promise herself this wouldn’t happen anymore. That she would become someone stronger? Calm down. Calm down. Calm down.

“Mmm, I think I pity you just a tad. Whether you are aware of it or not, you so thoroughly play the fool. It is no virtue. Tis merely a thin shell within which you conceal your weakness. It is as repellant to the eye as your face,” Priscilla spat in disgust. Even Miss Prissy-and-Pissy knew Subaru’s demeanor was just an act.

Just like Anastasia. Tia was right. She was a woman of many faces. So many masks, so many shells, so many facades. Underneath the veneer of a high-class merchant, was a scavenger who only took from people. She took from everyone. And left them nothing. Like a coward, all she does is take and run. Ricardo. Mimi. Hetaro. Tivey. Julius. Now, Subaru. All she does is take. A parasite. Is she so different from the others? From all the people who hurt Subaru? How could she act like she was better. She’s the worst. Scum beyond all measure. Selfish to her core.

Even now…all she can do is focus on herself, pitying herself despite Subaru suffering far more than she ever could. How disgusting.

-------------------------

“…You both are so stupid,” Anastasia couldn’t fathom the amount of pure idiocy that was happening right in front of her. But she could. Because her past self was standing right next to her, also not fathoming how stupid her knight was. It’s just now she realized how actually stupid Subaru was acting too.

It was quite odd seeing a stream of events occur differently from how she remembered it. During the selection, all she remembered was that Julius had a debate with a disgruntled knight who she couldn’t remember the name of and ended up dueling. Besides being turned into a public showing, the event was not very noteworthy in her mind.

Now, she had to face this new reality that Gluttony stole from her.

Subaru and Julius dueled. It was Subaru’s fault, objectively. He ended up insulting a bunch of important people despite not needing to, especially since Emilia and Roswaal effectively created a pretty good first impression. With context, it made sense why Subaru acted as he did. Subaru was far from okay mentally. However, from an outside perspective, Subaru’s actions were quite rude. In a last-ditch effort to feel useful, he ended up making a mockery of himself and the candidate he represented. Subaru, for lack of better words, and despite her love for him, was an idiot.

“You are irredeemably powerless. You have no place by her side,” Julius spoke proudly as Anastasia wanted to slam her head on the ground. Repeatedly.

Julius, for lack of worse words, and despite her fondness for him, was also an idiot. She watched as Subaru breathed heavily, barely able to stand as Julius did all he could to beat Subaru senseless. To anyone else, it would seem like Julius was sadistically putting Subaru down physically and verbally. To Anastasia, who knew Julius quite well, she knew the knight was having the absolute worst time. Guilt and regret were practically dancing within his eyes. He must have thought Subaru was stronger than this. His initial plan must have been to show Subaru as a threat that the knights should not quarrel with. Defeat him and preserve the honor of the Royal Knights but let Subaru show off, preserving his candidate’s reputation as well.

 However, Subaru was weaker than a child. Which Julius would know if he thought through his actions for once! Julius can’t just throw the match or else the knights will treat Subaru as an easy target, while also disgracing Julius’s name as a coward. So now Julius is overcompensating, most likely panicking, and doing what he usually does when in a sticky situation: go big or go home. Because he’s an over-achieving moron. Julius is now acting like the villain from his stupid fantasy novels and is beating Subaru so thoroughly, to such a pitying degree, that the knights would be turned off from trying something similar.

Anastasia watched as Julius finished Subaru off, sending him into unconsciousness. Anastasia could only feel one emotion: cringe. Subaru’s home really had the most descriptive slang. Embarrassment did not truly describe how awful this whole situation was to see. Cringe was more fitting. Seeing your lover beaten to near death by one of your closest companions was pretty bad. Knowing that both had the stupidest reasons for getting into this situation, made everything so much worse. They both had good intentions. But they were both dumbasses.

“What’s worse is that Julius probably likes Subaru, given how he reacted to his words…” Anastasia muttered to herself, facepalming, and remembering the scene inside. The knight was practically leaning in, touched by Subaru’s loyalty to Emilia. His eyes were lit with passion and respect, though a bit annoyed by his words. But given Subaru’s reactions, he probably didn’t view Julius like that. He probably thought Julius was judging Subaru’s actions severely and was actively denouncing his self-proclamation. Which…given Julius’s words, she didn’t deny that anyone would think the same.

She peered over to her other self, standing by the rest of the candidates. Everyone had a mix of horrified, bored, or disgusted expressions. Except past Anastasia, who only had the placid mask she always wore. But Anastasia knew better. Her other self’s eyebrow was slightly twitching and her breathing was a little off. If Anastasia could guess her past self’s thoughts, it was probably akin to: Julius. You are my knight. I trust you beyond a single doubt. And I will always support your decisions. But why, in Volcanica’s name, are you like this?! Do you really have to beat a servant to near death?! How am I supposed to spin this positively?! Probably paired with a lot of internal screaming.

As the world slowly shifted into the next memory, Anastasia could only whisper to herself, dismayed beyond compare, “…This was my romantic dating pool. Am I just attracted to dumbasses?”

Ignoring her possible terrible taste in men, she had one more objective after this was all over: have Subaru and Julius confess their dumbassery to each other. She is not letting them think the other was acting with any sort of purpose or thought during this debacle. It was one thing if they were rival camps. The fact that she was going to marry Subaru was another. If she has to feel this much second-hand embarrassed, they’ll be feeling ten times the first-hand embarrassment. And she’ll enjoy watching them squirm.

------------------------------

“Subaru, I don’t understand…” Emilia whispered.

You probably never will. That’s his curse.

Subaru’s face was filled with dread, “That can’t be…helped. But it’s true. You saved me. That’s why I tried to…pay back the favor…but now, it’s…”

Subaru. Why are you like this? You owe her nothing. You paid each other back several times over. I know your struggling, I know your attached to her but…

Emilia lashed out, “I told you, I don’t understand!! I saved you? I did no such thing. The first time I met you was at the loot cellar. I’d never seen you before in my life!”

I hate this. If it weren’t for that damned taboo, he could at least try to explain earlier. This wouldn’t have happened! He could choose. He could actually be in control of his life!

“No, listen to—”

“If I’d met you before that, if that was true, I’d… I’d…!”

“Maybe you don’t understand, but listen to me anyway. It’s the truth! The first time we met when I came to this world—”

The world froze. The shadow rose forth, beckoning towards Subaru to even dare saying anything more. Anastasia could barely control herself from throwing a chair at the shadow, stifling the rage that continued to bubble inside of her.

Get away from him. Stop. I said, stop! What do you even want-

“Once again, you’re not saying anything,” the world resumed as Emilia spoke, disillusioned.

You moron. He can’t speak. Think for once! If he can’t say it, and he looks that afraid, don’t you think there is something more insidious!

That wasn’t rational. Of course, Emilia wouldn’t know. Again, she has been isolated for so long. It’s not her fault that she hasn’t developed socially or mentally that much. Calm down.

He asked, “Why…don’t you understand…?”

“…Subaru.”

“I thought, you…you of all people would understand…”

“The me inside your head is really something, isn’t she? She understands it, all of it, without even having to ask. Your pain, your sadness, your anger—she feels all of them as her own,” Emilia was on the brink of tears, “If you don’t say it, I can’t understand, Subaru.”

…That’s on him. It was the only way he could cope with everything. He needed you as a guiding light. Otherwise, he would have nothing. But can you really blame him for wanting someone to understand?

Subaru looked broken, like he had no idea what to say or do, muttering, “Everything…I’ve done…”

Anastasia saw the emotions fly through his face. Regret. Sadness. Pity. Hatred. Anger.

Subaru suddenly shouted, “You got this far because of me, didn’t you?! Like at the loot cellar when your crest got stolen! I saved you from that uber-dangerous serial killer! I put my body on the line! All because you’re important to me!!”

Oh Subaru…

Subaru stumbled over his words, his voice coarse, his appearance unkempt, yelling without mercy as he continued, “Like at the mansion! I barely hung on there! My skull got cracked, my head went flying, but everyone in the village got saved anyway, didn’t they?! And things turned out the best way possible with Ram and Rem, I’m sure of it! That’s because I was there, right?!”

You just wanted to be seen. To be heard. To have all your hard work be worth something. Your deaths worth something.

He grit his teeth, he didn’t look like he even wanted to say these next words, “You have to owe me something for everything I’ve done for you—!!”

“Subaru, I owe you a huge, incredible debt for many things you’ve done, so…”

“Yeah, that’s right. That’s why I—”

“So, I’ll repay it all to you. Then we can end this,” Emilia didn’t want to say these words either.

Emilia took a deep breath, before ending this charade, “That’s enough, Natsuki Subaru,” she then stood up slowly, letting the words simmer in his head as she approached the door. She looked like she was on the brink of breaking down herself, her head flickered backward for a moment.

Her lips wobbled, her voice cracking, “I…got my hopes up. I thought, just maybe, you…you wouldn’t give me special treatment, Subaru. I thought you could look at me like an ordinary person, like an ordinary girl, the same as any other…”

Subaru couldn’t look her in the eyes, only shaking his head as if his whole world was collapsing, “I can’t…do that. Even if you tossed out every other person in the whole world, I couldn’t do that. I can’t look at you the same as everyone else, I just can’t.”

…Am I the same?

And with that, Emilia left the room, shaken by his words. Subaru closed in on himself, clutching onto Emilia’s embroidered robe that she threw at him in the initial outburst. Silence persisted. Anastasia sat nearby, shaking with barely contained rage. She didn’t know who to be angry at.

She saw the thread flicker into existence. A moment of hesitation ran through her mind, What can I even say?

Her eyes glanced over to Subaru. His form was shaking, not from rage, but from pure guilt and melancholy. She could hear him sniffling. He was alone.

She didn’t hesitate anymore.

“…Subaru.”

He stopped shaking, but he did not lift his head, “It’s you…” he laughed weakly, “I guess…I should have expected you’d see this too.”

“…”

“…My worst moment, by far. You know what’s funny? I always laughed at guys who would act so needy or like…you know, incels?”

Anastasia could help but snort, “Yes…I…have.”

“Of course. You must have, given you’ve been seeing my life, no doubt. I just…always thought I would be better. That I wouldn’t treat a girl wrong. My mom would tell me stories of creeps all the time. And I never wanted to do that. I never wanted to hurt anyone. I never wanted to be like this!” Subaru yelled as his hands slowly wrapped tighter around himself, “…I just…wanted to help people. And here I am, making the girl I like cry. I’m pathetic. I…haha. And here I am, acting even worse in front of another pretty girl.”

Compared to Emilia, I’m not.

Anastasia swallowed her own self-deprecation, “…Subaru. You were holding in so much. You were scared. Terrified of being abandoned. Of being useless.”

“But that doesn’t excuse my behavior.”

“…It doesn’t. You’re right on that. But that doesn’t mean you should just beat yourself up about this.”


Subaru sniffled, “I know. Trust me, I know. But what else can I do? The real me, the me that actually experienced all of this, didn’t accept his flaws. I just kept pushing the realization away. I kept trying to justify myself, try to not face my reality. Because accepting that I’m a loser…it’s hard. It’s a horrible reality. Even though I know, deep within, that it’s true.”

Anastasia stared at him for a few seconds, before starting to climb onto the bed, making him flinch. She slowed down her movement, “Sorry. Do you mind if I sit next to you?”

“…Sure.”

“Do you mind if I hug you?”

“…Why?” Subaru lifted his head at the question, thoroughly baffled by her behavior, “Aren’t you grossed out? I’m disgusting.”

“So am I,” Anastasia blurted out.

Subaru shook his head, chuckling as if she said a joke, “No you’re not.”

“I am,” before he could retort, she put a finger on his lips, “Trust me, I am. I’m a disgusting person too. I nearly threw away my happiness because I couldn’t handle the fact that I wouldn’t have a perfect relationship with the person I love. It’s not the exact same, but you and I both idealized. You idealized Emilia, I idealized…love. I wanted to have an equal relationship with whoever I loved. Something I am starting to realize was impossible to begin with. I should have accepted it. But I didn’t. And I nearly lost my whole family.”

Probably lost. Their names are back but…what if that means their dead?

She couldn’t handle that reality, so she pushed it away. Subaru stared at her, “You…that isn’t terrible. Is it so wrong to want that? To be a good lover?”

She smiled at him softly, “And is it so wrong to be there for the person you love? Isn’t that what you initially wanted?”

“…But I was delusional. I didn’t see Emilia as who she really was-“

Anastasia interrupted him, “Why are you focusing on just your mistakes?”

“So I don’t do them again.”

“You already regret them. You obviously will never forget this lesson. Why pummel yourself forever? Why push yourself to be punished? You aren’t some villain. You’re just some poor boy who has been dealing with too much, all at once. It’s good to be honest with your flaws but you shouldn’t ever let them ever overtake your own self-love.”

“…What is there to love about me?”

Anastasia scoffed, “Everything. You’re social, funny, good with sewing, kind, perceptive-“

Subaru blushed, “Okay, okay, that isn’t-“

“-not finished. You see the good in people. You never give up. You’re always optimistic. You work hard. You give everything your all. And much, much more.”

Subaru was red as a tomato, “…Who are you?”

Anastasia hesitated. It was obvious who she was, Subaru saw her past self. But Anastasia’s clothes, hair, and vibe were completely different. Maybe this Subaru thought she was her past self’s sister? Or maybe he just can’t comprehend that the Lady of the knight who beat him to near death would care for him so dearly. She didn’t understand exactly how much this Subaru knew. He knew so much yet so little. She had a dozen questions about what and who exactly he was. If this was actually her Subaru slowly remembering his whole life or some weird manifestation of his psyche. But none of that mattered now.

“My name is…Pleione,” Anastasia did not lie. That was also her name. She was the wife of Atlas, and she will never give that up.

Subaru blinked, “That…is kind of funny given my name.”

Anastasia giggled, “I know.”

“…”

“…”

“…Can I have…that hug, possibly?”

Anastasia did not hesitate, wrapping her arms around him, feeling his heartbeat, his warmth flow through her.

She missed this. She missed Subaru. She missed everyone.

She…needed to find a way out of here. Find a way home. Find a way to truly help Subaru.

But for now, she’ll enjoy this small quiet respite.

And hopefully this Subaru also feels the same.

 

Chapter 47: ______ Is Sweet

Summary:

Anastasia's relationship with the courtesan continues...

Chapter Text

“What is this?” Anastasia frowned as steam wafted from the small table placed before her. Metal and ceramic containers of various sizes lay in front of her with a pair of chopsticks lying next to them. Anastasia glanced over at the courtesan who simply smiled as she stretched and yawned on top of her bed.

“Breakfast,” she said before turning over to the other side, away from Anastasia, “A gift from me to you.”

Anastasia’s mouth watered, the scent of freshly cooked veggies and what smelled vaguely of poisson seeped out of the containers. She hadn’t eaten in days, so thoroughly enraptured by the various snippets of Hoshin’s tales and journeys that she had been lost in her own imagination. “…What’s the catch?” Anastasia wasn’t stupid.

Or at least that was what Subaru thought, as he watched the little girl’s eyes constantly glance over at the food with a growing hunger. He chuckled as she sucked in some drool, “It’s so cute how she can’t hold back her emotions.” His memory went back to the first days he spent with Anastasia in Banan. She had a habit of hiding her reactions with a constant polite smile or a cheerfully cute persona. Only revealing her more crude and sassy personality to him during private moments.

The courtesan didn’t even turn around, waving her hand in the air lazily, “The catch is simple. You shall eat while I nap. If you can do so without dirtying your hands or causing a mess, I shall reward you with another page.”

Anastasia eyed her with suspicion, “But you get nothing out of this.”

“I get a few quiet moments to relax. My schedule is oh~! So~! Busy~!” She said dramatically, arching her back, “Nowadays that I can rarely find time for reprieve. Hence why your visit has come at an uncomfortable but opportune time.”

Anastasia ruminated for a moment before speaking, “Why would me being here get you out of work?”

Her answer went unheard as the courtesan chose not to respond, settling her body into a comfortable position before soft snores could be heard. Anastasia frowned, peeved about being ignored before her stomach grumbled. Her eyes returned to the set of food before her, her body naturally desiring the nutrients it so desperately needed for her still maturing body. Subaru could guess that she was weighing her options. The Anastasia he knew would most likely be suspicious of the courtesan’s intentions. Perhaps there was some sleeping medication or some type of poison mixed in. It would be hasty to simply trust-

And little Anastasia immediately tore off the lids of each bowl, ready to gorge on the food without mercy or hesitation. It was a simple selection of rice, stir fried vegetables, and what looked like some type of grilled mackerel look-a-like. Whatever it was, it didn’t matter, as Anastasia was too hungry to care if the food was tampered with. While Subaru face palmed in the background, her hand stopped, hovering for the rice.

“Hmm, without dirtying my hands,” she mumbled to herself as she flexed her palm towards herself. She then eyed the bowls before looking around, peering within the cracks and crevices for some type of familiar utensil. She had experience with forks, spoons, and knives given her initial foster family. But not chopsticks as she held the two sticks awkwardly in each hand.

She held each like a dagger, angling them precariously over each dish as if calculating the precise way to use the sticks without getting her hands dirty. To Anastasia, this was a matter of life or death, given that a page of Hoshin was at stake. For Subaru, this was downright adorable and hilarious.

It’s so cute! Look at her with her widdle hands. Subaru cooed as she ineffectually tried stabbing the fish with one stick, trying to awkwardly skewer it and perhaps shove it into her mouth. But the fish was greasy, slipping out of her stick despite the attempts. For several minutes, she continued to try picking up any of the food with little to no progress. Frustrated and pouting, she was about to throw the chopsticks at the courtesan but was interrupted by a sweet voice, “Having trouble?”

“…No,” Anastasia grumbled.
“You are quite awful at lying. Another flaw we will need to iron out,” the courtesan still faced away from Anastasia, “But we must take each step as they come. I could teach you how to use the chopsticks effectively.”

Anastasia knew what to expect, “For what price?”

The courtesan chuckled, “Ah. You really do learn fast. The price is a simple one. What is your name?”

Anastasia blinked, “I don’t have one.”

That caused a reaction from the courtesan as she lifted her head and slowly turned around, side-eyeing Anastasia, “You don’t?”

“No. I don’t remember ever having one at all,” Anastasia shrugged, “Though I guess I have been called stuff before. Brat, Little Twerp, Fucking Hyena, and…Little Sprout.”

The courtesan blinked, “Hm, quite fitting.”

“So, what, do you want something else?”

The courtesan hummed before answering, “What kind of name would you like?”

“You’re giving me one?” Anastasia huffed, putting her hands on her hips. Subaru nearly had a heart attack looking at her acting all angry. If he could, he would take thousands of pictures and tease the hell out of his wife later. For once, he really regretted selling his phone to Rusell Fellow.

…Maybe I can convince him to sell it back to me. The company was doing well so there was no shortage of money that Subaru could use to financially persuade the shady guy to give Subaru back his phone. If that wasn’t enough, Halibel could easily help with a more subtle approach. And if that didn’t work, Tia.

Tia was enough of a persuasive argument for most people.

Subaru was broken out of his future plans by the courtesan chuckling, taking a sip from her nearby chalice before speaking, “Such an act would be meaningless. What good would giving you a name bring?”

Anastasia narrowed her eyes, “I don’t understand.”

“Then I shall explain. A name is important because it is what anchors us to people,” the courtesan pointed at her heart, “When one meets another, the first thing you would memorize is their physical appearance. You will be reminded of that appearance and all the special quirks or traits that differentiates them from others. But that does not anchor them into your mind. No. Usually, what anchors them is their name. It is why we usually designate a title or name onto strangers in order to fully remember the ones we meet in our lives. A name is important because it is what lays the foundation for memories. It is what lays the blocks for a relationship. And it is what chains us to people. A name is what defines us to the world. Our existence, our way of being, our history. All of which is recorded through our names.”

Anastasia tapped her foot on the ground, impatient, “What’s your point?”

“My point is that it would be a crime to name you. An orphan who survives on their own skills or merit. Given a name by one who hasn’t sired them. A parent deserves the right to name their child because that is the bond that they share. A special bond that can never be replaced.”

Anastasia gripped the hem of her raggy robes, her face scrunching in abject sorrow. Subaru felt his bloodlust spike. He calmed it. This was just a memory. There was no use in getting angry at nothing. Anastasia whispered to herself, “A parent huh…so I can’t ever have a name.”

“You misunderstand. I cannot name you. But you can. Such is your right as a child of the slums, a scavenger of the wastes. Your plantations are the rot and trash of the wealthy. You pick from the discarded fruits of those who do not cherish what they have. You are the one who decides. Just as you have always decided, every day, whether to survive or to sit down and perish. Prove your own existence on this mortal realm and choose your own, proper name.”

“I-“ Anastasia hesitated, her eyes flickering back and forth awkwardly, “…I don’t know. I can’t choose.”

The courtesan blinked before smiling, “Very well. Perhaps you will gain the courage to say the word on the tip of your tongue soon. But not now,” the courtesan then rose from her seat, grabbing a bell nearby in one fluid motion. The ringing echoed through the air. She slowly crept towards Anastasia as doors from across the room opened, revealing a man dressed in servant attire. At first, Subaru assumed it was a slave, but on further inspection, what appeared to be an iron collar was more of a thick necklace with a pink flower in the middle.

A water lily?

The servant was carrying a dish that held an ornate pair of chopsticks, gingerly presented to the courtesan who picked it up with her dainty hands. She then gestured to the servant to leave, who did so without another word. Subaru couldn’t put his finger on it, but for some reason that servant creeped him out. The courtesan then prepared her hand, “Now then, let me show you the proper way to eat.”

The courtesan was interrupted by Anastasia raising a hand. The courtesan cocked her head but tapped her chopsticks to the table, giving her the go-ahead, “I…haven’t heard your name yet.”

The courtesan raised an eyebrow, “Does that mean you wish to learn of mine? You wish to anchor myself into your world?”

Anastasia sputtered, “I-I mean, I don’t know. You aren’t terrible. I guess. I mean, you haven’t done anything weird to me. And like, you’re giving me food. And well, I don’t exactly want to keep calling you, well, ‘you.’”

“Hmm, I see, we’ll have to work on your poise under pressure. But very well then,” the courtesan smiled. She seemed way too happy by the progression of events, “I shall give you my name as a gift. Take this as a gesture of good faith, for the start of our relationship.”

Subaru’s spine tingled, he didn’t like how that sounded. Not at all. Anastasia on the other hand seemed transfixed, completely excited to hear the name of her benefactor after so long. Though her eyes did hold some doubt, “You said there wasn’t a catch last time. What about this time? Is there something wrong with this gift?”

The courtesan giggled, “There wasn’t and there still isn’t. With enough time, you could have figured out the methodology. You simply do not have the patience. But now you have learned a move valuable lesson: that when you cannot accomplish a task yourself, you can request support from others who have the necessary skills.”

“This was a lesson?”

“An introduction to commerce. I gave you a gift but that does not mean you can use it. Just as resources can be available to you freely, it does not mean you are capable of utilizing them to your fullest capacity. You will learn quickly that the most powerful individuals are not those who are the strongest, the fastest, or the most adaptable. It is those who can move people’s hearts. Power lies within knowledge and knowledge imbues us with understanding. When we understand people, know how they work, and their capabilities, we become powerful. When people move as a whole, guided by purpose, and given roles that are fitting for them, anything is possible. Because as Hoshin once said, ‘An individual can move a rock. A town can move a boulder. A country can move a mountain. But a nation-“

“-can move the world itself,” Anastasia finished, the courtesan’s grin growing even wider than before, “Because a nation is not just a large population of people. It’s an identity.”

“And those of a common identity, have purpose beyond themselves. Their hearts lie in that commonality and without even a word, they are moved to follow said purpose. That is power. That is what it means to be a citizen of Kararagi.”

“…Can we eat now?” Anastasia’s stomach growled, making her blush.

The courtesan blinked, “Very well.”

And so, the courtesan taught Anastasia slowly, guiding her hand and allowing her to fumble and succeed at using the chopsticks. Her movements were precise, calculated. But on the outset, the whole situation appeared to be quite homey. It was like a mother was teaching her daughter how to eat without making a mess. To any outsider, this would be the picturesque definition of mother-daughter bonding.

But to Subaru, he was conflicted.

I don’t understand. Ana-pop acted like she was literally Satan herself. I know people can act kind to try to manipulate you.

Visions of Echidna flashed within his mind.

And as much as that dummy keeps saying it, Ana was never manipulating me out of malic. This is…different.

The courtesan was shady, undoubtably so, but she had genuine care for Anastasia. Her eyes revealed so much: curiosity, fondness, amusement. It wasn’t like Echidna. Echidna faked it. He could tell now. This was genuine. She didn’t see Ana as an experiment. She saw her as a person. So, Subaru did not understand. Yet, his discomfort grew worse, like a building sense of dread. For some reason, it peaked right as he heard the courtesan’s name.

Lotus.

------------------------

Days drifted into weeks drifted into months. All the while, Anastasia’s walls slowly fell as she got used to visiting Lotus nearly every single day. And with each visit, the Lotus rained gifts onto Anastasia. Food, kimonos, books. High-quality artifacts that she could never find elsewhere. Her cheeks became more plump, her clothes less ragged, her posture more refined. Anastasia learned more and more under the tutelage of Lotus but she still had the viciousness ingrained into her from her time as a hyena.

“A man enters the store and buys one bundle of bread, two lemoms, and four appas in Banan. How much does he have to pay?” Lotus asked.

“One silver coin and five copper coins,” Anastasia said in under a second.

“Good. Now, if he were to travel to the neighboring cities, what is the optimal amount of money he can profit from selling such commodities?”

Anastasia stayed quiet for ten seconds, “Kyo is the closest to Banan, but its prices are not that much better than Banan’s. He would only get a profit margin of around 8 copper coins. The other cities are too far to justify the effort, as the cost of traveling would go above the profit of Kyo.”

“Great catch. So will he sell in Kyo then?”

“…No. At the very least, he would not stop at just Kyo. He would sell what he bought at Banan in Kyo and use the money to buy thirty strowberry bushels. Kyo is known for having an excess supply of berry produce. If he were to then travel to Priestella, he could then sell the strowberries at a higher price. This is because Lugunica is known for having a climate that does not cater towards strowberry farming. Traders from Lugunica would easily buy his goods and his profit margins would be around 12 silver coins, even if we consider travel expenses,” Anastasia ended her speech and sat expectantly.

Lotus ruminated for a moment, intending to put faux pressure on Anastasia before saying with pride, “Masterful work. You have come very far since we first spoke,” Lotus clapped as Anastasia preened at the praise.

Anastasia leaned back before pushing herself forward and hopping onto her feet. Subaru snickered at her adorability. She then held her hands out, “Gimme.”

Lotus looked at her, unamused, “I see decorum and manners is still in progress. A shame that this is where we will have to end our lessons.”

Anastasia frowned, “What do you mean by that?”

The Lotus stood up, careful and elegant in every action, she then took out a few papers before putting them into Anastasia’s hands, “It is as I say. This is the end of our lessons. I do not have anymore of Hoshin’s adventures to give you.”

Anastasia sputtered, “W-wait! That doesn’t make sense. There is no way this is all Hoshin did!”

“Of course not,” Anastasia perked up at Lotus’s words, “But this is the last that I can give you.” Anastasia deflated. “The rest of his stories are locked away in our library.”

Anastasia’s frown returned, “I can’t go in there?”

“Not unless you are an official inhabitant of the Pale Flower Pavilion.”

The Pale Flower Pavilion. Lotus was a member of this community of prostitutes. They were a highly revered group of courtesans who were known for their skills, class, and high-tier service. To Subaru’s surprise, the job of a courtesan was not limited to simple sex work. They were entertainers, masters of relieving the boredom of their patrons in all sorts of manner: intellectually, spiritually, and artistically. Some played music, painted, or played games. But all of them were beautiful women and all of them tempted their male customers with the possibility of spending a night with them. Because the idea of deflowering one of them attracted prideful men from across the country, all of whom wished to be the one that is chosen and eager to claim their prize.

Ana never mentioned them, nor did she ever show me this location. I wonder why…did they die off? Did they disband? Or maybe something more sinister.

Subaru blinked. His eyes squinted.

Or maybe I’m an idiot. What kind of woman would bring the guy they like to a red-light district?

He then frowned.

I mean we did visit near the slums. But back then, I don’t think Ana liked me in that way. Actually, when did she fall in love with me? I really should have asked her. It was definitely not when we first met, I mean what kind of maniac falls in love with someone who points a knife at them when they first meet? So, if not then, and probably not during any of my loops, then it should have been during the festival?

Subaru’s cheeks darkened at the memory of their first kiss. Shaking his head rapidly.

Oh my God, what is wrong with me?! We’ve done so many worse things now!

His mind then raced to their first night together. And all the subsequent nights. Mornings too. And middays. And sometimes all day and night. His blush became an inferno. One that he was only able to quench by smacking his head on a wall repeatedly.

Stop it. Stop it. Stop it! NOT NOW!

Meanwhile Anastasia was trying to act coy, but her desperation was leaking out, “W-what if I make some money? I can buy the books off of you!”

Lotus smiled. Now sitting on her little bed-throne. Subaru seemed to have missed some of the conversation during his rumination and panic. “Not possible. That book I gave you was my personal possession. The library is shared and I do not think the others would be happy with selling those books without permission. It is unfortunate but there is no way I can supplement our time together anymore. Quite a shame but with your talents and knowledge, I am quite confident you will now be able to escape from your scavenger status easily. With enough money, you could possibly trade for the books yourself, though it will take some time no doubt.”

“…” Anastasia stood there, hands clutching her dress, legs shaking.

Lotus took a breath from her pipe and smiled, “…We do have an opening in the Pavilion, however.”

Anastasia’s head sprung up as Subaru stopped pounding his skull into the wall, now laser-focused on the conversation. Oh. It was all building to this, wasn’t it. Just one long cast of bait after bait, just so she can reel Anastasia in without her expecting it. Or maybe she did expect this.

Lotus continued, “I am looking for an apprentice. Someone who I can nurture to become my replacement. Or at least someone who can handle a share of the burdens I bear for this little business of ours. Of course, that person will also be provided with room and board. Breakfast, lunch, dinner, and even snacks during teatime. In addition to access to the library and other resources.”

Anastasia looked intrigued but hesitated, “You want to hire me?”

“Perhaps. You have the skills. The talent. All you need to do…is say yes.”

Subaru whispered, “No, no. No. Ana, this is a trap. Don’t do it.” Even if he thought this woman was relatively normal, he trusted Anastasia’s stories than his own perception. This woman was the devil and Anastasia would only suffer by accepting her offer.

Anastasia stared for a brief moment, contemplating whether to take the offer or not. “I-” she stumbled, her eyes widening slightly, glancing all around her before focusing back onto Lotus, “I would like some time to think on it.”

Lotus drifted her head from side to side before answering, “Sure. Take your time. The position will remain open for now. But do be aware. It does not last forever. Just like all opportunities, do not waste your chance because of fear,” and with that, the conversation was over. Punctuated by the smoke from the hookah, ebbing in the air.

--------------------------

Subaru watched as Anastasia packed her belongings into a little rucksack, taking care to hide whatever she couldn’t take with her into the cracks and crevices within the tree. It seemed Anastasia made a decision, though she was laying the foundation of a possible backup plan if things went wrong.

“Alright. That should be everything,” Anastasia muttered to herself, picking up the bag and hoisting it onto her small body, nearly falling over from the weight. She then slowly made her way towards the door. Tiptoeing over the roots and rocks. Only to stumble slightly and knock one of the books out.

She looked down, frowning, picking it up into her hands and whispering, “I almost forgot this was already in there…”

It was the Princess & the Shadow. A book that Anastasia kept for so many months despite hating its contents. At first her hands reached over to possibly re-secure it within her bag. But she hesitated. Awkwardly holding it in front of her once more, squinting and grinding her teeth, as if she didn’t know what to do. Subaru meanwhile was trying his best to will the thread of light back into existence. It hasn’t appeared in so long and he wishes he could just intervene. Try to push Anastasia away from this path. But despite all of his efforts, it just wouldn’t come out.

His concentration was broken by the thud of the book hitting the ground and lying wide open, thrown over Anastasia’s shoulder in disgust. She looked briefly at it before turning towards the door and finally leaving. Subaru scrambled towards her, aiming to follow but also took a glance at the book’s contents. He recognized that section.

As faint whispers of wind brushed against the book, wafting the pages slightly in the air, he could vaguely read the scene written before him. It was during the early stages of the story, when the shadow monster met the little princess, each introducing themselves to each other:

The shadow rippled, “Are you not afraid?”

“Why would I be?” Asked the princess.

“I am a monster.”

“That does not matter. You saved me. You’re my friend.”

“You do not know that. I could still hurt you.”

“Possibly. I don’t know. But just because I don’t know, doesn’t mean I cannot learn. I want to get to know you better!”

The shadow slithered away slightly.

The princess took a step forward, “Can you tell me your name?”

“…Kuro.”

“That is a lovely name.”

The shadow softened, “I…thank you. What is yours?”

The princess smiled.

“Anastasia.”

Chapter 48: The Slothful Awaken in ______

Summary:

Anastasia's journey continues, as much as she hates it...

Notes:

(See the end of the chapter for notes.)

Chapter Text

Anastasia was sick of this. She was sick of watching this horror show. She hated every single second of it because she felt there was no purpose. What was there to do besides watching her loved one suffer and die time after time with nothing substantial for her to do? Was she just here to cry and react with horrified expressions? Was that her purpose here? Besides wallowing in self-pity and loathing for nearly everything and everyone, all there was to do was watch. Watch as Subaru gets torn to shreds, running to his death without a second thought.

“Our connection grows stronger, but the past is the past. You can’t change it. All you can do is watch, understand, and lessen the pain. Heal my regrets,” Anastasia thought to herself the implications of that. But what does that mean exactly? Is her presence here beneficial to Subaru? Is she actively healing his psyche? How in the world is she doing that and what is the magic that allows her to do this?

“Unless…” Anastasia muttered to herself as Subaru trained with Wilhelm in the background, “It’s an Authority.” Her own knowledge of those nasty Witch Factors was too limited. She had spent the greater part of the week after learning about them, training, and the subsequent week after having a mental breakdown. She chided herself internally for such a blunder as any information about them could help her get out of this predicament.

“Let me think: Authorities are often based on someone’s personality, often an extension or manifestation of the Witch Factor’s power. The ones that Subaru has are Sloth and Greed. I doubt this is related to Sloth so it must be Greed. Is this—wait a moment—do I have an Authority then? Is this my Authority?” Anastasia continued to talk to herself as Subaru fell to the ground panting, his body not capable of keeping up with an experienced warrior. “But Subaru has it, unless, when he saved my life, did the Witch Factor create an Authority for me? But Betty never told me I had the scent, she should have noticed. Or maybe it’s been in hiding this whole time, hibernating. In that case, if this is an effect of my own Authority, an extension of Greed, then that must mean I can control this world. Or at the very least, it should be related to my personality in some capacity.”

This makes sense. Anastasia knew herself quite well. She was excessively greedy and always vied for the world and all its treasures: people, places, power. So, this Authority allowing her to go into Subaru’s memories and ‘save him…’ doesn’t sound like her at all. No. This doesn’t make sense anymore. Wouldn’t Greed allow her to claim Subaru or to take on his burdens like she wanted? To share everything. Of course, she was sharing his memories but that feels tangentially related. She can’t exactly share his burdens if all she can do is watch. Though, the fact she can feel the pain he feels is definitely in line. There is too much that compliments and counteracts the theory. She might be on the right track but not the right conclusion. Authorities, Witch Factors, Greed, and memories. All linked but why?

“Subaru-dono. Let’s stop for now,” Wilhelm held his hand out towards Subaru, barely out of breath himself.

Subaru hesitated, “Wait, just a little bit more-“

“Pushing yourself is nonsensical. The path to the sword is not one that can be rushed. I’ve told you since the beginning, take this seriously or I will cease these training sessions entirely.”

“I am taking it seriously!” Subaru yelled before sheepishly backpedaling, “I-I’m sorry Wilhelm, I didn’t mean to say it like that. I just, want to get stronger is all.”

“…I understand. Trust me, I do. I was young like you once. But pushing yourself to the point that your potential becomes limited in the long-run, is an egregious mistake. One I wish to personally emphasize upon you, which Felix has no doubt agreed with during your medical treatments,” Wilhelm’s words caused Subaru to clutch his abdomen, most likely understanding what Wilhelm was implying. Subaru kept silent for only a few more seconds before grabbing Wilhelm’s hand and allowing himself to be pulled up, “It’s only the second day. Take some time to let your muscles rest.”

“I-sure. I will, Wilhelm,” Subaru said. His stomach then grumbled, making him blush slightly, “A-ah. Must be time for lunch. Good timing.”

Wilhelm chuckled, “Yes, it should be soon. Luckily, Rem-dono has done our household a favor by offering to treat us to her cooking.”

Subaru perked up at that information, “Awesome!” He then backpedaled again, “O-oh. I didn’t mean to say it like that. I just, well like, the mansion’s food is really great, it’s just-“

Wilhelm patted Subaru on the shoulder shutting him up, “But you prefer the cooking of your companion.”

“…I guess yeah,” Subaru’s cheeks darkened even more as Wilhelm laughed, “Hey!”

“I am not making light of you, Subaru-dono. I am simply finding myself amused and nostalgic. Now come, we have worked hard this morning and deserve a proper meal,” Wilhelm said as he ushered Subaru back to the mansion, both of them famished and tired but eager to fill their gullets.

Note to self. Practice cooking when I get back. Anastasia blinked. Hungry. Food. Memories. Gluttony. That would make sense. If an Authority is involved and it was related to Gluttony, then maybe that is why she is here. But the only problem is that she was nowhere near the Gluttony Archbishops before this occurred. Her last memory was getting in a fight with Subaru, running away, and then…no. Wait. Her memories are off. She remembers running to Rem’s room. She remembers thinking about offing that idiotic maid. And then…nothing. There was a bird. Yes. There was a bird but—her brain winced again.

It hurt, it hurt, it hurt! She clasped her head, feeling her brain turn to mush before stabilizing. She gasped, “W-what the fuck was that?” That wasn’t normal. It was like her mind was telling her to not look into that memory. Maybe that’s why she hasn’t been thinking of it for so long. The reason she was here. It’s like those memories have been locked away or cut into ribbons or mashed into dust or something! It didn’t make sense. She needed to know what happened back then.

Maybe Subaru knows. If I’m in his memories, maybe that means I’ll get to that point at the mansion. Which will be a long time from now. She could wait but a part of her was impatient to see what happened to her. She needed to find a way to fast forward this experience.

She clutched her chest, looking down and frowning. If this is an Authority, my Authority, then maybe I can control this world. Maybe the next time I see that thread, I can try to see if there is more to it than just interacting with that version of Subaru.

Either way, it was a waiting game now.

------------------------

“Alright, alriiiiight, Ferri will stop using the treatment to brainwash him,” Anastasia had to hold back all of her bloodlust. She really hated this cat, but this wasn’t something necessarily bad, though the idea of brainwashing made her nauseous. If anything, the cat was trying to prevent Subaru from confronting Julius and possibly getting hurt again. Good intentions, bad method.

“From here on, I shall be present for all treatments,” Rem said. On the other hand, bad intentions, bad method. No, wait, stop it. For this specific situation, Anastasia understood that Rem cared for Subaru’s well-being. Did that mean Anastasia would be any less spiteful? Does one, two, three good things really clear up the multitude of screams and bodily harm that she still gets nightmares of? No. No it does not.

Anastasia could only think of the irony of these two individuals being healers with very caring personalities and being the two individuals responsible for torturing Subaru endlessly in two separate time periods. The fact that Subaru doesn’t even hate either of them baffles Anastasia to no end. She leaned on the wall next to him, tapping her fingers on the surface. At the very least, there will be no sympathy from her when she returns to the real world. One is definitely going to die or be sent to prison and the other can do whatever she wants as long as it’s away from Anastasia’s husband.

Muttering to herself while trying not to get annoyed by the close proximity of Rem and Subaru at the current moment, “Greed. Or Gluttony. What are those to me?” It was never like she had to question or analyze herself like this before. She was greedy. She wanted everything in the world. And while not particularly gluttonous, she did have some tendency to overindulge. But it seems that wasn’t enough, just desiring something wasn’t enough. Was this what Subaru was complaining about? That there was more to it than simply wanting more and more.

Her eyes flickered to Subaru’s smiling face, jealousy taking flight as dying embers in her cold stomach, annoying her to no end. She stared for a few moments before sighing. It was clear as day what her desires were, but now it felt embarrassing to speak out loud. Love was supposed to be pure, wasn’t it? Not…like this.

She chuckled before sliding down onto the floor, curling into herself, “Though that’s been our relationship since the beginning, hasn’t it? Messed up, toxic, codependent.” She wished things could have started differently. That they met differently. That they fell in love like normal people. And not like these weird traumatic messes that ended up attaching themselves to each other out of pure necessity. She wished-

Her eyes stared longingly at the quiet moment between Subaru and Rem. She hated this feeling. It kept creeping up on her, but it was hard to ignore. Along with so many intrusive questions that she didn’t want the answers to, there was an ever-present reality that she just couldn’t accept no matter how much her logic told her otherwise. She hated it. She wanted out of here. She didn’t want to be alone anymore. She was sick of all of this.

Anastasia exhaled, not even realizing she was holding a breath for so long, “…I miss you so much.” She needed to keep it together. She needed to get out of here. She needed to see Subaru—the real Subaru—her future husband, now.

She doesn’t know how much more of this she can take.

---------------------

No eyes.

Subaru.

No organs.

Please.

Burnt corpses.

Don’t go.

All of them are dead.

Stop.

It’s cold.

Stop it!

Subaru please. Just run. This isn’t worth dying for! You can’t-

No. No. No! NO!

---------------------

“-but there is nothing Ferri can do for the mind, nya,” Anastasia ignored their words. She was curled up next to him in the bed. Her hands phasing through his body but still trying desperately to hold him.

“Fuck, fuck, fuck!” Anastasia could barely think, “Come on, where are you, where are you?!” Why won’t the thread come out?! Let her comfort him. He needs her. This is one of his regrets, isn’t it? She is here to heal him so let her fucking heal him!

What is wrong with this world? He’s barely been here for less than a few months and he’s experienced so much cruelty. Killed within his first day, betrayed by people he called friends in the next week, and now he’s not only been abandoned by the person he loves, but was also shown the gruesome slaughter of so many innocent people. This isn’t normal. No one goes through this much trauma and comes out normal. No wonder he’s barely functioning, he’s practically in shock.

“Ferri just hates people who lose their will to live, pure and simple,” Anastasia threw a pillow at his head, it went sailing through the cat.

Anastasia snarled at him, “Shut the fuck up!” She pointed at him, “You don’t know shit. If you saw all that, if you were pressed into a situation where your death was the only way to get all those kids back to life, you would not be saying this bullshit!” She needed to calm down. Calm down. He doesn’t know. Given his current knowledge, he was right. In other situations, she would say the same. She would absolutely agree because people who give up on their life are idiots. Anastasia has always thought this. She needs to calm down and-

“But it’s not right to save people who don’t want to live. Even if you heal the body, isn’t it just saving an unused life? If that’s the case, end it before it causes other people trouble. Well, in this case it already has, meow,” Felix said bluntly.

Anastasia blinked, her eyes soulless as they stared blankly at the memories of Crusch, Felix, and Rem. “…I’m going to kill you.”  She ignored their conversation, her rage seething too brightly. “I don’t know how long it takes. I don’t care what Subaru or anyone says. I’m going to find you and kill you. You, Rem, and every fucking disgusting person who has taken advantage of him or mistreated him or hurt him. I don’t care anymore. I’ll kill you. I just-“ her eyes glanced over at Subaru before returning to the others, “I don’t understand. I really fucking don’t understand Subaru. How does he…hahaha!” Anastasia ran her hands down her face, a broken smile etched across her face, “How does he do it? How does he get over this?! How does he look at you all…and get over this?!”

Anastasia shook, her wrath unnoticed by the people in front of her, but she didn’t care. She jumped off the bed and onto the floor, stomping around the room. She grabbed whatever was nearby, throwing it at the apparitions. Cups, vases, anything. It didn’t matter, she was furious. Her mind was connecting the dots fast, “He gets over this. He finds a way. He convinces us to hunt the White Whale. He succeeds. He then convinces us to kill the Archbishop, which was probably his original goal! And he succeeds! He does all of this, he even puts himself through Priestella and no doubt dies several times in its defense. He fucking succeeds! He does it for everyone. Everyone! And after all that, all that pain and suffering, does he get what he deserves?!”

The thread had manifested but she was too angry to notice, too viscerally entrenched in her own wrath, she continued yelling, “NO! He gets fucking forgotten! After all that suffering, he gets forgotten and thrown into a cell, treated like the people he hates the most! How is that fair?! How is that justice?! How is anyone supposed to stay sane after that!?” The three were already gone, leaving only a catatonic Subaru and a raging Anastasia amidst the shattered porcelain on the floor, “No one should stay sane! Not after all that! How? How?! HOW?!” Anastasia screamed.

And screamed.

And screamed.

Until her throat felt coarse, panting and breathing deep, sobbing, “How does he stay so kind despite all of that…” She didn’t know how or when she got on her knees, her body trembling. She finally noticed. She grasped that thread, tightly. She felt it glow brighter in her hands, Subaru’s quiet guttural noises were loud within this empty room. She crawled her way to Subaru once more, desperately shaking him, “Please. Subaru. Please. Wake up!”

Besides faster breathing, there was no sign of consciousness. She didn’t stop trying, “I understand now. You aren’t alone. That’s why you’re like this, right? You couldn’t handle the insanity. You couldn’t handle all of this. No one is here to listen or care. And you couldn’t handle the inhumanity. No one to confide in. No one who would believe you. The horrors. They were too much. So, all you could do was break. But I’m here. I’m here! Subaru, please, just wake up! Wake up! WAKE UP! Why won’t you wake up?! What am I doing wrong?!” She cried.

He didn’t move a muscle. The tears were back but she did not care, whispering to herself, “Subaru. I’m so sorry. No one. No one should go through this. I can barely go through this. I’m not strong enough. I feel so alone. These aren’t you…these versions of you aren’t my Subaru! I’m sorry. I can’t do this anymore. I can’t. I can’t see you suffer all this time and do nothing! I need you. I need you more than ever before.”

He still did not move, not a twitch. Anastasia slammed her fist onto his chest, pounding it several times without mercy, “What the fuck is the point of this?! What am I even here for?! I can’t even help him! Is this just to torture me?! To show me that I could never do anything in the first place! Is this…is this hell? This must be. Because there is no way this could be anything else. This is my personal hell, forced to watch Subaru die and suffer and only given barely any chance to help him. You’re poisoning me with hope. You fucking disgusting wretches. I hate you. I hate you! I! Hate…” her fist lay on his chest, she couldn’t stop shaking. She lifted her head slightly, her eyes widening as she scrambled to open his tracksuit and lift his shirt. Her irises became pins when she realized his chest had bruised from her tantrum. She hurt him. She hurt Subaru. She…she needed to. No. No more. No more! “I need to leave. I need to get the fuck out of here. Get me out. Out!”

She panicked as she grabbed the thread firmly with both hands, she yelled as she shook it in front of her, “Get me out of here! Send me forward! No more of this. Show me the way out. Come on. Come on! Comeonecomeoncomeoncomeoncomeon!” The thread began to get brighter and brighter, as if responding to her will, “Let me out, let me out, let me out, letmeoutletmeoutlemtoutletmeout-“

And then everything turned grey.

Flabbergasted, Anastasia barely reacted before the world began to shift around her. Time was moving forward, faster and faster. She saw maids flicker in and out of the room. Rem appearing and disappearing. Felix and Crusch visiting once more. Sun rising and falling. Their location changing. Leaving the Karsten Estate. In the carriage. Everything was moving so fast. The Witch Cult. Subaru kidnapped. Her brain. Her brain was melting. She needed to stop!

She let go of the thread and was sent sprawling onto the ground. Everything was dark. Her brain trembled, so much information pounded through her skull. Time moved faster but so did what she saw. She skipped forward in time but everything that had happened was shoved into her brain at the same speed. She remembered everything that happened between now and before. Every detail, as if she experienced it all in real time. The carriage ride, Rem trying to help Subaru, everything. Anastasia brought her trembling hand, still wrapped in the glowing thread, to her face, smearing blood onto her fingers as it ran down her nose. “W-what did I just do?” She said to herself.

“It is the result of your actions. You were slothful and did nothing. And because of that, she is dead! Because you killed her!” A strange voice called out. Anastasia’s head felt dizzy, but she was able to muster the energy to look upon the new character. A creepy man in Witch Cult garb was taunting Subaru while holding a broken and mangled Rem in the air with large black hands.

“…You,” Subaru whispered, his face appalled.

“It was by my hand! It was by my fingers! It was by my flesh! But it was you, you, you, you, you, you who, who…who…who are you?” The creepy man turned his head and focused on Anastasia, causing her to blanch.

Anastasia did not understand, “You…what?” She looked closer at the man and realized something strange.

There was a thread, almost imperceptible connecting from him to Subaru who was meters away, chained to the wall. The same thread that connected her to Subaru was also connecting to the man. The man who…was the Sin Archbishop of Sloth. He introduced himself earlier. Her mind finally processed all the information. But this wasn’t his normal behavior. He looked upon her strangely, no longer giving Subaru nor the battered body of Rem his attention, just looking at her with an odd expression.

He spoke calmly, “You…how strange.” He then peered down at his hands, flexing them, “I…huh. This is not normal. I remember. But that shouldn’t be possible. Unless Flugel-sama’s theory was correct. But we tested the Witch Factors, they shouldn’t hold this level of consciousness. Unless, because I held Sloth for so long, my personality imprinted longer. But in that case,” he turned his head toward Subaru, “Greed should be Regulus Corneas. In theory, it should. Or perhaps his personality has been subsumed, the current user having a higher affinity. Or perhaps the personality lays dormant. This whole situation is already strange; the inner Od should not be this close to reality. Which means there must be an Authority at work here, or maybe…it could be Witch Factor disharmony. Sloth, Greed, and two others. No. Three. That is concerning,” the Sin Archbishop continued to mumble to himself.

Anastasia blinked. Her brain felt like it was dying and her body was drained of energy. So all she could say was a simple, “What?”

Petelguese turned his attention to Anastasia once more, looking oddly embarrassed, “A-ah, my apologies. Where are my manners,” he then dropped Rem’s body carefully onto the ground before walking over to Anastasia bowing slightly, “Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti. Archbishop of the Witch Cult, representing the Moderate faction.”

Anastasia was stunned, “…”

He lifted his head and smiled, “But you can call me Geuse.”

Please give her some love!

Chapter 49: Revelations in ______

Summary:

Anastasia learns more than she bargained for...

Chapter Text

“Though I guess Moderate wasn’t our technical title. We were workshopping what our official position was, but over the years, that was what we were called. It was more of a derogatory statement as odd as that might be. If I could explain just a tad about that, many of the Witch Cult found our ‘moderate’ stances to be a bunch of wishy-washy nonsense. That we were cowards for not taking a stance. Which is also a load of nonsense as Flugel-sama was the type to think of all situations and all perspectives. It is not a coward’s way to simply believe that the best choices are the result of compromise rather than stalwart stubbornness. Though I do always recommend one should stand up for what they believe is right, it isn’t exactly as straightforward as one would like to think,” Petelgeuse rambled on in front of Anastasia who simply stared at him, eyes nearly bulging out. Geuse noticed and waved his hands in the air with the awkwardness of a substitute teacher, “A-ah, apologies. I have a habit of talking endlessly. A force of habit from Sloth’s influence. You will be pleased to know that its corruptive nature does not linger after death, mainly due to my soul not being present. Though even then, my soul would most likely be cleansed once it passes through Od Laguna, becoming pure and unstained by the Witch Factor. Though on the other hand, that soul would not technically be me which defeats the point entirely-“

“What are you?” Anastasia interrupted, still staring at Geuse. “I-I don’t, what? I. What?” For once in Anastasia’s whole time here, she did not have a single shred of understanding for this situation. All she could do was blink at the apparition in front of her, a phantom from the past that should not be speaking with self-awareness akin to a cognizant person.

“Oh. Oh! I see what is wrong, how rude of me. This situation must be quite unnerving for you, given that I was currently in the middle of…killing an innocent woman in cold-blood. Oh dear, I am so sorry!” Geuse dropped Rem’s corpse on the floor. He then panicked as her body limped unceremoniously on the floor. He stared at her for a few seconds, awkwardly turning his head towards Anastasia multiple times before poking Rem with one of his Unseen Hands, “Uh… are you alright, Miss Rem?”

Anastasia could hear a faint gurgle coming from Rem’s mouth. For once, she was happy to see the poor maid alive. Though the bewildering situation hasn’t really made any sense yet, her mind was beginning to recuperate. Unlike a certain someone who was still yelling right behind her, “I’LL KILL YOU! I’LL KILL YOU, I’LL KILL YOU, I’LL KILL YOU!”

That would be a rational reaction in any other situation but given how the Archbishop was acting like he was crying over accidentally kicking his puppy, Subaru’s reaction felt a bit off. Though Anastasia could understand that at least, the poor boy was catatonic for days and the last vestiges of his conscious mind had to see his dear friend and potential lover get thrown around and nearly killed like a sack of tatoes. Her instincts would normally point her to calming him down but given what was currently happening in front of her, her current mindset is troubled by the faint idea that all of this is an illusion. How else would that explain a dead Archbishop coming back to life?

“Are you real?” Anastasia asked, her mind scrambling for all the questions she had no answer to, “How are you talking to me like this? How are you even here? Where am I? What is my purpose here?! Is this actually Subaru or is this some illusion of him?! How did I even get here in the first place?! Why are you only speaking to me now?! What is going on-“

“Please calm yourself Miss Anastasia,” Geuse double checked that Rem was breathing before walking over to Anastasia, trying his best to seem harmless. It wasn’t helping that Subaru was still screaming in the background, he grimaced with each glance towards the boy’s direction, “This isn’t the place for a conversation.” He looked down at the thread connecting to his heart from both Anastasia and Subaru. His hands gripped the thread that connected him to Anastasia while two of his Unseen Hands tightened their grasp over the connections of both Anastasia and Geuse to Subaru. Anastasia watched as the scene changed, rapidly moving forward the chain of events. She saw Rem revive herself, saving Subaru from his imprisonment. She saw him carry the now dead Rem out of the cave and towards the Mathers Mansion. She saw the cold creep in, the monster burst out, the world slowly turning to ice and snow.

And then Subaru died again.

--------------------------------

“Oh Puck, what have you done to yourself? Emilia-sama would never want this from you. From anyone. What kind of madness did Echidna inflict upon you to take on such a burden?” Geuse muttered to himself as the world reset to Lugunica’s capital city once more. Subaru was no longer catatonic, standing in front of Kadomon’s stand.

Anastasia took a mental note of that, as well as another mental note to never let that spirit ever see the light of day again. She did not care what Subaru would say, that rat needs to either die or be restrained in some capacity. Calm down. Fuck calming down. Fuck all of this. Fuck this whole dream. She wants out. She doesn’t want this anymore. She wants-

“Lady Anastasia, are you alright-“

“What are you?” Anastasia cut him off, turning to him as they stood meters away from Subaru and the rest. “You are the Archbishop of Sloth, are you not? How are you here, talking to me, as if you aren’t dead? Answer my questions.”

Geuse stared at her. His face was gaunt, eyes sunken, looking like a corpse that doesn’t know it has been revived from the grave. But there was some life renewed in him. He looked better than before. His body looked like it was slowly shifting, becoming something different. Younger. Kinder. It was strange. After some time, he finally spoke, “I am Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti, as you already know, and I should be dead. However, my personality lives on within the Sloth Witch Factor.”

Anastasia thought for a moment before responding, “Beatrice mentioned once how Witch Factors could be ‘alive’, but I didn’t know it copies your personality.”

Geuse shook his head, “Not exactly a copy. An imprint. Witch Factor’s have been theorized to be living, malleable, entities as you said. But that is far from the truth. To identify them as alive would be wrong. They do not breathe. They do not think. They do not have a conscious mind. But they do react. They react to emotional stimuli and grow stronger from feeding. This in turn, leads to the opening of one’s Authority.”

“Like a parasite,” Anastasia’s mind raced, “A non-living parasite that only knows how to do two things: feed and activate an Authority. These are connected and so if you feed it more, the Authority grows.”

Geuse smiled, “Right you are, Lady Anastasia. The Witch Factor acts as a sort of key, the emotions are the energy, and the Authority is similar to a door. Opening the door allows greater versatility and width of the Authority’s influence over Od Laguna’s domain. However, the cost of feeding the Witch Factor is nothing to scoff at. Your emotions are not able to be simply siphoned from your mind. There needs to be a catalyst, an anchor that allows the emotions to manifest as energy for the Witch Factor to draw upon.”

Anastasia understood what he was implying, “The Od.”

“Exactly. The Witch Factor connects to our soul through the Od and gathers the emotions of the user. However, the process isn’t efficient, the Witch Factor cannot specifically take only the emotions of the user, it must take everything. Personality, memories, habits. All of which are absorbed and stored within the Witch Factor’s database.”

“So, you’re the remnants of the previous user. The Sloth Archbishop. But wait, if it takes on everything doesn’t that mean Subaru’s personality is also within you?” Anastasia glanced at Subaru who was walking towards the Karsten Mansion with a fierce expression.

Geuse nodded, “Yes. Subaru-sama’s information is also stored inside me. Technically, I can draw upon his memories and personality, but they are quite fragmented. His use of Invisible Providence is rare and as a result, his personality has not taken root within Sloth. I am more likely to remember certain aspects of his life than I can ever replicate his mannerisms. Given that I, Geuse, was the possessor of Sloth for nearly one hundred years, my ego takes precedence. Which is why I am able to speak to you. I am not Geuse. But I am also Geuse. If that makes sense.”

Anastasia processed that information, “It does.” As insane as this all is, it does explain the insanity of the situation a bit. She looked down at the thread that wove between her hands and into her heart. It was still glowing strong. She frowned. I don’t know how long this will last. I need information. The more I can learn, the better I can make use of this situation. Better make the seconds count. And I know just what I need to ask first. “You mentioned Authorities are like a door. What do you mean by that? And do I have an Authority?”

Geuse looked her over, his eyes scanning her body quickly before shaking his head, “To answer your second question, you do not have an Authority. Your soul shows no sign of corruption, nor do you hold any of the telltale signs of Witch Factor influence.”

“That being?” Anastasia raised an eyebrow.

“The miasma. A byproduct of energy leaking from the open ‘doors’ of your soul. The more you use your Authority, the more the soul leaks such waste out. Think of it as similar to the heat cast off from metias as they convert mana into mundane utility. The Authority acts as a gateway for your soul to manipulate the world, or more accurately Od Laguna, to your will. As a result of that interaction, your soul leaks corrupted mana from the stains you inflict upon both your soul and the world around you.”

“The door. You keep talking about a door.”

Geuse thought for a moment, he noticed their environment shifted to the Karsten Mansion. He watched as Subaru and Rem entered through the gates. He pointed towards the front door, “Imagine that the mansion over there holds within it, the passageway to Od Laguna.” He then pointed to the guard opening the front entrance for Subaru and Rem, “That guard holds the key, or the Witch Factor, that can open a door to Od Laguna. But the key cannot open a door by itself. It needs someone to use it. It needs a human. It needs a soul.”

“But why a soul? I understand that the Witch Factor is immobile and thus needs a host but how does any of that allow it to passage to Od Laguna, and why would it even want to go after Od Laguna in the first place? It feeds off emotion, right? Then it should…it should…” Anastasia realized her mistake, her eyes widening as she turned to Geuse, “I misunderstood, didn’t I? It doesn’t feed off emotion.”

Geuse smiled and slowly shook his head.

Anastasia paused as the revelation took hold, she continued rambling, “All souls are processed by Od Laguna. That means there must be an innate connection that guides the soul to Od Laguna. The soul…isn’t just the holder of the key. It’s also a literal gateway to Od Laguna. But the only reason the Witch Factor would do such a thing, would be to-“

“Feed off of Od Laguna. Yes,” Geuse finished for her, his expression somber, “Witch Factors are not parasites for our souls and emotions. They use the emotions and energy to power the opening of doorways between our souls and Od Laguna. They are parasites of this World’s very soul. Wishing to feast upon it through manipulation of its laws and doctrines.”

“That-“Anastasia stuttered, her brain comprehending the magnitude of such information, “That is insane! So you’re telling they’re natural enemies?”

“That is the theory. Unfortunately it is unknown how Witch Factors were created, nor why they have such a unique connection with certain compatible people. The relationship between the Witch Factor and the user is mutually beneficial. In return for the Witch Factor being given free reign over Od Laguna, the user is allowed to rewrite the world’s laws through this connection. Molding Od Laguna’s mana to their will and subsequently changing how reality works to their soul’s choosing. This is why an Authorities often manifest based on the personality of the user. It is an extension of their very soul.”

Anastasia’s mind was able to make even further conclusions with such information. “Wait…if you’re here and you are technically a manifestation of the Sloth Witch Factor. Does that mean I’m…inside Subaru? His Od?”

Geuse blinked, “Subaru-sama’s memories were quite right about you. You are brilliant. The fact that you were able to process all that information without much time, and infer even further, is applause worthy.”

“Answer my question,” Anastasia would normally backpack off such praise, but time was ticking and her anxiety was spiking.

Geuse flinched at the blunt response and quickly spoke to rectify his faux pas, “Y-yes, this is his Od. Or perhaps more accurately, it is the cradle of memories of which his Od carries. It is a crude copy of the Corridor of Memories that Od Laguna harbors, acting as a makeshift area where memories reside. Usually, this area is a dark expanse that holds Subaru-sama’s various memories, the various Witch Factor’s he carries, and a connection to his soul. A sort of…shadow garden.”

“So that is what you meant when you said ‘the inner Od should not be this close to reality,’” Anastasia watched as their environment shifted and now, they were within Crusch’s office. Subaru was currently having an argument with Crusch’s camp, trying to convince them to assist in an impending Witch Cult invasion. “So why is it different? An Authority?”

Geuse watched in silence, his eyes dancing with pity at Subaru’s increasing frustration at the situation. He then realized Anastasia was waiting for a response, “Yes. Subaru-sama’s Od has changed. Its laws rewritten. But not by just one Authority, several actually.” He lifted the thread between them that guided to Subaru’s chest. Anastasia now realized that Subaru should be noticing their presence, given that the thread should be revealing them to him. Why not this time? Geuse seemed to guess her question as he answered without prompt, “The Subaru-sama before you is a manifestation of the Greed Witch Factor’s imprint of Natsuki Subaru. I am currently using Sloth to prevent its connection to us so that we can have some privacy.”

“I thought your Authority could only crush people with invisible hands,” Anastasia remembered Subaru explaining his fight with Sloth. This power seemed more versatile than just extra appendages.

Geuse chuckled, “In theory, that is its base utility. However, Sloth has more applications when you truly understand it. My soul was incompatible with the Witch Factor and was unable to fully use its arsenal. My imprint does not have such limitations. As a result, I can bend reality in greater ways. My Unseen Hands can not only grab matter and bend it to my will, it can also grasp the fabrics of reality. For example,” Geuse stopped talking as multiple Unseen Hands sprouted out of his back, one holding onto Anastasia’s torso, while the rest gripped the air. For a second, it appeared as if Guese had somehow been able to grip nothing, folding reality slightly with his hands. And then…nothing.

Nothing was happening anymore. Anastasia looked around as everyone stood motionless. The memory had essentially paused with Geuse’s Authority. The hands stalling any forward movement from the rest of the world, even preventing the Greed Witch Factor from moving. Anastasia did a double take when she looked again at Subaru. Why was he holding a spoon like he was about to stab someone?

I…questions for later. Not important. Whatever this world does, it forwards the information into my brain eventually, so I’ll just review why Subaru is planning on murdering someone with a spoon later.

Anastasia instead turned her attention to Geuse, “So you can stop time?”

“I can put the world on hold,” Geuse corrected her. Anastasia didn’t understand why that was any different but given how Authorities were completely insane, there was most likely some convoluted reason for it. “Not only that, but I can also interact with other aspects. Mental, emotional, and spiritual. My only limits are my creativity.”

“I see,” as Anastasia spoke, Geuse let his Unseen Hands release the world around them, continuing the weird confrontation between Subaru and the Crusch Camp. “So that isn’t my Subaru,” her eyes lingered on Subaru’s angry expression. Her heart felt like it was breaking from the truth.

Geuse put his hand on her shoulder, “Yes and no. It is him. His compatibility with the Witch Factor is so strong, that his personality even supersedes the previous user. Which is astounding given what I know of Regulus Corneas. Nevertheless, this is a version of him whose only goal is to accomplish their one desire: their greed. Just like me, he exists to further Greed’s goals. So, believe me when I say that this Subaru’s actions are genuine. His emotions are genuine. His love…is genuine.”

“…”

“…His love for you, is as deep as his bottomless greed.”

“How do you now?” Anastasia’s lip wavered.

“Because I can feel it through the connection,” Geuse held up the thread with one of his Unseen Hands, “This manifestation of an Authority. I have never seen one so purely crafted with such love and devotion before. It was made out of pure adoration. Out of boundless affection. Loyal only to you. His desire stems from an intense need to be understood, to not be alone within this dark, frightful world of his. But it blossomed into a yearning that eclipses its original purpose. He does not want to be understood by just anyone. He wants to be understood by you,” Geuse pointed to Anastasia’s chest, “This thread burns brightest and is strongest when it connects from him to you. His Greed is solely directed towards you. Everything about you, he yearns for. Your body, your mind, your love, your care, your life. Such a love like this…I have only seen from one other person.”

“I…” Anastasia didn’t know how to respond. How could she respond? She knew he loved her beyond her wildest dreams. But could she give him back just as much? She loved him. But was her love enough?”

Geuse saw her hesitation and gripped her shoulder in support, “When such diligence is given to you, expressed with such raw emotion, it is only natural to respond in kind. Anastasia-sama…what is it that you want?”

What she wants? It was obvious what she wants.

She wants Subaru. More than anything else in the entire world, barring her camp. She wants him. He is. He is the sun that peers over the horizon.
