He is the stars that light up this dark canvas of a world. He is the voice that brings mirth and joy into her heart. He is the rain that washes away all of her sadness and pain. He is the storm that brings both fear and excitement into her life. He is the soft morning that greets her at dawn. He is the soft shimmering hope that never dwindles despite the odds. He is the warmth of an embrace that never yields and always holds true. He is salt and pepper that greets her tongue and fills her with joy. He is the smile that shines brightest to her and only her. He is the shadow that always follows her every step. He is the fool who keeps her curious and the genius who keeps her guessing. He is the quiet cacophony of a midday nap amongst the trees and birds. He is the loud silence of a midnight nightmare amongst the stars and bats. He is the man who always stands, who never bends, who always carries the weight of the world on his shoulders. He is the boy who grieves for the innocent, cries with every failure, and bears the sins of the world on his back. He is everything to her.

He is her love, her other half, her soulmate. He is Natsuki Subaru and Anastasia Hoshin is his.

…But is he mine?

Anastasia does not know. And she does not dare to ask. And until she knows for certain. Until she knows that he is hers, forevermore, she cannot state her truest desire. No. She cannot. She does not deserve it. She did not pay the cost in full. The negotiation must be equal and fair, as it rightfully should. So, until she pays her debts, and they stand on equal ground, all she can say is,

“…I want to go on a date with my husband. I want to go home.”

Geuse gave her a soft somber look before looking forward, watching Subaru angrily barge out of the room with Rem in tow, “Then you shall have it.”

“How? I don’t even know how or why I am here, much less a method to leave this place,” Anastasia pulled Geuse’s hand gently off her shoulder and glanced at him from the side.

Geuse gave her a reassuring smile, “Then you will be happy to know that you are in the presence of someone who was not only Beatrice-sama’s ethic’s teacher, but also the Witch of Greed’s research partner. I had helped her extensively with her Witch Factor research, in service of Flugel-sama’s will. Paired with Sloth’s power, I believe I am fully capable of assisting you.”

“Again, how?” Anastasia wanted to hold hope, but her time here has slowly deteriorated her will. She feels like she is one step away from dropping into the abyss and she will not cling to a vague hope that will only shatter whatever willpower remained in her grasp.

Geuese spoke with a soft tone, “You mentioned not knowing how you entered Subaru-sama’s Od, correct?” Anastasia nodded, “Do you mean you do not know or cannot recall?”

“The latter. It feels like my head wants to crack open every time I try.”

“Your mind must be repressing the information,” Geuse smiled, “Then it is simple. The reason you are here is because your soul somehow entered his Od through a collaborative effect of multiple Authorities and Witch Factors colliding. If I can gain access to your memories, I can comb through that repressed region and take out the restrictions. This will allow us further insight into what Witch Factors were involved, and we can then find and target them within Subaru’s Od.”

“So, you are essentially saying we go on a Witch Factor scavenger hunt?” Anastasia asked, disbelief seeping into her tone.

Geuse’s smile turned sheepish, “As crude as that sounds, yes. It would be like meeting me. We would just have to follow the memories and eventually come upon the manifestations of the other Witch Factors that have taken root as memories in his mindscape. Once we gathered the others, we would just have to recreate the exact parameters that shunted you into this world and hopefully reverse the process in your favor.”

It wasn’t exactly a plan but more of a ‘hope for the best’ type of situation. There was no guarantee that going into her memories would reveal exactly what they needed. Nor was there any guarantee that finding the other Witch Factors would even lead to the solution. But what other choice did she have? So, all Anastasia could say was, “Let’s do it. What do I need to do for you to go into my memories?”

“I will need to enter your soul and adapt to your Od. This will take some time, and I will most likely have to stay dormant within you until I am done processing your soul. In the meantime, I would recommend you continue following Subaru-sama’s memories. You may be able to find the other Witch Factors before I finish my tasks.”

“Is that a good idea?” Anastasia couldn’t help but be doubtful, “What are the chances they will be as friendly as you?”

“If they were absorbed by Subaru-sama, then they will most likely be pacified by his soul. Subaru-sama is…special. I am sure that no matter what, you are safest in his Od,” Geuse was oddly confident of such a fact. Anastasia didn’t know why he had such faith, but she’ll question him later before she leaves.

“…Okay, let’s do it then,” Anastasia braced herself as she watched Geuse morph inward, becoming smaller and smaller until he was a writhing mass of shadows which then burst towards her and enter her chest. It felt disgusting for just a second before her body settled into normalcy. Anastasia sighed to herself as she finally started paying attention to what was happening to Subaru. Let’s hope the worst is behind us. At least until Priestella.

“—I may not look it, but I am a surprisingly avid reader,” said a very familiar and irritating voice.

Anastasia blinked before pinching her nose bridge, “Oh Od, please not her.”

Chapter 50: No Gambling in ______

Summary:

Anastasia's stay with Lotus begins well...

Notes:

Sorry for the delay! AO3 was down during all of my free time to upload, so it is only going up on AO3 now. Within Two Months will still update same time.

Anyways, enjoy!

Chapter Text

“…I raise,” Anastasia spoke confidently.

Subaru didn’t know what he was expecting when Anastasia left her life in the Slums for a calmer life within the abode of a courtesan. His bias against her aside, which did make him think of the worst possibilities, he thought there would be more formalities. Basics in etiquette, learning how to serve patrons, and studies on business management. From Subaru’s observations, Lotus seemed to be grooming Anastasia into her possible successor, it would be the only possibility that would make sense given her constant desire to teach the little girl lessons in both negotiation but also practical applications of social dynamics.

He just didn’t realize poker existed here.

“Call,” Lotus said in a nonchalant voice. Her tone and body posture was aligned, her body lying on the floor with eyes fluttering on the cusp of sleep. She looked like she was barely paying attention to the game, “Last card.” The fifth card on the river was an ace of clubs. There was a king, a five, a two, and a ten. Subaru’s knowledge of the game was limited but Anastasia’s king and a four meant she had one of the highest pairs up until now. If it was him, he would probably keep raising just to increase pressure. Anastasia, however, was looking quite anxious, here yes glancing back and forth between her cards, to Lotus, and back to the board.

Anastasia thought for a few minutes before saying, “I check.”

“I check as well. Shall we show our hands?” Lotus didn’t wait for a reply, putting her cards down neatly, revealing an ace and a three. Any confidence Anastasia had, shattered as her eyes locked onto that ace, making her pair of kings moot. She dropped her cards on the floor and pouted as Lotus chuckled and pulled her winnings.

“This game is dumb, why did you even keep going?  You didn’t even have a pair until the end!” Anastasia grumbled.

Lotus laughed harder, “I shall tell you why once the game is finished. You still have money. We will continue until you admit defeat or when you have nothing. Or do you wish to surrender now?”

Anastasia glared, “Nope. Let’s go. I’m going to get my money back.” Lotus enjoyed Anastasia’s grit and determination, having a servant shuffle the deck as she drank from her glass. Anastasia continued to grumble as she nibbled on some snacks placed nearby.

Subaru wanted to pick little Anastasia up and squeeze her before twirling her around until she either threw up or bit him. Her chubby cheeks pouting was picturesque bliss, a soulful dose of pure sweetness that he couldn’t help but gush over. Anastasia was still slightly underweight, but Lotus’s constant supply of food and sweets have fattened her up a considerable amount. She wasn’t a bag of flesh and bones but was now reminiscent of a healthy child. It brought him to near tears, and it’s only been a couple months since Anastasia had moved into her new home.

-----------------------------

Her first days were filled with suspicion, her eyes always drifting behind her and being wary of every shadow as they passed the halls of the luxurious home of Lotus. Servants were abundant, each one with that titular flower marked on some part of their clothes or body, passing by without even glancing at the little girl roaming around without supervision. That was another odd point. Lotus trusted Anastasia way too much. She practically had free reign over the whole area, with no surveillance or guardians to be found if Lotus was busy with her duties at the brothel. Anastasia could have easily stolen any of the various goods, food, or knickknacks scattered about with ease. Yet she didn’t, whether out of fear or some sense of morality, Subaru had no idea.

When Anastasia slept on a bed for the first time, a real one that wasn’t just bits of trash or assorted clothing, her reaction stunned him. Subaru remembered it clearly. The little girl had checked the place out thoroughly, afraid there was something wrong with her surroundings or someone might have been hiding in the shadows. It broke his heart how paranoid she was. It broke his heart again when she laid down on the soft pillow and bedding and couldn’t feel comfortable no matter how much she tried, thrashing about for nearly an hour. And his whole heart and soul shattered when she pulled up the blanket over her, and her first words were a soft, “So warm…”

Anastasia could barely hold her tears in that day. Subaru couldn’t.

But old habits die hard. Once the one-month period passed by, Anastasia gathered enough courage to sneak into the kitchen in the dead of night. She was hungry, forgetting to ask any of the servants—which was a difficult thing to adjust to initially—before they all went to their resting quarters. Her stomach grumbling, she tip toed through the halls, keeping her ears open to even the slightest movement or sound. She managed to snag a few pieces of meat and a bundle of fruits before running as quietly as possible back to her room. Anastasia was fairly sure she had not been discovered. Only for her to arrive at her bed the next night, a plate full of snacks by her bed and a note saying, “You do not need to be so cautious. You are allowed to take whatever you want from the kitchen.”

He remembered Anastasia staring at that note for several minutes.

Weeks passed. Anastasia got used to living in the estate, finding herself getting more comfortable and keeping her guard down as she no longer checked every corner for a possible threat. In contrast, Subaru was slowly becoming more suspicious of everything. “None of this makes sense. All the servants are acting so…weird,” Subaru mumbled to himself as he saw Anastasia walk to the library, a skip in her step that made his heart nearly explode from how cute it looked.

He watched as a man and a woman, both with flowers adorning their arms, walked past the little girl, not even blinking at her presence. Subaru took a closer look at them and frowned, “They definitely don’t act like normal people,” their eyes were slightly glazed over, “Hell, they barely react to Ana’s presence besides when she gets their attention,” he looked at their bodies for any signs of abuse or neglect. But no, nothing obvious. No scratches, scars, or anything. The only thing he could notice was they were slightly sweaty and some of their movements looked off but that could be attributed to working and moving so much than anything concerning.

Subaru kept analyzing their bodies but was frustrated by his lack of perception. He wasn’t good at this stuff. This was Anastasia’s domain. She could easily take their postures, their weird actions, and any small details that stuck out and make an incredible hypothesis of what was going wrong. She was amazing like that. Easily remembering and noticing details he could never bother with. Subaru scratched his head in annoyance as the scene shifted and he was now in the library, watching Anastasia hum to herself as she climbed on stacks of books to reach up towards the higher bookshelves.

“I just wish I could know what you’re thinking,” Subaru whispered to himself. Another problem he was facing was his lack of understanding of this version of Anastasia. Throughout the multiple years of watching Anastasia’s early life, he couldn’t really say that this Anastasia was either completely foreign or familiar. Her behavior was similar to his Anastasia at times but there were some parts that felt so distinctly different that she felt like an entirely different person. Does he even know Anastasia that well to begin with? They’ve only known each other for several months, not including loop time. Perhaps it was the fact that he couldn’t just corroborate the image of this hyena with the mild-mannered and teasing merchant he knew her as. If anything, her early life and attitude reminded Subaru of Felt. That hunger to survive and that desire to do whatever it took to get ahead was reminiscent of that other citizen of the slums.

I’m surprised they never talked with each other that much. From what I can recall, she seemed closer to Priscilla or Crusch than Felt. Hell, I think she sent more letters and had more tea parties with Emilia. Which must have been awkward given the whole…Subaru felt shivers in his spine. Next time he has the chance, he is having an actual talk with Julius. They already settled their differences and there were no more grudges to be found—at least on Subaru’s side—so all that was needed was a polite discussion about finally putting that duel behind them. And to also inform Julius that he was marrying his candidate. And for his blessing. And possibly begging Julius not to challenge him to another duel for those previous two statements.

Subaru then took a moment to think as Anastasia wobbled with the seven books she was barely keeping in her small arms. He kept his eyes locked onto her, worried she would fall over. She then stopped shaking and slowly stepped down, maneuvering through the staircase of books she made. She calmed down once her feet reached solid flooring. Smiling triumphantly, she walked forward to the nearby chairs. Before immediately tripping and dropping all her books. Anastasia sniffled but wiped her tears quickly before gathering the books all at once and trying again, this time more carefully. Subaru’s body shook. He finally made a decision.

Subaru was ready to kill Russel Fellow for his cellphone.

It was no longer an if, more of a when. He needed it back. If his daughter or son was as cute as this in the future, he needed evidence to remember forever. Lugunica will survive without one man. He could not survive without permanent memorabilia of his adorable future family. The only problem was finding a way to restore the battery but if he still had Roswaal on his side, he could probably convince him to figure out a way to do it. Maybe he’ll sweeten the deal and say that Roswaal could also take pictures of Echidna’s dead body. Subaru paused his thinking for a moment, I know she wouldn’t probably mind but that whole scenario sounds very creepy to me out of context. Selling pictures of some dead woman’s corpse to her weird disciple who lives forever isn’t something anyone should say with a sane mind.

Subaru then blinked. And immediately started screaming into his hands. Why am I even thinking these things?! Have I gone insane?! No of course he has. Subaru knew this. He had gone insane ever since he left that hell loop. You don’t go through several years of trauma and deaths just to come out normal. No one could. And he isn’t that special. Not like her. Not like Beatrice. Or Halibel. Or Zarestia. Or Emilia. Rem. Garfiel. Ram. Otto. He was just a normal guy way over his head. Not some hero or special guy who can solve everything. An idiot who can only slam his head into every obstacle until it either breaks or he gets lucky. Wasn’t that how he got through every single problem? Luck. He got lucky back during that whole Bowel Hunter fiasco when Reinhard came in clutch and saved everyone. The whole White Whale hunt and Petelgeuse fight was barely his win. If Julius or the other weren’t there, he couldn’t have accomplished anything. Same with Sanctuary, Priestella, Banan. Subaru wasn’t the main character of this story; he was just some idiot who kept interfering with the world because he’s too stubborn to let things be.

Subaru sighed as he walked over and sat at the table next to Anastasia. She was happily reading more of Hoshin’s tales, a whole collection of hundreds of thousands of his memoirs and tales were scattered throughout this whole place. Subaru couldn’t help but smile as her face shifted from excitement to dread to excitement again at each passing plot twist. This is such a new side to you. You usually don’t show such emotions easily. Always trying to seem affable or happy or in control. Well, at least until I’m involved. I never expected you to act like that at the Royal Capital. You looked…awful back then.

He remembered those days. Subaru was an absolute mess, but Anastasia was far worse, at least in his eyes. She was always on the cusp of a nervous breakdown but hid it behind so many layers of repression that you could hardly tell. She acted so different back then, especially when you compared her to Priestella or back when they met during the beginning of the Royal Selection. He could never imagine that same Anastasia would save him at his most vulnerable, keep him company during the night, chastise and berate him openly with so much emotion, and swear at the top of her lungs like a dirty-mouthed sailor.

Subaru couldn’t help but laugh at those memories, despite the pain he felt in his heart. He rested his head between his arms, positioning himself to watch Anastasia greedily read through more and more literature.  He couldn’t help the thoughts that continued to flood his mind. Ideas that began festering in his skull ever since he saw Anastasia’s soul break for the first time. I did this to you. This was my fault. I made you this way. You could have been living a normal life, away from danger. Away from me. You could have made a normal company, gathered enough money to return to Lugunica, bought your old company, and reinsert yourself into the lives of your family. You could be happy. You could have fallen in love with Julius. He would have treated you better than me. Anyone could have.

Such a stupid thing. If Anastasia was here, she would yell at him for having such thoughts. Why worry about possibilities when the future was what matters? But in this weird dimension, where he was stuck watching her past, he couldn’t help but think that he had dragged Anastasia into a worse hell than even her worst life experiences. Starvation, survival of the fittest, slavery. Horrifying to deal with as a child. But has Subaru given Anastasia a better life, if at all? No.

His first meeting with her made Anastasia implicit in helping an escaped convict run away. Their next few days involved barely sleeping while getting attacked by vicious bandits who killed them several times. Then when they got to Banan, they were killed by some mentally ill Oni who was targeting Subaru for his smell. And then, Anastasia was drained of all her life energy and forced to die over and over again because of the Witch Cult’s schemes. None of these situations would have happened if Subaru had simply ignored Anastasia’s presence at the Capital. He should have just left her to go about her life. Succeed. And go home. He should have just focused on escaping, hunting down Gluttony, and settle all of this without anyone else getting hurt.

Subaru tucked his head deeper into his arms. A thought occurred to him. The future that could have been if he simply ignored Anastasia and continued his plans. “I would have probably made it out of the city one way or the other. Maybe a loop or two more. Then all I needed to do was track down a carriage and an Earth Dragon. It would take some time, but I could probably trial and error my way into finding Gluttony’s location. Look for clues. It might have taken years but finding them wouldn’t have been too bad. Then all it would take would be me finding someone to help me kill them or loop spamming until they die. Not the most efficient plan but it would have worked eventually,” Subaru mumbled to himself.

Then the names and memories of people would finally be released. Anastasia would have her name back and be able to be a bit happier, given he expected her to have already reintegrated herself into their lives at that point. It would just be a pleasant surprise for her. Rem would be awake. All the Gluttony victims would reunite with their families. And Subaru…

Subaru thought to himself, And I would probably be a nobody again.

Or like he always was. Several years of hunting Gluttony would mean the Royal Selection would have finished. Emilia or Felt or Priscilla would have taken the lead and become the new Queen. He hoped Emilia would still win, even though it hurt him that his absence wouldn’t make a difference. But at least everyone would be happy. He would have his name back but would returning do any good? Selfishly, he could try worming his way back into their hearts and lives. But it would have been so long. So much time would have passed. Everyone would have moved on and Subaru’s impact on them would simply be too small for them to care. Sure, they would be nice and probably take pity on him, give him a nice welcome back and perhaps some help so that he can live like a normal person again.

But they didn’t owe him anything. This wasn’t his job anymore. He wouldn’t be a knight anymore. He would just be Natsuki Subaru again. And maybe that was fine. What good was being a hero or a knight? His short tenure as either was plagued with mistakes and suffering. Constantly dragging other people into his muck and problems. It would suck but he would simply have to move on. Watch his friends live prosperous lives from afar. Watch Anastasia from afar. Live her life. Be happy. Without…him.

Subaru heard a sniffle.

He lifted his head and watched Anastasia wipe her tears away, most likely on some harrowing tale of Hoshin fighting for survival while detailing his mourning of several of his dead companions. Anastasia was always such an empathetic person. Always caring for people. Always wanting to help them even if they didn’t deserve it. Always trying to act like she wasn’t kind at all. Someone who deserves so much, who always wants so much, can’t help but give a little to every person she comes across, even if they don’t appreciate it.

I know it’s selfish. I know in such circumstances, you would be much happier. I know I am a rotten monster of a person who does not deserve you. But I would rather throw away all those futures, all those possibilities, and settle on this one timeline, where we are together. I hate that I bring you so much harm and I hate that I can’t help but want to stay with you despite that. You deserve so much more than me. Yet, I would drag you down into Hell with me, just so that I can be by your side. I’m a fool. A moron. An idiot. But if I could ask for one thing. Just one thing.

He reached over to Anastasia. He hesitated. He placed his hand on the table and sighed, I just want the chance to make you happy. Like all the times you made me.

He just needed to understand her more. See what these memories hold for him and what he could do with them. Maybe he can figure out how to punt Gluttony out of Anastasia once he gets to the point where they separated. Until then, he’ll continue watching and learning. He’ll try to. He was always good at that, at least.

--------------------------

“And you lose again,” Lotus’s words made Anastasia’s eye twitch, “So sorry.”

“I hate this game,” Anastasia folded her arms, annoyed that she lost all her money within three matches, “I don’t even see what the point of this is. It isn’t like there is anything to learn from pure luck.”

Lotus snapped her fingers and had her servants gather the cards and chips together. She hummed to herself before speaking, “Do you really think luck is something uncontrollable?”

“I mean, it’s luck,” Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “You’re either unlucky or lucky.”

“Not true. If you regard all luck as simply bad or good, you end up missing the opportunities that lay before you,” Lotus held out her hand and stopped the servant before he could clean up the river. She pointed at the five cards in front of them, “Take this for instance. Three, two, four, seven, nine. There is a possible straight here for either of us if we have the correct cards.”

“But I didn’t have it. I had a king and a jack. I was hoping you didn’t have any high cards or that another one would come and I would get a pair.”

Lotus smiled, “And I already had a pair of aces. I have essentially won since the beginning.”

“Which is why you raised so much since the start.”

“And you thought I was lying, or more accurately, I was bluffing,” Lotus’s words made Anastasia click her tongue.

“You already won since the beginning. I should have just given up from the start. But I didn’t know that, so I lost. You had a better hand, which makes it all luck.”
Lotus blinked, “And yet, there were ways this could have gone either way. Look at your king and jack. They are both red. The four and seven were also red. You had a possible flush on your hands if there was a third red.”

“But I didn’t.”

“But you could have made me think that,” Lotus corrected, “I did not know if you had two reds or two blacks. Or a mix. You could have made me think you had only blacks. The three, two, and nine were black. If you raised higher than me instead of calling the whole time, you would have put pressure on me.”

“But that wouldn’t have won me the game.”

“It would have made me scared. The more pressure I have, the less likely I would want to take risks. Risks are what gives us advantages in negotiation. The more risks someone has, the less likely they are to take a decision. Just like during a business negotiation, it all depends on what each side knows about each other.”

“And that’s why you told me to stop showing what I’m thinking all the time,” Anastasia said.

“Correct. It’s why you should really learn how to speak with a Kararagi accent,” Lotus sighed, “A shame you didn’t naturally gain one. You’ll be seen as an outsider unless you practice it so thoroughly that it sounds natural.”

“What’s so bad about that?”

“For one, it makes you seem less reliable. Kararagi is known for their mercantilism, as such, you gain an advantage by feeling like an authentic merchant. It is the same as smiling during a first impression or showing no fear during a poker game. First impressions matter and, in all negotiation, you must control the flow of information.”

“So then how does that relate to luck? This all feels like stuff you can control that isn’t even related to being lucky,” Anastasia said with irritation.

“Luck is interwoven with information because only those who can see where the jackpot lies, can take advantage of such an opportunity,” Lotus pointed at the first three cards. “Look here. There was an opportunity at the start to also raise big. If you raised higher than I did, I would have either thought you had a straight or a possible flush with blacks.”

“But if I raised higher, I would have went all in. That’s so risky!”

Lotus’s smile became all the more vicious, “And that is what it means to gamble. In both poker and in business, fortune favors the audacious. You cannot hope to win if you do not take the opportunities that allow you the greatest victories. Sure, the smartest plays are to simply drain money from your opponent through small victories. But that does not lead to legends like Hoshin,” that got Anastasia’s attention, who was now listening with greater rapture, “When you see an opportunity that will change your life, you grab it and don’t let go. Even if the risks are blatant, trust your instincts. This is what divides the normal merchants from the second coming of Hoshin.”

“Hm, alright, I think I get it,” Anastasia nodded as the rest of their game was taken away. Lotus motioned her to follow as they stood up. It was dinnertime and the two were to have their weekly meal together. Subaru didn’t understand why it was only one time a week that they ate but Anastasia did not question it, so neither did he. He followed the line of people as they marched down the various hallways. Only for Anastasia to stop for a brief second, looking to a staircase that went deeper into the lower levels of this mansion. For some reason, the staircase unnerved Subaru. Maybe it was just the lone lamp that hanged right at the bottom, illuminating a door that had no sign. Maybe it was the eeriness of just one staircase leading to the basement in this whole entire building. Maybe it was the fact that Subaru never once saw anyone go down there during the day.

Whatever the case, Anastasia’s eyes constantly fixated on it every time they passed by. “Come child, dinner will get cold if your feet are too slow,” Lotus said, already getting farther away. Anastasia winced as she walked away. However, Subaru still stood where she once was. Staring at the staircase.

“Trust my instincts, huh,” Subaru muttered to himself. If his instincts were right, whatever was down there was bad news. He just hoped Anastasia wouldn’t be too traumatized by what’s to come.

 

Chapter 51: I Do Not Belong in ______

Summary:

Subaru doesn't want to be here anymore

Chapter Text

Red-Sun, Blue-Sun, Yellow-Sun, Green-Sun. The seasons passed rapidly, cycling, and with each repetition, Anastasia grew. No longer fettered by her environment, she grew into a proper lady of refined culture. Eating well, her body was no longer skin and bones, finally looking her age. Trained in the arts, educated on various histories, and given etiquette lessons, she had all the requirements to manage Lotus’s facilities without any concern. Though she was never involved in the actual catering of clients, Anastasia was given enough information to understand their daily habits and necessities, allowing her to properly understand the business from an external perspective. She ingratiated herself with several other courtesans, with varying personalities that ranged from mild-mannered to slightly eccentric, though none could match the relationship between Anastasia and Lotus.

“So Little One, have you finally decided on a name?” Lotus inquired. They were having a meal in the dining room. A simple set of poisson and rice with stir fried vegetables.

Anastasia dabbed her mouth with a napkin, her technique with chopsticks had improved in the last few years. “None match the requirements I decided on. I need more time.”

“Well, Little One shall be your moniker for quite a while longer. I do not think you should be so picky­—”

“I am not,” Anastasia placed her chopsticks gently down on the table, “I simply wish ta make sure my choice is worthwhile. It is a name I will carry forever, is it not?”

Lotus waved her hand, “Fine, fine. Just know that you cannot delay the inevitable.”

“May I be excused?” Anastasia moved to leave but was stopped by Lotus’s hand.

“In one moment. I just need you to answer this one question.”

Anastasia paused, raising her eyebrow, “What is it?”

“Have you gone to the basement floor yet?”

Anastasia’s eyes widened slightly, “…No. You specifically mentioned that I am not allowed down there under any circumstances.”

Lotus smiled, “Good girl. You are now given access whenever you wish.”

That made Anastasia have a greater reaction, slightly backstepping, “You,” she paused, not knowing what exactly to say, “Why now?”

“I simply deemed it as the correct time to do so.”

Anastasia waited for Lotus to elaborate. Yet, even as the seconds passed, Lotus was fine with letting the silence persist. Anastasia lacked the will to continue such nonsense, “I see. If that is the case, then I shall leave. Is that fine?”

Lotus’s smile brightened even more, “Wonderful. You may go.” Anastasia did not linger, letting her feet guide her out of the room and down the halls, back to her room. Subaru followed behind her. He watched as her movements were much more graceful than before. Every footstep was precise and dainty compared to the rough paranoia he sensed from before. It was concerning to him how different she was now, like night and day, the rough hyena was slowly morphing into the Anastasia he knew and cared for. The mask she wore, the appearance of a polite Kararagian merchant was becoming forged in front of him. He always wondered if such a mold was crafted by Anastasia’s own perception or through the influence of various environmental factors and years of experience.

Turns out, it was all and also none. He could see semblances of what would eventually become Anastasia’s external persona, but this version was too stiff. Lotus’s teachings were familiar, given how much was repeated to him by Anastasia during his life in Banan. Negotiation, connections, the power of ethos. All necessary for any successful merchant but also for any businesswoman. It did not matter if the work was dirty or not, the rules were consistent: money is power. Lotus knew that and she made sure Anastasia not only embraced it but accepted the tools of the trade. That the river of currency was not filled by coin, but people.

In a morbid sense, slavery in Kararagi is an extension of that cultural mindset. Money is power. People carry money. People are power. If you own or collect people, you are powerful. Subaru didn’t know when it started, but he began to see Kararagi in a more nuanced way. Perhaps it was due to his extended stay in Banan or his perspective through Anastasia’s early years, but he doesn’t see Kararagi as he would previously. If his transmigration into this world began in Kararagi instead of Lugunica, he would have been morally disgusted by the slavery and transactional nature of Kararagi’s very culture. But now, it was less moral disgust, and more of an analytical disgust. Anastasia would probably be proud of his development.

In terms of how he views Banan and Kararagi as a whole, the culture and environment appeared similar to Japan but the attitudes and ideals varied. While in both worlds, hard work is valued, there is an inherent lack of community and authority within Kararagi that is ever-present in Japan. Halibel’s community of shinobi and mercenaries made Banan a very habitable area for both Anastasia and Subaru. But without that, the city was cutthroat. Rent prices, jobs, climbing the ladder. All of it required connections and skillsets that outclassed others. Rather than survival of the fittest, it was more akin to survival of the most adaptable.

It made Subaru appreciate Anastasia even more. In so many ways, her influence on him was what allowed him to survive so well. Her words, actions, lessons. She was his guiding star during those early loops. He wasn’t lying when he said he wanted to be like her. He remembered that conversation they had outside, right around the time they first met Tia. How Anastasia looked so conflicted. He already knew Anastasia was suffering from the effects of Gluttony more than him. He was already used to the idea of people forgetting him. She, however…

I can’t imagine how she must have felt. Her friends, family, everything. Gone. All within just a few moments and all you can do is accept it. Because what else could you do? You can’t scream at your family to remember you. Beg for them. Bargain. I can only imagine how terrified she must have been. Or maybe she was in shock. Or maybe she started thinking about her hyena days. Or maybe…I don’t know.

Subaru didn’t know anything. Why did he ever think he was good at watching and learning? For as much as he memorized about her—her habits, her mannerisms, her appearance—he was absolutely awful at understanding people. Case in point, Subaru didn’t even know that much about her past beside some random snippets here and there. There was too little time for him to ask her about any specific moments. About her childhood. About how she felt during Priestella. About everything. Why? Because Subaru was stupid. He was too busy wallowing in self-pity and she was too busy saving him from such a state. Constantly preventing him from self-harm. Putting him first. Subaru took advantage of that. He made everything about him. Like he always does.

Subaru blinked, shaking his head in disgust. Why am I acting like this? Have I become more insane than before? He was no longer worried for Anastasia’s safety, Lotus showed no sign of malicious intent, which meant there was no reason for him to analyze everything so deeply. With nothing to actively comment on, Subaru became more and more lost in his own thoughts. Unfortunately, he preferred someone else’s. Subaru watched as Anastasia lay on her bed, obviously ruminating over Lotus’s words. He clutched his chest and willed his desires as best he could. He wanted to help her. He wanted to understand her. He wanted Anastasia to understand him! This was his Greed, right?

…Nope. Nothing. Not a single thread of light had appeared and it frustrated Subaru to no end. He knew what his Greed was! He saved Anastasia! He knew how the Authority worked! This should be easy! Why is it not easy?! Why does he fail at everything, over and over and over again?! Does the universe just want him to pound his skull into each wall until it breaks? Is that what this is?! Does he need to die again and again?! Why can’t he talk to her again?! He needs to talk to her. He wants to talk to her. He wants to ask her so many questions. He wants to hear her voice. Not this child version or whatever this memory thing was made of. He wanted his Anastasia. He wanted his wife.

Subaru leaned onto the wall, his back slowly sliding down until he was now sitting on the floor, his hands clutching his hair. He hated everything. This was taking too long. That hell loop was worse but at the very least he had some sense of progress! This was a different type of agony. He couldn’t do anything! All he can do is watch and what good does that do him! He was too stupid. He wasn’t like Anastasia. He can’t find a solution like she does. She was always fixing his problems. And if it wasn’t her, it was Beatrice, Halibel, or Tia who were doing all the heavy lifting. Him? All he had was Return by Death.

Subaru blinked. He looked around the room and saw a pen on Anastasia’s desk. Standing up and sauntering over, he carefully picked it up before ramming it right into his hand without hesitation. There was no puncture or any blood leakage. Subaru couldn’t even feel the pain. He clicked his tongue before throwing the pen away. He whispered to himself in frustration, “I can’t die. I can’t even loop. What good am I now?”

This was all pointless. If he was going to learn about Anastasia’s past, especially the most traumatic parts, he’d rather listen to the source directly. He needed to either get out of here and continue his plan to remove Gluttony, though much more carefully, or figure out a way to remove the bastard from here. He needed to think. He was terrible at thinking, but he had to do something. Think. Think! THINK!

Whatever this place is. If I had to guess, I must be inside Anastasia’s soul. That would be the only possible theory that would make sense. Or…

He needed to go further. From what Subaru could gather, this was most likely some weird simulation of Anastasia’s memories brought about by his Witch Factors. Most likely Greed but there was a good argument for Sloth. He used Invisible Providence to reach into Anastasia’s body and rip out that parasite, only for some strange reaction to occur that shunted him into this odd world. Which could only mean one thing: his Witch Factors all reacted with Gluttony. Gluttony is a memory-based power so there is a possibility that he might not even be in Anastasia’s soul but in some inner part of the Witch Factor.

If that’s the case, wouldn’t that mean all he had to do was cause a ruckus, possibly destroy as much stuff as possible, and kill Gluttony from the inside. It could be a valid strategy. But how to implement it? He’s tried interacting with the world. No matter how much stuff he throws around or breaks, it doesn’t really affect anything. In that case, does he need a special way to start damaging his surroundings? Perhaps the way he entered this situation was the key to exiting it.

Subaru braced himself and reached deep within once more. He breathed in deep before saying aloud, “Invisible Providence!”

…Nothing happened.

“Invisible Providence!” He yelled again.

…Again. Nothing.

“Invisible Providence! Invisible Providence! Invisible! Providence! INVIS! IBLE! PROVI! DENCE!” He continued screaming for several minutes. Subaru gasped for air, panting. He waited, trying to see if his body would finally react and create a shadowy hand for him to manipulate. But no matter how much he screamed or tried, nothing would happen. He had no Return by Death. He had no Invisible Providence. He had no—

“Ops Basiliskos!” He tried to channel his eyes, narrowing and focusing them to no avail. He couldn’t see any lights. Of course that wouldn’t work. Greed was attaching this thread between them. And if that can’t manifest then of course he can’t use its basic functions. It wouldn’t even help him in the slightest compared to his other Authorities. He was stuck. Trapped within this prison of memories with no idea what he is doing and no actual idea what’s going on outside. Are Beatrice, Tia, and Halibel okay? What about their friends and family? Is time linear here in relation to the outside world? He really hoped not.

Goddamnit! I’ve been too narrowminded! There are so many factors and possibilities I haven’t even considered.

Who’s to say this isn’t some elaborate scheme created by Gluttony? An illusion that traps the enemy in endless memories created from someone they’ve captured. Authorities could evolve, given his own experience with Greed. It could be possible his meddling led to Gluttony’s own progression of power. Wait a minute.

Hold on. What was that parasite’s name? Louis Arneb? The two others were Lye Batenkaitos and Roy Alphard. If they are anything like Regulus and Petelguese, they must be associated with constellations. Which means they must be Arneb, the star of Lepus. Baten Kaitos, the star of Cetus. Alphard, the star of Hydra. Lepus, the hare. Cetus, the whale. Hydra, the many-headed serpent.

Subaru blinked. He then screamed even louder than before, throwing his hands in the air, “Oh my God, they’re just the Great Witchbeasts!”

That’s so stupid but it makes sense. The constellations are related to the most famous creations of Daphne. The Great Rabbit, the White Whale, and the Black Serpent. And given how the naming scheme has related to their Authorities, there is a possibility the same can be applied here. Gluttony is unique. Compared to the others, the variety of skills and powers it provides are wider than most. Memory manipulation, existence deletion, skill copying. It even shares Sloth’s ability to split his Witch Factor into several pieces. Which explains the three Archbishops as well as the puppeteering of his friends and Anastasia.

“I wonder if each Archbishop has a special ability that matches their name and respective Witchbeast. The White Whale could erase people entirely, cause them to go crazy, and can create illusions. The Great Rabbit just eats and multiplies constantly. And I don’t know anything about the Black Serpent. But that’s fine. Louis Arneb took over Anastasia, which means she is the most important one to target. But what was the Great Rabbit’s weakness?”

Hunger and mindlessness. Those things had no sense of preservation, just constantly wanting to eat and gorge themselves on anything that moved and breathed. Subaru took advantage of this by baiting them all together before defeating them in one fell swoop. But Subaru doubts he can do the same here. He would still need to find a way to eliminate all of the Witch Factors at once. Something to connect them all. But he can’t. None of the people around him had any way of extracting Witch Factors nor could they deal with the possessions without possibly killing his friends. He was stuck.

He blinked again, facepalming, “And I don’t even know if Return by Death is working.” Even more issues. Even in the worst case scenario, where he find a way to die, his usual fail-safe was possibly non-existent. He hasn’t died yet and a part of him is honestly scared to try. He never got used to the pain nor the absence of life itself in the few moments between death and revival. But he no longer feared it. He had gotten too used to the sensation, barely flinching when he slits his own throat. But this was new. He had gotten so used to the idea of dying that the inverse felt so…foreign.

And isn’t that funny? He’s finally been abandoned by the one person who has been by his side since the beginning. And who can blame her? He chose Anastasia over everyone. Perhaps this is what he deserves for being so greedy. He should have been happy with what he had. Did he not accept that this was his lot in life? Back in that prison where he died and suffered countless times without mercy. The stress and pain of back-to-back deaths with no end and feeling the full brunt of Felix’s excruciating magic constantly. He needed an out. An end to his misery. Everyone had left him. He was alone. So. Alone.

Emilia. Rem. And even Satella. Until she remembered him.

He wasted her love and this is the price he was paying. And the funnier part is he doesn’t regret it at all. He never chose her. He never wanted her love. He never wanted any of this. He was forcefully given this power and all this pain and affection that he never asked for. Cherish himself? What a joke. Satella might care for him, but the Witch of Envy does not. She never did. All she wanted was him. Not a happy Subaru. Not a safe Subaru. Not a stable Subaru. A Subaru that submitted his whole entire being to her. And that’s what he gave her. The debt for freedom from that cold prison. The Witch of Envy was simply collecting her dues.

Well then fuck her. Enough of this. He was sick and tired of being put through hell time and time again. He hated it. He hated her love. How she whispered in his ear all the time. Singing platitudes of love he never reciprocated. He hated her. He hated how she chained him down, forced him to say goodbye to Anastasia, and did all she could to isolate him. He hated her. He was sick of it all. Subaru didn’t give a shit if she loved him or not. He never loved her back. Whatever sick twisted feelings he felt was out of desperation. He never chose her. Not like Emilia. Rem. Or Anastasia. So if she wants to abandon him, then so be it. He’ll survive. He’ll save his wife. He’ll do whatever it takes to win. He isn’t some Archbishop of Envy. Nor some self-proclaimed knight of Emilia. Nor Rem’s hero.

He was Natsuki Subaru. A nobody. A worthless fool. A monster. Anastasia Hoshin’s monster.

He climbed out of Hell itself to save her and he’ll do it again and again if he has. He’ll slaughter all of the Witch Cult if it means providing a safe haven for his love. He’s going to break every single one of Gluttonies’ bones and force them to vomit everyone’s names before butchering them for all to see. A warning to the rest that he’s coming for them. Lust? Pride? Vainglory? He hasn’t forgotten what they did to Anastasia. That he remembers every death she experienced. He remembers every second of her screams as her Od collapsed. He memorized it all. He burned it into his mind, and he’ll make sure they pay for every second with their own screams. That’s a promise.

“What do I do?” Anastasia’s voice broke Subaru out of his murderous musing.

Subaru blinked, he looked around. The scene had shifted so much. It was no longer evening but dusk. Midnight possibly. Subaru was no longer standing in Anastasia’s room but was back in the corridor that led to the staircase below. Anastasia stood at the top of the staircase while Subaru was sitting on the floor meters away from her, hyperventilating and curled up tightly. He did it again. His mind kept deteriorating into madness at random. He needed to focus. He can’t go back to that mindset. He needed to limit himself but it’s becoming increasingly difficult. He needs his Anastasia. To ground him before he makes a mistake again, like he nearly did at Roswaal’s mansion. Anastasia. He needed her. Where is she? He’s so alone. Not this one. Anastasia. Where were you?

Subaru gazed upon the only figure reminiscent of his beloved. That memory of her was standing stock frozen, unable to make a decision. He couldn’t understand her. He knew Anastasia. She wasn’t the type to hesitate. She faced her problems head on. She never ran away.  This wasn’t her. Subaru blinked again, whispering, “Maybe that’s the problem.”

He stood up slowly before walking towards the younger Anastasia, speaking aloud, “I keep making the same mistakes again and again. Just like before, I keep making you out to be someone you’re not. Just like Emilia. I put you on a pedestal.”

He finally reached her side. He peered around her to look at Anastasia’s face. Conflicted. Breathing heavily. Pupils dilated. Inaction gripping her soul. She was scared. Subaru wanted to cry, his voice trembled, “I keep thinking you can survive this all. That you’re so strong willed. Back in Banan, I thought you would be able to fix whatever was bothering you, yourself. But just like when you died from Tia-Two, or when I met you on that fateful day, I keep assuming. Because I’m so used to that mask you always wear.”

Subaru walked past her and started heading downward towards the basement. His voice echoed off the walls, “You are strong. You are brave. You are stubborn. You are tenacious, well-spoken, and brilliant.”

The lights from the nearby lamps flickered, the shadows they cast onto Subaru grew as he descended. It felt like his voice was growing even louder, despite still being a whisper, but perhaps that was all in his head, “But you are also weak. You are scared. You can be indecisive. You are evasive, crude, and an idiot. You are a paradox in so many ways. Where does the mask end and where does the real Anastasia begin?”

Subaru arrived at the bottom and reached for the handle. He expected there to be no give but the door easily opened, left ajar and leaking more light into the hallway. Subaru shuddered. He didn’t expect this. He thought Anastasia needed to see this first but perhaps he wasn’t inferring enough. He could interact with the environment. So maybe he could take a peak into an area that Anastasia will see in the near future. He wasn’t thinking, just following his vague instincts. But he knew he needed to see this. This was important for Lotus, and this must be related to Anastasia’s stories about her. He needed to see the horrors that Anastasia faced. He needed to understand what grips her soul to this very day. What changed her mind in such an irreparable way that she became the person she is today. And why she struggled so much to tell him this. Yes. That was it. He wanted this. He wanted to know. He knew so much about her, but this was still an enigma. Perhaps that was his true Greed. A horrible and disgusting desire. But one he needed to admit.

Subaru swallowed dryly. He couldn’t bear to say it aloud.

Are you a monster like me?

He pulled—

Subaru’s motion was stopped, his arm kept firmly in place by a hand that was too small for how much force it was using on him.

“This isn’t your story,” the familiar voice of that small hand etched right into his soul. It was Anastasia, staring right at him. But what caught Subaru’s eye was the presence he so desperately sought for so long.

The thread of light had finally returned. And it was brighter than the sun.

 

Chapter 52: We Will Not Meet in ______

Summary:

Subaru sees the worst of Anastasia, while Anastasia sees the worst of herself...

Chapter Text

“This isn’t your story,” Anastasia said as her grip tightened around his arm. Subaru was shaken out of his stupor, his eyes focusing on this autonomous version of Anastasia’s memories. Or was he wrong about his assumption? Was this not just her memories? What is this? Who is she? “Don’t get ahead of yourself.”

“What are you?” He couldn’t help but blurt out. Her mannerisms felt so stiff, just from a glance he wasn’t sure if this Anastasia was smiling or frowning, her lips moving awkwardly. Her body was robotic, as if fighting its own instincts. Her eyes were empty, but flickers of life appeared every so often. If Subaru hadn’t known any better and this wasn’t some weird memory world, he’d honestly consider the idea that she was having a stroke.

Anastasia blinked, “I…we…do not know.”

Subaru raised an eyebrow, “You don’t know who you are?

Anastasia blinked again, “We…yes,” she nodded, “Strange. Very strange. So little time, yet the affinity is high. How absurd her—my—desires are.”

“What are you talking about?”

Anastasia stared intensely at Subaru, her eyes shifted into life once more, no longer empty, “We—I—recognize you,” her body shifted, morphing from her child self into the form he was most used to. Just like the Anastasia he knew and loved. Wearing that white kimono he stitched himself. He had to restrain himself, as every instinct in his body was screaming at him to run to her. To pick her up, hold her close, and never let go. He lost her once, nearly twice now, and thrice will never occur. He’ll purge the world sooner than to ever let that happen again. Her voice was a mixture of sullen and sincere fondness, “You are everything to us.”

Subaru did a double take at that, “I—what?” He did not know what that meant.

“Everything,” she repeated.

Subaru couldn’t comprehend what she just said. He could understand objectively, but subjectively, “I’m nobody.”

“That is not true.”

“It is. I don’t know who you are, but you aren’t going to trick me about this.”

“Do you not believe we love you?”

“I know that!” Subaru yelled, irritated at such a question, “I will never doubt that!”

“Then what do you not understand?”

“I’m not everything. Or whatever weird shit you were trying to imply. Ana wants so many things. Her family, money, a whole kingdom. How in the world am I more than any of that? That’s what you were trying to say, huh? Well, you fucked up! You can’t manipulate me,” Subaru reached for his knife automatically. Unfortunately, it had disappeared since he first arrived. He was annoyed by his habits and even more by the fact that whatever this apparition was, it was trying to feed him false lies.

“…I see.” Anastasia’s hand reached up to her chin, as if contemplating this situation completely, “You are an idiot.”

Her imitation of Anastasia was very convincing, “I already know that, asshole.”

“You don’t. You accept your ignorance simply because it is easier than understanding the truth.”

“And what is that truth?”

“That Anastasia Hoshin loves you beyond comprehension. That I love you beyond thought or reason. That we love you to the point of insanity.”

Subaru was getting more irritated by the second, “I told you, I know—”

“You know she loves you in theory but not the extent. Why is that?”

“Ana isn’t insane, okay. She’s logical. Sure, she’s incredibly emotional, kind, and lets her heart guide her. But she isn’t dumb. She thinks clearly. She wouldn’t love me like…some people. Because that doesn’t make sense. I don’t offer her anything of value like that. She’s the type of person to hold her emotions back all the time. Logic is her bread and butter.”

The memory of Anastasia wasn’t convinced, “I see. Do you even know why we reacted so horribly during that terrible week?”

Of course, Subaru knew, “Ana found out about Return by Death somehow. And she probably was thinking about what that implied. Whether our whole relationship was a lie. Or whether I’ve been manipulating her this entire time, since we met. I don’t blame her for reacting like that. I would be the same in her position.”

“You,” Anastasia paused and started to laugh hysterically. It felt unnerving and off-putting to Subaru.

“What’s so funny—”
The imitation of Anastasia looked at Subaru oddly, as if fixated on something, “She didn’t even consider that as a possibility. She loves you. So much. To the point that such an idea, that you would manipulate us into some relationship, is absurd. Our first thought wasn’t, ‘was it all a lie?’ No. It was, ‘I could never hope to pay you back for all you’ve done.’  And, ‘you must have not trusted us given you haven’t told us any of this.’ As well as, ‘we must have failed you.’ Our relationship is not equal. You will always be suffering alone, for our sake, because that’s the type of person you are. Self-sacrificing, kind, ignorant. We are worthless compared to you.”

“…No, that’s not possible,” Subaru shook his head, “You’re lying.” That doesn’t sound like her at all. Anastasia never thought so low of herself. She always seemed to value herself highly. He remembered how she called herself a goddess of commerce on the day they first met in the capital.

“Why do you think that?”

Subaru grit his teeth, “I haven’t done anything for her that would lead to such emotions. I know she got attached to me, but I didn’t do shit! She doesn’t remember the other timelines, she doesn’t remember what I did for her! I got lucky, okay?! Anastasia was feeling lonely and I was there to comfort her. It’s like that suspension effect or trauma bonding or whatever! She tricked herself into liking me to survive! The moment our names come back, I know she’ll realize how stupid this all was,” Subaru blurted out all of his fears, his anxieties, the bitter truths he kept close to his heart, “She’ll have her family back and will have no need for my presence. She has a stronger Od now and can live happily without worrying about it. She won’t be alone anymore. She won’t need me anymore.”

Subaru held back his tears, he hated saying these words, but they were the truth. The end of this story wasn’t a happy one for him, and all he could do was laugh at that fact, “Everything will be as it should. She’ll return to her candidacy. And…I might be a burden on her. Candidates can’t get married, right? Well, we’ll figure that out when it comes. But I won’t stop her if she wants it…gone,” Subaru felt rancid saying that last part. Subaru hated it but a part of him accepted that this was always going to happen. Everything he does only leads to Hell. He just drags everyone with him. He’s a parasite that clings to their love and affection like a drug. He doesn’t deserve any of it. “It was all my fault anyway; I trapped her in that marriage proposal. If we dated for longer, she would have probably realized this wasn’t going to work. And she knows it. That’s why she was so depressed. That’s why she was so desperate to come with us. She was worried that I was going to do something to her family. That I was some psychopath who wants to isolate her from everyone she loved.” And he did not blame her, he wasn’t exactly mentally stable to anyone with a brain. But he didn’t care. He just wanted her happy. He wanted to stay by her side and make her happy no matter what. And if she eventually wanted him gone, so be it. But he’ll selfishly cling to her until then, “I don’t understand what your game is here but stop trying to mess with me. It’s not working.”

Anastasia’s expression shifted, from confusion to pity to rage to pure loathing, “Don’t say that.”

“You—”

“Don’t you ever say that again!” Her form shifted back to a child, wrathful and filled with so much contempt. She walked up to him and pointed at his chest, pressuring his position despite her smaller stature, “You are not leaving!”

“Wait that’s only if—”

Subaru was interrupted again by her, Anastasia’s body shifted again. Her child form changed from the kimono she wore in Lotus’s palace to a slightly older version. But back to the rags of her hyena days. Subaru assumed this was the version of her that eventually left Lotus and went back to the streets, meeting Ricardo eventually. He couldn’t ruminate on that for long as Anastasia grabbed his collar and pulled him down to her level, scowling, “You don’t get to come into our lives, making us happy, and just leave as if it’s better for us!”

Her body shifted to her appearance during the Royal Selection. Before he could speak, she continued her rant, “We won’t need you? A burden? Trapped us into a marriage? Is that what you thought this entire time? Do you really think so little of yourself—of us—that this was your conclusion?!”

Subaru tried to say something, “But—”

Anastasia was not having it, “No! Enough of this! If words alone can’t convince you, then perhaps you need more direct persuasion.” Anastasia’s hand reached over to the door handle and nearly ripped the door off its hinges. Subaru peered through and shuddered. Pitch black darkness. “You lack understanding. Your mind cannot comprehend it naturally. We will guide you. And maybe you will finally understand who Anastasia Hoshin really is.”

Subaru couldn’t respond as he was unceremoniously pushed through the entryway. And all he saw from that moment forward, were nightmares.

----------------------

“Throw out this repulsive fool. Or cut him in half, I care not,” Priscilla said, her tone scathing.

Anastasia expected this to happen. She knew how the Baroness functioned and Subaru’s current mental state would not gel well with her expectations. Despite what many would believe, Anastasia doesn’t hate Priscilla Barielle. They were rivals for sure which led to some tension here and there. And sure, Priscilla’s personality left much to be desired, given how flighty and homicidally volatile she was. And sure, Anastasia was starting to understand her homicidal tendencies after watching her kick Subaru’s nose. But that didn’t mean Anastasia hated her, per se. She wanted to punt Miss Prissy-and-Pissy into the sun but that was more akin to how absolutely annoying she was to deal with on a constant basis. Anastasia still respected Priscilla and understood her actions. Just like how she understood Crusch’s actions. She didn’t necessarily think they were terrible people but were reacting as anyone would in their situations.

“That ain’t funny,” she could feel Al’s presence turn cold and imposing. Anastasia raised an eyebrow at his response but did not react to it. She quietly catalogued his behavior for later and would investigate the man more thoroughly when possible. She already had plans for the twin maids. Perhaps Al would be a great source of information.

“Subaru. If I lend you my shoulder, can you stand?” Rem said. Her voice sent a bolt of spite through Anastasia’s body.

…Perhaps I’m being too biased. But at least Crusch was reacting like a noble would and Priscilla just kicked Subaru out. She didn’t torture him with healing magic or kill him several times.

Anastasia thought for a moment. Now that she considered it, it was intensely ironic that out of everyone who killed Subaru, it was the girl who loved him dearly and outwardly, who was responsible for most of his suffering at this point. And not the homicidal princess who kills people at the drop of a hat. Nor the Witch Cult. Both times Subaru died, it was to that rat Emilia keeps in a rock. She wondered if this would continue to be a trend.

“Disgusting. Every single one of you,” Anastasia couldn’t help but voice her revulsion. She knew logically that she should lend the same sort of leniency to those of the Emilia camp, but she couldn’t help it. Every time she tried, she was proven again and again that his worst enemies were always right next to him. They were his friends. Not some—

“Wow! Hey you, mister! You look really hurt! Are you all right?” That familiar voice stopped Anastasia in her tracks. Her movements were robotic as she saw Mimi wave at Subaru, happy as can be. She missed such a sight. She missed Mimi. Hetaro. Tivey. The triplets she would spoil every day despite Ricardo’s protests. She couldn’t help it. She loved those three like they were her children. No. They were her children. Nothing would change that.

“Hey, Mimi. Don’t be causing people trouble. You know you shouldn’t make so much mischief.”

…No.

“I’m very sorry that my girl caused you trou…Mmm?”

No. She didn’t.

“You’re…that’s right. You’re Subaru. Emilia’s knight, Subaru Natsuki. So, you’re still in the capital, huh? What an unexpected surprise,” the past Anastasia spoke with a smile that infuriated the current Anastasia beyond relief.

She did. Unexpected her ass, this was all planned. Anastasia gripped her own hands furiously. She should have known. She was too enthralled by everything else that was going on that she didn’t even notice her own past self’s machinations. Of course, Anastasia would be taking advantage of this situation. She would be keeping a keen eye over the Karsten Mansion. And given that Subaru stormed out of there, this would be a prime opportunity to snatch some info.

“Should one of the big players in the royal selection be walking without an escort these days?” Anastasia blinked at Subaru’s words. Why did that sound familiar?

“Why is a royal candidate leaving the capital in the middle of the night with not a knight or mercenary in sight?”

Oh. No wonder he reacted so poorly to her back then. He assumed this was a trap. That she was tricking him again. Just like what she was seeing right now. Anastasia felt her heart sink as she watched Subaru get led by the nose to a nearby shop, with promises of a dragon carriage being teased every step. It made sense. Anastasia could envision her thoughts on that day given what she knew, as she watched them enter the eatery and order food.

Lucky me, I caught the dumbass before he left town. Now I just have to push him towards the info I want. But first I gotta ingratiate myself. See if I can make a good first impression. He already dislikes Julius but something tells me he is a sucker for beautiful women.

“It’d be even harder to say that. Anyway, about the dragon carriage,” Subaru said, his tone indicating a bit of hurry.

Her past self chuckled, “Cuttin’ right ta the chase, hmm? You won’t please yer business partner if ya prioritize only what you want. The core of negotiation is how much ya can please the other party. You’re not too good at that, Natsuki,” she then bit into her meal. Anastasia groaned as she noticed how cutely she was eating. This was a planned action. She remembered how that abominable woman would teach her how to eat properly as a child. And how Anastasia completely ignored that advice when necessary. People who are of low-born background often don’t care about table manners that much. Nobles were the opposite, often grimacing or staring in amazement. So, this was one of Anastasia’s tactics, using her own lack of manners to create a conversation starter and to possibly confirm her theories about his background.

Case in point, Subaru caught the bait and began staring at her lack of decency. Her past self noticed and continued the attack, saying, “It’s a little awkward if you stare at me while I’m eatin’. I wasn’t raised with very good manners, y’see. Am I doin’ something strange?”

Anastasia groaned even harder. It’s so cringe. It’s even worse since I don’t remember this. But seeing my own manipulations from an outside point of view makes me want to throw up and die.

Subaru’s answer was interesting, however, “I haven’t been educated in high culture enough to judge something like that…I don’t think it’s weird at all. You just don’t, uh, often see a woman opening her mouth wide like that.”

Anastasia and her past self blinked, simultaneously. While her past self kept the façade on her face, politely smiling, Anastasia herself started to laugh. Her smile was genuine, unlike her past self. Why? Because her past self was probably about to misunderstand what he said. And sure enough, she did, “…Are ya tryin’ ta get into my good graces? If so, ya gotta do way better’n that,” her past self snickered.

Subaru looked genuinely confused, “Um, I’m not kidding around here. I’m really in a bind, that’s why I wanna get to the point.”

“If ya wanna appeal to my sympathy, that’s the worst plan possible when you’re dealin’ with a girl like me. But I applaud ya for tryin’,” Anastasia laughed at her past self even more. Because it was obvious what was going on. Her past self thinks he was some idiot who was half-assing a negotiation. That he was really trying to convince her for help for whatever he needed but Anastasia knew better. Subaru’s act of flattery and his appeal to sympathy were not intentional. He was being sincere. He really thought her manners were not weird and Subaru really was in a rush. What was even funnier was that her past self was considering if he was acting the fool.

Anastasia watched as the negotiation began in earnest. Her past self took the initiative and began to use the location of a dragon carriage shop to entice Subaru into a conversation with her. Subaru obviously found this a lot of work for nothing because he would honestly answer all of Anastasia’s questions without even thinking of the ramifications, if she was sincere about it. Because he’s stupid. And dumb. And Anastasia loved him for it. But her past self didn’t know that. So, she had to do this whole song and dance, using Mimi as a way to smooth relations and get Subaru’s guard down. Which again, wasn’t necessary as when Anastasia asked about his origins, all he said was, “I was born in Japan on Earth, and this is a tracksuit, probably the only one in the world.” The complete truth.

Her past self frowned at the answer as well as his explanation of being from beyond the Great Waterfall. It was interesting. The information she was gathering about Subaru was quite enthralling. Despite her past self’s goals, this was much more unsettling. Anastasia theorized that her initial assumption was that he was some kind of run-away noble from Kararagi. But with this new bit of information and his contrasting traits. How he doesn’t understand certain Lugunican or Kararagian customs and wears unique clothing. The fact he sincerely said he was from some place beyond the Great Waterfall. It all pointed to him being not of this world. Anastasia knew this was a failed loop. Because if her past self had this information previously, there would be no way in hell Subaru would have been left alone for a year without her meddling in his affairs. The opportunity for a possible Great Waterfall dweller was too juicy.

If Subaru succeeded here, would our relationship have blossomed earlier?

Her heart desperately wanted to say yes. But her mind knew the real answer. Because she was watching the exact reason why it would have never happened, right this second. Their conversation detoured into the realm of personal matters as Subaru got lost in the conversation, as her past self anticipated. His voice cracked as he asked, “How can you do that much…? Aren’t you afraid of failure?”

Her past self teased him, “Oh my, my, my. Natsuki, have you finally taken a proper interest in me?” Her past self’s eyes fluttered but Anastasia could see the memories begin to shift in her mind behind that cheerful mask. Of all the times she’s failed and nearly failed. Of her first failure, her personal failure. “Failure, huh? I’d say I’m afraid of that, too. I’m not exactly claimin’ I’ve won every battle I’ve fought ta get ta where I am now. I’ve just kept winnin’ the ones that really mattered.”

“You never wonder if you’ve won enough of your bets?” Never. It was never enough. “I mean, you have plenty as it is. You’re quite a big-time merchant, you have lots of people around you, and—”

“Can I really say I have plenty? I don’t even know what would satisfy me,” Anastasia nodded along to her past self. She could never be satisfied. She always wanted more and more. Her greed, her desires, was bottomless. And the reason was simple, “I…have a dream.” Her past self tapped a finger onto the counter. It was interesting. Her past self did not have to go this far but something must have lit a flame inside her to get this passionate, “I’ve carried that dream with me since my time in the slums, never knowin’ what the next day would bring, tryin’ my hardest to live…I want everythin’ I can get my hands on.”

“Everything…you can get your hands on…” Subaru said carefully. Anastasia’s eyes lingered over Subaru. Her heart burned.

“My dream is to see just who I can become, just how far I can go. But I won’t compromise one bit until I’m satisfied I’ve done that. As long as I live, everything I can reach and take hold of will be mine. Will I die penniless? Or will I die fulfilled by the innumerable possessions around me? My life is one big contest until I get one result or the other.” Anastasia felt bitter about her little speech. She still embodied such ideals and desires, but could Anastasia really say such a dream was worthwhile? How far could she go?

Because she did lose. Her family, her possessions, her history. Die penniless? She couldn’t accept that anymore. She didn’t want to let go of any of it. Which was why she ran away. She couldn’t face such a reality, an unthinkable present, where she remembered all her cherished memories, and everyone looked upon her with thoughtless ignorance. It was a horrifying idea that she so desperately wanted to rid herself of. And she couldn’t help but feel immense sorrow for Subaru for. Because her worst day was Subaru’s every day. Dying alone, without anyone knowing his pain, isolated, and with not a soul who could relate or understand. Everyone forgetting the times you spent together. You don’t even get to choose.

“I think you’re the pot calling the kettle black, especially when you’re the one poking into their business…” Anastasia blinked at Subaru’s words. Her mind strayed from the conversation for a few minutes and only returned at the use of this familiar idiom. But it only cemented her previous thoughts. Such a small detail, but one that her past self caught, her eyes slightly twinkling at the odd turn of phrase. Anastasia was sure her other self would have followed up on these words later, just like Anastasia did during their first carriage rides together. How somber. Even without Gluttony, she would never remember this moment. A connection between two people, erased for one but not the other.

“Hey, when ya compare the people goin’ for tiny piles of coins ta a gal who’s after a whole kingdom, they’re pretty pathetic. Besides, in business, speed is the name of the game. When ya look at what people with a nose for money are doin’, ya see more of the big picture,” her past self was right. Take every opportunity as quickly as possible. And Anastasia wasn’t the type to restrain herself, given how she rushed for Subaru the moment she confirmed her feelings. Or the fact that she got engaged to him in less than a few months, not even courting for that long. It was ironic given her previous views on romance. She changed so much in such little time but also so much of her is still the same as she always was.

Still a hyena, feeding on the remains of monsters and heroes. Like Subaru.

…Do you regret marrying me, Subaru? No. That was impossible. He loved her dearly. She knew this. But a part of her couldn’t help but hate how it came about. A desperate move to save her life. In some ways, she took advantage of his attachment to her. Made him feel in-debt to her for simply being a shoulder to cry on and comfort him when he lost everyone he loved. He lost half of his life expectancy and gave up any opportunity to return to his camp like nothing ever changed. Isn’t that funny? Anastasia could return to her camp with her name, and everything would be just as it was. If Subaru returned, everything would crumble. His candidate would not be able to handle the reality that she abandoned her lover. His friends? Despite her limited information, Subaru’s stories implied they cared for him a decent bit. Their ignorance of his suffering aside, she doubted they lacked the humanity to not feel guilt for abandoning him. Adding onto the fact that Subaru would be joining her camp and the Emilia camp was finished.

The only regret Anastasia had was that Subaru would never be happy with that situation. The idiot cared so much about them that he probably couldn’t bear to see them suffer. He wouldn’t even comprehend that their suffering was because he suffered. It sickened her because there was no complete happy ending she could give him. If he stayed with her, he would feel regret towards his old camp. If he didn’t stay, she would have no way of repaying him back for everything he gave her. In so many ways, Anastasia won everything from her relationship with Subaru. She took so much from him, and he got almost nothing in return. Just the love she could promise him. Which was not enough.

But perhaps that was normal of her. Always taking. Always winning.

Her past self said it best, “Workin’ the market to favor you is more than enough reason. Merchants collude with one another quite a bit,” the memory of her said with a slightly malicious grin, “If they think something’s worth getting’, they’ll grab it by the throat.”

And then throw away the bones after devouring them. And Anastasia was about to see her past self do the same thing to Subaru.

----------------------

Subaru could hear the dripping of water from a nearby tap. The sound of water splashing against stone reminded him of worse days. “Please. Please. Please, please, please, please, please!” Someone spoke in rapid succession to the left of him, her voice a middle-ground between a whisper and a croak.

But those memories were a helpful distraction from the literal hellscape he was witnessing currently. The memory of Anastasia beside him spoke calmly, “We witnessed this nearly a month after Lotus gave us permission. It was strange, we didn’t understand why, but we just couldn’t come down here. It was like we were instinctively afraid of what’s to come.”

“I’ll be good…I’ll be good! I swear, I’m not bad! Don’t abandon me!” Someone else screamed from Subaru’s right.

“…We were right to be afraid.”

“What the fuck is all this?” Subaru couldn’t help but ask. The basement was like a prison; bars separated the rooms like walls and the air was musty with sweat and filth. Subaru could smell mold, vomit, and soil permeate the entire air. Each room held a basic cot and mattress along with several pillows and cushions that were strewn about the floor. What horrified Subaru the most, however, was the multitude of people going insane in each cell.
