Every single one was either muttering madness, vomiting into a bucket, sweating uncontrollably, or slamming their head into a pillow repeatedly. It reminded Subaru too much of his time in the prison tower.

“This isn’t a prison by the way,” Anastasia whispered to him.

“Then what is it then?”

“A quarantine.”

“They’re sick?”

“Not physically. They have no disease other than the one that clings to their mind,” Subaru didn’t understand Anastasia’s words. She noticed given her subsequent lecture, “Years ago, Lotus came upon a traveling merchant who was selling flowers and fruits from all across the lands. She was just a simple citizen of Banan at that time and was dreaming of a future of riches and luxury. But she was not the most talented person. She lacked many of the skills necessary for success and was thus downtrodden. However, that did not stop her. Taking a chance, she bought some flowers from the merchant and used them to make a fanciful bouquet. The next day, she offered the bundle of flowers to her boss as a peace offering for a previous argument.”

Subaru wasn’t following. At least, not until Anastasia said these next words, “Over the following weeks, her boss fell hopelessly in love with her.”

That struck a spark in Subaru’s mind. “The flowers did something to him.”

Anastasia nodded, “At first, the changes were subtle. There was less tension in the air, and her boss began to compliment her more and more. Then came the stares, the more elaborate praises, and the gifts. It then reached a breaking point when her boss left his wife and children and confessed to Lotus publicly. Of course, Lotus was bewildered and immediately rejected him. He did not react well.”

“Did he—”

“He did. Lotus only realized what had caused such a reaction when she was going through his office after the funeral. The flowers were still there. Resting on his desk in a vase. Taken care of without a hint of wilting. It was an opportunity from Heaven that was laid before her. And like any proper Kararagian, she took it immediately. She abandoned her old name and took upon the flower’s moniker: Lotus.”

Subaru began to connect the dots, “The flowers on her servants!”

Anastasia didn’t even react, “The very same. However, those are not real. Just a brand to mark them as hers. The real flowers are grinded and processed until they become a fine powder. She then slips them into their food and beverages and slowly enthralls them to her.”

“That’s…insane!” Subaru felt disgusted beyond relief.

“A smart decision, logically. She receives loyal servants who genuinely love her, while they receive happiness beyond compare.”

“But it’s artificial,” Subaru argued, “None of it’s real! It’s just some sick twisted chemical making them feel love!”

“Does that matter? They are happy. A lot of these people were outcasts, impoverished serfs, and former slaves suffering on the streets without anyone to care for them. Here, they get food, water, and warmth.”

Subaru waved his hand over to the suffering servants, “Does this look like happiness to you?”

Anastasia finally turned her head to him, “A small price to pay for salvation. And as long you don’t make any mistakes, Lotus will continue to give you the flower and you never have to be down here. Besides, is it any different from real love?”

“You don’t believe that, do you?”

“…” Anastasia said nothing, only pointing towards a specific cell before taking Subaru’s hand and guiding him towards it. He quietly followed her as the moans and groans of the people around them pierced his eardrums. His hatred for that courtesan rose by the second. And it peaked right as they arrived at the cell and he recognized the figure, collapsed on the floor and panting for air.

The figure’s eyes flickered to them, filled with madness and anxiety. He licked his dry lips before speaking, “Little Sprout, is that you?”

Anastasia’s form regressed into a toddler, barely a few years old. Her expression was scared, remorseful, and filled with guilt. Her voice was calm, however,

“…Hello Turrel.”

Chapter 53: The Beast Gnaws on ______

Summary:

Two Witch factors collide as the paths of two stars mix...

Chapter Text

“What the hell?” Subaru whispered.

“That was what we thought when we discovered Turrel down here. We could not believe this was all some weird twist of fate. It must have been planned. It must have all been orchestrated,” Anastasia flicked her wrist, causing the word to shudder and morph. The environment twisted and bent before reforming into Lotus’s chambers. The wooden pillars and walls replaced the iron bars and stone masonry of the basement. Lotus sat bored on top of her ivory throne. “Do not worry, this is only a memory. She cannot notice me or your odd behavior.”

Wait, that doesn’t sound right. Subaru thought for a moment, “Wait, but didn’t I change things before? When I pulled you away from Turrel. Or was that just for you?”

Anastasia frowned, “We…do not know. That is not part of our abilities. Perhaps it is your ability that allows you to do so. To have such power is a King’s responsibility. Not a Beast’s.”

Subaru raised an eyebrow, “King? Beast’s?” But Anastasia did not respond, only waiting for the scene in front of them to progress. Subaru looked down at the thread that connected his heart to Anastasia’s. Is there more to Greed than I thought? The implications made Subaru shudder. His knowledge of Witch Factors was already vast from discussing with Beatrice but even she said her knowledge was only waist-high. Witch Factors were present for eons. Even before humanity crept onto the lands, there was something lingering in the darkness, waiting for them. The thought made Subaru’s spine tingle.

“Ah, it seems you have finally found my little secret ingredient,” Lotus spoke, her eyes peering down at them.

Anastasia did not react visibly, but her voice was defiant, angry, “Was this all planned?”

“Does it matter?”

“Was it all a lie?”

Lotus stared at Anastasia for a few seconds before walking off her throne and walking slowly towards her. Each step an echo within this lonely hall, the only inhabitants these two. Subaru felt a presence on his hand and looked down. Anastasia’s childlike hand gripped his. A spark of guilt struck his heart. He almost forgot, No matter who this is. This is still Anastasia. She went through all this herself, scared and alone.

Even if it was a lie, Subaru couldn’t help but comfort any version of Anastasia

Lotus arrived right in front of Anastasia and Subaru, towering over the little girl. Subaru squeezed Anastasia’s hand, scowling at the courtesan who didn’t even glance his way. She spoke softly, “I have never lied. I told you, I did want to nurture you into something beautiful. And you may believe I staged this all, that those two who fostered you as a child, were grooming you specifically for my purposes. I will deny that as well. I had no idea you existed until we met that very day you were captured. It was only coincidence that we met, despite fate guiding you to me all along.”

Lotus placed her hand upon her stomach, “The cruelty of this world has left me barren. A blessing for those in my line of work. A curse for me. I lacked the power to bring life into this world, and it left a deep mark upon my soul. The very process that brought me into power, destroyed whatever lineage I could bare. Ironic, isn’t it?”

She placed her hand upon Anastasia’s cheek, “Grieving for the possibility that could never be, I chose the second-best option. I sent word that I would buy any child of a few years of age, so that I may nurture as one of my own. And it just so happens that one of my agents, Danzi, found an abandoned baby in the depths of Banan’s slums. Coincidence or not, you were fated to be by my side.”

Anastasia stared at her robotically, but her body was trembling, her voice almost a whimper, “But Turrel—”

“Decided to act against me. He assumed I would be feeding you my love just as the others. The useless moron. What a baseless assumption. Why would I do such a foolish maneuver? I already understood the effects of such a method. Why persevere and repeat it upon a child? It would bring me no conclusion that would satisfy me,” Lotus’s eyes turned manic.

“What conclusion were you looking for?”

Lotus stared down at Anastasia. Silence took hold before Lotus ripped it out, grabbing Anastasia’s face with both hands and bringing her close, face to face, as Lotus spewed her tale and song, “I sought to nurture a child into a simulacra of me.”

Subaru tried to pull Anastasia away from the madwoman but the little girl’s hand pulled back to defy him. She whispered to him, “Don’t. Just listen.”

“And you were a perfect base for such a possibility. Born within this wastes, within the muck and filth of Banan’s underbelly, you were a magnificent child gifted to me by Od itself. I wanted to see what a child who was born in the same conditions as me could become. Would my care and love bind you to this place, to my path, to become a daughter worthy of carrying on my legacy? Or will you devour me and everything I hold dear, and surpass all my expectations? Either ending would be glorious and I am to eager to see which you shall choose.”

“What the fuck is wrong with this woman?” Subaru could not help but mutter. His eyes glared at Lotus as she finally let go of Anastasia’s face and turned back to her throne.

She turned her head slightly, “That is your fate. So tell me, what shall you do?”

Anastasia said nothing to her, only turning towards Subaru, “We fled from this place the second she turned her back.”

Subaru squeezed her hand, “I see. I’m sorry.”

“Don’t be. You were not responsible.”

“But you still suffered. And if no one will apologize, I will.”

Anastasia smiled at him for a brief moment before her smile returned to a somber expression, “Your words are sweet. But we are undeserving of them. We haven’t suffered. In fact, we cast a blind eye to others.”

“That isn’t your fault! You were just a child.”

Her eyes were cold, “…A child who came back two days after this and acted as if nothing had happened at all.”

------------------------

“But I won’t apologize for using you. It’s an ironclad rule among merchants to take anything that isn’t bolted down. Besides, neither of us said anything that hurts us personally, did we? You asked me whatever you wanted, and you answered several of my questions, Natsuki,” the memory of Anastasia finished speaking. Subaru angrily spouted drivel in response, lashing out at her because it was the only thing left to do.

The real Anastasia, meanwhile, sat quietly next to them, idly tapping her finger on the table. She watched the whole interaction. The conversation was an anomaly to her. She remembered sitting in this very café, eating and playing with Mimi just as shown here. But her memory was certainly different. She remembered the smell of coff in the air, the taste of crisp letteuce with strips of pork, the ambient chit-chat of the people around her. The people around her currently were the Iron Fang hiding in plain sight, most likely a precaution placed in case Subaru turned out to be hiding his fangs. She knew herself well enough that this version of her has decided Subaru is worthless.

Sure, there were signs of possible value, that Subaru was one of the Great Waterfall’s denizens was certainly something she can’t ignore. Which is why Anastasia understood her own actions greatly. This Subaru was angry and spiteful. To the past Anastasia with no context, all she knew was that he was still reeling from the duel with Julius. There was no negotiating with someone who held a grudge so deep without understanding the reasons why. Even if the past version of herself explained Julius’s actions, she doubted Subaru would understand or agree. It was useless to try. But even then, there was no use in cutting off a connection completely. It was why the past Anastasia left Subaru the information he needed to acquire a carriage. If Subaru were to become more rational and mature, he’d recognize the boon she gave him despite her trickery and would seek her aid once more. Anastasia knew all this and her mind accepted her own logic.

But even then, she couldn’t help but think of one singular thought.

 …I should kill myself.

“Stop.” His voice rang out, along with a gentle touch to her hand. Anastasia glanced upward and saw Subaru looking down upon her with a gentle gaze. Her heart would race normally if she didn’t already know who this was. “You did nothing wrong.” Such sweet words. If only they didn’t come from the one person she never wanted to hear that from.

Anastasia smiled at him as he sat down in front of her. She noticed that the memory had not shifted yet, no one else was in this café besides her and the personification of the Witch Factor of Greed. So whatever this was, it was purely by the design of this eldritch creature in front of her. She knew this was some imprint of Subaru. That no matter what, this was Subaru in his entirety. His Greed, manifested as a human being. Her heart fluttered just from the sight of him, and it disgusted her at her core. This wasn’t him. This wasn’t her Subaru. Even if it was him in some capacity, it did not replace the real one. Whatever kindness it spouts, was not his. Just a reflection of the insanity it brings upon his soul.

Anastasia continued to smile despite how brittle it felt, “Oh, don’t worry. I’m not going to die that easily.”

Greed looked at her as if he didn’t believe a single word, “You are not at fault.”

“So you say.”

“I do not blame you for it.”

“…You aren’t the one who can say such things. That isn’t your right,” Anastasia could barely hold back her emotions.

“But it’s the truth. I, no, Natsuki Subaru holds no grudges against you for such actions. You may not comprehend it, but I am an extension of his will. Whatever Natsuki Subaru believes in, whatever he wishes, whatever he desires. All that is within reach, and even that which is beyond, I shall seek and claim for him. It is his divine right, one that I shall enact as King of this realm.”

Anastasia’s eyes narrowed, “So you’re finally showing who you really are.”

Greed blinked before scratching his neck in embarrassment, “I-I’m really not lying! I am him. I just…am not at the same time.”

“Like Sloth?”

Greed became serious, “No. Unfortunately, the Hunter lays dormant.”

“The Hunter?” Anastasia narrowed in on that name.

Greed continued on as if Anastasia didn’t ask, “I hold his personality and his desires in fullness. His memories are mine as well. He and I are one and the same. So you do not have to be so rigid with me. I will not harm you.”

“You ignored my question. Who is the Hunter? And why are you so different from Geuse?”

“…Humans and other mortal beings have always named us after the desires we feasted upon. But that wasn’t what we were originally called. Our monikers matched our original roles, and we prefer such titles more than simple human desires. The one you call Sloth was known as the Hunter. Just as I was known as the King.” Greed’s eyes felt foreign to her now, looking into her soul. “As for why, my synchronization with Natsuki Subaru far surpasses Regulus Corneas, unlike Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti. His affinity is abysmal which means his he was unable to feed the Hunter enough to awaken. All that remains is the imprint of Geuse.”

Anastasia wasn’t phased in the slightest, “So in that case, were you messing with me all those times. Every single moment where I intervened, where this thread appeared,” Anastasia raised it in the air, it shimmered and connected her to Greed, “Was it all a way to satisfy your curiosity?”

Greed looked upon her softly, “No. I will state it as many times as possible. I am an extension of Natsuki Subaru’s will. And in his will, he wanted closure to so many of his regrets. And he wanted you most of all to know about them.”

“Why?”

“Because he loves you.”

“I know that damn it,” Anastasia pounded the table, infuriated, “Stop messing with me!”

“I’m not trying to—"

“You! Everything about you just pisses me off!” Anastasia couldn’t hold back her rage anymore, “Even if it were the case that you are him, which you’re not! You think I’d be satisfied with such an excuse!”
“Please calm down.”

No. Anastasia was sick of all this. She didn’t care about this anymore. Witch Factors. Return by Death. Her own sins. It was too much. She wanted to go home. She wanted to see Subaru and run away from all this nonsense. “You really think I would be okay going through all that, just for it to be revealed that you aren’t him?! That this all is some sick game for you to feed off his desires more. I hate this. I hate you! You look just like him and it sickens me! You aren’t him and you aren’t going to convince me anytime soon. Was it fun for you to watch me comfort Subaru, when it wasn’t really him?! Was it funny for me to lie and call myself Pleione?! Is it fun for you to say such sweet words, knowing it will have an effect on me?!” She stood up ready to walk away. A part of her knew there was no point, but she’d rather rebel against this disgusting wretch than let him disgrace Subaru’s visage any longer in front of her.

Just as she was about to leave, Greed grabbed her hand, “Please don’t leave.”

She tried to pull away, “You’re not my husband. Stop acting like him. Now let go.”

“Please.”

“I said, let go—”

“I may not be your husband!” Greed shouted, “But he and I are the same. I am his messenger. His greed for you is unmatched. If you hate me, so be it. I did not mean for you to suffer this much. I only wished to satisfy his wants and wishes. I wanted to make up for my mistake.”

“Your mistake?” Anastasia couldn’t help but be curious.

“…If it was not for me, your emotions would have not been so turbulent after you formed a bond with him.”

-------------------------

“Even so, you can’t blame yourself for this—”

“Really? We cannot blame ourselves for such an action?” Anastasia said, “We saw what happened down there. You saw what happened. And we ignored such inhumane acts of cruelty, all so we can enjoy the pleasures Lotus offers us. A soft bed. Nice warm meals. No sense of danger or sleepless nights. All at the cost of some innocents being driven mad.”

“You were just a child!” Subaru shouted back.

“That is no excuse!” Anastasia screamed. She threw her hands out as the scene shifted back to the basement, punctuating her rage. Subaru could hear the dripping of water and the moans of all those who were tormented here. It was suffocating, “We let this happen. We lived here not just for a few days. But a whole year! We should have been satisfied with what we had. We could have survived out in the slums with the knowledge we accrued. But we didn’t. We stayed here and watched as all these servants were turned into slaves of love and affection. Look at them! Do you see what she did to some of them?!” Subaru winced upon closer inspection. So many had scars on their bodies. In areas only the depraved would reach and mutilate. It sickened him to his core. He remembered Anastasia’s words, but he didn’t realize the reality.

“But she was abusing you! You told me so. She emotionally abused you,” Subaru tried to squeeze her hand, but Anastasia ripped it out of his.

“…She did. After we returned, she would taunt us. Hit us. Test how far we could be pushed. We withstood it all. For a time, we thought it was just because we did not want to return to the slums again. To suffer once more.” Anastasia grasped her face, as if ashamed, “But when she finally died, we cried. We loved her in spite of the cruelty.”

“You were attached to her, it wasn’t your fault.”

“Is everything not our fault?!” Anastasia tearfully said, “To what end will you justify our sins. To what end will you see us with no fault. We cannot stand it. It is abhorrent. We have made you into a replica of these drug-addled slaves. Just like her. We have driven you insane with our love. Don’t you see, Lotus won. However, many years it took, we became just like her.”

“That isn’t true at all!”

“Is it not?” The scene shifted to something Subaru never wanted to see again. It was a café in Banan that he had seen hundreds of times. The Anastasia before him morphed into a stunning image. Her adult self dressed in a classic white dress, wearing a side ponytail, along with a silver necklace and matching earrings. He could never forget this attire. It was the same attire he woke up to during that whole waking nightmare. “Tell us, how many times have you died for us?”

“Stop it.” Subaru took a step back.

“When Lotus died, Turrel and all the other servants killed themselves,” she took a step towards him, her expression haunting, “They couldn’t live without her. They were so entrenched in that drug, in their lust for her, the mere thought of her death brought them to their knees. And we did nothing! We were too busy grieving to notice that her mansion had turned into a mass burial!”

“Stop!” Subaru took another step back.

“How many times have you died for us, Subaru? How many more times will you do so? This debt is too large. We cannot pay it and it infuriates us!”

Subaru was hyperventilating, “Please. Why are you telling me this?”

------------------------------

“…If it was not for me, your emotions would have not been so turbulent after you formed a bond with him.”

“What do you mean by that?” Anastasia asked.

“The connection that saved your life, that filled your Od with life, also brought with it all the pain and suffering he had endured. All the fears, trauma, and self-hatred. It flowed right into you. I’m sorry. He is sorry. But we have cursed you with our love,” Greed held onto her hand for dear life. “He blames himself for pushing you into insanity. He believes that the reveal of Return by Death has made you think that everything you’ve gone through is false.”

“Wait, that isn’t what I think at all!” Anastasia protested.

“But that is what Natsuki Subaru believes. He views you as his savior, his light, his one and only lover. But he cannot bear to think that he has mislead you. He thinks you are undeserving of him. That you deserve better. Natsuki Subaru’s desire is for your happiness. Your safety. And above all, for you to understand who he really is.”

Anastasia’s confusion must have been visible as Greed added succinctly, “He is a monster in every way, shape, or form.”

“That isn’t true!” Anastasia yelled, “Stop lying!”

“That is who Natsuki Subaru is. He is I, and I am him. I know it within my heart that Natsuki Subaru has thrown away all of his humanity, for your sake. He does not breathe, unless it is for you. He does not walk, unless it is for you. He does not die, unless it is for you. You are his everything and he will give you everything he has. That is his greed, his eternal desire.”

“…Why are you telling me this?” Anastasia couldn’t help but ask.

------------------------------

 “Please. Why are you telling me this?”

Anastasia’s voice started to drift, becoming lighter, ethereal, and not of this world, “…We hate ourselves. We cannot stand ourselves. We are a disgusting fool who only takes and takes and takes!” Anastasia grabbed his hand and knelt, “But even if we are the worst of the worst, we cannot bare the thought of you ever leaving us. So please. Do not leave us. Do not think of us as too good for you. We are worthless, selfish, and horrible. Do not think of us as someone who you should sacrifice yourself for. Please. Stop. Stop running away from us. Be with us forever. Proclaim yourself to us. Do not look at anyone else. We want you. We need you. We cannot live without you.”

------------------------

“…Why are you telling me this?”

Greed’s voice became darker, deeper, as if drenched in shadows, “He hates himself. He deems himself worthless. He is a fool who only gives and gives and gives!” Greed knelt onto the ground before her, “But even if he does not deserve you. He will do all he can to make you happy. So please. Use him. Do not waste your time nor your life, drowning to save him. He is not worthy of such care. He does not need to be saved. Please. Stop. Stop running towards him. Let him fall forever. Denounce his presence. Do not look at him as a hero. He wants you. You do not need him. You can live without him.”

------------------------------

“When we lost our name. When we were alone for a whole month, the pain was too difficult. At first, we were determined. We had obstacles before. We’ve dealt with loss before. We’ve had nothing before. This should be easy. We were Anastasia Hoshin, Goddess of Commerce, second coming of Hoshin.”

------------------------------

“When he lost his name, when he was thrown in a cell with no one to care for him, it was finally too much. In the beginning, he did not give up. This was just like all the other times. He was alone before, lost all his companions, and dealt with the pain of being forgotten. This was nothing. It should be easy. He was Natsuki Subaru, Rem’s Hero, Emilia’s Knight.”

------------------------------

“…But we were not Anastasia Hoshin. Not anymore. We had no connections, no history, no money. Even the insignia would no longer work. We were just like a hyena again. We had nothing. It should have been easy, but it was not! The memories kept flooding into us. We couldn’t handle it. We couldn’t handle the idea that everything we ever worked for was all gone in a blink of an eye. It would have been fine if we just lost our money and power. But Ricardo? Mimi? Tivey? Julius? That we could not bear. Our relationships would not be the same. Even if we tried to reconnect, it would never be the same. The Triplets would not see us like family. Ricardo would not see us like a daughter. And Julius would never see us as his Lady! We should have been satisfied with just a small connection…but it wasn’t enough. It was never enough. And so we ran away.”

------------------------------

“…But he wasn’t Natsuki Subaru, not anymore. It was just like when he first arrived but worse. Because even Satella no longer remembered him. He messed up. He pushed Felix’s buttons too far. And the poor healer couldn’t handle the effects of Gluttony and lashed out. He died. He expected to revive a day before or hopefully before his imprisonment. But he didn’t. Just a few seconds. Again. And again. And again. And again. And again. Dying endlessly to the feeling of his nerves being fried. It was too much. By the time he escaped, his mind was barely coherent. Return by Death was malfunctioning. It sent him back randomly. But always within the prison. He kept messing up and he couldn’t solve his problems anymore because Felix was too paranoid and Gluttony’s fangs were too entrenched. He didn’t want to see those cold stares from his friends anymore! He begged for someone to save him. He didn’t want to kill Felix. He didn’t want to hurt his friends. He was not enough. And Envy answered.”

------------------------------

“Do you see? We abandoned our family, all because of our intense hunger for more! Stop looking at us like we deserve better. We don’t! Stay with us. Be ours.”

------------------------------

“Do you see? Because of his greed, he lost everything. Stop looking at him as if he deserves better. He doesn’t. Let him suffer in Hell. You don’t belong here.”

------------------------------

“We would destroy everything that makes you unhappy. Carve a little part of the world to keep you safe. Let us make you happy.

------------------------------

“He would slaughter all in his path to reach you. He would pave the road to your ascension in blood and terror, if it would give you peace. Let him make you happy.

------------------------------

“We love you.”

------------------------------

“He loves you.”

------------------------------

“So please.”

------------------------------

“So please.”

------------------------------

“Do not die for us.”

------------------------------

“Do not kill yourself for him.”

------------------------------

“Please. Please. Please,” Anastasia muttered endlessly in Subaru’s arms. He doesn’t remember when he started clinging onto her so desperately, but it did not matter. Subaru heard her cries, her pleas, her inner most thoughts. He won’t abandon her. Never. Ever. Even if his entire being screams at him to let her go, if she wishes for it, he’ll forever attach himself to her.

“I won’t. I promise, I won’t,” Subaru whispered. He looked down at Anastasia, hoping his words would calm her down.

Only to realize, she was no longer there. No. Someone was in his arms, but it wasn’t her. Blonde hair, white dress.

“Oh thank Od, we’ve finally taken back control,” Louis said as she looked up at him, smiling. Subaru tried to let go. It was easy when he did not have half of his appendages anymore.

“Ah finally~,” Louis stretched as Subaru tumbled backwards onto the floor. “We almost lost ourselves. Who knew that girl had such a strong desire that it would nearly eclipse ours? A shame given how much she wastes it on such nonsense.”

“Y-you…” Subaru could barely speak, it felt like his mind was collapsing. His body could not move, despite no sense of pain or shock coursing through his body. His arm was gone, his leg devoured, and yet he felt nothing. Physically nothing, mentally it felt like he was melting.

“Shhh,” Louis said, a finger to her lips as she stood over Subaru’s body. “It will be all over soon.”

“W-what are you doing here?”

“We should be asking you that,” Louis said as her lips turned into a frown, “Your little scheme brought you right into little Ana’s Od. We would have devoured you immediately if it wasn’t for your connection and that damned Hand of the Hunter.” Louis spat onto the floor, “Whatever you did, put us into some form of hibernation while little Ana’s personality started to fester in us. We woke up as some kind of version of her. So weird, we really did become her. We then latched onto her memories, acting like her because of your King’s Authority. It’s disgusting how your desire is so strong that it was even able to influence other Witch Factors.”

Subaru realized who this was, “You’re Gluttony aren’t you? Not the Archbishop, but the Witch Factor itself!”

Louis laughed as she clapped her hands, “Amazing job! We only had to lead you to such a conclusion. You really are a complete dumbass for it to take you this long to understand. How disappointing. Imagine how your beloved would feel if she was here. She would be like,” Louis shifted her head into Anastasia’s, becoming some weird chimera version of her, “You fucking idiot! Use your brain! I taught you better than this!” She then morphed back and laughed more.

“You fucker, I’m going to kill you!” Subaru’s goal was right here. If he could either kill this thing or punt it out of Anastasia, then they could figure out a way to do the same for the rest of his friends. He just needed to…to…to…

“None of that,” her voice drifted into his skull. He felt like his mind was being erased, piece by piece, “You can’t control us.” Louis waved her hand in the air. The world shifted as she spoke, changing to various different environments, “You aren’t king of this world anymore. These memories are ours to rule over. And without your little connection,” Louis held up the broken thread of light that was slowly dissipating into motes, “You have no authority over us.”

“Stop…it…” He needed to do something. Anything.

“It’s okay. You won’t have to worry about a thing anymore. We’ll finish what our dear brother started, leaving you as an empty shell,” Louis said while grinning, her sharp teeth bared, “But first, let’s finish our appetizer. And I know just where she is.”

Louis’s body transformed, becoming a writhing mass of shadows, flickers of various animals and beasts formed momentarily before dissipating back into formless darkness. Several copies of Louis popped out of the shadows. The eldritch abomination dived into Subaru’s torso, as the other versions of Louis laughed in the background. That horrendous laughter echoed through his ears as his conscience slowly disappeared into nothingness.

----------------------

“What’s going on?!” Anastasia could only panic as Greed’s body was convulsing. What was happening to the Greed Witch Factor? “No, no, no! Please—”

Before she could finish her words, darkness burst from Subaru’s abdomen. The shadows writhed in the air, its shape lingered momentarily on various forms: snake, whale, rabbit. The rabbit remained for a few moments before its shadowy head began to devour itself, eating its own flesh starting from the legs and working up the body until it was nothing but a head that was constantly biting at its own neck stump. Cracks began to form along the rabbit’s head before it broke open. Revealing a child with long blonde hair and a white dress, floating in mid-air, and landing right in front of Anastasia. Her voice was manic as she shrieked with glee, “Yes! We knew it! We are a genius!” She looked around triumphantly, “If her soul was not within her Od, it must be in his!” The child finally turned to Anastasia, “Hello, again.”

“H-hello? Who are you?” Anastasia stuttered, too shocked by the turn of events to comprehend what was happening.

Louis smirked as she bowed in front of Anastasia, “It seems we must introduce ourselves, yet again. Louis Arneb, Archbishop of the Witch Cult, representing Gluttony.” She then thought for a moment before shrugging, “Or the Witch Factor of Gluttony. Or the Archbishop of Satiation.” As she introduced herself, her flesh molded slightly, her face extended and drooped. Anastasia thought she was seeing an illusion until the morphed flesh separated from Louis and became its own blond-haired child. It then ran over to Greed’s—no, Subaru’s— catatonic body and began gnawing at his leg. “Or perhaps the Beast. Our names are vast and we have no preference.”

Anastasia reacted appropriately, “Get the fuck off him!” She scrambled to her feet and was about to kick the child, until the first version of Louis slammed into her body, sending Anastasia tumbling away from Subaru. By the time Anastasia recovered, she saw that the copy of Louis had made another version of herself. And another. And another. And another. All of whom were biting and devouring Subaru piece by piece.

“Can’t let you do that~,” Louis said in a sing-a-long voice, “We can’t let the King recover until I finish up here. We might not be able to kill him, but suppressing the little shit should be easy.” She pointed at Anastasia, “And as for you, would you like to play a game?”

“You fucking monster,” Anastasia spat. She didn’t care who this was. Whatever it was doing, it was hurting Subaru. And it needed to die.

Louis chuckled, “What was it that our little Poobaru says? Pot, kettle? Am I using it right?”

“I’ll kill you!” Anastasia was back on her feet and sprinting towards Louis.

Louis grabbed her by the throat and lifted her up, “He really is your weakness. You’re not even thinking rationally. What made you think running at an Archbishop was a good idea? Most people would run away.” Louis’s smile got even wider, “You know what, that’s a good idea for a game. Better than hide and seek with that worthless knight, Julius.” Louis threw Anastasia to the ground and snapped her fingers.

Several Louis clones lifted their heads from their Subaru-shaped meal, all staring at the original. Louis pointed her finger at Anastasia and spoke aloud,

“Run.”

They all turned towards Anastasia and smiled.

 

Chapter 54: Falling from ______

Summary:

Anastasia is reaching the end of her journey...

Chapter Text

Anastasia could not feel exhaustion and yet her legs felt like they could drop any moment. Running as fast as possible, dashing over boxes and broken rocks. She couldn’t understand where she was running. The scene shifted every time she blinked. First it was the Royal Capital of Lugunica. Next it was Banan. And then Priestella. Royal Capital. Banan. Priestella. Again and again. The environment melted around her, architecture twisted and bent, trees sprouting from houses. It was as if the whole world was chasing after her. And maybe it was.

“You can run! You can hide! But you can’t escape~,” a chorus of voices behind her said in unison, “Run, run, run! We’ll find you either way!” Anastasia took a brief glance to look back and regretted her decision. Those blonde children were running on all-fours, chasing after her like a pack of hounds. As they ran after her, their numbers multiplied by the second, slowly morphing from a rush of beasts into a wave of death, clawing and climbing over each other in furious motion. Hundreds of hands and feet moving as one, clones that were unluckily on the bottom were crushed to death but quickly replaced by several others. It was a horror show manifested into reality. And Anastasia did not dare to look back again, pushing as much strength into her legs as possible to run as fast as she could.

Anastasia jumped over a pile of corpses, as a fire burst next to her. A dragon’s roar could be heard in the distance. Cultists were slaughtering people left and right beside her. She couldn’t stop to stare. Any mistake would be her death sentence. Whatever Gluttony did, it was devouring the Greed Witch Factor and keeping it restrained. Gluttony could control this reality more than Greed ever could. She needed to figure out a plan. Try to get Greed away from them. It wasn’t a good plan, but it was better than nothing. She just needed to find a way out—

She tripped on nothing and fell into the void. Bracing herself for impact…that never came.

She looked around struggling to see anything at all. But saw nothing. Just pitch black darkness. It felt so familiar and so strange. Like she had been here several times before. It wasn’t like she was floating or falling in air. No. It was as if the shadows shifted around her, acting as some sort of river of nothingness, slowing and resisting her descent. She could swim, despite not knowing where up is anymore. The hole she fell through was nonexistent. For a while, it felt like time had stopped.

“Where are you?” A voice drifted into Anastasia’s ear, like a droning echo from the beyond. Anastasia moved her head to the source but found nothing, “Where are you? Where are you? Where are you?” The voice repeated those three words incessantly. Drowning out Anastasia’s thoughts as the words pounded through her skull. The voice was unpleasant, sad, melancholic, and above all, pissing her off by the second. Like the world around her, the sound was familiar, the oppressive feeling around her was familiar. Everything was familiar. And it only took her a moment to connect why.

The taboo.

Whatever other thoughts she had were interrupted by a grasp to her throat. Hundreds of shadowy hands materialized from the depths of this cold abyss. For a second, Anastasia thought the Louis horde had followed her inside and found her. But she was wrong. It was something far worse.

“You. Not you,” the voice was close to her ear, but no face appeared. Only a veil of darkness, “You’re not him. You,” suddenly bloodlust encompassed her body. Anastasia could feel the hand tighten around her windpipe, ready to end her life in an instant. But just as suddenly as the wrath of the shadows appeared, it completely disappeared, “You…No. No. No! NO! LEAVE!” The voice cried out, the hands dissipated as her body was thrown across the endless sea of nothing. Before suddenly everything returned to normal, her body scrapped across the floor of a house.

Anastasia looked around confused. The world of darkness was gone, replaced by the quaint little living room that she had become accustomed to in Banan. Panting and massaging the imprint left on her throat, her mind was racing.

What was that? Who was she talking about? Why was she trying to kill me? Why didn’t she kill me? What the—

“Oh, Ana-chan~? Where are you~?” Louis’s voice broke her mental spiral. Anastasia braced herself, holding her breath as the voices of hundreds of children echoed through the nearby window. She desperately crawled to the wall and did not make a sound. The stampede of hands and feet sprinting past the building made her heartbeat quicken. “Come out, come out, wherever you are!” She could hear them sniffing the air, trying to locate her presence. A few seconds passed by in silence.

And then the splatter of a body hitting the wall next to her reverberated throughout the room. She heard Louis screech, “Where the hell did you go?!” Anastasia could hear Louis growl and roar with rage. Nearby windows broke as debris and even more bodies slammed into the buildings around her. The little girl was having a tantrum. She could vaguely hear Louis’s teeth grind as the wave of copies ran past her window, hoping to locate her once more.

Anastasia waited as long as she could before finally letting out a breath. That was too close. Okay…okay. Let’s think. What the hell did I just see?

Barring the fact that Gluttony can just duplicate itself infinitely, there was that shadowy presence. If it was related to Subaru’s taboo, it must be connected to Return by Death. And if that’s the case.

That must have been his Witch Factor.

His secret one, besides Sloth and Greed. What did Guese say?

“Sloth, Greed, and two others. No. Three.”

Yes. Three. If Gluttony was included in that, then only two remain. If one allowed Subaru to use Return by Death, then she only needed to find the other one. The problem was she didn’t know if this one was friendly like Greed and Sloth, or an enemy like the others. It was infuriating to her that she had no easy way forward. If she were to continue Sloth’s plan, she would need to hunker down and wait until he returns. With Guese’s help, she could save Greed and use her memories to figure a way out of here. The only problem was where to hide. This was not a secure location.

“Hello?” Case in point, Anastasia did not even hear the door open as someone stepped through. Her instincts flared as she was ready to jump out the window and begin the chase again. Only for her heart to stop at the sight of who just walked in.

“Ana-pop? Is that you?” Salt and pepper hair tied back into a ponytail. A part of his bangs left to cover his eye partially. Covered in scars that barely poke out of his haori. Sharp eyes that were softened by the kindness in his irises. She could drink in his appearance for days, months, years, no. Eternity. She didn’t realize how much she dearly missed her beloved until she saw his true form once more. If this was the real him, she would have thrown her whole body towards him, wrapped him up, and never let go.

“Get the fuck out of his body, you disgusting cultist,” Anastasia snarled. But Anastasia knew better. She was no fool. Even on the off chance his real soul somehow made it into this world, her mind did not lie to her.

Subaru stepped back alarmed, “A-Ana-pop?! What’s wrong? Why are you looking at me like that?”

“Stop it. Whatever you think this is, it isn’t going to work on me. I know who my husband is. And you aren’t him.”

“How? How could you say something like that? Can’t you recognize me?”

Anastasia was ready to jump out the window, but her rage bade her to say one last comment, “The way you look at me. Subaru can’t help but stare at my face but you keep looking away every other second. The second I called you a cultist, Subaru’s hand would have drifted to his arm. But your hands did nothing. And the way you’re standing is all wrong, it’s too tall, too straight, he’d be slouching slightly. You’re nothing like him.”

“…You both are insane,” the Subaru in front of her dropped the act, sighing, “Always ruining our fun. Well, no matter.” He snapped his fingers, “It doesn’t change the result.”

Anastasia was about to jump to the side but was halted by a hand clutching her leg. A Louis burst from the floor, hands keeping Anastasia from moving, baring her teeth in a wide grin as several others burst from the ceiling and walls, grabbing at Anastasia and pushing her to the ground. The Subaru in front of her shifted from the man she loved into the horrible gremlin she hated with a passion. Louis smiled with glee as she leaned down towards Anastasia’s face, “You really thought you could escape? We told you. No matter where you go, we always know. We don’t know how you were able to teleport like that but that isn’t going to happen again.”

Louis snapped her fingers and the world shifted from brown wooden walls to white and grey. A snowy field as far as the eye can see, the only surrounding fauna being a nearby forest. Anastasia’s head was pulled up by her hair, “You bastards! I’ll kill you­—” One of the Louises punched her in the throat and gagged her mouth with a hand.

“Unfortunately, we don’t know if we were born out of wedlock or not. So sorry,” Louis said, “Now shut up and watch.”

Watch what? All Anastasia could see was a version of Subaru from the past walking through this white landscape. He was wearing his old tracksuit so this must be when he was still in Lugunica. But Anastasia did not recall there ever being a blizzard in the last year. Not to this level. She watched as Subaru trudged forward while Louis spoke, “We were planning on having some more fun. Chasing you, pretending to be your loved ones, making you lose your mind. But you just keep ruining everything, just like that horrid boytoy of yours. So we thought of a solution.”

Subaru stopped walking as he was met by a strange sight. A bunny with red eyes and a small horn.

Louis’s tone turned malicious, “If you really want to indulge yourself in his memories, seeing everything that he ever faced, we’ll let you. We’ll even give you a special highlight reel of our favorite moments.”

“A rabbit? Why is there a rabbit here?” The memory of Subaru said as he reached towards the white bunny.

“Just don’t choke on it.”

-------------------------------

Julius did not know what was going on anymore.

He had barely recovered from the revelation that his own candidate had been missing for several months, ever since the end of the Battle of Priestella. Now he was standing only meters away from mortal death (separated only by a thin wall of wind), orchestrated by four all-powerful warriors having a furious battle right in front of him. Halibel, the Admirer. Zarestria, the Great Spirit of Wind. And the two Archbishops of Gluttony who were responsible for his greatest mistake. He couldn’t keep his eyes off of them.

“How annoying, I suppose,” the words of Beatrice knocked him out of his trance as he quickly got on his knees to help the little spirit with whatever she needed.

“Beatrice-sama, what is wrong—”

“That wasn’t meant for you, purple nuisance,” Beatrice sweated as her eyes glanced up at Julius, “And Betty told you to stay as far away from me as possible, in fact!”

Julius quickly obliged, scooting away towards the wall again, past his comrades who lay unconscious near him. He felt tremendous guilt for their current status, half of them still covered in dried blood around their orifices, a remnant of whatever curse possessed them. It took the combined effort of Julius and Beatrice to knock them out one by one while the strongest of Kararagi kept Gluttony busy. Julius could barely keep his eyes open, too much mana used to recover from the grievous wound and to heal his fallen comrades. And yet, he couldn’t keep his eyes off the two laying next to Beatrice: his Lady, Anastasia Hoshin and her husband, Natsuki Subaru.

Husband. The word still felt foreign to Julius’s mouth.

“Beatrice-sama, how are they?”

Beatrice did not look up this time, “Sister is trying her best but whatever Betty’s Subaru did, it put them into a comatose state.”

He couldn’t help but wonder, “Is there anything I can do?”

“Like Betty said, shut up and stay away from me. That’s all you need to do, in fact,” Beatrice’s words were cutting but her meaning was practical. Julius was useless as is. He needed to recover his strength and was deadweight if he even considered joining the fight outside. Clones materialized by the dozen, raining shrapnel and kunai all around while Lye danced between each version of Halibel, parrying blades and striking blows one after the other. He could see Roy shifting through reality, disappearing and manifesting across short distances rapidly while dodging all of Zarestia’s wind blades, the spirit carving scars into the stone floor and walls like an indoor hurricane. It frustrated Julius to be so useless.

He could hear Beatrice sigh, “…What do you wish to know?”

“Pardon?”

“Betty is as useless as you are right now. Only acting as a mana battery while Betty’s sister tries to break through their Od’s,” Beatrice was cradling a white fox in her hands as it slept on top of Subaru and Anastasia’s hands, interlocked, “Betty knows how you must be feeling. So ask, I suppose.”

Julius thought for a moment. He had multiple questions burning into his skull. What happened to his Lady? Is she hurt? Was she captured? How did she escape? Those clothes, she must have been in Kararagi. Did she stay there for her own safety? Was she scared to leave? Did she meet her husband there? What did she do there? Why did she not contact them? Why did she leave Lugunica? Why did she not return to them? Did they meet and rebuff her? Did Julius do something wrong? No, of course he did something wrong. He abandoned her through his indecisiveness. He should have chased after Gluttony when it grew tired of him. And because of his mistake, his Lady had become lost to the world.

All of these questions, but only one was said, “Have they married, yet?” He nearly blushed at his choice.

Beatrice raised an eyebrow, “That’s your question?”

“A-apologies, I did not mean—”
“It’s fine. To answer your question, no. They have not. They just became engaged only a week or two ago.”

A part of Julius felt relieved. He was worried he had missed such an important moment in his Lady’s life. Though it was slightly soured by the fact that he had been unable to judge the man who wooed his candidate in such little time. He didn’t doubt his Lady’s tastes, but he did want to have a little fun, perhaps scaring the poor lad into taking care of Anastasia like a princess, as she deserved. Another part of him—the particular aspect that he pushed deep within himself—was shamefully disappointed when hearing about the engagement.

He could not deny that his feelings for his candidate had fluttered into romance from time to time, but there was little room for either of them to partake in said romance. Anastasia with her candidacy and Julius with his knightly duties. Such thoughts were merely dalliances in his mind when boredom crept in. What ifs. Possibilities. Nothing real besides the occasional flirtation. And despite his desires, he couldn’t help but be happy that his Lady found love within the murk of despair. It’s why his next question was so poignant.

“Is she happy?”

Beatrice stayed quiet for a time. Though the wind wall blocked all noise, the vibrations of the battle outside rocked the very foundations of the tower. Her voice was quiet but reverberating, “That’s a question you should ask her yourself, I suppose. In Betty’s eyes, Ana has suffered quite a lot during her time away.”

“…I see.”

“But despite that, she has found her own source of happiness with not just Subaru, but those two other idiots fighting out there. Betty suggests not comparing yourself to them.”

“I did not mean to imply that.”

“Betty is not stupid. But if you wish to deny your own self, Betty would be a hypocrite to lambast you for it, in fact.”

Julius pondered her words. It felt rancid for him to think, for such words would be shameful when spoken. So he quietly kept them to himself, looking back towards the battle. Where Zarestia had created a miniature tornado that chased the two Archbishops. Upon further investigation, the little natural disaster was filled with a multitude of kunai that every so often shot out towards one of the Gluttonies. Halibels dashed in and out of shadows and secluded areas, taking pot shots at either Roy or Lye as they effortlessly kept up with the assault. If only Julius could muster enough strength, call upon one of his buds, and just make an opportunity—

“Enough,” Beatrice’s voice anchored him to reality again, “Do not distract them. Tia is already double tasking our protection while assisting the mutt. You will do them no service intervening and causing a disturbance, I suppose.”

Then what can he even do now! Is what he wanted to say, but that would be rude to a powerful spirit such as Beatrice. Instead, he said, “Zarestia-sama and Halibel-san are as powerful as I imagined. While I faced the Gluttonies before, I did not expect them to be so well-matched.”

“Do not get the wrong idea. Betty has faced that disgusting fellow over there,” with a free hand, Beatrice pointed at Lye as he laughed with glee, “Tia would eviscerate both of them without a sweat given better circumstances. Unfortunately, she cannot use her magic to the fullest extent due to the necessity of keeping everyone else alive. Not even mentioning how destroying the tower would be detrimental to the pair of monsters downstairs.”

“Monsters?” Julius could only think of one person that could possibly be called, “The Witch of Envy?”

Beatrice nodded, “The Sword Saint is trying his best to keep her occupied while we settle things here. Destroying the building that was specifically made to incapacitate her would ruin our chances of surviving this at all. Betty is just surprised that murderous wind idiot understands this innately, in fact.”

A battle between the strongest right beside him, and a battle between two behemoths below. Julius had rarely felt so small since he fought the Blue Lightning all those years ago. It was infuriating, “Then all we can do is wait, it seems.”

“Yes, I suppose.”

It was maddening. He hated this feeling. To simply watch as events passed by, unable to participate in fear of losing the broader picture. Weak, tired, filled with regret. Julius could barely stand on two legs, as well as stand his own weakness. So much so, he couldn’t help but blurt out, “Do you think she will forgive me?”

He cursed himself. An agonizing embarrassment to utter such a blatant insult to Anastasia. It did not matter how he felt. Yet still, Beatrice was magnanimous to respond, “Betty does not know. From the little time Betty has known her, that girl holds grudges. She does not let things go easily, in fact.”

That he can agree on, “Yes. I have seen such anger before. Woe to any who faces the brunt of it.”

“However, Betty has also heard from the girl’s own lips that she would do anything to return to Lugunica. Perhaps you may not believe it, but that girl still thinks the world of her camp. Do not doubt her attachment to you all.”

“I do not doubt that Anastasia-sama cares for us,” Julius said, “But forgiveness is a different matter.”

“Betty understands. For the longest time, Betty could only dream of a past that never existed. Once that past returns, Betty will be sure to feel as hollow as you do now,” Beatrice said, “But that issue shall be faced when it happens. For now, Betty has done all she could. And despite how Betty does not deserve it, forgiveness was already gifted to me. It would be a disservice to languish in melancholy anymore, I suppose.”

“Melancholy…” Julius couldn’t help but laugh at the absurdity of this whole situation. It infected his next words, “Would Natsuki-sama be willing to grant me a place within the groomsmen?”

Beatrice smirked at him, “Ask Subaru yourself. Betty believes the answer will be as expected.” Julius could see there was something humorous there that he was not understanding. “Betty is curious, however. Why are you so fixated on the idea of the wedding?”

Besides it being the only normal topic that could be discussed without Julius feeling his heart squeeze to dust, he couldn’t help himself, “Can’t a knight admire the idea of his Lady finding romance within the abyss?” A cruel fantasy but one he couldn’t help but hope for, “If nothing else, the only worthwhile future I can see, is watching my Lady walk down the aisle with a smile on her face.”

“I agree! But I would prefer to be the groom than a groomsman. My only regret is not seeing Crusch in white before I died...”

Julius whipped his head around, looking for the source of that voice. But it disappeared just as quickly as it manifested. He had a feeling who that was, but it troubled him deeply about the implications. Once this is over, he would need someone to investigate his mind thoroughly.

“Seeing ghosts?” Beatrice asked.

Julius tightened his grip on his sword, “…Possibly. Perhaps this tower has left more of an impact on me than I perceived.”

“Stay vigilant then. Even if this issue is resolved, we will most likely need to explore this whole building for a solution to our Witch problem. Betty is not looking forward to such tribulations, in fact.”

Neither was Julius. His focus returned to the two stars laying on the ground, linked to one another. Covered in grime and dirt, dark ink moving and twisting between their fingers. If there was nothing else he could do, Julius opted to simply pray. Pray that whatever his Lady and her husband were facing, would be resolved swiftly. And they would wake up from this twisted Hell together.

  1. 150. 150. 150. 150. 150. 150. 150.

“Hmm, wow. He died again. How surprising,” Louis’s voice was bored.

  1. 150. 150. 150. 150. 150. 150. 150.

“What do you mean you can’t find the Hunter? He should be in her soul! There’s not much in there,” Louis shouted beside Anastasia. She was talking to another copy of herself. Or at least, that was what Anastasia assumed. Her attention was not on them but on the visions in front of her.

Louis patted Anastasia’s head as she couldn’t help but stare ahead, “You keep watching. We’ll be right back. You all, keep watch of her and make sure she doesn’t miss anything. And you guys, make sure Greed doesn’t get up.” The sound of gnashing teeth and viscera splattering on the floor was the only response.

The various Louis clones restraining Anastasia’s body, keeping her arms tied behind her back and body planted onto the floor, her eyelids peeled open, nodded at their main progenitor as Anastasia felt that visceral feeling of the Witch Factor worming its way into her soul, corrupting her with each movement. Anastasia would have usually squirmed at the feeling, but not now. Her mind was too focused. She watched as the memory of Subaru in front of her caressed her hand at the dead of night. Crying as the memory of herself took her last breath.

And watched as Subaru in one practiced motion, slit his own throat.

  1.  

 

Chapter 55: Let Me Into ______

Summary:

Make it stop.

Chapter Text

I am different.

That was the thought Anastasia so desperately wanted to believe in. She wanted to think she was smarter, more capable, more brilliant. Egotistical, yes. But factually incorrect? No. Her success through life cemented this. So, it was no wonder her self-confidence was so high. She couldn’t help but think that she could do the impossible, that not only was she the second coming of Hoshin, but that she could surpass his legacy and then some. 

Not only in business but in all aspects of her life. Relationships, skills, and even love.

So, as she learnt of Subaru’s past, as she slowly fell for him, she couldn’t help but scoff at the idiocy of his camp. How could they ignore the obvious signs that he was unwell? And if they didn’t, how could they live with themselves in being so useless? It was absurd. If Anastasia was in their place, she could have been so much better. Even as she watched his past in-person, her opinion did not change. In fact, it was exacerbated. Her contempt for Emilia and Rem especially increased with each death she saw. Subaru was at fault for many of his decisions. But those two were just as responsible. It was unfair but Anastasia could care less. Subaru was hers now. She would do better.

“Stop,” Anastasia pleaded.

“Hmm, nah. Let’s watch a little more. I want to see if he falls over and dies or not,” Louis said with glee.

…But Anastasia was wrong. She wasn’t better. She was just like them. She was a fool who thoughtlessly believed she could save Subaru from himself. That she could not only be his light, but someone he could rely on. She had the skills, the knowledge, the smarts. But it meant nothing if all she did is chain him to even more suffering.

Louis made sure she knew that. Her control over the world was precise, fine-tuned. She could easily fast forward the timeline without overloading Anastasia’s mind with knowledge. A full mental collapse would have been a mercy compared to the hellish visions she saw. Of Subaru being eaten alive. Of Subaru’s head being crushed alongside a whole crowd of people. Of Subaru being tortured endlessly by Felix.

No wonder he was so adamant to ignore that period of his life. She watched as Subaru’s first loop in that prison began so innocently. He was so optimistic. He truly believed that everything would work out. Because why wouldn’t it? He’d been through similar before. People forgetting him wasn’t new. People seeing him suspiciously wasn’t new. His friends and allies betraying him wasn’t new. He just needed to win them over again. He didn’t even waver when his old camp all met him slowly, cautious but curious of this boy who expressed familiarity towards them.

But a whole month passed with no progress. Despite the promises—Reinhard and Julius made vows to help him—bureaucracy and sloth won out. Crusch’s ailment was progressing and Felix was not handling it well. 

Subaru’s constant pleas were not helping. He didn’t know it back then, but Gluttony’s effects were invasive and self-correcting. Subaru’s existence was an anomaly and Felix’s brain could not handle it. It made him violent. Coupled with the stress of his Lady’s impending death, and the result was obvious: Felix fried Subaru’s nerves not out of malice but desperation. He needed something. Anything. And no matter what Subaru said, it only made his mind more addled. 

When Subaru first died, he vowed to not make the same mistakes. He tried to reason with everyone. Tried to get Felix some help. Informed people that his jailer was mentally unwell. None of it worked. He got close, so many times was he almost able to persuade Emilia, Julius, Reinhard, and all the others onto his side. Only to have Gluttony mess everything up. Anastasia realized it sooner than Subaru did, he was ruined from the start. Gluttony’s mental barrier prevented anyone from fully accepting his existence, especially in such a short period of time since he lost his name.

Coupled with Return by Death malfunctioning, causing his loops to be unstable: sending him to random checkpoints, looping him in six second intervals where he experienced death several times over, constantly having to keep track of different timelines. The strain on him was immense and Subaru was not able to cope. By the thirtieth loop, he begged for it to all stop. For a chance to just let the suffering end. To not have his friends look at him with disdain anymore or Felix to torture him anymore. He prayed for the one person who could possibly save him.

And she answered. 

Return By Death was fixed and Subaru was sent to the very beginning of his tenure at the prison. He didn’t question why the Witch didn’t send him back earlier. All he wanted was for the pain to stop. So instead of trying so hard like before. He gave up. He experimented with his new Greed authority. Watched and listened. His final loop was spent being a quiet prisoner who goaded his captors into exhaustion. He let time progress while preventing as much conflict as possible. And it worked.

He waited until the perfect moment and escaped. That should have been the ending. Subaru ran away only to never return. But as always, nothing turned out as expected. He never expected a candidate to be alone in the middle of the night. Nor did he expect to become attached. Nor to fall in love. It wasn’t fate but just circumstance. And he paid the price for it.

“Stop it, please,” she begged.

“Hmm, nope! Look, his legs are starting to fall apart. Which one of us bet his legs would pop off? You two? Okay, which one bet the closest to six hours,” Louis joked with her other selves.

The bandit encounter was worse than she ever thought possible. Subaru died two times. The first loop, they were caught unaware and forced to do their bidding. From Anastasia’s memory, it seemed they were unlucky. Beatrice and Eridna just barely missing them as the bandits captured Subaru and Anastasia, bringing them back to their camp. They fortunately did not put Subaru in harms way. Anastasia…Anastasia did not want to think of what she did to make sure Subaru was kept safe. Perhaps nothing happened. At the very least, Subaru never saw, and that was enough.

Subaru was not satisfied, however. As soon as he connected the possible dots, she watched as he immediately bit off his tongue and started killing bandits left and right. Even though they were able to escape, their efforts were short-lived as they were hunted down and killed. The second loop did not fare better. Subaru’s visceral reaction to dying led to her moving her head an inch too close. What would have been a harmless warning shot turned into a near-fatal headshot to the eye. Subaru did not react well either, slaughtering only a few bandits before the rest ran off. Subaru had a choice to make: leave Anastasia to die or put her out of her misery. Those would have been the smartest choices. Anastasia wanted him to make one of those choices. But of course the idiot—the absolute moron—decided to take a third option and run towards the nearest village as fast as possible. All while bleeding and dying. They had no carriage, their earth dragons shot and killed, and no knowledge of Beatrice or Eridna’s whereabouts. So Subaru ran.

And ran. And ran. And ran.

“Stop. Please, just stop,” Anastasia whimpered.

“Aww, are you sick of watching your husband slowly kill himself for you?” Louis mocked Anastasia, “Too bad. Hey let’s watch something more fun.”

Louis snapped her fingers and immediately shifted the scene to Subaru getting mauled by rabbits. His screams pierced Anastasia’s eardrums as she begged, “No, no, no! I’m sorry! MAKE IT STOP!”

“Hmm,” Louis made a goofy face, “Should we? But we’re just getting to the best part. You see, right here is when one of the rabbits digs right through his torso and burrows up his stomach and into his esophagus. You can just see it bulge right out of there and,” Louis made a popping sound as a burst of blood rained down on them, “We love that part.”

Anastasia screamed, “I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I’m—”

Louis rolled her eyes, “Ugh, we hate it when you’re like this. Fine, we shall skip ahead. It was getting boring seeing him run for nearly ten hours straight. We don’t understand how stupid someone can be. It’s not like you were even going to die. If he just killed himself, everything would have been back to normal,” Louis picked her ear with her finger, grimacing at Subaru. She then lit up like a Christmas tree, “Oh! We have an idea. Let’s watch your first weeks in Banan. That was a special treat.”

“No, please, no,” Anastasia tried to look away but the other Louises forced her head forward, laughing as they pulled her eyelids back.

The environments morphed, showing a memory of Anastasia and Subaru traveling to Priestella. Louis frowned, “Ew. Skip.” It showed their quiet moments together, sleeping under the stars, “Skip.” Her and Subaru holding each other close under blankets, “Oh my Od, skip!” Subaru and Anastasia eating together. He laughed as she got annoyed at something he said, “Skip, skip, skip! Seriously, who watches this crap! It’s so gross. We want carnage, suffering, fighting! Not all this romance bullshit. Oh here we go.” They were now in Banan.

No. Don’t pervert my memories. I don’t want to know. I don’t want to see how I failed him. Please. I don’t want to think about this. I don’t want to see this! I just want to go home! I want to go home right now!

Anastasia tried not to think. Louis would not let that happen. She gripped Anastasia’s hair and pulled her closer to the scene. Anastasia tried to ignore it, blank out her mind. “Oh no you don’t. If you’re not going to watch, we’ll help you out,” Louis said as she began to narrate, “So this is a story of two lonely idiots who decided to be all codependent and crap before yadda yadda. None of that matters. What matters is how this dumbass right here,” Louis pointed at Subaru, “Decided to waste his power by doing nothing for nearly a whole week. He tried to get a job. Failed. Tried to help find a house, failed. Tried to help you, failed. Got all depressed and so you took him on some stupid date that got him to slowly fall for you. Then you died because that copycat took one smell of the idiot.” She snapped her fingers, “Anyways, want to see how that happened?”

No—

“I heard a yes!”

A version of Subaru and Anastasia manifested into reality, the soft glow of lanterns illuminated them both under the night sky. Unlike her own memory of the festival, these versions wore kimonos and haoris that were a tad less fancy. Second-hand black and white, with some rips and tears, worn down by time. And yet the smiles on both their faces made Anastasia’s heart flutter. The gift, the rain, the kiss. She remembered it so clearly.

Subaru’s eyes were filled with shame, “…I don’t know what I’m doing anymore.”

“That’s okay,” Anastasia said as she patted his cheek, “You just need to keep moving forward. I told you, be greedy. And if you can’t do that, then just follow me. I’ll show you the way to live your life as happy as can be.”

Subaru chuckled, “You say it like it’s so easy.”

“Sometimes the hardest things are easy. You just have to take a leap of faith. And when you finally open your eyes, it was like that huge mountain was just a lump of dirt on the road.”

“You really like putting things in perspective. I feel like ever since I started traveling with you, things don’t seem as bad as they could be, if that makes sense,” Subaru said as he looked away. A thought occurred in his mind as his brow furrowed. He then muttered as he turned back to Anastasia, “Listen, if you don’t mind I—”

His words were cut short as he realized he was looking at nothing. Just a headless stump that still believed it was alive. He could barely react as his expression morphed into horror, his eyes glanced to the side and focused on a figure in white that whispered, “Die.”

Before he too was killed.

Louis yawned, “Anyway, that was the only cool part. The rest is boring. Guy gets revived, turns out that copycat was stalking him the entire time and kills him the second he comes back. Subaru runs away, he dies. Then he figures out how to escape this time because those spirits help out at the last second. Blah, blah, blah. Lots of stuff I don’t remember happen. He dies a few more times and meets that Halibel guy. Figures out how to hide his smell using flowers. Keeps trying to put you in a safe place only for you to ruin everything.”

“I…I ruin everything?” Anastasia repeated.

“Yep. He keeps trying to leave you at home or that temple or really anywhere. And you just keep following him and dying. Happens so many times. You guys got in tons of arguments,” she skipped ahead to another point in the timeline.

This time the memory of Anastasia and Subaru were pointing and scowling at each other within a dilapidated room.  Subaru yelled, “Why can’t you just understand that this is not your problem anymore?!”

“Not my problem?” Anastasia said in dismay, “Not my fucking problem?! Did you really just tell me that?! You know what’s my problem, you’re my problem. You keep running away and telling me nothing! How is that supposed to help our situation? I’m doing everything I can to help us survive and all you do is disappear time and time again!”

“I’m doing this so we can survive too! This is for your own good, just don’t worry about me. Ignore me. I’m not helpful anyways, you’d be better off without me,” Subaru said as he turned towards the door of their apartment.

Anastasia grabbed his hand, “Don’t you dare just leave again! You can’t just run off, expecting me to accept that! For my own safety?! What gives you the right to decide that? To leave me behind… just so you can die alone…”

Subaru stared at her, “I’m not,” he choked, “You don’t understand.”

“Then talk to me. Just talk to me please so I can!”

“…It’s pointless. You won’t ever understand. And that’s for the best. It’s better this way.”

“Subaru. Subaru!” Subaru didn’t turn around as the memory of Anastasia cried out. “Stop! Don’t! Don’t—” she sputtered, “don’t leave me alone. Please.”

Louis made a face, “Ugh. What was that word? Cringe? Yeah, cringe. Disgusting, honestly.” Louis leaned onto Anastasia’s head, “If you really wanted him to stay, you should have just manipulated him. Threatened you’d kill yourself. It worked wonders later. Though not in these loops. You just kept making Subaru’s life miserable.”

The memory changed to another scene, where dawn was encroaching the horizon. Subaru held onto a battered and mauled Anastasia as he himself had lost his arm and leg, his guts nearly spilling out from open wounds all over his torso. Even as he lay dying, his remaining arm would not let go of her. Nearby, the copycat lay dead as Halibel solemnly stood over her. A familiar little girl with spiral pigtails and a white fox wrapped around her neck was crying nearby.

“Please…live… don’t die… I wish I met you sooner… I’m sorry…in fact,” Beatrice cried to herself.

Halibel approached the two stars, “Are ya sure ya want this?”

Subaru’s eyes were lifeless, only focusing on the dead body of Anastasia that was still leaking blood onto the muddy streets. He nodded and didn’t say a word.

“…Sorry bout this, Su-san. If we meet again in another life, I’ll make sure ta keep ya safe. No matter the cost,” Halibel said. And with those final words, he tapped a needle into Subaru’s neck, painlessly sending him to the next loop.

Anastasia watched this all, trembling. Louis whistled, “Isn’t that funny? No matter what you did, you ended up being more of a load than any other person in his life. Always trying to help him, always trying to pay him back, trying to be useful. And all you do is make things worse. The more you tried to hold onto him, the more you killed him.” Anastasia wanted to die. She wanted to bite her tongue off. She hated this. She hated Louis. She hated everything. Most of all, she hated herself. Just kill her. Please, let this end. Louis chuckled, “Who am I kidding. Even if you did nothing, you would still hurt him. Your very existence pushed him into Hell. And I think it’s about time we showed you.”

314.

Subaru died 314 times.

For her.

314.

Even his time in prison, compounding all the different timespans, was only a measly eight months.

314.

  1. 314. 314. The number would not leave her head. Like a prayer or a mantra, she repeated it endlessly, ignoring all other stimuli. She watched as Subaru slowly lost touch with himself, with his humanity. As he killed himself like a machine, using every possible second to push his plans forward. He’d memorized plans, schematics, knowledge and pushed them forward with each iteration of his loops. Nothing was wasted. Even his enemies. He didn’t become a remorseless killer, but torture was not off the table. And he knew how to make people suffer.

He became a monster all for the small chance to save Anastasia’s life.

“Finally, we thought you would never break.” Louis stretched her limbs, “We were getting bored watching the same old thing over and over. Cutting back to the Great Rabbit every twenty loops didn’t help.” Some Louises poured out of Anastasia’s soul, all with frustrated expressions. The original clicked her tongue, “Shame. Even after all that time, the Hunter eludes us.” Louis kicked Anastasia’s torso.

Anastasia ignored her, continuing to mutter to herself, “314, 314, 314, 314…”

“Well, no matter. If he won’t come out, it changes nothing. We still have dinner to look forward to,” Louis smiled, “Our dear brothers have the wrong idea. It isn’t the quality of the food, nor the amount, it’s how you prepare the course that matters most. The people you dine with, the ingredients, the process. All of it culminates into a satisfying meal.”

“314, 314, 314.”

“Thank you Anastasia Hoshin, for the wonderful meal you will become. We will use your body well and take good care of your loved ones. Have fun watching from here, tsu~!” Louis unhinged her jaws as she prepared to feast upon Anastasia one last time. Just as her teeth were inches from Anastasia’s neck, a feather got caught in her throat.

She choked and spat out the sudden intrusion, “What the—who?”

“Louis Arneb. How flagrant your disregard for my wishes are. Did we not have a deal?” An otherworldly voice boomed from Anastasia. Louis eyes widened in recognition as soft tendrils made of light leaked from Anastasia’s body, slowly coalescing into a human shape. However, in the middle of its formation, eyes and wings pulsed and shuddered in and out of existence. Her body molded into distinct shapes before rubber banding back into humanity. It was as if she was rejecting a part of herself at every step of creation. Until finally, a beautiful woman with platinum hair, pale blue eyes, and a flowing white dress touched down onto this Od-forged world.

Louis bit back fear as she struggled to keep eye contact, “V-vainglory. We still do. But you told us we could do whatever we wanted.”

“Within limits. The limits being that you refrain from completely devouring her personality,” Pandora smiled as she always did, “I told you that you would have a new sister, not a slave.”

Louis muttered to herself, “What’s the difference?”

“Hm? Did you say something?”

“We said that you cannot just take away our meal like this. Even if we have a deal, our efforts must bear fruit! We are the Beast! We hunger for Satiation. Do not starve us just before we take a bite.”

Pandora cocked her head, “Hm, I see. Then in that case, perhaps it is best that you do not deal with such hunger pangs in the first place.”
Louis stared, “What?”

“Louis Arneb’s Gluttony Witch Factors should not be here. They should be in the Hall of—”

“Wait, wait, wait! Stop!” Louis begged, “We…we were being arrogant, Saintess. We apologize.”

Pandora’s smile became a little bit bigger, “Apology accepted. Now if you do not mind, I shall be relieving you of your tasks for now. Please continue devouring the Sage Candidate’s memories as we agreed.”

Louis appeared furious but only nodded as her response, motioning her clones to follow. The others dispersed from Anastasia’s body, leaving the girl sprawled out on the floor as a muttering mess. She glanced over to the side, the Greed Witch Factor was still being devoured by the Gluttony clones without pause.  Pandora approached Anastasia with agile steps, not even making a sound. She leaned down and inspected Anastasia’s body. Anastasia did not even notice, “314. 314. 314.”

“Do not hold a grudge against her. The Beast does not care besides devouring all in its wake, but Louis Arneb is different. That personality template felt threatened due to your intrusion. Your affinity to Gluttony is astounding to the point that you even rival Daphne.”

“314…314…314.”
