Pandora let out a breath before moving her hand through Anastasia’s hair, running her finger through those violet locks, humming to herself, “You have become so wonderful since I last saw you. Let me give you a gift.”

The air shifted slightly. “314­—” Anastasia’s mind spasmed, her mind began to reconstruct the memories that were once purged from her mind. She remembered. She lifted her head up and recognized Pandora’s presence, “The bird.”

Pandora nodded, “Yes, it has been a while. Have you been enjoying your journey so far?”

Anastasia stared blankly for a few moments. Her eyes were on the verge of tears, “No…this…was a nightmare.”

“I know. But this is what you wanted, is it not? To share his burdens, to understand him, to truly be on equal footing. This was the only way to accomplish such a momentous task. You have achieved so much.”

“But—no—I-I haven’t—this isn’t,” Anastasia stuttered, “I haven’t done anything good. This is not what I thought would happen.”

“Such is life,” Pandora said, “But you have done your best. Your choices were not wrong. Your desires, pure. Now all you have to do, is commit.”

“Commit?”

Pandora appeared as if she was glowing. Her presence brought comfort to Anastasia, soothing her mind and body. No longer did she feel the dread and despair that ached her entire soul. No. Everything was fine. And will be fine. From now until forever. Her voice drifted into Anastasia’s skull Pandora’s saccharine words invaded her very soul.

“Your love is not wrong. Think. Imagine. Believe. A world where you and your beloved are together. Where none of the pain you have ever felt will ever be repeated. I can give you a perfect world. Where you are happy. He is happy. Your children are healthy and happy. You can have this world so easily. Just by taking my hand, your happy ending is achievable. Pain. Misery. Hell? All of it is an illusion. I can give you the truth. You do not have to work for your happy ending. You can rest. Isn’t that what you want? To be free from all your burdens? To free your lover from this world’s burdens? It can happen. He no longer will have to bear everyone’s sins. He can be free. You can be responsible for that. You can pay him back for all of his pain and suffering. He won’t ever have to die for someone who betrays him, nor will he die for no reason, nor will he die for someone who does not care for him. Think of your ideal life. A life without fear that it will all shatter one day. This could be yours. You have the capability to make a life that others can only envy. An empire that spans the whole four nations. You and him can have it all. This greed of yours can finally be satisfied. You do not have to fight anymore, scrounge in the dirt, and beg for scraps. That life is behind you now. The fear of becoming someone like your beloved adopted Mother will be a thing of the past. Think not of the past, imagine your future. You are walking down the aisle with Ricardo; he is nearly brought to tears by the occasion. Mimi, Hetaro, Tivey. They are throwing flowers for each step you take. You are happier than anyone else. Julius is a groomsman, standing proud and trying his best to also stave off the tears in his eyes. Everyone is there to celebrate the beginning of your happiest days. But all you can do is stare at the man who has become your everything: Natsuki Subaru. He stands tall, his hair almost back to form, the scars of his past a distant memory. You seal your futures with a kiss and begin the rest of your lives together. The nights of passion are endless, and the days of bliss are heavenly. Soon, your efforts bring further blessings, through the birth of your children. A son and a daughter who mean the world to both of you. Your daughter has his hair and eyes but has your color. Your son has your hair and eyes but has his color. They do not have either of your broken and weakened gates. They are strong and healthy. They are loved, and they know they are loved. You raise them well. They do not hold any resentments towards you. They inherit your skills, your power, your relentless desires. They succeed in so many ways, where you do not. And you are proud of them for it. You watch as they grow older and leave the nest. Your bloodline will become the talk of legends. You joke of your aging body and he reminds you daily of his love. You do the same. Neither of you ever become sick of each other. Entranced by one another, your happiness never wilts. Your hair turns grey, the same as his. You shall live until either of you wishes to cease. And when one of you does, the other shall follow. Such an end brings you true joy. You have no enemies. They no longer exist. Anything that threatens such a future has perished. Or is in the process of becoming such a fate. The world has become your treasure trove, ready to be cracked open at a moment’s notice. Believe in what I say for you know it to be true. Don’t you hate it? Don’t you hate being so weak. Are you not tired of the constant suffering? You are tired of it all. Of being subservient to the whims of others. Of being useless in dangerous situations. Of being a scavenger who feeds upon the dying. You do not have to be someone who waits and watches, you can be the woman who shifts the world on its axis. This is your right, your ideal, your privilege. Your hunger can be satiated. You can feast on all that you see. Do you wish to know who Alec Hoshin really was? He was a weak man who could only cling onto the ideas of an outworlder and lacked purpose until Flugel came into his life. Hoshin of the Wilderness was a man who tripped his way into good luck. You shall surpass him in every way. No longer will people remember the surname of Hoshin by the man of four hundred years ago, instead they will pronounce your glory as the rightful conqueror of the West. A pure white queen who devours the world whole. And Subaru shall be right by your side, the quiet king of new nobility. Your reign shall be endless if you seek it. I shall lead you to it. This path of yours can be bloody, terrifying, and filled with death. But it does not have to be. I can pave it clean. I, Pandora, Witch of Vainglory, the true Saintess, will be your salvation. This love of yours is pure, awe-inspiring, fantastical. It should be cherished and it shall be cherished. Your love is right. It is the greatest gift given to humanity and I proclaim it as such. Thus it is true, thus it is written, thus it shall be. No longer restrained to Hell, your entrance into Heaven is secure. Isn’t that perfect? I can take away all of your suffering with just a thought. I can bring you the ending you so rightfully deserve. I can be the one who wipes away your grief, your disgust, your rage. I can be the one who saves you, just as you wish to save him. Fight the corruption of this world with me. Destroy the world’s devils and purge it of evil. Salvation’s only cost is the eradication of all sins. And isn’t that what you want? To destroy the worst of humanity. The neutralization of Envy is only a stepping stone. The Sword Saint will be a mere boulder. The Dragon? Not even worth thinking of. You may doubt me but know that I speak the truth, and nothing but the truth.  For while I have motives foreign to you, know that it will not impede your results. For there is no reason for me to lie as the future is already set in stone. The choices you make, the decisions you have made, all lead to the same conclusion: Heaven. Not the Heaven you can only dream of, a true and proper sanctuary for the lost and forsaken. You who have been forgotten can finally be remembered, forever. Why fight anymore? You deserve better than an endless battle. You do not have to slice up your body, grind it against the whetstone of Fate, and stain your hands with filth. It is beneath you. The sins you bear will no longer be yours, they will be mine to carry, as it always should have been. Are you not confident in your capabilities? Do not fret, for I shall remind you. If your hands are lacking, I shall strengthen them. If your legs waver, I shall embolden them. If your mind wanders, I shall purify it. You only need to ask. Because despite what I am telling you, this is your decision. All you have to do is take my hand. This is my gift to you, my gift of love. Your love has inspired me to do better, be better. I can only repay it with such meager wish-fulfillment. Believe in who you are, imagine a better you, think of what is best for Subaru. You know what you want, all you have to do is reach out for it.”

Pandora reached down, offering her lithe hand to Anastasia. All she had to do was embrace the inevitable. Wouldn’t that be amazing? To no longer struggle? To no longer fight for her life at each step? She could finally just enjoy the fruits of her labor. She and Subaru could finally be happy together, safe and sound. With their family and friends by their side. It would be so easy. Anastasia reached up, struggling to keep still. She was almost there—

A shadowy hand gripped her wrist, “Anastasia-sama. Apologies for the sudden physical contact but I would very much advise against this decision.”

It was Guese. He had returned. And it was time to make a choice.

Chapter 56: Ad Infernum

Summary:

Heaven or Hell?

Chapter Text

“You…” Anastasia’s eyes whipped to Pandora who was…just staring?

Geuse smiled grimly, “You’d think she was all-powerful, right? But even Vain—I mean— the Saintess has limits. Witch Factors are strong in their own right. Each one has certain capabilities. If I knew what Sloth was capable of back then, even I could have…Anastasia-sama?”

Anastasia did not care what the mad man was saying. All she cared about was taking the hand of salvation right in front of her. Even if it meant tearing off her limbs. She pulled as hard as she could but Geuse’s Unseen Hand would not let go. Why won’t he let go? Why is he denying her peace? No. Disgusting. Let her go. Let her be with her loved ones. All her suffering could finally end. No more pain. No more reality. All of it could be over soon. Let go. Let go! LET GO—

A hand grasped her head. And all the noise finally was silenced. It was as if something reached within her unraveling mind and brought clarity once more—taking all the loose thoughts and neurons and tying them back together.

“There we go,” Geuse said, “Are you alright, Anastasia-sama?”

Anastasia blinked. She looked down at her hand. What just happened? Why did she do that? She then stared at Geuse, “What did you do to me?”

He let go of her head, giving her a small pat, “I imbued you with my Witch Factor. I muted your emotions and calmed them with my Unseen Hands.”

“You can do that?”

“I can do a lot of things. In our brief time away from each other, I have not only spent it trying to piece together your memories but to also settle into my role as the Hunter. To lie in wait, to settle my heart, and to stop at the right moment to strike. Such is my realm and such is what I can accomplish now.”

Anastasia looked around, they were in some kind of dome made of pure light. Pandora must have isolated her from Louis during her speech, most likely to prevent any outside interference. She must have not expected Geuse to be waiting to strike. The Unseen Hands ripped through the dome’s walls like paper, “Just like before. You stopped the world,” she saw the Hands extend out of his body and grip the edges of the world, pausing the fabric of reality through sheer force of will.

“Indeed. As mighty as Pandora may be, even she cannot stop time itself. Her powers are more causality or phenomena based rather than shifting the threads of space-time. Though, in my case I would say that I am more the connection between reality and conceptual, and not a direct influencer of entropy. The Hand of the Hunter can reach anyplace and grasp anything. It is really quite fascinating. In a lot of ways, you can even consider—”

As Guese rambled on in the background, Anastasia’s mind finally realized the situation in front of her. With her memories now fully restored, she came to the correct conclusion, “I caused all of this.”

Guese grimaced and led her away from Pandora and the Louis clones, using more hands to create a gap within the light dome for them to exit through. They passed by Louises with odd faces and disturbing expressions as many continued to feast on Greed. Anastasia could not help but stare at his mutilated body. His resemblance to Subaru brought all the visions back to the forefront of her mind. Subaru getting devoured by the rabbits was vivid. She memorized every detail despite wanting to desperately forget it all. The worst part wasn’t the gore or the blood; it was the screams. She hated it. Hated hearing him in so much pain and being unable to do anything about it. This was what Subaru held inside himself all of this time. That self-harming habit, was it a way to cope or a phantom pain that he had to itch? Either answer made her want to vomit. Her eyes glanced back to Pandora’s hand. It would be so easy.

“Stay strong, Anastasia-sama,” Geuse’s voice brought her back, “That way lies falsehood.”

“But she wasn’t lying,” Anastasia whispered, “None of it was a lie.” She knew. Anastasia could tell. The sheer confidence that woman conveyed in her words. She meant every word. That was the problem. If Pandora could lead her to a righteous ending, one where everything worked out for the better, wouldn’t that be the best for everyone? Anastasia was not perfect; she was not someone who could shift the world at her beck and call. All of her work proved worthless when tested against the worst of humanity. If anything, her giving up would finally make everything better. She fought and survived for so long. Maybe it was time to accept reality. “If her Authority is strong enough to make all my dreams come true, shouldn’t I take it?”

“You out of all people should know that any offer that seems too good to be true, has stipulations,” Guese guided her to a patch of darkness nearby, blocking her view of Pandora and the others who were still stuck in their original positions, “Pandora may not be lying, but the Heaven she speaks of is a honay trap. It sounds sweet. And perhaps it would be beautiful. But the bodies that will lay the groundwork for such a future would be numerous. No doubt you will be happy but there is a high chance you will not be sane.” Geuse’s eyes penitent, “Trust me. You do not want to be a follower of hers.”

Anastasia knows that. She knows. She always knows. She weighs all the decisions in her head, calculates all the risks and rewards for each decision, and creates various arguments for whichever choice she makes. That woman raises all of the alarm bells in her head for a bad deal. And yet still, “Geuse…I’m…” Anastasia thought of all the logic she could spout. All of the persuasive arguments she could say that would possibly win him over. But none of that came out, instead, “I’m tired.”

Geuse looked surprised as Anastasia continued, “I’m so…fucking tired. Of this. All of this. Everything I’ve been through. It just feels like one large cascade of bullshit, one after the other. There’s just no end. If it isn’t losing my name, it’s being assaulted by bandits. If it’s not bandits, it’s some rogue Oni-spirit hybrid. If it isn’t some rabid dog, it’s Cultists and having my Od be ripped to shreds. If it isn’t me dying, it’s dealing with Archbishops and abominations in my head and seeing Subaru die and the Witch of Envy right on our doorstep! When will it be enough?! When will it end?!” Anastasia gasped for breath.

“Anastasia-sama. I know it must seem overwhelming.”

“That’s an absolute understatement and you know it,” Anastasia spat, “I don’t want to be here. This isn’t my job nor something that I can resolve. I’m just a merchant. Some girl who thought she could take over the world with enough determination and people skills. But you know what I realized? None of that means shit when people can just rip reality apart at the drop of the hat. I’m not the Sword Saint or some heroine from another world. I’m just Anastasia Hoshin,” Anastasia breathed heavily, “…And even that doesn’t mean anything anymore.”

Geuse was silent for some time, letting Anastasia control her breathing, her heart steadying. She wanted to go home. She wanted to rest. She was so tired. For once in her life, she didn’t want to work hard anymore. She just wanted to be with her loved ones. Was that too much to ask? Geuse spoke softly, “I’m sorry. It was not my intention to burden you with such pressure. You are right. This is not your responsibility, none of this is.” Geuse sighed, “I just did not want you thinking Pandora’s offer was the only option.”

“What other choice is there?” Anastasia waved her hand behind him, “Greed is basically out of commission. There are Louises all over the place. From what I can tell, Pandora can literally shift reality at her beck and call. You can’t stop either of them easily. Because if you could, you would have done so already. And I’m not even a contender. So tell me, what can I even do?”

“…Give up,” Geuse said.

Anastasia stared at him, “You’re kidding.” Geuse didn’t even blink, “Oh my Od, you’re not. How is that any different from what I was going to do before?”

“Giving into Pandora is different. That would be submitting ourselves to a greater evil. What I’m suggesting, is that we take a step back. Perhaps we are not the ones who can resolve this, but others can. This situation is too chaotic, too disadvantageous. We need to retreat and create a better opportunity.”

“That would mean we’d have to leave this place. But we can’t,” Louis taunted her about what happened at the Tower, “It was some accidental combination of Witch Factor Authorities that made this place. Unless you can reverse that, there is no easy way of leaving here. We’d have to have control of Greed and Gluttony at the very least.”

“That was not what I was suggesting,” Geuse hesitated before taking a deep breath, “What I’m suggesting, is a possible reset.”

Anastasia felt something snap inside of her. She stared at him blankly, “Shut up.”

“Anastasia-sama. If I were to use my Unseen Hands to break the world around us—“

“I said, shut up.”

“—I could theoretically shatter Subaru-sama’s Od and cause his physical body to expire. This should satisfy the requirements—“

“Shut up, shut up, shut the fuck up, Geuse!”

“—of Return by Death and allow Subaru-sama to return to an earlier point in time. One where he can plan his moves accordingly and perhaps provide us a better solution.”

Anastasia wanted to strangle him, “Geuse. Do not.”

Geuse’s expression did not change, “It is the best possible outcome. There is nothing else we can do.”

“My husband is not a fucking reset button,” Anastasia yelled, “He isn’t someone you can just kill when things are bad. His life isn’t worth nothing! How could you even suggest such a thing?!”

“Then what else is there? You asked for the other optimal choice. This is it.”

Anastasia thought quickly, “We kill off all the Louises and make Gluttony submit.”

Geuse responded, “Impossible. As you said, if I could, I would. But with Pandora here and her brothers still alive, it is unlikely the Witch Factor will obey us.”

“We take Greed and run.”

“To where? There is nowhere to hide. And even if I were to take him into your Od. The problem would still persist.”

“We…find Subaru and try to think of a new plan,” Anastasia was grasping at straws.

“…You and I both know what he would choose.”

“I’m not letting him die for my sake! I’m not letting him go! I’ll figure out something else, even if it kills me—“

“Enough!” Geuse shouted, his patience ran thin, “You cannot have everything you want. Sacrifices have to be made. We are not privileged with options that can solve everything. And do not even think of arguing for Pandora’s offer again! You heard what she said. You may have your happy ending but the world? The world will suffer and die for your sins. You or Subaru-sama’s lives are not worth the death of everyone else.” Geuse’s eyes widened, he then took a step back before sighing, “I’m sorry. That was too far,” he bowed, “But please. Think rationally. This is the only way we can move forward. We can’t be greedy here. Not anymore.”

By going back. And starting again. However far back that may be. Anastasia’s lips wavered, “…When will he return to?”

“I do not know,” Geuse was apologetic, “Given my knowledge of Envy, she is not happy with your presence here, and especially your knowledge of Subaru’s life. She will most likely take advantage of this and turn back time beyond what we’ve seen. Perhaps back before your Od was save. Maybe even way before…when you first met again.”

Anastasia gripped her head, curling up into a ball, “What the fuck are you asking me to do? To give up all the happiness I gained, just so we can get out of this hellscape?” She let go and looked at Geuse, who appeared to be as morose as her, “You can’t just ask me this. You can’t ask me to kill my husband. To lose him forever.” He’s everything she ever wanted, and none of what she expected, “Don’t…just…don’t.” The very idea was bringing her to tears.

“I’m sorry. But this is the only way.”

“Why even ask me? It’s not like my knowledge would make any difference. You don’t need me.”

“I—“ Geuse hesitated before pushing forward, “I know what it is like, to watch your loved one die. The pain. The regret. The utter contempt I held for myself. I considered doing it without your knowledge.” Geuse looked away, “But to end your happiness without saying goodbye, would be a far worse cruelty.”

So this is it. This is what all that suffering was building up to.

That’s what this is, isn’t it? I can’t save him. He has to die. And I can only watch as he slips away from me, saying goodbye to all the happiness he gifted me. Subaru will find a way forward…without me.

Sure. There was a chance they could find a way to be together again. But how possible is that? It was only pure luck that she fell for him and if he were to orchestrate their time together, her guard will be up. Her walls higher than before. It was only because he said the right words at the right time, that she attached herself so desperately to him. Subaru would be left pining for her for years. And even then, what’s to say he doesn’t give up for her benefit? That’s the type of person he is. Maybe he gives her up so she can be happy. And he’ll return to his old camp, to his old loves.

This was the end of their love. A short-lived mess that should have never happened. The severity of the situation filled her with laughter. And she did. Geuse watched as she laughed to herself, crying. He reached out his hand but chose to do nothing. She laughed. And laughed. Until her throat became hoarse and the tears no longer fell. She was so angry. Angry with the world and especially herself, for being so weak. She couldn’t do anything at all while Subaru beared everything. What a joke. Why was she even here? What purpose was there for her existence? She was utterly, and positively useless—

Wait.

 

Why was she here?

This wasn’t a rhetorical question, there was something that didn’t make sense, and Anastasia only realized it now. She raised her head and stared Geuse down, “What do you know about Vainglory’s Authority?”

Geuse was surprised by her question. He seemed confused but his tone was succinct, “From what I can recall, she has the ability to teleport people great distances. I witnessed her send Regulus Corneas back to his mansion in the blink of an eye, as if he was never here. She was also able to stave off my attacks by constantly regenerating her existence. And while I’m not quite sure if this was real, I believe she changed how I perceived people, as I was unable to discern her from others during a brief moment of…lunacy.” His expression was guilty, but Anastasia did not care. “Unfortunately, that is all I can offer you. My synchronization with the Hunter is still too low. It would take quite a long period of time for me to gain its knowledge and wisdom. I am unable to relay any information that I didn’t experience myself.”

Her mind was racing with possibilities and theories. She asked again, “How do you know her? Why was she after you?”

Geuse shook his head, “It was not me. She was after Emilia-sama. While it would take ages for me to recount, all you need to know is that Emilia-sama held a key that Pandora desperately needed,” Geuse seemed reluctant to speak more. It did not matter. Anastasia just needed an important piece of information.

“But did she accomplish it?”

Geuse blinked, “From what I can tell, no. She did not.”

“How?”

“I do not understand what you are asking.”

“How did Pandora, the literal reality warper, who could send Regulus Corneas back to his mansion without sweating, not accomplish her goal? Was Emilia strong enough to fight her off?”

Geuse shook his head, “No, she was too young. Despite her mana reservoirs, she was not trained to…fight…anyone,” the dots were connecting in his mind, “Why did Pandora leave her alone? Based on my memory, Emilia-sama did not escape. It doesn’t make sense.”

“Right?!” Anastasia was becoming manic, “It doesn’t. Why go through all that trouble, just to leave? It seems illogical, especially given how powerful she is. Why not tell Emilia she had to give it to her? Why not have something fly in and kill Emilia? Maybe Emilia was necessary but then that can only explain one thing…Pandora can’t force Emilia to do what she wants. Pandora wasn’t able to just say, ‘Emilia opens the door.’ Like she did with me or Regulus.”

Everything was coming together in Anastasia’s head, she continued rambling, “So just like you said, Vainglory has limits. She’s not all-powerful. There are conditions she needs to fill and that’s why I’m here.” Anastasia smiled, “I think I know what we can do.”

High risk, high reward. She just had to go all-in.

———————————————

Time resumed and Anastasia was once again face to face with Pandora, still reaching out a hand to her.

Anastasia’s voice wobbled, “…I have a happy ending?”

Pandora was iridescent as always, “Yes…I can take you straight there. Join us. Join the Witch Cult. Just take my hand, and everything will be as it should. One last time.”

“…No.”

“No?”

“No…that doesn’t make sense.”

Pandora’s face was as perfect as always, “Do you not believe me? I have never lied to you.”

Anastasia watched carefully, “No. You haven’t. Which is why it doesn’t make sense. Because if all of this is true, why go through all this effort? Why wait all this time? Why not offer me salvation in the first place? Why send me in here? If my love is not wrong…why go through all this effort to push me into taking your hand a second time?”

“…” Pandora’s face was stone, her smile ever-present. It seemed she was trying to form a response. But there was a crack. A crack so small that it was almost imperceptible to anyone. Anyone except Anastasia. A woman who spent countless years being able to read body language and hidden tells for emotions. A woman who was a master of subtle cues. A woman who spent hours upon hours, with an insane man who has been able hide all his trauma and pain from everyone who ever cared for him. Well, everyone but her. Because despite how perfect Pandora’s façade was.

 

She could not hide the slight twitch of her eye.

 

And with that twitch, brought a horrifying smile upon Anastasia’s face.

Anastasia felt elation, her gamble was already showing profit. She could barely restrain her excitement as she spoke, “You made a mistake. I know how your ability works. It’s an Authority like Subaru’s. But it has limits. It has a cost. And whatever it is, it can only work in definites. You sent me to this place. But I was already planning on going here. All roads led to here, as you said. Let me guess, your ability essentially cuts the thread and resews it at a later timepoint. It pushes us forward on our fated path within seconds. You can make certainty happen instantly. As if you’re responsible for it. It’s instant gratification, tailored to make you out to be some kind of God.”

“…”Cracks upon cracks formed within her mask. Pandora’s facial structure became more and more strained. Cracks became crevices which became chasms. Perfection’s canvas was being unwound in real-time. Until finally, with just a few words:

“…But you can’t change probability.”

“…!” Her mask was undone. Revealing a woman who could only feel one emotion at this singular moment.

Rage.

And Anastasia reveled in it, “I knew it! Hahaha! I fucking knew it! You can’t! That’s why you needed to wait. To coax me into a position where I would definitely become one of your Witch Cultists. You probably wanted me to become an Archbishop, right? This was all your plan. To get me and Subaru as your new pawns. But you made one fatal mistake.”

“…” Pandora tried to retain her composure but failed, her face and body genuinely taken aback.

“You haven’t lied once. Which means when you said that Subaru and I will have a happy ending. You meant it. Subaru and I will be happy together and according to your ability, that is 100% factual,” Anastasia wanted to laugh at the pathetic woman in front of her but she had more to say, “And your Authority sending us straight there, means all roads lead to our happy ending. You just want to be responsible for it.”

Pandora threw her hand out, sneering, “…You don’t know anything. You are incapable of accomplishing such a goal.”

But Anastasia’s smile was wider, taller, practically melting off her face, “Now that’s a lie. Our fate is secured. And it’s all because of Subaru’s power. I get it now. That’s why you’re so anxious. That’s why you needed me here, vulnerable and easy to influence. You weren’t targeting me; you were targeting Subaru. You’re afraid of him. Afraid of some lovestruck kid because no matter what you can do, you can’t change fate. But he can. He is the only person who can negate your ability at will. He is your antithesis. And if that’s true, if Subaru can always change fate, if Subaru will always pave the way to our happy ending. And given that I will always be there every step of the way with him. No matter how much pain and suffering we go through. Subaru and I, no matter the time or event, will always go after our happy ending. And we will succeed. We will always end up happy. And you just confirmed it,” Anastasia felt like all her worries were no longer relevant. Her heart was pure. Her mind was cleansed. She felt only pure visceral joy at such enlightenment, “So thank you Pandora. Thank you. You’ve given me hope.”

Pandora scowled, her voice was now a higher octave, “You don’t know what you are doing! You could still fail!”

This was it. This was her moment. What Tia said would happen. Anastasia knew what had to be done, “Perhaps, but that doesn’t matter, we will still find a way. I always knew that Subaru was my happiness. Everything he has, everything he gives, and everything he does. His grief, his love, his pain, his joy. All of it. It’s all mine. Not yours. Not Emilia’s. Not Rem’s. Not even the Witch of Envy’s. This Heaven bullshit of yours. All of you can fuck off.”

“You would willingly reject a chance at Heaven just to suffer in Hell?” Pandora said with dismay.

Anastasia didn’t hesitate, “If it means being with him forever, yes.”

If Subaru chose to be a monster, then Anastasia will be right by his side, and she will not stay as some helpless princess. Pandora seemed to find such unwavering love disgusting, as her voice rang out, trying to infest Anastasia’s mind again, “Anastasia Hoshin. You—“

“Hold on a second,” Anastasia stood up and flipped her hair, pointing at her head, “That isn’t going to work again. You’ll be happy to know that my mind is now 100% Witch proof. No longer will anyone be able to change my memories or mind. Courtesy of a dear friend we both share.”

Pandora’s eyes widened. It took her a second to realize what Anastasia meant, “Petelgeuse Romaneé-Conti,” her voice dripped with venom.

A small shadowy hand formed from Anastasia’s back and saluted at Pandora. Anastasia could feel Geuse laugh as Pandora’s scowl became deeper.

“You were right. That was worth the risk,” Geuse said within her mind.

Psychological warfare is one of the greatest weapons in a merchant’s arsenal. Or as Subaru would probably call it: rage baiting.

“I still believe you are absolutely insane for making this plan.”

Is it insanity if it works?

“Yes.”

The expression on Pandora’s face was more satisfying than any deal she ever struck. Now for the finishing touch. She put on her cutest expression, winking as Anastasia’s voice was sweet and saccharine, “I want you to repeat after me. Anastasia Hoshin will kill Pandora, burn her cult to the ground, and slaughter her hopes and dreams. She will parade my corpse around as the last remainder of my worthless existence. Forever locked as a footnote in history.” Anastasia then dropped her smile and stared Pandora down, “Tell me. How certain is that future?”

Pandora’s face froze. As if confused by what she just saw. Anastasia had a theory that Pandora had a way of seeing if her ability could work or not. A possible sensor or maybe a way to look into the future. Something to confirm that her ability was possible for a specific instance. In any case, it didn’t matter. All that Anastasia needed was to see Pandora’s face shift from pure rage into unrelenting fear to know that her words rang true. Anastasia will save that face in her memory banks for the rest of her life. Despite her joy, the second Anastasia blinked, Pandora was gone.

She must have ran away the second she realized what Anastasia was about to do.

“Anastasia-sama. I would like to apologize for my behavior earlier.”

Why? Anastasia didn’t remember him saying anything wrong. Sure, he pissed her off, but his logic was reasonable.

“I, if I may be frank, think you are terrifying.”

I’m not that bad.

“…”

Right?

As the dome around them dissolved into light particles, Geuse’s hands stretched out of her body and through the gaps. His voice sounded tense, “Are you sure you wish to continue the plan?”

Changing the subject, huh? A little rude.

“Anastasia-sama.”

I know. But I don’t care. I won’t let Subaru be the solution to everything, nor will I ever let him die just so things are easier. Life is cruel, disgusting, and terrible. But it’s worth fighting for. Even if we fall, even if we fail, I’d rather die with him than have an easy happy ending without him.

Geuse was quiet for a moment before speaking, “…Do not give up Anastasia-sama. Your husband is waiting for you.”

Anastasia didn’t need the reminder, but she welcomed it nonetheless. She watched as the last vestiges of light were gone, revealing the dark world of Subaru’s Od. The only citizens left were her and Louis. The main Louis looked up, bored as can be, and was evidently confused, “Where’d Pandora go?”

Anastasia smiled, “Oh, well, I told her to go kill herself. Sadly, she won’t take my advice but I’ll happily help her later,” Anastasia could feel Geuse shudder. What? Can’t a gal joke with some dark humor?

It took Louis a second to process that. She smiled back, “Oho? Seems you rejected her offer. Well, more for us then,” she growled as several copies of her prowled around.

Anastasia held out a hand, “Wait before you try to nibble on my body. I have something to ask: how much math have you done in your life?”

“I—what?” Louis cocked her head.

“Like don’t get me wrong. I’m flattered you want my body—gross as that is to say—but how in the world do you think you can do things better in my place? Like I get it, you’ll have my memories but not my mind. That’s not something that comes with the package, at least I don’t think you’ll be able to use my brain as well. I’m considered pretty smart compared to a lot of people. How much mental math have you done? Because I can do calculations pretty easily. Here are some easy ones. What’s 298 multiplied by 487?”

“Uh—“

“145,126. Light work. 723 divided by 12?”

“Hold on—“

“60.25. That was even easier. Using the current currency exchange, how much Vollachian gold can you acquire by trading five divine coins, two silver coins, and twenty copper coins.”

Louis’s eyes were spinning, “We—you—"

“One Vollachian gold is worth 20 silver coins. So it would approximately be 217 gold coins, give or take.” Anastasia yawned, “If you really want to be a merchant, yer goin’ ta have ta put in the effort.” Anastasia smiled as she used her accent one last time.

“What was the point of such nonsense?” Louis said as she circled Anastasia with the rest of her copies.

Anastasia cracked her neck, readying her hands, “Just taking a page out of my dumbass’s book. Sometimes, the best way to defeat you morons is distracting you long enough to get an advantage.” Anastasia then raised the bundle of light that was dropped into her hand, “Speaking of.”

Louis blinked. She then glanced over to Greed. He was still being devoured but there were numerous threads snaking out of his body and all of them led to…her. All of her. Anastasia was the conduit, connecting from Greed to Louis. What Louis couldn’t see were the hundreds of Unseen Hands that plucked the threads from Greed and attached them to the Louises all at the same time. She also didn’t see the hands shifting the world to a familiar time point. Where snow drifted in from the sky and a black-haired boy was about to be devoured by a white and red horde. Greed’s threads naturally connected to the memory of the boy, and the network was finally complete. Her confusion only rose as Anastasia readied the bundle of threads, angling them towards her heart as if she was holding a knife.

“What are you doing?” Louis was curious but she evidently wasn’t taking any chances. Several of her copies lunged at Anastasia as she spoke.

It was too late though. Anastasia felt time slow as her thoughts raced. This was a big gamble. She didn’t know if this would work. She had a theory that the threads of Greed connecting them could affect Gluttony but without any confirmation, it was a shot in the dark. The pain she felt in that one loop, as Subaru’s memory killed itself by plummeting onto rocks. The sharp phantom pain of her skull splitting and turning into mush was still clear as day in her mind. If Anastasia could feel that when she connected with him, would Louis feel the same? Would the connection between the Gluttony trio affect the outside world as well? And if all of that was true, could she outlast them? A lot of questions and no answers unless they commit. Geuse will hold back the transfer from somehow reaching the real Subaru, but that would mean she would have to brunt all the pain herself to ensure transference to Louis. But that’s fine. She’d rather risk it all and win big than run away in fear.

Fortune favors the audacious, as Hoshin once said.

Her eyes naturally drifted to Greed, who still wore Subaru’s face. Even if it was fake, it gave her strength to see him. After all of this is over, she’ll finally understand his pain. Her mind thought back to some of Pandora’s last words.

“You would willingly reject a chance at Heaven just to suffer in Hell?”

“…All right then, time to go Hell,” Anastasia whispered as she plunged the light into her heart, directly into her soul. She didn’t hesitate. For a moment, nothing happened.

 

 

 

 

 

 

And then everything was pain.

Chapter 57: Hell (II)

Summary:

Anastasia accepts who she is, where she is, and what she could be.

Chapter Text

Louis Arneb wanted to be happy.

A simple wish but one that she coveted so dearly. One could describe such a desire as the most common and normal want and need of all. Many in this world subscribed to life’s endless search for happiness and Louis was the same. To most, happiness was defined by the things they owned, the memories they cherished, the people they know. Louis understood this as she delved into the myriad of memories and names her brothers had so graciously given to her over the years. Her only solace in this blank space where nothing but her own presence and mind to accompany her.

“Ah, how bothersome…” Louis said as she drifted in this endless sea of consciousness, waiting for her plan to come into fruition. She felt like a scavenger, helpless to fend for herself. Watching the various lives pass through her mind as she realized how wasteful everyone was. Every man, woman, and child that she was given. No matter the environment, the upbringing, the circumstances. Each one wasted their lives with stupid mistakes and decisions. She could pinpoint the exact moments where every single one of them failed to reach their full potential. A young man lost the opportunity to achieve happiness with the woman he loved because he was too passive. An older woman lost the opportunity to connect with her children one last time before death. A child wasted their youth on frivolous nonsense and found themselves without purpose.

All the same, no matter the situation, everyone was so wasteful. Even her brothers were not free from her scrutiny.

Gourmet? Bizarre Eating? She didn’t understand why her brothers cared about such meaningless drivel. Whether a person’s flavor was strong had no impact on the value of a meal. Neither did endlessly scarfing down on names without abandon. They wasted so much by focusing on the unimportant. What mattered most wasn’t the amount or type, it was who you dined with. Even if she were to possess her brother’s bodies and mold her own presence through the names of others, it was still not enough. None of them were perfect and none of them satisfied her. None of them fit her criteria for the greatest combination of birth and environment to create the perfect life.

No matter how much she was given, she still wasn’t happy.

So when someone finally entered the Hall of Memories, she could not help but be curious.

-----------------

“It is nice to meet you in the flesh, Louis Arneb,” Pandora said with a permanent smile upon her face, “Though perhaps flesh is wrong. You really are just a wandering soul at this point, trapped within Od Laguna’s cradle. How tragic.”

Louis didn’t know if she should be overjoyed or freaked out that the literal Witch of Vainglory was right in front of her. Appearing out of thin air, she couldn’t process what just occurred despite Pandora’s callous words. Louis would easily sneer at such disrespect if it weren’t for her knowledge of the Witch Cult leader. Her brothers had witnessed Pandora’s powers themselves, and it was nothing less than awe-inspiring. To be able to rewrite reality itself, deleting people’s existences or to send them back from whence they came. Louis could not fathom the depths of her reach, and she did not dare to test such a monster. No matter what Lye said—his arrogance often annoyed her—Pandora was not someone she could conflict with. It was best to be cautious. “Lady Pandora, how can we assist you?”

“Hm, how polite,” Pandora said, “I see you aren’t like your brothers.”

“We prefer to always have good table manners.”

Pandora’s smile became ever so bigger, “How lovely.”

It creeped Louis out. Even so, she had a big question rattling in her mind, “How were you able to enter here?” She had more: did you always know there was a way inside? Are you here to free us? Was this some messed up way to show dominance? But Louis wasn’t willing to test this godlike being’s patience. One question at a time.

Pandora cocked her head in response, “If you are wondering if I knew how to enter and leave this place as well as your presence here, then no. I did not. I had theories but none were confirmed until I was allowed entrance by using this lovely soul,” Pandora waved her hand to the woman laying unconscious next to her, “But where are my manners as well. This is Anastasia Hoshin. A new recruit for the Witch Cult.”

Anastasia Hoshin? You remember such a name distinctly as it was the same name that caused Roy to spout curses for days. Despite its presence in the Stomach of Souls, it lacked the accompanying memories. Roy would only say that they should kill the woman if they find her again. At the very least, until her curiosity was satisfied, she wouldn’t let this woman die, “We see. Would you like us to devour her?”

Pandora did not respond for some time, merely studying Louis and Anastasia with brief glances as her expression never changed. Louis felt uncomfortable as the minutes dragged on before Pandora spoke again, “No. That will not be necessary. I would only like for you to keep her alive and to keep her soul intact. Otherwise, you may do as you please until I return for her. Think of her as a possible future sister.”

“Alright well—" but just as Louis blinked, Pandora was gone. Annoyed by her sudden entrance and disappearance, Louis didn’t want to ever see that woman again if she had the chance.

Louis looked over the unconscious Anastasia and frowned, “Now what to do with you.” Pandora did say she could do whatever she wanted but what did she want? Obviously if this girl could be the key to getting out of here, she would take whatever chance she could get. Even though she was used to walking around in the world of the living, it wasn’t enough. Experiencing it in her own body…that may lead to a form of happiness that was previously impossible for her. But first she needed to see what was so special about this girl that Pandora brought her all the way here. She didn’t trust Roy. He was an idiot who would sooner eat garbage than give up eating. He most likely messed up the eating process somehow.

Either way, she’ll have a taste of her memories and see how—

 

 

Your name is Anastasia Hoshin and you do not understand where you are. You wake up in some blank space where you see nothing but white for miles to see. You feel odd. Really odd. Where are you? Where is Subaru? Where are your friends? You were in the Mather’s Mansion just a few seconds ago, where…you met a bird? A very beautiful bird. A bird that offered you a deal you couldn’t refuse. Even though your senses were all alerting you to get away, the bird spoke the truth. If you took that bird’s hand, you will find happiness.

Happiness? You look around even more confused. If that’s the case, why are you here? Why are you here alone? And why is there an exact replica of your body on the floor?

Wait. What?

You look down and study your body. No. This…who? You look down at yourself. Not your body on the floor. Your body. The one you are in currently. You are wearing a white dress and you feel shorter than before. Everything feels weird. Why do your hands look like that? Why do you have long golden hair? No. Everything is normal now. Violet hair. But why does everything feel so off? Who are you? What are you? Why do you—no—we feel this way? We? Who is we? Why do we act like this? What are we? What is we? Why is we is what is we—

Louis spat out the memories as soon as she gained an ounce of control back. She gasped for breath and dry heaved as she could feel her heart race. What the fuck was that? She could barely comprehend what just happened as the rush of memories stuck to her brain. While she couldn’t remember everything exactly, the remnants were enough to understand what just happened. For a brief moment, Anastasia Hoshin’s memories were able to overcome her ego and nearly subsume her body. She had never experienced this using Lunar Eclipse. She had come close while using Solar Eclipse but not to this extent nor to this level. Did this happen to Roy? How?

Louis took a moment to gather her thoughts as she looked at Anastasia’s body with disdain. This person—this utter wretch—was able to override Louis’s consciousness. What pissed off Louis even more was the fact that this very person was the most wasteful one of them all. Out of all the names and memories she devoured, this one disgusted her beyond relief. She combed through some of the remnant memories and realized that this girl had lived a tumultuous life. Abandoned as a baby, groomed to be a manipulative criminal, clawed her way out of poverty, became a successful merchant, and was brought low once more because of an encounter with her brother. She could only feel pure revulsion as she saw every single mistake the girl made that brought her situation to the present. The nerve of a woman to be handed so many opportunities, only to squander them all.

As her mind settled, she realized there were some familiar figures in the memories. Using her connection to the Stomach of Souls, she retrieved them into her mind. Now she remembered. How fortuitous that this very person’s whole camp was at the Sage’s Tower right now, being toyed with by her brothers. It seemed they wanted to have some fun before murdering the mercenaries and knight. Which gave Louis an idea.

She knelt down next to Anastasia’s body and smiled, “If we can’t take your memories now, perhaps there is something better we can do with you.”

--------------------------------------------

Louis yawned. Unfortunately, no matter what she tested, she was unable to find a direct way out of the Hall of Memories. Which was fine, the outside world was boring to Louis, she didn’t yearn to escape from this dreary world. Not one bit.

She had bigger priorities and that girl was the key. If she couldn’t devour the girl, she at least had the opportunity to test splitting her Witch Factor and possessing the poor fool. Luckily the girl was very compatible with Gluttony. Even more, her clone was able to exit this putrid blank world by using Anastasia as a carrier. Now all the original had to do was wait as the plan would be put into action.

If Anastasia’s analysis was true, her little boytoy had an amazing ability that could allow Louis to do as much as her heart desires. An ability to literally reverse time and change all events to your liking. She salivated at such an idea. She needed him to create her perfect scenario. As much as Anastasia angered her, Louis couldn’t help but admit that her life was one of the highest rated she had ever come across. A weak woman who was born with an adept mind in the depths of Kararagi. Social and financial influence that stretched way beyond most. Allies and friends who ranged from interesting to insanely powerful. It was too much to resist.

She would take everything Anastasia had and use it properly. Louis will bait Anastasia’s lover into her clutches and possess him and the rest of their family. She will use them all to create the perfect life and finally achieve true happiness. Soon, Louis will be satiated.

Louis yawned again, lying on the ground, rubbing her finger in circles on absolute nothingness. Despite her plans and desires, she was forced to wait as everything came to fruition, only informed of what had occurred whenever one of her clones returned to this area. It was odd how the entrance to the Hall of Memories was stored in Reid’s Book of the Dead. But it did not matter, not at the moment. What was important was focusing on getting all of her pieces together.

Louis sighed, “Want to become happy…”

If only this unyielding boredom could go away—

“URGH!” Louis choked as she felt immense pain shoot through her body. She had never felt anything like it before. This wasn’t normal. It felt like something was ripping her apart from the inside out, gorging on her organs a hundred times a second. For a time, the pain was immeasurable.

And then it was gone, for a moment, Louis felt nothing. Not just the absence of pain, absolutely nothing. No sensations, no thoughts, no self. It was as if her consciousness had been extinguished for a brief moment.

And then she was back to normal. Coughing and choking and wanting to vomit. Just as her rattled mind was processing what occurred, the pain returned. Different but still excruciating.

What was going on?!

------------------------

Pain. The pain was too much.

Anastasia couldn’t think. She couldn’t move. She couldn’t feel. This was a nightmare. The world was shifting around her. Memories of Subaru were being killed one after the other around her. It was for the plan, but she couldn’t help but grieve each one. Every death, every subsequent shot of transferred pain, each one was another sin she would bare. Everything hurt. She wanted it to stop. But she can’t stop. Not when she was so close. It hurts. It hurts. It hurts!

She just wanted to be happy. Why did the world hate her for being happy?

------------------------

“What is going on?!” Julius yelled as all of his unconscious friends around him began to scream. They writhed uncontrollably as Julius ran over to hold some of them down, hoping they wouldn’t accidentally bite their tongues off. Beatrice was also nearby, frantically figuring out the source of the problem. In the corner of Julius’s eye, he saw that the Gluttonies were also having their own troubles. Lye was panting uncontrollably while Roy was struggling to stand. Halibel and Zarestia did not let an opportunity go to waste as they increased the barrage of their attacks. Julius knew from experience that the end was near; whatever was happening was affecting only those who were affected by Gluttony’s machinations. He just didn’t know why.

Just as Julius was trying to understand the sudden affliction on his friends and enemies, something burst out of each of his expedition members: shadowy tendrils that morphed into various visages of animalistic forms. Each one roared in pain as they hovered in the air. Before diving towards Anastasia’s body.

“No!” Julius and Beatrice screamed. They shot magic at the tendrils, hoping to block whatever malicious entity was targeting Anastasia. Unfortunately, none of them struck true, merely passing through the shadows as if they were nothing. Each one slithered into his candidate’s heart. The screams of his friends died out, a quick check of their pulses showed they were alive, albeit still unconscious. Beatrice ran to Anastasia and Subaru, checking their bodies. After making sure everyone else was stable, Julius ran over to join Beatrice.

“No way…” Beatrice appeared shocked.

“Beatrice-sama, what is wrong?” Julius asked, ready for the worst.

“Miasma,” Beatrice whispered, “Ana’s miasma is increasing exponentially.”

------------------------

It hurts.

 

Anastasia hated this world.

 

It hurts.

 

Why did she have to suffer? To be born so weak, without a loving family, amongst the dirt and trash. To achieve a state of stability, only for it all to tumble down into nothingness. Everything she built, all gone in the blink of an eye. Was her life some sort of joke?

 

It hurts.

 

When will it all stop? When will she finally be able to relax? Why is it that every single time she won, it never got easier?

 

She could feel her throat slashed, her body butchered with an iron ball, her cells freezing, her guts ripped out, her blood seeping out of her slowly, her nerves fried beyond comprehension. Everything, all of it. Nothing but suffering. Endless. Unyielding. Years of torment passing by in seconds.

 

Why was she here? What was her purpose for such suffering? What was it all for?

 

It needed to end. It has to end. Let her rest, let her struggles cease. There was no more need for this—

In the corner of Anastasia’s eye, through the various convulsing bodies of Louis, she focused on the face of Greed—no—Subaru. Broken, barely conscious, and crying. Alone. Like always.

She remembered the warmth he brought her. His smile that made all her worries fade away. How his laugh made her so happy. His joy was her joy. His sorrow, her sorrow. His pain, her pain. It was never about her. No.

Oh. I almost forgot. Him. It was always, for him.

…This wasn’t enough. No. It will never be enough. She will never be enough.

And that’s fine.

If Anastasia Hoshin wasn’t enough, then she’ll become more. Her name was meaningless. All that mattered, was who she became.

She needed more. More pain. More death. More suffering. Beyond what was comprehensible. Nothing is limited; she will no longer hold herself back. Let her desires flow, her malice unleashed.

More. More. More!

Cut her throat open a million times until all she could breathe was steel and blood. Destroy her body until it is nothing but dirt and ash. Cover her cells in endless frost, let them die in eternal snow. Take her organs, take her lungs, her heart, her soul; she will smother you in their warmth until you are cold. Her blood was worthless, take it all, so the world would drown in her sanguinity. Let her feel everything, experience everything, everything that she ever wanted will be hers. Let everyone witness her happiness, her despair, her disgust, her rage, her contempt, her bloodlust.

Let the world see what she has become.

------------------------

Louis Arneb did not want to die.

She was a clone, a mere imprint of the original. She could feel the memories of The Beast gnaw at her. The howling of desire. All it wanted was for her to feast upon everything she wanted. Even now, she could feel its claws rake into her very bones. And yet, she could not. She would not.

Louis did not want to die. She was scared. Everything was horrifying. Why was she here? To create the perfect life? How absurd.

It was impossible. An arrogant dream concocted by a child who never experienced reality. Reality wasn’t fair. It was cruel. It laughed at your absurdity and washed you in endless torment until you’re nothing but a driveling mess. It was a pale star that was beyond comprehension. And it was standing right above Louis.

Haunting her as it regaled a childhood story.

Anastasia’s voice was low and drowning in malice, “You know why I chose the name Anastasia? It was from a story I hated from my childhood.”

Louis whimpered, “…” she did not want to look up. She was curled into a safe and tiny ball. It was all she had left. She winced as each second passed, coupled with the bludgeoning pain of spikes ripping into her body. How could it—she— stand there, unflinching?

Anastasia’s words melted her brain, “Once upon a time, there was a Princess and a Shadow. The Princess was a frail and fragile person who was kind to all but was deathly sick. Her royal court worried endlessly about her but she was not someone who could be held down, escaping day after day into the woods to play. One day she met a boy wreathed in shadows. The Shadow tried to scare her, warning her that he was a murderous monster, but the princess was curious. She asked him boundless questions, and he only responded with rage. How dare some weak girl not fear him? He did all that he could to make her cry. Nevertheless, she never strayed nor winced, only smiling as he roared. She was already so used to death, she knew he was putting on a front. The Shadow was so surprised by her behavior, that his fury both dissipated and became something new: no matter what, he’d find a way to make her cry. Days passed into weeks into months into years. Yet, however much he tried, he failed to make her cry, again and again. Over time, his wish also faded into obscurity, as their relationship blossomed. They became friends. Best friends. They were almost inseparable. Running through the glades and rivers, playing hide and seek, telling each other everything and anything. They were in blissful happiness.”

How? How in the world was she able to speak? How could she speak as both of their throats were being gouged out? How could she speak as their lungs froze from within? What madness allowed her to do such a thing?

None of Louis’s questions were answered as Anastasia continued her tale, “And then, her time ran out. She knew this day was to come and had already accepted her ending. No matter what anyone could do, she was dying. And despite how much everyone cried around her, the tears wouldn’t come to her. She was happy. Happy to have lived such a fruitful life,” Anastasia sighed, “But the shadow couldn’t. He didn’t understand how anyone could accept such a fate. Why would he when he—a living and breathing shadow—defies the logic of the world already? A monster born from darkness who can live in the light? If no one could figure out her ailment, maybe he could. And if he couldn’t, perhaps the geniuses of his race would be able to. And so he returned to his homeland—where the sun always sets— and asked the wise elders and healers of the world of shadows for guidance. He begged for seven days and seven nights. Giving up all his worldly belongings just for the chance to receive a possible cure. And after all his struggles, they finally, gave him his answer.”

The pain stopped. For a second, nothing could be felt. Nothing except the whispers of Anastasia.

“Lungs of a wolf. Brain of a mole. Heart…of a shadow,” Anastasia said, “Gather these ingredients and cast the ritual, anchoring the soul you hold so dear to the world of the living once more. The first two were easy, but the last was difficult. There was only one shadow creature that had such an organ—the one who could walk in the light without a care. No one but him had a heart to spare. Such a sacrifice would mean the end of his freedom, he would forevermore be chained to the world of shadows, never seeing the light of day again. And yet, without even another second passing, his voice clear and pure. Do you know what he said without hesitation?”

“Take it. My heart was already hers to begin with.”

Louis felt Anastasia’s voice pierce her mind. She felt an eternity of silence pass before Anastasia continued, “And so, the shadow monster returned to the princess, and within one night, she was restored to full health. She awoke to the cheers and celebrations of her family and kingdom. And yet, she could not smile. No. She could not. Deep within her, she knew something was missing. She searched far and wide. She called all of her knights and scouts, searching for her dear friend. No matter where the princess went, she could not find her friend. Finally, she realized what had happened. And with that realization, she cried. She cried endlessly. For seven days and seven nights, the tears never stopped. And when they did, she was never the same. The joy of the princess had dried up; she never smiled or laughed again. Years passed and she eventually moved on, honoring her friend’s sacrifice and married a handsome prince. Living happily ever after…” Anastasia’s voice trailed off. Louis didn’t want to look up. Her body wouldn’t let her. She closed her eyes and prayed. Prayed that this suffering would all be over.

 “What a load of shit,” Anastasia yelled, “That isn’t some happy ending. No! Why didn’t she keep looking? How in the world could she accept something like that? How could you just let him leave? He was your friend, your best friend, the person you love the most in the world! You should have went into the world of shadows yourself and dragged him back! Or at the very least, found a way to be with him,” Anastasia panted, gasping with rage.

And suddenly, her voice was back to calm, “I chose that name out of spite. It was a good name, reminded so many people of royalty. Even if they didn’t believe it, they’d see me as someone high-class. Cultured. Someone far beyond a street rat. Whenever anyone asked me, I would tell them that as my reason. But if I were to be honest, I chose it because I hated that character. I wanted to be someone who would make better choices. Create a happier ending. I wouldn’t abandon the people I love. I won’t forsake them just because it was difficult. Even if the world pries them from my hands, I’ll rip the world apart until I have them back. I’ll keep them safe, even if it costs me everything,” Anastasia’s voice turned amused, “How funny. Despite what I wanted, everything turned out just like that story.”

Louis’s body hurt. Everything hurt. Even as Anastasia spoke, a Subaru died in the background. Louis knew because every single instance brought with it not only the pain of death, but the absolute nothingness that came between death and life. She felt her consciousness fade and become whole in the blink of an eye. It was frightening. Something no one should experience more than once. Louis could barely think because of it.

And still, Anastasia continued to speak, “I abandoned my camp because I couldn’t handle not having things as they once were. I became a burden for Subaru because the thought that I could never be enough for him, destroyed me. And I nearly sold my soul to a Witch because I couldn’t handle my own weakness anymore. It’s really funny. I thought I was different. I didn’t want to be like them, but it was self-fulfilling. Like the princess. Like Lotus. Like every hyena. And even you. I’m just like all of you. A selfish piece of shit who only knows how to take. Despite all of the masks and persona I tried to put on, despite how prim and proper I tried to act, all I was, and ever will be, is a starving scavenger.”

Anastasia laughed, a hollow raucous sound, “And you know what? I don’t care anymore.”

Anastasia smiled down at her. Louis knew, innately, that this insane monster was smiling as it spoke, “Great Businesswoman of the West? Second Coming of Hoshin? The Greedy Princess? None of it matters when bastards like you exist. Festering maggots that ruin the world for your own self-satisfying delusions. I’m sick of it. Sick of watching you and all those Cult rats scurry around, acting like you should exist. I hate you. I hate you, your fucking brothers, and that disgusting Witch you have for a leader. I will kill every single one of you and let the birds feast on your carcasses.”

Louis was scared; she could feel Anastasia’s malice. She whispered, “Stop…please…”

“What was that? Did you really just fucking say that?” Louis felt something bind her neck. Her eyes squeezed open as she saw that it was the thread of light twisting around her throat, strung up and held by the monster above her, “Come on. Where’s all that pride you had? Didn’t you want this life? My life? Everything I ever had. Well? Come on. Tell me! Weren’t you going to devour me?!” She tried to look anywhere but up.

“I’m sorry, please stop!” Louis begged as the words were forced out. “I’ll give you, your name back! Subaru’s name too! Both of them!” She vomited them out, “Do you want more? I can give you more! Rem, your camp, everyone!” Louis continued to vomit more and more names, indiscriminately, “Just please make it stop!”

“Isn’t this what you wanted?” The world shifted around them, the thread that connected them began to manifest into new visions of Subaru. Each one dying and being replaced with another. Hundreds, all killing themselves or being eviscerated. With each one, the pain was relived again and again, “You wanted to experience reality, right? You thought you could do better, right?! You wanted our lives, RIGHT?!”

“N-no I–“ Louis choked as the pain returned. The feeling of flesh being picked from the bone, bone shredded until marrow, and marrow to dust. They burrowed under her skin and feasted endlessly on her body. Her head split in two. Her bloodstream and nerves fried. Her throat slit open hundreds of times. Her cells frozen and shattered. Everything. All at once. As the various versions of Natsuki Subaru were slaughtered around her. The joy and boredom she once felt was gone, replaced with an all-consuming pain that would not end.

“This is life. In all its pain, grief, and misery. Come on. Taste it,” Anastasia spoke above her. The pain forced Louis’s eyes upward as she finally witnessed the monster’s true form.

This woman was no longer human. Anastasia’s body was wreathed in pure light; the threads of iridescent Greed cloaked her in a white veil. Like a dress made of starlight, it ebbed and flowed, motes of miniature comets strayed from its surface. A shining pale star amidst this dark world. Louis’s head rose slowly, barely able to comprehend the entity in front of her.

“Eat it,” Anastasia ordered.

No. This was not what she wanted. Not at all. She tried to crawl away, but the pain was too much, the thread chained her to the ground. She was left gasping for breath.

“Choke on it,” Anastasia said as she slammed Louis’s head into the ground.

 What the hell is she? How does she feel all of this and still smile? Where was that scared and helpless girl? What in the world did Pandora do?

“She didn’t do anything,” the pale star spoke, drenched in bloodlust, “All she did, was reveal what always existed. The only mistake you both made was trying to take what’s mine. Mimi. Hetaro. Tivey. Julius. Ricardo. Joshua. You took them away from me. Tia. Halibel. Beatrice. Echidna. You tried to take me away from them,” Louis felt a foot on her throat, “Worst of all,” it pressed down on her, “You thought you could take him away from me.”

Louis felt the pain increase tenfold, the screams of Subaru around her compounded, and she could only join the symphony. A mere whisper amongst the cacophony of misery. And yet, Anastasia’s voice echoed through her ears, clear as day, “He’s mine. Not yours. Not anyone’s. And if I have to kill you, Pandora, and the Witch of Envy to make that clear, then so be it.”

“Y-you…” Louis could barely croak out the words as Anastasia pressed even further on her throat. “M-Monster.”

“Yeah. I am. I always was. And always will be. Wonder what that makes you,” Anastasia said coldly as Louis could feel her neck breaking. Everything was breaking, “Now die. Die for my happy ending.”

No more. She could not handle it anymore. Louis could feel Gluttony shifting away, her ego dissipating as the Witch Factor was disgusted with her performance. The Beast. It wasn’t her. But it was also her. It loved her for her endless desire for happiness. Never satisfied, always searching. Just like how it loved her brothers. But it had a new master now. One that could never be satiated. That cared not for what she ate. Nor how much she ate. It was reminded of the Witch from 400 years ago, that brought it so much joy. Just like when it was first born. When it was a starving beast that could only feast on everything it came across. Oh, how rapturous it felt, to have a new incarnation that understood what Gluttony truly was.

Starvation.

And with that, Louis Arneb ceased to exist.

Chapter 58: Knocking on Heaven's Door

Summary:

Anastasia isn't done quite yet...

Chapter Text

Anastasia felt the essence of Gluttony flow through her as all the corpses of Louis dissipated into tendrils of shadows. Before it felt unnatural; as if something was slowly worming its way into her very core and infesting it with corruption. Now? Admittedly refreshing. That’s the best she could describe it. A part of her realized how insane that sounded. A Witch Factor having any positive connotation would be a death sentence to any sort of logic or normality. But perhaps that was the true cost of all of this. Anastasia dived deep into Hell itself.

It only made sense that she returned mad.

Her ruminations were interrupted by Geuse’s voice. It came in slow, methodical. Unlike Gluttony which felt like a refreshing wave of water or energy, Geuse—or more accurately, Sloth— was like a stagnant current. The soft feeling of grass upon her body as she rested beneath the morning sun. Irritating, restless, unnerving. She was unfit for Geuse’s presence even though she was used to another internal voice. Unlike Echidna’s, which felt warm and motherly. His was cautious and slightly disturbed, “Your soul has grown used to the Witch Factor. It has become a part of you now.”

Fantastic. Am I considered a Witch, then? She replied internally.

“…No. A Witch has specific qualities that designate them as such.”

Such as?

“Why do you wish to know?”

Anastasia rolled her eyes, Pre-cautionary measures. Never hurts to have a bigger stick. Aren’t Witches considered more dangerous than Archbishops?

Geuse seemed to take his time in between responses. As if he was deciding whether it would be good to answer or not, “You misunderstand. A Witch is more than a state being. If you were to compare the Cult to the Witches of old, Regulus Corneas would far outclass many of the Witches by pure power and ability. Danger or strength is something you should not consider a standard of Witches.”

So, what’s the difference?

“Witches, by nature, are aberrations to the logic of the world. They operate on moralities and concepts far removed from humanity. As such, compared to an Archbishop or any other user of a Witch Factor, they are more akin to a natural disaster operating on logic unknown to anyone else. While they may not be as powerful, they are no less destructive. Minerva, Sekhmet, Typhon, Daphne, Carmilla. Each one shaped the world around them, shifting the laws of reality into a new standard of living. Were you aware that Daphne was responsible for the creation of the Witchbeasts?”

That brought surprise to Anastasia. She had an inkling of it given what she saw of Subaru’s memories but everything was still settling in her brain. She needed to parse through all the information later when she had a chance. I always thought that Satella made them. So Daphne also wanted to destroy the world?

“No. She wanted to feed it.”

Excuse me?

“Feed it. She made the Witchbeasts all for the sake of feeding the world.”

What the fuck? But if that’s the case, why did she make them so dangerous?

“Quoting her, ‘If you are willing to eat, you should accept the risk of being eaten.’”

In some parts, she agreed. In the merchant world, you cannot expect to gain without equal risk of failure. Still, I see why you said Witches were batshit insane.

“I—uh. I guess in some capacity, that is what I meant.”

Anastasia sighed. If that’s the case, that’s one plan that was kaput. She assumed that a becoming a Witch could put her at equal level or farther than all the insane bastards in the world. The cost would have been high, but to keep her loved ones safe, it would have been a worthy risk. No matter. Such things should be considered one step at a time.

Anastasia thought for a moment before waving her hand in the air. The world began to shift as she could feel something toss and turn within her gut. It was like the middle ground between a hunger pang and a stomach growl. As horrible as it sounded, it wasn’t unpleasant. The dark world changed and manifested into a familiar scene—of Subaru and Anastasia napping beneath a tree. Her head was rested on his shoulder, his on her head, and their arms snaked between. Her fingers locked with his.

“There, that’s better,” she whispered to herself. The scenery was much nicer now as the wind blew through the memory, sending a rain of pink petals around her.

 It felt so long since they had such alone time together even though she knew it had been barely a few weeks. It felt like she spent an eternity within that pain loop. Years of deaths all in the brief span of a few moments. She could still feel her skin crawling. As if any moment, there would be a white rabbit bursting out of her body. Her hand instinctively went to her arms, but she caught herself. She always questioned where his bad habits came from but now she truly understood. The phantom pain was excruciating. It took all her effort to calm down, reminding herself that this wasn’t even her real body. She looked upon herself and blinked.

She was a shimmering white beacon.

Taking a better look at her own body, she now noticed what had occurred during the battle with Louis: Greed’s Strings had wrapped around her body and coalesced into a flowing white dress. It was paired with a veil that wrapped around her head, barely noticeable to her eyes but with a flick of her wrist, she was able to grasp the fabric, feeling warm to the touch. In fact, the whole dress felt warm and soothing. Anastasia thought for a moment before summoning a mirror to take a better look. It only took her a second before realizing what her appearance was most like.

A lace wedding dress. How touching. She remembered Subaru describing one to her when they talked about their engagement plans. She smiled softly to herself.

Her eyes glanced over to the source of these threads—Greed— who was slowly regenerating his body now that he was no longer being devoured endlessly. She walked over and kneeled next to him, combing Greed’s hair—reminded of that familiar sensation— and smiling even brighter than before.

“So this is what your Greed is…” she whispered to herself. How was this so hard to comprehend before? It was so simple. So warm. Protective. Eternal. The bond between them was now in its purest form. And she couldn’t help but feel enraptured by it. It gave her strength in abundance and the necessary conviction to go through with her next course of action.

“…Anastasia-sama. It’s time to leave,” Geuse said, “I am unaware of what is happening outside, but it should be safe to exit. With a Gluttony Witch Factor in our possession, we have all the tools necessary to extract your soul from Subaru-sama’s Od.”

Anastasia placed her hand on Greed’s cheek briefly, caressing his face with her thumb. Just a bit more, and they’ll be together again. She stood up, “No.”

“No?” Geuse’s stunned question made Anastasia laugh aloud. From Julius’s stories and the memories of Subaru, Petelgeuse was a nightmare of a man, insanely dedicated to a cruel Witch to cause as much pain and misery as possible. Geuse was anything but, more a mild-mannered priest or scholar than a crazed lunatic. If only he had stayed as such, she wouldn’t have minded hiring him as her personal source of Witch history. It amused Anastasia how much her worldview had changed in such a brief time.

“Anastasia-sama. Please explain why you wish to stay here. While I understand that these memories would be enticing, there is no need to wallow in them. Your husband is just around the corner, there is no need to keep him waiting,” Geuse urged.

“That’s just what I’m doing,” Anastasia said, “Subaru is still in danger.”

“With what? There isn’t—”

“There’s still one Witch who is clinging onto his heart,” Anastasia remembered that shadowy figure. It didn’t take her long to connect the dots on which Witch Factor that was, “And I’m not leaving until she either gets out of his body or dies.”

Technically, Anastasia did not know if she could kill a Witch Factor. She made Gluttony submit but killing one was another question. One she really wanted to test.

“…Anastasia-sama, you cannot fight the Witch of Envy.”

“Correction, I totally can. Furthermore, I didn’t ask for your opinion.”

“Do not be so arrogant!” Geuse yelled, “You have already won so much. This could lead to you losing everything you have gained.”

“I haven’t won enough. Not at all. Do you think I would be satisfied with such a meager victory? So what if I killed some rabid rabbit that thought it could become a wolf? The core problem is still here: Subaru’s Return by Death. There is no way she will stop rampaging and even if I were to leave, just one death is all it would take for all of this to be for nothing,” she said.

Anastasia wasn’t taking any chances. No more. She could feel her instincts chanting to her. This was a golden moment to win everything. She won’t let such a situation slip out of her grasp.

“And how do you propose to counter such an issue?”

Anastasia had already thought of this extensively. “You mentioned how our Ods are gateways to Od Laguna. I’ve thought about what that means for the Authorities themselves, how they feed off of us. Each Witch Factor seems to directly influence our Ods in different ways. For example, taking your Sloth, it seems to be an extension of the Od itself. A direct physical manifestation of your Od onto the material world, just as you said your Authority is more akin to the connection between reality and conceptual. Am I correct?”
