Geuse was silent for a few moments, “Yes you are.”

“Now let’s take Gluttony. From what I can tell, Gluttony’s Authority seemed to take people’s names and memories by swiping it from Od Laguna itself. You said our souls go to Od Laguna after death, right? Then there must something that anchors us to it. A marker that gravitates our souls after death. If the Od is the gateway, then there must be some way that Od Laguna recognizes us. My guess is that our names are related to that and if so, that is how we are essentially forgotten from the world when our name is taken. Given that Gluttony can also copy people’s techniques and bodies, my hypothesis is that Gluttony can take these portions of Od Laguna and anchor them to their user’s Ods or souls instead. This allows them those aforementioned copy abilities.” It wasn’t perfect but her logic had some sense.

Geuse’s lack of retort spoke volumes of how close she was getting, “Be that as it may, how would this knowledge help you?”

“I’m going to anchor Subaru’s soul to mine using Gluttony and Greed as conduits,” she could feel Geuse shudder with alarm. Her words must have rattled him profusely for it to cause an effect on her, “Greed has the ability to connect our souls and Ods together. It can even transfer mana from one gate to the other. If I can anchor our souls to each other—tying our names to each other souls— using Gluttony, then theoretically, even if Return by Death were to activate, my soul should return with him. Or at the very least, the memories from my soul will be sent back with him and transfer to my past self. Either way, same result.”

It was a huge gamble but if it’s even 0.001% possible, she’ll bet on it. The only problem was that Anastasia would just need to fight Envy afterward. There was no way that Witch Factor would let her do whatever she pleased if their souls were chained together. She was only lucky that it was not actively going after her at the moment. It seemed to be too distraught about Subaru’s soul disappearing than anything else.

“…”

“…Am I wrong?”

“Have I mentioned you are insane?!” Geuse shouted.

Anastasia ignored his question, “So I’m right. Good to hear.”

“You—” Anastasia suddenly heard a cascade of curses that she was never aware of. Must have been words that slowly phased out through the centuries. Her mental image of Geuse was shifting slightly, “Do you realize how ludicrous such a proclamation is?!”

“Who in the world says ludicrous these days? And stop asking me rhetorical questions and get to the point.”

“Your souls would be anchored to each other rather than Od Laguna. That means if you were to die permanently, instead of being sent to the afterlife, you have a high chance of being forever chained to the earth. And that is the least of your concerns. There is a nonzero chance such a fusion could go far beyond a simple connection. You could very well combine into one person. Your souls may not be able to differentiate from one another. You could become an amalgamation. Your Ods may collapse from the sheer pressure. The risks are exponentially higher than whatever gains you are thinking of.”

Anastasia thought for a moment and then shrugged, “Honestly being chained to Subaru forever doesn’t sound like a bad idea. We could be ghosts haunting our kids and descendants together. It’s kind of romantic, even with the whole soul fusion thing.”

Geuse sounded exasperated, “Even if you succeed and were to confront Satella-sama, do you think you’ll have a chance given it took Reid, Volcanica-sama, and Flugel-sama to incapacitate her? You are just one girl.”

“I have to at least try.”

“Would you take this seriously for once?!”

“I am being sincere,” Anastasia looked towards the memory of her and Subaru again. They were talking about books from Subaru’s world. About this one with vampires and glowing skin. Her heart warmed hearing Subaru’s laughter in the distance, “This is the only chance I have to never let Subaru be alone again. He won’t have to suffer being the only one who remembers everything. Or to fight with all the pain and baggage that comes with death. He can finally have someone who understands him. Don’t act like I am not considering all the possibilities and probabilities. This is the only way that gives me the biggest payoff.” Anastasia narrowed her eyes, “And instead of chastising me, how about you be honest yourself?”

“What do you mean?”

“You’re not worried about me or Subaru. At least, that’s not your main concern. No, you’re worried about Satella, aren’t you?”

“…”

She hit it right on the bullseye, “If you were someone who was part of the Witch Cult willingly, then that devotion to the Witch of Envy wasn’t faked. You hold some loyalty to her that goes beyond mere pretense. So what is it? Why do you really not want me to fight her?”

“…Satella-sama is not your enemy,” Geuse whispered in her head, “She’s just a normal girl who made a bad decision. She wanted to save her loved ones and paid the price dearly.”

Anastasia was reminded of that Tia copycat. “So what? Should I just allow my husband to suffer because of her love? Should I allow the world to suffer because of one girl?” A rabid animal was a rabid animal. It needed to be put down before it could harm more people.

“No. But you would do the same Anastasia-sama. If Subaru-sama was in a terrible situation and it would require you to throw away all of your morals. You would do the exact same as her.”

Anastasia’s eyes widened. Her first reaction was to deny such a claim. But she couldn’t necessarily disagree, it was true. Her mind thought of all the holes in that logic, but she couldn’t shake the hypocrisy of her own dissent. She knew that if Subaru or her camp were in such a situation, she would be the same type of person. Carving up the world and all of its inhabitants just for a chance for them to be safe.

Despite this, she hated the Witch and would rather see such an abomination purged from the world than to let it have the chance of ruining her happiness. “Even so. If I am a hypocrite, then let me be one.”

“Then I cannot let you go any further Anastasia-sama,” An Unseen Hand snaked out of her torso and wrapped its fingers around Anastasia’s neck, ready to crush her windpipe at a moment’s notice. “Do not try me. Even though I am grateful for your help in combatting Pandora, I will not let you harm Satella-sama in any way.”

Anastasia did not even flinch. He must really see her as a threat if he was going to such lengths to stop her. Either he is overestimating her capabilities after the Pandora confrontation, or he thinks she has a real chance at murdering a Witch. Either way, she merely looked down at the hand and sighed, “Geuse, you are making a mistake. Don’t make me put you down too.”

Geuse was silent. It seemed he made his choice. And so did she.

She could feel his alarm as Gluttony howled with glee within her. She didn’t know what was going on but she was sure he was currently surrounded by whatever shape or form it had taken. “You really have become one with the Beast.”

“Final warning. I’m doing this out of courtesy for helping me but don’t think that gives you leeway in stopping me,” Anastasia glared at the hand in disdain. “I like you Geuse. Let’s keep it that way.”

She could feel Geuse’s fear, smell it even. Even so, he was resolute, “Unfortunately, Anastasia-sama, I cannot. Thank you for all you have done but I will not stand down. Not ever again.”

Not again? Anastasia focused on his Unseen hand. Despite its grip, it hadn’t tightened at all despite the increased tension. In fact, it was shaking.

Anastasia blinked. Geuse, shaking?

Even when they were confronting Pandora, the Witch of Vainglory that was responsible for all of Geuse’s problems, he had never once staggered in his resolve, despite his fears. It was something else. But what would make someone like him shake?

A sound brought her attention to the memory again. Subaru was humming to himself as he let Anastasia sleep on his lap. Braiding her hair and looking at her with such tenderness. His hands were careful, but every so often, she could see them tremble. As if afraid of hurting her.

Oh.

Still staring, Anastasia felt the Beast’s howl lessen into silence. “Geuse. Before you went insane, did you ever kill anyone?”

He seemed to be confused but he soon responded, “…I was but a scholar.”

So he hadn’t. Anastasia finally understood. He wasn’t shaking because he was scared of her. He was shaking because he was scared of hurting her. Because he didn’t want to hurt her. Because he was only doing it to protect someone he swore loyalty to. Because deep down, Geuse was a kind man.

Anastasia sighed deeply and ran her hand down her face. She chuckled to herself, causing Geuse to yelp. Perhaps Gluttony was copying her laughter, it must be such a disturbing sight to see if that was so. But she couldn’t help but laugh. Because despite how much she hated Envy, she was curious about Satella.

Who was Satella? Why did she care for Subaru? What was she like to inspire such fierce devotion from her followers? To make men like Geuse, who seemed to be pacifists by nature, to fight and kill for her sake. It reminded her of the Triplets. Of the day where Mimi, Tivey, and Hetaro swore that they would always protect her with their dying breath, when they were a mere 9 years old. They didn’t have to be soldiers, but they wanted to, for her sake. It brought her to tears to see them grow up into fine mercenaries.

She couldn’t help but be sentimental. Maybe it was a consequence of going through Subaru’s memories, but she could sense the love Satella had for him. It was pure. Warm. Filled with regret and sorrow. And hope. She related to what little she knew about the woman. They both loved the same man and were willing to do whatever it took to keep him safe. So much so, that even if her hatred ran pure, so did a measure of empathy. A glimmer of understanding.

And maybe that was enough.

As Anastasia looked at the memory of her and Subaru, all she could think of was the future. Of who she wanted to be. Where she wanted to go. What she wanted to become. At the end of the day, did she want to be a bloody conqueror taking everything she ever wanted? Or was there a better path?

“…Geuse,” Anastasia said, “Let’s make a deal.”

-----------------------

All that there was, should have been nothingness. That was the feeling Natsuki Subaru should have felt as he returned to the land of shadows within his own soul. He was tired. Exhausted. He had been on a long journey and his muscles ached, his mind was heavy, and his bones were weary. He just wanted to sleep or rest. Or finally mold his entire being with the nothingness surrounding him.

“—love you.”

Subaru barely reacted. The same words as always. Subaru remembered this. Just like always. A voice that crept into his skull, ready to welcome him with endless affection and adoration. Every time he died. Every time he felt lost. Every time he was broken. She molded him back to reality without his consent. He would soon forget and the cycle would begin again. He had lost and was now within the grasp of a woman who was all he had left. Because all he had done was forgotten. It was fine. It was just like always. He’ll just have to begin again. And strive to his happy ending once more.

Alone.

“Dumbass. Can’t believe you did all that stupid shit for me. You’re lucky you’re not awake right now.”

…This was not the shadow garden. That voice was familiar but not the same as always. Not like a shadow seeping into his brain, and more akin to sunlight drifting into his soul. It felt nice. But he couldn’t put his finger on who it was despite it being on the tip of his tongue. He knew. He knew. He knew! It was different but why?

No. In reality, everything was different. He thought he had returned to nothingness but with closer inspection, he had not. Warmth flowed through his body. A cool breeze wafted upon his skin. He could feel something soft on the back of his head, paired with fingers that ran through his hair. Subaru was wrong. It was not nothingness. It was…everything. He could feel everything.

“You know I’m kind of annoyed you didn’t tell me about Natsumi Schwartz. You told me all of your stupidest secrets, and that’s the one thing you refrained from? The second we get home, I’m raiding my closet and we are not leaving until I’m satis—”

Okay. Where the fuck is he? Who is this? What the fuck is going on?!

Subaru’s eyes fluttered, straining as if he had been asleep for years, until finally they opened to blinding light. His eyes slowly adjusted to his new environment. Expecting a dark world, he was instead shown a world of pure light. White blankness as far as the eye could see. It was also familiar but not for his soul. His soul wasn’t like this. But that wasn’t what he focused on. No. He focused on the person smiling on top of him. The person that drew his breath away and nearly made his heart stop.

Mauve hair, light blue eyes, soft cheeks. A smile that was as mischievous as it was beautiful. A veil of white drifted down from the top of her head, the cool breeze shifted the lace mask and revealed her face as it ebbed and flowed like water around her. He had dreamt of this image for so long. A promise that he wanted fulfilled as soon as their names had returned. To see it so soon, he could only describe the moment as rapturous.

He would never forget this moment until he died, and maybe even beyond. Her smile seemed to brighten even more as she noticed his expression. Her voice was everything he ever wished for, worthy of worship and adoration, “Good morning, ya little shit.”

Subaru knew where he was.

He was finally home.

Chapter 59: Heaven

Summary:

Together again.

Chapter Text

“Morning, ya little shit,” Anastasia blurted out. She blushed slightly as her smile threatened to literally jump off her face. She couldn’t help it. She was happier than ever.

Subaru blinked, staring straight at Anastasia with an expression that could only be described as dumbfounded beyond existence. “…”

Anastasia continued to smile until the silence became more and more uncomfortable, the lack of reaction being both unexpected and fairly disconcerting.

“Uh, Subaru?” Anastasia was expecting something more expressive. Maybe a desperate hug or crying or even a passionate kiss. She’d prefer any of those more than just a blank stare. It was kind of creeping her out. She poked his cheek, “Ya just going to stare?”

Subaru did not blink, still boring a hole through Anastasia with such intensity that it made her feel embarrassed. Anastasia, not wanting to make it more awkward than it already was, continued to poke his cheek. He then caught her finger with one hand and brought the other to her face. She could feel the palm on her own cheek. It was warm. So warm.

“Am I dreaming?” He said with a voice that was on the cusp of breaking. “Is this real?” His lips wavered, as if not knowing whether to smile or frown, “Are you real?”

Anastasia shuddered. She was beginning to understand why he was reacting like this. She put her hand on his, letting him feel her warmth from both sides, “Does this feel real?” She tried to give him an earnest smile, but it seemed to be the wrong decision given he flinched. “Subaru—”

“I…how do I know you’re you. And not, well—”

“Some weird copycat, memory clone, or manifestation of a Witch Factor?”

Subaru finally blinked, “Yeah. That.”

Anastasia chuckled. It’s been a very weird week all things considered. She thought for a second, putting a finger on her lips, “Well let’s see. Can’t say anything that is memory related. And if someone were pretending to be me, you would be able to tell, right?”

Subaru nodded. She remembered seeing him reveal how he knew Louis was a fake based on the way she breathed and blinked. It was very creepy. And very touching. She would have considered it romantic if she wasn’t in the middle of a nervous breakdown back then while watching. Still, there’s a much simpler way to tell.

She channeled Greed and pushed a finger onto Subaru’s chest and slowly lifted it up, revealing a thin thread of iridescent light. Pulling it towards her own chest, she allowed the connection to stabilize and waited as the emotions and thoughts began to transfer.

Subaru’s face morphed from bewilderment to confusion to a mix between understanding and terror, “Wait, how—”

“Shh, just wait,” she put a finger on his lips, “We’ll talk more after this but this will be much faster.”

A few more seconds passed before a rush of warmth filled Anastasia’s body. And then cold. And then hot. And then a visceral emptiness, filled with darkness. And finally, a soft beacon of desire that spread into seven hopeful clusters, lighting the way. It was odd how Greed translated Subaru’s soul to her but it felt very fitting. A paradoxical man who ends up lighting the way when all else is lost. She wondered how Subaru perceived her. Staring wistfully off to the distance as she thought, she was alarmed when she looked down to find a peculiar sight.

Subaru was crying.

She blinked. Oh—

And then he embraced her, nearly throwing her onto the ground from both his weight and velocity. She responded in kind, hugging him back just as deeply. Despite her new sense of unyielding happiness, she couldn’t help but release a well of emotion. Her joy did not wipe away all the negativity that had built up. The desperation she felt for so long. The disgust within her. The desire to be with him beyond all cost. The fear of him—and everything she knew from the last few months—ceasing to exist. It was all too much.

She did not want to let go of him ever again.

“It’s you,” Subaru nearly choked out, “It really is you. I can’t believe it. I can’t,” Subaru sobbed, making her hold him tighter than before, “How…how in the world? What happened? Where are we? Why do you look so…so…” Subaru seemed to be at a loss for words, “…I don’t know how to describe you. It’s like I’m looking at some goddess or angel or both!” Subaru laughed weakly, “…Please don’t be a dream. I don’t want to wake up. I don’t want to go back. Not yet.”

“You won’t ever have to again. And even if you do, I’ll be there, every step of the way,” Anastasia said, rubbing his back, “I won’t let you die again.”

Subaru chuckled again, he didn’t sound like he believed her, “Now I know this is a dream, because…that’s just not going to happen.”

“It is,” She he would react like this, “I already made sure you and I will never be separated again.”

She then blushed slightly. That sounded very creepy.

Subaru then slowly let her go and pulled away, making her feel cold. She wanted him back in her arms again. He still held onto her—grabbing her shoulders—but he looked at her with a very concerned expression, “What exactly happened while I was knocked out?”

“Well…”

-----------------------------

Anastasia-sama. As grateful as I am, I would still like to state again: this is a horrible idea.

“Opinion noted and discarded,” Anastasia said as she helped Greed onto his feet, the personification of a Witch Factor was barely able to stand, “Has anyone ever told you that you are a wimp, Geuse?”

Geuse sounded insulted, Some of my followers have said that I have the disposition of a Kararagian general from Fusumi.

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “You talk good, but when it comes to personal matters, you run away like a little bitch?”

Geuse was silent for a second before shouting, That’s what that means?!

Anastasia sighed, “How do you not know the story of General Hisa during the Warring City-States period? Weren’t you alive for centuries?”

Apologies but I was a scholar of witchcraft, magic, and spirits. Not military history. Even with all the time in the world, it is nearly impossible to specialize in every single category. Well, unless you are the Witch of Greed. Geuse grumbled within her mind. I cannot believe Ingrum called me that, the nerve. I thought it was a compliment all this time!

“Well I wouldn’t be too pissed, the guy was known to be fairly competent at his job. It’s just he was kind of a coward when it came to love. Pining after a woman up until his death and being well known for it after they found the thousands of love letters he kept locked in his drawers,” Anastasia remembered learning about him when Ricardo began teaching her about tactics. Though her main lesson from that particular topic was to burn anything shameful before she died. “I doubt you were as bad as him.”

…

“Geuse?”

So what is the first step?

Alright. Reminder to herself, needle Geuse about his love life later. If she survives this. Or if she remains conscious in the weird amalgam homunculi mix of her and Subaru. Romantic homunculi wasn’t on her bucket list of things to do with Subaru but she’ll adapt if worst comes to shove. “First step is having you all in the same area.”

She looked at Greed who was still a little dazed after regenerating his entire body. The poor guy looked like he was about to collapse. She spoke a little softer, “You think you can do that? I just need you to go into my Od and help Geuse and Gluttony out.”

Greed winced, as if hearing her was too much, losing his balance and falling over. Anastasia was about to catch him from plummeting to the floor when his body slowly unraveled into bright lights; her hands phased through the lights as if they were not even there. The bright lights flickered as they flowed into dark vines and leaves before entering Anastasia’s chest. For a second, she felt a wave of nausea hit her, causing her to stumble to the ground before feeling an intense feeling of dread permeating through her body.

“W-what’s happening?” Anastasia sputtered.

Geuse shouted with alarm, Anastasia-sama?! I told you this would have happened! You could barely handle two Witch Factors in your Od, a third is causing your soul to corrupt from the pressure. One of us needs to get out of you before it’s too late!

“NO!” She was so close, she could feel it, “N-not yet, just, help me! How do I use your guys’ powers?!”

Geuse hesitated before relinquishing the information, You need to channel your desires. Accept them. Revel in them.

“I already—”

The root, not the result. You need to reach deep within and say what you always wanted. Sincerely. Earnestly. We need to move quickly. You must focus. Think of what you most desire. What you wish for beyond a single doubt. What makes you want to covet everything in the world? What makes you want to devour all in your wake? What makes you abstain when the world harangues you?

“I-I don’t, I can’t—” Anastasia felt like she wanted to vomit, like her eyeballs were about to burst. Her body was about to rupture. She needed to focus, but what could she do?

…Tell me why you want Subaru. Why you need to stay linked to him at all costs. What does Anastasia Hoshin—no, the hyena called Little Sprout—want most in the world?

Geuse’s voice rang inside her head. A mere drop in the static that threatened to engulf her entire mind. She was about to scream—to cry out at the absurdity of the world as it threatened to tear her limb from limb. But right before dipping into the mental abyss, she thought of Subaru.

And in the next second, her mind was clear.

What did she want? It was simple.

Hunched over and filled with despair, she whispered her deepest desire, “I don’t want to be alone again.”

And then everything turned white.

 

 

 

 

 

 

And then black.

 

 

 

 

 

 

White.

 

 

Black.

 

White.

Black.

White. Black. White. Black. White. On and on, she felt her soul spiral into light and darkness rapidly. It felt like her body was being ripped apart, cell by cell, atom by atom. And just as her mind began to dissipate, as the thoughts in her head became strands of entropy. Just as her entire being ceased to exist.

She felt someone grab her hand.

Hand? She didn’t have a hand. No. She did. She always did. Just like she always had a brain. A mouth. A head. A torso. A body. She had a body filled with blood, nerves, muscles, and skin. This felt familiar. As if she had crafted herself into being time and time, again and again. Whether in the real world or in this shadow world, she always was self-made. Born from nothing, crafted through sheer will. No one was responsible for her creation, except her. She was always alone.

No.

Not exactly. Even when she was down on her luck, when she felt like a lone pebble in the mountains, there was always someone reaching out to her.  Turrel, Lotus, Ricardo, Subaru. Even if she didn’t want it at first. Even if she was scared or suspicious. She would eventually take their hand and never want to let go.

Because the fact was that she was lonely. Breaking a loaf by herself, as she hid away from the bakers who chased her throughout Banan’s slums. It always tasted so bland. And it wasn’t because of the quality, nor from how little she had. It was because there was no one to share such joy with. No one there to eat with her, complain about the hard crust and mold. No one to cry with her as the hunger grew worse. No one to hug for warmth as the cold night air crept into the alleyways. No one there to tell her that everything would be okay.

The cruelty of being given companionship was that you notice the absence even more. She had grown so used to the ramble and bustle of the Iron Fang, that she became arrogant. She believed that all of the hard work she did would lay the foundation for her future. No matter what happened, she would always be able to get back up.

Until she lost everything.

The name she chose, the family she chose, and the life she chose. All gone in the blink of an eye. And the emptiness she had once felt had returned with greater intensity. Like a starving beast that had been fed for so long, she longed for the ecstasy that she drowned in before. Because when she was just a hyena, you could not crave what you did not know.  Even when she felt her head get bashed in and her body crumple onto the cobblestone, she could not even fathom the betrayal, because all she had ever known was violence.

If Turrel could kill Danzi for a simple squabble, despite how close they were, then such a small act of cruelty paled in comparison. Anastasia simply chose wrong. She chose to be kind instead of practical.

And yet, as she remembered nearly dying on the streets on that silent night. As she felt her body grow cold and her blood trickle out. As she grasped whatever weapon was nearby. As her rage boiled over from the cruelty of this world. As she bludgeoned her enemies until they no longer twitched. As she grabbed what remained of her meal and hid away from the world, hungry for more. As she screamed in her nightmares and dreams, hoping for anyone to answer her call.

Anastasia rejected such a reality. She hated the idea that kindness was a weakness. She hated it all. And because of her hatred, a seed was planted in her heart. A seed that sprouted into rage, and an unyielding desire to tear the status quo to shreds. To not suffer alone anymore.

Anastasia Hoshin did not run away from such a reality. No. She fought. Tooth and nail, again and again. Her rage unending, her fury unquenchable. She wanted to survive. She wanted to live. She wanted what others had and more. She accepted that the world was cruel, and so she had to be cruel as well.

She told herself, every time. To think of what would benefit her the most. To be practical and not kind.

And yet, she couldn’t help but yearn for kindness. Her cherished memories always reminded her of what she truly wanted. How Danzi always tried to find her the best toys. How Turrel would find a way to bring milk and food home everyday. How Ricardo gave her a job for a ‘debt’ that he never expected to be repaid. How Subaru would stop in the middle of the street to check on a lost candidate. Even when he was running away. And even when he was tired, and riddled with trauma and mental exhaustion, he would cry for a woman who suffered far less than he ever did.

Anastasia wanted to be cruel. She wanted to be someone who won. Who played it smart. Who no longer was forced to eat bread alone but could choose what she ate and with who.

But at the end of the day. She could reject reality but not who she was. Despite how much she locked away and hid behind cunning masks, she was weak to kindness. She could not help but love kindness. At her core, she saw the kindness of the world—battered, beaten, and betrayed—and wanted to be its friend. She wanted to stretch her hand out, to all those who longed for love where there was none.  

Because if the world is so cruel, that it would repay kindness with destruction.

Then she would subsume the world and repay kindness with kindness.

 

Ha, how simple. When you break it all down, she wasn’t greedy for much. Nothing complex.

 

Money. Power. Love. All necessities to survive, but not her deepest wish.

 

At the end of the day, she just wanted to be kind.

 

Like him.

 

Subaru.

 

What is Subaru?

 

He’s the love of her life. But what is he at his core?

 

If Anastasia wanted kindness to have a friend, then why does she do this all? For him? Because he was kind?

 

Selfish at times, but also beyond selfless. Always wanting to make others happy because he wanted to make up for his own inadequacies.

Never satisfied. Always wanting to be someone better. Always looking at people as if they were enough, but he never was.

Subaru wanted to be like his father, loved by all. He wanted to be loved by anyone and everyone. He wanted to be someone special. If that meant being a knight, or a hero, then he would do it. Because if someone believed in him, then all was right. If everyone believed in him, then he was acceptable. If no one believed in him, then he shouldn’t even exist.

How cruel.

Anastasia found such cruelty disgusting. She remembered how she first saw him. Not on that fateful night but way before, back when the Royal Selection began. She understood who he was from the moment she laid eyes on him. Young, naïve, and desperate to prove himself. If it wasn’t Emilia, it would have been someone else. Someone who could give him a hand and guide him. To be the one who believes in him and pushes him forward as the dark clouds lingered over his eyes and soul.

It reminded her of herself. How despite her wish to be self-sufficient, self-made, she always looked for a hand to hold her own. Because she was weak. Born without a functioning gate. Only able to rely on her intellect and quick thinking to survive day after day. Yet always wishing someone would hold her hand through it all. It made her feel ashamed. Like that weak hyena was all she was and will ever be. A starving beast that was only led around by her own desires. And not cold rationality.

No wonder her past self sought to take advantage of the boy, teaching him a lesson before he ended up killed.

But perhaps that shame was what she needed to accept. The hatred she felt for her own irrationality was because she did not want to be that hyena again. That starving beast. But why not? That same starvation, that hunger to survive, allowed her to flourish. It was what allowed her to become who she was today. It allowed her to not bend when others sought to dominate her. It allowed her to reject the safety of a delusional future. Allowed her to not break under the weight of an unthinkable present.

Anastasia did not need to change. She needed to accept—no—love who she always was. Not just what benefited her. But also all the warts, scars, and troubles that came with it.

That she wasn’t someone who only thought with logic in mind. She was emotional.  Idiotic at times and silly at other times. Someone who could be lazy and petty. She was a fool who craved affection just like any other. Just like everyone. Just like…him.

Isn’t that interesting? They would both stand up for their loved ones. And they would both die for their loved ones. And they would both yearn for the people who made them happy. And they would both fight for their happy ending. And they were both greedy. They were stubborn. They were both weak. But they made up for it by using their minds. By being resolute when it mattered most.

Despite the external differences, internally they matched in so many ways. At their core, Anastasia and Subaru were the same. Well, no. Not exactly. But so similar, it was as if they were intertwined at the soul.

Yes! To be with each other even beyond the end of existence, that is something she desired. Shouldn’t they be together? Even their gates were complimentary. His could only absorb, while hers could only expel. It was like they each had half of a functioning gate. What if they fused into a one? Shared between them. But the only problem was that hers had an affinity to Yang while his had an affinity to Yin.

Hm.

What did Beatrice say again? Yin-Yang magic. That’s a dumb name. But if their gates fused together, then that could be possible. Why not change their affinity into something impossible? They could be something new. Something this world had never seen before.

And at that point, isn’t anything possible? If their souls were intertwined, their gates fused into one, couldn’t their Od’s become connected. Couldn’t they share everything. Thoughts, ideas, desires. Everything. Hair, eyes, lungs, hearts, stomach, kidneys—

Anastasia ripped away from the singularity. That was too close. She needed to be more careful. No romantic homunculi fusions.

Where was she? Right, similarities and differences. No. That wouldn’t make sense. Internally they were similar, but externally they were different. Different personalities. Different appearances. Anastasia liked how she looked. She loved her purple hair, cute face, and though her body wasn’t the ideal feminine physique, she could never trade it away for something different. Plus, Subaru loved how she looked. And she liked how Subaru looked.

Black hair, sharp brown eyes that were scary but kind, and a not so muscular body. Ah, but she liked his white hair. It made him look mature. She secretly hoped his hair would stay as a salt and peppir mix. She knew he felt insecure about it, like his scars. But Anastasia loved them all. She wouldn’t want them to be wiped away. She wouldn’t want him to change. She wouldn’t want him to be like her exactly. She wanted them to be different. Distinct but similar.

Intertwined. Like how the cursed dragon’s blood was shared between them. Their gates, souls, and Ods should be shared. Conflicting but coexisting despite all odds. Just like their relationship. It shouldn’t work. They should be a volatile mess that was on fire and streaking towards death every second. But they don’t. They were alive and well. They were an anomaly beyond comprehension.

Subaru and Anastasia. Anastasia and Subaru. Forever together, but never one. Two stars, dancing across the night sky. That was all she wanted. To never be alone again.

When she saw Subaru on that fateful night, she saw someone who was alone like her. And how right she was. Because with Return by Death, he would always be alone. No one to talk to, no one to cry to, no one to hear his woes. Always holding the memories that only he can remember.

Never again.

But something was missing! As Greed, Gluttony, and Sloth bound them together. She could feel that the connections were slipping. It was too unnatural. It needed something permanent. Something integral so that their existences wouldn’t tear each other to shreds.

And Anastasia knew just what to do. As her lungs were formed out of darkness and light, her voice carried out through the endless abyss,

“Natsuki Subaru. I, Anastasia Hoshin, once again promise to always make you happy. That in sickness or great health, whether we are poor or healthy, old or young, I’ll always be faithful to you. No matter the challenge. No matter the struggle. No matter the situation. We’ll press forth and fight it together. All my burdens. All my sins. All my flaws. I’ll lay bare to you. And if you are willing, I will carry all you bare to me. And you the same for me. I promise…for death shall never part us. Always yours, Pleione,” the words echoed back to her. And for a brief moment, it was as if the last word was replaced with a different name.

 

Anastasia fell to the ground gasping for breath, coughing as she looked around to get her bearings. Once she said what was needed, it felt like her consciousness finally stabilized. It seems her gamble worked. And boy, did it work in unexpected ways. Her eyes widened as she realized what became of the Od-world after the fusion. Before, she only saw darkness as far as the eyes could see. It was still present right behind her. But now she saw a far-reaching white blankness that stretched across infinite in front of her, only for it to stop where she stood. It was as if the world split in two: a world of shadows and a world of light.

So entranced by what she did, that she didn’t realize someone walked past her. A very familiar person wearing a flowing black veil and dress. Satella’s presence sent shivers down Anastasia’s spine as she realized where she was heading: a little tree surrounded by bright green grass, an oasis of color within the world of light. And sleeping soundly right below the foliage, was Natsuki Subaru.

Anastasia moved to snatch him from her clutches but slowly stopped as she saw what Satella did. As the monstrous witch kneeled down and touched Subaru’s cheek precariously, Anastasia could hear her vaguely whisper, “There you are. You are finally safe.”

“No thanks to you,” Anastasia spat. Was it childish to provoke the literal Witch of Envy? Yes. Did Anastasia regret it? No.

That got the Witch’s attention. Satella’s head motioned upward before looking over her shoulder. She did not say a word before standing up straight and turning towards her.

Anastasia struggled to hold her flinch. The black veil on her head covered her face but Anastasia already knew how she looked. It was still jarring. Satella was the exact same as Emilia. Facial profile, eyes, hair, stature, body language, everything. It was like they were twin sisters and the implications were not lost on Anastasia.

They both stared at each other, neither saying a word. In the backdrop of the world, the Witch of Envy was a dark void in the endless white canvas that spread out behind her. On the opposite end was Anastasia, still wreathed in iridescent light that flowed from her body, a bright star in the black abyss that laid in the background. Two opposing figures, anomalies in their own respective worlds.

And just as Anastasia blinked, Satella moved from her spot near Subaru to right in front of Anastasia. She nearly got in a fighting stance, ready to fight the Witch into submission, before feeling something warm surround her. Arms wrapping around her body with an intensity that felt raw and personal.

“Thank you,” she whispered in Anastasia’s ear.

Anastasia could barely process what just happened.

-----------------------

“What the fuck?” Subaru said in dismay.

“Yeah that’s what I said,” Anastasia sighed, “Words cannot describe how I felt at that moment.”

There was one thing etched in Anastasia’s mind that she did understand, and she chose not to linger on it. She threw that possible existential crisis into the broken vault and taped it shut. The very idea made her viscerally nauseous and that wasn’t even considering the fury of emotions that sprouted as the Witch hugged her like a lover would. She’ll go through that can of worms later when she had a better idea of what was going on anymore. At the very least, she and Subaru were on the same page now.

“No that’s not what I was cursing about,” okay maybe not. Subaru ran his hand through his hair, his face on the verge of a scowl, “I just…you didn’t have to do all that.”

Anastasia moved the white veil out of the way, frowning, “…What do you mean?”

Subaru waved his hand in the air, “This! All of this. I can’t—I, I don’t…” Subaru seemed to be at a loss for words.

“Subaru—”

“You didn’t have to do any of that,” Subaru blurted out, manic insanity darting within his eyes, “There was so much risk and you didn’t even know if it would all work out. Why would you do that all. For me?!”

“Because I love you,” Anastasia answered simply.

Subaru stared at her as if she was insane, “I didn’t do anything to deserve that.”

“You didn’t have to.”

“That isn’t the point!” Subaru cried out, regretting his outburst evidently by his expression, “…You saw everything, didn’t you? Why…why don’t you hate me? Why aren’t you disgusted by me?!”

It nearly broke her heart in two when she heard those words, “I would never hate you.”

“That doesn’t make any sense.”

“Why not?”

“Because I am the reason for all your problems!” Subaru squeezed his chest and threw his other hand out, “If I wasn’t with you, you would have had no problems. The bandits, Tia-Two, your Od, Pandora, everything. I made your life significantly worse just by existing. How…how could you forgive me for that?”

“Because that wasn’t your fault? All those problems were not because of you, you idiot!” Anastasia yelled back, “You were a victim in all that.”

“I wasn’t.”

“You were.”

“I wasn’t!”

“You were!”

“No I wasn’t! I was never a victim!” Subaru cried, his voice breaking, “I chose to be there. I chose to keep being near you. I chose to make your life worse because I couldn’t bear the thought of leaving you.”

“That still doesn’t make you responsible! Why do you keep acting like everything is your fault?! Like you have to solve everything?!”

“Because if I’m not then why did I have to suffer?!”

“…” Anastasia said nothing as he covered his face, and sobbed, a mental dam breaking in front of her.

He continued to cry quietly, his breathing becoming erratic and deep as he tried to stop the well of tears from falling. And failing.

“…If it wasn’t my fault, then why did I—” Subaru choked, almost hyperventilating.

“Subaru?!” She quickly rushed to his side.

He grit his teeth as he slowly forced out, “Why did I…” he punched his leg, “Why did I…” he tore at his clothes, as if it took all he could to say it, “Why…”

Anastasia held onto him, “Stop it! You don’t have to—”

“Why did I have to die?!” Subaru screamed out.

“…”

“What was the point in all of this?! Being killed, tortured, again and again and again!” Subaru poured out his emotions, pushing away from Anastasia, “All my friends hating me and forgetting time after time! If it wasn’t my fault, then whose was it?!” Subaru’s face was disgusting. Rancid, filled with so much self-hatred and self-pity that it reminded her of the scene at the capital, “If I wasn’t such a weak person, I wouldn’t have to die so much! If I could fight, I wouldn’t have to be a burden on my friends! If I was smarter, I could have solved all my problems! If I’m not the problem, then who is?!”

Anastasia stayed quiet as Subaru continued to rant. A part of her felt like this was something he had been wanting to say for a long time.

“I didn’t mean to look like a Witch Cultist or smell like one. I didn’t even know why I was so suspicious in the first place. I didn’t know how Lugunica worked! I didn’t know Satella wasn’t a good name! I didn’t know how to bargain or to negotiate or to do diplomacy or any of that bullshit! I was just some stupid fucking kid who wanted to be cool! Do you know who you just confessed your love to?! You saw it! I’m just some sick pathetic moron who gets obsessed with women and dies for them! I’m a nobody! I’m less than a nobody! Why do you love me?! Why don’t you hate me?! Why is it so easy for you to tell me?! Why?! Just…why? Why are you still looking at me like that?”

Subaru waited for Anastasia’s response, “…Like what?”

“Like…like none of that matters.”

“It does matter,” before he could argue, Anastasia pulled him towards her, not letting him escape again. She held him tightly, not making the same mistake as before, “Because you matter. I don’t hate you. I don’t think you are disgusting. Everything you are. Everything you do. Everything you will be. To me, all of it matters. Because every single thing you are, the worst parts and the best parts, I love every single thing that makes you, you.

Subaru shifted, evidently trying to get away from her and failing, “I don’t understand.”

“Can’t you believe it?”

“Love isn’t unconditional,” Subaru chuckled weakly, “I know that for sure. The only unconditional love there is, is between a parent and a child.”

Anastasia pulled him in tighter, “That’s true. My love isn’t unconditional. I’m a greedy bitch like that.”

Subaru laughed again, though this time it felt more genuine, “It’s what I love about you.”

She smiled, “My condition is simple. Just love me back.”

“That’s it?”

“Well, no, you have to love me forever.”

She could feel Subaru’s arms wrap around her body, returning the hug finally, “Done. You were already going to receive that.”

“Good because I have more,” Anastasia nuzzled his neck, “You have to be a dutiful husband. I expect you to be the last thing I see before I sleep and the first thing I see when I wake up. I want at least one kid and we’ll decide if I can handle having more. I want at least four kisses every day.”

“Only four?”

“Only so you don’t forget. I’m expecting us to break records every day.”

Subaru snorted, “Competitive as always.”

“You know me. Also, no other girls. This is not a harem.”

“I—that wasn’t even on my mind?”

“Good. Now get ready, because here are the hardest conditions.”

“I thought you said this was going to be simple,” Subaru remarked.

Anastasia bit him in response, he yelped adorably, “It is.”

“Wait I can feel pain here now?”

Anastasia ignored him and continued her list, “You are not allowed to die on your own anymore.”

“…”

“Subaru? Do you disagree?”

“No it’s just, well,” Subaru stuttered, “I don’t know how to explain it.”

“We can talk about that more later when you are comfortable,” Anastasia rubbed circles on his back.

“Yeah…but yeah I still agree.”

“You sure?”

“Ha, what can I say? If my wife is telling me I can’t die, I guess I shouldn’t.”

He didn’t sound sincere, but Anastasia will take what she can get. Baby steps, “And finally, no matter what happens from now on. No matter what we face. You and I are always going to face it together. No going in separately, no acting like either of us shouldn’t be there. Everything, from here on out, it is either Subaru and Anastasia or nobody. Am I clear?”

“Crystal. So that’s it? Seems simple.”

“Says the guy who was panicking that he wasn’t worthy of me,” Anastasia teased.

“Pot, kettle. You were the one who spent a whole week crying that you couldn’t pay me back. And now look at you, I feel like my debt is larger,” Subaru shot back.

“No mine still is. I only went through like, what, an hour of excruciating pain? You went through weeks of it.”

“Technically only a week.”

“Aren’t you my age now?”

“…I might be older than you actually,” Subaru said.

Anastasia shrugged, “That’s fine. I always liked older men anyway.”

Subaru choked, “Yeah…uh. Still can’t believe that your first crush was Ricardo. Not to say there is anything wrong with Ricardo, I love the guy. It’s just—"

“Don’t you dare call me a furry!”

“I wasn’t!” Subaru panicked, “Man, I hate that you know Earth slang now.”

Anastasia smirked, “Sucks doesn’t it. Now the tables have turned!”

She could feel Subaru shudder, “Oh God.”

“Hm? Are you cringing?”

“Please stop.”

“I guess I’m too based for you—EEP!” Anastasia started to giggle as Subaru tickled her sides relentlessly.

“No more! I can only handle so much mental trauma at this point—wait, wait, wait, let’s talk about this!” Anastasia began tickling him back. They started tickling and tackling each other, rolling all over the grass without a care in the world, laughing nonstop.

After an extensive period of tickle fighting, they both laid on their backs next to each other, smiling. Drinking in each other’s company.

“…”

“…”

Subaru spoke first, “I missed this.”

“Me too,” Anastasia replied, sneaking her hand into his. He wrapped his fingers around hers. “Do you feel better?”

She looked over to see Subaru nod, “Yeah. But it all feels so unreal. Like this is all a dream. And I’m going to wake up to a real life nightmare again. And…”

She could understand what he was implying, she squeezed his hand, “I told you. This is real. You’re safe. I’m safe. And we’re together. That’s all that matters.”

“You aren’t going to disappear?”

“Never.”

“…”

“Say it.”

“I wasn’t going to say anything.”

“I know you, you hesitated,” Anastasia urged him to be more honest.

“…You aren’t interested in Julius, are you?”

Anastasia stared at him, “I mean not anymore.”

“Okay that’s good. That’s…good.”

“You really thought I still liked him?”

“Kind of? I mean, he’s like the picturesque knight in shining armor,” Subaru said with a little awe.

“Be that as it may, while I’m not quite sure how Julius felt about me. There was nothing between us besides some flirting,” Anastasia thought for a moment, “Frankly, I’m more concerned that he has feelings for you.”

Subaru blinked, “Say what now.”

“I mean, Julius has praised you every time you came up in conversation. Never really understood it until now.”

“…You’re joking.”

“I’m really not.”

Subaru face palmed, “Okay, I’m going to delete this conversation from my mind now.”

Anastasia laughed and poked him, “Oh come on. I like that you were a little jealous. But I can’t believe you thought I still liked him considering all I’ve done and said to you.”

Subaru grimaced, acting a little sheepish, “I mean I wouldn’t blame you. He’s a very handsome guy.”

“And I have a handsome guy as my husband. Stop talking shit about yourself.”

“Haha, I didn’t mean it like that,” Subaru put the back of his free hand over his eyes, “It’s just that I don’t want you to restrict yourself.”

“Subaru, I mean this with my whole heart, I will never love anyone else,” Anastasia put her hand on her chest and looked at him seriously. “You are the only one. And if you disappeared, life isn’t worth living.”

“Wait hold on, what are you trying to say?”

“We both know what I said during that one loop. Even though I don’t know what that me was thinking, the fact still stands.”

“Ana—”

“This is the only way I can get through to you, you idiot,” Anastasia sighed, “I don’t want you to ever doubt me.”

“I don’t! I guess… I understand why you were so worried about Emilia and Rem.”

Anastasia gave a morose smile and rolled over to him, rubbing her face into his side and breathing in deep, “Yeah. But not anymore.”

“Why?” Subaru asked as he grabbed her shoulder and tucked her in even closer. She squirmed into a good position and rested her head on his chest.

“I’ve seen your whole life. I saw what you said at Roswaal’s. I know how you feel now.”

Subaru sighed, “Well that’s good. Sucks that I only saw like less than half of your life though.”

“We can watch it together later,” Anastasia waved her hand as the black and white world shifted into Lugunica’s forests. “Gluttony has its perks.”

“Wow, I guess so,” Subaru looked around in sheer wonder. He then paused in thought for a moment before looking down at her, “Wait, where is it? And Geuse? And Greed? Did they just disappear?”

Anastasia shook her head, “After Satella hugged me. Geuse appeared with the rest of the Witch Factors. They all talked for a bit before deciding to leave me and you alone for a bit. Seems there is a small pocket dimension or whatever where they can hide from us. At least it gives us some privacy.”

“Huh. The more and more I learn about these things, the more confused I get.”

“You and me both,” Anastasia curled her hair over her ear, “There’s definitely going to be an adjustment period after all of this is over.”

“Yeah…if what you said is true, there’s a lot to get used to once we wake up,” Subaru said wistfully.

She rubbed her cheek on his chest, “We’ll handle it together.”

“Yeah, together.”

“…”

“…”

“…”

“…Ana?”

“Yeah?”

“I think I’m broken.”

“Me too.”

Subaru chuckled, “Sorry about that.”

“No. It wasn’t your fault, you little shit,” Anastasia pinched his side, making him wince, “I was always broken. Ever since I was a child, I never really had the time to realize it. Always moving forward. Trying to survive. It never hit me how messed up I was until now.”

“I guess we’re both broken then.”

“Yeah, we are. A pair of broken people. Who make one whole person.”

She could feel his hand loosen on her shoulder. She was confused until he rolled on top of her, hovering right over her face, “I love you.”

Anastasia smiled. She could feel his lips touch hers, as warm and delicious as always. She missed this more than anything else. And in between breaths, she was able to whisper back a soft, “I love you too.”

Life was hell. Their troubles were just beginning. And even after all this was said and done, they were still not done with the current crisis at hand.

But just for a moment, both Anastasia and Subaru enjoyed this brief period of respite. Together again, finally.

In this little slice of Heaven, they made from Hell.

Chapter 60: Settling Debts in Heaven

Summary:

Now that the situation has calmed, what is there to do next?

Chapter Text

“Is it wrong that I don’t want to wake up just yet?” Subaru asked, guilt creeping up his back.

“No, I get it,” Anastasia rubbed her head on his chest. Despite technically not being in their actual physical bodies, he still smelled like he always did. It made her feel comfortable, “There’s so much we have to deal with once we wake up.”

Subaru rubbed his nose on the top of her hair, “Yeah. First thing is making sure all the Gluttonies are dead. Second thing is having to explain what happened to us. I doubt Beako or Hal or Tia will let us off with a ‘it’s complicated.’”

“To be fair, it really is complicated,” Anastasia snorted, “Like half of the shit we just went through can’t be explained in one sentence.”

Subaru thought more a moment and frowned, “Yeah. I’m getting a migraine just trying to remember everything. And then we have to also deal with Julius and explaining all of that and also our whole camps are still possessed, aren’t they?”

“No, I actually don’t think so,” Anastasia raised her head to look into Subaru’s eyes, “From what I could tell, Louis’s Witch Factors all came back to me. So, they should be okay. As for Julius…” Anastasia trailed off. That was a can of worms she was definitely not ready to tackle at the moment. So much to explain, so much to apologize for, and a whole new factor in their lives they now have to deal with.

“Hey it will be fine,” Subaru cupped her cheek with his hand, “I don’t think he’ll be mad at you. He loves you. Your whole camp does.”

“…Doesn’t help the guilt. And the regret. And the feeling that I could have done better.”

“People aren’t always making the best decisions,” Subaru chuckled as he pointed at himself, “Come on. You’ve seen me at my worst. Sometimes our fears creep up at the worst times. And sometimes we don’t know how to go back. It happens.”

“Saying is better than believing,” Anastasia sighed but smiled, “Still, thanks.”

“I’ll be there for you the whole way,” Subaru kept holding onto her hand, “Even if you don’t think so, I don’t think your camp will blame you.”

“…And yours too.”

Subaru winced at that, “Yeah.”

“I don’t think they’ll hate you for being selfish.”

“Emilia will,” Subaru said, downtrodden, “At the end of the day, I abandoned her and our relationship.”

“A relationship that never realized itself because she pushed it off. Promises are important but not at the cost of your health,” Anastasia pointed at his heart, “That’s just how life is. Opportunities come and go. Luck never lasts forever. At the end of the day, you either seize your chances or wallow in regret.”

Subaru chuckled weakly, “A little harsh but yeah. I guess I just feel like an asshole. And that she deserves better.”

“…Subaru, we need to live our own lives,” Anastasia pushed off his chest and straddled his torso, “You can’t keep thinking of how to improve everyone else’s. They have to be responsible for their own.”

“I know it’s just—”

“A bad habit,” Anastasia said, “That’s why I’m reminding you that you don’t have to. Just like how you mind my own insecurities, I’m there for yours. We’ll deal with the aftermath of this. Together.”

Subaru smiled and leaned up, positioning her more comfortably on his lap and giving her a quick peck on the lips. He wrapped his arms around her and brought her close, “You’re making this really difficult. I just want to stay here forever.”

Anastasia smiled back and kissed him back. And another. And another. And some more. Subaru was fighting for air by the end of it when they separated, “Same here, ya little shit.”

“…What should we do after this is all done?” Subaru asked.

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “Get married of course. Like actual wedding, whole bells and whistles.”

Anastasia was not letting fate or any other bullshit get in the way. The second they get out of here, she is jumping Subaru and dragging him to bed. After that, going down to find a Miko to officiate their marriage. Then back to bed.

They were not going to leave the house for at least a week. Maybe a month.

Subaru laughed, “That’s obvious but I’m more talking about your candidacy.”

Anastasia blinked, “Oh right.”

Subaru’s eyes widened, “Oh, right? That’s all you have to say?”

Anastasia shrugged, “There’s nothing else. It’s just something on the list that we have to eventually tackle.”

“Ana. They won’t like us getting married.”

“And I don’t give a shit,” she narrowed her eyes. “If the council decides to get in the way of our happiness, then they can fuck off for all we care.”

Subaru seemed happy to hear that but his worries did not lessen, “Not only that, there’s the issue with…my imprisonment.”

“They won’t bother you again,” she’ll make sure of it. Every single one involved will get their just reward.

“That’s not what I meant. Crusch—”

“Can deal with the consequences.”

“Ana—”

“Subaru,” she stopped him before he could continue, covering his mouth, “I have a plan for all of this. Everything will work out. I promise.”

“…”

“Trust in your wife,” she said before lifting her hand and kissing him deeply, “I’ll get us our happy ending.”

Subaru looked dazed, “…You’re a little trigger happy.”

Anastasia smirked and licked her lips, “Can’t a gal indulge?”

Subaru laughed and gave in, “Yeah. You can. I trust you.”

They’ll figure this all out once the current crisis passes. But first…

----------------------------

“This is it?” Subaru said as they arrived at a very specific spot in his Od. Anastasia looked around. It was hard to discern how far they had gone given that everything was pure darkness. And yet, Anastasia knew by pure instinct that they were in the right spot.

Anastasia gripped her chest.

It was strange how it felt here. Compared to her Od—where she felt rather normal—there was an odd sense of pure bliss she felt with each step. An all-encompassing love that persisted within her bones and rattled her heart. An alien feeling that could barely be described other than heavenly. No wonder her mind was so scrambled while watching the memories.

“Ana?” Subaru asked, putting a hand on her shoulder, “You okay?”

“…Yeah,” Anastasia gave him a reassuring nod. It made sense given whose Od this was. Subaru’s emotions were blatant and true, as always. “Alright then, Geuse, you there?”

For a moment, nothing happened.

And then hands encased in shadows began to morph out of the darkness, slithering in the air and coalescing around each other. A mass of tendrils and appendages emerged from nothingness and with each passing second, a large mound made of the same material began to form. The hands molested the mound, pushing and carving and molding it slowly. Until the figure of a man was clearly formulated. The man began to crack, fractures manifesting all over the figure’s shadowy casing until all the pieces ruptured and dissipated back into nothing, leaving only what remained underneath.

The friendly face of Geuse Romanée-Conti.

Anastasia gave him an unamused look, “Really?”

Geuse scratched his head, embarrassed, “Apologies. I wanted to join in with the others. Subaru-sama was especially adamant that I improve my entrance.”

Anastasia looked to her Subaru and frowned. Subaru, meanwhile, had an incredibly confused expression. Subaru blinked and pointed at himself, “Me?”

Geuse blinked back in horror and blushed red, “A-ah, not you specifically! Greed! A-apologies, I am still getting used to this new arrangement.”

“I didn’t even know you guys were sentient, feels weird given you guys were inside me this entire time…” Subaru muttered.

Anastasia and Geuse grimaced in revulsion. Anastasia pinched Subaru and said, “Please don’t ever describe it like that. Again.”

Geuse nodded rapidly, “Not the best combination of words Subaru-sama.”

Subaru went pink, “You guys are just dirty minded!”

Anastasia ignored that faux pas, “So how is everyone, Geuse?”

Geuse smiled, brighter than ever before, “You’ll be happy to know that we have finally acclimated. Not only have all of us stabilized but so have your souls. It is truly a miracle that your gamble paid off.”

“And you called me insane~,” Anastasia teased.

“…Yes. You are definitely mentally stable,” Geuse said, his eyes not meeting Anastasia.

Anastasia’s eye twitched, “Hey now that we have the chance. Let’s talk about your love life—”

“Anyways!” Geuse cried out, “I doubt you came here for just pleasantries. How may I be of service to you, Anastasia-sama, Subaru-sama?” Geuse bowed, though he seemed a bit too stiff.

Subaru did a double take at Geuse and back to Anastasia. He looked utterly bewildered, “This is Petelgeuse?”

He still seemed to be processing that this was the same guy that not only slaughtered all of his friends and many innocents but was a raving lunatic spirit that tried to possess him. It must have been jarring to see in person.

Anastasia nodded in response, “Yep. Trust me. He’s a lot better now that his original personality is back.”

“I almost can’t believe it…” Subaru muttered.

“You do not have to,” Geuse said, though he was still bowing at a ninety-degree angle. His eyes were facing the floor and his tone was rather morose, “I could barely believe it myself when my mind became clear…I have sinned far more than I could ever be forgiven for. I won’t dissuade you from viewing me like the monster I was. And still am. His sins are mine to bear. Despite how little it may convey, I would like to apologize for all I had done to you, Subaru-sama.”

Subaru stared at him for a moment before sighing, “…This is going to take some getting used to. But I understand.” Subaru looked at his own hands and frowned, seeing something that only his mind could conjure, “There were so many points where I felt like my mind was on the brink of destruction. Killing people, sacrificing others, becoming a monster. It all felt so easy. The only reason I didn’t is…well…” Subaru brought his hand down and reached for Anastasia’s, gripping it close, “Because Ana was here.”

Geuse continued to bow, “…I am glad you did not fall from grace.”

 Like he did, was the implicit meaning behind Geuse’s words.

Subaru was having none of that, as he strode up to Geuse, Anastasia in tow. “You’re misunderstanding. I did fall. I’m not normal anymore and I probably won’t ever be.” He laid a hand on Geuse’s shoulder, patting him, “So you’re in good company, Geuse.”

Geuse shuddered, “I do not deserve such a luxury.”

Subaru sighed, scratching the back of his head, “Man, stop being an idiot and look at me.”

“I—”

“I said, look at me!” Subaru yelled.

Geuse sprung his head up and finally gazed at Subaru. Anastasia did not know what Geuse saw, but the man appeared lost and melancholic. Almost nostalgic. “Apologies. For my disgraceful behavior.”

“You’re forgiven. Not just for that apology. But for everything.”

Geuse didn’t seem to believe him, “Subaru-sama. You do not have to—”

“This isn’t pity. Or some sense of justice. Or some kind of weird hero thing in my head,” Subaru’s eyes appeared so old. “I’m just tired.”

“…”

“…I’m tired of being angry Geuse. Of feeling guilty. Of all of this,” Subaru waved his free hand everywhere, “There’s so much more to life than being stuck on the past.”

Geuse, “I do not deserve such clemency.”

“Nobody does. But everyone deserves a second chance,” Subaru clapped him on the shoulder, giving Geuse his brightest smile, “Even monsters. We may not find forgiveness, but that doesn’t mean your story should just end there.”

Geuse seemed to be on the verge of tears, “My story?”

“What’s important isn’t the beginning or the middle. But how it ends,” Anastasia could feel Subaru shaking, “How do you want your story to end, Geuse?”

And with those words, the dam broke.

Geuse fell to his knees, praying, tears streaming down his face. “Oh Flugel-sama…you haven’t forsaken me yet.”

Alarmed, Subaru tried to pick the poor soul up, “Hey—”

Anastasia grabbed his arm and pulled him back. She slowly shook her head, not saying a word. Staring back at her for a few moments, he nodded before stepping back and giving Geuse space as the spirit-turned-Witch-Factor became a mumbling mess of religious ramblings.

Crying and begging for a Sage that no longer shined in this world.

--------------------------

“…Apologies, once again,” Geuse said with puffy eyes.

“You gotta stop saying sorry man,” Subaru said.

Geuse nodded and smiled, “Then thank you. Thank you for…everything.”

“That’s better,” Subaru smiled warmly.

Anastasia poked her head into the moment, “If you really want to thank us, some information would be a lovely trade, don’t ya think?”

Geuse chuckled, “Yes, I see what you are saying. So what shall I impart upon you both?”

“Well first we need to know how to get out of here. You seemed to have a vague idea last time we chatted. Second, I have some questions about the Sage and Witch Factors. And third…” Anastasia ran her hand through her hair, “We need to know how to re-seal the Witch of Envy.”

Geuse’s demeanor became serious in the blink of an eye, “I see. And our deal?”

“Still in effect,” she felt Subaru nudge her, his eyes boring into the side of her head. Oh shit. She forgot to explain that part to him. To be fair, he was too engrossed in everything else to catch that detail. But she was definitely getting a lecture later. “But Satella can’t be let loose like she is at the current moment. I don’t think Reinhard can fight her forever,” Anastasia squinted her eyes and thought for a moment, “Probably. Anyway, doesn’t matter. We need to figure out how to put a stronger restraint on her, if possible.”

Geuse ruminated for a few seconds, “For your first request, exiting is simple. Given that this space was made by a combination of both of your Authorities. You both may simply wish for your removal, and your Ods should grant it.”

“That’s…really easy.”

Geuse nodded, “In many cases I would highly doubt it would be that straightforward. Yours is very—how you say—unique.”

Anastasia got what he implied, replying, “Because of the Sage Candidacy, right?”

“That is what you wish to know more of, I take it?” Geuse sighed, clearly not comfortable with stating such knowledge freely, “Please be aware, this type of information is highly forbidden. I would suggest not spreading it to those you do not trust.”

“Why is that?”

“Because a Sage Candidate has often been associated with the end of the world.”

That brought Anastasia and Subaru’s full attention onto Geuse, who quickly began to explain, “While it is unknown where and when the superstition had started, Sage Candidates have been known to be associated with destructive events throughout history. Our prevailing theory for this is that Sage Candidates are often persecuted due to their incredible affinity with Witch Factors, scholars often subscribed to the idea that Sages were directly related to their creation. It certainly explains why Sages have the ability to obtain multiple Factors and not suffer the consequences.”

Subaru’s eyes nearly bulged out, “Wait, what? So you’re telling me I am going to cause the end of the world?!”

Geuse held out his hand, “Not necessarily. Again, it has been associated but it isn’t exactly correct to say they cause those kinds of events. Remember that Witches have the predisposition to shatter the status quo of whatever era they are active in. Sages have a similar potential and their relationship with Witches are both deeply intimate and complicated. You could say that Sages are in actuality the minders and arbiters of such apocalypse scenarios,” Geuse thought for a moment before speaking in a more succinct tone, “Flugel-sama, the previous sage, was a great example. Because of his efforts, Sages are highly regarded in Lugunica. Even the other three nations have slowly forgotten their infamy, though remnants remain.”

Anastasia ruminated for a brief moment before asking, “So what makes Subaru a Sage candidate? Is it his soul? Or the fact that he was transported here?”

“I don’t know.”

“…That’s it?”

“Unfortunately yes,” Geuse shrugged awkwardly, “There is no direct correlation with a physical, mental, or even spiritual aspect with Sage Candidacy. The only way one could know of their own candidacy, would be to take in multiple Witch Factors and survive. Usually this would lead to a persistent stench of miasma but that is similar to all Witch Factor users. We have had multiple discussions on what makes a Sage…a Sage. But nothing has been definitively decided.”

Anastasia sighed, “Great.” She then blinked, “Wait, is it genetic?”

Geuse cocked his head, “Possibly? While we have records of some Sage bloodlines, they have been neither confirmed nor denied.”

Cool. So, there was a nonzero chance her kids were going to be targeted if anyone figured out they were possibly Sage Candidates. That’s another thing to prepare for during maternity.

Subaru spoke up, “So is Ana going to be okay? Technically, if our Od’s and souls are connected, then doesn’t that mean the Witch Factors will corrupt her?”

Geuse shook his head, “Because of that very connection, her soul shares your candidacy as well. Do not worry. I have checked. Whatever mental instability she displays would not be directly correlated with our presence.”

Anastasia stared at him, “What do you mean by that?”

Geuse ignored her and looked to Subaru, making her eye twitch, “Do you have any other questions, Subaru-sama?”

Subaru hesitated before asking, “…Why does Satella love me?”

Geuse paled and looked away, “I cannot answer that.”

“Why not?”

“It is not my place.”

“Geuse—”

“Subaru-sama,” Geuse’s expression was a mixture of guilt and fear. He seemed to be choosing his words very carefully, “It would be my privilege to tell you all that occurred 400 years ago. But there is so much even I do not know. Even worse, so much I cannot explicitly state…because of a promise. A covenant. Trying to answer your question to the best of my ability…would be a disservice to not only you. But everyone else involved in that event. Maybe one day I will be able to provide you the information you need. But not now.”

Subaru seemed frustrated but acquiesced, “Fine.”

Anastasia squeezed his hand in support. She understood why this was so important to him. To know why the person who was both his greatest ally and worst nightmare has such a great interest in him, would be anyone’s top priority. She decided to move this along, “Alright I just have one last question Geuse,” for now. If they could easily leave this space, that means they could also easily return. And she wasn’t done grilling Geuse for everything he knew, “If you can’t answer why she loves Subaru, then could you answer why doesn’t she hate me?”

It boggled her mind how Satella’s first instinct was to hug Anastasia instead of ripping her into pieces. Sure, she was relieved she didn’t have to fight the Witch but the implications were too uncomfortable.

Geuse tilted his head, “…Because she loves you too.”

Anastasia was dumbfounded, “Because of the soul link?”

“Yes and no,” at her increasing confusion, Geuse explained, “Anastasia-sama. While the Witch of Envy has always hated you, Satella hasn’t. In fact, I’d say her love for you is as high as your husband’s.”

Anastasia did not know what to think about that, “And let me guess, you can’t explain why she loves me for the same reason you can’t tell Subaru?”

Geuse just smiled, confirming her hypothesis.

She massaged her temples, “Great, fantastic actually.”

She could feel Subaru squeeze her hand, payback for earlier. At the very least they were suffering together.

“Now if all of your questions have been settled, as for your last request, that will take some time to explain,” Geuse cleared his throat, “You may want to sit down for this…”

----------------------

Subaru felt nauseous as his soul returned to controlling his body. It really was that simple as Geuse said. Just a quick thought and wish and he was back in the real world. If only the process didn’t leave him sick to his stomach. He could only hope Anastasia was fine.

“Hng…” he could barely hear her whimper which confirmed she was also suffering from some sort of soul return motion sickness. He would be more concerned if his attention wasn’t on the conversation in the background.

“What the fuck is going on with you two?” Tia exclaimed.

“Oh Od…what have I done?” Julius moaned in dismay. It wasn’t just him either, Beatrice was wailing in the background, uncontrollably.

Subaru tried to squeeze his eyes open, but they felt heavy, as if he had been asleep for years. Try as he might, he could just barely lift himself up and glance around. Zarestia and Halibel were standing awkwardly as Julius was on his knees, face down towards the ground, dry heaving. Next to him, Beatrice was curled up into a ball, sobbing. Looking closely at the bodies nearby, the rest seemed okay. Unconscious but the faint lift and fall of their chests suggested they were alive. That was one worry they did not have to deal with.

Subaru moved his hand towards Anastasia and shook her awake, “No…stop…” she muttered.

Unfortunately, this wasn’t the time. Subaru used all of his energy to help the poor girl sit up, cleaning up her messy hair that had gotten frazzled during the semi-coma. His poor wife looked like she was on the verge of vomiting. He rubbed circles on her back and looked back at the commotion. Only to catch the eye of Halibel.

Halibel then looked back at Julius and Beatrice, before doing a triple take at the two stars. The pipe in his mouth dropped on the floor as his mouth gaped open. Zarestia glanced over and said, “The hell is up with you?”

“They’re awake,” Halibel blurted out, causing Zarestia’s head to whip over to their direction.

Within two seconds, she smacked both Julius and Beatrice out of their mental breakdown, pulling them by their hairs to look straight at Subaru and Anastasia. They both blinked several times. Before scrambling to their feet.

For a moment, the group just stared at the two stars, who were groggy and ready to pass out again. However, Subaru had enough mental capacity to say two words, all the while smiling.

“…We’re back.”

Chapter 61: Heaven Welcomes All, Old and New

Summary:

They're back...

Chapter Text

“…We’re back,” Subaru said with a smile that Julius could not comprehend. It wasn’t uneasy or with the sense of some hidden melancholy.

He looked genuinely happy to see them. Not just his other companions. Subaru looked straight at Julius and smiled. A sincere smile. Not one mixed with contempt, nor a drop of hatred. How in the world could someone still be so pure after the Hell they experienced?

It did not take long for Julius to connect the dots once his memories of Subaru flooded back into his brain. And with that flood, brought a cataclysm of guilt. The guilt that he had felt for abandoning his candidate in her hour of need was still present. But a part of him understood that he could have done nothing at that moment. Gluttony, Anastasia’s own decision to leave, and his own incapability in providing her assistance: all culminated in his acceptance of helplessness. Even if Julius were to rationalize every possible decision that could have led to a better outcome, what’s done was done. His heart was soothed by the fact that Anastasia had not succumbed to a worse fate.

This, however, was different.

Subaru was tortured. For months.

All under Julius’s watch.

Sure, he was not aware of such insidious dealings and actions performed by his dear friend Felix during that time period. But what kind of excuse was that? He was one of the most trusted knights of the whole Royal battalion. He should have known. He should have checked in on his friend. He should have made sure the prisoners were being interrogated properly. But he didn’t. And because of his sloth, Subaru had been thoroughly ravaged and beaten to an inch of his life for multiple weeks. He could only guess that no matter what Subaru said, they didn’t believe a word that he was innocent.

Even when he was screaming for his life.

The thought made Julius nauseous. Like he wanted to tear out his own throat, heart, and lungs. He should have stabbed himself right then and there for his own ignorance. Because his lack of action resulted in not only an innocent man—and a dear friend that he respected greatly—to be treated inhumanely, but it also led to said friend becoming broken from the trauma. He remembered the knights’ testimonies and some of the reports. Subaru had become eerily quiet and despondent during part of his tenure. And no wonder. To be rewarded with disgust, betrayal, and hopelessness for all he has done for the kingdom. Subaru had been responsible for bringing back hope for all the downtrodden and lost in Priestella. He had defeated great beasts that had antagonized Lugunica for decades. He threw himself directly into harms way­—all for the sake of his candidate—time and time again and again. Julius had bore witness to nearly every single time. And every time, he had been enthralled.

Julius could not help but admire such a man.

And yet, Julius had failed him. In his time of need, Julius had done nothing. Everyone, had done nothing.

Even with the excuse of Gluttony’s magical ignorance, there was nothing to excuse cold-blooded torture. The ramifications of this event will shake the very foundation of the kingdom. They spread Subaru’s name and description all across the kingdom—along with the qualifier that he was an Archbishop. The people will have questions. And the people will not like the answers.

But Julius did not focus on that. Despite his loyalty, he could give less than a single shit about any of that at this current moment.

All he cared about, was that the boy in front of him had grown into a completely different man. It had only been half a year since he last saw him. But it felt like decades had passed. His face looked older. His hair longer with bits of white and grey. Much more wise, less innocent, the passion that was once lit in his eyes was gone. Replaced with an almost sullen acceptance. As if he no longer dreamed of greater ambitions, only the here and now. It was reminiscent of many of the veterans of the Royal Knights. Men who had lost so much and fought so many, that all they could see was a battlefield. The only dream they now sought was the comfort of their home, where the clashing of blades and the screams of comrades, was a distant nightmare.

And yet, Subaru smiled at him.

How? How could he have faced so much and remain unphased? Julius’s eyes glanced to his candidate who looked viscerally ill.
