Her expression made him want to march right over and help her in any way he could. But Julius froze when he finally connected the last thoughts in his mind. The dots that felt so alien to him, that the very notion was something out of a fictional fantasy.

Subaru’s hand was placed gently on Anastasia’s back, rubbing circles and helping her acclimate to the sudden nausea. Subaru’s eyes, which were previously empty, looked upon Anastasia with a fire that burned far greater than Julius had ever seen before. Even greater than that fateful day at the beginning of the Royal Selection. And Anastasia, trying her best to not succumb to the disgust, looked at Subaru with not only gratitude, but an equal amount of passion. Actually, no. Julius didn’t know if the fire that burned in Anastasia’s eyes was even more than Subaru’s. A part of him felt like with each second, they stared into each other’s eyes, the fires within shined brighter than before. As if they fed off each other constantly into a glorious, all-consuming inferno.

And with those thoughts in mind, the two dots in his mind connected.

Oh, how romantic.

“Indeed! Dare I say that the only reason either are not mentally in the abyss, is because of each other. Love is the greatest lifeline, after all.”

Julius ignored Fourier’s voice and instead tried to plan his next course of action. His eyes glanced over to Beatrice who still looked on the verge of a panic attack. Quite reasonable given the situation. If Julius had reacted as poorly as this, Beatrice must have experienced far worse. He could only imagine how his buds would feel if he had ever disappeared.

Just as he was about to—

“Stop being a bunch of pussies and get the fuck over there!” Zarestia yelled as she lifted them both up with wind magic and tossed them straight at Subaru and Anastasia, “DIE!”

Unfortunately, Zarestia’s aim was slightly off the mark. Julius barreled right into Subaru’s chest, while Beatrice slammed her skull into Anastasia’s, sending Anastasia back onto the ground.

“…Did ya really have ta yell ‘die?’” Halibel asked.

Zarestia spat on the ground, “They were being a bunch of weenies. I was sick of watching them just stand there.”

“Aren’t ya just tryin’ ta blow off steam cuz ya didn’t get ta kill anyone?”

“No.”

“Ya said that way too quickly.”

“Shut up or I’ll kill you.”

Halibel sighed as he walked over, “Ana-bo, Su-san, ya good?”

Subaru groaned along with Julius. Evidently, Anastasia and Beatrice were both knocked out. Again.

-----------------------

“What the fuck is wrong with you?” Anastasia yelled at Zarestia. “We could have died!”

Zarestia picked her ear, “Yeah. But you didn’t.”

Anastasia wrung her hands at Zarestia’s neck as Halibel clapped her back, making Anastasia stumble forward slightly. “When were ya goin’ to tell me that we met before?”

Anastasia blushed slightly as she mumbled, “There wasn’t really a time to mention it.”

“It really hit me how much ya grew. Back then ya were just some shorty who stood her ground for the people she cared bout,” Halibel chuckled, filled with warmth. “Seems not much has changed. Either in height or kindness.”

Anastasia huffed, “You’re lucky I’m in a good mood or I would have kicked ya for that height comment.”

Halibel laughed, making her leg tingle with the increasing need to kick him in the balls. Unfortunately, there were bigger things to worry about, “So what happened while we were out?”

“Good news or bad news?” Halibel asked.

“Bad news first.”

“Well the other two Gluttonies escaped.”

Anastasia sighed, “Well that sucks, anything else?”

Halibel stared at her, “…You’re not…mad?”

“Why would I be mad? We’re just going to hunt them down and kill them later anyway,” Anastasia shrugged. Honestly it might even better this way. She now had to opportunity to butcher them personally.

Halibel continued to stare at her as Zarestia smiled, “Well look at you, you’re finally acting like ya always should have been. I should send you into a coma more often.”

Anastasia glared at Zarestia before sighing, “I can’t even argue against you. Today’s been both the worst and best day of my life so far.”

On the one hand, absolute nightmare fuel. On the other hand, Anastasia has never felt more refreshed than before. It’s as if all the restraints on her mind—especially the ones she was unaware of—were gone. It was like she was born anew.

“Well, besides the multitude of questions and concerns I now have,” Halibel said, “I’m glad yer takin’ this better than I thought.”

“So what’s the good news?” Anastasia asked.

“Wait one second. We still have bad news,” Halibel scratched his chin. “Ya might want to sit down for this…the Witch of Envy is right below us and the only thin’ not stoppin’ her from murdering us all is the Sword Saint.”

Anastasia didn’t skip a beat, “Yeah, we’ll have to work quick on that. I don’t know how long Reinhard can keep her at bay, but I don’t want to test it.”

Halibel stared at her with increasing concern, “…Ya sure, yer okay?”

Anastasia ignored him, “Alright, now the good news?”

“Well—”

Zarestia interrupted him, “The good news is that your lame camp is all fine. We checked. Also I cut off one of those Archbishop fuckers legs and one of them lost both arms before they could escape. There, it’s done, now can we get to the more important shit,” Halibel face palmed as Zarestia pointed at Anastasia, “What the fuck was that shadow stuff that entered both you and Su’s bodies?”

Anastasia blinked, “Oh. That.”

“How are ya so nonchalant bout all of this?!” Halibel cried out, his patience thoroughly tested and his mind bewildered, “I get ya must be in some form of shock, but it feels like ya already knew most of this.”

Anastasia looked to the side, “…Well.”

 

While Anastasia explained everything to Halibel and Zarestia, Subaru was having his own conversations a few meters away. Sitting down and resting an unconscious Beatrice on his lap, he wrapped Eridna around his neck and felt that pleasant cool breeze in his mind.

“Su. What did you and Ana do to your bodies?” Subaru shuddered as he felt Eridna’s imposing voice rattle his skull.

Subaru scratched his chin and thought, Ah. You noticed.

“Answer me, Su. Now,” sometimes Subaru forgot how motherly Eridna was. It was a nice contrast compared to the original Echidna. Though perhaps he was wrong, that specific Echidna he met was different from the original. From how Beatrice described her, her mother was a lot more kind when she was alive despite her propensity to inflict untold horrors on people just for the sake of an experiment or to sate her curiosity.

Well, after we got knocked unconscious, both Ana and I got locked in each other’s Ods and we saw each other’s memories. Then it turned out that the Witch Factors were all alive. Then Louis, who was in Ana, tried to take over her whole body and everything. Pandora, the Witch of Vainglory, tried to trick Ana into becoming an Archbishop. Ana told them both no. Then she took over Gluttony and killed Louis, I think. After that, Ana decided to fuse our souls together.

“…What?” Eridna sounded very confused. And for good reason.

“Ya fused yer souls together?!” Halibel yelled in the background. That was the loudest he had ever heard Halibel scream. And Subaru fed him 900,000 scoville hot sauce once. They were out of milk for days.

I can explain it all later in greater detail if you want.

“Yes, that would be good,” Subaru imagined Eridna pinching her nose bridge with an imaginary hand, “In any case, I am glad you are both okay but it was a little shocking to see that your Ods have almost become one.”

You can see that?

“I can see a lot from within. Despite how impossible it sounds, it’s as if a section of your Od melded with hers. It propagates out into a space before disappearing into an iridescent thread that connects to Ana’s body. The fact that it is not visible to normal people is also interesting. Not only that, but your gate is also different. It’s no longer broken, but also incomplete. As if part of it is missing, even though I can see it functioning like a perfecting normal gate. However, I can sense Ana’s gate within yours. Adding onto that, I do not know if the affinity is Yin or Yang anymore. Your Od, your soul, your gates. They are all so strange. Foreign yet familiar. My first reaction was that someone else was occupying your bodies but given how you are reacting to my possession…”

It’s all very weird, isn’t it?

Eridna sighed within his mind, “Not the most optimal way to describe it and yet any other would not fit. I am still processing the return of my memories. I can barely look in Ana’s direction.”

She doesn’t blame you. Subaru tried to soothe Eridna’s worries.

“That I do not doubt. But it is quite difficult for my guilt to coexist with logic. The emptiness I once felt is now filled with regret. A tad better and yet a wholistically different type of pain. I once feared of a past that never existed. Now…I can only accept that it does. And all the horrors that come with it. Sister is most likely experiencing something similar, though on a significantly worse scale.”

Yeah, I can tell. It’s probably why Beako is pretending to still be asleep.

“You noticed?”

You tend to notice people’s sleeping patterns when you sleep in the same bed. I teased her once that she snored super loud at night. Now whenever we take naps and she doesn’t want to actually sleep, she’ll pretend by doing this cute little snoring. It’s kind of funny actually.

“Well that explains quite a bit. I simply accepted that she found it amusing to do so.”

Nah, she just doesn’t like me thinking she has better things to do. Beako is cute like that.

“Do you also find ignoring Julius, cute?” Eridna’s words made Subaru glance at Julius who was sitting on his knees next to Subaru. Evidently trying to not make eye contact but also looking like he was on the verge of shitting himself.

Subaru was really hoping it was just the stress getting to him and making him look antsy. Otherwise, he is booking it as far away as possible.

…I honestly thought if I ignored him long enough, he would go talk to Ana finally.

“I think he is prioritizing you at the moment.”

Haha, nice joke.

“…”

That was a joke right?

“It was not.”

There’s no way! His candidate is literally right there!

“The same candidate who did not return to their camp after getting forgotten. Julius most likely has questions beyond questions, but he is waiting until Ana approaches him. He probably does not think he is worthy of her or that Ana herself has a problem with him and the camp.”

Subaru looked towards Anastasia who was currently double checking her unconscious camp members bodies. As much as Anastasia tried to put the thoughts away, he knew she was deathly worried about the Triplets and Ricardo. It was obvious to anyone with a brain that Anastasia loved them to death.

Though Subaru did not consider Julius to have the greatest brain capacity.

Well I’m not talking to him.

Somehow, the vision of Eridna giving him a frown was etched into his mind. “Are you really going to let the poor boy stew?”

Yes.

“Subaru.”

…It’s not like I’m the best person to talk to him.

“What is the real reason you are so obstinate against the boy?”

…

“If you don’t answer, I will immediately wake sister up and you can deal with that instead.”

Wait, wait, wait! Okay, fine! The reason I don’t want to talk to him…

“…Is?”

…Because I think it would be really awkward.

“Subaru—”

Like REALLY awkward. Like, he’ll probably start asking me shit like ‘oh how did you and Lady Anastasia meet?’ Or ‘were you already in a turbid love affair way before being forgotten?’ Or ‘what about Lady Emilia? Have you forsaken your knightly vow and descended into debauchery? With my Lady of all people?!’

“Subaru. For how accurate your inner voice of Julius is, you really do not understand him.”

I understand him perfectly fine. If I was him, I would have questions upon questions and a very itchy fist for the man who deflowered his Lady.

“Crude but I doubt Julius cares about that specifically at the moment. You do realize he probably feels regret for you.”

For what?

“…Are you serious?”

Yes, wait, what?

“Okay. I see where this is going. You have three seconds before I wake up sister. Talk to him.”

Wait—

“One.”

ERIDNA.

“Two.”

Fuck. “Julius!” Subaru blurted out.

Subaru heard Julius scramble beside him, most likely not expecting Subaru to yell his name. “Uh… Subaru?”

Cool, cool. What the fuck do you say now?! Subaru thought quickly, “So, why are you here?”

Shit. Balls. What kind of question is that?

“I, uh…” Julius went quiet for a second, “I do not know.”

Goddamn it Julius.

“You don’t know why you’re here?”

“That is…well…you see…I,” Julius stumbled over his words. It felt out of place in Subaru’s mind. He was expecting Julius to say something with a bit more class or perhaps berate Subaru or throw a witty remark. For some reason, hearing Julius not know what to say sobered his own mind. Perhaps they were both awkwardly trying to figure out what their dynamic was now.

Subaru sighed, “Why aren’t you going to talk to your candidate?”

“…I…do not feel…it is my right to be there by her side,” Julius admitted.

Subaru cringed at the confession, “Horseshit. Go talk to her. She missed you.”

“…She did?”

“Of course! She would always talk about how much she missed you guys! All the time. Hell, sometimes she would cry in her sleep and say your guys’ names,” Subaru winced at his own words. Too much information! “Well, I mean when we took naps together. By that I mean we were sleeping on a couch or bed but like fully clothed!” Fuck, fuck, fuck! “Like, nothing weird happened! At all! Like, yes we may have done the deed, but you know it’s just—”

“Subaru. Please stop talking,” Subaru took a glance at Julius and saw his hands covering his face.

Subaru was about to cringe out of existence, but he had to add on this last part, “She really didn’t hate you guys. She left because she was scared. Not because of you.”

“…” Julius let his hands fall, “So she did not trust us to be a part of her lives.”

Subaru’s eye twitched, “No. She didn’t trust herself. She thought about how you guys would treat her and the thought that it would not be the same, broke her heart.”

“How is that not our fault?”

This annoying piece of shit. Subaru glared at Julius, “Because it isn’t! How the fuck would it be your fault when she was the one who ran away first?”

“It’s just—”

“Stop being so wishy washy and tell me what’s actually up with you!”

“I’m trying to—”

“Your candidate is right there. After being gone for months. Grow a pair and talk to her. I don’t understand what’s keeping you so—"

“I don’t know!” Julius yelled out, glaring back at Subaru, “You are acting like I have an answer but I do not! I don’t know why I am so fearful, I do not know why my feet won’t do as I say, and I especially do not understand what these emotions are! I don’t understand where everything went wrong! I do not know why I feel this way, but I do! I cannot help the fact that I, a knight that was sworn to protect his Lady at all costs, failed and feel terrible! I do not know why it is my fault, but it is certainly better than blaming her!”

Julius was panting, out of breath. His eyes then widened as he looked away with regret. His voice wavered, “Apologies. I did not mean to say that. That was not what I wanted our first interaction to be—”

Subaru punched him in the face. Sending the knight onto his back and onto the floor. In the last few seconds after Julius’s outburst. Subaru carefully put Beatrice down on the floor with Eridna on top of her. Stood up. Stretched his muscles, cracked his neck and then his fists.

Before sucker punching Julius in the face. He then waved his hand in the air, “Otto was right. Violence does solve everything.”

Julius, stunned, stared at Subaru, “Why did you do that?”

“Because you were being a self-pitying idiot and since you really want to be punished so badly, I’ll just punch you in the face until you realize you’re stupid.”

“But—”

“Listen. I don’t give a shit about how much you regret, bout me or Ana. I don’t care if you think you don’t deserve anything or that you could have done better. And I don’t care if you don’t understand how you feel. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again. I’m sick of constantly thinking that I don’t deserve to exist! I’m sick of being in a constant state of self-hatred when the people around me deserve better than that. And I’m sick of constantly seeing people I know doing the same bullshit as me. It’s tiring. It’s stupid. And we all need to finally grow up. So you can either keep being a wuss and avoid happiness or you can be the cool knight that I know that you still are, and actually face your regrets head on.”

“…You think I’m cool?” Julius asked, baffled.

Subaru narrowed his eyes, “I’m going to punch you again.”

Just as Julius braced himself for another smack, he felt a light tap on his head. A hand outstretched in front of him. Subaru muttered, “You’re lucky Ana cares about you so much.”

Julius looked at the hand and then Subaru’s eyes before giving a soft smile. The guilt in Julius’s eyes were still present but at the very least, they didn’t seem as all-consuming as they were before. Julius took Subaru’s hand, expecting to be pulled up…

Only for Subaru to not have the strength to do so. “Oh shit!” Subaru screeched.

In fact, Julius was so heavy that Subaru toppled forward on top of him.

“Well…at least that has not changed about you,” Julius deadpanned.

“I will fucking fight you, don’t tempt me Juukuulius!”

Julius smiled, “Should we have another duel?”

“Haha, you little—”

“My dear husband-to-be, could you please get off my knight before I believe you will take his purity?” Anastasia asked as she stood over them.

Subaru and Julius blushed, they both scrambled off each other.

“With him? Never in a thousand years!” “I would never try to take him from you Lady Anastasia!”

Subaru did a double take at Julius’s words before deciding it wasn’t worth processing, deleting it from his memory.

Anastasia giggled, “So, it seems you have become reacquainted with each other.”

Subaru and Julius gave each other the side-eye. Subaru sighed, “Yeah. Besides him being an idiot.” He then nudged Julius forward to Anastasia.

Julius stumbled slightly before sputtering, “M-my Lady I…how…”

Anastasia didn’t seem to mind. She simply looked at him and smiled, “…It’s good to see you again, Julius.”

Julius blinked and gave a small smile back, “Likewise. I am…sorry. About everything. I do not know how I can hope to ever—”

“Do you still want to be my knight?” Anastasia cocked her head. It seemed she wanted to get to the root of the matter without any more nonsense.

“Of course!” Julius blurted out. His cheeks blushed in embarrassment, “If…you would have me.”

Anastasia giggled, “Remember what I told you Julius, I won’t be satisfied until everything in the world is mine. You’re still included in that.”

And at those words, Julius’s face scrunched, filled with emotion. He bowed deeply and took Anastasia’s hand, “I will always be at your command.”

Subaru sighed as he sat down once more. Happy to see that they avoided some of the initial pitfalls already. While it annoyed him that he had to be the one to push Julius forward, it was a nice start. Baby steps. Obviously, none of this would be solved in a conversation or a day.

Subaru felt someone tug on his robe. Looking to the source, he gave a soft smile towards Beatrice. The poor girl’s eyes were puffy and pink. He picked her up without another word and gave her a big hug.

“…Betty is sorry.”

“I know. It’s okay,” Subaru cooed. He could hear her sniffle and sob. Subaru knew this was going to happen. And he knew that Beatrice would likely never forgive herself anytime soon. But that is fine. Just like how Julius was still dealing with his own demons, they all needed time to heal.

But neither Anastasia nor Subaru will let them run away. They were both tired of running.
“Now then, what was that about a duel?” That chilling tone of Anastasia’s voice sent shivers down Subaru and Julius’s spine. Anastasia was smiling but it did not feel real. “Thanks for reminding me by the way. I have something you both need to finally address.”

Subaru and Julius gulped.

----------------------

“—and that’s why I challenged you to a duel.”

Subaru stared at Julius. “You…admired what I said…and inspired by that…beat me to near death?”

Julius looked like he wanted to die right then and there, “At the time, it felt like the right decision.”

“Who the fuck thinks beating the shit out of a servant is a great way to express their love and affection?”

 

Somewhere in a war-torn part of Vollachia, Priscilla sneezed again. Covered in blood and tired, she was in need of some stress relief. Unfortunately, Al was currently occupied with something important and was nowhere near her. Despite this, she planned on hitting him when she saw him again. She just had a feeling he deserved it.

 

“My thoughts exactly,” Anastasia sighed as she pinched her nose bridge, “You should have seen my reaction when he explained everything to me the night after. I thought he had a whole plan or that he was doing this to put a rival camp at a disadvantage. But nooooo. He gave me the bullshit reason of ‘trying to prevent a courageous boy from being killed.’”

Julius visibly cringed, “Again, I believed I was doing you a favor. My intention was to set the stage for you to prove your worth. I assumed you had the combat skills to back your statements.”

“How in the world would you—” Subaru then thought for a moment, “Actually. Scratch that. From what Felt said, her little maids could easily beat me to death with their bare hands. Physical appearances mean nothing here. Okay, I can kind of see where you were going with this.”

Julius smiled, “Thank you for understanding.”

Anastasia face palmed, “No! He did not have a point! He was just rolling with the punches! There was nothing logical about this!”

Subaru shrugged, “I don’t know Ana, I’m kind of warming up to the fact that Julius should have beat me to death harder.”

Julius frowned, “Well I don’t think—”

Anastasia pinched Subaru’s ear, “You little shit, stop trying to make your bullshit dick measuring contest cooler than it actually is!”

“It’s not a dick measuring contest! Besides, I’ve only done that once, to be fair.”

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “With the clown?”

Subaru pointed at her, “We don’t speak about that.”

“How do you think I felt seeing it? I saw where your eyes were looking.”

“I said we don’t speak about it! Besides, there was nowhere else to look!”

“Literally anywhere else was an option!”

Julius watched in abject curiosity and confusion as he wasn’t used to this new dynamic between his candidate and his fellow knight. Halibel chuckled next to him, lighting a new kiseru, “Coin for yer thoughts?”

“…I have never seen Anastasia-sama be this lively before.”

“He has that affect on her,” Halibel said. “I’d say he brings the best and worst out of her.”

“I…see…” Julius could not help but feel like he was seeing his candidate in a new way. He had seen her argue and react with pettiness before. But not to this scale nor with this amount of enthusiasm. She looked so free. Adding onto that, she wasn’t even using her accent anymore. It felt disorienting to see. And yet also…refreshing.

Zarestia yawned. She was crouched beside Otto’s unconscious body and was using her wind to flap his mouth and nose, making very unflattering expressions out of his face. “Alright. I’m getting bored. Are we doing anything else or can we finally destroy this whole tower?”

Anastasia stopped poking an embarrassed Subaru’s cheek and focused on the group, “Not yet. We still have to deal with the Witch of Envy and there is only one way to do that.”

Anastasia sighed.

“We’re going to need to find Flugel’s diary.”

 

Chapter 62: Heaven Waits For No One

Summary:

They're off to see the Sage ('s diary)! The wonderful Sage of Lugunica!

Chapter Text

“Apologies Anastasia-sama…I should have had a tighter grip on that blasted book,” Julius muttered somberly.

Anastasia rolled her hand in the air, “What’s done is done. No need to fret.”

Anastasia meant to say that as cheerfully as possible, an opener for greater conversation. But it had the opposite effect given how Julius looked even more despondent at her side. She sighed internally as she felt that warm presence sink into her soul once more.

“The boy wishes to apologize to you in more ways than one.”

Obviously, Anastasia mumbled in her mind. I know Julius well enough that he is probably kicking himself for what happened. It’s stupid but it’s not something I didn’t expect.

Anastasia absentmindedly grabbed at a hand that wasn’t next to her anymore, trying not to frown. It made sense why their current formation was like this, but it still annoyed her extensively. Halibel at the front as their vanguard, Julius and Anastasia in the middle to provide support, and Subaru and Beatrice in the back. It allowed them to easily deal with any more surprises. Zarestia was—to the Spirit’s great annoyance— absent and was guarding their unconscious friends in the Pleiades Watchtower’s Green Room.

Anastasia knew that Zarestia was very uncomfortable with leaving them to just Halibel as their guard, a fact that she explicitly said very loudly much to Julius’s dismay. But they needed a strike force to find Flugel’s diary as quickly as possible. The fact that the diary had a spell that made it teleport back to Flugel’s room made it easier to locate. Unfortunately, getting to that room was another issue entirely. Given how the tower turned into a spatial maze where left, right, up, and down no longer were consistent with reality—they were in for a headache.

Echidna. You don’t have to hold back.

“…What do you mean?”

Anastasia turned her head to look back and saw that Subaru and Beatrice were in their own little discussion. Now that their names had returned, there was a lot of baggage they needed to get rid of. That meant addressing the problems their companions had and making sure they weren’t blaming themselves for nonsense.

We’ve known each other long enough that I can tell you’re upset. So spill.

“I…” Eridna seemed to squirm on her shoulders.

I don’t blame you either.

“That is not it. Well, not exactly.”

Anastasia laughed in her mind. I’m fine. You’re fine. We all ended up fine. How could you know that I existed if we got separated? It’s nonsensical to blame yourself.

“Logic and emotion rarely compromise. And as much as I want to say, ‘It is good to see you and I am happy I finally remember you fully.’ I can’t say the latter.”

Why not? We’ve spent the last few months together again. You didn’t leave me for that long.

“That’s not the point…even if it was not directly my fault, or if our time separated was short. To cast you aside to face all your misery alone; it does not sit right in my mind and it may never will.”

Anastasia was stunned by such a proclamation. Not because it was unexpected but because she had a memory shoot through her skull. Of watching a white-haired woman with a similar voice and personality who would very much express the opposite. Anastasia could not help but wonder what the purpose of Eridna’s creation was. The original Echidna must have had a reason for crafting a copy of her personality and placing it within a spirit. But what was stranger was the addition of emotions.

It didn’t take Anastasia that long to clock that the original Echidna was an absolute sociopath. Her emotions were either dampened or were never there in the first place. Every move, every smile, every word was calculated. As if she was making the perfect preconceived moves to complete her goals. Subaru’s memories of her, even in Anastasia’s own manic state, stood out. Something about that Witch made Anastasia feel rancid and oddly…familiar. She couldn’t tell why but it felt similar to how she felt about Satella. And both were not cans of worms she wanted to deal with at the moment.

But returning to Eridna. While the reasons for her existence escaped Anastasia’s mind, that did not change the fact that the Spirit did the one thing the original could never do.

“I think it’s fine to regret. It’s what makes us human. But letting that prevent us from having happiness. That’s a worse mistake than having none,” Anastasia said aloud. Julius glanced at her, alarmed. Eridna was now quiet in her mind.

Anastasia did not know how to fix her companions’ misery. But she wasn’t going to let them stew. Life was too short. Even if her Od had strengthened, her gate fixed, that did not mean you should waste the precious time you still had. Nothing lasts forever.

“My Lady?” Julius asked with concern etched in his eyes and face.

“What have you been up to while I’ve been gone?”

“I…” Julius caught his breath, not expecting such a question, “I have been performing my duties as optimally as possible. Due to your…absence…I became a liaison between the camps in order to strengthen our united front against the Witch Cult. In addition, Hoshin Company became part of our domain and was for some reason gifted to us by Chuuden. Or at least, that is what the official documents and my memory explained. I tasked my brother with managing the internal affair of the company in my absence.”

Anastasia tapped her chin. That aligned with what she already knew. Gluttony did not seem to be the most eloquent rewriter of history. It really did only seem to try to connect the dots as logically and quickly as possible and made sure everyone who was involved had a similar recalling of the deleted history. The added bonus of the ‘filter’—or Gluttony’s Mist, as Subaru cutely wanted to call it— made it difficult for anyone to look into that too deeply. “Oh, speaking of Joshua. We found him in Banan and brought him with us. He’s gotten a bit taller since I last saw him.”

Julius choked, making Anastasia giggle, “You did what now?

“Don’t worry. From what I can tell, Subaru brought him as far as the Mather’s Mansion before sending him back to the Juukuulius domain.”

“I see…but why bring him in the first place?” Julius asked.

“Preparations. Subaru wanted him to warn the council of what was happening at the tower in case we failed. I, on the other hand, gave him some helpful information that should give us breathing space once we return to the capital.”

Even while she was steeped in self-hatred, she prided herself on long-term planning. Joshua should have remembered both her and Subaru now and so her last message to him should make a lot more sense. If Joshua completed his tasks, negotiations with the Sage Council should run smoothly in the near future. She always had a soft spot for that kid. She’ll make sure he gets rewarded for not only helping them indirectly but also running her company while she was gone.

“You are returning to the capital?” Julius asked with incredible confusion.

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “Yes? That is our first objective once this is all finished.”

“I see…and what will you do afterward?”

Anastasia was about to tell him that she was going to bleed the council dry for everything they had. Which was both a joke and not a joke. But then she realized the greater implications of what he was asking. “We’re not going back to Karaagi.”

“Oh.”

“Not yet anyways,” Anastasia added. Going back to Banan was good for her and she really did miss her homeland. However, she wasn’t going to return until all of her business in Lugunica was done. And that may take a while depending on the Royal Selection, the Witch Cult, and when she wanted kids. A lot of things to consider nowadays. “Besides, I was thinking a wedding in Lugunica would not be bad. And I wouldn’t like one of the groomsmen to have to travel so far for my special day.”

Julius nearly stumbled, making Anastasia chuckle, “I-I see.” His eyes then bulged out as he processed what she said. Pointing at himself in alarm, “Me? A groomsman for Subaru?”

Anastasia snorted, “Who else would you be? Unless you want to be a bridesmaid—”

“If that is you wish, I am at your call.”

“—but it is not an order,” she quickly added. While Julius in a dress was funny to her, she had a vague feeling she didn’t want Subaru to see him cross-dressing. “But I want you to be there with everyone else. No matter what happens. I don’t want you to ever think you aren’t allowed to be there.”

Julius looked away from her, “…I would be happy to do so.”

Baby steps.

-----------------------

Subaru rocked Beatrice back and forth in his arms as he awkwardly watched Anastasia and Julius not talk to each other for minutes. From what he could tell, she was most likely having her own discussion with Eridna while Julius was probably going through two of the five stages of grief on loop. Mainly directed towards himself.

“Betty is sorry, in fact…” Subaru patted Beatrice’s back.

“None of that. I already forgave you,” Subaru whispered.

“How could you forgive me so easily?” Beatrice sobbed.

How? How could Subaru forgive Beatrice for making a mistake that anyone would have done in her situation? To Subaru it seemed only right to forgive someone who was not in the right headspace, lacking key information, and who would have reacted like anyone else. He had forgiven people for worse, and for situations that never happened in the first place. To him, something like this was natural.

But that wouldn’t be right to say. He couldn’t say something like that because even if the taboo was not relevant, she wouldn’t understand. She would not understand what Subaru meant because to do so would be to explain all the myriad of emotions he had felt in his time in Lugunica. All the pain and suffering and grief. And the loss. All of it. All so he could tell her that none of it mattered.

None of it mattered because the happiness he felt in the present, having the people he loved around him, mattered more than any previous sting of betrayal. When all you felt was pain for so long, the nuances no longer mattered.

All that mattered was the people who were still here.

Still, Subaru had to say something. And what felt right, was a story, “…There was only one time that I saw my dad cry. And it was when I made a big mistake as a kid.”

Beatrice stopped sniffling and began to pay attention.

Subaru continued, “I was looking through my dad’s old stuff and found some of his cigarettes. He stopped smoking when I was born but he must have kept them as some sort of souvenir or something. And me being me, I was curious. Because I remembered seeing pictures of him smoking all the time and I thought it looked super cool. So I took one of them out and went over to find a lighter but couldn’t find one that worked. So I went to the kitchen and lit it on the gas stove and I was so excited to try it that I didn’t remember to turn the gas off. So right as I took a breath, I dropped the damn thing on the floor, coughing and dry heaving and all that. And well...our house was a bit messy at the time and there was a bunch of papers and stuff everywhere. So, the second I dropped it, everything started to light on fire. And panicking, I accidentally hit stuff onto the stove, and that stuff caught on fire as well. Honestly, everything was on fire.”

“…”

“You should have seen my dad’s face when he woke up to the fire alarm and me coughing my lungs out. He was able to easily put it all out with some water and some carpets but man was he pissed at me. He saw the cigarettes and put two and two together and yelled so loud that I thought my ear drums popped. That was the first and only time he hit me. He got so mad, telling me that what I was doing would ruin my life, all the while he smacked me upside the head.”

“How terrible, I suppose,” Beatrice muttered.

Subaru chuckled at that, “It wasn’t that bad. Just a love tap all things considered. And I didn’t blame him for it, but I felt super guilty because I thought I made such a huge mistake. I blamed myself all day and cried like a little baby.” Subaru’s voice slowly became somber, “…Later that night, I remember waking up to my dad sitting outside. He was out on the porch, and I could hear him crying to himself. And I thought, ‘oh, it’s all my fault.’ But then…well…”

It was hard for Subaru to explain, like all memories of home, the more he talked, the more his melancholy built. He could feel Beatrice cling to his chest tighter. Subaru continued despite the lump in his throat growing. “I heard…I heard him say, ‘I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.’ And for a time I thought it was because of me. That, he had such a useless and idiotic son who makes dumb decisions, that he was apologizing to God or my Mom.”

He could feel Beatrice shaking and his own voice was wavering, but he kept going, “But turned out, he was apologizing to me. The day after, I woke up to him hugging me and not saying anything about last night. And then like nothing ever happened, he was back to his cheerful self. I didn’t know it back then, but I think he was crying because of what he did to me. Maybe. I don’t know, it’s kind of a far-reaching theory in my mind but I can’t help but think of how…little I know about him. I don’t much about my Dad. I don’t know what my Dad did all those years before I was his son. I don’t know that much about my grandparents, and I definitely don’t know what type of stuff haunted him at night. I know why he reacted so poorly, any parent would. But the fear he had that night…I wonder what made him cry so much. I wonder…if it’s anything like how you felt.”

“…Betty does not know. But Betty does know that I am nothing like your father. He hurt you out of love. Betty abandoned you out of fear, in fact.”

“That isn’t quite true,” Subaru said. “You did leave me. But you didn’t remember me. You can’t just act like you didn’t have a reason. And even so, you came back. You tried to fix your mistakes.”

“That’s no excuse. Betty did not even try until it was nearly too late.”

“But you still did! That’s more than enough, even if you don’t think so.” Subaru patted Beatrice’s head, “Beako, you can’t just think you’re at fault for all of this. Remember what I said Beako, we can’t just keep hating ourselves—”

“That isn’t fair!” Beatrice cried out. Subaru looked ahead and saw Julius and Halibel look back with concern. Anastasia did not, she continued striding forward. Subaru gave them both a reassuring nod before refocusing on Beatrice who yelled, “How can you just act like this okay?! How can you act like this is all fine?! You were tortured! Betty left you there, for months! How could you just accept me back so easily? How could you just act so normal?”

“But I didn’t. I didn’t exactly forgive you immediately and I did wait and well…” How could he ever explain that in the countless loops that he spent saving his wife, that Beatrice was there every step. Her boundless loyalty. Her willingness to dive into Hell with him without even a single doubt. Her genuine faith in him as they spent countless times discussing ways to save Anastasia’s life. Any leftover resentment had slowly washed away in the trials he endured. There was no point in lingering on them anymore. Subaru couldn’t explain any of that. So, he was left to ponder what made her so distraught. Was it the memories? Did knowing the full extent of their time together lead to a resurgence of her despair? How could he solve this?

“It’s not like this is the worst thing I ever faced,” Subaru muttered.

Beatrice stared at him with a mix of horror and pure internal agony, “Betty knew it. There was a reason for all those nights…”

“What?”

“Why didn’t you tell Betty how much you suffered?”

“Wait but I did. I told you about my time in the prison—”

“Before!” Beatrice looked viscerally angry, “Was it in the mansion? Was it at Sanctuary? Was it before you came to Lugunica, I suppose?”

“Beako—”

“Who hurt you?”

“No one.” That was a lie. And she knew it. “No one who isn’t already dead or gone or…doesn’t deserve punishment.”

Beatrice’s rage subsided into horror and pity, “Betty doesn’t understand.  Why won’t you tell me the truth?”

“…” If he could, he would. But the only one who could ever know, was walking ten feet ahead of them. And that was enough.

“…So, Betty failed you even before I abandoned you, in fact?” Beatrice muttered.

“Beako?” Subaru tried to get her attention again, but the little girl went mute against his chest and not saying another word.

Subaru sighed as he realized this would be much more complicated than he anticipated. He dreaded what would happen once the others woke up or once they returned to Lugunica.

------------------------

“So, this is it?” Anastasia asked as they entered the secret room. It took quite a while to find the secret room as it seemed to have transported from its initial position, or so Julius claimed. Strangely enough, it opened itself to them once more when Subaru took a book from the shelves. She didn’t understand how some guy named Forstetz Beal was related to Flugel.

Nor why Julius was highly adamant they do not open any of the books. Apparently, the books let you see someone’s past and the effect can be highly variable. And haunting. He specifically emphasized how haunting it was and Anastasia did not know if he meant literally or figuratively. It seemed Julius most likely opened one himself and was not happy with what he saw. So she pocketed the book for now and would open it later if needed.

It’s fine, she already has so many things possessing her body nowadays. What’s one more?

“Indeed, this was where Otto and I hid as a safe haven from our adversaries,” Julius explained, “I did not realize this was the Sage’s room at first.”

“Shaula didn’t mention it?” Anastasia asked.

Julius grimaced, “The Sage—I mean—the Sage’s apprentice was not forthcoming with information. She seemed downright melancholic with our presence and refused to interact with any of us. Just giving a rare piece of information or a necessary direction when asked. Nothing more, however.”

Anastasia pondered the implications. It was interesting that the Sage had an apprentice and more interesting that for such a long time, the apprentice was thought to be the Sage. Geuse explained that there was a complication in history most likely. Either a purposeful obfuscation on Flugel’s part or an error on the scholars. Either way, Geuse explained that if they couldn’t find anything worthwhile in Flugel’s notes, Shaula was the next best thing.

Unfortunately, “What are the odds she is dead?”

Julius’s brow furrowed, “Unclear. The last I saw her, she was fighting the Witch of Envy alongside Reinhard.”

Anastasia noticed something on Julius’s face, “What? Something wrong?”

Julius shook his head, “No I just remembered something unpleasant. Do not mind me.”

Subaru poked his head in front of Julius, “Well you can’t just say that and not elaborate. Come on man, say it!”

“…When we first arrived at the tower, Shaula’s first reaction to us was shooting her magic at Reinhard multiple times before proceeding to go unconscious.”

“…”

“…”

“…What did he even do to make her so mad?” Subaru asked, baffled.

“If I could answer that, perhaps our time would not have been spent hitting our heads against the wall,” Julius sighed. “Reinhard blamed himself for the Sage’s lack of assistance. But I am doubtful she could have helped. That trail was frankly impossible to decipher. Nothing we did gave us any hints at solving it.”
“You think this Flugel guy has any other puzzles? Could be some in this room.” Subaru suggested as he pointed a thumb at their surroundings.

“The guy definitely has secrets,” Halibel said as he ran his hand on the wall and lingered on a specific brick before pressing into it deeply. The brick began to shudder before pushing back out and revealing a hidden compartment. Reaching inside he brought out an amulet as Anastasia walked over to the desk and found Flugel’s diary sitting right on top, without a speck of dust on it. She frowned as she recognized words inscribed on top, picking it up.

“Subaru—”

“Woah!” Subaru exclaimed, interrupting Anastasia’s words as he looked at the amulet in Halibel’s hands, “I know that symbol!”

That caught her attention. She narrowed her eyes onto the jewelry and tried to trace her mind through Subaru’s memories. It then hit her right as Subaru spoke aloud, “That’s the Yin-Yang symbol.”

It was an odd ornament. A metal chain where a circular piece of metal with half its surface painted black and half its surface painted white. Each colored side was almost entirely solid except for a dot of white or black that blemished the purity. Anastasia remembered the name of that symbol twice fold. Once when Subaru was scrolling on the internet. The second…

“Fun fact, it’s called the Taiji symbol. Back home, it’s from another country nearby that uses it to describe a supreme absolute. I don’t remember much but apparently it’s about the harmony between opposing forces or something.”

“Mother of Taiji…” Anastasia muttered as she walked over to them.

“Hm?” Subaru looked over to Anastasia and winced at her intensity, “Wait, mother of what now?”

Anastasia grabbed at the amulet and frowned. Taiji. Pandora mentioned this briefly. Why? What in the future did she see for it be relevant to Anastasia? And why does the amulet feel so ominous. Bringing her finger to the symbol. She felt a spark of pain rush through her hand and dropped the thing along with the book in her hand.

“Ow!” Subaru grasped his own hand, mirroring Anastasia’s movement as the people around them rushed to their sides in dismay.

Ignoring the onslaught of concern, Subaru’s eyes widened as he looked down, “That’s Japanese!”

Anastasia nodded, waving her hand and trying to release the slight numbness that remained. “Looks like our little Sage friend was also from Japan.”

“How interesting,” Julius muttered as he knelt down and picked up both the book and amulet. He handed the book to Subaru while he held the amulet in his own hands, obviously not wanting a repeat of the previous incident.

Subaru did not hesitate as he opened the book to a random chapter and began scanning the pages. Anastasia also looked over his shoulder. Both of their faces began to slowly frown as they read each word.

Halibel raised an eyebrow, “Somethin’ wrong?”

Subaru and Anastasia slowly raised their heads.

Subaru spoke for both of them, “…This guy’s an idiot.”

Chapter 63: Heaven Needs Friends

Summary:

Julius is trying to ignore the elephant in the room...and fails.

Chapter Text

“Are…are you sure?” Julius asked, baffled that they seemed to be insulting one of the supposed greatest heroes in Lugunican history. After calling the sage an idiot, the two stars read through several sections of the diary rapidly and both looked increasingly frustrated.

Subaru pointed at the page he was reading and said aloud, “Man Satella-tan is so pretty! She is the prettiest in the world! I could just stare at her for days. Super pretty! Light of my life! Beautifulest woman in the world!”

He said that all in the most monotone voice.

Julius, Halibel, and Beatrice stared at Subaru and slowly turned their heads to Anastasia who just nodded while massaging her temples. “He’s not joking. Like at all.”

“Beautifulest? Did you not mean most beautiful, in fact?” Beatrice asked.

Subaru turned the book around and pointed at a specific section, “Beautifulest. Right there.” His expression was deadpan as he then flipped the page, “This keeps going for like several pages. It then talks about lunch, dinner, and other stuff. Some small bits about Echidna. No, it’s not that important. It’s mostly about how she was annoying him about random stuff. Also, I think, maybe, possibly, Echidna had a crush on him. Or wanted to experiment on him. I have no idea which. And then it goes right back to simping for Satella!” Subaru flipped the pages rapidly, “Twenty pages of it!”

Anastasia grabbed the book and pointed at another section, “Right here it says, ‘We were working on a possible solution to Daph’s hunger problem. Unfortunately, it would require some more studies into curses and ritual spells. Dona had some ideas but I don’t think its ethical to throw humans into what was roughly the equivalent of a magical blender. What was interesting was that we could possibly isolate the Witch Factor and its effects and maybe create a sort of limiter for the user. This may be able to allow people who suffer from side effects, like Daph and her hunger pains, to live relatively normal lives.’”

Halibel nodded, “That seems like somethin’ that could possibly help us. Maybe not the exact same but if he can isolate a Witch Factor, maybe that was what led ta sealin’ the Witch of Envy.”

Anastasia pointed at Halibel, “You would think, right? But no, after this, he swerves off the topic and goes straight into how he was going to have this person called Daph, do an eating contest. Then its several pages of how Satella looks wonderful eating food. And how great she would be as a housewife. And in an apron and in…a…” Anastasia trailed off in disgust.

Subaru nearby was cringing, “Yeah let’s not talk about what happens after that. There are children here.”

“Betty is…not a child…in fact,” Beatrice tried to retort but it seemed like she hesitated with every word. Subaru, without looking, dragged Beatrice into his arms and just started smothering her.

Without skipping a beat, he said, “You’ll always be a child to me, Beako!” And started rubbing his cheeks on Beatrice’s, making her squirm. The spirit appeared melancholic but at least a little happier than before.

Subaru then pointed at the book, “But yeah, I don’t know what Flugel’s deal is. Like…he’s an idiot. And I should know.”

Subaru looked particularly aghast while Anastasia, who was still reading the diary front to back rapidly, had an incredibly exasperated expression. It was giving Julius an uncomfortable feeling at the pit of his stomach that he couldn’t quite describe nor understand.

“Julius. Correct me if I am wrong, but could it be that you find their sudden affection for each other, incomprehensible?”

Julius bristled but chose to not answer the ghost in his mind. That wasn’t the cause of this weird feeling. That was completely different and not even remotely true!

“…It is not healthy for you to ignore me forever.”

I disagree. I believe it is perfectly normal for me to ignore something that doesn’t exist and any action to address you is, frankly, bordering on insanity.

“I understand this must be hard to accept but I am not trying to harm you in the least. My goal is to assist you in your troubles as there is nothing else I can provide you at the moment.”

You can provide me silence as that will allow me to properly think! You…you don’t exist. Prince Fourier died over two years ago. That book was evidence of it! But whatever you are…you are just a figment of my imagination. A lingering scar from what I saw.

“Perhaps. And perhaps just like how you ignore my existence, you ignore your own feelings regarding these two in front of you.”

How dare you insinuate such a notion?! Anastasia-sama has the right to love whoever she sees fit. My opinion matters not. Furthermore, Subaru is a wonderful man who no doubt gives her everything that she wishes. I am happy that they have found solace in each other.

“The fact that you said such statements, proves my point. Nevertheless! I did not intend to demean you as someone who rejects their love but rather someone who doesn’t fully understand the how, when, and why. These are two different situations. Of course, you would support them but that does not mean you have to fully understand them.”

…How…how is that any different?

“Hmm, how to convince you…let me give an example. In the beginning, I will admit, I did not fully understand my beloved Crusch nor did I fully understand Ferris. Dear as they were to me, some of their ideals were alien to my reasoning. Crusch’s love for the Lion Kings was incredible but I could not fully grasp the extent. Not at first at least. Nor did I grasp the reasoning behind Ferris’s choice of clothing. To me, it was obvious that believing in an ideal would drive our souls to great heights. I assumed such for both Crusch and Ferris.”

And you were wrong?

“I was partially correct. In truth, the reasons behind such ideals were more complex. Ferris believed in his own sense of femineity, but it was to mask his own insecurities. His self-doubt. His destructive tendencies toward himself. It’s why…I am saddened by what he has done recently.”

Julius could agree. He was somewhat aware that Felix struggled with his own perception and in many ways, the loss of Fourier made him so fragile when it came to his own candidate. Felix would have done anything for Crusch. And when temptation met desperation, he ended up betraying his own ideals for his loyalty.

In the end, Felix’s fault was as much his own, as it was the people around him. To look at someone and be convinced they could handle themselves but not offer care at their lowest points. It was only natural Felix would become his own worst enemy.

“Crusch was the same. Strong, valiant, courageous. I believed she could accomplish everything and anything. That drive to reach the peak of honor just like the Lion Kings was something incredibly admirable but…if what your memories showed me was true, then perhaps my fears were right. Crusch is strong but she lacks some foresight. Flexibility. She does not adapt as well as others when adversity strikes. And it seems her current self is suffering from it. Her ideal made her rigid. And as a result, she never addressed our shared friend’s pain, until it was too late. Because she believed he was just as strong as her.”

…What is the point you are trying to make?

“That we are all flawed and capable of mistakes that do not make sense, initially to us. That my initial understanding of my most trustworthy comrades was in good faith but lacked true thought behind their actions. And that you too, have not fully grasped your loved ones decisions and reasoning. It is good that you accept the sudden changes but to deny your own emotions is equally detrimental as rejecting theirs. You have the right to feel uncomfortable, to question what happened to them, to feel uneasy by their sudden romance. To give them doubt so that you no longer have any. It is better to address your problems sooner rather than later.”

That isn’t—

“Julius!” Subaru got in Julius’s face, interrupting his internal conversation.

Panicking, Julius blurted out, “S-subaru, what is it that you have need for me?”

Subaru stared at him, “Were you not listening?”

“I…no. I am sorry,” Julius felt a wealth of shame pool up in his gut.

Subaru frowned and then sighed, “Alright. I think you should go take a walk.”

Julius’s eyes widened, “Would you like me to…leave you all alone for some time?” He already failed, again. They deemed his useless and must want him to assist in some possible way. How disgusting of him to force their hand. He needs to be more vigilant. Less preoccupied by his own thoughts.

Subaru scratched his neck, “Listen. Come here for a second.” Subaru grabbed Julius and lured him away from the group and to the entrance, “I think I might have been a little wrong. I shouldn’t have forced you to talk to Ana so soon.”

Julius’s eyebrows raised in alarm, “No! You were completely right in doing so.” He would have been a coward, otherwise. Without Subaru’s goading, they would have never even started rebuilding their relationship. They needed to fix everything as fast as possible. That was the only way to make things right.

Subaru raised an eyebrow at Julius and then glanced back at the group before returning his attention to Julius, “No. I wasn’t. Or at least, my intentions were good, but I should have been a bit more careful. I feel like we keep making these same mistakes here and it’s getting annoying now that I’m kind of aware of them.”

“What do you mean?”

Subaru rolled his hand in the air, “Oh come on. The duel. The Sloth hunt. Literally every conversation we’ve ever had. I feel like you and I keep diving headfirst into our problems and we end up making the other confront stuff in the worst way possible.”

“That’s…not inaccurate,” he still remembered the scolding Anastasia gave them both. The shame ran deep. He wasn’t aware of how much Subaru had gone through at the time. To think the poor boy was dealing with an assassination attempt on his candidate, his own recent failures, and countless attempts at his life. And he wasn’t even a warrior or trained for such situations at the time! Now wonder Subaru had acted so irrationally. While Julius still admired Subaru for his actions, the context brought clarity.

Subaru was just a simple, sheltered boy when they first met. And Julius took that passionate and naïve boy and beat him to near death in front of not only his loved ones, but the whole capital. Realistically, it was shameful of him to do so. To not even recognize someone who was suffering…was something he really needed to address. Because it seemed like he had made the same mistake already.

“I don’t think you deserve to have all of this shit thrown at you all of a sudden. It hasn’t been even like, one hour since you remembered me. And hell, it’s been barely a few hours since you remembered Ana, right? So you must be overwhelmed and it make sense you’re spacing out all of the time,” Subaru said. Julius felt embarrassed. He wanted to explain that he had a ghost constantly talking to him in his head, but would Subaru even believe that? No. He’d think Julius was insane. Julius couldn’t believe how annoying it was to have something so bothersome but having no way to explain it to those around you. “That’s why I’m telling you to go take a walk and clear your head. We’re going to probably confront some of the tower’s challenges soon and we need you to be at top form, unfortunately.”

Julius gripped his sword, “I see…”

Subaru punched his chest lightly, “Stop taking that the wrong way! I’m not blaming you nor expecting you to be the best of the best! And that’s not me looking down on your or whatever, it’s just…” Subaru looked like he was trying to find the right words. He then sighed again and looked rather downtrodden, “…I just want you to take some time for yourself. Ana and I had time to accept what happened to us. You didn’t. Try to collect your thoughts and come back. Again, this isn’t something we can just fix in like, a day. Probably not for a while. But…I guess I just want to make sure you aren’t suffering alone or anything and well,” Subaru stuttered as he lost his train of thought again. “Just…stop trying to make it seem like you’re responsible for everything, okay! I’m not perfect! Ana isn’t either! And you aren’t at fault for all of it!”

Julius blinked but he began to understand, “You want me to…not blame myself. And to think less of you?”

“Yes. No. I mean, argh!” Subaru scratched his head, “I want you to be…fair. To yourself and even to us. Ana messed up and it wasn’t like her to do that, and you aren’t wrong for…getting annoyed at her, is what I’m saying.”

Julius cocked his head at Subaru, “You want me to be annoyed?”

“…I think anyone would be when the person they love and care for didn’t even try to reconnect with them.”

Julius stared, “…”

“…”

“…Pfft,” Julius began to laugh.

Subaru blushed, “What?”

“It is just,” Julius snickered, “I did not expect to have this conversation with you. Ever.”

“What, like me trying to get your head out of your ass?”

“No, to have you be so sincere with me,” Julius smiled as he spoke. “Do not get me wrong, I am not implying that you are dishonest with me. But if I may be frank, I felt that our conversations, ever since the capital…have had something similar to a barrier between us. I never felt like I was able to talk to you in a straightforward manner. This is quite nice, all things considered.”

Subaru scratched his head, still blushing, “I know! It’s not like I was trying to be like that, or anything. It’s just hard getting rid of all that history between us,” Subaru tapped his foot on the ground and looked away. “But I guess I want to change that. At least, a little bit, is all. Because well…we’re going to be seeing each other more…and I don’t really…want…you to be uncomfortable with us.”

“…Subaru. I do not understand how you seduced Anastasia-sama,” Julius confessed. “Do not misunderstand, I accept your relationship wholeheartedly. But it is quite hard to believe you two would be together given your…personalities.”

Unexpectedly, Subaru chuckled at his comment, “No I completely agree. I thought the same. I never expected to get with her and, hell, we probably would have never gotten together in a normal situation.”

“Then, if you could explain, what drew you to her?”

“She was the only one who cared at the time,” Subaru said with a mournful look. “Which, don’t get me wrong, is a pretty terrible way to fall for someone. But to be honest, it’s been pretty consistent for me. I got attached to her, hard. And it’s because she was the only one I could rely on when everyone forgot. And over time, we got to see each other without all the…stuff we try to do to hide ourselves. Maybe it’s because we both lost so much at the time, but it was really easy to just act as our real selves. No trying to impress anyone or try to make ourselves strong. We were just…our worst selves.”

Julius nodded despite how he didn’t quite get what Subaru was explaining. To love each other because they revealed their worst selves, was such a strange and yet romantic idea to him. Still, there was one question he wanted to ask, “Subaru, could I ask you an uncomfortable question?”

Subaru raised an eyebrow, “Depends on the question.”

Julius bit his lip, hesitating, “…Are you still in love with Lady Emilia?”

Subaru didn’t hesitate, “No. Not anymore.”

“I see and…” Julius didn’t know if he should ask the follow up question. They were already making such good progress, and he didn’t want to aggravate Subaru with a thoughtless remark.

Subaru, however, seemed to have guessed what he wanted to ask, “I did. I was in love with Emilia and…Rem…for the longest time. But when I was in that prison cell, a part of me gave up on the idea that I could ever have a life with them. I felt like every time I went through something, everyone I loved would leave me to deal with it. Sure, that was bullshit. It was just me coping with the pain and loss. There even was a time where a friend got it in my skull that I could ask them for help. That they would be there to help and I would not have to be the only one responsible.” Subaru’s eyes looked very old, “…But a part of me realized people only cares because of circumstance. If the circumstances change, so does the level of care. If I were to try again and again, I’m sure I could reach that same level. But…I was tired.”

“Subaru—”

“I know. It’s a weak excuse but I was tired of it all. Tired of having everything good in my life, get taken away. So, when I met Ana, I never wanted to fall in love again. It was difficult for me to want something that could so easily be taken away with such short notice. I should have been stronger, I should have been someone who could deal with it all but…” Subaru chuckled weakly, “I guess I wasn’t the person I thought I was. But also, I was the same kid who arrived here just a year and a half ago. I fell in love again, despite everything. And worst of all, I loved Ana, but I still had lingering feelings for two other girls. What a terrible person I was.”

“…”

“…But then Ana got sick. And I realized I may never be able to experience something wonderful with her, just because I was scared of committing. Scared of hurting two people’s feelings who may never reciprocate again…so I made a selfish decision. Be with Ana and throw away everything else. Not the most knightly thing to do but…if it meant I could be happy for just a little bit, I thought it was worth doing.”

Julius waited for Subaru to continue but it seemed the man was done. Julius never expected to hear this all from Subaru but because of such a confession, he felt a part of the weight within him, become lifted. Julius did not understand everything. Some aspects brought disappointment and disapproval. But others?

Julius couldn’t blame someone for wanting to be happy in spite of the world.

So, Julius only had one thing to say, “…While the Finest of Knights would find your lack of loyalty to your Lady disagreeable, and outright blasphemous to our Order’s creed, I, Julius Juukuulius, cannot say the same.” Subaru appeared surprised by his words. “You made a vow to care for your candidate until your last dying breath. I too, made the same promise. As a fellow knight, I would have to banish you for breaking your oath for such promiscuous reasons, Natsuki Subaru,” Julius felt his resolve waver, but he pushed forward. “However, Natsuki Subaru did not exist during such actions.”

Subaru’s expression, which morphed into irritation and solemn acceptance, turned into confusion and then surprise again, “I-what?”

“Your name was forgotten. You were no longer a knight. And therefore, your actions, while dishonorable, had no weight. You had no responsibility for anyone. Not to me, not to the kingdom, nor to your Lady.” Julius glanced over to Anastasia and then back to Subaru. “And yet, you were able to rise to the occasion where I could not. How could the Finest of Knights reprimand you, when I have also failed. As such, even if it may not be worthwhile to you, as a knight of the Royal Guard, I absolve you of your sins. Your actions during the escape, during your banishment, and even now, were all justified in my eyes.”

Subaru seemed to not know what to say, “…”

“…But if I may, as Julius Juukuulius, I would like to absolve you of your worries. Love is a complex monster to deal with. While Lady Emilia deserves better than a sudden departure by her sworn knight, you deserve better than constant suffering. You deserve better than bearing the weight of responsibility, for a kingdom that abandoned you at your worst. You deserve…to be happy.”

“…I don’t know what to say,” Subaru said. He seemed genuinely lost.

Julius could understand. But he felt right in his decisions. While there was so much for him to still process and uncover, Julius was not wrong in his current actions. Because despite how his morals were screaming at him to enact justice upon his fellow knight, his heart disagreed. They had fought together. Bled together. And obtained victory together. Julius knew that Subaru wasn’t the type of person to give up so easily. So, for him to have given up on his candidate, especially his love for her; it must have been a very difficult decision. He must have struggled for some time, and all for the sake of Julius’s own candidate. The candidate he had failed.

Julius may not be a good knight, not anymore. But at least he could be a good friend.

And even if Subaru didn’t see him as one, they could start now.

“That is fine. I do not know what else to say either but—” Julius struggled. It may be too selfish to say but he wanted to at least try, “…if possible. Once we have exited this predicament, could we possibly…talk more?”

Subaru blinked, “Like hang out?”

“…Yes.” It felt embarrassing to say. But Julius always wanted to do something fun with Subaru. Go to a bar and share stories. Just like with Reinhard and Felix.

Silence persisted for what felt like eons until Subaru finally removed it, “Yeah. I would like that.”

“Good.”

“Yeah.”

“…”

“…”

“…I should…perhaps…go then,” Julius said awkwardly.

“Y-yeah!” Subaru stuttered, “Go take a walk…and clear your head.”

“Yes, I shall.”

After a few seconds of waiting, Julius finally walked away down the corridor to exit into the library. However, just as he was one-third of the way there, he heard a voice behind him, “Hey Julius!”

He turned his head and saw Subaru look awkwardly around before continuing, “I…I’m glad you’re my friend! You dick!”

Julius took a second to process what Subaru just said before letting out a breath that he did not know he was holding. He then smiled, “I am grateful as well! You…asshole?” Julius didn’t mean to say that as a question, but it came out as such. Still, Subaru ignored his mistake and simply reflected his smile.

Small victories.

“So, do you feel better?”

…Yes. I do.

“Haha! It seems I was not wrong in my observations! Good to see!”

Yes, yes. Perhaps you are not a simple hallucination after all, Julius chuckled. He then had an idea, Fourier-sama. Would you mind answering a few questions of mine?

He must have imagined it, but he felt the ghostly voice perk up in response, “Happily! What do you wish to know?”

Why did you not confess to Crusch-san sooner?

“…Could you possibly ask another question?”

No.

Julius laughed as the prince sputtered in his brain.

Julius didn’t know exactly where things would go at this point.

But he felt like that was alright.

-------------------------

Beatrice did not know what to do anymore.

“It’s going to take so long to find what we need,” Anastasia sighed beside her.

How could she do such horrible things to her special person? The person she chose? How could she ignore his problems for this long?

Halibel took a puff of his kiseru, “Not like we have a time limit. As much as ya say that Reinhard can’t keep her at bay forever. There’s a high chance that he really can.”

Was she stupid?! Subaru had suffered for months! Night after night, hurting himself and having horrible nightmares. There must have been a reason. And if Subaru was telling the truth, then it must have been related to his first months in Lugunica. There was no other way.

And given what she knew about his Authority…

It made her sick. Disgusted in not only herself but also everyone else. What did those creatures do to her Subaru?! The twins…they must have done something. Beatrice knew it! The blue one must have done something to Subaru during his first week. She knew what that maid was like. If she smelled Subaru’s scent, she could only imagine…

It made the spirit feel rancid. Too many possibilities ran through her head. Rem, Ram, Roswaal, Otto, Garfiel, that one girl in the basement. Maybe even Emilia. They must have either hurt Subaru in some capacity or led to him being harmed. She needed to think. Logically pinpoint who was responsible for what and exact revenge on all—

“Betty,” Beatrice felt a hand on her head, “Calm down.”

She looked up at Anastasia and winced, “…Betty is calm. What are you talking about, in fact?”

Anastasia smiled but her expression was laced with concern, “Let’s talk.”

Chapter 64: Heaven Forgives

Summary:

Beatrice has a talk with Ana...

Chapter Text

“What is there to talk about, I suppose?” Beatrice turned her head away from Anastasia, heat creeped up her neck as she felt something drop in her stomach.

Anastasia replied by picking up the poor girl and putting her on her lap.

“What are you doing, in fact?!” Beatrice protested.

Anastasia chuckled as she patted the spirit softly, “It’s what I usually did for Mimi all the time. She’d love it when I patted her on the head or scratched her ears while we talked.”

“I am not one of your adopted children!”

“Aren’t you technically Subaru’s child?” Anastasia raised an eyebrow.

Beatrice pouted, “Betty is whoever Subaru needs.”

Whether it was daughter, mother, or sister. She would be Subaru’s family, no matter the role. If Beatrice could be Subaru’s confidant, she would be it in a heartbeat. If Beatrice could be the one by his side every second, she would be. If she could be his only comfort when the world was against him, she would hold his hand and never let go. To Beatrice, Subaru was everything. He was the one she chose. Her special person, not divined by any book or Authority.

And yet, she failed him.

“Well either way, that also makes you part of my family as well,” Anastasia cooed.

Beatrice felt Anastasia squeeze her in a tight hug as Halibel sat down next to them on the ground. Beatrice hated this, “Stop pitying me, I suppose.”

“I’m not. I’m comforting you.”

“Well either way, stop,” Beatrice didn’t deserve this. Not love, pity, or any sort of understanding. She deserved hatred, scorn, remorse. Nothing less given the mountain of mistakes that she made. They all deserved Hell for what they did to him.

“Betty,” Anastasia’s voice was stern. “Tell me what’s wrong.”

“You already know,” Beatrice grit her teeth. “Betty doesn’t have to explain the obvious.”

“It’s better if you do it yourself. You’ll feel better getting it out.”

“…”

“…Okay, then I’ll say it,” Anastasia took a deep breath. “All the memories came back to you and now you’ve realized Subaru wasn’t the man you thought he was.”

Beatrice stilled, “What did you just say?”

“You saw Subaru be this amazing hero for so long. And you’re disappointed that he ran away without even talking to you guys.”

What was this girl even saying? What kind of bullshit was she spewing?

“Ana.”

“You don’t know why he decided to just up and leave you guys, but you feel it was unjustified. You think he was someone who could withstand any kind of work. Any kind of danger. And yet, after just a short time of imprisonment, he left you all. He didn’t even try to reach out to you.”

“Ana!”

“Just one mistake, and he resented all of you. Left you behind while he started this affair with me. It sickens you to think that you cherished this man because how could one year of fun be thrown aside just because of factors outside of your control? It must be infuriating. You must feel deeply hurt. You must despise him—”

“SHUT UP!” Beatrice finally burst. “Stop it!”

But Anastasia didn’t stop, “Oh so it’s not that? Then you must be so angry and sad because you blame yourself. Is that it? You made one incredibly horrible mistake and because of that, you threw away all of your happiness. You hate yourself. Don’t you?”

Anastasia’s words cut deep but not because they were accurate. They were so close to the root cause of her despair but she continuously tip-toed around the problem, goading her with specifically chosen words to poke her where it hurt. She knew this. She knew what she was doing. Beatrice knew what Anastasia was trying to do.

That didn’t stop it from affecting her.

Beatrice tried to squirm her way out of Anastasia’s arms, but it was not possible, Anastasia held onto her tight with strength unbefitting of the relatively weak woman. “Enough! Stop talking nonsense, in fact!”

“You have to tell me, or else I won’t know what is bothering you. So I’ll just keep talking until you say something,” this woman was so infuriating. She knew. She absolutely knew. And yet she continued to play this game, “You must hate yourself because you realized how little your relationship mattered, at least to him. You could have done more. You could have been better, you could have been someone he wanted to stay near, no matter what. But you failed and all you could think about are, ‘what ifs.’”

Beatrice looked toward Halibel for help, in a desperate last attempt to abscond from this situation. Halibel, however, merely shrugged, “This is for yer own good. The sooner ya give in, the better.”

This mutt. No wonder Zarestia wanted to beat him to death half the time, “This won’t solve anything. What good would saying it, even do? It won’t get rid of anything. It won’t change anything. And it certainly won’t make me feel better, in fact!”

“So what, will you just sit there, stewing over it all as if that will be any different?” Anastasia glared, “Betty. You just want to have someone punish you, right? Because that will be the only way to make up for all of your mistakes. I get it. I was the same as you. Back in Banan, and back in the mansion, all I could do was wallow in my own self-pity. But that’s not the way to live. And I’ll be damned if I let you just do the same.”

No. That’s not it. It was partially the reason, but it wasn’t the exact root cause for her rage. The reason wasn’t just because of her. There was something more malicious and insidious to direct her ire toward, “That isn’t what Betty is bothered about. And there are much more important things for us to focus on.”

Anastasia rolled her eyes, “This?” She held up Flugel’s diary, “It’s 90% nonsense and 10% actual substance. It would take days for us to carefully dissect. I have a plan for it, but it won’t last that long. This, however, you’re whole mental crashout thing? I want to deal with it and nip it in the bud.”

Beatrice cocked her head, “Crashout? What?”

“Oh. Sorry. Forgot that’s slang,” what does that even mean. “Anyways, doesn’t matter. We can either sit here, arguing forever and get nothing done. Or you can finally stop being a baby. Your choice.”

“…”

“…Do you really hate yourself that much?”

“…No. Betty hates the others much more,” Beatrice finally admitted.

“Others?” Anastasia raised an eyebrow.

Beatrice shifted in her grasp. “Betty hates them. Every single one. The more Betty thinks, the more Betty knows they’ve hurt Betty’s Subaru more than Betty could ever imagine.”

Beatrice gripped her hands with disdain. It all made sense now. Every odd behavior. Every single weird thing that she noticed but decided not to comment on: Subaru’s strange words with certain people, how he flinches when he hears chains or sees rabbits, how he just knows things that no one else does. Beatrice did not want to pry as Subaru had the right to keep his secrets. She wanted to relieve his suffering, but she could not be his minder. It wasn’t her right.

And maybe it never was.

Beatrice wanted to say that she was always someone who would have helped him out, no matter what. But was that really true? Before she chose Subaru, how many times did she reject his affection? How many times did she push him out of her room or ignored his efforts? How can Beatrice be sure that she wasn’t responsible for negligence? For ignoring him during his worst moments.

She knew who she was. Who she once was. She could imagine Subaru coming to her for aid, and constantly, consistently, remaining aloof. Subaru must have suffered during his time at the mansion. He must have suffered at the capital. He must have suffered at Sanctuary. Everyday, he must have suffered. And what did Beatrice do?

She must have just watched with such self-righteous pity. Seeing him as an idiot who knew no better. Time after time, throughout all of the moments that no longer existed, she must have been one of his worst enemies.

No wonder he looked so desperate in that moment. No wonder he reached out to her with pleading eyes. No wonder he spoke with such determination and sadness. He must have been at the end of his rope to seek her for help.

Perhaps he did not even think he would have succeeded that time? Maybe he carefully worded his sentences to give himself a better chance, just so Beatrice could so graciously provide him basic human decency.

It made her sick to her very core. It disgusted her. Enraged her. She hated her past self. For being so slothful, and above all, so negligent. She was just like everyone else around her but that did not mean they deserved any less contempt. Because despite how ignorant she was, Beatrice knew she would never hurt Subaru directly.

But that did not apply to the rest of the Emilia camp.

Emilia aside, she knew the others were capable of great malice. The twins. Now that she had memories of the blue one, she knew why Subaru was suffering so much during that first week. It made sense now. If Subaru could go back in time, especially when his life was in-danger, then he must have done so because of the twins.
