The red one was stupidly obsessed with the clown for no good reason. But the blue one…she had a bone to pick with cultists. She could smell the miasma.

Beatrice always knew that her behavior was weird. When Beatrice told the others that Subaru was not an issue, the only one who did not relax was the blue one. She must have done something to Subaru. Her behavior after the first week was even stranger but it all made sense now. She didn’t fall in love with Subaru naturally. She fell in love with Subaru because it was the only way he could get her to stop going after him.

What a sick joke.

…How many times did she just watch him nearly die then? Countless, probably. The Beatrice from back then would rather watch a poor boy suffer than leave her room. Because that’s all she was, an aloof spirit, ignorant of the suffering of others because she wallowed in her own so much more.

It reminded her of the tiger boy from Sanctuary. From what the others said and by his own volition, he was a brat who constantly picked fights with the group during their tenure there. The tiger boy must have harassed Subaru to no end. He wasn’t the gentle type. How many times must he have broken Subaru’s bones over a misunderstanding or an argument? Countless no doubt.

And the rabbits.

…Beatrice did not want to think about the implications of that. Nor the implications of the White Whale hunt, or when he fought Geuse. It was too much.

But there was at least one conclusion she had: the second she got home, she was going to kill Roswaal.

The man had lived too long. He had hurt too many people. And he especially hurt Subaru. He was the one who called upon the rabbits. He must have had Subaru face them countless times. And whose to say that Subaru turned back time right as they attacked him. They must have hurt him in some capacity.

Too much maybe.

Was that why he scratched at his arms? Why his nightmares were plentiful? Why he screamed about things being ‘inside of him?’

Ram and Otto were hard to pinpoint but Beatrice could guess what they might have done. Ram was loyal only to her sister and the clown. While she had a soft spot for Subaru, she doubted that meant she would always be on his side. Whose to say that she wouldn’t ignore his suffering for her own twisted love.

Otto was possibly the worst but for the most unexpected reasons. He was someone who Beatrice could tell held great affection for Subaru and the rest of the camp. Someone loyal who could be considered Subaru’s closest friend—his best friend.

But Beatrice had seen Otto’s intelligence upfront. The man was capable of so much more than he showed. He was an absolute moron, had little masculine energy, and was overall pathetic. But his capability for destruction and malice was far greater than anyone else in the camp, even the clown was not up to par.

The fact that Otto sewed explosives into his clothing was a testament to how paranoid the merchant was.

Whose to say that Otto’s wrath was not directed to Subaru once upon a time? Rem was similar and so she could not help but doubt Otto’s innocence in light of that.

Hatred. That was all Beatrice could feel. For the injustice that plagued Subaru for so long and for how long he had been in the company of heartless monsters. Each one didn’t deserve any kindness. Not the twins. Not Garfiel. Not Roswaal. Not Otto. Not Emilia.

Not even her.

Sure, Emilia did no damage to Subaru. But she was still the de-facto leader of their camp. She held responsibility. And if Subaru suffered all of this time under her watch, then Beatrice could not trust her. Not anyone. Before, she was willing to allow Subaru to be with Anastasia because he was so happy. She had no memories of his romantic involvement with either Emilia or Rem, so it was an easy decision all things considered.

However, now, her reasoning was even more enforced. Not because he was happier now. No. It was because Subaru was not surrounded by a bunch of people who hurt him in some capacity.

Julius aside, he would be much safer here. He would be safer with the Anastasia camp or the Banan group. There was no reason for Subaru to return to the Emilia camp and she would rather die than allow that to ever occur.

…Perhaps it was selfish of her to do so and yet still remain by his side. But to leave would mean hurting Subaru greatly. And she was not willing to do that. Not anymore. May everyone suffer for his happiness.

Anastasia patted Beatrice’s head softly, “Do you want me to tell you the truth?”

Beatrice did not say anything. She was right, saying it did not change how she felt. Just a gaping hole in her chest filled with rage and sorrow. “…”

“Emilia’s camp did hurt Subaru in some capacity. Almost every single one of them. The hatred you feel is right. But whatever you think happened, it does not describe the worst that Subaru witnessed. Not even close.”

“…Was that supposed to make Betty feel better?”
Anastasia shook her head, “No. I wanted to reaffirm how you felt. Because you are right to be angry. Because I was the same. The conclusions you made were similar to what I had just a few days before. At the very least, you are not alone when it comes to such ideas.”

“So what? Are we to commiserate our feelings, I suppose? Such nonsense.”

Anastasia chuckled, “Don’t worry about that. This gal doesn’t care for such emotional therapy or that kind of nonsense.”

Beatrice turned her head up to look at the girl, “Emotional therapy what now?”

Anastasia just smiled, “Don’t worry about that. Just worry about how we are going to kill the whole Emilia camp.”

“…What?” Beatrice blinked.

Anastasia continued to smile but there was an edge of malice there, “Wasn’t that what you were thinking?”

“…Betty had that as a possibility but…not at the forefront of my mind,” Beatrice was too surprised by her blunt answer to speak clearly. She did not expect someone to simply speak her most intrusive thought out loud.

“Then what are you going to do then? You are angry at them, and it seems you are willing to act on such hatred. So come on. Spill what your plans are. You do have them, don’t you?”

“…Betty had thought of a few but nothing concrete, I suppose.”

“Cool. Then we’ll just do it my way. Remember that list of people? Yeah it’s basically the same. We’ll just grab Tia and have her chuck like 500 tornadoes at Lugunica.”

Beatrice stared at Anastasia, “You’re not serious, are you?”

Anastasia was still smiling. It unnerved Beatrice, “As Hoshin once said. Always have a nuclear option.”

“Betty does not think Hoshin said that.”

“Alex? No. Anastasia? Yes.”

“Stop joking around, it isn’t funny.”

“I’m not. Sure it might be a little difficult but, again, we have Tia and Halibel. Like I doubt any one of them can deal with both of the strongest of Kararagi at the same time. We’ll have to slowly pick them apart but it’s not like it would be hard. Have to kill Otto first though. Suwen is way too smart to keep alive. After that, we really just have to kill Emilia and have Puck explode and all is well. Any of the remaining members would be too frostbitten and it will just be us sending kunai storms on mass. I doubt any would be able to survive that besides Roswaal.”

Beatrice blinked. Anastasia was not joking in the least. This was, as rough as it was, a sincere summary of what she would do if she had to kill the Emilia camp. She looked to Halibel again for assurance. Surely, he would be reasonable enough to tell Anastasia to stop messing around.

Halibel just shrugged and said, “Sure. Again, never really liked Lugunica all that much. So long as we don’t kill any innocents, I’m game.”

Stupid, lazy, mutt! Beatrice was going to have Zarestia finally neuter the useless dog. Beatrice looked back at Anastasia, “Don’t act like that would be so easy. You haven’t killed anyone before.”

“No, I have,” Anastasia’s eyes turned cold. “Betty. Don’t doubt the depths of my own cruelty. I grew up in Banan’s slums, and my hands were not kept clean. I was not someone who could just survive on words alone and I will kill again if it means keeping my precious people safe and sound. Whether it’s the Witch Cult, Lugunica, or someone who Subaru loves. I’ll tear them apart and make them choke on their own filth, before standing over them, laughing at their demise. Sure, it would be cruel. But I’d rather be cruel than helpless again.”

Beatrice shuddered. This girl, she really did change during her time in a brief coma. The longer she thought about it, the more she was curious of what actually happened during that period. “Even so, Betty thinks this is too rash.”

“Weren’t you the one stating you hated them all?”

“…Betty does not know anymore.”

Perhaps it was the sudden shock of Anastasia’s words, but a lot of her rage had been quelled. Something about the destruction of people she knew for at least a year, the bonds they shared despite the damage that had been done. To just destroy it all, felt sobering. It was hard for Beatrice to say she actually hated them or not.

She was still angry but to be so cruel as to actually slaughter them wholesale, was something even she didn’t know if she was capable of.

Anastasia’s smile turned gentler as she combed Beatrice’s hair with her fingers, “There we go. You finally calmed down.”

Beatrice grumbled, “How did you do that? Betty didn’t even notice.”

“Sometimes you just need to help people follow their thinking to its logical conclusion and then they start to realize what was wrong, all by themselves. You were angry. Hurt. You wanted to lash out at yourself and the people who hurt Subaru. So you harbored all of these dark thoughts without understanding what that would mean if you enacted them. It’s normal.”

“…How could you say such words so sincerely? Betty did not think you were someone capable of such actions.”

Anastasia stopped combing and Beatrice felt a sense of dread before Anastasia wrapped her hands around Beatrice’s body, holding her close, “People change. Or rather, people become who they truly are. I was always someone who could never…let go. I just don’t care about wearing a mask anymore.  At the root of it all, I’d rather tear apart the whole world than lose what I love. So if it is needed, I’ll be as cruel as I should be. And I would happily go to sleep without a single regret.”

“…Betty wishes Betty could be the same, in fact.” Beatrice would do anything and everything for Subaru. But her being happy about it would be different. Killing people she cared about, would still hurt.

“No, I don’t think you should,” Anastasia said. “It’s not bad to feel conflicted. To have different feelings about a person, both good and bad.” Anastasia’s eyes glazed over before returning her attention to Beatrice, “It’s hard. Sometimes you can’t just help how you feel. You can hate a person for certain things but cherish the love and good you experienced. You can have both, one does not deny the other.”

“Betty wants to make things right. How could Betty do that if Betty is not willing to do what’s best for her Subaru, I suppose?”

“Does Subaru want the Emilia camp to suffer?” Anastasia asked.

“…No,” Beatrice knew what Subaru would say. But was that right? For him to just gloss over everything and move on? She didn’t like that. Not one bit. No one should be satisfied with suffering so much and allowing those who did so, to just get away with it.

Even her, she deserved punishment for her sins.

“But Subaru would be sad if the people he loved were to suffer,” Anastasia sighed. She then looked over at Subaru who was still talking to Julius. “That’s just how he is. He’s an idiot. A very kind idiot. But still an idiot. He doesn’t think things through sometimes. He gets stuck in his head all the time. He has the worst self-confidence issues that I’ve ever seen in a person. He forgives people way too easily and doesn’t talk about his feelings and instead just likes assuming shit without actually having any reason to assume things. He’s absolutely the most annoying person I have ever dealt with—”

“Is there a point to this or are you just going to insult your soon-to-be husband, in fact?”

“But! I love him,” Anastasia smiled. It was the warmest smile Beatrice had ever seen, “I know all of his bad traits. I’ve seen all of his worst moments. I’ve seen him be cruel and kind and everything in between. Despite how much I dislike some parts about him, I can’t help but love those parts and more. And because I love those parts, I have to respect what he wants. Subaru does not want revenge, and so I won’t.”

“It’s that simple, huh,” Beatrice grumbled. “Betty loves Subaru too…but Betty hates that part about him too.”

Anastasia chuckled, “It’s the same as others. You can hate them for their mistakes. But you can also love them for the good as well. It’s your decision whether to continue hating or loving them all-together but to use Subaru as an excuse to be so angry…I don’t think that’s worthwhile.” Anastasia finished her words with another pat on the head, “It’s a waste of time to be so angry. Especially now where it does nothing productive. Think about what you want the most. What you desire, beyond all measure. What do you want to do right now?”

Beatrice thought long and hard. What did she want? It was simple. It was something that gnawed at her all the time, ever since she had lost that spark in her life, because of her own fear and disgust. Even if she didn’t know it, she wanted it more than anything in the world.

“…Betty wants to hug her Subaru. And never separate from him ever again.”

“Then you shall have it,” Anastasia said as she pointed at an approaching Subaru.

Beatrice felt Anastasia’s arms let go of her as she was finally free to do whatever she wanted.

It might be cruel of her to do so. To take advantage of her contractor’s kindness. There was so much for her to still process. So much anger, hatred, and disgust. Directed at everyone and especially herself.

But if she could be happy. And more importantly, if she could make Subaru happy.

She would throw it all away, just to have both.

It was greedy of her.

But it felt right.

------------------------

Anastasia watched as Beatrice ran over to Subaru and gave him a big hug. She saw her whisper in Subaru’s ear and whatever she said, it made Subaru smile. Anastasia couldn’t help but do the same at such a sight. She was excited to see the Triplets again when they woke up.

“If only solvin’ our little Witch problem was as easy as solvin’ our emotions,” Halibel said.

Anastasia sighed, “Both are hard. I just have more experience dealing with one over the other right now.”

“That right? Ya actin’ like you’ll get used to Witch huntin’.”

“If I can mount at least one Witch’s head on my wall,” Pandora’s face streaked through Anastasia’s mind. “I’ll be satisfied.”

Halibel laughed, “I sure took on some troublesome wards.”

“Biggest mistake of your life, huh?”

“Yep yep,” Halibel smiled at her. “But also my biggest blessin’.”

“…Aren’t you curious about all of this? I haven’t really told you everything that went on when we were comatose.”

Halibel shrugged, “Sure I have a hundred and one questions. But it doesn’t seem like it would be safe for ya and Su-san to explain it all to me. Maybe one day, but I’m satisfied with just knowin’ ya both are safe. That’s all I need right noe.”

Anastasia felt warm, “Thanks again Hal. We’re really grateful to have met ya.”

“I could say the same.”

Subaru finally walked over with a much happier Beatrice, “So everything good over here?”

His eyes conveyed gratitude to Anastasia. He most likely understood that Beatrice’s improved mood was most likely because of her.

Anastasia nodded, “Yep. What about Julius?”

She was still worried about the poor guy. He seemed overwhelmed and she didn’t have any idea to help him. Usually she would try to get the guy to relax but in the tower? She had no easy distractions.

Subaru nodded, “Yep! Got him to go on a walk to clear his head. He’ll be fine.” Subaru then scratched his face sheepishly, “Also…might have…promised him to go hang out later.”

Anastasia raised an eyebrow, “Ya sure I shouldn’t be worried?”

“Hm? Oh don’t be so paranoid! We’re not going to fight!”

“…That’s not what I meant.”

“…”

“…”

“…Ana. I’m not sexually interested in Juliuses.”

“Your memories beg to differ.”

“Stop! I do not want to know!” Subaru said as he had Beatrice cover his ears.

Anastasia laughed. This was a good reprieve before they dived back into the problem at hand. Flugel’s book aside, they would need to check and see if there was anything else in this room that could possibly help—

Something crashed through the floor and into the ceiling. Something white and red just sailed past Anastasia at incredible speed. Bewildered, Anastasia looked through the hole in the ceiling and saw that it stretched far beyond what was humanly possible. She swore she could barely see the night sky in the distance, something twinkling right at the end of this huge makeshift skylight.

“Was that Rein?” Subaru asked as Anastasia looked through the hole in the floor.

She was greeted with a shadowy hand that wrapped around her skull.

And felt it squeeze.

Chapter 65: Made in Heaven

Summary:

Anastasia was going to die...

Chapter Text

Anastasia’s heart nearly stopped as she realized what was about to happen.

The fingers locked around her face lovingly as they increased in pressure and intensity. They felt so warm. So disgusting. It was as if darkness itself was latching onto her soul and dripping through her body through the pores. She had felt nothing like this before.

And just as suddenly, it was gone. Beatrice and Halibel reacted quickly, slicing a kunai and Minya through the hand and severing its connection from the Witch. Anastasia felt weightless as Halibel picked up both her and Subaru under each arm as he jumped away from the influx of shadowy hands from below. He looked through the hole Reinhard made in the ceiling.

“Tch, the openin’ is too small. Bea-chan!” Halibel yelled.

“Betty already knows!” Beatrice said as she grabbed Eridna from Anastasia’s shoulders and wrapped it around herself. She then pointed her finger at the ceiling, “Jamak!”

Swirling shadows and light compressed to the point of her finger, combining into one, before shooting out and decimating the roof over them fully. Not even taking a second to breathe, Halibel and Beatrice jumped and used all of the falling debris around them as leverage to climb through the crumbling tower.

“Shit, why now?!” Anastasia yelled as she scanned the environment. She clutched the amulet and the book to her chest as Halibel and Beatrice desperately kept both Anastasia and Subaru safe. Shards of Minyas blasted downward to delay the advance of the shadows while Halibel sent clone after clone after kunai at any approaching shadows.

But it was not enough.

The shadows were encroaching too quickly and despite their actions, they were nowhere near the top. Books and pieces of stone fell all around them as Anastasia desperately read through Flugel’s book for anything she might have missed. Anything that could possibly allow them to get out of this situation.

But there was nothing!

Just tons and tons of garbage about Satella or morning exercises or nonsensical rants about it being too hot and cold! Anastasia was about to go crazy as Halibel and Beatrice did their best to protect them from the onslaught. They were getting closer and closer to the next level but so were the shadows. Anastasia didn’t dare to look down or else—

Subaru. Why was he looking down like that?

He then locked eyes with her. His expression morphing from horror to guilt to acceptance. It didn’t even take her a second to realize what he was about to do.

“NO—”

“Sorry Ana-pop,” he said right before dropping right into the abyss.

Anastasia didn’t blink. She lunged forward, aiming to go with him but was stopped by two familiar hands.

“Ana-bo—” “Ana—”

She turned her head and glared, “Let go. Now.”

Her eyes wandered to both Halibel and Beatrice who looked as if they were expecting this. Subaru must have used Basiliskos. That was the only way they could have concocted this all in such a short amount of time without her knowing. It didn’t matter though. None of this did. Subaru was falling all alone now, and she needed to be there with him.

So, she made a split-second decision she would surely regret.

She aimed at the arm holding her with a well-placed Jiwald and shot. It made Halibel lose focus enough for her to leap away from him and dive down to where Subaru should be.

She ignored their yelling.

It would be fine, in the next life they won’t remember.

Anastasia just hoped she did.

Diving past all of the falling rubble and books—past the shadow hands that were confused by her actions—even through the expanse of darkness surrounding them and below, she could see him. Sense him. Even if he blended into the background, her eyes would still find him. The guiding star of her life.

Pushing off rock after rock, getting closer and closer to the ground, she went as fast as possible to catch up to him.

She would be damned if he would die alone again.

Closer and closer.

Until finally, she grabbed his foot. She saw his head roll in panic before looking up at her in sheer horror. She couldn’t help but smile at his reaction, winking at him, “Hey there you little shit.”

Subaru’s horror turned into rage as she climbed down to his eye level, “Ana…what the fuck—”

She kissed him. Sure, she was filled with immense anger and was prepared to eviscerate whatever nonsensical reason he had for taking such an action. But if this was going to be his last moment with her in this life, she was not going to make him angry or sad. She would rather they die together, happy, than bicker until the end.

She separated from his lips, and he stared at her with confusion, “Why?”

She hated that. Hated how he still didn’t understand. As if there was some mental block that prevented him from understanding her actions. He knew she loved him. But did he know how far she would go? That even the smallest of circumstances, she would try proving it again and again?

No. He didn’t. And until he did, she would do it again and again.

So, to answer his question, all she said was, “Always together. Even in death.”

She smiled and kissed him again as they fell through the tower. Ignoring everything around them. Subaru, at first, held her loosely. As if afraid. Before hanging onto her for dear life as if he didn’t want to ever let go again. The idiot. The self-sacrificing moron. If he didn’t want to die alone, then he should just be honest.

Her eyes drifted to their impending doom. The tower was tall and they were dropping at great speeds, but it felt like an endless abyss with no end. And yet still, she could see her.

The Witch of Envy. The nucleus of this shadow nexus of horror. She stood right at the bottom, looking up at them with that black veil covering her expression. Even from this distance, Anastasia could tell she was pissed. Her shadow hands were gliding along with their descent. As if waiting for the right moment to strike.

Anastasia’s mind worked fast and realized what was going to happen. The Witch of Envy would wait for their impact or a chance to separate them. And either kill Anastasia first or keep them both alive so Return by Death did not occur.

Would it work if only Anastasia died?

Probably. Even if not, Subaru was fated to die instantly when she did. Geuse said their souls were so entwined that dying was a paired event. They literally could not live without the other. Their souls would collapse without both being stable.

And that was fine for Anastasia. She didn’t like the idea of living without her other half anymore. Perhaps that made her insane. Or maybe love really made her go crazy. Or maybe she was always like this.

But it didn’t matter.

Despite her complicated feelings about Satella, her stance on the Witch of Envy was unwavering. And she needed to make sure that bitch knew where they stood.

So, before the hands would grab them and before they met their end by gravity or Witch, Anastasia raised her free hand and placed a finger to her temple. She stared down at the Witch of Envy without blinking and made another declaration of war.

“He’s mine.”

The Jiwald then pierced her skull.

--------------------

It burned. In theory it shouldn’t, as her brain no longer had a gaping hole in it. Hell, even with that hole, it should have severed any connection to the pain center within the maze of neurons in her head. And yet, it still burned.

She could remember the sensation of it piercing through her skin, her bone, and then the soft tissue that lay beneath. Cauterizing everything around it while vaporizing the contents it struck. It hurt beyond anything she could even imagine. She thought she would be used to this. She experienced the pain of thousands of deaths, all of the ones that Subaru went through. She thought it was fine.

But experiencing a memory versus witnessing it in person was vastly different.

She felt her body lose consciousness and a vague emptiness take up her sense of self.

There was nothing. Absolutely nothing. No thoughts, no dreams, no sensations. Nothing.

That was death in its fullest capacity.

And then in the next moment, she was brought back. The sheer scale of that paradox was agonizing on her body. Her soul and mind could cope but not her physical body. It knew her mind was stressed from the sudden death, but it could not know pinpoint the reason. So it panicked. It did not know how to react and so her body was having a full-blown panic attack.

The neurons and pain sensors firing without understanding the source.

She writhed on the ground in sheer agony, wanting it all to stop. To return to that emptiness and yet the fear of it all kept her from desiring it. Paradoxes upon paradoxes assaulted her entire being. It was pure insanity.

The only way she could cope would be to ignore its existence entirely. It was a dream. It should have been a dream. None of this was real.

But she knew. Her mind was already processing it all. She knew better and she had the memories and experience to rationalize it all in the best way possible. Which was why her first instinct when waking up was to slam her head into the ground to stop the pain of the burning.

She needed to die. She needed to go back. She wasn’t meant for this world. She did not deserve to exist—

“Ana!” His words brought her back. It was Subaru. Of course, he should have returned with her. Where was she?

She felt her body return to normal. It wasn’t burning anymore. No. The only sensation she could feel was his arms wrapped around her head, placing her face firmly on his chest.

There was no burning, just warmth.

Her heart was beating rapidly. She was out of breath.

She was alive. Her mind and body were alive.

It was fine.

She was okay.

“I’m sorry…I’m sorry…I’m so…sorry,” Subaru muttered, “Please. Just be okay…just don’t…”

She felt guilt wash over her as she wrapped her arms around his torso. Why was he so—

No. Of course he would react like that. She killed herself right in front of him.

All so he wouldn’t have to experience death again. But she killed herself. Someone he loved. Right as he was embracing her. Right after she told him they would be together in death. She decided to go first and have him witness it himself.

How horrifying.

“I’m…okay,” Anastasia weakly responded. She should be fine. But her body was still out of sync. How was Subaru able to endure this all so many times?

“Ana?” Subaru lifted her head from his chest and looked all over her body. He should know she was fine. They returned from death together. Her theory was correct. She couldn’t help but smile. As messed up as it was, it meant even if they died, they would be together.

Wait.

Where were they?

She looked around and realized they hadn’t returned to a checkpoint but back to the black and white world from before. Subaru wanted to call it the Shadow Garden or whatever. Anastasia thought that was a dumb name and instead called it The Od-World.

They were still arguing about what to call it.

She was about to bring it back up again when Subaru grabbed her cheeks with his hands and brought her face close to his. Which was brimming with anger, “What the fuck is wrong with you?!”

She blinked before yelling back, “What the fuck is wrong with me?! What the fuck is wrong with you?!” She smacked his hands from her face and pointed at his chest, “Do you realize—”

“No, we are not doing this!” Subaru crossed his arms in an X shape and pushed back at her, “You are not going to redirect this to me! You can’t just ignore what you just did!”

“And what did I just do, huh?!”

“YOU KILLED YOURSELF!”

“You…you…” Anastasia fire dampened. She knew this. She thought about it. She felt guilt over it. But she had to do it. There was no other option. It was either that or he would have to die. But that didn’t hold back the pain in her chest at seeing his reaction.

“…You didn’t have to do that. Why did you ever think of that as your first option? Are you insane?”

And then the fire came back, directed right at him, “You’re calling me insane? You fucking hypocrite! Do you realize how many times I’ve seen you kill yourself, again and again for the stupidest fucking reasons?!”
“I HAD TO DO THAT!” Subaru bit back, “I had to do it because there was no other option! Every time I’ve killed myself, it was to protect the people I love! To make sure they can come back instead of staying dead! You didn’t have to do that! I wasn’t dead! None of us were! There was no reason to die yet! And even then, you didn’t have to! If I can die, then no one else has to! I’m used to it! I can deal with it! I can always deal with it, because I’m the only one who can…who can return by d-death!” Subaru stuttered at the end, his eyes wavering slightly.

Anastasia stared at him disbelief, “You can’t even say it. Are you even hearing yourself?! Do you think this world is all about you?! That you can just take everything on and act like everything is okay as long as you suffer?! Is this some kind of stupid joke?! How many times do I have to do this?! Do you really not realize what I just did! I died and we returned! That’s what happened! It’s no longer just about you! It’s us! US! You fucking idiot!”

Subaru grit his teeth, “Even so…you can’t just throw away your life for nonsense. I had a plan. I was ready to distract her as long as possible so that you could figure out how to seal her. You didn’t need me. You could have done it all by yourself.”

Anastasia could feel her blood pressure spiking, “You are an idiot, aren’t you? What part of ‘it’s us,’ do you not understand? I don’t need you? I could do it all by myself? Sure. Yeah. I could. But what the fuck does that matter? None of it does if I don’t have you by my side. If you aren’t there, I could care less.”

“Ana that doesn’t make sense—”

“Nothing does!” Anastasia stepped towards him, making Subaru step back, “Logic died when we came to this tower and delved into each others memories. None of this makes any sense anymore! Everything about us is fucked beyond relief! We are not normal in any sense of the word! But that’s why I have to do this. I know you so well to the point that this is a necessity. I have to be as blunt and in your face as possible, because you are so dense and cursed with so much self-hatred that the only way to make you listen is to beat it into your stupid, stupid, skull! So let me make it clear, again. If you throw your life away, I will kill myself.”

Subaru’s eyes widened as he no doubt remembered that particular loop, “Stop—"

Anastasia grabbed his collar and pulled him close, she was glaring into his soul, “You don’t get to throw your life away just because you think it’s right. No one owns you. Not anymore. But we made a promise. Together, even in death. And what that means is that your life isn’t just yours anymore. It’s mine. Just like yours is mine, mine is in your hands. And that means you don’t get the right to throw it away without me. I killed myself? That’s because you threw away yours first. So let that be my only warning, Natsuki Subaru.”

“You—”

“Do you hear me?” Anastasia placed his hands on her throat, “This isn’t me just making a half-hearted statement or a joke or whatever! This isn’t like that stupid bullshit that one loop version of me told you. You and I are in the same boat. So, if you die, that means you’re responsible for killing me. And if that is the only way I can make you actually cherish your life, then so be it.”

“…” Subaru was stunned.

“…You’re not alone anymore. So please…stop acting like you are.”

She felt awful. She didn’t want to say this. She didn’t want to see Subaru’s eyes like this. She didn’t want him to be saddled with her insanity like this. She wanted them to be happy. She wanted Subaru to be a normal boy and she a normal girl. Together and able to make good memories until they grew old and wrinkly.

But they weren’t. They were far from normal. Broken and messed up from everything that had happened.

But that’s fine. Even if she can’t fix it all, she’ll mend his spirit with hers. She’ll make him value himself through her. And slowly, they’ll survive together.

“…Ana. I—” Subaru took his hands off her neck. His hand hovered near her cheeks before dropping to his sides, “I’m sorry. I thought…this was the best path. I didn’t think about how that would look to you and I didn’t think I had time to explain it all to you. I just…when I saw that hand nearly crush your face. All I could think about was making sure you were okay. I didn’t want to see you die. I couldn’t see that. If I saw you die again. I don’t…I wouldn’t…”

Subaru was on the verge of tears. And with it, brought her own, she put her hand on his and the other on his cheek, “I know. Trust me, I know. I felt the same. When I saw you going down there, all I could think about was being right beside you. I couldn’t bear the thought of you being in her grasp so…” she wiped a tear from his face. “I don’t want you to die anymore. I can’t stand it. I’ve seen it enough. I’m tired of watching you suffer and it made me so upset to know you might have to do it again that I just…I wasn’t thinking. I just had to take the fall for you, and I know how that sounds but it was either me or you. And…I would rather die than let you do it even one more time.”

“But that wasn’t something anyone should experience. No human should ever have to die and come back.”

“Aren’t you part of that?” Anastasia said, “Aren’t you human too?”

“…I don’t think I am anymore.”

“Then I’m not too.”

“You’re still human.”

“I’m not,” Anastasia shushed him, “You’ve seen what I am in here.” Her body glowed as the veil of white began to drape over her again, “I didn’t get this by being diplomatic or by being a merchant. By being compassionate. I became something irreversible. I can barely think rationally without you being next to me anymore.”

“…I’m sorry—”

“It’s not your fault. It was my choice. None of this is your fault. I chose to be here, with you. I chose to die before you. I chose to be by your side forever.”

“…”

“…Please don’t say you don’t deserve it. That I deserve better. That life was better before.”

“I’m sorry. Even after all of this time, I can’t help but think that…” he paused.

“What is it? Tell me.”

“It’s nothing.”

“It doesn’t seem like that.”

“It is. Just nonsense.”

“Please. Tell me.”

“…Even when you say these things. Even when you tell me how much you love me. And even when you did so much for me. There’s a disgusting, stupid voice in my head that keeps telling me…” Subaru looked like he was in pain to admit this, “…That it won’t be forever. That no matter how happy I am now. It always goes away.”

“…Subaru.”

“Stop. It’s stupid. I know it’s stupid. It isn’t realistic, it isn’t logical. It isn’t something that makes sense. It’s just a stupid fucking voice that I need to ignore,” Subaru tried to let go but Anastasia pulled him back.

Anastasia embraced him, “It’s real though. It’s normal to be afraid. It’s normal to have an irrational voice in your head, telling you that your worst fears will come to light.”

He let his arms loose, “…Is it? Is it normal to think that it will all come crashing down? That one day I’ll wake up and be back in a fucking prison? Is it normal? I don’t…I don’t think it is.”

“…Maybe there is no way for me to shut that voice up right now. I can’t think of anything to tell you that will settle those fears.”

“I see—”
“But that doesn’t mean I can’t physically show you,” Anastasia pulled back slightly to kiss him again.  She whispered into his ear, “Even if you can’t believe it at first, I’ll remind you, again and again. I’m real. You are here. You are safe. And I’ll never leave you behind. Happiness will never end. Maybe we will suffer, but I won’t ever disappear. That’s not just a promise. That’s an oath. A lifelong covenant. And I’ll tell you it, each time. I’ll always save you.”

He won’t have to save her or anyone else anymore.

No.

She would be the one to save him.

He shuddered, “Ana—”

“You don’t have to say anything. I know you want to tell me you believe in me. That my words made an impact on you. But it’s hard. I know. It’s hard to accept that things are okay, finally. But I don’t want you to lie that you are, when you aren’t. You don’t have to lie anymore while you’re near me. You can cry. You can be frustrated. You can be your worst self. I’ll accept it all.”

“…I love you,” Subaru said as dived into her mouth.

Anastasia accepted it wholeheartedly, taking a breath, “I love you too.”

Before indulging in each other as if their lives could end at any moment.

----------------------

“Anastasia-sama? Subaru-sama?” Geuse asked, “Are you both alright?”

Subaru and Anastasia looked at each other quickly to make sure there was nothing out of place. They tried not to blush and turned to Geuse, both saying, “Yeah.”

Geuse didn’t look like he believed them, “…Okay. Well, I wasn’t expecting you both back so soon. I assumed you would be taking care of business in the real world for a while.”

“That’s the thing. Your advice to look for Flugel’s archives wasn’t the best,” Anastasia tried to word it politely, “…He’s kind of stupid.”

She failed.

Thankfully, Geuse laughed, “Yes. Yes, he was. But despite such a personality, he was the wisest of us all.” Geuse looked slightly morose, “I’m sorry he wasn’t of use to you both.”

Subaru then chimed in, “Actually, he might still be. We found this amulet or artifact of his that looked like something from home.”

That got Geuse interested, “Oh really? What was it?”

Anastasia conjured the memory into her hand. She hung the ornament from its chain in front of Geuse and asked, “What do you know about the Taiji?”

Chapter 66: The World Over Heaven

Summary:

Time to learn and it's almost time to end this...

Notes:

(See the end of the chapter for notes.)

Chapter Text

Geuse frowned as he crept closer, his eyes analyzed the amulet slowly as if taking in all of its details. Silence crept around the Od World as Anastasia and Subaru stood motionless, waiting for Geuse to finish. Unfortunately, the two were still preoccupied with what happened just before, their eyes kept glancing at each other for anything odd.

Anastasia looked at Subaru’s clothes and saw a loose bit of purple hair on his shoulder. She frowned. She wanted to brush it off, but she had to stay still lest Geuse’s concentration was interrupted. It seemed Subaru noticed as his eyes drifted to where she stared.

He then smirked at her, making her raise an eyebrow. What was he—

Before she could even think, instead of raising his hand to pick out the stray hair, his fingers strayed to her head and delicately picked up the long strands. Anastasia realized she had not wrapped it back into a ponytail before seeing Subaru’s true purpose. He raised the end of her violet locks to his lips and gave it a chaste kiss, giving her a wink all the while.

It was stupid. It was dumb. It was something out of some romance novel.

But dear God did it make Anastasia blush wildly like a girl in puberty. What? She couldn’t help it. There was something about a man—especially the one you love— treating every part of you with care and affection that really got her heart racing. Maybe she was just a sucker for such notions or maybe it’s been so long since Subaru and her had any alone time but if Geuse wasn’t here, she would be jumping her husband right this second and dragging him to the nearest bed.

Unfortunately, she had to stay in place due to their current goals. And even more unfortunate, the little shit was smiling at her, fully knowing she couldn’t attack him back directly.

But Subaru was too shallow in his thinking.

She smiled back at him and used her free hand to brush her hair behind her ear and lower the collar of her kimono slightly: revealing the mark he had left her right near her collarbone. She then pointed to her lips and mouthed a few words to him that he would assuredly understand.

And he did, given he started to blush furiously, even more than she did. Dumbass. She knew his preferences inside and out.

“Would you both please stop flirting while I am working?” Geuse stared at them both.

Anastasia and Subaru nearly stumbled in place, both now red with embarrassment.

“S-sorry!” “M-my bad, Geuse!”

Geuse sighed, “I swear, if it isn’t you, it’s Greed and Gluttony.”

Subaru raised an eyebrow about that, “Are they causing trouble?”

“…Depends on what you call trouble,” Geuse finally looked away and stood up.

“What have they done?” Anastasia asked.

“What haven’t they done…” Geuse mumbled.

“Will you just give us a straight answer?!”

“Fine!” Geuse’s temper won out, “They’ve been all over each other since the moment you two left!”

“…Like they’re fighting?” Subaru asked blankly.

Geuse’s expression shifted to discomfort, “If it was just fighting, I would not be complaining.”

Subaru and Anastasia looked at each other and then at Geuse. It clicked for Anastasia faster than Subaru, “Ohhhhhh, yeah no, that tracks.”

“What tracks?” Subaru glanced at Anastasia.

Some pink returned to Anastasia’s cheeks as she explained, “Well if we’re…like this. Then what do you think the copies of us who are the epitome of our greedy and gluttonous desires would be like?”

Subaru blinked, “…Oh fuck.”

Anastasia nodded, “Exactly.”

Subaru rubbed his neck sheepishly, “I mean, is it really that bad—”

“It’s bad, Subaru-sama,” Geuse stared him down. “I have barely got any peace while those two have been either bickering or laying hands on each other every second. I can’t even separate them because Gluttony often threatens me with, and I quote, groin dismemberment.”

Subaru grimaced while Anastasia nodded with understanding, “That makes sense. If anyone tried to do the same to me, I would also make them become a eunuch.”

Geuse looked at Anastasia like she was insane before turning his head and smiling at Subaru, “Besides how psychotic Gluttony is—”

“Hey!” Anastasia grumbled.

“—I believe I may be able to give you an answer regarding this Taiji.”

Subaru and Anastasia stood in rapt attention to Geuse’s words. He spoke slowly, “First, what do you know about the symbol, Subaru-sama?”

“Not much besides what I read on Wikipedia and in a book once. Taiji was about unity of yin and yang and having opposites work in harmony. But that’s really all I know.”

Anastasia raised her hand, “Couldn’t we just bring up the memory of you reading those? It may help.”

“Not necessarily,” Geuse said. “While yes, we would gain better understanding of the Taiji from Subaru-sama’s world, that isn’t why I asked such a question. The Taiji was a concept that Flugel-sama theorized through his studies of magic with Echidna-sama. While combining magic was not fundamentally new, he wondered if there was a way to combine the mana itself. Such as putting fire mana and water mana together. Of course, what would usually occur is that the mana would either bounce off each other, negate the other, or fundamentally fizzle out. To have two particles of mana existing in the same space would be impossible.”

They both nodded.

“So what did they do? Did they ever figure it out?” Subaru asked.

Geuse shook his head, “I don’t know. From how Flugel-sama would talk about such experiments with great annoyance, it seemed they weren’t able to learn how to replicate it in humans. However, Echidna-sama did theorize that maybe spirits would be different.”

Anastasia connected the dots, “Beatrice and Eridna!”

Geuse nodded, “You thought correctly. While they were not made by Echidna-sama for such a purpose, she had hoped that her copy would eventually possess a Yin user and be able to unionize the two different mana types in some capacity.”

“So, she was meant to be like a clone,” Subaru pointed out. He always had a theory that Echidna was trying to cheat death in some way. It would explain why there was a version of her in the Castle of Dreams while her real self was still dead.

“Yes and no,” Geuse began to explain, “The one you call Eridna was meant to be an experiment for two purposes: a possible way to resurrect her mind and body and a way for her to extend her bloodline.”

Subaru blinked, “Wait, you’re saying…she wanted kids?”

Geuse looked away, “Again, yes and no. Echidna-sama was never direct about her emotions besides her desire for knowledge, but she was someone who valued family and love. Even if she was unable to understand it naturally.”

Subaru was shaken by such a notion, “I just can’t imagine it. She’s…well—”
“A sociopath with a learning fetish,” Anastasia finished for him.

“Yeah that.”

Despite how rude she was acting, Geuse laughed at her words, “An apt description for Echidna-sama. In many ways, you are very similar to her, Anastasia-sama.”

“That is not a compliment,” Anastasia felt revulsion from such a comparison.

“I didn’t mean for it to be.”

Anastasia’s eye twitched, “I’m nothing like her!”

“You do hold some key differences. Unlike her, you hold great love and care for the people around you. Additionally, you wouldn’t manipulate or try to use the people you love for purposes other than care and concern. And finally, your greed may be bottomless, but you are more attached to relationships compared to her.”

Anastasia grumbled, “So what’s so similar then?”

“You both would become a Witch for a single person.”

“…Who?”

Geuse smiled, “Unfortunately, I won’t answer that question. It is too personal and it is not relevant to our discussion.”

Anastasia’s head hurt from such a revelation. The idea that Echidna, a vile woman who was one of the most cruel Witches she had ever witnessed, had similar motivations to Anastasia was nauseating. A part of her didn’t want to accept it.

So, she chose to move on, “So why was the Taiji so important for him to make a medallion out of it? And why did Pandora call me the Mother of the Taiji?”

Geuse took a deep breath before explaining more, “This may all be hypothesis, but I believe Flugel-sama was interested in its harmonic power. Two opposite energies, purely mixing into something stable could have so many possibilities. Flugel hoped it would revolutionize magic in the future. The medallion must be all that’s left of those experiments. Perhaps it will have use if you were to use both Yin and Yang on it at the same time. As for Pandora…have you both considered why she wanted you both in the first place?”

“I always thought she wanted new Archbishops. Given the fact we kind of killed two of them, I assumed she just wanted to recruit us to bolster her forces,” Subaru shrugged.

“That would make sense, but I have another theory. It’s possible…she saw the future that you both could pave and found it tantalizing. A future where your offspring inherited your new Gates and were able to make the fantastical idea of the Taiji into a reality.”

“…Geuse. What are you trying to say? I thought our Gates were normal now,” Subaru was nervous.

“Subaru-sama. You both linked your souls together in the most unnatural way possible. There was no possibility your Gates would work normally. The fact that they were fused through an Authority has made the impossible, possible now.” Geuse saw their expressions and sighed, “I’m suggesting that it’s highly likely you both are now the only users who can combine Yin and Yang magic into a new form: Taiji.”

“…” Anastasia was stunned again. Despite this, she had enough mental capacity to say, “At least it’s better than Yin-Yang magic.”

Subaru shook his head, “Okay. But how do we even know that this is even possible? This is all theory. We haven’t tested any of it.”

“Well, why not try?” Geuse waved his hand at the world around them. “This environment is tailored towards you both. A sort of reality within your souls that replicates everything, even down to lost hair follicles. I would suggest trying out some spells.”

Anastasia thought for a moment before conjuring a memory of the wooden practice dummies Julius would use for training. Three wooden human figures on posts appeared out of thin air a couple meters away.

“Alright, let’s try,” Anastasia pointed her finger at the doll and shuddered as she said, “Jamak!”

…Nothing happened.

“Pfft!” Subaru couldn’t help but chuckle, making Anastasia whip her head at him and stormed over, poking his sides. “Hey, hey, hey! Stop!”

“You try it this time!” She said while pouting.

Subaru continued to laugh as he pointed his hand out and said, “Jamak!”

…Nothing happened again.

“Pfft!” Anastasia laughed as Subaru ignored her. Thinking for a moment, he then cried out, “Shamak!”

A blast of shadows pushed out of his palm into the realm of white. It stayed there for a second before Subaru said, “Jiwald!”

A beam of light shot out of his palm and pierced through the shadows.

“Shamak! Jiwald! Shamak! Jiwald!” Repeating each incantation, a cycle of darkness and light formed and dissipated out of his hand every second.

Subaru panted before shouting, “Sha—wald!” Interrupting the incantation with the second spell.

This time, the shadows coalesced in his hand for a second before immediately being replaced with a shot of pure light.

Subaru groaned, “Goddamnit! Yeah, I don’t think we can do it like that.”

But it did give Anastasia an idea as she walked forward. Thinking back to her lessons with Beatrice, she remembered how the little spirit told her to use her imagination when processing the mana for a spell. Because her Gate was connected to her Od and thus had a connection between her soul and mind, there was an indirect connection between how she interpreted the spell and how it materialized through reality.

She stood next to Subaru as she imagined the two different mana types: Yin and Yang. If she were to interpret them as two separate populations of particles in her body, then wouldn’t it be possible for her to use both spells at the same time? The reason why Beatrice was able to combine them so easily was because she has incredible control over both mana and her Gate. However, Anastasia was a human. Her control over mana was limited due to her lackluster experience. But this meant she had no limitations on what was possible and impossible.

Experienced mages often were too narrow-minded. Years of trial and error obfuscating the simplest answers to their complex solution. There was a similar problem in any profession, merchants included. Anastasia herself had fallen into the hole of increasing complexity when something more mundane could be much more effective. That was why she imagined them as two populations that existed next to each other. Both manifested through her Gate.

Using these two populations, she sent Yin to one hand and the Yang to the other. Casting both spells at the same time needed incredible concentration but it was enough. Within one second of casting, a beam of light burst from her left finger and a blast of shadows from her right.

“Alright! That’s my Ana-pop!” Subaru gave her a thumbs up and a wide smile.

Smiling at her success she moved onto the thought experiment Beatrice suggested. She imagined the two populations rapidly shooting at each other, the particles of Yin and Yang bouncing off each other with increasing velocity. She didn’t have two Gates like a possessed Beatrice did so she had to make do with their combined one. However, the more she did , the more a heat began to build up in her body. Slowly, she could feel sweat seeping out of her skin and her vision began to get blurry. The particles were colliding constantly, creating more and more energy—
Before she could react, a small explosion sent her flying to the ground.

“Ana!” Subaru flew to her side and helped her sit up, “What the hell happened?”

Coughing up smoke, her voice was raspy, “I almost got it to work. But there was too much energy build up.”

Beatrice warned her about this but apparently the little spirit had no problems keeping up with it. Was it because she had a body made out of mana? That would be the only thing that could make sense. Their bodies could handle excess amounts of energy and therefore heat because they barely cared if it was hot or cold!  But she was a human, too much heat may lead her to overload. She was lucky all it did was create a small explosion.

Hold on. Currently, Anastasia was just a soul, wasn’t she? She shouldn’t be sweating, feeling heat, or even feeling pain.

She pinched herself and felt a small microcosm of pain run through her nerves. That was new. So was that feeling of heat. She looked around at the black and white world and realized that though the environment was largely the same, there were some small changes. For one, there was a breeze.

Anastasia didn’t know from where, but she could feel a wind drift through her scalp. She just didn’t realize it. She also didn’t realize that her body was now able to feel small bits of pain. And that explosion. The sensations she felt when coming back—especially when it was not paired with Basiliskos. The…senses she experienced with Subaru.

This Od World was changing, and it was as if it was becoming a some sort of pseudo-reality. But why? It should just be a replica of their memories.

She grasped her hand back and forth and thought long and hard about the possible reasons. It could be because this world was a direct product of their Authorities, that it would change along with their desires. Their Witch Factors could get stronger, right? Then that would mean the byproducts of those Authorities would be affected as well. It would explain a lot…

But not everything.

She manifested the amulet in her hand. Raising it up and letting its odd design flicker side to side in front of her eyes. She saw that its dual nature mirrored the world around them. Black and white. She frowned. This…was it all a coincidence?

Taiji. The Od World. Subaru and Anastasia’s whole journey. Satella’s behavior with her. Flugel’s familiar mannerisms. Everything.

There was an answer formulating in Anastasia’s head. And it wasn’t a pretty one.

“Ana?” She felt Subaru’s hand on hers. Without answering him verbally, she simply nuzzled her head onto his shoulder, sighing as his arm then wrapped around her body.

Even if the answer was uncomfortable, it was still worth asking the question.

“Geuse?” Anastasia closed her eyes as she felt Subaru’s warmth permeate through her body.

“Yes, Anastasia-sama?” Geuse materialized behind them.

“…Was this all planned?”

“What do you mean?” Geuse sounded confused but there was a hint of something there. Whether it was dread or anticipation, Anastasia could not know.

Did she really want to know the answer? “Just tell me one thing. Was Flugel…similar to anyone you currently know?”

“…”

No answer. She could feel Subaru swallow a dry cough next to her. There was no way that he wasn’t also thinking the same thing. During their quick read of Flugel’s diary, she remembered how Subaru reacted. How his eyes glanced at the handwriting and how he had to look at her for confirmation. She recognized the handwriting too. Because it was all she saw during her time in Banan in the last few months. The same handwriting as all those notes he gave her way back when.

“Geuse—”

“I don’t know. And that isn’t something that I can’t say under oath. My…memories. There are areas that are foggy. And one of those is how Flugel appears to me. When I imagine his voice, his face, and his mannerisms. I can vaguely tell you his characteristics but nothing specific. It’s as if I am slowly forgetting him despite how impossible that is. A part of me wants to answer your question with the answer you seek but the doubt that currently grips my soul. I…do not wish to give you false information. Especially when it comes to someone very important to me,” Geuse’s voice was trembling. “I am sorry Anastasia-sama. Truly. But know this, I am not guiding you to a predetermined destination. This is all new to me. This ‘Mother of Taiji,’ I do not believe Flugel knew about it.”

“…But what about Echidna?” Anastasia asked.

“That—” Geuse paused, “She might know something about that. The knowledge she knows of both the future and past is vast. If there is anyone who could know of what Pandora speaks of, it’s her.”

“I see,” she grabbed Subaru’s hand. “Then we’ll have to go find her after all of this is done.”

She opened her eyes and stood up. Looking at Subaru, his expression was filled with contemplation. She could guess all of his emotions in a blink of an eye. Guilt, irritation, confusion, and slow unsettling acceptance in his gut. She put her hand on his cheek and pulled his attention towards him, “No matter what happened in the past or what happens in the future. You’re still my Subaru.”

She smiled at him as sincerely as possible.

And though he faltered for a second, he couldn’t help but smile back, “I guess that makes you my Ana-pop then.”

Even as he said that, Anastasia noticed his lips waver. Subaru was still scared. Maybe this whole time. Ever since they met again, he’s been scared. If it was the version of her from before, she would say it was just paranoia caused by him being abandoned by his campmates. But with all she knew about his life. The answer was more complex.

Fear of losing everything because of his power.

Fear of losing his sanity when all hope was lost.

Fear of being alone.

These were all things Anastasia experienced herself and more. And she was sure Subaru himself had processed all these emotions. Time after time. She’d seen him regress in both time and emotion. He had relied on the people he loved and when he needed them most—through no fault of their own—they couldn’t save him. The certainty he had grown comfortable with, failed him due to bad luck.

People needed certainty. They needed a stable pillar in their lives to latch onto. It’s why humans sought out relationships. As social creatures, humans couldn’t help but attach themselves to the first people they could rely on. Because otherwise…the anxiety and fear of living was too much to bear.

For Anastasia and Subaru, it was their respective camps.

Losing the people they loved made their hearts vulnerable. So, they latched onto each other. But when Anastasia saw that Subaru was in an unreachable spot—her body panicked. Her mind could not handle that reality. At least until she was given the certainty of happiness from Pandora.

But Subaru did not have that. He still had the shadow of the Witch hanging over his shoulder. He still did not believe they could be happy together. Because he had long accepted that happiness was not eternal, so long as he existed as Natsuki Subaru.

But that’s fine.

The world—the very present they live in—was an impossibility. And yet, it still occurred. They were still here. Together. Despite all that could have happened. To Anastasia, impossibility was simply a hurdle to find a way around. Something to either persuade. Or kill.

No matter the cost, she would find a way to kill that fear. Even if it meant killing the Witch of Envy herself.

She squeezed Subaru’s hand and aimed her free one at the dummies in front of her. But first, she would have to figure out how the Taiji could help them—

Without even casting, her finger shot out a burst of white and black energy that slowed right before impact.

And created an enormous explosion, annihilating all the dummies in one second.

Anastasia blinked several times before turning to Subaru, “Did you do that?”

Subaru also blinked rapidly, before shaking his head the same amount of times, “Nope. Did you?”

Anastasia looked around, trying to find what was so different to cause such a reaction. Even Geuse looked befuddled. It wasn’t until she looked down that she realized what had happened.

Their hands—linked together—were brimming with energy.

-------------------------

It’s been a long week for Halibel, the Admirer.

Halibel shrugged, “Sure I have a hundred and one questions. But it doesn’t seem like it would be safe for ya and Su-san to explain it all to me. Maybe one day, but I’m satisfied with just knowin’ ya both are safe. That’s all I need right now.”

“Thanks again Hal. We’re really grateful to have met ya,” Anastasia replied softly.

He took a deep breath of his kiseru, “I could say the same.”

Because he really was grateful. Ever since he began living with the two of them as a bodyguard, he had been blessed with fun and entertainment near daily. It was something he began to cherish in the short time he had known them. And his care for both of them grew even more as he not only remembered Anastasia fully but also learned more about Subaru’s past.

To Halibel, these two had become incredibly important to him—far beyond their roles as his contractors. So having the two be separated and go through turmoil, both emotional and physical, was agonizing to deal with.

So now, after what felt like months of pain and suffering (though it really was just one week), Halibel could happily say that things were finally starting to look up—

Anastasia fell to the ground, panting.

Halibel was immediately alert and checking her for any wounds, “Ana-bo, what’s wrong?”

Anastasia didn’t answer as she caught her breath and quickly got to her feet. Before sprinting immediately at Subaru. Halibel was too shocked by her actions to realize that Subaru was also sprinting at Anastasia with a serious expression.

Running at each other at top speeds—with Beatrice confused and hanging onto Subaru’s arm for dear life—the two each raised a hand and high fived each other, wrapping their fingers together. They then both lifted their free hands to the sky before screaming, “EL JAMAK!”

A burst of light and darkness surged from both their hands and combined into one large pillar of energy, shooting through the roof and causing explosions throughout the tower. Halibel blinked in horror and surprise before muttering, “Did they just use Yin-Yang magic?”

The two then separated, Subaru running towards Halibel while Anastasia ran towards the exit. He then watched as Anastasia almost tripped as she turned her head, still sprinting in the same direction, “SUBARU! You forgot to give me Betty!”
“Shit!” Subaru stopped in his tracks and twisted his body while raising Beatrice in his hand. “Sorry Beako! Don’t cry!”

“Wait, what—AHHHHHH!” Beatrice screamed as she was tossed by Subaru, spinning in the air rapidly before being caught by Anastasia, who rolled on the ground and then immediately went back to sprinting like her life depended on it.

Halibel could barely comprehend what just happened as Subaru ran to his side, panting and out of breath, “Su-san. What was that—”

Subaru then raised a finger and took in a deep breath, “…”

“Uh.”

A large object rocketed through the floor and up towards the ceiling at a high velocity, making Halibel jump as he recognized the form and hair color of said object. Was that the Sword Saint?

“REINHARD READ MY MIND RIGHT NOW!” Subaru screamed with all his might as Reinhard shunted past them into the sky.

Halibel was just about to lose his mind when Subaru jumped into his arms, making the poor wolfman nearly have a panic attack, as Subaru hugged him for dear life, “HALIBEL GO UP NOW! GO, GO, GO, GO!”

“I­—uh, why?” He asked as Halibel still did what he was told, jumping rapidly off the walls to get as vertically high as possible.

Subaru answered by pointing downward multiple times with what could only be described as an expression of pure fear and adrenaline. Halibel looked down and could barely keep his composure any longer as he saw the Witch of Envy barreling towards them from the basement with millions of shadowy tendrils flying at him.

…This week was going to get worse, wasn’t it?
