Chapter 67: Into Hell, Into Heaven, Together

Summary:

It's time for the end...and a new beginning.

Notes:

(See the end of the chapter for notes.)

Chapter Text

Halibel, the Admirer.

Some may say that his life was something others could only dream of. The strongest of Kararagi and someone who was beloved by his people. Whether that was the nation he represented or the tribe he came from, both respected him for all he had done. And Halibel had pride for all his life accomplished. So much so that he had little regrets where his path took him. For despite his shortcomings and despite where he currently was, he was satisfied.

And yet…Halibel had become bored.

It wasn’t to say that his life had suddenly took a downturn. Rather, his life had become too monotonous. Despite the odd job or difficult assassination request here and there, Halibel had grown accustomed to his daily routine. Work, sleep, and laze around when he can. It was something that anyone would envy if instability was their daily life and yet…perhaps Halibel had craved the return to such roots.

An insane concept, but a real one to Halibel. He did not want to be bored but it was something he had to deal with constantly. His life had become too consistent. A fact that he despised, albeit not outwardly.

Boredom meant peace. And peace was good.

Compared to the constant turmoil and anxieties he felt in his early life, this was a marked improvement. To live as a man who only had to accomplish his duties, was something he could barely imagine in his youth. Because when the wolfmen were despised, when his heritage was a shadow that covered the futures of all his brethren, his only thought was paving the way.

Responsibility was all Halibel knew. And it was a flag he wore on his sleeves and back with passion and prestige.

And yet, again, he had become bored.

Perhaps that was why he had become much pickier with the jobs he chose. Before he would take any and all jobs to prove his worth as not only an assassin but also as a wolf human. This was done to spread his fame throughout the world to prove his heritage had value and to stand proud as the wolfmen’s spokesperson. But nowadays, he does not have to do much. His name was already known across the four nations, and his actions were slowly healing their reputation.

Now it was just a matter of time. Of waiting. For both assassins and pathfinders, the hardest part was waiting. Because unfortunately, the greatest force of the universe was time. You cannot reverse it, forward it, or pause it. All you could do was wait as your actions slowly took effect. Like a slow acting poison.

So Halibel waited, doing what he could before his life inevitably would end through a fatal job or at its natural demise. He waited and watched. And admired.

Until one fateful day when a young man entered the bar he was drinking in. When he was at the height of boredom and was ready to go on a trip to a foreign land based off a request from the council. A young man approached him with a smile and an extended hand. At first Halibel was amused by his audacity, but on a closer look, his curiosity was piqued. The young man was…damaged.

Halibel knew victims of war as well as he knew victims of abuse—scarred from years of inhumane trauma that could barely be comprehended through a single conversation. It was something any veteran could notice when they looked into the victim’s eyes. Because all you could see was a reflection of the void—where death and pain became so consistent, that all they could see were the remnants of it in the world around them.

And yet, Natsuki Subaru was both this and none of this. He was someone whose body was riddled with scars, his hair bleached from stress, and his general demeanor suggested constant anxiety and awareness that could make a soldier wracked with pity at such a sight. But within his eyes held no void. No, it held something familiar.

Responsibility.

Perhaps that was why Halibel humored him, making a bet to satiate his curiosity. To see what this young man had in store for him and whether he could relieve the boredom that made up Halibel’s normal days.

And boy, was Halibel’s instincts proven true each time. Whether it was summoning a literal monster with just a word or having said monster’s bloodthirsty lookalike as an ally, there was nothing short of excitement for Halibel ever since he met Natsuki Subaru. And with that excitement, brought understanding.

They had only spent a few months together and yet within that short amount of time, he had become incredibly close with not only Subaru, but all those he met afterward. Anastasia, Zarestia, Beatrice, Eridna, and even Patrasche. Each one he admired for their individuality and the entertainment they brought into his life.

He enjoyed sneaking the black earth dragon some snacks while he quietly napped near her stable. He enjoyed poking fun at the two artificial spirits, enjoying the heated reactions of the child and the colder yet warm reactions of the fox. He enjoyed banter with the murder spirit and the quiet mutual respect they had for each others’ skills. He enjoyed Anastasia’s wit and tenacity, her acumen with business was as sharp as her tongue, and yet he couldn’t help but admire the soft kindness that lay in her heart. He enjoyed Subaru’s frankness and shamelessness, his bravery was as bold as his desires, and yet he couldn’t help but admire the hardened resolve that lay in his soul.

And yet, and yet, and yet!

Halibel couldn’t help but go on and on about such aspects. For Halibel was already satisfied with his life, not craving anything more than what was needed. Which was why he couldn’t help but feel grateful for the blessings that were given to him without him ever asking.

Blessings that came in the form of people.

He enjoyed watching Subaru and Anastasia grow closer, the two hopelessly bound at the hip, and found satisfaction in watching their romance blossom. It was as if he was witnessing a tale from his childhood! He watched them struggle with their emotions, fight endlessly because of their differences, and survive hand in hand due to the bond they shared. He loved watching their story unfold and it was why Halibel couldn’t help but admire them.

He admired them because a part of him couldn’t help but see his own life reflected. To see Subaru struggle with a responsibility he could never fully articulate, brought empathy to Halibel’s soul. To see Anastasia struggle with her desires versus her commitments, brought clarity to Halibel’s heart. The two were a matchmade in hell, opposing in so many aspects, fundamentally different in almost every possible way. And yet…he wanted to see them succeed.

Perhaps it was because of the boredom. Or perhaps it was because Halibel had grown to cherish them. Or perhaps it was because of his admiration of all things.

Either way, he wanted to see the two happy together. He wanted them to have their happy ending.

Which was why Halibel took his role as their protector so seriously. He was already the type to hold his contracts as the highest priority, but the underlying reasons simply motivated him more. He trusted them both and he trusted Subaru the most. Because that young man looked upon Anastasia and all he cared about like how Halibel gazed upon his brethren. Not an obligation born out of blood but born out of genuine love and loyalty.

So, when Subaru jumped into his arms and asked him to climb, he did.

When Subaru’s ability transferred all the necessary information to his brain in a single moment, he did not reject.

And when they burst through several floors and arrived in a beautiful landscape with clouds, trees, and prairies all around them, he did not hesitate to raise his kunai against one of the most powerful men in history.

Reid Astrea.

“Hm? A weakling and a furball, ay?” Reid said as he scratched his chin. “Tch. Not a babe in sight. Were you both the reason for all that commotion downstairs?”

Halibel was ready to create an opening, possibly shunt a clone with Subaru up to the next area, when his ward said something that caught him and Reid off guard. Subaru held out the odd necklace they found and exclaimed, “Reid Astrea! You are hereby relinquished from your role as test examiner.”

…Huh?

Reid was doubly confused, “What the hell are ya on about pipsqueak—”

“Satella is out of her box. This is an SSS-class danger level. Code word—” Subaru shuddered for a second, “…Echidna was right.”

Reid’s confusion morphed into realization as his eye went blank for a second. His conscience returned immediately after with a grin and a crack of the neck, “So it’s this timeline, ay? How fun.”

Halibel looked between the two with increasing confusion. Subaru looked back at Halibel with exasperation and a silent message through Basiliskos.

Trust me. This is the easiest solution. Everything else sucked.

Subaru said no more through their connection. Subaru then spoke quickly, “If you could provide us at least fifteen minutes, that should be enough.”

Reid rolled his shoulder, “Yeah, yeah. Don’t think you can order me around, pipsqueak. This is just because Satella-chan is a higher priority than beating you both into submission. Oi, furball, hand me your sword.”

Halibel glanced over to Subaru who nodded before throwing the one on his belt over, “Careful. Don’t cut yerself.”

Reid snickered, “Ya got a loyal dog, don’t ya pipsqueak.”

Reid drew the sword and admired it for just a second, before practicing a swing to his side.

Within half a second, a large crevice erupted from where he swung­—carving a manmade valley into the room— nearly causing Halibel to grab Subaru and run but his ward’s cool expression calmed him down. Reid smiled viciously at their reactions and said, “Seems there’s more to you than just being a weakling, pipsqueak.”

“Are you going to help us or not?” Subaru asked.

“Yeah, yeah, just testin’ out the sword was all. Shitty but it would have to do,” Reid tried to walk by them and reach the opening they made in the ground earlier. Only for Subaru to say something that nearly stopped Halibel’s heart.

“Don’t touch Ana.”

“Hm? The fuck you say pipsqueak?” Reid turned his head and glared.

“I said, if you touch a girl with purple hair on any part of her body. I will fucking murder you,” Subaru doubled down while glaring back just as fiercely.

The two continued their stare off and Halibel was ready to create as many clones as possible to attack Reid from all angles. Until Reid began to laugh, “…You really do remind me of him. You’re the exact same. Though I guess your hair is a bit different.”

Subaru raised an eyebrow, but Reid didn’t elaborate, merely jumping backwards and into the hole while shouting, “If ya survive, come find me. I’ll beat you to death like old times.”

“Absolutely not!” Subaru sighed, facepalming, “I really hate that guy. It could have been that easy this entire goddamn time?!”

Halibel was about to ask how Subaru knew to do all that when—

Shadows began rupturing through the room, breaking through the blue sky and grassy plains and covering the miniature world in darkness. Halibel rushed fast, grabbing Subaru and looking for a way upward. Unfortunately, no stairway or ladder materialized so he had to get creative. Creating several clones, he had a lightweight one get launched into the air as far as possible, right when a shadow hand grabbed onto his foot.

Halibel smiled, “Too slow.”

Using his shinobi technique combined with a curse on the lightweight clone, he switched places with it, sending him flying into the sky but nowhere close to the next floor. He continued making clones and having them continuously launch themselves further and further upward. But it was too slow and the process brought little space between them and the shadows, which were getting more and more furious as they tried to climb over each other to reach him and Subaru.

Halibel thought quickly and found the only worthwhile solution.

Wait, no!

If ya have somethin’, better. I’m all ears.

…Hal you could die.

Emphasis on could.

No. You WILL die. You can’t. Please.

…Su-san. Do ya trust me?

What kind of question is that? Of course I do.

Then bet on me. Bet on my survival.

…

Come on. Weren’t ya the one who claimed ya would win our bet, 100%, when we first met?

Hal. I-I don’t think I can do that anymore. There’s too many possibilities. We have too little time and I can’t—it’s impossible.

Su-san. Nothin’ is impossible, when it comes to ya.

Calming down a murderous Shinigami spirit? Most people would call you insane. And yet, he had done so.

Getting together with your absolute opposite? Many people would call you naïve. And yet, he had done so.

Time reversal? Halibel would call you crazy. But he had a guess that a certain someone could prove—and has proven—him wrong.

Believe in me. Just like I believe in ya.

…Don’t die Hal. Please.

Course. It’s my responsibility as yer bodyguard to see our contract through. Still gotta couple of years on that left and I’d hate ta leave it high and dry.

Halibel could hear Subaru laugh through their connection. An odd thing what an Authority could do. Halibel didn’t exactly have a conversation but had all of this information transferred into his skull lightning fast. All of which he interpreted through Subaru’s presence.

Like a warm summer night, where you peer up at a cloudless sky and see seven shimmering stars, guiding your path in the vast void of the infinite. Incomprehensible, and yet, a lifelong friend that’s always near.

See you soon, Hal.

…See ya later, Su-san.

And with that, Halibel sent Subaru flying as high up as he could with a clone meant to send him the rest of the way through. Halibel could have went with him but his added weight and trying to protect Subaru at the same time would have cost them too dearly. Now, free to do as he pleased, he could fight at full capacity.

Halibel held out several kunai in each hand and smiled at the monster below him: sparks and flashes of light were all that he could see of Reid Astrea’s battle with Satella below. How terrifying. How exciting. This could be his last mission.

However, he had a responsibility to survive. And Halibel wasn’t one to shirk his duties.

-----------------------------

Zarestia, the Most Beautiful Shinigami, was annoyed.

First, her two favorite humans abandoned her with all the annoying humans and didn’t even tell her how long they would be gone.

Second, she had to stay in this annoying room with an annoying spirit that wasn’t even a good conversation partner.

Third, she couldn’t even kill one of the humans that smelled like disgusting liquor because, unfortunately, he was one of Subaru’s favorite humans. And she couldn’t kill him because it would make Subaru sad.

Even though technically that one and the yellow haired one were part of the reasons why Subaru was hurt in the first place, she had to reign in her bloodlust because, unfortunately, Subaru was stupid and didn’t want to kill the people who hurt him.

He was lucky Anastasia was better at that aspect than him.

Speaking of Anastasia, her humans were better. Though the dog reminded her of the mutt, and the purple one was too bright, she at least liked the little ones. Their cheeks were squishy and she spent most of her time poking them. She now understood why Anastasia liked pinching little Beatrice’s cheeks all the time.

Fourth, she wasn’t able to kill the two fuckers who made her two favorite humans go through hell and was already itching to hunt them down and make mincemeat out of their corpses.

Fifth, she was kind of bored and there was nothing to kill but time.

Which was why she was very happy when Anastasia came running back with little Beatrice and the purple one in tow, screaming incoherently about some Witch or whatever. It didn’t matter. Little Beatrice was now forced to take care of the ingrates and teleport them outside the tower and keep them safe from all the Witchbeasts along with Echidna the fox.

The purple one tried to argue with Anastasia but with a swift punch to the gut and hit of the neck, he was out cold. Anastasia yelled at Zarestia for nonsensical reasons but she immediately shut up when Zarestia grabbed her and began flying through the tower.

Finally, she was able to relieve some of that pent up bloodlust.

Unfortunately, it really only involved holding Anastasia—in a comfortable position because apparently holding her only by her leg was really uncomfortable—and shredding through a mountain of shadows in an effort to get Anastasia up to the highest point of the tower. Fairly simple. She just made an air bubble and had her wind blades constantly tearing through everything around her as they flew.

The only annoying part was Anastasia’s stare, “What?”

Anastasia took a deep breath, “…Once we get up there, I’m going to need you to trust me—”

“No.”

“Because it’s really important and I understand you may not—”

“No.”

“…Can you—”
“No.”

“Can you say literally anything else but no?!”

“Sure,” Zarestia turned her head to Anastasia. “Nope.”

“Why?!”

“Because it hasn’t even been three days since you went batshit insane and made Su sad. Of course, you did return to normal sanity and even better sanity now, but that’s beside the point.”

“Better sanity?” Anastasia questioned.

Zarestia shrugged, “You’re no longer holding back. I like it.”

Anastasia sighed, “Why are you always like this?”

“Because it’s funny,” Zarestia shrugged again. “And because you calm down and focus.”

“Wait—what?”

“You get angry. And then you focus better,” Zarestia said as if it was obvious. Because it was, “It worked before and it would work again. Like now”

“…I hate you,” Anastasia grumbled and pouted. Zarestia smiled because it was already working. “Seriously, every time.”

When Anastasia arrived at the Green Room, it looked like she had seen a ghost or something. Zarestia did not know why Anastasia was acting like that, but she didn’t like it. Nor did she like how the girl was trembling in her hands or how she was panicking while telling Beatrice the exact coordinates to teleport the others to.

She did not understand the reasoning—and didn’t really want to—but that did not mean she didn’t care. She cared for her two favorite humans. And little Beatrice and her artificial sister. And the mutt. Sometimes. Not all the time but every other week, at least.

…It had been so long since she last felt anything other than bloodlust. To Zarestia, time had taken its toll on her. She had lived for so many years as a bloodthirsty reaper that it was all she ever knew.

And she had no desire to change that. She liked how she was. Up until she met these two. They were frail, emotional, idiotic, and weak as hell. But they were also fun, warm, and compassionate. She liked being near them. She liked watching them. And she liked living in Banan with them.

To the point that when she got her ball back, all she could feel was relief…and sadness. A distinct desire that she didn’t know would persist. A desire to stay by their side even though she knew every fiber of her being wanted to slice them into ribbons. But she didn’t want to kill them. It was paradoxical. To Zarestia, it would be impossible for her to live with them.

…But she wanted to try. She really did. She had been trying her best, repressing as much as she could and going on nighttime excursions to relieve her wrathful desires. A part of her hated it. It felt like she was wearing a mask and restricting her own freedoms. All of which had previously disgusted her about humanity.

And yet, she couldn’t help but enjoy the love they gave her. It reminded her of the two dumbasses from the past. Whose names she had forgotten but the emotions they imprinted on her had lasted as long as the burning rage that drove her very being. It had always saddened her that she forgot so much in so little time.

But yesterday was no longer today. Tomorrow was no longer a distant morning. The present was her choice and how she lived was her decision. Whether it would be filled with regret or bloodshed, would be hers to bear. To live with a mask was maddening, but so was her decision to live amongst humans.

Perhaps she was mad. Perhaps the past would repeat once more. But it does not matter either way. Even if change was an impossibility, she would rather try and fail than let her happiness burn away again. Their lives were limited. They would soon pass like any storm. But Zarestia would not forget their names, like the world once did.

Nor will she let them forget hers, so long as they lived.

Which was why when Zarestia felt her connection to Subaru flare up, she could barely keep her bloodlust in check. Funny enough, she could feel someone else’s bloodlust spike almost to her level, paired with a hand that gripped her kimono fiercely as they both looked upward.

She could feel the shadows working hard to pierce her ball of wind. It was slowing them down extensively. Zarestia didn’t need to think twice.

“Ana.”

Anastasia turned her head to Zarestia who asked, “You have an actual plan?”

Anastasia paused for one second before answering, “It’ll be a gamble. But we have no other options. If you can get me up there, I’ll be able to catch up with Subaru and we can finish this once and for all.”

“Okay. I’ll launch you up there.”

Anastasia lit up with alarm, “Wait, just me?!”

“Yes I—”

“No way! You need to come with me or else—”
Zarestia flicked her forehead, “Dumbass. Let me finish. You go up there. I’ll go save the mutt.”

That got Anastasia’s attention, “Where’s Hal?”

Zarestia pointed downward, “He’s down there somewhere. He’ll die if I don’t go after him.”

Anastasia was speechless, “…No. Shit. Do I have to—”

“Don’t,” Zarestia could tell something was off. It reminded her sometimes of Subaru’s behavior. “I can take care of him. You take care of Su.”

“…I thought you didn’t trust me?” Anastasia asked. Her voice sounded so small.

“I didn’t. But now I do,” Zarestia rolled her eyes at Anastasia’s confusion. “Your eyes are much better now. I think you can handle everything by yourself.”

She remembered when Anastasia first lifted her mask. When her eyes no longer were helpless and out of sync, but filled with malice, piercing her soul. It was as if Zarestia had laid eyes on a beast that considered her both prey and an enemy. Just for a moment, Zarestia could see a kindred spirit in this foxlike woman. For some time, she couldn’t see it, masked by mania and regret. But now, those piercing blue eyes were all she could witness.

Anastasia was no longer a frail human but a beast that could carve up the world. She just needed a reason to let loose. So, despite how she needed a little prodding here and there, Zarestia trusted her.

“Go save your mate. I’ll save that dumb fuck.”

“…Technically, he’s also a dumb fuck,” Anastasia snarked.

Zarestia smiled, “Go.”

Without another word, she separated herself from Anastasia and covered her in a thick ball of sheering winds before launching her with all her force to Subaru’s location. She then locked in on Halibel’s signature via Subaru’s Authority.

She barreled after it at top speed. The Witch was Anastasia’s prey but no one but her was allowed to kill the mutt.

------------------

Anastasia rolled onto the floor panting, the last remaining traces of Tia’s wind dissipating around her. She was on the top of the tower, surrounded by clouds and shadows, the only light remaining was from the distant moon up above. She couldn’t think. She just needed to run. They were so close. So many different tries. So many deaths.

She was at her limit: mentally and physically. Subaru was barely above her in that regard and the only reason she was even conscious was because she wouldn’t dare leave him alone in all of this. They had all the materials. The pendant allowed them to read Flugel’s secret messages. They just needed to get everything together at the right moment.

Volcanica’s breath.

Reinhard’s sword.

And a Taiji spell that combined high tier Yin and Yang magic.

It was infuriating that this was all thanks to both Flugel and Echidna, but it was better than nothing. They needed to win. This was the closest they’ve gotten to where everyone survived.

Anastasia bit her lip as she prayed to Od that Tia got to Halibel on time. Otherwise…another loop. This time it was her turn. She didn’t care what Subaru would say. He wasn’t getting another death.

Speaking of, where is he?!

Anastasia looked around desperately before her eyes locked onto Subaru’s form along with…

An incredibly huge dragon. Volcanica. It was speaking to him. She couldn’t hear it but they were having a conversation—

She ducked and rolled away from a shadow hand that almost crushed her skull. Out of breath, she started sprinting even harder than before. Not caring how her legs were screaming at her. They just needed to time it right. Hopefully, Reinhard arrives in time.

Duck again. Dodge.

Too many were coming. “Makra!” Murak and an ancient yang spell called Akra. Former was anti-gravity while the latter boosted her muscle strength. Combined, they relieved the pain in her muscles and gave her extra speed. She was much faster and able to dodge the cascade of shadows erupting from the floor.

Too many. There was just too many.

Does she need to reset? No. They were so close. If…maybe. No. Subaru. He needed to live. If it that was what it took—“ANA!”

Anastasia didn’t even realize Subaru was right in front of her, tackling her away from another wave of shadows right as she heard a roar from above. Just as she thought everything had failed again, she opened her eyes and saw a veil of blue light.

Anastasia and Subaru were standing within a dome barrier, scared as Volcanica roared behind them, protecting the area from an onslaught of shadows, hands, and death. It was like night itself eclipsed the very ground and air, the abyss swallowing any semblance of light.

“Echidna…Flugel…stay back…” Volcanica’s voice was strange. He seemed incoherent. Weightless and absentminded.

Also.

“Did he just call me Echidna…?” Anastasia muttered in Subaru’s arms.

“Fuck, am I Flugel?” Subaru whispered near her.

They were interrupted by something slamming into the dome, Volcanica roared back, strengthening the light.

The only thing they could see outside were hundreds of writhing tendrils of hate and malice, dark hands of pure ebony slamming into the barrier every second.

Anastasia could barely process what was happening as she looked within the hellish landscape and saw a monster wreathed in darkness step forth, slowly making her way to them.

At first Anastasia’s body flinched, her eyes widened. She was scared out of her mind. Every inch of her body wanted to leave right now and never come back. That was death, personified.

And then she felt someone shiver and whimper next to her, gripping her arm with one hand, trying to stand tall.

It was Subaru.

Despite it all, clothes torn, his face marked with cuts and bruises, dried blood etching his body. His long hair had remnants of white and grey. His eyes were wavering, filled with fear and longing. His legs wobbling.

He was still standing tall. For her.

She nearly cried on the spot at the realization.

For him.

That’s why she was here. For him.

And this woman in front of her. No. This Witch. She made his life an isolated hell. And for what? Love?!

…That wasn’t love.

Anastasia clung onto Subaru, using him as support, and stood up. Straightening her back and glaring into the abyss.

Her eyes narrowed, fury unleashed, a fiery madness blazing within her irises. She focused on the monster in front of her and stepped forward, leaving Subaru’s grasp.

The boy reached out, “Anastasia, no!”

His voice filled with desperation and fear.

“HEY WITCH! Is this your love?! Is this what you think he wants?!”

She gritted her teeth, her legs were no longer shaking, she stood strong, “That isn’t love…it’s just some disgusting obsession. You made him a slave…isolated him. Made him into someone that would only be yours. Well guess what?! You don’t own him. He was never yours. He will never be yours. The only person he’ll ever be with, until the very end of it all, is right here. RIGHT IN FRONT OF YOU!”

Her heart was pounding. Every fiber of her being wanted to run away. But in this very moment, Anastasia couldn’t help but bare it all.

For him.

She struck a pose and pointed her thumb at her heart.

“Anastasia Hoshin, future Anastasia Natsuki, the greatest merchant greedier than the Witch of Greed herself!”

She looked at the mass of tendrils and hate with steel-eyed resolve.

“I’ll share his burdens, his pain, and all his memories. I’ll take all of his love for myself. I’ll make sure he gets the happiest ending he could ever dream of! And I’ll accomplish all of mine and his dreams without sacrificing our humanity, that’s my greed. So, look on and despair: because the greediest, most gluttonous, merchant and hero pair will not back down.”

She laughed wildly. She didn’t care how she sounded. This was her third declaration of war. Her final one.

Anastasia briefly looked back at Subaru and gave him a sincere smile, a hand stretched out to him, “That’s my last proposal to you, Subaru. My final offer, forever yours. No matter what, I’ll save you.”

Suddenly, a bright light shined behind Anastasia’s head. It rushed down from the heavens, piercing through the veil of darkness that nearly snuffed out the moon.

A red-haired meteor was barreling in from above, slicing and cleaving the shadows, making its way to the two stars.

Anastasia ignored it, still gazing at the love of her life with all she had.

---------------------------------

Subaru was kneeling on the floor shocked. As the darkness of his soul was trying to desperately separate the two, he could only stare and reflect.

Imagine if you will, a storm. A storm that felt unyielding, never ending. Where you are all alone, adrift in the tumultuous gales. The darkness infinite, and the future unknown. For Natsuki Subaru, that was all he knew since the moment he was snatched from home.

Hey, Mom. Dad. I know it’s been a while but…

Constant danger.

I miss you.

No way home.

Every day.

Nary a single moment of respite, the rarest occasion leading to more conflict.

Ever since I got here, has been hell.

Not a single constant anchoring him. Only himself.

I’ve been trying so hard.

And every single ray of light: Emilia, Rem, his friends. All one day leave him to brace the storm alone, once again.

And when I found a home again, it was gone. Like everything in my life.

Yet, one day, despite reaching the apex of the storm, at the height of his loneliness. One single star persisted despite the gales of fate pushing her away.

I thought…I’ll always be alone. I’ll never find love. I’ll never be happy.

Through the unlikeliest of means, the unlikeliest of allies, came to him in the unlikeliest of situations. Comforted, nurtured, and loved him.

But I was wrong.

Despite how desperately he wanted to believe otherwise, a fear persisted: all good things end. Like everything in his life, she too will leave, and all that remains, would be the storm.

I thought she would be just like the others.

Yet in this moment, Subaru couldn’t look away. He saw Anastasia in her entirety: bloodied and covered in dirt. Her dress a torn and muddy rag. Her hair, a disgusting rat’s nest.

…Greedy, selfish, manipulative. For a time, I hated her. For even longer, I didn’t trust her.

Seeing her standing in the face of that very storm, unyielding. Embracing the wind and rain that came with it. Taking his hand and anchoring his very being to the ground. And above all else, defying the storm’s grasp over him in the name of her infinite greed, her infinite love. For him.

Yet…she proved me wrong each time. Gave me hope, when I had none. Love, when I didn’t deserve it. Trust, when I couldn’t believe it.

She was smiling, hand outstretched to him, as the darkness was cleaved behind her head by a red comet, her body shining amidst the cosmos.

I wish you could see her now.

To Natsuki Subaru, it was the most beautiful sight in the world. A core memory that could never be forgotten, even beyond his death.

I think you would have liked her.

A bright star that would never leave his sky again. That desires all of him, his burdens, malice, and sins included. That banished the darkness and dared it to return.

Because after all is said and done…

That is what Anastasia has become to the one called Natsuki Subaru. To the future Hoshin Subaru.

Despite all the bullshit, all the baggage I bring…

His brightest star. His home. His other half.

She still stayed. Held my hand and never let go.

The love of his life.

Mom. Dad.

Subaru’s eyes watered. He could barely comprehend the beauty. The love. The compassion. The joy. It was all too much. His mouth felt dry, he couldn’t breathe.

I’m afraid. I don’t know what to do. I’m useless. Terrible. An idiot beyond all measure.

He was no longer shaking. Breathless and stunned.

I don’t deserve anything…

Subaru, choked up with emotion, could only nod. The only thing on his mind, after seeing Anastasia in such a state while staring down an eldritch monstrosity plaguing his life since day one: was that she was the most beautiful woman in this world. No. This universe.

But if I could ask for only one thing…just one last fucking thing…

“Ana…” he could barely speak, his voice almost silent. “Please…save me.”

Let me walk with her, until the end. Into Hell, together.

He reached out his hand and clasped hers. Their hands radiated magic, Yin and Yang sparking, a vibrant combination of black and white mana.

Anastasia smiled, “A deals a deal. Let’s go get your happy ending.”

She brought him close, hugging him tight, their enjoined hands pointed forward, together. Against the writhing abyss.

She smiled at Subaru before staring at the face of death, “And to you Satella: thank you. Thank you for keeping him safe and bringing him here. While I hate that he suffered so much since he arrived, I don’t regret being with him, here and now. Don’t worry, you’ll also have a place in our happy ending.”

The Witch stopped moving. No longer walking forward. Underneath the veil of envy and sheer malice, a small smile was visible. Her mouth moved slowly, but no words came out.

The merchant’s eyes hardened, focusing solely on the rage she harbored for so long. No matter the cost, she won’t let anything slip from her grasp again. Subaru and Anastasia’s eyes glowed a mix of yellow and purple.

Volcanica behind them, channeled mana from within, gathering it in his mouth. Flexing its wings, its body pulsated with sheer power and pure mana.

The stars, once lost and forgotten—found once again— channeled their magic into one focal point, two orbs of black and white formed and spun in front of their combined hands. Spinning faster and faster, until you could barely tell the difference.

They screamed, “OL JAMAK!”

Reinhard was slicing faster and faster through the maelstrom, a raging tornado of sheer strength, streaking towards the witch from above. He channeled his strength for one last attack, the Dragon Sword Reid glowing with sheer holy power. His arms stretched back, the sword ready for one last swing.

The Two Stars, the Dragon, The Sword Saint. All at their apex. Combining their strength to defeat the Witch of Envy.

Just as they were about to all release their attacks, the Yin-Yang attack disappeared for one second.

Anastasia whispered, “Return to death, you disgusting Witch.”

The Yin-Yang attack reappeared and shot forth, a spinning spell of pure energy as Volcanica released a torrent of mana behind it, just as Reinhard sent a slash of pure energy and power. All aimed towards the witch.

And just as they all collided.

Everything went to white.

Notes:

AN: And that's the end of the main story! Don't worry, there will be a multi-chapter epilogue that will go into the Emilia camps reactions, the kingdom's reactions, the aftermath of reforgor, Felix, Crusch, and more. In addition, there will be multiple side stories that will deal with IF scenarios, future scenarios (such as their kids), a possible theater chapter (if yall are good). Again, this is only the main story ending. TFS won't exactly stop updating yet as there are still things to wrap up. The reason I did it like this will be delved into a separate afterword but to summarize: this was the original ending of a three part story that was never planned to go further than three chapters. It was supposed to be a story that mainly dealt with the Anabaru romance in a way that people would not only enjoy but would make sense. Once the two officially were together, the main story would finish. And I only consider the romance finished when Subaru and Anastasia fully commit to each other and have their happy ending. Anastasia had her moment when fighting Louis, committing herself to Subaru, Hell or not. Subaru's was when he finally realized that he won't ever be alone again.

And well, if a girl literally fights the manifestation of Satan in her world for you, it's kind of hard not to accept her love as real.

Anabaru was my favorite ship because I generally liked incompatible people somehow ending up together. Opposites attract. Hate to love tropes. All that and more. In my mind, I could never see Anastasia and Subaru ending up together in canon easily. But I focused on it because I saw there was not that many Anabaru fics. None that were particularly outstanding nor any that finished and actually had them together.

So I kind of wanted to write one myself.

This story was my first writing endeavor and one year ago I never expected it to become so popular. I never wrote fanfiction before, much less stories or fiction or did anything creative besides academic work. I've never written before last year. I barely got into fanfiction and even reading novels since two years ago. Two Forgotten Stars was written as a vent piece because I was betrayed by people close to me. I only wanted to publish one or three chapters. And then never write again.

I never expected this story to become popular. I never expected so many people to love what I write. And I never expected my life to change so much. I met so many wonderful people because of this and I have gained a passion and obsession with writing that has changed the direction of my entire life.

All I can say is, thank you. Thank you for being blessings in my life. Every single one of you, those who read and commented since the beginning. Those who supported me in so many ways that I can and can't say. And every person who wants to see me write more.

You are a blessing and for that, I will always love you.

-KnockTok

Chapter 68: Afterword

Notes:

(See the end of the chapter for notes.)

Chapter Text

Hello! Knocktok here.

Unfortunately, I’m a little preoccupied with work again so there won’t be an epilogue chapter coming out today but do tune in to next week where we will not only get into the aftermath of the tower debacle but also begin delving into the Emilia Camp’s reaction to Subaru’s return. Spoilers: it’s not pretty.

However, I hate not giving people something to read so for this week I’ll be giving you an afterword that goes into depth about the writing process of TFS as well as my other stories. Perhaps it may give insight into people about me as an author and everything that has gone on this past year and three months. In addition, there will also be a sneak peek into my original webnovel, To Kill a God, for all tiers coming in one hour. The first chapter will be released here before the first 10 will be released for free on Royal Road. If you haven’t been to the website, Royal Road, I highly recommend it as it not only caters to amateur webnovelists but also fanfiction. Lots of fun stories to read there.

But anyways, let’s talk about what most people are here for Two Forgotten Stars!

…I honestly never planned on writing this whole story like this. And while there was a general outline it was mainly a hodgepodge of different plot ideas and plot bunnies that I ultimately scrapped around chapter 10. Two Forgotten Stars was my first writing endeavor and it really shows in the first chapter and its prose. It was mainly written in a whole night through venting and emotion. My life back then was not great as my family was going through a crisis, all because some of our family members were selfish bastards who lied to us for years and took our money in the name of ‘love.’ Questions haunted my mind constantly: how can someone hurt you despite still loving you? How can they justify their actions? And how should I feel afterwards?

And why do I still love them despite it all?

I ultimately channeled those emotions into both characters and published it on AO3 on a whim. I never planned on writing that much and it was mostly just for a quick bit of fun by suggestion of my mother. A way to cope with everything.

I then woke up to nearly 300 kudos in a single night, around 30 bookmarks, and multiple comments all gushing about the first chapter. This was right around when I was going on a trip to South Korea to visit family which meant that I woke up after the plane ride, groggy and incoherent, to an insane amount of emails in my inbox.

Frankly, the whole moment brought me to tears and it made me so motivated to write another chapter that I took out my phone, and wrote a whole unplanned second chapter in notes and published the next chapter almost immediately.

Then that was almost as well received as the first. So I got excited and wrote a third. Then a fourth. Fifth. Sixth. Seventh.

Until we got the ending right at 67. Originally, I only planned on writing three chapters: the first, Hell, and the ending. It would have included some quick narration about what had happened and led up to these moments but that would have been all TFS would have been, if it weren’t for the massive surge of people wanting more.

So I began writing in earnest, even after I returned home from my vacation, and it slowly changed from a whim to a hobby to a goal to an obsession. I would pour hours upon hours into my writing, not even thinking but just pouring all my ideas into the page and publishing immediately or saving the draft for later. And I’ve been continuing this sort of method since last year.

I found out people call this ‘writing by the seat of their pants’ around 11 months ago.

Again, this was my first writing endeavor. I never wrote anything fictional, story-based, or even remotely with characters. Everything I wrote beforehand was purely scientific and was published in journals. I never liked English classes. I abhorred literature majors. And I especially disliked reading books that were boring. So, to me, this felt like an incredible shift in my usual daily life. But it was fun. It was incredible. It was new.

And it became everything to me.

Roughly around chapter 24, after I published Hell, was around the time when my PhD program was about to occur. At that point, I realized I wouldn’t have any time to write. I would have to dedicate almost all my time to studying and working and I would barely be able to write, let alone publish.

It was weird but that realization made me really want to die. So, out of annoyance, and because I’d rather not let my story go unfinished, I sped up the pacing of TFS and was planning on ending it roughly around chapter 40. The Mather’s plot point, the tower, and the ‘watching the memories’ plot point would all be condensed into only a few chapters and then speedran to the ending. Which was why Pandora was brought in to speed up the plot process even more. It’s probably why a lot of people felt TFS go insane around that time because I was pretty much trying to end the series quickly at that point.

Then, it turned out, my PhD program wasn’t able to fund me. So I had to drop out of the program and find a job out of nowhere. This then led to TFS no longer needing to be finished so quickly but also the pacing of the story became an absolute mess. I was originally going to have a lot of fluff chapters after Hell and show the slow corrode of Ana’s mind as she realizes the implications of Subaru’s actions and changed behavior. But that all got thrown to the wayside as I was now stuck deep in the plot and I couldn’t really go back now, could I?

So I ended up saying, ‘fuck it. Let’s experiment.”

I thought I had a wonderful opportunity, having a huge audience and all, to experiment with the various styles and proses and ways to write chapters. Formatting and how the dialogue was written continued to change. I started to read a lot of different types of novels. I learned what character-driven versus plot driven stories were. Again, I have zero knowledge on how stories were written. I was basically a newbie to so much stuff. So, to rectify this, I tried experimenting and trying everything I wasn’t good at.

I mainly liked writing romances and while I would love writing hundreds of chapters focusing on the complex relationships of characters and how to use it for drama, fluff, and angst, I was already kind of good at that. I didn’t know how to write large overarching mysteries, how to write huge action scenes that engross the reader, or how to write stuff with big themes. Ironically enough, I don’t usually think of the themes and reasons for each story. I mostly discover them while writing and thinking of the characters as real people with real emotions and real thought processes unique to them and how these could develop in specific situations. The themes come out naturally over time.

I became meticulous in what I wanted to experiment with, right down to how much chapter length I can trim until someone gets pissed off.

However, as a result of this, TFS kind of became a mess around chapter 30-50. I experimented so much that I could see a lot of readers being drained but it did give me so much insight into how the audience reacts to certain story elements and what they actually want to read in stories that it would hopefully help me make all my future stories that much better. I also learned a lot about myself and what I’m good at. Because of this, while TFS may not have developed as best as it could, I do not regret writing it this way.

It was a messy and complicated process filled with tons of emotion, sudden life changes, and incredible amounts of obsession. But, funny enough, one could say that about TFS as a whole. TFS was about two characters who frankly have no right to interact or love each other in canon but have a host of personality traits that are ripe for a good toxic romance. One where each character becomes so attached to each other, so hopelessly in love, that you can’t help but root for the romance.

It’s really funny how much people wanted Anastasia and Subaru to be together. Like an absurd amount of you loved my versions of the characters to the point I got multiple comments and emails talking about how they never were really fond of Anastasia or the ship itself but not only fully boarded it with my fic, and are especially ride or die for my interpretation of them. So much so that I eventually came to the conclusion that TFS Subaru and TFS Anastasia were their own separate characters from canon. Very similar to their original counterparts but so many differences that you could easily put them in the same room and see that they are almost different characters. It really touched me to my core that people fell in love with them and wanted them to be happy. And it also made me realize how often I wrote without keeping canon in mind.

Don’t get me wrong. I love canon and it was why I started writing the story in the first place, but I always hated being constrained by it. It’s why despite however many times I thought ‘well this character wouldn’t exactly react like this in canon,’ it was ultimately defeated by the thought of, ‘but the in-canon reaction isn’t as entertaining as my interpretation of it.’ It is a flaw for me as a writer but I also find it to be a virtue. I believe writers should follow their own story rather than one outlined by others or the original source. Because otherwise your story will simply be washed away through multitudes of others, rather than standing out as its own separate entity.

But I digress, because I understood this part of myself, I slowly began to drift away from focusing on fanfiction. I realized I often want to write my own stories. My own lore. My own characters who all act and react as I meticulously characterized. This was right around the time I also realized that while writing fanfiction was incredible fun, it wasn’t something I could do forever. One day I will have to prioritize my career or maybe even other parts of my life.

Which made me want to die even more.

So, to not feel like my heart was being squeezed by despair, I made a plan. Right around chapter 40-50, I began writing original novel works. Of course, I dabbled in original works a few times before during TFS’s infancy but those were more for fun than anything.  Now, with my obsession on the cusp of insanity, I felt I had a better chance at writing something magnificent. I decided that the only way I could truly be happy now, was if I eventually laid the groundwork for becoming a full-time writer. Maybe it would take years or decades, but I’d rather put all my effort in chasing that dream than dying bored and regretful.

This was why my other fanfiction works had to be put on hiatus. I could only write so much in a given day because of my job priorities. Don’t get me wrong, I want to write and finish them but at the moment, I had to prioritize other projects. Namely TFS and Within Two Months which were both immensely popular and more romance based than the other two. As a result, I trimmed the stories from four updates per week to three to now two, with only TFS and Within Two Months updating. Divine Dragon Comedy and Vagrant Royalty are still in the works to be continued but not until TFS or WTM finishes updating. Or at least until I can become a full-time writer.

It’s frustrating to me because I am constantly having this itch in my brain to write but I can’t do it for like 9 hours a day, Monday through Friday and sometimes weekends. Unfortunately, I need to work to survive, and writing can’t satisfy that necessity yet. At some points, I consider it an addiction of sorts. I often forget to eat and get so engrossed in writing that I’d rather do that all day than anything else.

But I digress, how does this relate to TFS? Well, TFS was a big inspiration for a lot of my original novels. The toxic obsession, focus on romance, and comedic dialogue mixed with heartfelt moments would all continue in both spirit and form in my upcoming original works. So, if you like the romance in TFS, the comedy of Divine Dragon Comedy, the drama and mystery of Vagrant Royalty, and the heartfelt bonds of Within Two Months, then stay tuned for my two upcoming novels: To Kill a God and Courting Death Daily.

The former will be a dark fantasy comedy where a Bugs Bunny-like character is transported to a land of Gods and slowly learns how to become a God himself. The latter would be a wuxia/murim inspired martial arts story focusing on a crass female lead who keeps avoiding martial arts tropes because she does not want to be a heroine. Both will involve toxic and obsessive romances and both will have lots of fun. So, if you enjoyed all of my works or even just some, please take a look at both once they release. I hope you enjoy those works just as much, if not more.

Anyways, thank you again for all of the love and support throughout this whole journey. It’s been fun being a part of the community despite some boring parts and boring people. Being a part of Cluster has also been a blast and I made a ton of different friends. Some of which I consider will become lifelong.

To all of you who believed in me since the beginning and are still here, thank you. You truly changed my life for better. I wrote TFS as a way to vent but it eventually paved the way for a new way of life. I have never been happier before than I am right now. For those of you who came later but were so involved in either the comments sections, sending me personal DMs, or supporting me in other ways, I love you all. Each and every reader. No matter who you are. You are all blessings to me. I hope you enjoy the epilogues and side stories. And once those end, I hope you also enjoy the many tales and stories I’ll write until the day I die.

 

Or maybe I won’t die,

KnockTok.

Me!
