Chapter 70: Epilogue 2

Summary:

Otto considered this all might be a dream...

Chapter Text

Otto could barely believe what he was seeing. Natsuki Subaru was right there. In the flesh, like he had never even left.

They were all sitting in a circle. Right outside the Sage’s tower—which was falling apart by the seams. They had just woken up and it seemed Gluttony spat their names out during their temporary comas, as each person subsequently remembered the existence of these two very important individuals in front of them. Otto could barely process what was happening when he woke up to a kick to the stomach.

“So, Ana and I met up at the capital. She was trying to grab some stuff before leaving—”
“To Kararagi,” Anastasia interrupted, “I was…not in a good headspace. I got it in my mind that I needed to rebuild my company and try to, I don’t know—”

Subaru intervened, “And it was purely because she got it in her head that if she were to try again and rebuild your relationship, it would be different from before. So she panicked and ran away. Because she’s super dumb.”

“…He also pointed a knife at me the second we met.”

“That is super out of context!”

“But it’s true!”

…How was he smiling?

He was right there. Black and white hair. Looking older than he should. At least, since the last time you saw each other in Priestella. It felt like so long ago. And maybe it was. Months had passed. But it felt like years. Subaru had disappeared in their lives and they had not even noticed.

Otto rubbed his hands together, feeling his sweat begin to pool. He was barely listening to their explanation. Otto could feel Garfiel’s leg bounce beside him, the poor boy’s attention thoroughly entranced by their story—though the grinding of his teeth and tight hands were a sign that he was having the same ideas as Otto.

So many thoughts. None of them good. About what had happened to him. What he experienced. And why he looked so tired.

He had scars. New ones. Very visible ones. On his face and through some of the openings in his clothes. At least, Otto thought they were new. Maybe some of them were not. Otto had not been paying attention to his friend—no—Subaru’s health as of late. Or perhaps at all. And wasn’t that something? Because of his negligence, nay, his sloth.

His friend had been abandoned in Priestella and they apparently didn’t know.

And apparently he had been thought to be a Witch Cultist, and was sent to the gallows without trial, practically awaiting death as he was tortured. Anastasia had been very thorough when explaining that, to Subaru’s opposition. Otto had listened with great attention during those moments, trying to recall everything he had done in the last six months, and he was glad Garfiel had only interrupted at least once from incredible rage.

He was also glad he had not vomited immediately. At the moment, he was only slightly nauseous due to the fact that the second he had felt something rise up his throat, the Wind Spirit of Death who kicked him earlier, released a fury of bloodlust that sent whatever was going up, straight back down.

He didn’t know if he welcomed the literal personification of violence right next to him or…no he definitely welcomed her. He deserved this. It was a bare pittance compared to everything his fri—Subaru had gone through.

“Ana almost died when we got to Banan.”

And apparently it wasn’t just him.

“WHAT?!” Otto’s eyes glanced over at the enraged and distraught Iron Fang and Julius. The Triplets immediately were on their feet and clamoring to their leader with teary eyes and panic, asking if she was okay rapidly.

Ricardo was worse, he was the loudest and though he calmed himself down immediately—he looked to be itching to do the same as his children checked his surrogate daughter for any wounds. Julius looked like he was on the verge of a panic attack.

“I’m okay, I’m okay!” She glared at Subaru, “It wasn’t anyone’s fault.”

“No. It was mine,” Subaru said without a hint of a joke. Before she could respond, “My actions led her to a situation where her lifespan had diminished greatly. For that, and for not protecting her in that moment, I’m deeply sorry. It was my fault. Because of me…you almost lost a loved one. Without even knowing about it. It was one of the worst moments of my life. And I take full responsibility for it.”

The Iron Fang were too stunned by the revelation to comment, and poor Julius was looking worse than ever. Subaru was on his hands and knees, doing a deep bow. Otto hated seeing that. Why was he acting like that?

“Let me explain!” Anastasia grabbed him by the collar and pulled him up.  She sighed and turned to them, her eyes just as tired as Subaru’s, “…When we arrived to Banan, the Witch Cult were doing a scheme to absorb a ton of mana. It ended up turning my lifespan from around ten years to like… a week. I don’t know why. I don’t know for what reason. But we put a stop to that. It wasn’t his fault. I was going to Banan anyway, with or without him, and I would have ended up in the same situation regardless. So again, not his fault and he’s stupid for trying to take responsibility.”

“But you—”

“And guess who nearly died several times protecting me and gave me half his lifespan?” She pointed to Subaru, “This dumbass.”
“WHAT?!” This time Otto and Garfiel stood up in exclamation.

Anastasia proceeded to explain how some deranged oni woman had stolen the Wind Murder Spirit’s ball and gain her power and become a doppelganger to then murder all of the Witch Cult and subsequently tried to kill Subaru because he smelled bad.

…Otto had to sit down again to process that.

She then explained that Subaru had found out about Anastasia’s sudden loss of life, and that he, without hesitation, had decided it was a great idea to share his whole lifespan with her.

And to propose to her.

Oh yeah. They were married. Or about to be.

It had been less than half a year.

“But what bout…” Garfiel muttered.

Otto stopped him right there, silently signaling that it wasn’t the time. There was so much left to discuss and if they opened that can of worms, it would be a nightmare to deal with and he wasn’t quite sure if he could handle that right now.

So Otto continued listening as Subaru and Anastasia finished up their explanation. Filling in any forgotten details such as them making a new company, finding out that Julius had been looking for them, and that they apparently made friends with both Halibel, the Admirer, and Zarestia, the Murder Wind Spirit of Hyper Death.

Again, less than half a year. Literal strongest of Kararagi on their payroll. And apparently, they made friends with these two in the first few weeks of arriving in Banan!

…Otto was this close to going insane.

“So…okay. There’s a portion of this story that will explain what happened to us afterward. And kind of, go into detail about how I saved Ana’s life,” Subaru said, nervous.

“But that requires us to say some very…important things. Details that should not ever be shared no matter what and that could put us all in grave danger if you do,” Anastasia finished for him.

They all leaned in, thoroughly curious of what they meant.

“…We want to share this with you guys, because we trust you and don’t want to hide anything. We don’t want to have secrets that aren’t necessary,” Subaru’s words made Otto feel rancid. He trusted them. After being abandoned. And tortured. “We’ll explain everything to the best of our abilities because, well, some of it is hard to accept. Like, really weird shit that is not fundamentally possible.”

“And if you guys don’t want to know, we’ll respect that,” Anastasia added on, fully sincere. “It’s a lot to take in and if you don’t want to hear it now, we won’t tell you.”

“Then don’t tell us,” Otto blurted out.

The others glared at him. Julius was the first to lash out, “You cannot be serious! Otto…this isn’t like you.”

“Can you really say that?” Otto bit back. “Look at the past few months! None of us have been…” Otto stopped. He turned to Subaru and Anastasia, “It’s not even about that. If its something so important, that you guys hesitate to even want to tell us, then don’t. You shouldn’t.”

“Ya cowardly little—" Ricardo began to say, too heated to care about his manners.

“Hey don’t talk shit like that ta Otto!” Garfiel stood in defense. “He’s got a good reason for sayin’ no.”

“Like what?” Tivey said, irritated. “I don’t see any logic in it. Ricardo’s right. Otto is just scared of what they’ll say.”

“You fuckin’—”

“ENOUGH!” Subaru yelled, “…That was our bad. We wanted to give you guys the chance to make a decision yourselves instead of having us dump that information onto you without your consent. This was probably just bad timing. There’s so much to process and obviously, your emotions are heated. So…let’s split up for now.”

“What?” Otto immediately stood up again. “That’s not what I meant. I didn’t mean—!”

“Split into groups,” Anastasia corrected, making Otto sheepishly blush. “Camp groups. That way we can ease the information in a little. I’m sure everyone has questions and its not like we have to rush this.” She patted Mimi and Tivey’s heads softly. “Let’s calm down. We’re not enemies here.”

One by one, they all assented and began moving into separate corners of the campsite. Anastasia’s camp in one, Subaru’s in the other. Halibel, Zarestia, and even Beatrice had chosen to not participate. They stood off in the distance, killing any Witchbeasts nearby so that they had some space to breathe. Reinhard was also not here though Otto had a faint idea that the guy was listening. He had given the excuse that he was checking the Witch of Envy’s seal, but it was more likely the poor Sword Saint did not know how to deal with all of this.

…To be fair, neither did Otto.

“So, what do you two want to know?” Subaru said as he sat down in front of them.

Otto didn’t know what to say. A part of him regretted saying what he thought out loud. But the other part of him was stubborn and believed he made the right call. It was a terrible thing to say. It was outright villainous to imply they shouldn’t confide in their friends. But it was the right call.

Because they weren’t friends. Not anymore. They ruined it. Otto ruined it. Garfiel ruined it. All of them did. One little mistake and their friend had been sent through Hell, and they were none the wiser. To go back to normal, to just act like that didn’t happen, was something Otto could not comprehend.

“…Yer not interested in Princess anymore?” Garfiel asked.

Otto whipped his head to Garfiel. This was not the time yet!

“No,” Subaru shook his head. He didn’t look sad or depressed or even…regretful. He looked like he was ready to accept everything that was going to happen. “I broke my promise with her. And…that’s my fault.”

Why? Why does he just accept it?

“Oh…” Garfiel was despondent, “Does that mean…yer going to leave the camp?”
Otto froze. He wanted to yell at Garfiel and tell him to stop talking. But what good would that do? The same question was on Otto’s mind. He was just too much of a coward to speak it.

“I don’t know,” Subaru said, though he looked pensive. “I doubt Emilia would let me stay. After what I’ve done, and…what I told her. I doubt she would even want to see me.”

What? That’s not true. That’s not true at all! Emilia loved him. She loved him so much that even when they all forgot, she was practically grieving his non-existence. The amount of times he saw her not able to study, constantly asking questions about love as if her life depended on it, and would walk around looking for Subaru, without even knowing it, was too much to even count.

Otto knew. Because he was in crisis mode the entire time Subaru’s gone.

“But it should be fine,” Subaru said, trying to smile. “I…abandoned you guys. I gave up. So, it’s not like there should be a place there for me anyway.”

What kind of bullshit was that?

“Dat’s wrong!” Garfiel stood up, heated. “You…” Garfiel struggled to say anything.

“It’s fine Gar, you all seemed to be doing fine without me. Though I guess Ros-chi was kind of going through an alcoholic phase, kind of reminded me of you, Otto,” Subaru chuckled but it felt like poison to Otto’s ears. “…Don’t worry. I talked to him. He should be fine now. And once we get back, Emilia should still be fine in regards to the selection. We have a plan to deal with all the fallout and it’s not like—”

Otto heard enough, “Stop.”

Subaru shut his mouth, “Sorry. I guess it’s wrong of me to assume that. But seriously. Ana and I will take full responsibility—”
“Just stop!” Otto couldn’t bare it anymore. If he heard anymore, his heart may break from the pain. “Just…Natsuki-san. Why?”

Subaru looked confused and guilty. Fuck. What was wrong with him? He shouldn’t be like this. He should be…

“…I don’t know. I guess. It was either this or hurting you guys more and I don’t want to cause more damage because of what I did. It isn’t right and I promise, I won’t try to interfere with the election or with Emilia or—”
“Why aren’t you angry?!” Otto’s voice broke before his heart fully could.

“…What?” Subaru blinked at him.

That just made Otto even more furious, “You were tortured. You were abandoned by us. You were all alone for months. You nearly died. You were all the way across the world and yet, you somehow ended up here. Saving us.”

Despite all they did to him. Or what they didn’t do for him.

“…It’s fine.”

“It’s not fine!” Otto held back the tears. “You should be angry! You should be tearing into us! You should be calling us assholes or monsters or just…anything! You should be giving us hell for what we did! Resenting us! Or even just…abandoning us to our fate.”

Otto should have died in there. From what little he remembered, it was his fault they stayed and it was his fault that they ended up in such a nightmare scenario. The literal Witch of Envy trying to kill them. And Subaru, the man who had started a new life in another country, decided to trek all the way here to save them. On a whim.

…Otto couldn’t understand. Nor could he comprehend. And a part of him didn’t want to.

“Otto,” Subaru’s voice was so soft, that it pierced his soul worse than any rage could. “I guess I’m just…tired.”

Od damn it. Od fucking damn it!

Subaru continued, “I’m tired of being angry. Of being sad. Of being regretful. It’s pathetic to say. But I feel so old now. I don’t really have the energy to feel vengeful or anything like that. Maybe that doesn’t make sense…but I guess I’ve come to terms with how weak I am finally. That even with all the help I’ve gained, I’m still someone who can’t really do anything meaningful.”

That’s not true. Everything. Everything he had done since they first met, was meaningful.

“But…for better or worse, I’ve become greedy,” Subaru smiled, though it felt more melancholic than anything. “More than before probably. Even if I’m not anyone special, I still want to keep the things I had. Or once had. And I don’t want to give up the things I have now. So even if it may not be possible, I still wanted to be your guy’s friend.”

…Otto began to cry, “Natsuki-san.”

Subaru was alarmed. “O-otto—”

“I’m sorry,” Otto didn’t know what else to say.

What could he say?

That for the last several months, he had been so lost. That he had been stressing nearly everyday, trying to figure out what had gone wrong since they left Priestella. That even though they had been trying to figure everything out, trying to make the best of things, it felt like something was missing. They were all in top form. The camp had so many achievements and their investments had paid off. But everyone had missed his presence.

That even if everything was fine, without him, it wasn’t good enough.

Or what about how Otto just realized how little that all mattered. That while they were languishing in luxury, Subaru was getting gutted daily. That apparently he had been so stressed, his body in such pitiful agony, that his hair had gone white. That was what those white streaks were, right? The fact that he had so many on the tips of his hair, cemented that once upon a time, he had a full bed of white hair. No black.

That wasn’t natural.

Or how about how Subaru didn’t even call Emilia, Emilia-tan anymore. How for some fucking reason, the guy who was head over heels, hopelessly in love with one girl for nearly a whole year, was so shattered by his experience that he gave that up. That his life had gone to such shit, that he couldn’t even bring himself to love anymore. Natsuki Subaru. Famous for doing whatever he could for the people he loved.

And Rem. Oh God. Rem.

Otto just remembered Rem. Subaru had adored that woman. Almost if not equal to Emilia. And yet, perhaps it was just instinct, but it felt like Subaru lost that as well. What kind of experience did he go through to push that out of him? It was like he was a completely different person. Was the torture that bad? Otto hated himself for even asking that. Of course it was.

…Why did he not talk to them? Did he hate their camp so much after those events, that he couldn’t bear to see them? He remembered meeting Subaru right as he was imprisoned. They were brought before Subaru, as he had told Felix and the guards that he was originally part of the Emilia camp. He didn’t speak one word. Why didn’t he try more? Did he not trust them? Did he already feel so betrayed that he couldn’t bear to speak to them?

And if that was all true, then why did he care?

Why did he care for them enough to say such horrible things? To say it was his fault or that he would take responsibility or all that nonsense. That he didn’t belong with them. That Emilia would hate him.

Please. That woman must be going crazy from grief and self-hatred. Why did Otto know? Because Otto was the same. They were all miserable selfish pieces of shit who would rather wallow in self-mutilation than even think of Subaru’s emotions. Even now, Otto couldn’t. He didn’t know what to say. What to do. What could he do?

They all failed. Every single day that Gluttony was able to reign free, they had failed. They failed Subaru the moment they forgot. He didn’t care if that didn’t make sense. Nothing made sense anymore. He didn’t understand why he was still alive. He didn’t understand how Subaru was here.

And he especially didn’t understand why Subaru still wanted to be his friend.

They were not friends. Not anymore. Because what kind of friend would abandon the other without a care, and the first second they saw each other, all that friend could do was create a pity party for himself.

It was nonsensical. Nauseating. Subaru deserved better than that. He deserved better than this convoluted fucked up situation. He deserved better than him. Or any of them.

…Maybe Ricardo was right. Otto was a coward.

“Natsuki-san. I don’t think I can be your friend,” Otto said before he turned and ran off. Not looking back and turning off his Divine Protection as much as possible.

He ran off because he couldn’t bear to say the truth. That he still wanted to be Subaru’s friend. That despite it all, a part of him just wanted to move on and let everything return to the way it was. No matter how impossible that could be.

Otto hated himself. He had not changed since he left his home. Still a coward. Still running from all his problems. And leaving his loved ones to deal with it.

He was a piece of shit until the very end.

----------------

…That could have gone better.

Subaru didn’t know what to do. He tried his best. But some scars weren’t easy to heal. And he said the wrong things. He should have been more mindful of Otto’s mental state. It hurt to hear such words from him, but he expected as such. Even Subaru wouldn’t want to be his own friend.

“Captain…” Subaru turned his head to Garfiel. “Do ya…really love dat girl?”

“…Yeah.”
“More than Princess or Rem?”

Subaru didn’t wait to say it, “Yes. More than you could ever know.”

“Why?”

“She…saved me. And is still saving me. And will save me,” at Garfiel’s confused expression, Subaru chuckled. “I know. Weird, right? But…it’s true. I know that’s a shitty reason for abandoning Emilia and Rem. I’m the worst type of guy, having wishy washy feelings that just go away out of nowhere. But…I guess I just fell out of love.”

Garfiel was silent. Ruminating and seemingly in a deep scowl. Subaru considered that Garfiel was thinking about whether to punch him or not. But the boy’s next words surprised him deeply.

“I fell out of love with Ram,” Garfiel confessed.

“Really?” Subaru couldn’t believe it. “How? You were in love with her since like, childhood.”

“Yeah but…I guess time took its toll. Sis was the same. She liked dat Clind guy despite him being a creepy fuck. And when she fell out of love, she told me it just happens. That if ya don’t nurture the love, it just dies. Dat it’s a part of life,” Garfiel sounded sullen. “For a time, I didn’t understand. But in the last few months, seein’ Ram care for that clown piece of shit despite everythin’ and despite gettin’ all Otto-like and alcoholic. I guess…I realized she and I would never be together.”

“Garf…”

“Tis fine. I’ve come ta terms with it. I was sad but…I guess time heals all wounds, even stuff in yer head,” Garfiel rubbed his neck. “I don’t know if that is the same with ya. If at all. But I guess I can understand the idea of fallin’ out of love. Though a part of me can’t stand the fact that ya gave up on Princess so easily.”

Subaru grimaced, “That’s understandable—”

“But another part of me can’t help but believe ya had yer reasons. That I’m too dumb to think of them. And that, no matter what ya might say bout yerself, I know ya aren’t the type to give up like that. Because…yer my Captain.”

Subaru didn’t know what to say, “…”

“Captain…I missed ya. We all missed ya. Even if ya think we didn’t, we did. I don’t know how ta convince ya ta stay, but I want ya ta still be with us. Yer my Captain. Our cool as fuck Knight. And ya not being there…it doesn’t feel right.”
Subaru was on the verge of tears, “G-garf…”

“Maybe it’s selfish. But I want ta still be bros with ya and Otto. I want ta still hang out, train, and act like nothin’ happened. Even if that isn’t possible, I’m too dumb to not try,” Garfiel chuckled. “…Shit. I don’t know what else ta say. Just…don’t talk like that again. Ya aren’t the one who abandoned us. Dat’s bullshit. And ya know it.”

Tears began to form at the corner of Garfiel’s eyes. And Subaru couldn’t stop himself from crying too. He held out his hand, “I…yeah.”

Garfiel couldn’t stop the tears. He clasped Subaru’s hand, before bringing him into a hug, “Welcome back Captain.”

“…It’s good to be back Garf.”

----------------------

“…Beatrice-sama. Why are you here?” Otto asked.

“Because you’re stupid, I suppose,” Beatrice said bluntly.

Chapter 71: Epilogue 3

Summary:

Otto doesn't know what to do...but Beatrice sure does.

Notes:

(See the end of the chapter for notes.)

Chapter Text

Otto and Beatrice sat comfortably on the edge of a sand dune, the wind blowing their hair as the midnight moon cast over head. The stars were stunningly beautiful out here—though it brought some bitterness to his soul. He remembered when they had gifted Subaru his own star, one made using contributions from everyone. It was a sweet memory. One that he cherished given how happy it made Subaru. Otto looked up into the sky and could not see that same star. For all he knew, it had gone dim within the last year, hidden behind the clusters and cosmos that made up the rest of the deep void in the night sky.

Or perhaps he had forgotten where it lay, not keeping tabs on it. Such things felt natural to Otto. When you’re happy, you often don’t think of how long it would last. Nor where something so ever present in your life is. You don’t look for it, expecting it to be always there. And when its finally gone, possibly months or years after it had left, you end up searching for it.

Only to find nothing, “You realized before all of us, didn’t you, Beatrice-san?”

“…Yes. But Betty only took action recently. Betty is the same as you all, I suppose.”

But unlike them, Beatrice abandoned everything, just to reunite with Subaru. It showed the lengths a spirit would go for their contracted partner. Could Otto say the same for the rest of them? Sure, every single one of them would not hesitate to say that they would. But in reality, had they known of Subaru’s existence and been thoroughly convinced of his prior existence, would they have dropped everything immediately to reunite with him?

Otto doubted it. Not because he considered his camp cruel but because he considered them to be practical. He could see Emilia wanting to meet Subaru again. But the others would most likely stop her, optioning that one of them could first meet with him and be convinced of his existence.

It could be a trick. A Witch Cult scheme. The ravings of a mad man. All were possible and while they wouldn’t necessarily kill Subaru on sight for it, they would definitely have enough distrust to be wary of him. Otto would have been probably the most vocal of his opposition, citing that they couldn’t waste resources on a person who no longer existed in their minds. Otto could imagine the exact words he would use, the exact reasoning, and how to leverage their emotions to get what he wanted.

All so that Emilia could achieve her dream and obtain queendom.

He was nothing like Beatrice, who would do whatever she could for the people she cherished, “Beatrice-sama. Are you happy with your choices?”

“What do you mean by that, in fact?” Beatrice raised an eyebrow.

Otto bit his lip, “You left without looking back. We haven’t heard from you at all in months.”

“And you assume Betty was happy with her decision?”

“You’re not?” Otto turned his head to her.

She frowned before sighing deeply, “Betty…could have been better.”

She began explaining what had happened since she left the mansion that fateful day. How she kept watch of Subaru but did nothing for so long. How she continued watching and watching for the perfect moment. Only for it to be almost too late.

“Betty could have saved her Subaru so many times. But Betty didn’t.”

“But you eventually took action,” Otto argued.

“And yet, Betty still feels like Betty could have done better,” Beatrice looked up at the stars. “Betty could’ve helped him escape more cleanly, nursed him back to health more directly, or even just be by his side since the beginning, I suppose. But Betty didn’t. And for that, Betty could only feel regret.”

“…I see,” Otto could not refute that. So many times, he thought of what he could had done better. If he had been better at settling his debts, or had better business know-how, things would most certainly be better. He would be at home, with his family, with a thriving business. If only he was better.

“But that was before,” Beatrice admitted. “Nowadays, Betty does not think too much of that.”

“You don’t?”

“…Betty tries,” she sheepishly admitted, blushing slightly. “When the memories returned, all Betty could think of was the hundreds of thousands of times, Betty had failed her Subaru. Something you must have thought as well, correct?”

Otto swallows a dry cough and nodded, “Maybe.”

Beatrice huffed, “Don’t lie to me, merchant. Betty knows you better than you know yourself.”

Otto looked away, “…I don’t get why he doesn’t blame us.”

“And that is why Betty called you an idiot,” Beatrice rolled her eyes. “One year with him and you still don’t understand what Subaru is like.”

“I guess I don’t,” Otto admitted. What did Otto even know about Subaru? He knew he was a foreigner from a far off land. He knew he had crazy ideas and a lot off it came from his home. He knew Subaru would sometimes act strange, in conversations especially. And he knew that Subaru would hide things from them.

…Sometimes he would walk down the hallways in the mansion, tired from working overtime, only to hear Subaru screaming in his room. It would be the dead of night, and he would be slightly tipsy, thinking that he might have misheard some dog or cat outside. Only for him to take a quick peak and see Beatrice healing something in the darkness—he could barely see, but the light of the magic was always blatant.

Otto didn’t question it. He didn’t want to pry into Subaru’s past, though he would often give hints that he was fully willing to hear him out with zero prejudice. He had hoped his efforts would pay off and one day, they would share a beer and commiserate over their shitty lives.

Now that kind of future felt impossible.

“I don’t know him at all maybe. I can’t even understand how he fell in love with Anastasia-sama of all people. They seem like complete opposites and yet, even back there, they were almost in sync,” Otto couldn’t help but say.

Beatrice hummed, “Are they really that different?”

“One is a logical woman who thinks and values only by what‘s profitable while the other is a man who thinks with his heart more than any sort of reason. The former is mindful of her words all the time while the latter can barely keep a grip on his mouth. Honestly, they seem the exact opposite of each other’s types,” Otto assumed Anastasia was already in a relationship with Julius. And he also thought Subaru would marry Emilia the exact day after the Selection ended. These were such assured notions in his mind that he couldn’t really comprehend them falling in love within only a few months and getting immediately married for that matter.

It felt impractical, insane, and out of character for both of them.

“Betty disagrees. They are fairly similar once you get past their surface level characteristics,” Beatrice raised her fingers one by one. “They are both incredibly emotional, it’s just that Ana has a better way of masking it. They often like hiding their true feelings when it comes to certain issues. They can be blunt when the situation calls for it. They both have weird food tendencies. They get very attached to people, especially those that they care about. Despite their weak bodies, they both are willing to go headfirst into danger if the situation calls for it. They are fairly kind and considerate to those around them. They are both very greedy, especially when it comes to their relationships. And above all, those two go after what they want without hesitation.”

Otto stared at Beatrice, “Oh…well.”

Beatrice blushed, “It’s obvious if you have eyes.”

She then, for some reason, lightly slapped Anastasia’s scarf that was now around Beatrice’s neck. Otto didn’t question it, but he could see that Anastasia had won over Beatrice to her side in that short time frame. Enough that the candidate trusted Beatrice with her prized possession. It seemed they not only lost Subaru but also Beatrice.

Otto pinched himself. It was not the time to be thinking of such things, “Still. I just never expected Natsuki-san to throw away his feelings so easily.”

“Who said it was easy?” Beatrice glared at him, “Subaru agonized over their relationship for weeks. He still wanted to reunite with Emilia and the blue one, despite everything. Betty knows because he would often confide how he couldn’t decide and felt guilty from both indecision and making any decision, in fact.”

“Then why did he?” Why did he move on? What happened to talking with his friends? Did they mean so little to him? Did Otto make a mistake? Did they treat him too poorly? What is Otto missing?

“Ana nearly died. And Subaru didn’t want to lose her,” Beatrice said simply.

“…So he fell in love out of desperation?”

“He already fell in love again. But he was still clinging onto everything from his past. Her near death experience was the impetus, not the resolution, in fact,” Beatrice explained.

“I just…can’t see it,” Otto felt like a piece of shit for not. But could anyone blame him?! He had seen Subaru fight tooth and nail for Emilia! He had seen that man do whatever it took to make her happy. It just felt, so sudden. As if none of what happened before, mattered in the end.

Beatrice sighed, “You don’t see it? Or you can’t understand why he chose Ana, a practical stranger, compared to his camp.”

Otto flinched, “I didn’t mean for it come off that way.”

“And yet you are hurt because you feel like your friendship provided him nothing.”

“…This isn’t about me. Natsuki-san deserves better than that.”

“And Betty agrees. But if you really care for Betty’s Subaru, then you need to accept the truth.”

“And what is that?”

Beatrice looked him in the eyes, “We failed.”

“I already knew that!” Otto stood up, glaring, “I know we failed! I know that we lost him! I know that we should have been better to him! But what does that matter now?! He’s hurt! But he didn’t trust enough to say how terrible it was! Anastasia-sama was the one who explained it all! And yet despite all of that, he still treats us so well! I just…” Otto fell back to the ground, his hands on his head, “I don’t understand. Why does he still look like he cares?”

Beatrice’s hand was on his arm gently, before slapping his head, “You moron.”

“Ow!”

“Knowing something and accepting it are two different things,” Beatrice snarled. “Just like how you knew that Subaru suffered for a whole year but could not accept that he wouldn’t tell you what for, I suppose.”

She knew. Of course, she knew. Otto paled, “I-I was waiting for him to tell me!”

“Just like how Betty waited for her ‘special person?’” Beatrice scoffed.

“That’s different!”

“Is it?” Beatrice raised an eyebrow, “Or how Emilia waited a whole year and still could not give Subaru a straight answer?”

“You waited centuries!”

“And that’s barely any time for a Spirit like Betty,” Beatrice stared into soul. “You‘re a human. Subaru is a human. Frail and weak. He could die from slipping on the floor with no one around and you’d regret not asking him sooner. Same for Emilia. A year may not be long to her but it is precious to those with short lives. You’re a merchant. You know just how fleeting opportunities are.”

“I…I…” Otto didn’t know how to respond to that. Because she was right. Their lives were short. Otto had assumed he would have a whole lifetime to coax Subaru into confiding in him. He originally did so out of courtesy and respect for his boundaries. But was that really the case? Was it because he wanted to be patient or was it because he feared what Subaru would say? Or maybe…he had become too drunk from the peace.

Maybe they all had. When Otto had been on his own, trying to recover from his debt, he had done all he could in the limited time he had to solve his problems. It was stressful, it was horrifying, and he could barely get a moment’s rest. And yet, his performance back then was higher than anytime now. He made a lot more mistakes, but he definitely improved his efficiency the most compared to his time in the Emilia camp.

The same could be said for the rest. In times of peril, people often change the most. Motivation comes from a human desire to survive. To obtain something they did not already have. And if that’s the case then, “We were so happy that we forgot to see if we were doing anything wrong.”

Beatrice nodded at his words, “And unfortunately, Betty’s Subaru isn’t the type to bring down others. He didn’t think his own pain was worth bringing up. Betty told you, we failed him. But we failed him long before his imprisonment.”

“…”

“…And yet, life moves on. We failed. And now, it’s time to move on.”

“How could you say that so easily?”

Beatrice shrugged, “Betty struggled with that as well. But…Tia woke Betty up.”

Otto thought for a moment, “The Wind Spirit?”

She sneered, “A thoughtless, bloodthirsty idiot, that one is. But she has lived far longer than Betty and has more wisdom to spare, I suppose. Betty believed she made an irrevocable mistake. Betty didn’t believe Tia when she said that life finds a way to survive. Thought it was some nonsense regarding nature. But life did go on, and Subaru eventually forgave Betty.”

Beatrice’s eyes glazed over as she once more looked up at the stars, still talking, “Betty didn’t believe it was deserved. That this wasn’t something that could be swept under the rug. But that annoying woman asked what the point was? Would Betty live with grief and regret throughout all of time? Wasting the precious seconds that she had left with Subaru? It was stupid. It was infuriating. But…she was right. Betty could live with regret or find happiness in what was left. Just like how Subaru could find happiness now or cling to a past that he had know way of knowing would return. Ana took that to heart faster than any of us. She had so little time left. Why waste even a moment thinking of what could have been?”

She ended her speech by pointing up, right in the galaxy of lights above. But right where she pointed—almost a speck of dust within the kaleidoscope of mana the sky contained—was a familiar dim particle of light. The star that they made.

“It’s still there,” Otto whispered.

“Nothing lasts forever, I suppose,” Beatrice stood up and wiped her dress clean. “But that’s why we need to cherish these few moments, in fact. Try our hardest. Love to the best of our abilities. Remind the ones we care, that we are here, and do care. Betty knows now that she has failed more than Betty could ever possibly imagine. And yet, Betty would be a fool to let regret win over happiness.”

She then turned and patted Otto on the shoulder, “Learn fast as well, merchant. You only get one more chance, in fact.”

As she walked away, Otto could hear two sets of familiar footsteps. Two people who he had grown to recognize and call brothers. One that was confident with each step, while the other who was a lot more casual and slow.

Yet now, the former felt uncertain. And the latter…

Tired, dragging, and almost as if he was barely hanging on. But there was purpose in his steps. Even though it was unrecognizable, that same careful gait and rhythm was still there. His friend was still there.

Otto looked down at the ground and sighed, “I’m such an asshole…”

“Otto,” his voice was filled with concern, making Otto’s heart begin to hurt again. “You mind if we talk.”

Otto didn’t want to do this. But he didn’t want to run away. Not anymore, “Please. Sit.”

Subaru sat on his left while Garfiel sat on his right. Otto chose to look at neither, and simply stare out in the distance. Silence was the appetizer to this horrible conversation. He felt Subaru shift, but he would not let Subaru take the lead here. This was his problem to rectify, not his, “I’ve been thinking of giving up on the Selection.”

Subaru lit up with alarm, and Garfiel was the same, “Wait what, why?”

Otto watched as the sand twisted into a small tornado before dissipating in front of them, “For the longest time, I thought we’ve been surviving purely on luck. That all of our victories were the result of circumstance and capitalization of those circumstances. Ever since Priestella, I had been at my wits end with trying to keep our camp manageable. But none of it felt enough. There was something missing. Something that couldn’t be replaced no matter how much we wanted to ignore it.”

Subaru was quiet as Otto sighed and finished his last words, “We missed you. Far more than I could ever explain.”

“Otto—”

“I didn’t want to be in that spot anymore. I felt like the captain of a caravan that was heading straight to hell. I was taking responsibility for the lives of people who could one day, out of nowhere, die because of my decisions. That even if I prepared all I could, the people that I cared for and loved, could disappear or turn into corpses, and there was nothing I could do about it. I felt I was shouldering countless people’s burdens without anyone even caring or noticing,” Otto breathed heavily. He felt like his throat was closing up but he needed to say what needed to be said. “It was…Hell. Honestly and truthfully, it has been the absolute worst half a year. Not as bad as being this close to being a debt slave, but the stress was comparable.”

“…”

“…Natsuki-san. Was this how you felt for so long?” Otto turned his head to a surprised Subaru. “I remember walking by your room and hearing screams. Did you have nightmares every night? If so, what were they about? What happened to you that was so bad that Beatrice-sama needed to heal you? Was there something wrong? Were you stressed, just like I was? What burdens were you carrying all of this time? And…and…and why didn’t you tell us about any of it?!” Otto hated how he sounded but he needed to let this out. Otherwise, he felt like he could never reconnect with Subaru ever again. “I would have listened! I would have helped with anything you were dealing with?! We could have dealt with it together! Or at the very least, I could be an ear to listen. I know that’s shitty of me to say because you obviously had your reasons and it’s not your obligation to tell me anything but…” Otto choked, “But…you’re my friend. And no matter what was the case, I would do whatever I could to help.”

Even if it meant taking someone’s life. Or committing the worst sins. To Otto, such actions were a pittance, if it meant his friend could be happy.

Otto didn’t look into Subaru’s eyes, scared of what he would see, “…You weren’t at fault for any of that. I didn’t tell you, not because I didn’t trust any of you. It’s because…”

Subaru clutched his chest, bringing Otto alarm and worry. So much so, he cast aside his own ineptitude and looked deep into his friend’s soul. And saw a broken man, on the cusp of falling apart, “Natsuki-san?”

“For a long time. I’ve dealt with something that I couldn’t tell anyone. I’ve…dealt with a lot. A lot of terrible and messed up things that you may not believe,” Otto wanted to refute that but Subaru wasn’t quite yet done. “I’ve been hurt. I’ve…been close to death.” Subaru gasped for breath and his eyes darted around before he swallowed his saliva, “I don’t know how best to explain it. But so many times, when I should have died. I didn’t. And it was…so awful. But I could never tell anyone. Not because I didn’t want to but because I just…just couldn’t.”

Was it a curse? Was it some kind of psychological aspect? Was there something deeply ingrained in his soul that prevented him from doing so?

All of these questions were unanswered but still, Subaru continued, “I didn’t mean to distance myself from you guys. I just…couldn’t find a way to cope with it all. I had to forget. To think everything was okay. But honestly, I guess I just realized it now, but…I’m not okay.”

“Captain,” Garfiel said softly right beside Otto. The poor boy sounded like he couldn’t bare to listen. But they both had to.

“I was up there. Facing something indescribable. And…I was so used to all the pain and everything that I guess I …I never thought…I could never even think about…what it would be like…where I could just relax. Where it didn’t feel like everything in the world was on top of me. Where life was never a constant never ending question of ‘would this last?’” Tears began to fall down Subaru’s face, “I lost my parents. They’re still alive, but I don’t think I can ever see them again. I lost…so many people. Who couldn’t remember me anymore. Time after time, again and again. It wasn’t just Gluttony. There were so many times, where I lost everything.” Otto didn’t think his heart could break anymore. He was wrong, “So when I lost you guys. When I was in that prison, I think I finally accepted that as a fact. Before…I didn’t acknowledge it. But then and there, I just had to face the reality that nothing in my life was permanent. That everyone could leave. And would leave. That no matter how happy I could be, I can’t ever cling to happiness. Because it would just hurt more when it’s gone.”

“…”

“…I ran away from you all. I just couldn’t handle it anymore. I didn’t tell you guys anything because I thought talking would lead to nothing. That even if I toed the line, tried my best, one mistake would throw it all away and I’d be back to square one,” Subaru laughed, it was pure and hollow, “I’m really a coward, aren’t I?”

“No!” Otto exclaimed, “You’re not! You did so much for us! You did so much for Lugunica and its people! You risked your life countless times. That’s not a coward, that’s a hero!”

“I’m not a hero,” before Otto or Garfiel could refute, Subaru raised his hand, “I’m no one special. I did all of those things because I believed in an ideal that Rem gave me. And even in the end, none of it mattered. When my name was gone, I realized that all I was, was just a normal guy trying to be someone he was not. If I was stronger, smarter, wiser, I could have solved this all without having to resort to breaking out. I could have talked to you all, and convinced you guys that I really existed. And life…would have been good again.”

“Captain, I—”

Otto tried to stop him but Garfiel pushed him aside and roared, “Ya are a hero ta me!”

Subaru was taken aback, “Garf?”

“I don’t care what ya say! I always knew ya were weak, not that smart, or like one of those dumbass sages. But that didn’t matter. Not ta me or Otto! You were…our captain. Even when life was hard, even when things were difficult, ya were the one who stepped up and led us ta victory! Ya got it through my thick skull that I was bein’ a dumbass asshole! Ya led the expedition against the White Whale! Against the White Rabbits! Ya saved Priestella!”

“But not alone! That was not me! I didn’t do shit! I didn’t—”

Garfiel grabbed Subaru by the collar, “I didn’t mean ya were alone! Ya had all of us! But without ya, none of that would be possible! Just because ya weren’t the only factor, doesn’t mean ya weren’t a lynchpin! Ya…you…”

Garfiel was on the verge of tears, “…You gave us hope. Who gives a shit if yer weak? Who cares if ya were following some stupid ideal?! None of that mattered because either way, what ya did, mattered most! Ya saved us! Ya saved me! And everyone back in Priestella!”

“I abandoned you! I abandoned all of you!” Subaru screamed back, “If I was so great, then I should have stayed and continued trying! I gave up!”

“Good then!” Otto was also up on his feet at this point, they all were. “You should prioritize yourself you fucking idiot! You don’t have to do everything alone! Leave! Live your life! Stop thinking like you deserve any less! We’re not that great of people!”

“What the fuck are you even talking about Otto?!” Subaru scowled.

Otto started pointing at his fingers, “Our camp is comprised of: a sociopathic clown whose sole goal is to revive his dead situationship,” Otto now knew where he learned that word. Thank you Subaru, “Twin maids, one of which is in love with said clown and the other who practically doesn’t even exist, a half-elf that has zero understanding of what sex is, a butler who really should not be near children, a drunk who is this close to popping a blood vessel, a dumbass tiger who can’t do much besides hit things really hard—”

“Hey Garf’s not dumb!”

“No, I am dumb!” Garfiel refuted.

Otto continued, “The only ones in this fucking camp who are even close to normal is a thirteen-year-old girl and Garf’s sister and that’s a low margin given how insane those two are.”

“Wait what’s wrong with Frederica and Petra?” Subaru was genuinely curious.

“Their taste in men are awful!” Otto didn’t elaborate, “Our whole group is stupid! Stop acting like you abandoning us is the worst thing in the world!”

“You don’t deserve that!”

“And you don’t deserve getting tortured but apparently, us not having you is totally worse than you getting your ribs broken every Oddamn day.”

“Well it was more like my blood was boiling—”

Otto stared at Subaru, “Do you even hear yourself? You fucking idiot! Why do you keep acting like that’s normal?! None of that’s normal! You know what’s normal? Being spiteful and petty because we left you in a literal Hellhole!?”

“But that wasn’t your fault! It was Gluttony’s!”

“How does that make it any better?! You were suffering all of this time, alone?! And you still think that it was your fault?! I should fucking punch you stupid fucking idiot! Only then could it get through your thick skull that you deserve better than the bare minimum!”

“Why are you acting like I’m not at fault?! I got engaged to Emilia’s rival! I broke our promise! I was supposed to be her knight! I should have been able to stay loyal despite all of the suffering, but I didn’t and—”

Otto punched him, growling, “You think I don’t know that?! But why are you acting like that should be your priority?! You love Anastasia-sama right?! Stop trying to be nice to us, embrace your actions, and be happy with that foxy seductress—”

Subaru punched him back, “Don’t you dare call Ana-pop a seductress!”

Before Otto could punch him back, Garfiel punched them both. They both looked at him in dismay and said, “Garf?!”

“You’re both fuckin’ dumb! Brotto can’t stop trying to act like some weird villain and Captain, stop trying to be so nice! Yer both pissin’ me off!”

“Wait, wait, Garf what are you—”

They all proceeded to start punching each other.

 

A good distance away, three spirits were watching with exasperated expressions.

“What the fuck are those three idiots doing?” Tia muttered. She then threw out a finger and decapitated an approaching Hungry Horse King. She then opened her hand and closed it, sending out a torrent of wind blades that turned the monster into dust.

Beatrice face palmed, “Boy stuff, I suppose.”

Eridna shook her head, “They remind me of Tivey and Hetaro during puberty. At least they aren’t slinging magic and mana everywhere.”

“So if I was a male, does that mean I could fight the mutt all day and night?” Tia asked.

Beatrice’s hand was still on her face, “No.”

“…What if I cut off his balls?”

Beatrice lifted her head slowly and stared at Tia, “Where did that come from, in fact?”

Tia shrugged, “If males can do that, then there must be a female equivalent.”

Beatrice was about to say no again but then she had a thought. She looked at her sister who just shook her head and said, “Do not ask me. Ana and Mimi were good kids, all things considered.”

“So we should test this, is what you are telling me,” Tia said, wind picking up around them.

Beatrice sighed and rubbed her temples, “Why did I call you wise, again?”

“Because I’m the smartest Spirit here and you should all listen to me.”

“You literally just said you want to cut Halibel’s balls off!”

“Does not refute what I said at all, dumbass.”

 

Back to the trio, who were all laying down on the sand, covered in bruises and scratch marks. All of the fighting had burned the emotions and stress out of them. So now they were left with what was most important.

“…Natsuki-san, I lied earlier,” Otto said.

“About what?” Subaru turned his head slightly.

“About not being your friend,” Otto tried his best to keep his emotions stable but it was too late, “I-I…I want to be your friend. Even if you choose to leave us to join the Anastasia Camp, I still want to be your friend.”

“…Otto,” he braced himself for Subaru’s answer. “I was always going to be your friend.”

Otto sniffled, “Really? You don’t…hate us?”

“How many times do I have to tell you guys. I don’t blame you. For anything or everything. I just…want to live now. Not as someone special, but as myself. And that means, I want to live a normal life. Hangout with friends, like a normal person. Get married, have kids, and die old.”

“…That sounds like a good life, Natsuki-san,” Otto wouldn’t mind having something similar. Maybe, perhaps. He’ll think about it once they get home. For now, he had one last thing he had to say, “Natsuki-san. It’s good to see you again.”

“…It’s good to see you too Otto.”

Still in pain and muscles creaking, they both reached over and fist bumped each other.

“Captain. Can I be yer best man at the wedding?” Garfiel didn’t hesitate to ask.

Otto whipped his head to Garfiel, “Hey wait a moment—”

“Sure, I don’t mind,” Subaru said leisurely.

“Let’s talk about this! Don’t just say yes!” Otto yelled.

Despite everything that happened, the three began to laugh and joke just like before. Even if it wasn’t perfect, and even if some scars remained, maybe they could still regain some happiness.

It was better than nothing.

-----------------

Up in a crumbling portion of the tower, Reinhard was staring down at the sight of the three men. A part of him longed to go down there, to reforge a friendship that he desperately cherished. But another part of him felt it was not his right.

Despite that, he couldn’t help but watch and listen.

He sighed to himself as something tried to stab his neck but failed. He chuckled and nuzzled the little scorpion on his shoulder, “Apologies Shaula-san, I unfortunately do not have the Divine Protection to talk to you.”
